children.translated_text: The diseases beginning with passion, constantly clinging, spread through the whole body, all of them,
which produce anxiety, delusion, and restlessness: homage to that unprecedented physician who destroyed them.
By one who desires life, the means for <s>dharma</s> (right order), wealth, and happiness,
the highest regard should be paid to the teachings of <s>Āyurveda</s> (the science of life).
<s>Brahmā</s>, remembering the Veda of life, taught it to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
He taught the <s>Aśvins</s>; they taught <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>; he taught sages such as <s>Atriputra</s>.

children.text: te 'gniveśādikāṃs te tu pṛthak tantrāṇi tenire
children.translated_text: They taught <s>Agniveśa</s> and others; these in turn composed separate treatises.
From those works, which were exceedingly scattered, generally a collection of the most essential matter
is made as the <s>Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya</s>, neither too brief nor too extensive.
Internal medicine, pediatrics, graha disorders, diseases of the upper body, surgery, toxicology, geriatrics, and virility therapy:

children.text: aṣṭāv aṅgāni tasyāhuś cikitsā yeṣu saṃśritā
children.translated_text: these are said to be its eight limbs, in which treatment is contained.

children.text: vāyuḥ pittaṃ kaphaś ceti trayo doṣāḥ samāsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Vāyu, pitta, and kapha: these are the three <s>doṣas</s> (humoral factors), in brief.

children.text: vikṛtāvikṛtā dehaṃ ghnanti te vartayanti ca
children.translated_text: When deranged and when not deranged, they respectively destroy and maintain the body.
Although they are pervasive, their seats are in the lower, middle, and upper regions, with reference to the heart and navel.
In age, day and night, and after eating, they go respectively to the end, middle, and beginning.

children.text: tair bhaved viṣamas tīkṣṇo mandaś cāgniḥ samaiḥ samaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By them the digestive fire becomes irregular, sharp, and dull; when they are equal, it is balanced.

children.text: koṣṭhaḥ krūro mṛdur madhyo madhyaḥ syāt taiḥ samair api
children.translated_text: The bowel is hard, soft, or middling; when those doṣas are equal too, it is middling.
When they are situated in semen and menstrual blood at birth, as with a poisonous worm from poison,

children.text: taiś ca tisraḥ prakṛtayo hīnamadhyottamāḥ pṛthak
children.translated_text: through them there are also three constitutions, separately inferior, middling, and superior.
One with balanced dhātus is the best among all; constitutions born of two doṣas are condemned.

children.text: tatra rūkṣo laghuḥ śītaḥ kharaḥ sūkṣmaś calo 'nilaḥ
children.translated_text: There vāyu is dry, light, cold, rough, subtle, and mobile.

children.text: pittaṃ sasnehatīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ laghu visraṃ saraṃ dravam ||
children.translated_text: Pitta is slightly oily, sharp, hot, light, foul-smelling, flowing, and liquid.

children.text: snigdhaḥ śīto gurur mandaḥ ślakṣṇo mṛtsnaḥ sthiraḥ kaphaḥ
children.translated_text: Kapha is oily, cold, heavy, slow, smooth, slimy, and stable.
Combination and full conjunction arise from the depletion and aggravation of one, two, or three of these.
Chyle, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and semen are the dhātus.
The seven are dūṣyas; the waste products too are urine, feces, sweat, and the like.
Increase of all comes from similar things; decrease is the reverse, from opposites.
The tastes are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent.

children.text: ṣaḍ dravyam āśritās te ca yathāpūrvaṃ balāvahāḥ
children.translated_text: They are six, dependent on substances, and, in the order stated, bestow strength.

children.text: tatrādyā mārutaṃ ghnanti trayas tiktādayaḥ kapham ||
children.translated_text: Among them the first three pacify māruta; the three beginning with bitter pacify kapha.
Astringent, bitter, and sweet pacify pitta; the others provoke it.

children.text: śamanaṃ kopanaṃ svasthahitaṃ dravyam iti tridhā ||
children.translated_text: A substance is threefold: pacifying, aggravating, and wholesome for the healthy.
There, because of the predominance of hot and cold qualities, potency is remembered as twofold.
The post-digestive effect of a substance is threefold, having the nature of sweet, sour, or pungent.
Heavy, slow, cold, oily, smooth, dense, soft, and stable,
together with subtle and clear, and with their opposites, are the twenty qualities.
The conjunction of time, sense objects, and action may be deficient, wrong, or excessive;
proper conjunction too should be understood as the sole cause of disease and health.
Disease is disequilibrium of the doṣas; health is equilibrium of the doṣas.
There diseases are remembered as twofold by the division into endogenous and external.
Their site too is twofold, by the division of body and mind.

children.text: rajas tamaś ca manaso dvau ca doṣāv udāhṛtau ||
children.translated_text: Rajas and tamas are declared to be the two doṣas of the mind.
One should examine the patient by seeing, touching, and questioning,
and the disease by its cause, prodrome, signs, relieving factors, and development.
Here region is said to be twofold, by the distinction between land and body.
Arid land is predominantly vāta, while marshy land is rich in kapha.
Ordinary land, with balanced wastes, should be taught as the third kind of terrain.
Time, beginning with a moment, and the stage of disease, determines the application of medicine.

children.text: śodhanaṃ śamanaṃ ceti samāsād auṣadhaṃ dvidhā
children.translated_text: Medicine is twofold in summary: purifying and pacifying.
For the doṣas born in the body, in order, the supreme medicines are

children.text: vastir vireko vamanaṃ tathā tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu
children.translated_text: enema, purgation, emesis, and likewise oil, ghee, and honey.
Knowledge of intellect, steadiness, self, and the like is the supreme medicine for the mental doṣas.
The physician, the substances, the attendant, and the patient are the four supports
specified for treatment, and each of these has four qualities.
The physician is skillful, has learned the meaning of the science from a teacher, has practical experience, and is pure.
The medicine has many formulations, many qualities, is complete, and is suitable.
The attendant is devoted, pure, skillful, and intelligent.

children.text: āḍhyo rogī bhiṣagvaśyo jñāpakaḥ sattvavān api ||
children.translated_text: The patient is wealthy, obedient to the physician, able to report, and strong-minded.
In a body capable of tolerating every medicine, in a young, self-controlled man,
a disease not gone to a vital spot, with slight cause, prodrome, and manifest signs, and without complication,
with dissimilar dūṣya, region, season, and constitution, and with the four supports complete,
with the planets favorable, limited to one doṣa and one pathway, and recent, is easy to cure.

children.text: śastrādisādhanaḥ kṛcchraḥ saṃkare ca tato gadaḥ
children.translated_text: A disease requiring instruments such as knives is difficult, as is one involving a mixture; after that, the illness
is manageable because life remains, through habitual wholesome regimen; when the opposite holds,
it is entirely not to be treated, being established in extreme adversity.
One that causes anxiety, delusion, and restlessness, shows fatal signs, and destroys the senses,

children.text: tyajed ārtaṃ bhiṣagbhūpair dviṣṭaṃ teṣāṃ dviṣaṃ dviṣam
children.translated_text: the physician should abandon, as also the afflicted person hated by physicians and rulers, one who hates them, or one hateful to them.
He should abandon one lacking equipment, distracted, disobedient, or whose life is spent,
one who is violent, afflicted by grief, fearful, ungrateful, or thinks himself a physician.
Now after this, the chief collection of chapters of this treatise will be stated.
Desiring life, daily regimen, seasonal conduct, prevention of diseases, and liquids,
knowledge of food, preservation of food, quantity, substances, tastes, and their bases,
knowledge of the doṣas and the like, their divisions, their treatment, and therapeutic procedures,
purification and the rest, oleation, sweating, purgation, evacuative enema, retention enema, and nasal therapy,
smoking, gargling, eye-affusion, nourishment, appliances, and surgical instruments.
the procedure for venesection, the procedure for surgery, and procedures with instruments, alkali, and cautery.
These are the thirty chapters of the <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>; the <s>Śārīrasthāna</s> is now stated:
the descent of the embryo, its disorders, and the division of limbs and vital points;
pathology, signs arising from the messenger, and, sixth, the general diagnosis of all diseases;
of fever, blood disorders, dyspnea, consumption, intoxication and the like, piles, and diarrhea;
of urinary obstruction, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), abscess and the like, and abdominal disease;
of anemia, skin disease, disorders caused by wind, and gout: sixteen chapters.

children.text: cikitsitaṃ jvare rakte kāse śvāse ca yakṣmaṇi
children.translated_text: Treatment is taught for fever, disorders of blood, cough, dyspnea, and consumption;

children.text: vamau madātyaye 'rśaḥsu viṣi dvau dvau ca mūtrite ||
children.translated_text: for vomiting, intoxication, piles, poison, and two chapters each on urinary disorders;
on abscess, abdominal tumor, enlargement of the abdomen, anemia, swelling, and erysipelas;
and on skin disease, white leprosy, disorders of wind, and gout.
These are twenty-two chapters; after this comes <s>Kalpasiddhi</s>.
The pharmaceutics of emesis and of purgation, their successful administration, and the preparation of enemas;
the successful treatment of enema complications as the sixth, and thereafter the pharmaceutics of substances.

children.text: bālopacāre tadvyādhau tadgrahe dvau ca bhūtage ||
children.translated_text: Next is the <s>Uttarasthāna</s>: two chapters on care of children, their diseases, their grahas, and spirit disorders;

children.text: unmāde 'tha smṛtibhraṃśe dvau dvau vartmasu saṃdhiṣu
children.translated_text: two each on insanity and then loss of memory, and on the eyelids and the eye-junctions;

children.text: dṛktamoliṅganāśeṣu trayo dvau dvau ca sarvage ||
children.translated_text: three on dimness of vision and loss of sight, and two each on diseases affecting the whole eye;
on the ears, nose, mouth, head, wounds, fractures, and fistula-in-ano;
two separate chapters on tumors and the like, minor diseases, and diseases of the private parts;
on poison, snakebite, insects, rats, and rejuvenation therapy;
and the fortieth chapter, on nourishment of the seed for those without offspring.
Now then we shall expound the chapter on daily regimen.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: brāhme muhūrta uttiṣṭhet svastho rakṣārtham āyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: A healthy person should rise in the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> to protect his life.
Having attended to bodily concerns, and then having performed the rules of cleanliness,
he should take a tooth-cleaning stick made from arka, banyan, khadira, karañja, kakubha, and the like,
in the morning, with a soft tip, and with an astringent, pungent, or bitter taste;
it should be as thick as the tip of the little finger, straight, and twelve finger-breadths long.
He should chew the tooth-cleaning stick without injuring the teeth and gums.
One should not use it when afflicted by indigestion, vomiting, dyspnea, cough, fever, or facial paralysis,
nor when suffering from thirst, disease of the mouth, heart, eyes, head, or ears.

children.text: sauvīram añjanaṃ nityaṃ hitam akṣṇos tato bhajet
children.translated_text: Then one should regularly use <s>sauvīra añjana</s> (collyrium), which is beneficial for the eyes.
The eye is fiery by nature; therefore it especially has danger from phlegm.
For that reason, once every seven nights one should apply <s>rasāñjana</s> for the sake of draining.
After that one should use nasal therapy, gargling, medicinal smoke, and betel.
Betel is unsuitable for those with wounds, excess pitta or blood, dryness, or aggravated eyes,
and also for those afflicted by poison, fainting, intoxication, or wasting.
One should practice oil massage daily; it removes old age, fatigue, and wind.
It makes vision clear and produces nourishment, long life, good sleep, good skin, and firmness.
One should especially make a habit of it on the head, ears, and feet.
Oil massage should be avoided by those overcome by phlegm, those who have undergone purification, and those with indigestion.
Lightness, capacity for action, kindled digestive fire, reduction of fat,
and distinct, firm limbs arise from exercise.

children.text: vātapittāmayī bālo vṛddho 'jīrṇaś ca taṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: One who has disorders of wind or pitta, a child, an old person, and one with indigestion should avoid it.
But strong people who eat unctuous food should practice it to half their capacity,

children.text: śītakāle vasante ca mandam eva tato 'nyadā
children.translated_text: in the cold season and in spring; at other times, only mildly.
Having done it, one should massage the body everywhere in a manner that feels pleasant.

children.text: tṛṣṇā kṣayaḥ pratamako raktapittaṃ śramaḥ klamaḥ
children.translated_text: Thirst, wasting, severe breathlessness, bleeding disorder, exhaustion, fatigue,

children.text: ativyāyāmataḥ kāso jvaraś chardiś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: cough, fever, and vomiting arise from excessive exercise.
Exercise, keeping vigil, walking, intercourse, laughter, speech, and other rash exertions:

children.text: gajaṃ siṃha ivākarṣan bhajann ati vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: one who indulges in them excessively perishes, like one dragging an elephant against a lion.
Dry rubbing removes phlegm and melts away fat.
It firms the limbs and is excellent for making the skin clear.
Bathing kindles appetite, is aphrodisiac and life-promoting, and gives energy and strength.
It conquers itching, dirt, fatigue, sweat, drowsiness, thirst, burning, and impurity.
Pouring warm water over the lower body gives strength,
but the same over the head takes away the strength of the hair and eyes.
Bathing is condemned for those with facial paralysis, diseases of the eyes, mouth, or ears, diarrhea,
abdominal distension, chronic nasal catarrh, indigestion, and for those who have just eaten.

children.text: jīrṇe hitaṃ mitaṃ cādyān na vegān īrayed balāt
children.translated_text: When food has been digested, one should eat what is wholesome and moderate; one should not forcibly impel natural urges.

children.text: na vegito 'nyakāryaḥ syān nājitvā sādhyam āmayam ||
children.translated_text: When an urge is present, one should not engage in another task, nor neglect a curable disease before conquering it.
All undertakings of all beings are considered to aim at happiness.

children.text: sukhaṃ ca na vinā dharmāt tasmād dharmaparo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And happiness does not exist without <s>dharma</s> (right conduct); therefore one should be devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
With devotion one should associate with virtuous friends and keep far from others.
Violence, theft, sexual misconduct, slander, harsh speech, and falsehood,
divisive talk, malice, covetousness, and wrong view:
these ten kinds of sinful action, by body, speech, and mind, one should abandon.
One should assist, as far as one can, those afflicted by loss of livelihood, disease, or grief.
One should always regard even worms and ants as oneself.
One should honor gods, cows, Brahmins, elders, physicians, kings, and guests.
One should not turn away supplicants, nor despise or insult them.
One should be chiefly helpful even toward an enemy intent on harm.

children.text: saṃpadvipatsv ekamanā hetāvīrṣyet phale na tu ||
children.translated_text: In prosperity and misfortune one should keep an even mind; one should concern oneself with the cause, not resent the result.

children.text: kāle hitaṃ mitaṃ brūyād avisaṃvādi peśalam
children.translated_text: At the proper time one should speak what is beneficial, measured, truthful, and pleasant.
One should be first to greet others, cheerful-faced, well-conducted, compassionate, and gentle.

children.text: naikaḥ sukhī na sarvatra viśrabdho na ca śaṅkitaḥ
children.translated_text: One should not be happy alone, not trust everywhere, and not be suspicious.

children.text: na kaṃcid ātmanaḥ śatruṃ nātmānaṃ kasyacid ripum ||
children.translated_text: One should regard no one as one's own enemy, nor oneself as anyone's foe.

children.text: prakāśayen nāpamānaṃ na ca niḥsnehatāṃ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: He should not display disrespect, nor lack of affection toward his master.
Observing people's dispositions, and the way in which each person is pleased,
he should behave toward each one in just that way, being skilled in pleasing others.

children.text: na pīḍayed indriyāṇi na caitāny atilālayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not torment the senses, nor should he pamper them excessively.
He should not undertake an action empty of the <s>trivarga</s> (three aims of life), and, without opposing it,
he should follow the middle course step by step in all matters of <s>dharma</s>.
He should keep his hair, nails, and beard trimmed, and keep his feet and bodily passages clean.
He should be given to bathing, pleasantly fragrant, well dressed, and bright without being garish.
He should constantly wear gems, perfected mantras, and potent medicinal herbs.
With umbrella and footwear, he should go about looking only a yoke's length ahead.

children.text: niśi cātyayike kārye daṇḍī maulī sahāyavān
children.translated_text: At night, and in urgent business, he should go with a staff, a head-covering, and a companion.
He should not step on shrines, venerable objects, flags, inauspicious shadows, ashes, chaff, or impurities,
nor on gravel, clods of earth, offerings of <s>bali</s>, or bathing places.

children.text: nadīṃ taren na bāhubhyāṃ nāgniskandham abhivrajet ||
children.translated_text: He should not cross a river by swimming with his arms, nor approach a mass of fire.
He should not climb onto a doubtful boat or tree, nor into a faulty vehicle.
He should not sneeze, laugh, or yawn with his mouth uncovered.

children.text: nāsikāṃ na vikuṣṇīyān nākasmād vilikhed bhuvam
children.translated_text: He should not distort his nose, nor scratch the ground without cause.
He should not make improper motions with his limbs, nor remain long in a squatting posture.
He should stop the activities of body, speech, and mind before fatigue sets in.

children.text: nordhvajānuś ciraṃ tiṣṭhen naktaṃ seveta na drumam ||
children.translated_text: He should not remain long with knees raised, nor resort to a tree at night,
nor likewise to squares, the precincts of shrines, crossroads, or temples,
nor to slaughterhouses, forests, empty houses, or cremation grounds, even by day.

children.text: sarvathekṣeta nādityaṃ na bhāraṃ śirasā vahet
children.translated_text: He should never gaze at the sun, and should not carry a load on his head.
He should not stare constantly at things that are minute, blazing, impure, or unpleasant.
He should not engage in the sale, preparation, giving, or receiving of liquor.
He should avoid headwinds, harsh sun, dust, dew, and rough winds.
He should avoid sneezing, belching, coughing, sleep, food, and sexual intercourse in an improper posture.
He should avoid the shade of riverbanks, a person hated by the king, wild beasts, and creatures with fangs, tusks, or horns.
He should avoid service to low, ignoble, or excessively clever people, and conflict with his superiors.
At the twilights he should avoid eating, women, sleep, study, and anxious thought.
He should avoid food in places crowded with enemies, sacrificial assemblies, groups, courtesans, or traders.
He should avoid making music with the limbs, mouth, or nails, and shaking the hands or hair.
He should avoid going between water, fire, and venerable objects, smoke, and taking shelter near a corpse.
He should abandon excessive attachment to liquor, and also overconfidence and independence in relation to women.

children.text: ācāryaḥ sarvaceṣṭāsu loka eva hi dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: For a wise person, the world itself is the teacher in all actions.
Therefore, examining worldly matters, he should imitate that very world.
Tenderness of disposition, generosity, and restraint of body, speech, and mind,
regarding others' interests as one's own, and the thought 'this is enough': this is the good vow.
Thinking, 'In what condition are my nights and days now passing?'
a person who is thus constantly attended by mindfulness does not become a sharer in suffering.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtsnadinaṃ nītvā rātrau yāme gṛhe gate
children.translated_text: Having passed the whole day in this way, and when a watch of the night has gone by at home,

children.text: devān ṛṣīn gurūn smṛtvā tataḥ śayanam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: he should remember the gods, seers, and teachers, and then go to sleep.
This, in brief, is the conduct by practicing which

children.text: āyur ārogyam aiśvaryaṃ yaśo lokāṃś ca śāśvatān ||
children.translated_text: one obtains long life, health, prosperity, fame, and eternal worlds.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter on seasonal regimen.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.

children.text: māsair dvisaṃkhyair māghādyaiḥ kramāt ṣaḍ ṛtavaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The six seasons are remembered in order, each consisting of two months, beginning with <s>Māgha</s>.
They are <s>Śiśira</s>, then spring, summer, the rains, autumn, and the cold season.

children.text: śiśirādyās tribhis tais tu vidyād ayanam uttaram
children.translated_text: The three beginning with <s>Śiśira</s> should be understood as the northern course.

children.text: ādānaṃ ca tad ādatte nṛṇāṃ pratidinaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: That is also called <s>ādāna</s> (taking away), for it takes away people's strength day by day.
For in that period, because of the nature of the course, the sun and winds are extremely sharp, hot, and dry,
and they diminish the cooling qualities of the earth.

children.text: tiktaḥ kaṣāyaḥ kaṭuko balino 'tra rasāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: Here the bitter, astringent, and pungent tastes become strong in sequence.
Therefore <s>ādāna</s> is fiery; the seasons beginning with the rains are the southern course.

children.text: varṣādayo visargaś ca yad balaṃ visṛjaty ayam
children.translated_text: This is <s>visarga</s> (release), because it releases strength.

children.text: saumyatvād atra somo hi balavān hīyate raviḥ ||
children.translated_text: For here, because of its cooling nature, <s>Soma</s> is strong and the sun declines.
When the earth's heat has been calmed by cold clouds, rain, and winds,
the sour, salty, and sweet tastes, being unctuous here, become strong.

children.text: śīte 'gryaṃ vṛṣṭigharme 'lpaṃ balaṃ madhyaṃ tu śeṣayoḥ
children.translated_text: In the cold season strength is at its best; in the rains and the heat it is slight, and in the remaining seasons it is moderate.
In <s>Hemanta</s>, because of obstruction by cold, the digestive fire becomes powerful.

children.text: bhavaty alpendhano dhātūn sa paced vāyuneritaḥ
children.translated_text: When it has little fuel, that fire, driven by <s>vāyu</s>, may digest the bodily tissues.
Therefore in this cold season one should use the sweet, sour, and salty tastes.

children.text: dairghyān niśānām etarhi prātar eva bubhukṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Because the nights are long, at this time one is hungry early in the morning.
After attending to necessary business, he should then practice the regimen as prescribed.
He should use massage with oils that counteract <s>vāta</s>, oiling of the head, and rubbing down,

children.text: niyuddhaṃ kuśalaiḥ sārdhaṃ pādāghātaṃ ca yuktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wrestling with skilled men, and appropriate foot-pressure massage.
Then, after the oiliness has been removed with astringent substances, he should bathe according to rule.
Anointed with saffron and fragrant paste, and perfumed with aloe-wood incense,

children.text: rasān snigdhān palaṃ puṣṭaṃ gauḍam acchasurāṃ surām
children.translated_text: he should take unctuous tastes, nourishing meat, jaggery liquor, clear <s>surā</s>, and <s>surā</s> wine,
as well as wholesome preparations made from wheat flour, black gram, sugarcane, and milk.

children.text: navam annaṃ vasāṃ tailaṃ śaucakārye sukhodakam
children.translated_text: He should use fresh food, fat, oil, and warm water for cleansing.
His bed should be covered with wrappers, skins, silk, rugs, blankets, and spreads.
Covered with light materials that are naturally warm, he should resort to bed.
He should always make judicious use of sun-rays, sweating, and footwear.
Beloved women with full thighs, breasts, and hips, full of passion,
remove the cold with their warm limbs, incense, saffron, and youth.
For one who moves about in heated inner rooms and houses warmed by charcoal fires,
no fault born of cold and harsh dryness ever arises.

children.text: ayam eva vidhiḥ kāryaḥ śiśire 'pi viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: This very procedure should be followed in śiśira, late winter, especially,

children.text: tadā hi śītam adhikaṃ raukṣyaṃ cādānakālajam ||
children.translated_text: for then cold is stronger, and so is dryness produced by the season of depletion.
<s>Kapha</s> (the phlegmatic humor), accumulated in late winter, when heated in spring by the sun's rays,

children.text: hatvāgniṃ kurute rogān atas taṃ tvarayā tyajet ||
children.translated_text: destroys the digestive fire and causes diseases; therefore one should quickly cast it off.
By strong emetics, nasal therapies, and the like, and by foods that are light and dry,
and by exercise, dry rubbing, and blows or massage, one should conquer the excessive phlegm.
Bathed and anointed with camphor, sandalwood, aloe, and saffron,
eating old barley and wheat, honey, and roasted meat of animals of dry land,
after tasting mango juices mixed in by his beloved and offered by her,
fragrant from contact with his beloved's mouth and marked by the blue lotuses of her eyes,
one should drink, with friends, wholesome and heart-pleasing drinks that create cheerfulness:
clear āsavas, ariṣṭas, sīdhu, mārdvīka wine, and mādhava liquor.
One may also drink ginger water, perfumed water, honey-water, and rain-water.
In places cooled by the southern wind, surrounded by flowing water,
where the sun is unseen, as if lost, and where jeweled pavements gleam,
where cuckoos call loudly and which are grounds suited to the work of love,
in fragrant groves with many-colored flowering trees,
a happy person should pass the midday with varied social conversations.
One should avoid heavy and cold things, daytime sleep, and oily, sour, and sweet foods.
Because in summer the sharp-rayed sun, with rays exceedingly sharp, seems to contract everything,

children.text: pratyahaṃ kṣīyate śleṣmā tena vāyuś ca vardhate
children.translated_text: <s>kapha</s> diminishes day by day, and therefore <s>vāyu</s> (the wind humor) increases.
So in this season one should avoid salty, pungent, and sour things, exercise, and the sun's rays.

children.text: bhajen madhuram evānnaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ himaṃ dravam
children.translated_text: One should resort only to sweet food, light, unctuous, cool, and liquid.
With the body sprinkled by very cold water, one should lick roasted grain flour mixed with sugar.

children.text: madyaṃ na peyaṃ peyaṃ vā svalpaṃ subahuvāri vā
children.translated_text: Wine should not be drunk; or, if drunk, it should be little and mixed with a great deal of water.
Otherwise it causes wasting, looseness, burning, and bewilderment.
One should eat rice white as jasmine and the moon, with meat of animals of dry land,
and drink meat broth that is not too thick, rasālā, rāga, and khāṇḍava.
Or one should drink a five-ingredient beverage kept in a new earthen vessel,
mixed with leaves of plantain and coca, slightly sour, and held in earthen shells.
One should drink water perfumed with pāṭalā flowers, with camphor, very cool.
At night, eating foods made cool by the moon's rays, one should drink
buffalo milk with sugar, cooled by the moon and stars.
In woods where the hot rays are blocked by sky-scraping great śāla and palm trees,
where there are grape clusters embraced by mādhavī creepers,
in a chamber whose hanging cloths are sprinkled with fragrant, cold water,
perfumed and variegated with mango shoots and hanging fruits,
and with soft plantain leaves, water-lilies, lotus fibers, lotuses, and blue lotuses,
on a couch prepared with delicate, laughing blossoms and young leaves,
at midday, afflicted by the heat of the sun, one should sleep, or else in a water-house.
There streams of vetiver-scented water flow from the hands, mouths, and breasts of artificial women.
And at night, on the roof of a palace flooded with the moon's rays,
for one whose mind is at ease, who is moist with sandalwood paste and wearing garlands,
who has ceased from the techniques of love and wears very fine, thin clothing,
water-moistened palm-leaf fans and broad lotus leaves,
gentle fanning motions and soft tossings that produce water-spraying cool breezes,
garlands of camphor and jasmine, necklaces together with yellow sandalwood,
children, mynahs, and parrots with charming, indistinct chatter,
and beloved women with lotus-fiber bracelets, radiant like full-blown lotuses,

children.text: jaṅgamā iva padminyo haranti dayitāḥ klamam ||
children.translated_text: like moving lotus ponds, remove his fatigue.
For those whose bodies are wearied by the season of depletion, the digestive fire, though low, sinks further;
in the rains the doṣas become vitiated when clouds hang heavy in the sky with water,
by wind that is suddenly cold and accompanied by mist,
by the earth's vapor, by sour digestive transformation, and by polluted water.

children.text: vahninaiva ca mandena teṣv ity anyonyadūṣiṣu
children.translated_text: And when the digestive fire itself is weak, as these factors mutually corrupt one another,

children.text: bhajet sādhāraṇaṃ sarvam ūṣmaṇas tejanaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: one should adopt everything moderate in general and whatever kindles heat.

children.text: āsthāpanaṃ śuddhatanur jīrṇaṃ dhānyaṃ rasān kṛtān
children.translated_text: With the body purified, one should use evacuative enema, old grain, prepared meat soups,
meat of animals of dry land, pulse soups, and old honey-ariṣṭa.
Or one should take whey rich in sauvarcala salt and sprinkled with the five pungent roots.

children.text: divyaṃ kaupaṃ śṛtaṃ cāmbho bhojanaṃ tv atidurdine ||
children.translated_text: One should drink rain-water, well-water, or boiled water; on a very cloudy day, the food
should have clear sourness, salt, and fat, should be dried, and should be as light as honey.
Not walking on foot, fragrant, and with garments constantly fumigated,
one should live on the upper floor of a mansion, free from vapor, cold, and spray.
One should avoid river water, churned drinks, daytime sleep, exertion, and the heat of the sun.
For bodies accustomed to the cold of the rains, when suddenly heated by the sun's rays,

children.text: taptānāṃ saṃcitaṃ vṛṣṭau pittaṃ śaradi kupyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>pitta</s> (the bilious humor) accumulated during the rains becomes aggravated in autumn.
To conquer it, one should use bitter ghee, purgation, and bloodletting.

children.text: tiktaṃ svādu kaṣāyaṃ ca kṣudhito 'nnaṃ bhajel laghu ||
children.translated_text: When hungry, one should take light food that is bitter, sweet, and astringent.
Rice, mung beans, sugar, āmalakī, paṭola, honey, and meat of animals of dry land are suitable.
Water heated by the rays of the hot-rayed sun and cooled by the rays of the cool-rayed moon,
made free from poison in every direction, day and night, by the rising of <s>Agastya</s>,

children.text: śuci haṃsodakaṃ nāma nirmalaṃ malajij jalam ||
children.translated_text: is pure, called haṃsodaka, stainless water that removes impurity.

children.text: nābhiṣyandi na vā rūkṣaṃ pānādiṣv amṛtopamam
children.translated_text: It is not obstructive, nor is it dry; for drinking and the like it is like nectar.
Bright with sandalwood, vetiver, camphor, pearl garlands, and clothing,
at the beginning of night, in palaces, one should enjoy the moonlight white as a palace.
One should avoid frost, alkali, excessive satiety, curds, oil, fat, and sunlight.
One should avoid strong liquor, sleeping by day, and the easterly wind.

children.text: śīte varṣāsu cādyāṃs trīn vasante 'ntyān rasān bhajet ||
children.translated_text: In the cold season and in the rains one should use the first three tastes, and in spring the last tastes.
In summer one should use the sweet taste; in autumn, sweet, bitter, and astringent tastes.
In autumn and spring food should be dry, and at the ends of the hot and rainy seasons it should be cooling.
This, in brief, is the rule for food and drink; at other times it is otherwise, the opposite.
One should regularly practise all the tastes, with the proper one predominant in each season.
The last and first seven days of two seasons are remembered as the junction of the seasons.

children.text: tatra pūrvo vidhis tyājyaḥ sevanīyo 'paraḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: There the former regimen should be abandoned and the later one adopted gradually.

children.text: asātmyajā hi rogāḥ syuḥ sahasā tyāgaśīlanāt ||
children.translated_text: For diseases born of incompatibility arise from suddenly giving up what one has been accustomed to.
Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the prevention of diseases.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
One should not suppress the urges of <s>vāta</s>, feces, urine, sneezing, thirst, and hunger,
nor those of sleep, cough, breath from exertion, yawning, tears, vomiting, and semen.
From obstructing downward <s>vāta</s> come <s>gulma</s> (abdominal masses), <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement), pain, and fatigue,
obstruction of <s>vāta</s>, urine, and feces, impairment of sight and digestive fire, and diseases of the heart.
From suppressing feces come twisting pain in the calves, coryza, and headache,
upward-moving wind, cutting pain, and obstruction of the heart.

children.text: mukhena viṭpravṛttiś ca pūrvoktāś cāmayāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: There may also be passage of feces through the mouth; the diseases previously mentioned are also remembered.
From suppressing urine come breaking pains in the limbs, stones, and pain in the bladder, penis, and groin,

children.text: mūtrasya rodhāt pūrve ca prāyo rogās tadauṣadham
children.translated_text: and mostly the diseases already mentioned. The treatment for these is
suppositories, oil massage, immersion baths, fomentation, and enema therapy.
For disorders arising from obstruction of feces, food and drink that loosen feces are useful.

children.text: mūtrajeṣu tu pāne ca prāgbhaktaṃ śasyate ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: For those arising from urine, ghee is recommended both in drink and before meals.
It is also to be applied near the end of digestion, in the highest dose, in a twofold application.
When used because of retention, this is called <s>avapīḍaka</s>.
From suppressing belching come loss of appetite, tremor, and obstruction in the heart and chest,
as well as distension, cough, and hiccup; there the remedy is as for hiccup.
From suppressing sneezing come headache, weakness of the senses, stiffness of the neck, and facial paralysis.
By sharp smoke, collyrium, smelling strong substances, nasal medication, and looking at the sun,

children.text: pravartayet kṣutiṃ saktāṃ snehasvedau ca śīlayet
children.translated_text: one should cause a blocked sneeze to proceed; one should also practise oleation and fomentation.
From suppressing thirst come wasting, weakness of the limbs, deafness, stupefaction, dizziness, and heart disease.

children.text: tṛṣṇāyā nigrahāt tatra śītaḥ sarvo vidhir hitaḥ
children.translated_text: There every cooling procedure is beneficial.
From suppressing hunger come breaking pains in the limbs, loss of appetite, exhaustion, emaciation, colic, and dizziness.

children.text: tatra yojyaṃ laghu snigdham uṣṇam alpaṃ ca bhojanam
children.translated_text: There light, unctuous, warm, and small quantities of food should be used.
From suppressing sleep come stupefaction, heaviness of the head and eyes, laziness, and yawning.

children.text: aṅgamardaś ca tatreṣṭaḥ svapnaḥ saṃvāhanāni ca
children.translated_text: There are also body aches; for that, sleep and massage are desired.
From suppressing cough come its increase, dyspnea, loss of appetite, and diseases of the heart.

children.text: śoṣo hidhmā ca kāryo 'tra kāsahā sutarāṃ vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: Wasting and hiccup also occur; here a treatment especially effective against cough should be carried out.
From suppressing breath caused by exertion come <s>gulma</s>, heart disease, and stupefaction.

children.text: hitaṃ viśramaṇaṃ tatra vātaghnaś ca kriyākramaḥ
children.translated_text: Rest is beneficial there, together with a therapeutic procedure that subdues <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: jṛmbhāyāḥ kṣavavad rogāḥ sarvaś cānilajid vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From yawning, the diseases are as from sneezing, and the whole treatment is one that conquers <s>vāta</s>.
From suppressing tears come catarrh, pain in the eyes, head, and heart, stiffness of the neck, loss of appetite, and dizziness.

children.text: sagulmā bāṣpatas tatra svapno madyaṃ priyāḥ kathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There may also be <s>gulma</s> from tears; for that, sleep, wine, and pleasant conversations are useful.
From suppressing vomiting come erysipelas, urticaria, skin disease, eye disease, itching, anemia, and fever,
together with cough, dyspnea, nausea, dark facial spots, and swellings.
Gargles, smoking, fasting, and vomiting it out after eating dry food are prescribed.

children.text: vyāyāmaḥ srutir asrasya śastaṃ cātra virecanam ||
children.translated_text: Exercise, bloodletting, and purgation are also recommended here.
Oil with alkali and salt is recommended for massage.
From suppressing semen come its discharge, pain and swelling in the genital region, and fever,
heart pain, retention of urine, breaking pain in the limbs, enlargement, stones, and impotence.
One should resort to rooster meat, liquor, <s>śāli</s> rice, enema, massage, and immersion baths,

children.text: vastiśuddhikaraiḥ siddhaṃ bhajet kṣīraṃ priyāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: milk prepared with substances that cleanse the bladder, and beloved women.
One should abandon as incurable a suppressor of urges who is afflicted with thirst and pain, emaciated, and vomiting feces.
All diseases arise from forcibly provoking or suppressing the natural urges.

children.text: nirdiṣṭaṃ sādhanaṃ tatra bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ye tu tān prati ||
children.translated_text: The treatment has been specified there chiefly with reference to those particular conditions.

children.text: tataś cānekadhā prāyaḥ pavano yat prakupyati
children.translated_text: Because through this <s>vāta</s> is generally provoked in many ways,
one should therefore use food, drink, and medicine that make it move downward.

children.text: dhārayet tu sadā vegān hitaiṣī pretya ceha ca
children.translated_text: But one who desires welfare both here and after death should always restrain the urges,
being self-controlled, of greed, envy, hatred, jealousy, passion, and the like.

children.text: yateta ca yathākālaṃ malānāṃ śodhanaṃ prati
children.translated_text: And one should strive, at the proper time, for the cleansing of the wastes.

children.text: atyarthasaṃcitās te hi kruddhāḥ syur jīvitacchidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when they are excessively accumulated and provoked, they may cut off life.
The <s>doṣas</s>, once subdued by fasting and digestive treatment, may sometimes become aggravated again;

children.text: ye tu saṃśodhanaiḥ śuddhā na teṣāṃ punarudbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but when they have been purified by evacuative therapies, they do not arise again.
Therefore afterward, in due order and as appropriate, one who knows the proper time should employ
proven rejuvenative preparations and aphrodisiac formulas.
When disease has been worn down by medicine, gradual strengthening with wholesome foods is prescribed,
with <s>śāli</s> rice, sixty-day rice, wheat, mung beans, meat, ghee, and the like,
combined with agreeable, appetite-kindling medicines that produce taste and digestion,
and with oil massage, powder-rubbing, bathing, decoction enemas, and unctuous enemas.
Thus he obtains comfort and the keenness of all the digestive fires,
clarity of intellect, complexion, and senses, virility, and long life.
Those diseases that arise from spirits, poison, wind, fire, wounds, fractures, and the like,

children.text: rāgadveṣabhayādyāś ca te syur āgantavo gadāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those arising from passion, hatred, fear, and so on, are external diseases.
Abandonment of errors of judgment, calming of the senses, mindfulness,
knowledge of place, time, and oneself, and following good conduct,
the pacification rites prescribed in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, and worship of adverse planets
The means for avoiding contact with spirits and the like has also been prescribed separately, each in its own place.
This procedure has been shown in brief for preventing their arising,
and also for pacifying endogenous and external disorders once they have arisen.

children.text: śītodbhavaṃ doṣacayaṃ vasante viśodhayan grīṣmajam abhrakāle
children.translated_text: One who in spring purifies the accumulation of <s>doṣa</s> produced by cold, and in the cloudy season that produced by summer,

children.text: ghanātyaye vārṣikam āśu samyak prāpnoti rogān ṛtujān na jātu ||
children.translated_text: and at the end of the rains properly and quickly clears the rainy-season accumulation, never incurs diseases born of the seasons.
One who always follows wholesome diet and conduct, acts after consideration, is unattached to sense-objects,

children.text: dātā samaḥ satyaparaḥ kṣamāvān āptopasevī ca bhavaty arogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is generous, even-minded, devoted to truth, patient, and attends upon trustworthy persons, becomes free from disease.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter called the Knowledge of Liquid Substances.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Life-giving, satisfying, good for the heart, gladdening, awakening the intellect,

children.text: tanv avyaktarasaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ śītaṃ laghv amṛtopamam ||
children.translated_text: thin, with indistinct taste, pleasant, cold, light, and like nectar,

children.text: gaṅgāmbu nabhaso bhraṣṭaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ tv arkendumārutaiḥ
children.translated_text: is <s>Gaṅgā</s> water, fallen from the sky and touched by the sun, moon, and winds.
Its wholesomeness or unwholesomeness further depends on place and time.
That rain by which clean śāli rice, when rained upon and left standing, appears bright,

children.text: aklinnam avivarṇaṃ ca tat peyaṃ gāṅgam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: not sodden and not discolored, is drinkable <s>Gaṅgā</s> water; otherwise it is not.

children.text: sāmudraṃ tan na pātavyaṃ māsād āśvayujād vinā
children.translated_text: Sea-water is not to be drunk except in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>.

children.text: aindram ambu supātrastham avipannaṃ sadā pibet ||
children.translated_text: One should always drink rain-water, kept in a good vessel and unspoiled.
In its absence, one should drink water situated on the earth that resembles atmospheric water,
in a clean, broad, dark or white region, struck by the sun and wind.
One should not drink water covered with mud, algae, grass, or leaves, or water that is turbid and spread over with refuse,
not seen by sun, moon, or wind, recently rained upon, dense, or heavy,
foamy, containing living creatures, hot, or so extremely cold that it grips the teeth,

children.text: anārtavaṃ ca yad divyam ārtavaṃ prathamaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: nor heavenly water that is out of season, nor the first seasonal rain-water,
nor water polluted by contact with spider-webs and the like, threads, feces, urine, or poison.
Rivers that flow to the western ocean, flow swiftly, and have clear water

children.text: pathyāḥ samāsāt tā nadyo viparītās tv ato 'nyathā
children.translated_text: are wholesome in brief; those opposite to these are otherwise.
Those whose waters are wearied by striking on stones, being thrown up, and being broken apart,

children.text: himavanmalayodbhūtāḥ pathyās tā eva ca sthirāḥ
children.translated_text: and which arise from <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Malaya</s>, are wholesome; but those same waters when stagnant
produce worms, elephantiasis, and diseases of the heart, throat, and head.
Waters arising in the eastern lands, <s>Avanti</s>, and <s>Aparānta</s> produce <s>durnāma</s> disorders; those born from <s>Mahendra</s>
produce abdominal disease and elephantiasis; those born from <s>Sahya</s> and <s>Vindhya</s>, again,
produce skin disease, anemia, and head diseases; those born from <s>Pāriyātra</s> destroy the <s>doṣas</s>,
and produce strength and virility; ocean water aggravates all three <s>doṣas</s>.
One should understand wells, ponds, and the like according to whether they are in dry, marshy, or mountainous country.

children.text: nāmbu peyam aśaktyā vā svalpam alpāgnigulmibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Water should not be drunk, or if unavoidable only a little, by those with weak digestion or <s>gulma</s> abdominal masses,
by those with anemia, abdominal enlargement, diarrhea, hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, wasting, or swelling.
Except in autumn and the hot season, even a healthy person should drink it only in small quantities.
Those who drink water during, after, and before a meal become respectively balanced, stout, and lean.
Cold water checks hangover, exhaustion, fainting, vomiting, fatigue, dizziness,
thirst, heat, burning, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, and poisons.
Hot water kindles digestion, digests, benefits the throat, is light and warming, and cleanses the bladder.
It is recommended for hiccup, distension, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, after immediate purification, and in fresh fever,
as well as in cough, <s>āma</s>, coryza, dyspnea, and pain in the sides.
Water that has been boiled and cooled is non-obstructive and light.

children.text: pittayukte hitaṃ doṣe vyuṣitaṃ tat tridoṣakṛt ||
children.translated_text: It is beneficial when the disturbed <s>doṣa</s> is joined with <s>pitta</s>; when stale, it aggravates all three <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: nārikelodakaṃ snigdhaṃ svādu vṛṣyaṃ himaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Coconut water is unctuous, sweet, aphrodisiac, cooling, and light.
It removes thirst, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>vāta</s>, kindles digestion, and cleanses the bladder.
In the rains, heavenly water should be taken; among waters it is the best of the better and worse kinds.
Milk is sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, unctuous, promoting <s>ojas</s>, and increasing the bodily tissues.
It removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is aphrodisiac, produces <s>kapha</s>, and is heavy and cooling.

children.text: prāyaḥ payo 'tra gavyaṃ tu jīvanīyaṃ rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: This is generally true of milk; cow's milk in particular is life-giving and a <s>rasāyana</s> rejuvenative.
It is beneficial for the wounded and depleted, promotes intelligence and strength, produces breast milk, and is laxative.
It removes fatigue, dizziness, intoxication, wasting misfortune, dyspnea, cough, excessive thirst and hunger,
chronic fever, dysuria, and <s>raktapitta</s> bleeding disorder.
Buffalo milk is heavier and cooling, beneficial for those with excessive digestive fire and sleeplessness.
Goat's milk is light because of little water-drinking, exercise, and eating pungent and bitter foods.
It conquers wasting, fever, dyspnea, <s>raktapitta</s>, and diarrhea.
Camel's milk is slightly dry, hot, and salty, kindles digestion, and is light.
It is praised for <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, abdominal distension, worms, swelling, abdominal disease, and hemorrhoids.
Human milk conquers <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, traumatic injury, and eye diseases.
It is used for nourishing eye applications, eye-drops, and nasal therapies; sheep's milk, however, is unpleasing to the heart and hot.
It removes <s>vāta</s> disorders, but produces hiccup, dyspnea, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: hastinyāḥ sthairyakṛd bāḍham uṣṇaṃ tv aikaśaphaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: Elephant's milk gives great firmness; milk of one-hoofed animals is hot and light.
It removes <s>vāta</s> in the limbs, is slightly sour and salty, and causes dullness.

children.text: payo 'bhiṣyandi gurv āmaṃ yuktyā śṛtam ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: Milk is obstructive, heavy, and immature when not properly boiled; when boiled with due method, it is otherwise.
When over-boiled it becomes still heavier; when warm straight from the udder, it is like nectar.
Curd is sour in post-digestive effect and taste, constipating, heavy, hot, and conquers <s>vāta</s>.
It increases fat, semen, strength, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood, digestive fire, and swelling.
It creates relish and is praised in anorexia, chills, and intermittent fever,

children.text: pīnase mūtrakṛcchre ca rūkṣaṃ tu grahaṇīgade
children.translated_text: as well as in coryza and dysuria; dry curd is useful in <s>grahaṇī</s> disease.
One should not eat it at night, nor hot, nor in spring, summer, or autumn,
nor without mung soup, nor without honey, nor without ghee and sugar candy,

children.text: na cānāmalakaṃ nāpi nityaṃ no mandam anyathā ||
children.translated_text: nor without āmalaka, nor daily, nor when immature; otherwise,
it causes fever, <s>raktapitta</s>, erysipelas, skin disease, anemia, and dizziness.
Buttermilk is light, astringent-sour, kindles digestion, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It treats swelling, abdominal disease, hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, urinary obstruction, and anorexia.
It conquers disorders such as diseases of the spleen, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), disorders from ghee, compound poison, and anemia.

children.text: tadvan mastu saraṃ srotaḥśodhi viṣṭambhajil laghu
children.translated_text: Likewise, whey is flowing, cleanses the channels, overcomes obstruction of stool, and is light.
Fresh butter, when new, is aphrodisiac, cold, and productive of complexion, strength, and digestive fire.
It is constipating and conquers wasting from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood, piles, facial paralysis, and cough.
But that which is produced from milk is constipating and conquers bleeding disorders and diseases of the eyes.
Ghee is recommended for intellect, memory, understanding, digestive fire, strength, lifespan, semen, and eyesight,
and for those who desire children, old age, offspring, beauty, softness, and voice.
It removes traumatic injury, wasting, spreading skin disease, and exhaustion from weapons and fire,
and it removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, poison, insanity, consumption, misfortune, and fever.

children.text: snehānām uttamaṃ śītaṃ vayasaḥ sthāpanaṃ param
children.translated_text: It is the best of fats, cold, and the supreme stabilizer of age.
Ghee has a thousand powers and, by proper methods, performs a thousand actions.
Old ghee conquers intoxication, epilepsy, fainting, and diseases of the head, ears, eyes, and <s>yoni</s>,
and it cleanses and heals wounds.
<s>Kilāṭa</s>, <s>pīyūṣa</s>, <s>kūrcikā</s>, <s>moraṇa</s>, and the like are strengthening.
They produce semen, sleep, and <s>kapha</s>; they are obstructive, heavy, and faulty.
Among products from cows, milk and ghee are the best; products from sheep and goats are censured.

children.text: ikṣoḥ saro guruḥ snigdho bṛṃhaṇaḥ kaphamūtrakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Sugarcane juice is flowing, heavy, unctuous, nourishing, and productive of <s>kapha</s> and urine.
It is aphrodisiac, cold, removes bleeding disorders, and is sweet in taste and post-digestive effect.
At the tip, when pressed by the teeth, it is slightly salty and equal to sugar.
When pressed mechanically from roots, tips, insect-eaten parts and the like, because of admixture with impurities,

children.text: kiṃcit kālaṃ vidhṛtyā ca vikṛtiṃ yāti yāntrikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because it has been kept for a little time, it undergoes alteration.
Therefore it is burning, heavy, and obstructive; among cane varieties, <s>Pauṇḍraka</s> is the best,
because of coolness, clarity, and sweetness; next after it is <s>Vāṃśika</s>.
<s>Śataparvaka</s>, <s>Kāntāra</s>, <s>Naipāla</s>, and others follow in order.

children.text: sakṣārāḥ sakaṣāyāś ca soṣṇāḥ kiṃcid vidāhinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They contain alkali, are astringent, warm, and somewhat burning.
<s>Phāṇita</s> is heavy, clogging, causes accumulation, and purifies urine.
Washed jaggery does not produce too much <s>śleṣman</s>, and it releases urine and stool.
The other kind abounds in worms, marrow, blood, fat, flesh, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: hṛdyaḥ purāṇaḥ pathyaś ca navaḥ śleṣmāgnisādakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Old jaggery is pleasing to the heart and wholesome, while new jaggery produces <s>śleṣman</s> and weakens the digestive fire.
<s>Matsyaṇḍikā</s>, <s>khaṇḍa</s>, and white sugar are aphrodisiac, beneficial for the wasted and wounded, and remove bleeding disorders and <s>vāta</s>.
In that order, they are increasingly excellent in quality.
<s>Yāsaśarkarā</s> has those same qualities; it is bitter-sweet and astringent.
All sugars remove burning, thirst, vomiting, fainting, and bleeding disorders.
Among sugar and sugarcane products, sugar and <s>phāṇita</s> are respectively the superior and the inferior.
Honey benefits the eyes, scrapes, and removes thirst, <s>śleṣman</s>, poison, hiccup, and bleeding disorders.
It conquers <s>meha</s> (urinary disease), skin disease, worms, vomiting, dyspnea, cough, and diarrhea.
It cleanses, joins, and heals wounds, and it aggravates <s>vāta</s>.
It is dry, astringent and sweet; honey-sugar is equal to it.

children.text: uṣṇam uṣṇārtam uṣṇe ca yuktaṃ coṣṇair nihanti tat ||
children.translated_text: When hot, when used for one afflicted by heat, in a hot season, or combined with hot substances, honey kills.

children.text: pracchardane nirūhe ca madhūṣṇaṃ na nivāryate
children.translated_text: In therapeutic emesis and in decoction enema, however, warm honey is not prohibited,
because in those two procedures it quickly returns before digestion has occurred.

children.text: tailaṃ svayonivat tatra mukhyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vyavāyi ca
children.translated_text: Oil is like its own source; among oils, sesame oil is chief, sharp, and diffusive.

children.text: tvagdoṣakṛd acakṣuṣyaṃ sūkṣmoṣṇaṃ kaphakṛn na ca ||
children.translated_text: It causes skin disorders, is bad for the eyes, is subtle and hot, yet does not produce <s>kapha</s>.
It is sufficient to nourish the thin and to make the corpulent lean.
It binds the stool, kills worms, and, when processed, conquers all diseases.

children.text: satiktoṣaṇam airaṇḍaṃ tailaṃ svādu saraṃ guru
children.translated_text: Castor oil is somewhat bitter and pungent, sweet, flowing, and heavy.
It conquers scrotal swelling, <s>gulma</s>, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, abdominal disease, and intermittent fever.
It also conquers pain and swelling situated in the waist, private parts, abdomen, and back.

children.text: tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ picchilaṃ visraṃ raktairaṇḍodbhavaṃ tv ati ||
children.translated_text: Oil from red castor is especially sharp, hot, slimy, and foul-smelling.
Mustard oil is pungent, hot, and sharp, and removes <s>kapha</s>, semen, and <s>vāta</s>.
It is light, produces <s>pitta</s> and blood, and conquers eruptions, skin disease, piles, wounds, and parasites.

children.text: ākṣaṃ svādu himaṃ keśyaṃ guru pittānilāpaham
children.translated_text: Oil from <s>akṣa</s> is sweet, cold, good for the hair, heavy, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Neem oil is not very hot, is bitter, and drives away worms, skin disease, and <s>kapha</s>.
Oil from flax and safflower is hot and produces skin disorders, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>.
Muscle fat and marrow both remove <s>vāta</s> and give strength, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: māṃsānugasvarūpau ca vidyān medo 'pi tāv iva
children.translated_text: One should know body fat too to be like them, and each conforms to the nature of the meat it accompanies.
Wine stimulates digestion and appetite; it is sharp, hot, and gives satisfaction and nourishment.
It has sweet, bitter, and pungent components, is sour in taste and post-digestive effect, and is flowing.
It is astringent, improves voice, health, intelligence, and complexion, and is light.
It is beneficial for those with loss of sleep or excessive sleep, and it vitiates <s>pitta</s> and blood.
It is beneficial for both the thin and the corpulent, is dry and subtle, and thoroughly purifies the channels.
When drunk properly, it removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>; otherwise it acts like poison.

children.text: guru tad doṣajananaṃ navaṃ jīrṇam ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: When new it is heavy and produces the <s>doṣas</s>; when aged it is the opposite.
It should not be drunk by one under hot regimen, nor by those who have been purged, are hungry, or are afflicted.
Nor should it be excessively sharp, too mild, made with too little material, or turbid.
<s>Surā</s> cures <s>gulma</s>, abdominal enlargement, piles, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and wasting; it is unctuous and heavy.
It removes <s>vāta</s> and brings about fat, blood, breast milk, urine, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: tadguṇā vāruṇī hṛdyā laghus tīkṣṇā nihanti ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vāruṇī</s> has those qualities, is pleasing to the heart, light, and sharp; it also destroys
colic, cough, vomiting, dyspnea, constipation, abdominal distension, and coryza.
<s>Vaibhītakī surā</s> is not very strongly intoxicating, is light, and is wholesome.

children.text: vraṇe pāṇḍvāmaye kuṣṭhe na cātyarthaṃ virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: In wounds, anemia, and skin disease it is not extremely incompatible.
Barley <s>surā</s> is obstructive, heavy, dry, and bad for all three <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Ariṣṭa</s> has the qualities of the substance from which it is made and exceeds all alcoholic drinks in quality.
It destroys <s>grahaṇī</s>, anemia, skin disease, piles, edema, wasting, abdominal enlargement, and fever,
as well as <s>gulma</s>, worms, and diseases of the spleen; it is astringent, pungent, and aggravates <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: mārdvīkaṃ lekhanaṃ hṛdyaṃ nātyuṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ saram
children.translated_text: <s>Mārdvīka</s> is scraping, pleasing to the heart, not too hot, sweet, and flowing.
It causes little <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and destroys anemia, <s>meha</s> (urinary disease), piles, and worms.
The date preparation has qualities only slightly different from this; it aggravates <s>vāta</s> (the wind humor) and is heavy.
The sugar preparation is fragrant, sweet, pleasing to the heart, not very intoxicating, and light.
The jaggery preparation promotes the passage of urine, feces, and flatus; it is nourishing and kindles digestion.
<s>Sīdhu</s> aggravates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> (the bilious humor), and removes disorders of fat and <s>kapha</s> (the phlegmatic humor).
It removes fat, swelling, abdominal enlargement, and piles; among these, the one made from fully ripened juice is best.
Honey-āsava is cutting and sharp, and conquers urinary disease, chronic rhinitis, and cough.
<s>Śukta</s> moistens blood, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>; it promotes the downward movement of <s>vāta</s>.
It is very hot, sharp, dry, and sour, pleasing to the heart, appetite-producing, and mobile.
It kindles digestion, is cold to the touch, and destroys anemia, eye disease, and worms.
Śukta made from jaggery, sugarcane, wine, and grapes is lighter in each succeeding case.
And that which is fermented from bulbs, roots, fruits, and the like should be understood in the same way.

children.text: śāṇḍākī cāsutaṃ cānyat kālāmlaṃ rocanaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śāṇḍākī</s>, another fermented preparation, and <s>kālāmla</s> are relish-producing and light.
<s>Dhānyāmla</s> is evacuative, sharp, hot, productive of <s>pitta</s>, and cold to the touch.
It removes fatigue and exhaustion, is tasty, kindles digestion, and relieves pain of the bladder.
It is recommended in evacuative enema, is pleasing to the heart, light, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Sauvīra</s> and <s>tuṣodaka</s> are endowed with these very qualities.
They remove worms, heart disease, abdominal tumors, piles, and jaundice.

children.text: te kramād vituṣair vidyāt satuṣaiś ca yavaiḥ kṛte ||
children.translated_text: Know them respectively as made from barley without husk and from barley with husk.
Urine may come from cow, goat, sheep, buffalo, elephant, horse, camel, or donkey.
It produces <s>pitta</s>, is dry, sharp, hot, pungent, and has a saline aftertaste.
Being light, it conquers worms, swelling, abdominal enlargement, distension, colic, anemia, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>,
as well as abdominal tumors, anorexia, poison, white skin disease, skin disorders, and piles.
By the groups of water, milk, sugarcane, oil, and alcoholic drink, in order,
this one section on liquids has thus been stated in general outline.
The auspicious <s>śāli</s> rices include red, great, <s>kalama</s>, <s>tūrṇaka</s>, <s>śakunāhṛta</s>,
<s>sārāmukha</s>, long-awned, <s>lodhraśūka</s>, and fragrant varieties,
<s>puṇḍra</s>, pale, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>pramoda</s>, and the two <s>gaurasāriva</s> kinds,
<s>kāñcana</s>, <s>mahiṣa</s>, awned, <s>dūṣaka</s>, and <s>kusumāṇḍaka</s>,
<s>lāṅgala</s>, those called <s>lohavāla</s>, <s>kardama</s>, and <s>śītabhīruka</s>,

children.text: pataṅgās tapanīyāś ca ye cānye śālayaḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>pataṅga</s>, <s>tapanīya</s>, and whatever other excellent <s>śāli</s> rices there are.
Their taste and digestive transformation are sweet; they are unctuous, aphrodisiac, binding, and produce little feces.
They have an astringent secondary taste, are wholesome, light, diuretic, and cooling.
Among awned grains, the red variety is best there; it removes thirst and the three doṣas.

children.text: mahāṃs tam anu kalamas taṃ cāpy anu tataḥ pare ||
children.translated_text: The great variety follows it, then <s>kalama</s>, and after that the rest.
<s>Yavaka</s>, <s>hāyana</s>, <s>pāṃsubāṣpa</s>, <s>naiṣadhaka</s>, and the like
are sweet and hot, heavy and unctuous, sour after digestion, and productive of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: sṛṣṭamūtrapurīṣāś ca pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca ninditāḥ
children.translated_text: They promote the passage of urine and feces, and each earlier one is considered inferior.

children.text: snigdho grāhī laghuḥ svādus tridoṣaghnaḥ sthiro himaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> is unctuous, absorbent, light, sweet, stable, cooling, and removes the three doṣas.
Among the <s>vrīhi</s> rices, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> is best, and the white variety is better than the dark-white.
After that, in order, come <s>mahāvrīhi</s>, <s>kṛṣṇavrīhi</s>, and <s>jatūmukha</s>,
those called <s>kukkuṭāṇḍaka</s> and <s>kalāva</s>, <s>pārāvataka</s>, and <s>śūkara</s>,
<s>varaka</s>, <s>uddālaka</s>, <s>ujjvāla</s>, <s>cīna</s>, <s>śārada</s>, and <s>dardura</s>,

children.text: gandhanāḥ kuruvindāś ca guṇair alpāntarāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: as well as <s>gandhana</s> and <s>kuruvinda</s>; they are remembered as differing only slightly in their qualities.
Other <s>vrīhi</s> rice is sweet, sour after digestion, productive of <s>pitta</s>, and heavy.
It produces abundant urine, feces, and heat, while the pale-red variety is indeed productive of all three doṣas.
<s>Kaṅgu</s>, <s>kodrava</s>, <s>nīvāra</s>, <s>śyāmāka</s>, and similar grains are cooling and light.
Grass-grains produce <s>vāta</s>, are scraping, and remove <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
They promote the joining of fractures; among them, <s>priyaṅgu</s> is nourishing and heavy.

children.text: koradūṣaḥ paraṃ grāhī sparśaḥ śīto viṣāpahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Koradūṣa</s> is extremely absorbent, cold to the touch, and removes poison.

children.text: rūkṣaḥ śīto guruḥ svāduḥ saro viḍvātakṛd yavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Barley is dry, cold, heavy, sweet, mobile, and produces feces and <s>vāta</s>.
It is aphrodisiac, gives firmness, and conquers urinary disorders, fat, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
It also conquers chronic rhinitis, dyspnea, cough, stiffness of the thighs, and diseases of the throat and skin.

children.text: nyūno yavād anuyavo rūkṣoṣṇo vaṃśajo yavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anuyava</s> is inferior to barley; bamboo barley is dry and hot.

children.text: vṛṣyaḥ śīto guruḥ snigdho jīvano vātapittahā ||
children.translated_text: Wheat is aphrodisiac, cold, heavy, unctuous, life-sustaining, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It promotes union, is sweet, gives firmness, and is mobile.
<s>Nandīmukhī</s> is wholesome, cooling, astringent-sweet, and light.
Pulse grains such as mung bean, pigeon pea, and lentil cause constipation.

children.text: kaṣāyaṃ svādu saṃgrāhi kaṭupākaṃ himaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: They are astringent, sweet, absorbent, pungent after digestion, cooling, and light.
They are beneficial in disorders of fat, <s>kapha</s>, blood, and <s>pitta</s>, and for plastering and sprinkling applications.
Among them, mung bean is best and only slightly excites <s>vāta</s>; <s>kalāya</s> is very <s>vāta</s>-provoking.
<s>Rājamāṣa</s> produces <s>vāta</s>, is dry, produces much feces, and is heavy.
Horse gram is hot and sour after digestion; it destroys semen, urinary stones, dyspnea, and chronic rhinitis,
as well as cough, piles, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>, but it greatly produces <s>pitta</s> and blood.
<s>Niṣpāva</s> produces <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood, breast milk, and urine, and is heavy.
It is mobile and burning, and removes disorders of sight, semen, <s>kapha</s>, swelling, and poison.
Black gram is unctuous, produces strength, <s>kapha</s>, feces, and <s>pitta</s>, and is mobile.
It is heavy, hot, removes <s>vāta</s>, is sweet, increases semen, and causes purgation.
The fruits of <s>kākāṇḍolā</s> and <s>ātmaguptā</s> should be known as like black gram.

children.text: uṣṇas tvacyo himaḥ sparśe keśyo balyas tilo guruḥ
children.translated_text: Sesame is hot, beneficial for the skin, cold to the touch, good for the hair, strengthening, and heavy.
It produces little urine, is pungent after digestion, and promotes intelligence, digestive fire, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Umā</s> is unctuous, sweet-bitter, hot, productive of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and heavy.

children.text: dṛkśukrahṛt kaṭuḥ pāke tadvad bījaṃ kusumbhajam ||
children.translated_text: It harms vision and semen and is pungent after digestion; safflower seed is the same.

children.text: māṣo 'tra sarveṣv avaro yavakaḥ śūkajeṣu ca
children.translated_text: Among all these, black gram is the worst; among awned grains, <s>yavaka</s> is likewise the worst.
New grain is obstructive; grain kept for a year is light.
So too are quickly grown grain, pulses, dehusked grain, and grain properly parched.
The lightness of <s>maṇḍa</s>, <s>peyā</s>, <s>vilepī</s>, and cooked rice
is in the order previously stated; among them, <s>maṇḍa</s> is beneficial and promotes the downward movement of <s>vāta</s>.
It removes thirst, lassitude, and the residue of <s>doṣas</s>; it digests and restores balance among the bodily tissues.
It softens the channels, produces sweating, and kindles the digestive fire.
It removes hunger, thirst, lassitude, weakness, abdominal disorders, and fever.
<s>Peyā</s> (thin gruel) moves the feces downward, is wholesome, and stimulates appetite and digestion.

children.text: vilepī grāhiṇī hṛdyā tṛṣṇāghnī dīpanī hitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vilepī</s> (thick gruel) is absorbent, pleasing to the heart, thirst-removing, appetite-kindling, and beneficial.
For those with wounds or eye disease, for those who have been purified, for the weak, and for those drinking unctuous substances,
rice that has been well washed, drained, steamed, and has not lost its heat is light.
So too is rice made from roasted grains and cooked in a decoction of fire-promoting herbs.

children.text: viparīto guruḥ kṣīramāṃsādyair yaś ca sādhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The opposite is heavy, as is rice cooked with milk, meat, and the like.
Thus everything should be prescribed according to substance, preparation, combination, measure, and the rest.

children.text: bṛṃhaṇaḥ prīṇano vṛṣyaś cakṣuṣyo vraṇahā rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> (meat broth) is tissue-building, satisfying, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, and healing for wounds.
Broth made from mung beans is wholesome for those who have been purified and for patients with wounds, throat disease, or eye disease.
Horse-gram broth moves <s>vāta</s> downward and conquers <s>gulma</s>, <s>tūṇī</s>, and <s>pratūṇī</s>.
Products of sesame oil-cake, dried vegetables, sprouted grains,
<s>śāṇḍākī</s> and <s>vaṭaka</s> injure the sight, aggravate the <s>doṣas</s>, waste the body, and are heavy.

children.text: rasālā bṛṃhaṇī vṛṣyā snigdhā balyā rucipradā
children.translated_text: <s>Rasālā</s> is nourishing, aphrodisiac, unctuous, strengthening, and gives relish.
<s>Pānaka</s> relieves exertion, hunger, thirst, and fatigue; it is satisfying and heavy.

children.text: viṣṭambhi mūtralaṃ hṛdyaṃ yathādravyaguṇaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: It is obstructive, diuretic, pleasing to the heart, and has the qualities of the substance from which it is made.
Parched rice cuts through thirst, vomiting, diarrhea, <s>meha</s>, fat, and <s>kapha</s>.
It calms cough and <s>pitta</s>, stimulates appetite, and is light and cooling.
Flattened rice is heavy, strengthening, and productive of <s>kapha</s> and obstruction.

children.text: dhānā viṣṭambhinī rūkṣā tarpaṇī lekhanī guruḥ
children.translated_text: Roasted grain is obstructive, dry, satisfying, scraping, and heavy.
<s>Saktu</s> (roasted grain flour) is light and removes hunger, thirst, fatigue, eye disease, and wounds.

children.text: ghnanti saṃtarpaṇāḥ pānāt sadya eva balapradāḥ
children.translated_text: When drunk, it nourishes and immediately gives strength.

children.text: nodakāntaritān na dvir na niśāyāṃ na kevalān ||
children.translated_text: One should not eat <s>saktu</s> without water in between, nor twice in a day, nor at night, nor by itself.

children.text: na bhuktvā na dvijaiś chittvā saktūn adyān na vā bahūn
children.translated_text: One should not eat it after a meal, nor after cutting it with the teeth, nor in excessive quantity.
Oil-cake is wasting, dry, obstructive, and injurious to the sight.
<s>Vesavāra</s> is heavy, unctuous, and increases strength and bodily bulk.
Preparations made from mung beans and the like are heavy and follow the qualities of their respective substances.
Cakes cooked in chaff-fire, on a potsherd, in a roasting pan, on a griddle, and in embers,
when made from the same source material, should be understood as successively lighter.
Hariṇa, eṇa, kuraṅga, ṛkṣa, gokarṇa, mṛgamātṛkā,
hare, sambar, cāruṣka, śarabha, and others are remembered as <s>mṛga</s> animals.
Lāva, vārtīka, vartīra, raktavartmaka, kukkubha,
kapiñjala, upacakra, cākrākya, cakora, and kurubāhu,

children.text: vartako vartikā caiva tittiriḥ krakaraḥ śikhī
children.translated_text: vartaka, vartikā, tittiri, krakara, peacock,
tāmracūḍa, baka, gonarda, and girivartikā,
as well as śārapada, indrābha, varaṭa, and others, are <s>viṣkira</s> birds.
Jīvañjīvaka, dātyūha, bhṛṅgāhva, parrot, mynah,
laṭvā, cuckoo, hārīta, pigeon, sparrow, and the like
are <s>pratuda</s> birds; frogs, monitor lizards, snakes, porcupines, and the like are burrow-dwellers.
Cows, donkeys, mules, camels, horses, leopards, lions, bears, monkeys,
cats, mice, tigers, wolves, mongooses, and hyenas,
foxes, jackals, hawks, blue jays, vāntāda birds, crows,
śaśaghnī birds, bhāsa birds, ospreys, vultures, owls, and kuliṅgaka birds,
dhūmikā and honey-eaters are called <s>prasaha</s>, seizing animals and birds.
Boars, buffaloes, nyaṅku deer, ruru deer, rohita deer, elephants,

children.text: sṛmaraś camaraḥ khaḍgo gavayaś ca mahāmṛgāḥ
children.translated_text: sṛmara, camara, rhinoceros, and gavaya are great animals.
Geese, cranes, kādamba birds, herons, kāraṇḍava ducks, plava waterfowl,
balākā cranes, utkrośa birds, cakrāhva, madgu, krauñca, and others move in water.
Fish, rohit fish, pāṭhīna fish, turtles, crocodiles, crabs,
oysters, conches, otters, snails, śapharī fish, varmi, candrikā,
culūkīna, krama, makara, porpoises, and timiṅgila sea creatures,

children.text: rājīcilicimādyāś ca māṃsam ity āhur aṣṭadhā
children.translated_text: as well as rājī, cilicima, and others: meat, they say, is eightfold in this way.
Among the species, goats and sheep are uncertain because their grazing range is mixed.
The first and last are considered dry-land and marshy, while the middle two are considered common.

children.text: tatra baddhamalāḥ śītā laghavo jāṅgalā hitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them, meats of dry-land animals bind the feces, are cooling, light, and beneficial
when <s>pitta</s> is predominant, <s>vāta</s> is moderate, and <s>kapha</s> is secondary in a combined disorder.

children.text: dīpanaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke grāhī rūkṣo himaḥ śaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hare is appetizing, pungent after digestion, absorbent, dry, and cooling.
Vartaka and similar birds are slightly hot, heavy, unctuous, and nourishing.
Among them the partridge is the best, promoting intelligence, digestive fire, strength, and semen.
It is absorbent, improves complexion, and is an excellent remover of combined <s>doṣa</s> disorder with increased <s>vāta</s>.
The peacock is not very wholesome, though it is wholesome for hearing, voice, age, and sight.

children.text: tadvac ca kukkuṭo vṛṣyo grāmyas tu śleṣmalo guruḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise the cock is aphrodisiac; the domestic one, however, produces <s>kapha</s> and is heavy.
Krakara birds together with upacakra birds promote intelligence and digestive fire and are pleasing to the heart.
The kāṇakapota pigeon is heavy, somewhat salty, and causes all the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: caṭakāḥ śleṣmalāḥ snigdhā vātaghnāḥ śukralāḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Sparrows produce <s>kapha</s>, are unctuous, pacify <s>vāta</s>, and are highly semen-producing.
From this point onward the groups are successively heavy, hot, unctuous, and sweet.
They produce urine and semen, strengthen, pacify <s>vāta</s>, and increase <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
The great animals are cooling; among them, the carnivorous <s>prasaha</s> animals again
have a salty aftertaste, are pungent after digestion, and increase flesh.
They are supremely beneficial for those afflicted by chronic piles, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, and wasting disease.
Goat meat is not excessively cold, heavy, or unctuous, and it does not aggravate the <s>doṣas</s>.
Because of its similarity to the bodily tissues, it is non-clogging and nourishing.

children.text: viparītam ato jñeyam āvikaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: Sheep meat should be understood as the opposite of this, though it too is nourishing.
Beef restrains dry cough, fatigue, excessive digestive fire, irregular fever, chronic rhinitis,
emaciation, and disorders consisting solely of <s>vāta</s>.
Buffalo meat is hot and very heavy; it produces sleep, firmness, and largeness of body.
Boar meat is similar; it removes fatigue and gives relish, semen, and strength.
Fish are extremely productive of <s>kapha</s>; <s>cilicīma</s> fish cause all three <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: lāvarohitagodhaiṇāḥ sve sve varge varāḥ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lāva</s>, <s>rohita</s>, <s>godhā</s>, and <s>eṇa</s> are respectively the best in their own classes.

children.text: māṃsaṃ sadyohataṃ śuddhaṃ vayaḥsthaṃ ca bhajet tyajet
children.translated_text: One should eat meat that is freshly killed, pure, and of an animal in its proper age; one should reject

children.text: mṛtaṃ kṛśaṃ bhṛśaṃ medyaṃ vyādhivāriviṣair hatam ||
children.translated_text: meat from an animal that died naturally, is emaciated, very fatty, or was killed by disease, water, or poison.
In males and females, the forepart and hindpart respectively are heavy; a pregnant female is heavy.
Among quadrupeds the female is light, but among birds the male is light.
Heaviness should be specified for the head, shoulders, thighs, back, waist, and legs,
and likewise for the stomach and colon, in the order already stated.
Among the <s>dhātus</s>, beginning with blood, each later one is heavier than the preceding one;
the testicles, penis, kidneys, liver, and rectum are heavier than flesh.
The greens born of <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>sūṣā</s>, <s>suniṣaṇṇa</s>, and <s>satīna</s>,
together with <s>rājakṣava</s> and <s>vāstuka</s>, remove all three <s>doṣas</s>, are light, and are constipating.
<s>Suniṣaṇṇa</s> kindles <s>agni</s> and is aphrodisiac; among these, <s>rājakṣava</s> is best.
It removes disorders of <s>grahaṇī</s> and piles, while <s>vāstuka</s> loosens the stool.

children.text: hanti doṣatrayaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ vṛṣyā soṣṇā rasāyanī
children.translated_text: <s>Kākamācī</s> destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> and skin disease; it is aphrodisiac, warm, and rejuvenating.
It is laxative and good for the voice; <s>cāṅgerī</s> is sour and kindles <s>agni</s>.
It is beneficial in <s>grahaṇī</s>, piles, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>; it is warm, constipating, and light.
<s>Paṭola</s>, <s>saptalā</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, <s>avalguja</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>,
reed-shoots, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>kutilī</s>, and <s>tilaparṇikā</s>,
<s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>karkoṭaka</s>, <s>kāravellaka</s>, and <s>parpaṭa</s>,
<s>nāḍī</s>, <s>kalāya</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, eggplant, forest bitters,
<s>karīra</s>, <s>kulaka</s>, <s>nandī</s>, <s>kucailā</s>, <s>śakulādanī</s>,
<s>kaṭhilla</s>, <s>kembuka</s>, and the cold group including <s>kośātaka</s> and <s>karkaśa</s>,

children.text: tiktaṃ pāke kaṭu grāhi vātalaṃ kaphapittajit ||
children.translated_text: are bitter, pungent after digestion, constipating, productive of <s>vāta</s>, and conquer <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Paṭola</s> is good for the heart, destroys worms, is sweet after digestion, and gives relish.
The two <s>bṛhatīs</s> increase <s>pitta</s>, kindle digestion, break up accumulations, and subdue <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Vṛṣa</s> removes vomiting and cough and is supreme for removing bleeding disorders.
<s>Kāravella</s>, along with <s>kaṭuka</s>, kindles digestion and is especially victorious over <s>kapha</s>.
Eggplant is pungent, bitter, hot, and sweet, and it conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It is alkaline, generates digestive fire, is good for the heart and pleasing to the taste, and does not increase <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Karīra</s> causes distension; it is astringent, sweet, and bitter.
<s>Kośātaka</s> and <s>avalguja</s> are purgative and kindle <s>agni</s>.
<s>Taṇḍulīya</s> is cooling, dry, light, and sweet in taste and after digestion.
It removes intoxication, <s>pitta</s>, poison, and blood disorders; <s>muñjāta</s> conquers <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: snigdhaṃ śītaṃ guru svādu bṛṃhaṇaṃ śukrakṛt param
