children.translated_text: It is unctuous, cold, heavy, sweet, nourishing, and especially productive of semen.

children.text: gurvī sarā tu pālaṅkyā madaghnī cāpyupodakā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pālaṅkī</s> is heavy and laxative, while <s>upodakā</s> also removes intoxication.

children.text: pālaṅkyāvat smṛtaś cañcuḥ sa tu saṃgrahaṇātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Cañcu</s> is considered like <s>pālaṅkī</s>, but it has a constipating nature.
<s>Vidārī</s> subdues <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, promotes urination, and is sweet and cooling.

children.text: jīvanī bṛṃhaṇī kaṇṭhyā gurvī vṛṣyā rasāyanam
children.translated_text: It is life-promoting, nourishing, good for the throat, heavy, aphrodisiac, and a rejuvenative.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is good for the eyes, removes all <s>doṣas</s>, and is sweet and cooling.
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, <s>tumbaka</s>, <s>kāliṅga</s>, <s>karkāru</s>, <s>ervāru</s>, and <s>tiṇḍiśa</s>,
as well as <s>trapusa</s>, <s>cīnaka</s>, and <s>cirbhaṭa</s>, produce <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
They are purgative, obstructive, channel-clogging, sweet in taste and after digestion, and heavy.
Among creeper-fruits, <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> is foremost and conquers <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It cleanses the bladder and is aphrodisiac; <s>trapusa</s>, however, is excessively diuretic.
<s>Tumba</s> is still drier and constipating; <s>kāliṅga</s>, <s>ervāru</s>, and <s>cirbhaṭa</s>

children.text: bālaṃ pittaharaṃ śītaṃ vidyāt pakvam ato 'nyathā
children.translated_text: when young are to be known as cold and <s>pitta</s>-removing, but when ripe they are the opposite.
When their stalk has withered, they are alkaline, increase <s>pitta</s>, and conquer <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
They are appetizing, kindle digestion, are good for the heart, remove <s>aṣṭhīlā</s> and distension, and are light.
Lotus fiber, lotus stalk, <s>śālūka</s>, and the tubers of <s>kumuda</s> and <s>utpala</s>,
<s>nandīmāṣaka</s>, <s>kelūṭa</s>, <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, and <s>kaseruka</s>,

children.text: krauñcādanaṃ kaloḍyaṃ ca rūkṣaṃ grāhi himaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: <s>krauñcādana</s> and <s>kaloḍya</s> are dry, constipating, cold, and heavy.
<s>Kadamba</s>, <s>nālikā</s>, <s>mārṣa</s>, <s>kuṭiñjara</s>, and <s>kutumbaka</s>,
<s>cillī</s>, <s>laṭvā</s>, <s>kaloṇī</s>, <s>kākurūṭa</s>, and <s>gavedhuka</s>,
<s>jīvanta</s>, <s>jhuñjhv eḍagaja</s>, <s>yavaśāka</s>, and <s>suvarcalā</s>,

children.text: ālukāni ca sarvāṇi tathā sūpyāni lakṣmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: all kinds of <s>āluka</s>, and likewise legumes and <s>lakṣmaṇa</s>,
are sweet, dry, somewhat salty, productive of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, and heavy.
They are cold, release feces and urine, and generally digest with obstruction.
When boiled, with their juice pressed out, and enriched with fat, they are not very aggravating to the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: laghupattrā tu yā cillī sā vāstukasamā matā ||
children.translated_text: But the thin-leaved <s>cillī</s> is considered equal to <s>vāstuka</s>.
<s>Tarkārī</s> and <s>varuṇa</s> are sweet with some bitterness and conquer <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Varṣābhū</s> and <s>kālaśāka</s> are alkaline, pungent, and bitter.
They kindle digestion, break accumulations, and destroy artificial poison, swelling, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.
The sprouts of <s>ciribilva</s> kindle digestion, subdue <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and are laxative.
The shoots of <s>śatāvarī</s> are bitter, aphrodisiac, and remove all three <s>doṣas</s>.
Bamboo shoots, however, are dry, burning, and productive of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Pattūra</s> kindles digestion, is bitter, and conquers spleen disease, piles, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Kāsamarda</s>, being laxative, conquers worms, cough, <s>kapha</s>, and fluid congestion.

children.text: rūkṣoṣṇam amlaṃ kausumbhaṃ guru pittakaraṃ saram
children.translated_text: <s>Kausumbha</s> is dry, hot, sour, heavy, productive of <s>pitta</s>, and laxative.
Mustard greens are heavy, hot, bind feces and urine, and produce all the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: yad bālam avyaktarasaṃ kiṃcit kṣāraṃ satiktakam
children.translated_text: The young radish, whose taste is undeveloped, somewhat alkaline, and slightly bitter,

children.text: tan mūlakaṃ doṣaharaṃ laghu soṣṇaṃ niyacchati ||
children.translated_text: removes the <s>doṣas</s>, is light and somewhat hot, and checks
<s>gulma</s>, cough, wasting, dyspnea, wounds, and diseases of the eyes and throat,
as well as weakness of the voice and digestive fire, upward movement of wind, and catarrh; the large radish, however,

children.text: rase pāke ca kaṭukam uṣṇavīryaṃ tridoṣakṛt
children.translated_text: is pungent in taste and after digestion, hot in potency, and productive of all three <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: gurv abhiṣyandi ca snigdhasiddhaṃ tad api vātajit ||
children.translated_text: It is heavy, channel-clogging, and unctuous; even so, when cooked with fat it conquers <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: vātaśleṣmaharaṃ śuṣkaṃ sarvam āmaṃ tu doṣalam
children.translated_text: Dried radish removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>; every raw radish, however, is aggravating to the <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Piṇḍālu</s> is pungent and hot, removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, and increases <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Kuṭhera</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>surasa</s>, <s>sumukhā</s>, <s>suribhūstṛṇa</s>,
and substances beginning with <s>phaṇijjā</s>, <s>ārjaka</s>, and <s>jambīra</s> are binding and evacuative.
They are irritant, pungent, dry, hot, good for the heart, kindling digestion and improving relish.
They benefit the eyes, semen, and worms, are sharp, excite the <s>doṣas</s>, and are light.
They remove hiccup, cough, poison, dyspnea, pain in the side, and foul smell.
<s>Surasa</s> and <s>sumukha</s> are not excessively irritant, and remove artificial poison and swelling.

children.text: ārdrikā tiktamadhurā mūtralā na ca pittakṛt
children.translated_text: Fresh ginger is bitter-sweet, diuretic, and does not produce <s>pitta</s>.
Garlic is extremely sharp and hot; its taste and post-digestive effect are pungent, and it is flowing.

children.text: hṛdyaḥ keśyo gurur vṛṣyaḥ snigdho rocanadīpanaḥ
children.translated_text: It is good for the heart and hair, heavy, aphrodisiac, unctuous, and kindles appetite and digestion.
It joins broken bones, gives strength, and vitiates blood and <s>pitta</s>.
It destroys <s>kilāsa</s>, skin disease, <s>gulma</s>, piles, <s>meha</s>, worms, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>,
together with hiccup, coryza, dyspnea, and cough; it is a rejuvenative.
<s>Palāṇḍu</s> has fewer of those qualities; it increases <s>śleṣman</s> and is not very productive of <s>pitta</s>.
It is wholesome for <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and piles, both in fomentation and when eaten.

children.text: tīkṣṇo gṛñjanako grāhī pittināṃ hitakṛn na saḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛñjanaka</s> is sharp and binding, but it is not beneficial for persons dominated by <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: dīpanaḥ śūraṇo rucyaḥ kaphaghno viśado laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śūraṇa</s> stimulates digestion, improves relish, removes <s>kapha</s>, is clear and light.

children.text: viśeṣād arśasāṃ pathyo bhūkandas tv atidoṣalaḥ
children.translated_text: It is especially wholesome for piles, while <s>bhūkanda</s> is very productive of <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: pattre puṣpe phale nāle kande ca gurutā kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In leaf, flower, fruit, stalk, and bulb, heaviness increases successively.

children.text: varā śākeṣu jīvantī sārṣapaṃ tv avaraṃ param
children.translated_text: Among greens <s>jīvantī</s> is the best, while mustard greens are decidedly the worst.
Grapes are the best of fruits: aphrodisiac, beneficial for the eyes, and promoting the free passage of urine and stool.
They are sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, unctuous, slightly astringent, cold, and heavy.
They destroy <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, bitterness of the mouth, and intoxication.
They also destroy thirst, cough, fatigue, dyspnea, hoarseness, injury, and wasting.

children.text: udriktapittāñ jayati trīn doṣān svādu dāḍimam ||
children.translated_text: Sweet pomegranate overcomes aggravated <s>pitta</s> and all three <s>doṣas</s>.
Sour pomegranate is not opposed to <s>pitta</s>, is not too hot, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ hṛdyaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ grāhi rocanadīpanam ||
children.translated_text: Every kind is good for the heart, light, unctuous, binding, and promotes relish and digestion.
Fruits produced from <s>moca</s>, date, jackfruit, coconut, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
from <s>āmrāta</s>, palmyra, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>rājādana</s>, and <s>madhūka</s>,
from <s>sauvīra</s>, jujube, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>phalgu</s>, and <s>śleṣmātaka</s>,
and <s>vātāma</s>, <s>abhiṣuka</s>, walnut, <s>mukūlaka</s>, and <s>nikocaka</s>,

children.text: urumāṇaṃ priyālaṃ ca bṛṃhaṇaṃ guru śītalam
children.translated_text: as well as <s>urumāṇa</s> and <s>priyāla</s>, are nourishing, heavy, and cold.
They remove burning, injury, and wasting, and clarify blood and <s>pitta</s>.
They have sweet post-digestive effect and taste, are unctuous, obstructive, and produce <s>kapha</s> and semen.

children.text: phalaṃ tu pittalaṃ tālaṃ saraṃ kāśmaryajaṃ himam ||
children.translated_text: The palmyra fruit, however, produces <s>pitta</s>; the fruit of <s>kāśmarya</s> is flowing and cold.
It removes obstruction of feces and urine, benefits the hair and intellect, and is rejuvenative.
<s>Vātāma</s> and the others have hot potency, produce <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and are flowing.

children.text: paraṃ vātaharaṃ snigdham anuṣṇaṃ tu priyālajam
children.translated_text: They are supreme removers of <s>vāta</s> and are unctuous; the product of <s>priyāla</s>, however, is not hot.
The kernel of <s>priyāla</s> is sweet, aphrodisiac, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: kolamajjā guṇais tadvat tṛṭchardikāsajic ca saḥ
children.translated_text: The kernel of <s>kola</s> is the same in qualities, and it conquers thirst, vomiting, and cough.
Ripe <s>bilva</s> is very hard to digest, produces <s>doṣas</s>, and causes foul flatus.

children.text: dīpanaṃ kaphavātaghnaṃ bālaṃ grāhy ubhayaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: The young fruit stimulates digestion, removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and is binding; both forms have those effects.

children.text: kapittham āmaṃ kaṇṭhaghnaṃ doṣalaṃ doṣaghāti tu ||
children.translated_text: Unripe <s>kapittha</s> harms the throat and produces <s>doṣas</s>, but when ripe it destroys <s>doṣas</s>.
When ripe it conquers hiccup and vomiting; every form is binding and removes poison.
The <s>jāmbava</s> fruit is heavy, obstructive, cold, and strongly productive of <s>vāta</s>.
It binds urine and stool, is bad for the throat, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
When young it produces <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood disorders; when its stone is firm, it produces <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: gurv āmraṃ vātajit pakvaṃ svādv amlaṃ kaphaśukrakṛt
children.translated_text: Mango is heavy and removes <s>vāta</s>; when ripe it is sweet-sour and produces <s>kapha</s> and semen.
<s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> is binding, dry, hot, removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, and is light.

children.text: śamyā gurūṣṇaṃ keśaghnaṃ rūkṣaṃ pīlu tu pittalam
children.translated_text: <s>Śamī</s> is heavy, hot, harmful to the hair, and dry, while <s>pīlu</s> produces <s>pitta</s>.
It removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, is laxative, and destroys spleen disease, piles, worms, and <s>gulma</s>.

children.text: satiktaṃ svādu yat pīlu nātyuṣṇaṃ tat tridoṣajit
children.translated_text: The <s>pīlu</s> that is slightly bitter and sweet, and not very hot, conquers all three <s>doṣas</s>.
The peel of citron is bitter-pungent, unctuous, and conquers <s>vāta</s>.
Its flesh is nourishing, sweet, heavy, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Its filaments are light and destroy cough, dyspnea, hiccup, and intoxication,
as well as dryness of the mouth, <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, constipation, vomiting, and anorexia.
They also destroy <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, piles, colic, and weakness of digestive fire.
The peel and flesh of <s>bhallātaka</s> are nourishing, sweet, and cold.
Its stone is like fire, promotes intelligence, and is an excellent remover of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: svādv amlaṃ śītam uṣṇaṃ ca dvidhā pālevataṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Pālevata</s> is of two kinds, sweet-sour, cold and hot, and heavy.
<s>Āruka</s> is pleasing, checks excessive digestive fire, and is sweet and palatable.
When ripe it digests quickly and is not excessively hot, heavy, or productive of <s>doṣas</s>.
Fresh grape and <s>parūṣaka</s> are sour and produce <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
Along with <s>karamardaka</s>, they are heavy, hot in potency, remove <s>vāta</s>, and are flowing.
Likewise sour are <s>kola</s>, <s>karkandhu</s>, <s>likuca</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, and <s>āruka</s>.
So too are <s>airāvata</s>, <s>dantaśaṭha</s>, <s>satūda</s>, and <s>mṛgaliṇḍika</s>.
Ripe and dried <s>karamardaka</s> is not very productive of <s>pitta</s>.
The dried fruit of tamarind and <s>kola</s> stimulates digestion and breaks obstruction.
It cuts thirst, fatigue, and exhaustion, is light, and is approved for <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Among fruits, <s>likuca</s> is the inferior one there, producing all the <s>doṣas</s>.
One should reject grain spoiled by cold, fire, heat, bad wind, snake saliva, and the like,
infested with creatures, sunk in water, not produced from the earth, or out of season,
mixed with other grain, weakened in potency, or spoiled by age.

children.text: dhānyaṃ tyajet tathā śākaṃ rūkṣasiddham akomalam
children.translated_text: Likewise one should reject vegetables cooked dry or not tender,
not fully developed in flavor, or dried, except in the case of radish.

children.text: prāyeṇa phalam apy evaṃ tathāmaṃ bilvavarjitam
children.translated_text: Fruit is generally the same, and so too unripe fruit, except for <s>bilva</s>.

children.text: viṣyandi lavaṇaṃ sarvaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sṛṣṭamalaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: All salt is known to be exudative, subtle, and to loosen the feces.
It removes <s>vāta</s>, undergoes digestion, is sharp and hot, improves relish, and produces <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: saindhavaṃ tatra sasvādu vṛṣyaṃ hṛdyaṃ tridoṣanut ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> salt is slightly sweet, aphrodisiac, good for the heart, and removes all three <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: laghv anuṣṇaṃ dṛśaḥ pathyam avidāhy agnidīpanam
children.translated_text: It is light, not hot, wholesome for the eyes, non-burning, and kindles the digestive fire.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> salt is light, good for the heart, fragrant, and purifies belching.
It has a pungent post-digestive effect, removes constipation, stimulates digestion, and gives relish.
<s>Viḍa</s> salt sets <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> moving properly upward and downward, and stimulates digestion.
It destroys constipation, abdominal distension, obstruction, colic, and heaviness.
<s>Sāmudra</s> sea salt is sweet in post-digestive effect, heavy, and increases <s>śleṣman</s>.
<s>Audbhida</s> salt is somewhat bitter, pungent, and alkaline; it is sharp and causes moist exudation.
In black salt the qualities of <s>sauvarcala</s> salt are present, except for fragrance.

children.text: romakaṃ laghu pāṃsūtthaṃ sakṣāraṃ śleṣmalaṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Romaka</s> salt is light; the earth-born salt is alkaline, produces <s>śleṣman</s>, and is heavy.
In the use of salts, however, one should employ them beginning with <s>saindhava</s>.
The alkali made from barley awns pacifies <s>gulma</s>, heart disease, <s>grahaṇī</s>, anemia, spleen disease, abdominal distension, and throat disorders,
as well as dyspnea, piles, <s>kapha</s>, and cough.

children.text: kṣāraḥ sarvaś ca paramaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaḥ kṛmijil laghuḥ
children.translated_text: Every alkali is supremely sharp and hot, kills worms, and is light.
It vitiates <s>pitta</s> and blood, promotes suppuration, cuts, is bad for the heart, and tears tissues apart.
Because of its pungency and saltiness it is unwholesome for semen, vitality, hair, and eyesight.
<s>Hiṅgu</s> removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, distension, and colic, but aggravates <s>pitta</s>.
It has pungent post-digestive effect and taste, is relishing, stimulates digestion, cooks the food, and is light.

children.text: kaṣāyā madhurā pāke rūkṣā vilavaṇī laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Harītakī</s> is astringent, sweet in post-digestive effect, dry, without saltiness, and light.

children.text: dīpanī pācanī medhyā vayasaḥ sthāpanī param
children.translated_text: It stimulates appetite and digestion, benefits intelligence, and is supremely stabilizing for age.
It has hot potency, is flowing, promotes life, and gives strength to intellect and the senses.
It overcomes skin disease, discoloration, hoarseness, chronic and irregular fevers,
and diseases of the head, eyes, anemia, heart disease, jaundice, and <s>grahaṇī</s>,
together with wasting, edema, diarrhea, fat disorders, confusion, vomiting, and worms.
It also conquers dyspnea, cough, salivation, piles, spleen disease, distension, poison, and abdominal disease,
as well as obstruction of the channels, <s>gulma</s>, stiffness of the thighs, and anorexia.

children.text: harītakī jayed vyādhīṃs tāṃs tāṃś ca kaphavātajān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Harītakī</s> conquers these diseases and the various disorders arising from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Āmalaka</s> is similar, but cold, sour, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: kaṭu pāke himaṃ keśyam akṣam īṣac ca tadguṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Akṣa</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, cold, good for the hair, and has those qualities to a slight degree.
This <s>triphala</s> is the best rejuvenative and removes eye diseases.
It heals, and overcomes skin disease, moist pathological exudation, fat disorders, <s>meha</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and blood disorders.
<s>Caturjāta</s>, when combined with saffron, consists of bark, leaf, and cardamom as <s>trijātaka</s>.
It aggravates <s>pitta</s>, is sharp, hot, and dry, and promotes taste and digestive fire.

children.text: rase pāke ca kaṭukaṃ kaphaghnaṃ maricaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Black pepper is pungent in taste and post-digestive effect, destroys <s>kapha</s>, and is light.

children.text: śleṣmalā svāduśītārdrā gurvī snigdhā ca pippalī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s>, when fresh, produces <s>śleṣman</s>; it is sweet, cold, moist, heavy, and unctuous.

children.text: sā śuṣkā viparītātaḥ snigdhā vṛṣyā rase kaṭuḥ
children.translated_text: When dry, it is the reverse of that; it is unctuous, aphrodisiac, and pungent in taste.
It has sweet post-digestive effect, removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, dyspnea, and cough, and is flowing.

children.text: na tām aty upayuñjīta rasāyanavidhiṃ vinā
children.translated_text: One should not use it excessively except according to a rejuvenation regimen.

children.text: nāgaraṃ dīpanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ grāhi hṛdyaṃ vibandhanut ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgara</s> ginger stimulates digestion, is aphrodisiac, absorbent, good for the heart, and removes constipation.
It is relishing, light, sweet in post-digestive effect, unctuous, hot, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: tadvad ārdrakam etac ca trayaṃ trikaṭukaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: Fresh ginger is the same; these three together are <s>trikaṭuka</s> and conquer
obesity, weak digestive fire, dyspnea, cough, elephantiasis, and coryza.
<s>Cavikā</s> and <s>pippalīmūla</s> differ only slightly in qualities from black pepper.
<s>Citraka</s> is like fire in digestion and removes edema, piles, worms, and skin disease.

children.text: pañcakolakam etac ca maricena vinā smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: This, without black pepper, is remembered as <s>pañcakolaka</s>.
It is an excellent digestive stimulant and removes <s>gulma</s>, spleen disease, abdominal enlargement, distension, and colic.
The great <s>pañcamūla</s> consists of <s>bilva</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, and <s>ṭuṇṭuka</s>.
It is astringent, bitter, and hot, and conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>anila</s> (<s>vāta</s>).
The small <s>pañcamūla</s> is remembered as consisting of <s>bṛhatī</s>, the two <s>aṃśumatī</s> plants, and <s>gokṣuraka</s>.
It is sweet in taste and post-digestive effect, neither too cold nor too hot, and conquers all <s>doṣas</s>.
The middle group consists of <s>balā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>eraṇḍa</s>, and the two <s>śūrpaparṇī</s> plants.
It destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, is not too productive of <s>pitta</s>, and is flowing.
The group called life-giving is remembered as consisting of <s>abhīru</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>.
It is good for the eyes, aphrodisiac, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>anila</s> (<s>vāta</s>).
The grass group, made up of <s>darbha</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, sugarcane, <s>śara</s>, and <s>śāli</s>, conquers <s>pitta</s>.
Food has been classified by awned grains, pulses, cooked rice, meat, vegetables, fruits, and medicines.
This small account of food for daily use has thus been stated.
The king should establish his life-physician near the royal residence.

children.text: sarvadā sa bhavaty evaṃ sarvatra pratijāgṛviḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way he is always watchful everywhere.
He should protect the food and drink especially of the king from poison.
Security and prosperity depend on that, since <s>dharma</s> and the other aims are founded upon him.

children.text: odano viṣavān sāndro yāty avisrāvyatām iva
children.translated_text: Poisoned boiled rice is dense and seems almost unable to be drained.
It cooks slowly, and when cooked it resembles stale rice.
Its heat is like a peacock’s neck and it causes confusion, fainting, and salivation.
It loses color, smell, and the like; it becomes slimy and is covered with pale patches.

children.text: vyañjanāny āśu śuṣyanti dhyāmakvāthāni tatra ca
children.translated_text: Side dishes dry up quickly, and dark decoction-like patches appear in them.

children.text: hīnātiriktā vikṛtā chāyā dṛśyeta naiva vā ||
children.translated_text: Their reflections or shades appear deficient, excessive, distorted, or not at all.
Foam, upward streaks, partings, threads, and bubbles arise.
Sauces, sour condiments, vegetables, and meat become broken in texture and tasteless.

children.text: nīlā rājī rase tāmrā kṣīre dadhni dṛśyate
children.translated_text: In broth a blue streak appears; in milk and curds a copper-colored one appears.

children.text: śyāvā pītā sitā takre ghṛte pānīyasaṃnibhā ||
children.translated_text: In buttermilk the streak is dark, yellow, or white; in ghee it resembles water.

children.text: mastuni syāt kapotābhā rājī kṛṣṇā tuṣodake
children.translated_text: In whey there is a dove-colored streak, and in husk-water a black one.
In wine and water it is black, in honey green, and in oil reddish.
Unripe fruits become as if cooked, and ripe fruits decay.
Wet and dry substances alike become withered and discolored.
In soft and hard things there is a reversal of touch.
A garland has split tips, wilting, and the arising of another smell.
On cloth there are dark circular stains and the falling away of threads and fibers.
In metals, pearls, wood, stone, gems, and the like, there is a staining as if smeared with dirt.
There is loss of unctuous touch and luster; in an earthen vessel, however, there is an unnatural brightness.
A poisoned man, with dark and dry mouth and a disturbed appearance, looks about in all directions.
Sweating and trembling, terrified and afraid, he stumbles and yawns.

children.text: prāpyānnaṃ saviṣaṃ tv agnir ekāvartaḥ sphuṭaty ati ||
children.translated_text: When fire reaches food that contains poison, it flares up violently in a single whirl.
Its smoke and flame resemble a peacock's neck; or it has no flame and gives off a fierce smell.

children.text: mriyante makṣikāḥ prāśya kākaḥ kṣāmasvaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Flies die after tasting it, and a crow becomes weak in voice.
Parrots, <s>dātyūha</s> birds, and mynahs cry out when they see it.
A goose stumbles; languor arises in the <s>jīvañjīva</s> bird.
The <s>cakora</s> loses the natural color of its eyes, and intoxication arises in the <s>krauñca</s>.
Pigeons, cuckoos, <s>dakṣa</s> birds, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds give up their lives.

children.text: udvegaṃ yāti mārjāraḥ śakṛn muñcati vānaraḥ
children.translated_text: A cat becomes agitated; a monkey voids feces.

children.text: hṛṣyen mayūras taddṛṣṭyā mandatejo bhaved viṣam ||
children.translated_text: A peacock bristles with delight at the sight of it, and the poison becomes weak in potency.

children.text: ity annaṃ viṣavaj jñātvā tyajed evaṃ prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing food to be poisonous in this way, one should carefully discard it

children.text: yathā tena vipadyerann api na kṣudrajantavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so that not even small creatures perish through it.
When it is touched, there are itching, burning, heat, fever, pain, eruptions, and numbness.
There is shedding of nails and hair and swelling; sprinkling and the other measures that destroy poison are recommended.
There, anointments are also praised, made with <s>sevya</s>, sandalwood, and <s>padmaka</s>,
together with <s>somavalka</s>, <s>tālīśapattra</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>nata</s>.
When poison has entered the mouth, there is salivation, stiffness of the tongue and lips, heat, and tingling.
There is tooth sensitivity, failure to know tastes, and stiffness of the jaw.

children.text: sevyādyais tatra gaṇḍūṣāḥ sarvaṃ ca viṣajiddhitam
children.translated_text: For that, gargles with <s>sevya</s> and the rest are useful, as is everything beneficial for conquering poison.
When it has gone to the stomach, there are sweating, fainting, distension, intoxication, and dizziness.
There is horripilation, vomiting, burning, and obstruction affecting the eyes and heart.
There are spotted swellings on the limbs; when it has gone to the colon, again,
one vomits matter of many colors, passes urine, and has diarrhea.
There are drowsiness, emaciation, pallor, abdominal swelling, and loss of strength.
In both cases, after the patient has been made to vomit and purge, one should use turmeric, <s>kaṭabhī</s>, jaggery,
<s>sindhuvārita</s>, <s>niṣpāva</s>, <s>bāṣpikā</s>, and <s>śataparvikā</s>,
the roots of <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, a hen's egg, and <s>avalguja</s>,
in nasal medication, collyrium, and drinks, for the pacification of poison.

children.text: viṣabhuktāya dadyāc ca śuddhāyordhvam adhas tathā
children.translated_text: To one who has eaten poison and has been purified both upward and downward,
one should give finely powdered copper dust at the proper time, with honey, for cleansing the heart.

children.text: śuddhe hṛdi tataḥ śāṇaṃ hemacūrṇasya dāpayet
children.translated_text: When the heart has been cleansed, one should then give a <s>śāṇa</s> of gold powder.
Poison does not cling to one whose body contains gold, as water does not cling to a lotus leaf.

children.text: jāyate vipulaṃ cāyur gare 'py eṣa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A long span of life is produced; this same procedure is prescribed even in the case of <s>gara</s> poison.
One should understand incompatible food also to be like poison and <s>gara</s>.
Meat of marsh-dwelling animals is incompatible with black gram, honey, milk, and sprouted grains,

children.text: virudhyate saha bisair mūlakena guḍena vā ||
children.translated_text: as well as with lotus stalks, radish, or jaggery.

children.text: viśeṣāt payasā matsyā matsyeṣv api cilīcimaḥ
children.translated_text: Fish are especially incompatible with milk, and among fish the <s>cilīcima</s> in particular.

children.text: viruddham amlaṃ payasā saha sarvaṃ phalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, every sour fruit is incompatible with milk.
So too are horse gram, chickpea, <s>kaṅgu</s>, <s>vallama</s>, and <s>kuṣṭaka</s>.
After eating <s>haritaka</s>, radish, and the like, one should avoid milk.
One should not eat boar with porcupine, nor spotted deer and cock with curds.
Raw meats are incompatible with bile, and radish with black-gram soup.
Mutton is incompatible with safflower greens, and sprouted grain with lotus stalks.
The <s>lākuca</s> fruit is incompatible with black-gram soup, jaggery, milk, curds, and ghee.

children.text: phalaṃ kadalyās takreṇa dadhnā tālaphalena vā
children.translated_text: The fruit of the plantain is incompatible with buttermilk, with curds, or with palm fruit.
<s>Kākamācī</s> is incompatible with <s>kaṇa</s> and <s>uṣaṇa</s>, with honey, or with jaggery.

children.text: siddhāṃ vā matsyapacane pacane nāgarasya vā
children.translated_text: It should also be avoided if cooked in a vessel used for cooking fish, or in a vessel used for cooking ginger,

children.text: siddhām anyatra vā pātre kāmāt tām uṣitāṃ niśām ||
children.translated_text: or if, after being cooked in another vessel, it has by chance remained overnight.
One should avoid long peppers cooked in the fat used for frying fish.

children.text: kāṃsye daśāham uṣitaṃ sarpir uṣṇaṃ tv aruṣkare ||
children.translated_text: Ghee kept for ten days in bronze is incompatible, and so is hot ghee with <s>aruṣkara</s>.
A <s>bhāsa</s> bird roasted on a spit is incompatible, as is <s>kampilla</s> cooked with buttermilk.
One should avoid rice pudding, liquor, and <s>kṛśara</s> taken together.
Honey, ghee, fat, oil, and water, combined two at a time or three at a time,
or together in equal parts, are mutually incompatible.
Even in unequal portions, honey and ghee are incompatible when rainwater is taken after them.
Honey with lotus seed, and honey together with <s>maireya</s> liquor and sugar preparations, are incompatible.
A milk preparation with <s>mantha</s> as its after-drink, and a turmeric preparation containing pungent oil, are incompatible.
<s>Upodakā</s> cooked with sesame paste leads to diarrhea.
The <s>balākā</s> crane is incompatible with <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor and with <s>kulmāṣa</s>.

children.text: bhṛṣṭā varāhavasayā saiva sadyo nihanty asūn ||
children.translated_text: That same bird, roasted with boar fat, immediately destroys life.
Likewise partridges, <s>pattrāḍhya</s> birds, monitor lizards, quails, and <s>kapiñjala</s> birds,
when cooked over a castor-wood fire and basted with that oil, are deadly.
The meat of the <s>hārīta</s> bird, skewered on a turmeric stick and cooked
over a turmeric fire, immediately destroys life.
The same is true when it is covered with ash and dust and mixed with honey.

children.text: yat kiṃcid doṣam utkleśya na haret tat samāsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever excites the <s>doṣas</s> and does not remove them: that, in brief, is incompatible.

children.text: viruddhaṃ śuddhir atreṣṭā śamo vā tadvirodhibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Here purification is desired, or pacification by substances opposed to it.

children.text: dravyais tair eva vā pūrvaṃ śarīrasyābhisaṃskṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or the body should previously be habituated by those very substances.
For those who exercise, are unctuous, have strong digestive fire, are in the prime of life, and possess strength,

children.text: virodhy api na pīḍāyai sātmyam alpaṃ ca bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: even incompatible food does not cause distress, if it is accustomed or taken only in small quantity.
Unwholesome food that has become habitual should be abandoned by quarters, or by quarter-quarters.
In the same way one should adopt wholesome food, leaving intervals of one, two, or three days.

children.text: apathyam api hi tyaktaṃ śīlitaṃ pathyam eva vā
children.translated_text: For even unwholesome food that is suddenly abandoned, or wholesome food that is suddenly adopted,
becomes, in another way, a cause of disorders of adaptation and non-adaptation.
When the <s>doṣas</s> have been gradually reduced and the virtues gradually built up,

children.text: santo yānty apunarbhāvam aprakampyā bhavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: the good pass into a state from which there is no return, and they become unshakable.
Since the corrupting <s>doṣas</s> are extremely near at hand

children.text: ahitair dūṣaṇaṃ bhūyo na vidvān kartum arhati ||
children.translated_text: a wise person ought not again to bring about corruption by unwholesome things.
By food, sleep, and <s>brahmacarya</s> properly applied,

children.text: śarīraṃ dhāryate nityam āgāram iva dhāraṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the body is constantly maintained, like a house by its supports.

children.text: āhāro varṇitas tatra tatra tatra ca vakṣyate
children.translated_text: Food has been described there, and will also be described in the respective places;

children.text: nidrāyattaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ puṣṭiḥ kārśyaṃ balābalam ||
children.translated_text: happiness and misery, nourishment and emaciation, strength and weakness depend on sleep,

children.text: vṛṣatā klībatā jñānam ajñānaṃ jīvitaṃ na ca
children.translated_text: as do virility and impotence, knowledge and ignorance, life and its absence.

children.text: akāle 'tiprasaṅgāc ca na ca nidrā niṣevitā ||
children.translated_text: Sleep taken at an improper time and in excess, or not taken at all,
would drive away a happy life, like another night of death.

children.text: rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ snigdhaṃ prasvapanaṃ divā ||
children.translated_text: Keeping awake at night is drying, while sleeping by day is unctuous;
but dozing while seated and moving is neither drying nor clogging.
In summer, because of the accumulation of <s>vāta</s>, depletion, dryness, and the shortness of nights,
day-sleep is beneficial; at other times it produces <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
But it is allowed for those exhausted by speaking, riding in vehicles, travel on foot, wine, women, and carrying loads,
by anger, grief, and fear, and for those suffering from dyspnea, hiccup, and diarrhea,
for the old, children, the weak, the wasted, the wounded, and those afflicted by thirst or pain,
for those with indigestion, those injured, the insane, and also those accustomed to day-sleep;

children.text: dhātusāmyaṃ tathā hy eṣāṃ śleṣmā cāṅgāni puṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for in their case it brings equilibrium of the bodily elements, and <s>śleṣman</s> nourishes the limbs.
Those who have much fat and <s>kapha</s>, and those who are habitually unctuous, should not sleep by day,

children.text: viṣārtaḥ kaṇṭharogī ca naiva jātu niśāsv api ||
children.translated_text: nor should one afflicted by poison or one with disease of the throat, indeed not even at night.
From sleeping at the wrong time arise delusion, fever, heaviness, catarrh,
headache, swelling, nausea, obstruction of the channels, and weakness of digestive fire.
In such a case one should prescribe fasting, emesis, sweating, and nasal medication as treatment;
for excessive sleep, sharp purgative collyrium and nasal therapy should be used.
Nasal therapy, lightening treatment, anxiety, sexual intercourse, grief, fear, and anger

children.text: ebhir eva ca nidrāyā nāśaḥ śleṣmātisaṃkṣayāt ||
children.translated_text: also destroy sleep by the very fact of excessive depletion of <s>śleṣman</s>.
From loss of sleep arise aching of the limbs, heaviness of the head, yawning,
stiffness, languor, dizziness, indigestion, drowsiness, and diseases born of <s>vāta</s>.
A small amount of <s>kapha</s>, stirred up by <s>vāta</s> and obstructing the vessels,
produces terrible drowsiness that takes away consciousness and causes stupor.
In that condition the eyes are partly opened, distorted, with the pupils turned about,
running and with the eyelashes disordered.

children.text: yathākālam ato nidrāṃ rātrau seveta sātmyataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore one should take sleep at night at the proper time, according to what is habitual;

children.text: asātmyāj jāgarād ardhaṃ prātaḥ svapyād abhuktavān ||
children.translated_text: if kept awake contrary to habit, one should sleep half that time in the morning, before eating.
One whose sleep is slight should cultivate milk, wine, meat broth, curds,
oil massage, rubbing, bathing, and satisfaction of the head, ears, and eyes.
The embrace of a beloved's vine-like arms, relief, the feeling of having completed one's tasks,
and objects agreeable to the mind give sleep and pleasure as desired.
For one devoted to <s>brahmacarya</s>, whose mind has no longing for vulgar pleasure,
and who is satisfied and content, sleep does not exceed its proper time.
In sexual activity one should avoid a woman lying on her back, a menstruating woman,
one who is disliked, of disagreeable conduct, or whose genitals are diseased or crowded with impurities,
one who is excessively fat or thin, recently delivered, pregnant, another man's wife,
a woman under vow, an improper orifice, and the dwelling of a teacher, deity, or king,
a shrine, cremation ground, sanctuary, crossroads, water, or a four-way junction,
festival days, defective limbs, daytime, and striking the head or heart.
One who has overeaten, lacks firmness, is hungry, has badly positioned limbs, or is thirsty,

children.text: bālo vṛddho 'nyavegārtas tyajed rogī ca maithunam ||
children.translated_text: a child, an old man, one afflicted by another urge, and a sick person should avoid intercourse.

children.text: seveta kāmataḥ kāmaṃ tṛpto vājīkṛtām hime
children.translated_text: In winter, when satisfied and strengthened with aphrodisiacs, one may engage in sex as much as desired;
in spring and autumn after three days, and in the rainy season and hot season after a fortnight.
Dizziness, exhaustion, weakness of the thighs, and loss of strength, tissues, and senses,

children.text: aparvamaraṇaṃ ca syād anyathā gacchataḥ striyam ||
children.translated_text: as well as untimely death, occur for one who approaches a woman otherwise.
Those restrained with respect to women become superior in memory, intelligence, life span, health,
nourishment, senses, fame, and strength, and they have slow aging.
After the cessation of sexual activity, one should use bathing, anointing, cool air, pieces of sugar, cool water, milk, meat broth, soup, and clear liquor,

children.text: seveta cānu śayanaṃ viratau ratasya tasyaivam āśu vapuṣaḥ punar eti dhāma ||
children.translated_text: and then sleep; in this way the splendor of his body quickly returns again.

children.text: śrutacaritasamṛddhe karmadakṣe dayālau bhiṣaji niranubandhaṃ deharakṣāṃ niveśya
children.translated_text: Having entrusted the protection of his body, without attachment, to a physician rich in learning and conduct, skilled in action and compassionate,
a king becomes abundant in brilliance, health, fame, and influence, enjoys the fruits of his own welfare, and lives long.

children.text: mātrāśī sarvakālaṃ syān mātrā hy agneḥ pravartikā
children.translated_text: At all times one should eat in proper measure, for measure stimulates the digestive fire;

children.text: mātrāṃ dravyāṇy apekṣante gurūṇy api laghūny api ||
children.translated_text: foods, whether heavy or light, depend upon measure.
For heavy foods half-satiety, and for light foods not excessive fullness,
is declared to be the standard of measure, so long as the meal is digested comfortably.
Food deficient in measure does not contribute to strength, growth, or vital vigor,
and it becomes a cause of all diseases of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: atimātraṃ punaḥ sarvān āśu doṣān prakopayet
children.translated_text: Food in excessive measure, again, quickly provokes all the <s>doṣas</s>;

children.text: pīḍyamānā hi vātādyā yugapat tena kopitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for <s>vāta</s> and the others, being pressed and provoked by it all at once,
enter that very corrupted, undigested food as <s>āma</s> and produce disorders,
causing obstruction as <s>alasaka</s>, or driving it out as <s>viṣūcikā</s>.
Through the lower and upper paths, suddenly, in a person without self-control,

children.text: prayāti nordhvaṃ nādhastād āhāro na ca pacyate ||
children.translated_text: the food moves neither upward nor downward, and it is not digested.
Having become inert in the stomach, it is therefore remembered as <s>alasaka</s>;
because of severe aggravation of <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>, with outbreaks of various pains,
it pierces the limbs as if with needles; thus it is <s>viṣūcikā</s>.
In that condition, pain, dizziness, distension, trembling, stiffness, and the like arise from <s>anila</s> (wind).
From <s>pitta</s> come fever, diarrhea, internal burning, thirst, collapse, and the like.
From <s>kapha</s> come vomiting, heaviness of the limbs, obstruction of speech, spitting, and the like.
Especially in a weak person, one with little digestive fire, and one who suppresses urges,
food oppressed by <s>māruta</s> (wind) and blocked inside by phlegm
becomes <s>alasa</s>, is agitated by the <s>doṣas</s>, and remains there just like a foreign body.
It produces severe pains and the like, but without vomiting and diarrhea.
That is <s>alasa</s>. But if the excessively vitiated <s>doṣas</s>, with their channels blocked by corrupted <s>āma</s>,

children.text: yāntas tiryak tanuṃ sarvāṃ daṇḍavat stambhayanti cet ||
children.translated_text: move obliquely through the whole body and stiffen it like a staff,
it is called <s>daṇḍakālasaka</s>; one should abandon that rapidly acting condition.
In one habitually given to incompatible food, overeating, and indigestion, the very dreadful <s>āmadoṣa</s>, marked like poison,
should be avoided as one designated poison.
This is because it has the form and rapid action of poison, and because the treatment for it is contrary.
Then, when <s>āma</s> has become <s>alasa</s> but is curable, one should quickly make the patient vomit.

children.text: pītvā sogrāpaṭuphalaṃ vāry uṣṇaṃ yojayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After he has drunk hot water with pungent and sharp fruit-drugs, one should then apply
fomentation and a fruit suppository that causes feces and wind to move downward.
Limbs that are bending should be strongly fomented and then bandaged.
When <s>viṣūcī</s> has become very severe, cauterization at the heels is recommended.
On that day he should be made to fast, and he should be treated as one who has undergone purgation.

children.text: tīvrārtir api nājīrṇī pibec chūlaghnam auṣadham
children.translated_text: Even if in intense pain, a person with indigestion should not drink pain-killing medicine.
Digestive fire covered by <s>āma</s> is not able to digest the <s>doṣa</s>, the medicine, and the food.
And a mistaken procedure in regard to these may suddenly kill the afflicted patient.
But when the food has digested, one should apply medicine in a stiff and heavy abdomen,
for the purpose of cooking the remaining <s>doṣa</s> and for kindling the digestive fire.
The calming of disorders of <s>āma</s> comes about through <s>apatarpaṇa</s> (depletion therapy).

children.text: trividhaṃ trividhe doṣe tat samīkṣya prayojayet
children.translated_text: It is threefold for the threefold <s>doṣa</s>; after examining the condition, one should apply it.
When it is slight, fasting is appropriate; when moderate, fasting together with digestive therapy.

children.text: prabhūte śodhanaṃ taddhi mūlād unmūlayen malān
children.translated_text: When abundant, purification is appropriate, for that uproots the impurities from the root.
In the same way, one should treat other diseases by applying what is opposite to their own cause.
But when a secondary complication is present, the physician should give up what is opposite to the cause
and, as appropriate, apply what is opposite to the disease.

children.text: tadarthakāri vā pakve doṣe tv iddhe ca pāvake
children.translated_text: Or he should apply what accomplishes that aim; when the <s>doṣa</s> is cooked and the fire is blazing,
oil massage, drinking of unctuous substances, enemas, and the like are beneficial when used with judgment.

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ ca kaphād āmaṃ tatra śopho 'kṣigaṇḍayoḥ
children.translated_text: Indigestion caused by <s>kapha</s> is <s>āma</s>; in it there is swelling of the eyes and cheeks,
belching as if the food had just been eaten, salivation, nausea, and heaviness.
The obstructed form, caused by <s>anila</s>, produces pain, constipation, distension, and fatigue.
The burnt form, caused by <s>pitta</s>, has thirst, confusion, dizziness, sour belching, and burning.

children.text: laṅghanaṃ kāryam āme tu viṣṭabdhe svedanaṃ bhṛśam
children.translated_text: In the <s>āma</s> form, fasting should be done; in the obstructed form, strong fomentation.

children.text: vidagdhe vamanaṃ yad vā yathāvasthaṃ hitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In the burnt form, emesis is useful, or whatever else may be suitable according to the condition.

children.text: garīyaso bhavel līnād āmād eva vilambikā
children.translated_text: From heavy <s>āma</s> that has become hidden, <s>vilambikā</s> may arise.
It has signs of <s>āma</s> connected with <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and its treatment is the same as theirs.
Because of a residue of nutritive fluid, there is lack of appetite and pain in the heart even when the belching is clear.

children.text: śayīta kiṃcid evātra sarvaś cānāśito divā ||
children.translated_text: In this case one should lie down a little, and during the day every indigestion patient should remain without food.
When hunger has arisen, he should eat a measured amount of light food.
Constipation or excessive evacuation, lassitude, and obstruction of <s>māruta</s>
are general signs of indigestion, along with obstruction, heaviness, and dizziness.
It is not only food in excessive quantity that causes <s>āmadoṣa</s>.
Food that is disliked, obstructive, burnt, unripe, heavy, dry, cold, impure,

children.text: vidāhi śuṣkam atyambuplutaṃ cānnaṃ na jīryati ||
children.translated_text: burning, dried out, or flooded with too much water does not digest.
So too food eaten by one afflicted by grief, anger, hunger, and the like.

children.text: miśraṃ pathyam apathyaṃ ca bhuktaṃ samaśanaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: A meal in which wholesome and unwholesome foods are mixed is considered <s>samaśana</s>.
One should know <s>adhyaśana</s> as eating again on top of food already eaten.

children.text: akāle bahu cālpaṃ vā bhuktaṃ tu viṣamāśanam ||
children.translated_text: Food eaten at the wrong time, whether much or little, is <s>viṣamāśana</s>.

children.text: trīṇy apy etāni mṛtyuṃ vā ghorān vyādhīn sṛjanti vā
children.translated_text: All three of these either bring about death or produce terrible diseases.

children.text: kāle sātmyaṃ śuci hitaṃ snigdhoṣṇaṃ laghu tanmanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the proper time, one should eat what is accustomed, clean, wholesome, unctuous, hot, and light, with the mind on it.
It should have the six tastes, be predominantly sweet, and not be eaten too quickly or too slowly.
One should be bathed, hungry, in a secluded place, and with feet, hands, and mouth washed.

children.text: tarpayitvā pitṝn devān atithīn bālakān gurūn
children.translated_text: Having satisfied the ancestors, gods, guests, children, and teachers,
and having looked after even animals and dependent retainers,

children.text: samīkṣya samyag ātmānam anindann abruvan dravam
children.translated_text: having properly considered oneself, without disparaging the food and without speaking,
one should eat food one likes, together with dear companions, brought by clean and devoted attendants.
One should reject food contaminated with grass, hair, and the like, food heated again,
food consisting mostly of inferior greens and grains, and food that is excessively hot or salty.
One should not habitually use <s>kilāṭa</s>, curd, <s>kūcikā</s>, alkali, sour fermented liquid, raw radish,
or the meat of lean and dried boar, sheep, goat, cow, fish, and buffalo.
Nor should one habitually use <s>māṣa</s>, <s>niṣpāva</s>, <s>śālūka</s>, lotus fiber, flour preparations, or sprouted grains,

children.text: śuṣkaśākāni yavakān phāṇitaṃ ca na śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: dried greens, <s>yavaka</s> grains, or <s>phāṇita</s>.
One should habitually use <s>śāli</s> rice, wheat, barley, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, and meat of wild animals,
<s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, tender radish, and <s>vāstuka</s>,
<s>pathyā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, grapes, <s>paṭolī</s>, mung beans, and sugar,
ghee, pure water, milk, honey, pomegranate, and rock salt.
At night, one should use <s>triphala</s> with honey and ghee for the strength of the eyes.

children.text: svāsthyānuvṛttikṛd yac ca rogocchedakaraṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: One should also habitually use whatever maintains health and whatever removes disease.
Substances such as lotus fiber, sugarcane, <s>mocā</s>, <s>cocā</s>, mango, sweet cakes, and <s>utkārikā</s>,

children.text: adyād dravyaṃ guru snigdhaṃ svādu mandaṃ sthiraṃ puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: being heavy, unctuous, sweet, slow to digest, and stable, should be eaten first.
What is opposite to these should be eaten at the end, and what is strongly sour and salty in the middle.

children.text: annena kukṣer dvāv aṃśau pānenaikaṃ prapūrayet ||
children.translated_text: One should fill two parts of the belly with food and one part with drink.
One should leave the fourth part empty as the abode of <s>vāta</s> and the others.
Cold water as an <s>anupāna</s> (after-drink) is suitable with barley and wheat.

children.text: dadhni madye viṣe kṣaudre koṣṇaṃ piṣṭamayeṣu tu
children.translated_text: But warm water is suitable with curds, wine, poison, honey, and preparations made of flour.
With preparations of greens, mung beans, and the like, whey, buttermilk, sour gruel, and fermented gruel are suitable.

children.text: surā kṛśānāṃ puṣṭyarthaṃ sthūlānāṃ tu madhūdakam
children.translated_text: For thin persons, liquor is for the sake of nourishment; for stout persons, honey-water is suitable.

children.text: śoṣe māṃsaraso madyaṃ māṃse svalpe ca pāvake ||
children.translated_text: In wasting disease, meat broth and wine are suitable, and also when there is little flesh and weak digestive fire.
When one is depleted by disease, medicine, travel, recitation, women, fasting, sun, or labor,

children.text: kṣīṇe vṛddhe ca bāle ca payaḥ pathyaṃ yathāmṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and in an old person and a child, milk is wholesome like nectar.

children.text: viparītaṃ yad annasya guṇaiḥ syād avirodhi ca
children.translated_text: Whatever is opposite in qualities to the food and yet not incompatible with it,
that, in brief, is always praised as the <s>anupāna</s>.

children.text: anupānaṃ karoty ūrjāṃ tṛptiṃ vyāptiṃ dṛḍhāṅgatām
children.translated_text: The <s>anupāna</s> produces vigor, satisfaction, diffusion, and firmness of the limbs,
as well as loosening, moistening, and digestion of the mass of food.
It is not beneficial in diseases above the clavicle, dyspnea, cough, chest injury, or catarrh,
nor during prolonged singing or recitation, nor in hoarseness of voice.
Those afflicted by a body over-moistened, urinary disorder, diseases of the eyes or throat, or wounds

children.text: pānaṃ tyajeyuḥ sarvaś ca bhāṣyādhvaśayanaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: should avoid drinking; and everyone should avoid speaking, traveling, and sleeping after drinking.
After drinking and eating, one should avoid sun, fire, riding, swimming, and being carried in a vehicle.

children.text: prasṛṣṭe viṇmūtre hṛdi suvimale doṣe svapathage
children.translated_text: When feces and urine have been passed, the heart is very clear, the <s>doṣas</s> are in their own channels,
belching is clean, hunger has arisen, and <s>vāta</s> moves along properly,

children.text: tathāgnāv udrikte viśadakaraṇe dehe ca sulaghau ||
children.translated_text: and likewise when the digestive fire is kindled, the senses are clear, and the body is very light,

children.text: prayuñjītāhāraṃ vidhiniyamitaṃ kālaḥ sa hi mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should take food regulated by rule and measure; that is considered the proper time.

children.text: dravyam eva rasādīnāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ te hi tadāśrayāḥ
children.translated_text: Substance itself is the foremost among <s>rasa</s> and the rest, for they depend upon it.

children.text: pañcabhūtātmakaṃ tat tu kṣmām adhiṣṭhāya jāyate ||
children.translated_text: It is composed of the five elements, but it arises chiefly grounded in earth.
Its production comes from the conjunction of water, earth, fire, wind, and space,

children.text: tannirvṛttir viśeṣaś ca vyapadeśas tu bhūyasā ||
children.translated_text: and its particularity also; but its designation is according to what predominates.
Therefore no substance has only one <s>rasa</s>, since it arises from a combination of elements.

children.text: naikadoṣās tato rogās tatra vyakto rasaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason diseases are not caused by only one <s>doṣa</s>; in this matter the manifest taste is called <s>rasa</s>.
The unmanifest is an auxiliary taste, and sometimes even what becomes manifest at the end is accepted as such.
The qualities beginning with heaviness, in a substance whose support of taste is earth and the other elements,
are attributed to the tastes by figurative usage based on association.
There, a substance dominated by the qualities of heaviness, grossness, stability, and smell
is earthy, bringing about heaviness, firmness, compactness, and increase.
One dominated by fluidity, coldness, heaviness, unctuousness, dullness, density, and taste
is watery, causing unction, flowing, moistening, refreshment, and binding.
One dominated by dryness, sharpness, heat, clarity, subtlety, and form
is fiery, and has the nature of burning, transformation, color, illumination, and wind.
One dominated by dryness, clarity, lightness, and touch
is airy, causing dryness, lightness, clarity, movement, and fatigue.
One dominated by subtlety, clarity, lightness, and sound
is spatial, producing porosity and lightness. Thus, in the world, no substance

children.text: na kiṃcid vidyate dravyaṃ vaśān nānārthayogayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: is known that is not a medicine, depending on its various applications and purposes.
Among them, a substance that moves upward is usually strong in fire and wind;
one that moves downward is mostly abundant in the qualities of earth and water.
Thus substance, and later the tastes with their divisions, will be taught.

children.text: vīryaṃ punar vadanty eke guru snigdhaṃ himaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: Some say that <s>vīrya</s> (potency) is again eightfold: heavy, unctuous, cold, soft,

children.text: laghu rūkṣoṣṇatīkṣṇaṃ ca tad evaṃ matam aṣṭadhā
children.translated_text: light, dry, hot, and sharp. Thus it is regarded as eightfold.

children.text: carakas tv āha vīryaṃ tat kriyate yena yā kriyā ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Caraka</s> says that <s>vīrya</s> is that by which whatever action is performed.

children.text: nāvīryaṃ kurute kiṃcit sarvā vīryakṛtā hi sā
children.translated_text: Nothing without <s>vīrya</s> does anything, for every action is produced by <s>vīrya</s>.
Therefore the name <s>vīrya</s> is said to be meaningful only among heaviness and the other qualities,
because they are the essences of all qualities and undergo excellence of power,
and because of their primacy for practical usage and because they include many foremost qualities.

children.text: ataś ca viparītatvāt sambhavaty api naiva sā
children.translated_text: And therefore, because of mutual opposition, even though it may exist,

children.text: vivakṣyate rasādyeṣu vīryaṃ gurvādayo hy ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>vīrya</s> is not spoken of among <s>rasa</s> and the others; hence heaviness and the other qualities are <s>vīrya</s>.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ śītaṃ dvidhaivānye vīryam ācakṣate 'pi ca
children.translated_text: Others also declare <s>vīrya</s> to be only twofold, hot and cold.
Although a substance is manifold in nature, it never at all transgresses
the two very powerful principles, fire and soma, just as the manifest and unmanifest world does not.
There, the hot produces dizziness, thirst, exhaustion, sweating, burning, and rapid digestion,

children.text: śamaṃ ca vātakaphayoḥ karoti śiśiraṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and it pacifies <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>; the cold, on the other hand, produces
refreshment, life, obstruction, and clarity in regard to blood and <s>pitta</s>.
The different <s>rasa</s> that arises through conjunction with the digestive fire in the stomach,

children.text: rasānāṃ pariṇāmānte sa vipāka iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the end of the transformation of the tastes, is remembered as <s>vipāka</s>.

children.text: svāduḥ paṭuś ca madhuram amlo 'mlaṃ pacyate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Sweet and pungent taste are digested into sweet; sour taste into sour.
The <s>vipāka</s> of bitter, hot, and astringent tastes is generally pungent.

children.text: rasair asau tulyaphalas tatra dravyaṃ śubhāśubham
children.translated_text: It has effects corresponding to the tastes; in this matter, a good or bad substance

children.text: kiṃcid rasena kurute karma pākena cāparam ||
children.translated_text: performs one action by its <s>rasa</s> and another by its digestion.
Some action is done by another quality, by <s>vīrya</s>, and some only by <s>prabhāva</s> (specific effect).

children.text: yad yad dravye rasādīnāṃ balavattvena vartate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever among <s>rasa</s> and the others exists in a substance with superior strength,
that, overpowering the others, takes on causal force.
When opposing qualities are joined, the smaller is overcome by the larger.

children.text: rasaṃ vipākas tau vīryaṃ prabhāvas tāny apohati
children.translated_text: <s>Vipāka</s> overcomes <s>rasa</s>, <s>vīrya</s> overcomes those two, and <s>prabhāva</s> overcomes them all,
when <s>rasa</s> and the others are equal in strength; this is their natural strength.

children.text: rasādisāmye yat karma viśiṣṭaṃ tat prabhāvajam
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> and the others are equal, whatever action is distinctive is born from <s>prabhāva</s>.
<s>Dantī</s>, though equal to <s>citraka</s> in <s>rasa</s> and the rest, is purgative;

children.text: madhukasya ca mṛdvīkā ghṛtaṃ kṣīrasya dīpanam
children.translated_text: and grape, though equal to licorice, and ghee, though equal to milk, kindles digestion.

children.text: iti sāmānyataḥ karma dravyādīnāṃ punaś ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Thus the action of substances and the rest has been stated in general, and that again
It differs according to the distinction of substances, which are produced from various causal conditions.

children.text: svādur guruś ca godhūmo vātajid vātakṛd yavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wheat is sweet and heavy and conquers <s>vāta</s>; barley produces <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: uṣṇā matsyāḥ payaḥ śītaṃ kaṭuḥ siṃho na śūkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fish are heating; milk is cooling. Lion meat is pungent, but boar meat is not.
Earth and water, fire and earth, water and fire, ether and air, fire and wind, and earth and wind
are, in order, the pairs of elements by whose predominance the tastes beginning with sweet arise.

children.text: teṣāṃ vidyād rasaṃ svāduṃ yo vaktram anulimpati
children.translated_text: Among them, one should know as sweet the taste which, when being tasted, coats the mouth
and gives delight to the body and clarity to the senses.
It is dear to ants and the like. Sour taste cleanses the mouth
and excites the hairs and teeth, while contracting the eyes and brows.
Salty taste makes the mouth water and causes burning in the cheeks and throat.

children.text: tikto viśadayaty āsyaṃ rasanaṃ pratihanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Bitter taste clears the mouth and checks the tongue's sense of taste.
Pungent taste agitates the tip of the tongue, producing a tingling sensation;
it makes the eyes, nose, and mouth discharge, and seems to burn the cheeks.
Astringent taste numbs the tongue and causes obstruction in the throat channels.

children.text: rasānām iti rūpāṇi karmāṇi madhuro rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus are the forms of the tastes. As for their actions: the sweet taste
because it is wholesome from birth, produces strong strength in the bodily tissues.
It is commended for children, the old, the wounded, the depleted, and for complexion, hair, senses, and vital vigor.
It is nourishing, good for the throat, promotes breast milk and union, and is heavy.
It promotes life span, sustains life, is unctuous, and removes <s>pitta</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and poison.
But by excessive use it produces diseases born of fat and <s>śleṣman</s>,
such as corpulence, weakness of digestion, stupor, urinary disorders, goiter, tumors, and the like.
Sour taste kindles the digestive fire, is unctuous, pleasing to the heart, digestive, and appetizing.
It has heating potency, is cool to the touch, satisfying, moistening, and light.
It increases <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood, and directs obstructed <s>vāta</s> downward.

children.text: so 'tyabhyastas tanoḥ kuryāc chaithilyaṃ timiraṃ bhramam ||
children.translated_text: When too much practiced, it may cause looseness of the body, dim vision, and dizziness,
as well as itching, pallor, erysipelas, swelling, eruptions, thirst, and fever.
Salty taste removes stiffness, accumulation, binding, and distension, and promotes digestive fire.
It is uncting, sudorific, sharp, appetizing, and causes cutting and splitting.
When overused, it produces blood and wind disorders, baldness, greying hair, and wrinkles;
it gives rise to thirst, skin disease, poison disorders, and erysipelas, and diminishes strength.
Bitter taste is itself unpleasant, but it conquers anorexia, worms, thirst, and poison,
and overcomes skin disease, fainting, fever, nausea, burning, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
It dries up moisture, fat, muscle-fat, marrow, feces, and urine.
It is light, intellect-promoting, cooling, dry, and purifies breast milk and the throat.
Through excessive use it causes depletion of the tissues and diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
Pungent taste conquers disorders of the throat, urticaria, skin disease, <s>alasaka</s>, and swelling.
It depresses wounds and dries up oiliness, fat, and moisture.
It kindles digestion, digests, is relishing, purifies, and dries food.
It cuts bonds, opens the channels, and removes <s>kapha</s>.
Through excessive use it causes thirst and loss of semen and strength,
fainting, contraction, tremor, and pain in the waist, back, and other parts.
Astringent taste removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, is heavy, and purifies blood.
It compresses, heals, is cooling, and dries up moisture and fat.
It checks <s>āma</s>, is absorbent, dry, and especially clears the skin.
When too much habituated, it causes constipation, distension, and heart pains,
as well as thirst, emaciation, loss of virility, obstruction of the channels, and retention of wastes.
Ghee, gold, jaggery, walnut, plantain, coca, and parūṣaka,
abhīru, vīrā, jackfruit, rājādana, and the three balās,
the two medās, the four parṇinīs, jīvantī, jīvaka, and ṛṣabha,
madhūka, madhuka, bimbī, vidārī, and the pair of śrāvaṇīs,
kṣīraśuklā, tugākṣīrī, the two kṣīriṇīs, kāśmarī, and the two sahās,
milk, sugarcane, gokṣura, honey, grapes, and the like form the sweet group.
The sour group consists of āmalakī fruit, tamarind, citron, and sour vetasa,

children.text: dāḍimaṃ rajataṃ takraṃ cukraṃ pālevataṃ dadhi
children.translated_text: pomegranate, rajata, buttermilk, cukra, pālevata, curds,
mango, āmrātaka, bhavya, wood-apple, and karamardaka.

children.text: varaṃ sauvarcalaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ viḍaṃ sāmudram audbhidam
children.translated_text: The salty group consists of vara, sauvarcala, black salt, viḍa salt, sea salt, audbhida salt,

children.text: romakaṃ pāṃsujaṃ sīsaṃ kṣāraś ca lavaṇo gaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: romaka, pāṃsuja, sīsa, and alkali.
The bitter group consists of paṭolī, trāyantī, vālaka, uśīra, sandalwood,
bhūnimba, nimba, kaṭukā, tagara, aguru, and vatsaka,
naktamāla, the two rajanīs, musta, mūrvā, and aṭarūṣaka,
pāṭhā, apāmārga, bronze, iron, guḍūcī, and dhanvayāsaka,
the great five roots, the two vyāghrīs, viśālā, ativiṣā, and vacā.
The pungent group consists of hiṅgu, pepper, kṛmijit, and pañcakola,
kuṭhera and the others, the haritakas, bile, urine, and aruṣkara.

children.text: vargaḥ kaṣāyaḥ pathyākṣaṃ śirīṣaḥ khadiro madhu ||
children.translated_text: The astringent class consists of pathyā, akṣa, śirīṣa, khadira, honey,
kadamba, udumbara, pearl, coral, collyrium, and red ochre,
bāla, wood-apple, dates, lotus fiber, lotus, blue lotus, and the like.

children.text: madhuraṃ śleṣmalaṃ prāyo jīrṇāc chāliyavād ṛte
children.translated_text: The sweet taste is generally phlegmatic, except in aged rice, barley,
green gram, wheat, honey, sugar, and meat from animals of dry land.
The sour taste generally produces <s>pitta</s>, except in pomegranate and āmalaka.
The salty taste is generally unwholesome for the eyes, except for rock salt.

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṭu ca bhūyiṣṭham avṛṣyaṃ vātakopanam
children.translated_text: Bitter and pungent tastes are mostly non-aphrodisiac and aggravate <s>vāta</s>,
except for amṛtā and paṭolī, and for dry ginger, black pepper, garlic, and so on.

children.text: kaṣāyaṃ prāyaśaḥ śītaṃ stambhanaṃ cābhayāṃ vinā
children.translated_text: Astringent taste is generally cooling and constipating, except for abhaya.
The tastes pungent, sour, and salty are heating in potency, each more so than the preceding one.

children.text: tiktaḥ kaṣāyo madhuras tadvad eva ca śītalāḥ
children.translated_text: Bitter, astringent, and sweet are likewise cooling.

children.text: tiktaḥ kaṭuḥ kaṣāyaś ca rūkṣā baddhamalās tathā ||
children.translated_text: Bitter, pungent, and astringent are dry, and they also bind the feces.
The saline, sour, and sweet tastes are unctuous and promote the free passage of feces, urine, and flatus.

children.text: paṭoḥ kaṣāyas tasmāc ca madhuraḥ paramaṃ guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: Astringent is heavier than saline, and sweet is heavier than that, being supremely heavy.

children.text: laghur amlaḥ kaṭus tasmāt tasmād api ca tiktakaḥ
children.translated_text: Sour is light; pungent is lighter than that, and bitter is still lighter than that.
The combinations are fifty-seven, while their full arrangement is of sixty-three kinds.
Because the tastes occur in combination, they are divided roughly as follows.

children.text: ekaikahīnās tān pañcadaśa yānti rasā dvike ||
children.translated_text: When one taste is absent from each pair, the tastes make fifteen twofold combinations.

children.text: trike svādur daśāmlaḥ ṣaṭ trīn paṭus tikta ekakam
children.translated_text: In threefold combinations, sweet enters ten, sour six, saline three, and bitter one.

children.text: catuṣkeṣu daśa svāduś caturo 'mlaḥ paṭuḥ sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Among fourfold combinations, sweet enters ten, sour four, and saline only once.

children.text: pañcakeṣv ekam evāmlo madhuraḥ pañca sevate
children.translated_text: Among fivefold combinations sour enters only one, while sweet participates in five.

children.text: dravyam ekaṃ ṣaḍāsvādam asaṃyuktāś ca ṣaḍ rasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: One substance may have all six tastes, and the uncombined tastes are six.

children.text: ṣaṭ pañcakā ṣaṭ ca pṛthag rasāḥ syuś caturdvikau pañcadaśaprakārau
children.translated_text: There are six fivefold combinations and six separate tastes; the fourfold and twofold groups each have fifteen varieties.

children.text: bhedās trikā viṃśatir ekam eva dravyaṃ ṣaḍāsvādam iti triṣaṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The threefold divisions are twenty, and one substance may have six tastes: thus the total is sixty-three.
These distinctions of taste, through primary taste and aftertaste and through gradations of degree,
come to exceed enumeration, and they should be applied according to the <s>doṣas</s> and medicines.

children.text: doṣadhātumalā mūlaṃ sadā dehasya taṃ calaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>doṣas</s>, tissues, and wastes are always the root of the body; the moving <s>vāta</s>,
when unvitiated, supports it by initiating vigor, exhalation, inhalation, movements, and urges,

children.text: samyaggatyā ca dhātūnām akṣāṇāṃ pāṭavena ca
children.translated_text: and by the proper movement of the tissues and the acuity of the sense faculties.
<s>Pitta</s> supports it through digestion, heat, and sight,
as well as hunger, thirst, relish, complexion, intelligence, understanding, courage, and softness of the body.
<s>Śleṣman</s> supports it through firmness, unctuousness, binding of the joints, patience, and the like.
Nourishing, sustaining life, coating, lubricating, supporting, and filling

children.text: garbhotpādaś ca dhātūnāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ karma kramāt smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and the production of the embryo are remembered as the chief actions of the tissues in order.
The function of feces is support; that of urine is the carrying away of moisture.
The function of sweat is the retention of moisture. But when increased, <s>anila</s> causes
emaciation, dark discoloration, desire for warmth, tremor, distention, and retention of feces,
as well as loss of strength, sleep, and sense function, delirious speech, dizziness, and wretchedness.
<s>Pitta</s> causes yellowness of feces, urine, eyes, and skin, hunger, thirst, burning, and little sleep.
<s>Śleṣman</s> causes weakening of the digestive fire, salivation, lassitude, heaviness,
whiteness, coldness, looseness of the limbs, dyspnea, cough, and excessive sleep.
The nutritive fluid too acts like <s>śleṣman</s>; blood causes erysipelas, splenic disease, and abscesses,
as well as skin disease, <s>vātarakta</s>, bleeding disorders, abdominal tumors, disease of the gums, and jaundice.
It also causes dark facial patches, loss of digestive fire, confusion, and redness of the skin, eyes, and urine.
Flesh causes swellings, tumors, nodules, and enlargement of the cheeks, thighs, and abdomen,

children.text: kaṇṭhādiṣv adhimāṃsaṃ ca tadvan medas tathā śramam ||
children.translated_text: as well as overgrowth of flesh in the throat and elsewhere; fat similarly causes fatigue,
breathlessness even with slight exertion, and hanging of the buttocks, breasts, and abdomen.

children.text: asthy adhyasthy adhidantāṃś ca majjā netrāṅgagauravam ||
children.translated_text: Bone causes extra bones and extra teeth, while marrow causes heaviness of the eyes and limbs.

children.text: parvasu sthūlamūlāni kuryāt kṛcchrāṇy arūṃṣi ca
children.translated_text: It may also produce difficult sores with large roots in the joints.
Increased semen causes excessive desire for women and also seminal stone.

children.text: kukṣāv ādhmānam āṭopaṃ gauravaṃ vedanāṃ śakṛt
children.translated_text: Feces causes abdominal distention, gurgling, heaviness, and pain.
Urine causes stabbing pain in the bladder and, even after voiding, the feeling that voiding has not been done.
Sweat is recognized by excessive sweating, bad odor, and itching.
Likewise one should recognize minor wastes such as ocular discharge by abundance, heaviness, and similar signs.
When <s>anila</s> is depleted, the sign is sinking of the body and scant speech and activity.
There is also confusion of consciousness and the arising of diseases described for increase of <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: pitte mando 'nalaḥ śītaṃ prabhāhāniḥ kaphe bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>pitta</s> is depleted, the digestive fire is weak, there is coldness and loss of complexion; when <s>kapha</s> is depleted there is dizziness,
emptiness in the seats of <s>śleṣman</s>, palpitation of the heart, and looseness of the joints.

children.text: rase raukṣyaṃ śramaḥ śoṣo glāniḥ śabdāsahiṣṇutā
children.translated_text: When nutritive fluid is depleted there are dryness, fatigue, wasting, languor, and intolerance of sound.
When blood is depleted there is fondness for sour and cooling things, looseness of the veins, and roughness.
When flesh is depleted there are weakness of the sense faculties, dryness of the cheeks and buttocks, and pain in the joints.

children.text: medasi svapanaṃ kaṭyāḥ plīhno vṛddhiḥ kṛśāṅgatā ||
children.translated_text: When fat is depleted there is numbness of the waist, enlargement of the spleen, and emaciation of the limbs.
When bone is depleted there is piercing pain in the bones and looseness in the teeth, hair, nails, and the like.
There is porosity of the bones; when marrow is depleted there are dizziness and seeing darkness.

children.text: śukre cirāt prasicyeta śukraṃ śoṇitam eva vā
children.translated_text: When semen is depleted, semen is discharged only after a long time, or else blood is discharged.
There is extreme piercing pain in the testicles, and the penis seems as if smoking.

children.text: purīṣe vāyur antrāṇi saśabdo veṣṭayann iva
children.translated_text: When feces is depleted, wind, with noise, seems to twist the intestines.

children.text: kukṣau bhramati yāty ūrdhvaṃ hṛtpārśve pīḍayan bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: It wanders in the abdomen, moves upward, and severely presses the heart and flanks.

children.text: mūtre 'lpaṃ mūtrayet kṛcchrād vivarṇaṃ sāsram eva vā
children.translated_text: When urine is depleted, one urinates little, with difficulty, and the urine is discolored or mixed with blood.
When sweat is depleted, there is falling of body hair, stiffness of the hair follicles, and cracking of the skin.
The depletion of the very subtle wastes is hard to perceive, but one should recognize it
by dryness, piercing pain, emptiness, and lightness in their own channels of waste.

children.text: doṣādīnāṃ yathāsvaṃ ca vidyād vṛddhikṣayau bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The physician should know the increase and depletion of the <s>doṣas</s> and the rest in accordance with each one's own signs,
and by the decrease of their opposite qualities and the increase of their own qualities.

children.text: vṛddhiṃ malānāṃ saṅgāc ca kṣayaṃ cātivisargataḥ
children.translated_text: He should know increase of the wastes from obstruction, and depletion from excessive discharge.

children.text: malocitatvād dehasya kṣayo vṛddhes tu pīḍanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the body is accustomed to wastes, their depletion is more distressing than their increase.

children.text: tatrāsthni sthito vāyuḥ pittaṃ tu svedaraktayoḥ
children.translated_text: There, <s>vāyu</s> is situated in bone, while <s>pitta</s> is situated in sweat and blood.
<s>Śleṣman</s> is situated in the remaining tissues; therefore, among these mutually related supports and supported elements,
the medicine that increases or diminishes one also increases or diminishes the other.

children.text: asthimārutayor naivaṃ prāyo vṛddhir hi tarpaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: But this is not so for bone and <s>māruta</s>, for increase of bone generally comes from nourishing treatment,
accompanied by <s>śleṣman</s>; therefore its depletion comes from the opposite, accompanied by <s>vāyu</s>.
Therefore, when disorders arise from increase and depletion,
one should quickly treat them in order with lightening and nourishing treatments,

children.text: vāyor anyatra tajjāṃs tu tair evotkramayojitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: except in the case of <s>vāyu</s>; disorders born from it should be treated with those same measures applied in the reverse way.
In particular, disorders arising from increased blood should be treated by bloodletting and purgation.
Diseases arising from increase of <s>māṃsa</s> (flesh tissue) are treated by surgical operation, caustic alkali, and cautery procedures.
Diseases born of <s>medas</s> (fat tissue) are treated by the therapy for obesity and emaciation; those born from wasting of bone
by milk and ghee combined with bitter substances, and also by enemas.
Those born of increase of feces are treated by the therapy for diarrhea, and those arising from depletion of feces
by such things as ram and goat meat, kulmāṣa, barley, and the two kinds of māṣa beans.
Those arising from increase and depletion of urine are treated by the therapies for <s>meha</s> (urinary disorder) and difficult urination.
Those arising from depletion of sweat are treated by exercise, oil massage, sudation, and wine.
The portions of the bodily <s>agni</s> (digestive fire), remaining in their own proper place, are lodged in the tissues.
Through their dullness or excessive intensity arise the increase and depletion of the tissues.

children.text: pūrvo dhātuḥ paraṃ kuryād vṛddhaḥ kṣīṇaś ca tadvidham
children.translated_text: An earlier tissue, when increased or depleted, makes the following tissue become of that same kind.

children.text: doṣā duṣṭā rasair dhātūn dūṣayanty ubhaye malān ||
children.translated_text: Corrupted <s>doṣas</s>, through the nutritive fluid, vitiate the tissues; both vitiate the wastes.

children.text: adho dve sapta śirasi khāni svedavahāni ca
children.translated_text: The two lower openings, the seven in the head, and the channels carrying sweat

children.text: malā malāyanāni syur yathāsvaṃ teṣv ato gadāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the wastes and the pathways of the wastes; therefore diseases arise in them according to each case.

children.text: ojas tu tejo dhātūnāṃ śukrāntānāṃ paraṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Ojas</s> is remembered as the supreme essence, the brilliance of the tissues ending with semen.
Though situated in the heart, it pervades the body and is the bond that maintains the body.
It is unctuous, lunar in nature, pure, and slightly reddish-yellow.

children.text: yannāśe niyataṃ nāśo yasmiṃs tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: When it is destroyed, destruction is certain; while it remains, one remains alive.
From it arise the various states that depend upon the body.
<s>Ojas</s> is depleted by anger, hunger, meditation, grief, exertion, and the like.
In its depletion one is afraid, weak, repeatedly broods, and has distressed senses;

children.text: duśchāyo durmanā rūkṣo bhavet kṣāmaś ca tatkṣaye ||
children.translated_text: one becomes of bad complexion, low-spirited, dry, and emaciated.
There the remedies are life-promoting medicines, milk, meat broth, and similar substances.
When <s>ojas</s> is increased, satisfaction, nourishment, and strength arise in the body.

children.text: yad annaṃ dveṣṭi yad api prārthayetāvirodhi tu
children.translated_text: Whatever food one dislikes, and whatever one longs for, provided it is not incompatible,

children.text: tat tat tyajan samaśnaṃś ca tau tau vṛddhikṣayau jayet ||
children.translated_text: by respectively avoiding that and eating it in proper measure, one may overcome those increases and depletions.
For the <s>doṣas</s> produce appetite toward what is opposite or similar to their condition.

children.text: vṛddhāḥ kṣīṇāś ca bhūyiṣṭhaṃ lakṣayanty abudhās tu na ||
children.translated_text: The increased and the depleted ones mostly reveal themselves, but the unwise do not notice them.

children.text: yathābalaṃ yathāsvaṃ ca doṣā vṛddhā vitanvate
children.translated_text: According to their strength and according to their own nature, increased <s>doṣas</s> extend

children.text: rūpāṇi jahati kṣīṇāḥ samāḥ svaṃ karma kurvate ||
children.translated_text: their symptoms; when depleted they abandon them, and when balanced they perform their own functions.

children.text: ya eva dehasya samā vivṛddhyai ta eva doṣā viṣamā vadhāya
