children.translated_text: The very <s>doṣas</s> that, when balanced, promote the body's growth, when unbalanced, cause its destruction.

children.text: yasmād atas te hitacaryayaiva kṣayād vivṛddher iva rakṣaṇīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they must be guarded by wholesome conduct from depletion just as from increase.
The large intestine, waist, thighs, ears, bones, and tactile sense organ
are the seats of <s>vāta</s>; among them the receptacle of digested matter is especially so.

children.text: nābhir āmāśayaḥ svedo lasīkā rudhiraṃ rasaḥ
children.translated_text: The navel, stomach, sweat, lymph, blood, nutritive fluid,

children.text: dṛk sparśanaṃ ca pittasya nābhir atra viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: sight, and touch are seats of <s>pitta</s>; here the navel is especially so.
The chest, throat, head, <s>kloman</s>, joints, stomach, nutritive fluid,

children.text: medo ghrāṇaṃ ca jihvā ca kaphasya sutarām uraḥ ||
children.translated_text: fat, smell, and tongue are seats of <s>kapha</s>; above all, the chest is so.
Because of the divisions beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>vāyu</s> is fivefold; here <s>prāṇa</s> is located in the head,
moves in the chest and throat, and supports the intellect, heart, senses, and mind.
It brings about spitting, sneezing, belching, exhalation, and the entrance of food.
The seat of <s>udāna</s> is the chest; it moves in the nose, navel, and throat.
It performs speech, effort, energy, strength, complexion, memory, and action.
<s>Vyāna</s>, situated in the heart, courses through the whole body with great speed.
Going, downward movement, upward movement, closing and opening of the eyes, and the like,

children.text: prāyaḥ sarvāḥ kriyās tasmin pratibaddhāḥ śarīriṇām ||
children.translated_text: indeed almost all actions of embodied beings are dependent upon it.
<s>Samāna</s>, situated near the digestive fire, moves everywhere in the alimentary tract.
It receives food, digests it, separates it, and releases it.
<s>Apāna</s>, moving downward, has the pelvis, bladder, penis, and thighs as its sphere.
Its action is the expulsion of semen, menstrual blood, feces, urine, and the fetus.
<s>Pitta</s> is fivefold; among these, that which lies between the receptacle of digested and undigested food,
although composed of the five elements, because of the rise of its fiery quality,
has given up its material liquidity and, through actions such as cooking, is called <s>anala</s> (fire).

children.text: pacaty annaṃ vibhajate sārakiṭṭau pṛthak tathā ||
children.translated_text: It digests food and likewise separates the essence and waste portions distinctly.

children.text: tatrastham eva pittānāṃ śeṣāṇām apy anugraham
children.translated_text: Remaining right there, it also assists the remaining kinds of <s>pitta</s>

children.text: karoti baladānena pācakaṃ nāma tat smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: by giving them strength; that is remembered under the name <s>pācaka</s>.
The <s>pitta</s> based in the stomach is <s>rañjaka</s>, because it colors the nutritive fluid.
Because it accomplishes desired aims through intellect, wisdom, self-regard, and the like,
the <s>pitta</s> located in the heart is called <s>sādhaka</s>; that in the eye is <s>ālocaka</s>, because it observes forms.

children.text: dṛkstham ālocakaṃ tvaksthaṃ bhrājakaṃ bhrājanāt tvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That situated in the skin is <s>bhrājaka</s>, because it gives radiance to the skin.

children.text: śleṣmā tu pañcadhoraḥsthaḥ sa trikasya svavīryataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣman</s> is fivefold. The one situated in the chest, by its own power, supports the upper back region
and the heart, and, from the potency of food, being situated right there, by its watery action

children.text: kaphadhāmnāṃ ca śeṣāṇāṃ yat karoty avalambanam
children.translated_text: supports the remaining seats of <s>kapha</s> as well.
Therefore it is <s>avalambaka śleṣman</s>. The one situated in the stomach
is <s>kledaka</s>, because it moistens the mass of food; because it perceives taste,
<s>bodhaka</s> abides on the tongue. The one situated in the head is <s>tarpaka</s>, because it nourishes the eyes.
Because of the cohesion of the joints, <s>śleṣaka</s> is situated in the joints.
Thus, in general, one should know the seats of the <s>doṣas</s> when their nature is uncorrupted,

children.text: vyāpinām api jānīyāt karmāṇi ca pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: and also their actions separately, even though they are pervasive.

children.text: uṣṇena yuktā rūkṣādyā vāyoḥ kurvanti saṃcayam ||
children.translated_text: Dryness and the other qualities, joined with heat, cause accumulation of <s>vāyu</s>.

children.text: śītena kopam uṣṇena śamaṃ snigdhādayo guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Joined with cold, they cause aggravation; unctuousness and the other qualities, joined with heat, cause pacification.

children.text: śītena yuktās tīkṣṇādyāś cayaṃ pittasya kurvate ||
children.translated_text: Sharpness and the other qualities, joined with cold, cause accumulation of <s>pitta</s>.
Joined with heat, they cause aggravation; dullness and the other qualities, joined with cold, bring pacification.

children.text: śītena yuktāḥ snigdhādyāḥ kurvate śleṣmaṇaś cayam ||
children.translated_text: Unctuousness and the other qualities, joined with cold, cause accumulation of <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: uṣṇena kopaṃ tenaiva guṇā rūkṣādayaḥ śamam
children.translated_text: Joined with heat, they cause aggravation; by that same heat, dryness and the other qualities bring pacification.

children.text: cayo vṛddhiḥ svadhāmny eva pradveṣo vṛddhihetuṣu ||
children.translated_text: Accumulation is increase only in its own abode, and aversion to the causes of increase;
and it is desire for things of opposite quality. Aggravation, however, is movement on the wrong path,
the manifestation of its own signs, ill health, and the arising of disease.
The evenness of what remains in its own place, the non-arising of disorder, is pacification.
The accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of <s>vāyu</s> occur in the three seasons beginning with summer;
but those of <s>pitta</s> occur in the seasons beginning with the rains, and those of <s>śleṣman</s> in the seasons beginning with late winter.
<s>Samīraṇa</s> (vāta) is accumulated by light and dry herbs and foods;

children.text: tadvidhas tadvidhe dehe kālasyauṣṇyān na kupyati
children.translated_text: being of that kind, in a body of that kind, it is not aggravated because of the heat of the season.
By waters with sour post-digestive effect and by foods of that sort,

children.text: pittaṃ yāti cayaṃ kopaṃ na tu kālasya śaityataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>pitta</s> undergoes accumulation, but not aggravation, because of the coldness of the season.
<s>Kapha</s> is accumulated by unctuous and cold waters and foods;

children.text: tulye 'pi kāle dehe ca skannatvān na prakupyati
children.translated_text: even though the season and body are similar, because of its congealed state it is not aggravated.
Thus this is the nature of the seasons; but under the control of diet and the like,

children.text: cayādīn yānti sadyo 'pi doṣāḥ kāle 'pi vā na tu
children.translated_text: the <s>doṣas</s> may undergo accumulation and the other states immediately, or may not do so even in their proper season.
An aggravated waste-matter suddenly pervades the body from the soles of the feet to the head;
but it recedes little by little, like a flood of water.
The aggravated wastes torment the body with various and countless
disorders of many forms; therefore their causes, shapes, and treatments

children.text: śakyaṃ naikaikaśo vaktum ataḥ sāmānyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: cannot be stated one by one, and so the general account is given.

children.text: doṣā eva hi sarveṣāṃ rogāṇām ekakāraṇam
children.translated_text: For the <s>doṣas</s> alone are the single cause of all diseases.

children.text: yathā pakṣī paripatan sarvataḥ sarvam apy ahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as a bird, flying about everywhere for the whole day,

children.text: chāyām atyeti nātmīyāṃ yathā vā kṛtsnam apy adaḥ
children.translated_text: does not pass beyond its own shadow, or just as this whole
mass of varied transformations does not transcend the three qualities,
so too the whole mass of disorders, though caused by inequality of its own tissues,

children.text: vikārajātaṃ trīn doṣān teṣāṃ kope tu kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: never transcends the three <s>doṣas</s>. The cause of their aggravation

children.text: arthair asātmyaiḥ saṃyogaḥ kālaḥ karma ca duṣkṛtam
children.translated_text: is contact with unsuitable sense-objects, time, and bad action.
That again is divided threefold by deficient, excessive, and wrong application.
Deficient application is slight contact of a sense organ with its own object, or no contact at all.
Excessive application is excessive contact. A form that is minute, dazzling, terrifying,
too near, too distant, unpleasant, distorted, and so on,

children.text: yad akṣṇā vīkṣyate rūpaṃ mithyāyogaḥ sa dāruṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when seen by the eye, is its dreadful wrong application.
In the same way one should understand sense-objects such as excessively loud, foul-smelling, and the like, each as appropriate.

children.text: vidyāt kālas tu śītoṣṇavarṣābhedāt tridhā mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Time is considered threefold through the distinctions of cold, heat, and rain.
Its deficiency is deficient cold and so on; its excessive application has excessive characteristics.
Wrong application is specified as having characteristics opposite to its own nature.
Action too should be divided threefold according to body, speech, and mind.
Deficient activity of bodily and other action is called deficient application.
Excessive application is excessive activity; suppression and forcible discharge of urges,
beginning actions with uneven limbs, falling, stumbling, and the like,
speaking while a meal is only half eaten, and passion, hatred, fear, and so on,

children.text: karma prāṇātipātādi daśadhā yac ca ninditam ||
children.translated_text: and the tenfold censured action beginning with taking life:

children.text: mithyāyogaḥ samasto 'sāv iha vāmutra vā kṛtam
children.translated_text: all this is wrong application, whether done here or in a former life.

children.text: nidānam etad doṣāṇāṃ kupitās tena naikadhā ||
children.translated_text: This is the cause of the <s>doṣas</s>; aggravated by it, they in manifold ways
produce various diseases in the branches, the alimentary tract, the bones, and the joints.

children.text: śākhā raktādayas tvak ca bāhyarogāyanaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: The branches are blood and the other tissues, together with the skin; that is the pathway of external diseases.
Based there are moles, dark facial patches, boils, abscesses, tumors, and the like,
and diseases of the outer part, such as <s>durnāman</s>, <s>gulma</s>, swelling, and so on.
The inner alimentary tract is the great channel, based in the stomach and colon,
and located there are vomiting, diarrhea, cough, dyspnea, abdominal disease, and fever.
Also in the inner region are swelling, piles, <s>gulma</s>, erysipelas, and abscess.
The vital spots such as the head, heart, and bladder, and the joints of the bones,
as well as the vessels, ligaments, tendons, and the like bound to them, form the middle
pathway of disease. Situated there are consumption, hemiplegia, facial paralysis,
diseases of the head and the like, and pains and seizures of the joints, bones, sacrum, and so on.
Dislocation, displacement, piercing pain, numbness, depression, pain, pricking, splitting,
obstruction, breaking of the limbs, contraction, twisting, horripilation, and filling,
trembling, roughness, porousness, drying, throbbing, and winding pain,
stiffness, an astringent taste, and a dark or reddish color:
these are the actions of <s>vāyu</s>. Those of <s>pitta</s> are burning, redness, heat, suppuration,

children.text: svedaḥ kledaḥ srutiḥ kothaḥ sadanaṃ mūrchanaṃ madaḥ
children.translated_text: sweating, moisture, discharge, putrefaction, weakness, fainting, and intoxication.
Its tastes are pungent and sour; its color excludes pale and red.
Those of <s>śleṣman</s> are unctuousness, hardness, itching, coldness, heaviness,
binding, coating, torpor, swelling, indigestion, and excessive sleep.
Its color is white; its tastes are sweet and salty; it acts slowly.
Thus the signs of the <s>doṣas</s>, which pervade all diseases without remainder, have been stated.
A careful physician should correctly recognize them by inspection and the other means.
Knowing the divisions of disease-stages, and observing the afflicted at every moment,
through practice one attains a vision that reveals success in treatment.
Knowledge of good and bad gems and the like does not arise from scripture alone.
Some disease is born from misconduct seen in this life, some from previous transgression,

children.text: tatsaṃkarād bhavaty anyo vyādhir evaṃ tridhā smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and another from a mixture of the two; thus disease is remembered as threefold.
That which arises from the <s>doṣas</s> follows its cause; that born of karma occurs without such causes.
An illness that has a great onset from a small cause is born of both <s>doṣa</s> and karma.
The first goes away by cultivation of the opposite; the karmic one by the exhaustion of karma.
But that born of both comes to destruction through exhaustion of both <s>doṣa</s> and karma.
Diseases are twofold according to being dependent on themselves or on another; the latter are again twofold.
Those that arise beforehand are called prodromal signs; those that arise afterward are complications.
They are relieved according to their own origin, are independent, and have clearly manifest symptoms.

children.text: viparītās tato 'nye tu vidyād evaṃ malān api ||
children.translated_text: But others, opposite to these, should be understood in this way, and the wastes likewise.
One should carefully observe them as they become altered in each fever.
When the principal condition is pacified, they too are pacified; if they do not subside, then likewise

children.text: paścāc cikitset tūrṇaṃ vā balavantam upadravam
children.translated_text: one should treat the complication afterward, or quickly if it is strong.
For in a body already afflicted by disease, it is still more tormenting.
A physician unskilled in the names of disorders should never be ashamed.

children.text: na hi sarvavikārāṇāṃ nāmato 'sti dhruvā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For there is no fixed certainty for all disorders by name.
The very same aggravated <s>doṣa</s>, because of a particular mode of arising,

children.text: sthānāntarāṇi ca prāpya vikārān kurute bahūn ||
children.translated_text: and after reaching different seats, produces many disorders.
Therefore, after understanding the natures of disorders, their different seats,

children.text: buddhvā hetuviśeṣāṃś ca śīghraṃ kuryād upakramam ||
children.translated_text: and the specific causes, one should undertake treatment quickly.

children.text: dūṣyaṃ deśaṃ balaṃ kālam analaṃ prakṛtiṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: The affected tissue, region, strength, season, digestive fire, constitution, age,

children.text: sattvaṃ sātmyaṃ tathāhāram avasthāś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: mental firmness, habituation, diet, and the many distinct stages
must be examined in their subtlest details when determining the <s>doṣa</s> and the medicine.

children.text: yo vartate cikitsāyāṃ na sa skhalati jātucit ||
children.translated_text: One who proceeds in treatment in this way never stumbles at any time.
The condition of a grave or slight disease may appear otherwise because of the strength or weakness of mind and body.
One should be attentive in that matter.

children.text: guruṃ laghum iti vyādhiṃ kalpayaṃs tu bhiṣagbruvaḥ
children.translated_text: But a so-called physician who imagines a disease to be grave or slight
and, through an inadequate reckoning of the <s>doṣa</s>, makes a wrong judgment about regimen,
then applies too little medicine, or medicine of too little potency, in a grave disease.
Improperly used purification would aggravate the diseases still more.
But purification used to excess, and the opposite error in the opposite case,

children.text: kṣiṇuyān na malān eva kevalaṃ vapur asyati ||
children.translated_text: would diminish not only the wastes, but would also throw down the body.
Therefore the trained physician, constantly considering everything in every way,

children.text: tathā yuñjīta bhaiṣajyam ārogyāya yathā dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: should apply medicine so that health is assured.
From here onward the <s>doṣas</s> will be described according to the distinctions of increase and depletion.

children.text: pṛthak trīn viddhi saṃsargas tridhā tatra tu tān nava ||
children.translated_text: Know the three separately; their combinations are threefold, and there they are nine.

children.text: trīn eva samayā vṛddhyā ṣaḍ ekasyātiśāyane
children.translated_text: With equal increase there are just three; when one is predominant, there are six.
Among them all there are thirteen, and six when two and one differ in predominance.
There is one case with equal predominance, and six more through the conception of gradation.

children.text: pañcaviṃśatim ity evaṃ vṛddhaiḥ kṣīṇaiś ca tāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus there are twenty-five among the increased, and just as many among the depleted.

children.text: ekaikavṛddhisamatākṣayaiḥ ṣaṭ te punaś ca ṣaṭ
children.translated_text: With the increase, equality, and depletion of each single one there are six, and again six more.
With the depletion of one and the increase of a pair, together also with the reverse,
sixty-two varieties are taught; the sixty-third is the condition that causes health.

children.text: saṃsargād rasarudhirādibhis tathaiṣāṃ doṣāṃs tu kṣayasamatāvivṛddhibhedaiḥ
children.translated_text: Through combination with nutritive fluid, blood, and the rest, and through distinctions of depletion, equality, and increase among these <s>doṣas</s>,

children.text: ānantyaṃ taratamayogataś ca yātān jānīyād avahitamānaso yathāsvam ||
children.translated_text: one should know, with attentive mind, that they reach infinity through gradations, each according to its own case.
The treatment for <s>vāta</s> is oleation, sweating, and gentle purification,
foods that are sweet, sour, salty, and warm, oiling, and massage.
Wrapping, startling, sprinkling, and liquor made from grain paste or jaggery are used.
Unctuous and warm enemas, regulated use of enema therapy, and a habit of comfort are prescribed.
Appetite-kindling and digestive substances, along with unctuous fats of many origins, are used.
In particular, there is nourishing unctuous enema with marrow, meat juice, and oil.
For <s>pitta</s>, there is drinking ghee and purgation with sweet and cooling substances,
as well as foods and medicines that are sweet, bitter, and astringent.
One should make use of fragrances that are pleasant, cooling, and agreeable to the heart.

children.text: kaṇṭhe guṇānāṃ hārāṇāṃ maṇīnām urasā dhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Strings, necklaces, and gems should be worn on the neck and chest.
Applications of camphor, sandalwood, and uśīra should be made again and again.

children.text: pradoṣaś candramāḥ saudhaṃ hāri gītaṃ himo 'nilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Evening, the moon, a palace, charming song, and a cool breeze are beneficial.
Unconstrained ease, a friend, and a son with uncertain, innocent speech are beneficial.
Beloved wives who follow one's wishes and are adorned with good conduct are beneficial.
So too are houses containing streams of cool water, gardens, and long ponds,
and sandy banks of reservoirs with good bathing places and broad, clear water.
One should stay at the edge of lotus-filled water, in places crowded with trees.

children.text: saumyā bhāvāḥ payaḥ sarpir virekaś ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gentle conditions, milk, ghee, and especially purgation are beneficial.
For <s>śleṣman</s>, properly administered sharp emesis and purgation are prescribed.
The food should be dry, scanty, sharp, hot, pungent, bitter, and astringent.
Long-aged wine, sexual pleasure, affection, and staying awake are prescribed.
Exercise of many kinds, worry, and dry rubbing are prescribed.

children.text: viśeṣād vamanaṃ yūṣaḥ kṣaudraṃ medoghnam auṣadham
children.translated_text: Especially useful are emesis, soup, honey, and medicine that reduces fat.
Smoke inhalation, fasting, gargling, and the absence of comforts conduce to well-being.

children.text: upakramaḥ pṛthag doṣān yo 'yam uddiśya kīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: This treatment has been taught separately with reference to the individual <s>doṣas</s>.
In combined and triple-doṣa conditions one should adapt it as appropriate in each case.
For <s>vāta-pitta</s> the summer regimen is generally used; for <s>kapha-vāta</s>, the spring regimen.
Because <s>vāta</s> carries what it is joined with, the autumn regimen is used for <s>kapha-pitta</s>.

children.text: caya eva jayed doṣaṃ kupitaṃ tv avirodhayan
children.translated_text: One should conquer a <s>doṣa</s> already at the stage of accumulation; when it is aggravated, one should not oppose it wrongly.
When all are aggravated, one should treat the strongest without opposing the remaining <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: prayogaḥ śamayed vyādhim ekaṃ yo 'nyam udīrayet
children.translated_text: A therapeutic application that pacifies one disease but provokes another

children.text: nāsau viśuddhaḥ śuddhas tu śamayed yo na kopayet ||
children.translated_text: is not pure; pure treatment is that which pacifies without provoking.
Because of exercise, heat, sharpness, and also unwholesome conduct,
and because of the swift nature of <s>vāta</s>, the <s>doṣas</s> go from the alimentary tract to the branches, bones, and vital points.
Likewise, from them they return to the alimentary tract through the clearing of the mouths of the channels,

children.text: vṛddhyābhiṣyandanāt pākāt koṣṭhaṃ vāyoś ca nigrahāt ||
children.translated_text: through increase, liquefaction, digestion, and the restraint of <s>vāyu</s>.
When situated there, they may linger, again awaiting causes.

children.text: te kālādibalaṃ labdhvā kupyanty anyāśrayeṣv api ||
children.translated_text: Having gained strength from time and the other factors, they become aggravated even in other seats.
When they are established in another's place, but the ones belonging to that place are weak,
one should perform their own treatment; when they overpower others by strength, the treatment is likewise their own.

children.text: āgantuṃ śamayed doṣaṃ sthāninaṃ pratikṛtya vā
children.translated_text: One should pacify the invading <s>doṣa</s>, or else counteract the resident one.

children.text: prāyas tiryaggatā doṣāḥ kleśayanty āturāṃś ciram ||
children.translated_text: For the most part, <s>doṣas</s> that have moved transversely trouble patients for a long time.

children.text: kuryān na teṣu tvarayā dehāgnibalavit kriyām
children.translated_text: In their case one should not act hastily, but should undertake treatment knowing the body's strength and digestive fire.

children.text: śamayet tān prayogeṇa sukhaṃ vā koṣṭham ānayet ||
children.translated_text: One should pacify them by suitable application, or comfortably bring them into the <s>koṣṭha</s> (alimentary tract).
And when one knows that they have entered the <s>koṣṭha</s>, one should remove them by the nearest route.
Obstruction of the channels, collapse of strength, heaviness, and bewilderment of <s>anila</s> (vāta),
laziness, indigestion, spitting, obstruction of stool, lack of appetite, and fatigue
are the signs of wastes that are <s>sāma</s> (mixed with āma); the signs of those that are <s>nirāma</s> are the reverse.
Because the heat has little strength, the first tissue remains uncooked;
the corrupted <s>rasa</s> located in the stomach is called <s>āma</s>.
Others say that <s>āma</s> arises from the <s>doṣas</s> themselves, when they are excessively corrupted and mutually mingled,
just as poison arises from kodrava grains.

children.text: āmena tena saṃpṛktā doṣā dūṣyāś ca dūṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>doṣas</s> and the vitiated bodily elements, when mixed with that <s>āma</s>,

children.text: sāmā ity upadiśyante ye ca rogās tadudbhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are taught to be <s>sāma</s>, as are the diseases that arise from them.
One should not remove <s>sāma doṣas</s> that have spread through the whole body,

children.text: līnān dhātuṣv anutkliṣṭān phalād āmād rasān iva ||
children.translated_text: that are embedded in the tissues and not yet stirred up, just as one does not extract juice from an unripe fruit.

children.text: āśrayasya hi nāśāya te syur durnirharatvataḥ
children.translated_text: For, because they are difficult to remove, they would bring about the destruction of their support.

children.text: pācanair dīpanaiḥ snehais tān svedaiś ca pariṣkṛtān ||
children.translated_text: After they have been prepared by digestives, appetite-kindlers, unctuous substances,
and sudations, one should purify them at the proper time with purificatory measures, by the nearest route and according to strength.

children.text: hanty āśu yuktaṃ vaktreṇa dravyam āmāśayān malān ||
children.translated_text: A substance properly administered through the mouth quickly destroys wastes arising from the stomach,
through the nose those arising above the clavicles, and through the anus those arising from the receptacle of digested matter.

children.text: utkliṣṭān adha ūrdhvaṃ vā na cāmān vahataḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: One should not restrain with medicines <s>doṣas</s> that are stirred up and moving downward or upward by themselves,

children.text: dhārayed auṣadhair doṣān vidhṛtās te hi rogadāḥ
children.translated_text: nor those that are carrying <s>āma</s>, for when restrained they produce disease.

children.text: pravṛttān prāg ato doṣān upekṣeta hitāśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who eats wholesome food should allow <s>doṣas</s> that have already begun to move.

children.text: vibaddhān pācanais tais taiḥ pācayen nirhareta vā
children.translated_text: Those that are obstructed should be digested by the appropriate digestive measures, or else removed.

children.text: śrāvaṇe kārttike caitre māsi sādhāraṇe kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In the months of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, <s>Kārttika</s>, and <s>Caitra</s>, the ordinary transitional months, in sequence,
one should quickly remove <s>vāyu</s> and the others that have accumulated in summer, the rainy season, and winter.
For summer, the rainy season, and the cold season are respectively excessively hot, rainy, and cold.

children.text: saṃdhau sādhāraṇe teṣāṃ duṣṭān doṣān viśodhayet
children.translated_text: At their ordinary junction one should purify the corrupted <s>doṣas</s>.
This is said with regard to the regimen of the healthy; in disease, however, one should act according to the disease.
After making the appropriate countermeasure against cold, heat, and rain,

children.text: prayojayet kriyāṃ prāptāṃ kriyākālaṃ na hāpayet ||
children.translated_text: one should apply the indicated treatment and should not let the proper time for treatment pass.
Medicine should be administered when there is no food, at the beginning of food, in the middle, at the end, between mouthfuls,

children.text: grāse grāse muhuḥ sānnaṃ sāmudgaṃ niśi cauṣadham ||
children.translated_text: with each mouthful, repeatedly, together with food, in the <s>sāmudga</s> manner, and at night.
When <s>kapha</s> is excessive in disease, and when both the disease and the patient are strong, it is given without food.
At the beginning of food it is desired when <s>apāna</s> is disordered; in the middle, when <s>samāna</s> is disordered.
For <s>vyāna</s>, it is given at the end of the morning meal and after the evening meal.
When the wind called <s>prāṇa</s> is corrupted, it is given between mouthfuls and at the end of mouthfuls.
Repeatedly it is prescribed in poisoning, vomiting, hiccup, thirst, dyspnea, and cough.

children.text: yojyaṃ sabhojyaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ bhojyaiś citrair arocake ||
children.translated_text: Medicine is to be used along with food in anorexia, with varied foods.
In tremor, convulsion, and hiccup, the <s>sāmudga</s> mode is used for light eaters.
In disorders above the clavicles, administration at sleep time is praised.
Because what is to be treated is twofold, treatment too is considered exactly twofold.
One is <s>saṃtarpaṇa</s> (repletion), and the second is <s>apatarpaṇa</s> (depletion).
<s>Bṛṃhaṇa</s> (nourishing) and <s>laṅghana</s> (lightening) are stated as their synonyms.

children.text: bṛṃhaṇaṃ yad bṛhattvāya laṅghanaṃ lāghavāya yat ||
children.translated_text: That which is for the increase of bulk is <s>bṛṃhaṇa</s>; that which is for lightness

children.text: dehasya bhavataḥ prāyo bhaumāpyam itarac ca te
children.translated_text: of the body is <s>laṅghana</s>. They are generally earthy and watery, and otherwise, respectively.

children.text: snehanaṃ rūkṣaṇaṃ karma svedanaṃ stambhanaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: The actions called oleation, drying, sudation, and restraining,

children.text: bhūtānāṃ tad api dvaidhyād dvitayaṃ nātivartate
children.translated_text: because the elements are also divided into two groups, do not go beyond those two.

children.text: śodhanaṃ śamanaṃ ceti dvidhā tatrāpi laṅghanam ||
children.translated_text: There too, <s>laṅghana</s> is twofold: <s>śodhana</s> (purification) and <s>śamana</s> (pacification).

children.text: yad īrayed bahir doṣān pañcadhā śodhanaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: That which drives the <s>doṣas</s> outward is <s>śodhana</s>, and it is fivefold:
evacuative enema, emesis, bodily purgation, evacuation of the head, and bloodletting.

children.text: na śodhayati yad doṣān samān nodīrayaty api
children.translated_text: That which does not purify the <s>doṣas</s>, nor stir up those that are balanced,

children.text: samīkaroti viṣamān śamanaṃ tac ca saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: but equalizes those that are uneven, is <s>śamana</s>; and that is sevenfold:
<s>pācana</s> (digesting), <s>dīpana</s> (kindling), hunger, thirst, exercise, sun, and wind.

children.text: bṛṃhaṇaṃ śamanaṃ tv eva vāyoḥ pittānilasya ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛṃhaṇa</s> itself is pacifying for <s>vāyu</s>, and for <s>pitta</s> accompanied by <s>anila</s>.
One should nourish those emaciated by disease, medicines, wine, women, and grief,
those depleted by carrying loads, travel, and chest wounds, and those who are dry, weak, and <s>vātala</s> (vāta-dominant),
pregnant women, women recently delivered, children, and the old; in summer one should nourish others also.
This should be done with meat, milk, sugar, ghee, and sweet, unctuous enemas,
and with sleep, comfortable beds, massage, bathing, contentment, and things that gladden.
Those with <s>meha</s> (urinary disease), <s>āma doṣa</s>, excessive unctuousness, fever, thigh-stiffness, and skin disease
and those with erysipelas, abscess, enlarged spleen, or diseases of the head, throat, and eyes,

children.text: sthūlāṃś ca laṅghayen nityaṃ śiśire tv aparān api ||
children.translated_text: as well as the obese, should always be lightened; in the cold season one should lighten others too.
Among them, those excessive in stoutness, strength, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> should be treated with purificatory measures,
as should those afflicted with <s>āma doṣa</s>, fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and heart disease,
or with constipation, heaviness, belching, nausea, and the like.
Those with moderate stoutness and the like, afflicted by these same diseases, should generally first be treated with digestives and appetite-kindlers.
Those afflicted by these same disorders but deficient in stoutness, strength, and the like

children.text: kṣuttṛṣṇānigrahair doṣais tv ārtān madhyabalair dṛḍhān ||
children.translated_text: and those of middling strength and firmness afflicted by <s>doṣas</s> should be lightened by hunger, thirst, restraint,
wind, sun, and exertion; how much more should men of little strength be so treated.

children.text: na bṛṃhayel laṅghanīyān bṛṃhyāṃs tu mṛdu laṅghayet ||
children.translated_text: One should not nourish those who require <s>laṅghana</s>; but those who require <s>bṛṃhaṇa</s> should be lightened gently.
Or, by proper reasoning, one should treat them according to place, time, strength, and the other factors.
When one has been nourished, there is strength and fullness, and diseases curable by that treatment diminish.
Clarity of the senses, evacuation of the wastes, lightness, relish for food,
the simultaneous arising of hunger and thirst, and purity of the heart, belching, and throat
are signs when one has been properly reduced by <s>laṅghana</s>; there is mildness of disease, energy, and disappearance of drowsiness.
But when these two are used without regard to measure and the other requirements,
they produce such conditions as excessive corpulence and excessive emaciation; these will be described together with their medicines.

children.text: rūpaṃ tair eva ca jñeyam atibṛṃhitalaṅghite ||
children.translated_text: And the condition of excessive nourishing and excessive reducing should be recognized by those very signs.
Excessive corpulence gives rise to excessive fatness, scrofulous swellings, urinary disease, fever, abdominal disease, fistula,
cough, stupor, difficult disorders, disorders from <s>āma</s>, skin disease, and other very severe illnesses.
In that case everything that destroys fat, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s> is regarded as suitable.
Horse gram, roasted grain flour, śyāmāka millet, barley, mung beans, honey-water,
whey, daṇḍāhata, fermented <s>ariṣṭa</s>, anxiety, evacuative purification, and keeping awake are suitable.

children.text: madhunā triphalāṃ lihyād guḍūcīm abhayāṃ ghanam ||
children.translated_text: One should lick <s>triphala</s> with honey, and also guḍūcī, abhayā, and ghana.
The use of rasāñjana, mahāt pañcamūla, guggulu,
and śilājatu is beneficial, together with the juice of agnimantha.
Viḍaṅga, nāgara, alkali, filings of black iron, honey,
and powder of barley and āmalaka form a preparation that overcomes the faults of excessive corpulence.
Vyoṣa, kaṭvī, varā, śigru, viḍaṅga, ativiṣā, and sthirā,
hiṅgu, sauvarcala salt, ajājī, yavānī, dhānya, and citraka,

children.text: niśe bṛhatyau hapuṣā pāṭhā mūlaṃ ca kembukāt
children.translated_text: the two niśās, the two bṛhatīs, hapuṣā, pāṭhā, and the root of kembuka:

children.text: eṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ madhu ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ ca sadṛśāṃśakam ||
children.translated_text: the powder of these, with honey, ghee, and oil in equal parts,

children.text: saktubhiḥ ṣoḍaśaguṇair yuktaṃ pītaṃ nihanti tat
children.translated_text: mixed with sixteen times as much roasted grain flour and drunk, destroys

children.text: atisthaulyādikān sarvān rogān anyāṃś ca tadvidhān ||
children.translated_text: all the diseases beginning with excessive corpulence and also others of that kind.
It removes heart disease, jaundice, vitiligo, dyspnea, cough, and constriction of the throat,
promotes intellect, understanding, and memory, and kindles the digestive fire.
Extreme emaciation, dizziness, cough, excessive thirst, loss of appetite,
and loss of unctuousness, digestive fire, sleep, sight, hearing, semen, vigor, hunger, and voice
arise from excessive reducing, along with pain in the bladder, heart, head, calves, thighs, sacrum, and sides, fever,
delirium, upward movement of <s>vāta</s>, exhaustion, vomiting, and splitting pain in the joints and bones,
as well as retention of feces and urine and similar disorders.

children.text: kārśyam eva varaṃ sthaulyān na hi sthūlasya bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: Emaciation is preferable to corpulence, for there is no effective medicine for the corpulent person.
Neither nourishing nor reducing therapy is strong enough there to overcome excessive fat, impaired fire, and <s>vāta</s>.
But emaciation is easily removed by sweet, unctuous, satisfying foods and by comfort.
Thinness and stoutness arise through extremely opposite modes of regimen.
In thinness one should employ every nourishing drink, food, and medicine.
Through freedom from anxiety, gladdening, and constant satiation,

children.text: svapnaprasaṅgāc ca kṛśo varāha iva puṣyati ||
children.translated_text: and through indulgence in sleep, a thin person surely grows stout like a boar.

children.text: na hi māṃsasamaṃ kiṃcid anyad dehabṛhattvakṛt
children.translated_text: There is nothing else equal to meat for making the body large,
especially the meat of meat-eating animals, because it is built up from meat.

children.text: guru cātarpaṇaṃ sthūle viparītaṃ hitaṃ kṛśe
children.translated_text: For the corpulent, heavy but non-satiating fare is beneficial; for the thin, the opposite is beneficial.
Barley and wheat are suitable for both, when prepared in ways appropriate to each.
Because of the movement of the <s>doṣas</s> and because of distinctions such as absorbent and evacuative action,

children.text: upakramā na te dvitvād bhinnā api gadā iva ||
children.translated_text: the therapies, though differentiated, do not go beyond the twofold division, just as diseases do not.
Madana, madhuka, lambā, nimba, bimbī, viśālā, trapusa, kuṭaja, mūrvā, devadālī, and kṛmighna,
vidula, dahana, citrā, the two kośavatīs, karañja, kaṇa, salt, vacā, elā, and mustard are emetics.
Nikumbha, kumbha, triphalā, gavākṣī, snuk, śaṅkhinī, nīlinī, and tilvaka,

children.text: śamyākakampillakahemadugdhā dugdhaṃ ca mūtraṃ ca virecanāni ||
children.translated_text: śamyāka, kampillaka, hemadugdhā, milk, and urine are purgatives.
Madana, kuṭaja, kuṣṭha, devadālī, madhuka, vacā, daśamūla, dāru, and rāsnā,

children.text: yavamiśikṛtavedhanaṃ kulatthā madhu lavaṇaṃ trivṛtā nirūhaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: barley, miśi, kṛtavedhana, kulattha, honey, salt, and trivṛt are ingredients for non-unctuous enemas.

children.text: vellāpāmārgavyoṣadārvīsurālā bījaṃ śairīṣaṃ bārhataṃ śaigravaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Vella, apāmārga, vyoṣa, dārvī, surālā, śirīṣa seed, bārhata seed, and śigru seed,

children.text: sāro mādhūkaḥ saindhavaṃ tārkṣyaśailaṃ truṭyau pṛthvīkā śodhayanty uttamāṅgam ||
children.translated_text: the pith of madhūka, rock salt, tārkṣyaśaila, the two truṭis, and pṛthvīkā cleanse the head excellently.
Bhadradāru, nata, kuṣṭha, daśamūla, the two balās,

children.text: vāyuṃ vīratarādiś ca vidāryādiś ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: and the groups beginning with vīrataru and vidārī should remove <s>vāyu</s>.
Dūrvā, anantā, nimba, vāsā, ātmaguptā, gundrā, abhīru, śītapākī, and priyaṅgu,

children.text: nyagrodhādiḥ padmakādiḥ sthire dve padmaṃ vanyaṃ sārivādiś ca pittam ||
children.translated_text: the nyagrodhādi group, the padmakādi group, the two sthirās, wild lotus, and the sārivādi group remove <s>pitta</s>.
The groups beginning with āragvadha, arka, muṣkaka, and asana,
and the groups beginning with surasa, samustā, and vatsaka overcome <s>balāsa</s>, that is, <s>kapha</s>.
Jīvantī, the two kākolīs, the two medās, mudgaparṇī and māṣaparṇī,
ṛṣabhaka, jīvaka, and madhuka: this group is called jīvanīya, life-promoting.
Vidārī, pañcāṅgulā, vṛścikālī, vṛścīva, devāhvaya, and the two śūrpaparṇīs,

children.text: kaṇḍūkarī jīvanahrasvasaṃjñe dve pañcake gopasutā tripādī ||
children.translated_text: kaṇḍūkarī, the two groups called jīvana and hrasva pañcaka, gopasutā, and tripādī
make up this vidāryādi group; it is good for the heart, nourishing, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
The group removes wasting, abdominal tumors, aching of the limbs, upward dyspnea, and cough.
Sārivā, uśīra, kāśmarya, madhūka, the two śiśiras,
yaṣṭī, and parūṣaka remove burning, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, thirst, and fever.

children.text: padmakapuṇḍrau vṛddhitugarddhyaḥ śṛṅgy amṛtā daśa jīvanasaṃjñāḥ
children.translated_text: Padmaka, puṇḍra, vṛddhi, tugarddhī, śṛṅgī, and amṛtā are the ten called jīvana.
They promote breast milk, destroy wasting and <s>pitta</s>, and are satisfying, life-giving, nourishing, and aphrodisiac.

children.text: parūṣakaṃ varā drākṣā kaṭphalaṃ katakāt phalam
children.translated_text: Parūṣaka, varā, grapes, kaṭphala, the fruit of kataka,
rājāhva, pomegranate, and greens overcome thirst, urinary disorders, and <s>vāta</s>.
Añjana, phalinī, māṃsī, padma, utpala, rasāñjana,
together with elā, madhuka, and nāgāhva, remove poison, internal burning, and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Paṭola</s>, <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>, and <s>candana</s>, joined with <s>madhusrava</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>pāṭhā</s>,

children.text: nihanti kaphapittakuṣṭhajvarān viṣaṃ vamim arocakaṃ kāmalām ||
children.translated_text: destroy fevers from <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), poison, vomiting, anorexia, and jaundice.
<s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>dhānaka</s>, and red <s>candana</s>
remove fever and vomiting from <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, burning, and thirst, and kindle the digestive fire.
<s>Āragvadha</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>kākatiktā</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>madhurasā</s>, <s>sruvavṛkṣa</s>, and <s>pāṭhā</s>,
<s>Bhūnimba</s>, <s>sairyaka</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, the two <s>karañjas</s>, <s>saptacchada</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>suṣavī</s>, <s>phala</s>, <s>bāṇa</s>, and <s>ghoṇṭā</s>:
the group beginning with <s>āragvadha</s> overcomes vomiting, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, poisoning, and fevers;
it removes <s>kapha</s>, itching, and <s>prameha</s> (urinary disease), and cleanses foul wounds.
<s>Asana</s>, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>bhūrja</s>, <s>śvetavāha</s>, <s>prakīryā</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>kadara</s>, <s>bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>śiṃśapā</s>, and <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,
the three <s>hima</s> plants, <s>tala</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>joṅgaka</s>, <s>śāka</s>, <s>śāla</s>, <s>kramuka</s>, <s>dhava</s>, <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>chāgakarṇa</s>, and <s>aśvakarṇa</s>:
the group beginning with <s>asana</s> conquers leukoderma, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and worms;
it also removes anemia, <s>prameha</s>, and disorders of fat.
<s>Varuṇa</s>, the pair of <s>sairyaka</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>dahana</s>, <s>moraṭa</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>viṣāṇikā</s>,
the two <s>bṛhatīs</s>, the two <s>karañjas</s>, the two <s>jayās</s>, <s>bahalapallava</s>, <s>darbha</s>, and <s>rujākara</s>:
the group beginning with <s>varuṇa</s> checks <s>kapha</s>, fat, and weak digestion;
it also checks <s>āḍhyavāta</s>, headache, abdominal mass, and internal abscess.
<s>Ūṣaka</s>, <s>tutthaka</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, the two kinds of <s>kāsīsa</s>, and rock salt,
together with <s>śilājatu</s>, remove dysuria, urinary stones, abdominal masses, fat, and <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Vella</s>, <s>antarāraṇikā</s>, <s>būka</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>aśmabheda</s>, <s>gokaṇṭaka</s>, <s>etkaṭa</s>, <s>sahācara</s>, <s>bāṇa</s>, and <s>kāśa</s>,
<s>vṛkṣādanī</s>, <s>nala</s>, the two <s>kuśas</s>, <s>guṇṭha</s>, <s>gundrā</s>, <s>bhallūka</s>, <s>moraṭa</s>, <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>, <s>karambha</s>, and <s>pārtha</s>:
this class beginning with <s>vīratara</s> removes diseases caused by <s>vāta</s>;
it relieves stone, gravel, dysuria, urinary obstruction, and pain.
<s>Lodhra</s>, <s>śābaraka</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>jiṅginī</s>, <s>sarala</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s>,
<s>kutsitāmba</s>, <s>kadalī</s>, <s>gataśoka</s>, <s>sailavālu</s>, <s>paripelava</s>, and <s>mocā</s>:
this group, called the <s>lodhrādi</s>, removes fat and <s>kapha</s>;
it removes disorders of the vagina, is styptic, improves complexion, and destroys poison.

children.text: arkālarkau nāgadantī viśalyā bhārgī rāsnā vṛścikālī prakīryā
children.translated_text: <s>Arka</s> and <s>alarka</s>, <s>nāgadantī</s>, <s>viśalyā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>vṛścikālī</s>, and <s>prakīryā</s>,

children.text: pratyakpuṣpī pītatailodakīryā śvetāyugmaṃ tāpasānāṃ ca vṛkṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>pratyakpuṣpī</s>, <s>pītatailā</s>, <s>udakīryā</s>, the two white plants, and the tree of the ascetics:
this class beginning with <s>arka</s> removes <s>kapha</s>, fat, and poison;
it pacifies worms and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and is especially cleansing for wounds.
The two <s>surasās</s>, <s>phaṇijja</s>, <s>kālamālā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>kharabusa</s>, <s>vṛṣakarṇī</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, and <s>kāsamarda</s>,
<s>kṣavaka</s>, <s>sarasī</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>kārmuka</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>kulahala</s>, <s>viṣamuṣṭī</s>, <s>bhūstṛṇa</s>, and <s>bhūtakeśī</s>:
the group beginning with <s>surasā</s> destroys <s>śleṣman</s>, fat, and worms;
it removes coryza, anorexia, dyspnea, and cough, and cleanses wounds.
<s>Muṣkaka</s>, <s>snuk</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>dvīpī</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>dhava</s>, and <s>śiṃśipā</s>
overcome abdominal masses, <s>meha</s> (urinary disease), urinary stones, anemia, fat, piles, <s>kapha</s>, and semen.
<s>Vatsaka</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>marīca</s>, <s>ghuṇapriyā</s>, and <s>gaṇḍīra</s>,
<s>elā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, <s>kaṭvaṅgaphala</s>, <s>ajamodā</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s>, and <s>vacā</s>:
<s>Jīraka</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>paśugandhā</s>, and the <s>pañcakola</s> group remove
mobile <s>kapha</s>, fat, coryza, abdominal mass, fever, pain, and piles.
<s>Vacā</s>, <s>jalada</s>, <s>devāhva</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>,
the two <s>haridrās</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>kalaśī</s>, and what arises from <s>kuṭaja</s>:
the groups beginning with <s>vacā</s> and <s>haridrā</s> destroy <s>āma</s> (undigested morbid matter) and diarrhea;
they remove fat, <s>kapha</s>, vāta from overnourishment, and disorders of breast milk.
<s>Priyaṅgu</s>, <s>puṣpāñjana</s>, the pair of lotuses, lotus pollen, <s>yojanavallī</s>, and <s>anantā</s>,
<s>mānadruma</s>, <s>mocarasa</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>puṃnāga</s>, <s>śīta</s>, and <s>madanīyahetu</s>:
<s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>namaskarī</s>, <s>nandīvṛkṣa</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>kacchurā</s>,
<s>lodhra</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, the kernel of <s>bilva</s>, <s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, and lotus pollen:
the two groups beginning with <s>priyaṅgu</s> and <s>ambaṣṭhā</s> destroy diarrhea after digestion;

children.text: saṃdhānīyau hitau pitte vraṇānām api ropaṇau ||
children.translated_text: they promote healing union, are beneficial in <s>pitta</s>, and also heal wounds.
<s>Mustā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>agni</s>, the two <s>niśās</s>, the two bitter drugs, <s>bhallāta</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and what is called <s>viṣā</s>,

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ truṭī haimavatī ca yonistanyāmayaghnā malapācanāś ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>truṭī</s>, and <s>haimavatī</s> remove diseases of the vagina and breast milk, and digest morbid wastes.
<s>Nyagrodha</s>, <s>pippala</s>, <s>sadāphala</s>, the pair of <s>lodhras</s>, the two <s>jambūs</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>kapītana</s>, and <s>somavalka</s>,
<s>plakṣa</s>, <s>āmra</s>, <s>vañjula</s>, <s>piyāla</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>nandī</s>, <s>kolī</s>, <s>kadamba</s>, <s>virala</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>madhūka</s>:
the group beginning with <s>nyagrodha</s> is beneficial for wounds, is constipating, and heals fractures;
it removes fat, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, thirst, burning, and diseases of the vagina.

The two <s>elās</s>, <s>turuṣka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>jaladhyāmaka</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>coraka</s>, <s>coca-pattra</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>sthauṇeya</s>, and <s>jātīrasa</s>,

children.text: śuktir vyāghranakho 'marāhvam aguruḥ śrīvāsakaḥ kuṅkumaṃ caṇḍāgugguludevadhūpakhapurāḥ puṃnāganāgāhvayam
children.translated_text: <s>śukti</s>, <s>vyāghranakha</s>, <s>amarāhva</s>, <s>aguru</s>, <s>śrīvāsaka</s>, <s>kuṅkuma</s>, <s>caṇḍā</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, <s>devadhūpa</s>, <s>khapura</s>, <s>puṃnāga</s>, and what is called <s>nāga</s>:
the group beginning with <s>elā</s> checks <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and poison;
it brightens the complexion and destroys itching, pustules, and urticarial eruptions.
<s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>dravantī</s>, <s>kramuka</s>, <s>kuṭaraṇā</s>, <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, and <s>carmasāhvā</s>,
<s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, <s>gavākṣī</s>, <s>śikharī</s>, <s>rajanaka</s>, <s>chinnarohā</s>, and <s>karañja</s>,
<s>bastāntrī</s>, <s>vyādhighāta</s>, <s>bahala</s>, <s>bahurasa</s>, and the fruits of the sharp tree:

children.text: śyāmādyo hanti gulmaṃ viṣamarucikaphau hṛdrujaṃ mūtrakṛcchram ||
children.translated_text: the group beginning with <s>śyāmā</s> removes abdominal mass, poison, anorexia, <s>kapha</s>, heart pain, and dysuria.

children.text: trayastriṃśad iti proktā vargās teṣu tv alābhataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus thirty-three groups have been stated; among them, when one is unavailable,

children.text: yuñjyāt tadvidham anyac ca dravyaṃ jahyād ayaugikam ||
children.translated_text: One should use another substance of that same kind, and should avoid what is unsuitable.
These groups, with regard to <s>doṣa</s>, <s>dūṣya</s>, and the like, when combined with paste, decoction, fat, linctus, and so on,

children.text: pāne nasye 'nvāsane 'ntar bahir vā lepābhyaṅgair ghnanti rogān sukṛcchrān ||
children.translated_text: whether for drinking, nasal therapy, unctuous enema, internally or externally, by applications and massage, destroy diseases even when they are very difficult.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the rule of <s>sneha</s> (oleation).
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
A medicine that is heavy, cold, flowing, unctuous, slow, subtle, soft, and liquid
is generally oleating; one of the opposite qualities is drying.

children.text: sarpir majjā vasā tailaṃ sneheṣu pravaraṃ matam
children.translated_text: Ghee, marrow, muscle-fat, and oil are considered foremost among unctuous substances;
and among them ghee is best, because it follows the properties of substances with which it is processed.
Because of its sweetness, because it does not cause burning, and because it is accustomed from birth onward,
they are, in the preceding order, removers of <s>pitta</s>; and in the following order removers of the other <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: ghṛtāt tailaṃ guru vasā tailān majjā tato 'pi ca
children.translated_text: Oil is heavier than ghee; muscle-fat is heavier than oil, and marrow heavier even than that.

children.text: dvābhyāṃ tribhiś caturbhis tair yamakas trivṛto mahān ||
children.translated_text: With two, three, or four of these there is <s>yamaka</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and <s>mahāsneha</s> respectively.
Those who are to be sudated or purified, and those attached to wine, women, exercise, or worry,
children, the aged, the emaciated, the dry, and those whose blood or semen is depleted,
those afflicted by <s>vāta</s>, discharge, dimness of vision, harshness, or sleeplessness,
are to be oleated; but not those with extremely weak digestion, sharp digestion, obesity, or debility,
nor those oppressed by thigh-stiffness, diarrhea, undigested matter, throat disease, poisoning, abdominal enlargement,
fainting, vomiting, anorexia, phlegm, thirst, or intoxication.

children.text: apaprasūtā yukte ca nasye bastau virecane
children.translated_text: Nor should it be used in women after abnormal delivery, or when nasal therapy, enema, or purgation is already being properly applied.
Among these, ghee is praised for those desiring intellect, memory, understanding, and the like.
Oil is for persons suffering from tumors, fistulous channels, worms, phlegm, fat, or <s>māruta</s> disorders,
and for bodies requiring lightness and firmness, and for those with a hard bowel.
In those whose tissues are depleted by wind, heat, road-travel, carrying loads, women, or exercise,
and in those who endure dryness and hardship, have excessive digestive fire, or whose passages are obstructed by <s>vāta</s>,
the remaining two are used; muscle-fat especially in pains of the joints, bones, vital spots, and abdomen,
and likewise in pains caused by burns, blows, dislocations, and pains of the vagina, ear, and head.

children.text: tailaṃ prāvṛṣi varṣānte sarpir anyau tu mādhave
children.translated_text: Oil is used in the rainy season and at the end of the rains; ghee is used otherwise, and the other two in spring.

children.text: ṛtau sādhāraṇe snehaḥ śasto 'hni vimale ravau ||
children.translated_text: In an ordinary season, <s>sneha</s> is approved on a clear day when the sun is unobscured.

children.text: tailaṃ tvarāyāṃ śīte 'pi gharme 'pi ca ghṛtaṃ niśi
children.translated_text: When there is urgency, oil may be given even in cold weather, and ghee even in hot weather, at night.

children.text: niśy eva pitte pavane saṃsarge pittavaty api ||
children.translated_text: At night only should it be given when there is <s>pitta</s>, when there is <s>pavana</s>, or even when the combination contains <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: niśyanyathā vātakaphād rogāḥ syuḥ pittato divā
children.translated_text: Otherwise at night diseases would arise from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, and by day from <s>pitta</s>.
One should administer <s>sneha</s> appropriately with edible foods and other foods, and by enemas,
nasal therapies, anointing, gargles, and nourishment of the head, ears, and eyes.
Through difference of tastes and through having one taste, the modes of administration are sixty-four.
They are remembered in order because the <s>sneha</s> is overpowered by other substances and because it is small in amount.
Since the stated reasons are absent, a mode of administration is not a clear fat to be drunk.
That preparation of <s>sneha</s> is best, because it quickly accomplishes the action of oleation.
The measures that are digested respectively in two, four, and eight watches
are the small, middle, and highest doses; and from these one should devise still smaller doses.
Having considered the <s>doṣas</s> and the rest, one should first prescribe the smaller dose.

children.text: hyastane jīrṇa evānne sneho'cchaḥ śuddhaye bahuḥ
children.translated_text: When yesterday's food has been digested, clear <s>sneha</s> in large quantity is for purification.
For pacification, it is praised in a moderate dose, without food, for one who is hungry.

children.text: bṛṃhaṇo rasamadyādyaiḥ sabhakto'lpaḥ hitaḥ sa ca
children.translated_text: For nourishment, a small quantity with food, together with meat-soup, wine, and the like, is beneficial,
and also in children, the aged, the thirsty, those distressed by oleation, and habitual drinkers,
in women, in those constantly accustomed to unction, in those of weak digestion, in the comfortable, and in those afraid of hardship,
in those with a soft bowel and little morbidity, in hot weather, and in the emaciated.
Taken before, during, or after the meal, it conquers diseases born respectively in the lower, middle, and upper body,
and produces strength in the limbs in the same order.
<s>Sveda</s> (sudation) is fourfold, according to the divisions of heat, poultice, steam, and fluid.
Heat is produced by cloth, iron plates, palms of the hands, and the like heated in fire.
A poultice is made with <s>vacā</s>, fermented gruel, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>,
with all grains, aromatics, <s>rāsnā</s>, castor root, and meat,
with abundant salt, moistened with fat, sour gruel, buttermilk, and milk.
For pure <s>pavana</s> this is used; when mixed with phlegm, it is made with the group beginning with <s>surasā</s>.

children.text: pittena padmakādyais tu śālvaṇākhyaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When mixed with <s>pitta</s>, it is made with the group beginning with <s>padmaka</s>; and again and again with preparations called <s>śālvaṇa</s>.
It should be unctuous, hot in potency, and soft, and bound with clean leather straps.
If these are unavailable, it may be bound with leaves that conquer <s>vāta</s>, or with silk or woolen cloths.

children.text: baddhaṃ rātrau divā muñcen muñced rātrau divākṛtam ||
children.translated_text: What has been bound on at night should be removed by day, and what has been done by day should be removed at night.
Steam, however, is to be applied with boiled cakes, heated bricks, potsherds, stones, and sand,
with broken leaves, grain, dung, sand, and chaff,
heated in many different ways, according to place and time.
From the broken leaves of <s>śigru</s>, <s>vāraṇaka</s>, castor, <s>karañja</s>, <s>surasā</s>, and <s>arjaka</s>,
of <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, bamboo, <s>arka</s>, jasmine, and <s>dīrghavṛnta</s>,
together with the leaf fragments, with substances beginning with <s>vacā</s>, and with meat from marsh and aquatic animals,

children.text: daśamūlena ca pṛthak sahitair vā yathāmalam
children.translated_text: and with <s>daśamūla</s>, either separately or combined according to the morbidity,
cooked with fatty substances, wine, vinegar, water, milk, and the like,

children.text: kumbhīr galantīr nāḍīr vā pūrayitvā rujārditam
children.translated_text: one should fill pots, sprinkling vessels, or tubes, and comfortably pour over the body afflicted by pain,
which has been covered with cloth and anointed with fat.

children.text: tair eva vā dravaiḥ pūrṇaṃ kuṇḍaṃ sarvāṅgage 'nile
children.translated_text: Or, in generalized <s>anila</s>, the patient should enter a tub filled with those same liquids,
and remain immersed there, also in pains such as piles and dysuria.
In a windless place, anointed both internally and externally, with food digested, one should undertake sudation,
making it medium, strong, or mild according to the disease, the patient, the place, and the season.

children.text: kaphārto rūkṣaṇaṃ rūkṣo rūkṣaḥ snigdhaṃ kaphānile
children.translated_text: One afflicted by <s>kapha</s> should receive drying treatment; one who is dry, unctuous treatment; and when there is <s>kapha</s> with <s>anila</s>, the dry patient should receive unctuous treatment.
When <s>vāyu</s> is situated in the stomach and <s>kapha</s> is lodged in the colon,
Sudation may be preceded by drying treatment, and likewise by oleation, according to the site;

children.text: alpaṃ vaṅkṣaṇayoḥ svalpaṃ dṛṅmuṣkahṛdaye na vā ||
children.translated_text: it should be slight in the groins, very slight for the eyes, testes, and heart, or omitted there.
When cold and pain have subsided, when the patient has been sudated and softness of the limbs has arisen,

children.text: syāc chanair mṛditaḥ snātas tataḥ snehavidhiṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: he should be rubbed gently, bathed, and then follow the regimen prescribed after oleation.
Aggravation of <s>pitta</s> and blood, thirst, fainting, weakness of voice and limbs, dizziness,
joint pain, fever, and the sight of dusky-red circles

children.text: svedātiyogāc chardiś ca tatra stambhanam auṣadham
children.translated_text: and vomiting arise from excessive sudation; in that case <s>stambhana</s> (checking therapy) is the medicine.
For those afflicted by poison, alkali, fire-burn, diarrhea, vomiting, and stupor too,

children.text: svedanaṃ guru tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ prāyaḥ stambhanam anyathā
children.translated_text: sudation is generally heavy, sharp, and hot; checking therapy is the opposite.
The medicine for sudation may be liquid or solid, flowing, unctuous, dry, and subtle;
checking therapy is smooth, dry, subtle, mobile, and liquid,

children.text: prāyas tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca madhuraṃ ca samāsataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, in brief, generally bitter, astringent, and sweet.
Checking is successful when strength has been regained and the diseases described have diminished.
By stiffness, contraction of skin and sinews, tremor, and catching of the heart, speech, and jaw,
and by dusky feet, lips, skin, and hands, one should recognize excessive checking.
One should not sudate those who are very corpulent, dry, weak, or fainted,
nor those needing checking therapy, the wounded, the depleted, the wasted, or those disordered by wine,
nor patients afflicted with <s>timira</s>, abdominal disease, <s>vīsarpa</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, consumption, or severe disease,
nor those who have drunk milk, curd, fat, or honey, nor those who have undergone purgation,
nor those with prolapsed or burned rectum, exhaustion, or those afflicted by anger, grief, or fear,
nor those suffering from hunger, thirst, jaundice, anemia, <s>meha</s>, or oppression by <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: garbhiṇīṃ puṣpitāṃ sūtāṃ mṛdu cātyayike gade ||
children.translated_text: nor a pregnant woman, a menstruating woman, a woman recently delivered, or a delicate person, except in an urgent disease.
In dyspnea, cough, coryza, hiccup, abdominal distension, and constipation,
in hoarseness, diseases of <s>vāta</s>, heaviness from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>āma</s>, and stiffness,
in aching of the limbs and catching of the waist, sides, back, belly, and jaw,
in enlargement of the testes, baldness, constriction, and <s>vātakaṇṭaka</s>,
in dysuria, tumors, nodules, obstruction of semen, and disorders dominated by <s>vāta</s>,
one should apply sudation as appropriate, according to the division of the medicines for each condition.

children.text: svedo hitas tv anāgneyo vāte medaḥkaphāvṛte
children.translated_text: Sudation without fire is beneficial when <s>vāta</s> is obstructed by fat and <s>kapha</s>.
A windless room, exertion, a heavy covering, fear,

children.text: snehaklinnāḥ koṣṭhagā dhātugā vā srotolīnā ye ca śākhāsthisaṃsthāḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>doṣas</s> that have been moistened by oleation, whether lodged in the bowel, in the tissues, hidden in the channels, or situated in the branches and bones,

children.text: doṣāḥ svedais te dravīkṛtya koṣṭhaṃ nītāḥ samyak śuddhibhir nirhriyante ||
children.translated_text: are liquefied by sudations, brought to the bowel, and properly expelled by cleansing procedures.

children.text: kaphe vidadhyād vamanaṃ saṃyoge vā kapholbaṇe
children.translated_text: In <s>kapha</s> one should prescribe emesis, or in a combined condition when <s>kapha</s> is predominant;

children.text: tadvad virecanaṃ pitte viśeṣeṇa tu vāmayet ||
children.translated_text: similarly purgation in <s>pitta</s>; but especially one should administer emesis
to those with recent fever, diarrhea, downward-moving <s>pitta</s> or blood, and <s>rājayakṣman</s>,
to those with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>meha</s>, scrofula, nodules, elephantiasis, insanity, and cough,
to those with dyspnea, nausea, <s>vīsarpa</s>, disorders of breast milk, and diseases above the clavicle.
Not to be given emesis are a pregnant woman, one who is dry, one who is hungry, and one constantly distressed,
children, the old, the emaciated, the obese, those with heart disease, the wounded, and the weak,
those with persistent vomiting, spleen disease, <s>timira</s>, or worms in the bowel,
those with upward-moving <s>vāyu</s> or blood, those who have been given an enema, and those whose voice is impaired,
those with urinary retention, abdominal disease, or <s>gulma</s>, those hard to vomit, those with excessive digestive fire, and those with piles,
those with <s>udāvarta</s>, dizziness, <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, pain in the side, or diseases of <s>vāta</s>,
except when the condition comes from poison, artificial poison, indigestion, or eating incompatible food.
In those with persistent vomiting, and generally in the early stage, even fever with <s>āma</s> is included.

children.text: dhūmāntaiḥ karmabhir varjyāḥ sarvair eva tv ajīrṇinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But all who have indigestion should be kept from every procedure up to and including smoking therapy.
Abdominal masses, piles, eruptions, facial blemishes, and jaundice are treatable by purgation,
as are chronic fever, abdominal enlargement, poison, vomiting, spleen disease, and <s>halīmaka</s>,
abscess, <s>timira</s>, <s>kāca</s>, conjunctival discharge, and pain in the large intestine,
diseases located in the vagina and semen, worms in the bowel, and wounds,
<s>vātāsra</s>, upward-moving blood, urinary obstruction, and retention of feces,

children.text: vāmyaś ca kuṣṭhamehādyā na tu recyā navajvarī ||
children.translated_text: and the vomitable diseases such as <s>kuṣṭha</s> and <s>meha</s>; but a patient with recent fever should not be purged.
Nor should purgation be given to those with weak digestion, downward-moving <s>pitta</s> or blood, anal injury, or diarrhea,
nor to those with a foreign body, those not prepared by decoction enema, those with a hard bowel, the over-uncted, or the consumptive.
Then, at the common proper time, one who has been oleated and sudated according to rule,
who is to be vomited the next day and whose <s>kapha</s> has been excited by fish, black gram, sesame, and the like,
having slept through the night, with food well digested, in the forenoon, after auspicious rites have been performed,
should be fasting, or slightly unctuous, or should have drunk ghee with thin gruel.
The aged, children, the weak, the impotent, and the timid, according to the disease,

children.text: ākaṇṭhaṃ pāyitān madyaṃ kṣīram ikṣurasaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: should be made to drink up to the throat wine, milk, sugarcane juice, or meat broth.
The medicine prescribed according to the disorder, combined with honey and rock salt,
with the dose determined after assessing the bowel, should be consecrated with a mantra.
May <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, Earth, Moon, Sun, Wind, and Fire,

children.text: ṛṣayaḥ sauṣadhigrāmā bhūtasaṃghāś ca pāntu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sages together with the hosts of herbs, and the assemblies of beings protect you.
As rejuvenation is to the sages, as nectar is to the immortals,
as ambrosia is to the best serpents, so may this medicine be for you.
Facing east, one should make him drink it; when it has been drunk, one should wait a <s>muhūrta</s>.
With his mind fixed on it, when nausea and salivation have arisen, he should then vomit.
Without strain, with the fingers or else with a soft tube,
not injuring the throat or palate, one should set in motion urges that have not begun,
and keep moving those that have begun, while the patient sits on a knee-high seat.

children.text: ubhe pārśve lalāṭaṃ ca vamataś cāsya dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: One should support both sides and the forehead of him as he vomits,

children.text: prapīḍayet tathā nābhiṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ ca pratilomataḥ
children.translated_text: and likewise press the navel and the back in the reverse direction.
In <s>kapha</s>, he should vomit with sharp, hot, pungent substances; in <s>pitta</s>, with sweet and cooling ones.
When <s>kapha</s> is mixed with <s>vāta</s>, he should vomit with unctuous, sour, and salty substances,

children.text: pittasya darśanaṃ yāvac chedo vā śleṣmaṇo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: until <s>pitta</s> appears or until the phlegm is cut off.
When the urges are weak, with waters containing <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s>, and salt,

children.text: vamet punaḥ punas tatra vegānām apravartanam ||
children.translated_text: he should vomit again and again. In that case, the failure of the urges to start,
or their starting with obstruction, or the passage of the medicine alone,
is deficient administration; from it arise spitting, itching, urticarial eruptions, fever, and the like.
In proper administration, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>anila</s> (vāta) move out unobstructed, in order.
But in excessive administration, the vomited matter has foam, moonlike patches, or blood,

children.text: vamitaṃ kṣāmatā dāhaḥ kaṇṭhaśoṣas tamo bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: and there are emaciation, burning, dryness of the throat, darkness before the eyes, and dizziness;
terrible <s>vāta</s> diseases or death may occur because the vital blood has issued forth.
After the patient has vomited through proper administration, let him rest for a moment and have him drink
one among the three kinds of medicated smoke; then the regimen of oleation should be prescribed.

children.text: tataḥ sāyaṃ prabhāte vā kṣudvān snātaḥ sukhāmbunā
children.translated_text: Then, in the evening or in the morning, when hungry and bathed with pleasant warm water,
while eating rice of red <s>śāli</s>, he should follow in order the regimen beginning with <s>peyā</s>.

children.text: peyāṃ vilepīm akṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yūṣaṃ rasaṃ trīn ubhayaṃ tathaikam
children.translated_text: A man cleansed with superior, medium, or inferior purification should take <s>peyā</s>, <s>vilepī</s>, unseasoned and seasoned <s>yūṣa</s>, and meat broth
gradually over three, two, or one meal-times respectively.

children.text: yathāṇur agnis tṛṇagomayādyaiḥ saṃdhukṣyamāṇo bhavati krameṇa
children.translated_text: Just as a small fire, when kindled gradually with grass, cow-dung, and the like,

children.text: mahān sthiraḥ sarvapacas tathaiva śuddhasya peyādibhir antarāgniḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes great, steady, and able to cook everything, so too the inner fire of one who has been cleansed becomes strong through <s>peyā</s> and the other foods.

children.text: jaghanyamadhyapravare tu vegāś catvāra iṣṭā vamane ṣaḍ aṣṭau
children.translated_text: For inferior, middle, and excellent cleansing, four, six, and eight urges are desired in emesis,

children.text: daśaiva te dvitriguṇā vireke prasthas tathā syād dvicaturguṇaś ca ||
children.translated_text: and in purgation they are ten, twice that, and three times that; the measure is also one <s>prastha</s>, or twice or four times that.

children.text: pittāvasānaṃ vamanaṃ virekād ardhaṃ kaphāntaṃ ca virekam āhuḥ
children.translated_text: They say that emesis should end with <s>pitta</s> and should be half of purgation, and that purgation should end with <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: dvitrān saviṭkān apanīya vegān meyaṃ vireke vamane tu pītam ||
children.translated_text: In purgation one should measure after setting aside two or three urges accompanied by feces; in emesis, what was drunk should be deducted.
Then this patient who has been made to vomit, again prepared with oleation and sudation,

children.text: śleṣmakāle gate jñātvā koṣṭhaṃ samyag virecayet ||
children.translated_text: should be properly purged after the time of <s>śleṣman</s> has passed and the bowel has been correctly assessed.
A soft bowel with much <s>pitta</s> is purged even by milk,
while a hard bowel with abundant <s>māruta</s> (vāta) is purged with difficulty even by <s>śyāmā</s> and similar drugs.
In <s>pitta</s>, purgation should be done with astringent and sweet drugs; in <s>kapha</s>, with pungent ones;
in <s>vāyu</s>, with oily, hot, and salty ones. But when there is no action, he should be given to drink
warm water, and his abdomen should be fomented with the heat of the hands.

children.text: utthāne 'lpe dine tasmin bhuktvānyedyuḥ punaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: If the evacuation is slight on that day, after eating he should drink again on the following day.
But one whose bowel has not been firmly oleated should drink purgation medicine after ten days,
his body once more prepared with oleation and sudation.

children.text: yaugikaṃ samyag ālocya smaran pūrvam atikramam
children.translated_text: He should properly consider the suitable combination, remembering the previous excess or fault.
Impurity of the heart and abdomen, anorexia, and nausea from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>,
itching, burning, pimples, coryza, and obstruction of <s>vāta</s> and feces
are the signs of deficient administration; proper administration is the opposite of what has been stated.
When feces, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s> have come out in order, there may flow
water devoid of <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>, white, black, or mixed with blood,
or like water from washing meat, or resembling pieces of fat.
Prolapse of the rectum, thirst, dizziness, and sinking of the eyes
occur in one excessively purged, as do the disorders of excessive emesis.
One who has been properly purged should be managed by the method stated for emesis,
except for medicated smoke; then, eating foods gradually as one who has vomited does,
he should return to his normal diet.
A person who has taken purgative medicine but has weak digestion, is not cleansed, is not emaciated, and is weakened by the <s>doṣas</s>,
and in whom the signs of digestion have not appeared, should be made to fast.
In this way he is not afflicted by accumulations from oleation, sudation, medicine, and the excited <s>doṣas</s>.
Through purificatory treatment, bloodletting, application of oleation, and fasting,

children.text: yāty agnir mandatāṃ tasmāt kramaṃ peyādim ācaret
children.translated_text: the digestive fire becomes weak; therefore one should observe the regimen beginning with <s>peyā</s>.
One in whom little <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> have flowed out, a drinker of alcohol, and one of <s>vāta-pitta</s> constitution

children.text: peyāṃ na pāyayet teṣāṃ tarpaṇādikramo hitaḥ
children.translated_text: should not be made to drink <s>peyā</s>; for them the regimen beginning with nourishing drinks is beneficial.
Emesis removes the <s>doṣas</s> when they are unripe; purgation removes them when they are being digested.
Therefore, for emesis, one should not wait for digestion.

children.text: durbalo bahudoṣaś ca doṣapākena yaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: A weak person with many <s>doṣas</s>, who through the maturation of the <s>doṣas</s>
is purged by himself, should be supported with foods that loosen the bowels.

children.text: durbalaḥ śodhitaḥ pūrvam alpadoṣaḥ kṛśo naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A weak man who has been purified before, has few <s>doṣas</s>, is thin,

children.text: aparijñātakoṣṭhaś ca piben mṛdv alpam auṣadham
children.translated_text: and whose bowel type is not known should drink a mild medicine in a small dose.
It is better that this be drunk repeatedly; otherwise it brings uncertainty and danger.

children.text: hared bahūṃś calān doṣān alpān alpān punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should remove many mobile <s>doṣas</s>, little by little, again and again;

children.text: durbalasya mṛdudravyair alpān saṃśamayet tu tān ||
children.translated_text: in the case of a weak person, one should pacify those few <s>doṣas</s> with mild substances.

children.text: kleśayanti ciraṃ te hi hanyur vainam anirhṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: For if they are not removed, they trouble him for a long time and may even kill him.
One with weak digestive fire and a hard bowel should be cleansed with ghee containing alkalis and salts,
after his digestive fire has been kindled and <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> have been overcome.
For those who are dry, have much <s>anila</s> (vāta), have hard bowels, are habituated to exercise,
and have strong digestive fire, the medicine digests without producing purgation.

children.text: tebhyo vastiṃ purā dadyāt tataḥ snigdhaṃ virecanam ||
children.translated_text: For them one should first give an enema, and after that an oleated purgative.

children.text: śakṛn nirhṛtya vā kiṃcit tīkṣṇābhiḥ phalavartibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Or, after drawing out some feces with sharp fruit suppositories,

children.text: pravṛttaṃ hi malaṃ snigdho vireko nirharet sukham ||
children.translated_text: an oleated purgation easily removes the fecal matter once it has begun to move.
Those afflicted by poison, trauma, pustules, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, swelling, and spreading erysipelas,
and those suffering from jaundice, anemia, and <s>meha</s>, should be purified when they are not excessively oleated.

children.text: sarvān snehavirekaiś ca rūkṣais tu snehabhāvitān
children.translated_text: All of them should be treated with oily purgatives, but those saturated with oil should be treated with dry ones.
Between the procedures, such as emesis and the rest, again and again,

children.text: snehasvedau prayuñjīta sneham ante balāya ca
children.translated_text: one should apply oleation and sudation, and oleation at the end for strength.

children.text: malo hi dehād utkleśya hriyate vāsaso yathā ||
children.translated_text: For waste matter, once excited from the body, is carried away, as dirt from a cloth;
likewise, waste matter excited by oleation and sudation is cleansed away by purificatory treatments.

children.text: snehasvedāv anabhyasya kuryāt saṃśodhanaṃ tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who performs purification without first practicing <s>sneha</s> (oleation) and <s>sveda</s> (sudation),

children.text: buddhiprasādaṃ balam indriyāṇāṃ dhātusthiratvaṃ jvalanasya dīptim
children.translated_text: properly undertaken purification brings clarity of intellect, strength of the senses, stability of the tissues, and kindling of the digestive fire,

children.text: cirāc ca pākaṃ vayasaḥ karoti saṃśodhanaṃ samyagupāsyamānam ||
children.translated_text: and it causes the aging of the body to mature only after a long time.

children.text: vātolbaṇeṣu doṣeṣu vāte vā vastir iṣyate
children.translated_text: In morbidities in which <s>vāta</s> is predominant, or in <s>vāta</s> itself, <s>basti</s> is prescribed.

children.text: upakramāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ so 'graṇīs trividhas tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among all treatments it is foremost; it is of three kinds:
<s>nirūha</s>, <s>anuvāsana</s>, and <s>uttara-basti</s>. By it one should treat
abdominal tumors, distension, <s>khuda</s>, splenic disease, purified diarrhea, and those suffering from colic,
chronic fever, coryza, and retention of semen, flatus, and feces,
inguinal swelling, urinary stone, suppression of menstruation, and severe disorders of <s>anila</s>.

children.text: anāsthāpyās tv atisnigdhaḥ kṣatorasko bhṛśaṃ kṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Those not to be given <s>āsthāpana</s> are: one excessively oleated, one with an injured chest, one extremely emaciated,
one with diarrhea from <s>āma</s>, one who is vomiting, one who has just been purified, and one who has received nasal therapy,
those with dyspnea, cough, salivation, piles, hiccup, abdominal distension, and weak digestive fire,
one with a swollen anus, one who has eaten, and one with obstructed passages, intestinal perforation, or watery abdominal disease,

children.text: kuṣṭhī ca madhumehī ca māsān sapta ca garbhiṇī
children.translated_text: also one with skin disease, one with diabetes, and a pregnant woman in the seventh month.
Those fit for <s>āsthāpana</s> are also fit for <s>anvāsana</s>, especially those with excessive digestive fire.

children.text: rūkṣāḥ kevalavātārtā nānuvāsyās ta eva ca
children.translated_text: But the dry, those afflicted by pure <s>vāta</s>, and the very same persons who are unfit for <s>āsthāpana</s>, are not to be given <s>anuvāsana</s>,
as well as those with pallor, jaundice, urinary disease, or coryza,
those who have taken no food, those with splenic disease, loose stools, a heavy bowel, or abdominal disease from <s>kapha</s>,
those with <s>abhiṣyanda</s>, the extremely obese, those whose bowels contain worms, and those with excessive <s>māruta</s>,
one who has drunk poison or artificial poison, one with indigestion, one with elephantiasis, and one with goiter.
For the two kinds, the nozzle should be made of gold and other metals, wood, bone, or bamboo.
It should be shaped like a cow's tail, without cracks, smooth, straight, and with a pellet-shaped mouth.
Before the year is complete it should be five finger-breadths; when that year is complete and up to seven years, six.

children.text: saptame sapta tāny aṣṭau dvādaśe ṣoḍaśe nava
children.translated_text: In the seventh year it should be seven; in the twelfth, eight; in the sixteenth, nine.

children.text: dvādaśaiva paraṃ viṃśād vīkṣya varṣāntareṣu ca ||
