children.translated_text: After twenty years it should be twelve only; in the intervening years
one should increase the measure after considering age, strength, and body.
At the base its thickness should equal the patient's thumb, and at the tip the little finger.
When the year is complete, the opening is taken as one finger-breadth and is increased by halves and quarters.

children.text: tryaṅgulaṃ paramaṃ chidraṃ mūle 'gre vahate tu yat ||
children.translated_text: The opening has three finger-breadths as its maximum; at the base and at the tip it should carry

children.text: mudgaṃ māṣaṃ kalāyaṃ ca klinnaṃ karkandhukaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: a soaked <s>mudga</s> bean, a <s>māṣa</s> bean, a <s>kalāya</s> pea, and a softened <s>karkandhu</s> fruit, successively.
At the end, according to the measure of the base-opening, a rim should be fitted.
It should be closed at the tip with a plug, and at the base, at the proper interval of two finger-breadths,

children.text: karṇikādvitayaṃ netre kuryāt tatra ca yojayet ||
children.translated_text: one should make a pair of rims on the nozzle, and there attach
the bladder of a goat, sheep, buffalo, and the like, well rubbed and firm,
reddened with astringent decoction, thin, and free from holes, knots, smell, and veins.
It should be well tied with thread and capable of holding the medicine comfortably.
In the absence of a bladder, one may place a limb-skin or foot-skin, or else a thick cloth.
The dose of <s>nirūha</s> in the first year is, at most, one <s>prakuñca</s>.

children.text: prakuñcavṛddhiḥ pratyabdaṃ yāvat ṣaṭ prasṛtās tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is an increase of one <s>prakuñca</s> each year until six <s>prasṛtas</s> are reached.
Thereafter one should increase by one <s>prasṛta</s> up to the twelfth and eighteenth years.

children.text: āsaptater idaṃ mānaṃ daśaiva prasṛtāḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Up to seventy years this is the measure; beyond that, ten <s>prasṛtas</s> is the maximum.
For <s>anuvāsana</s>, the dose is one quarter of the <s>nirūha</s> measure in each case.

children.text: āsthāpyaṃ snehitaṃ svinnaṃ śuddhaṃ labdhabalaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The person to be given <s>āsthāpana</s> should have been oleated, sudated, purified, and should have regained strength.
Knowing him to be fit for <s>anvāsana</s>, one should first administer <s>anuvāsana</s>.

children.text: śīte vasante ca divā rātrau kecit tato 'nyadā ||
children.translated_text: In cold weather and in spring this is done by day; some say by night, and at other times otherwise.
After being anointed and bathed, he should eat a suitable, wholesome, light meal, reduced by one quarter,
neither oily nor dry, with an after-drink, and including liquid and similar foods.
After walking about and passing feces and urine, on a comfortable bed,
not too high and without a raised pillow, he should lie on his left side.

children.text: saṃkocya dakṣiṇaṃ sakthi prasārya ca tato 'param
children.translated_text: He should contract the right thigh and then stretch out the other one.

children.text: athāsya netraṃ praṇayet snigdhe snigdhamukhaṃ gude ||
children.translated_text: Then the physician should insert the nozzle, its mouth smeared with oil, into his well-oiled anus.

children.text: ucchvāsya vaster vadane baddhe hastam akampayan
children.translated_text: Having expelled the air and tied the mouth of the bladder, without shaking the hand,
then, directing it toward the spinal column, neither too quickly nor too slowly,

children.text: nātivegaṃ na vā mandaṃ sakṛd eva prapīḍayet
children.translated_text: neither with excessive force nor weakly, he should squeeze it only once.

children.text: sāvaśeṣaṃ ca kurvīta vāyuḥ śeṣe hi tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: He should leave some residue, for air remains when there is a residue.
When it has been given, while the patient lies supine, he should strike the buttocks with the hand,

children.text: tatpārṣṇibhyāṃ tathā śayyāṃ pādataś ca trir utkṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the bed with the heels; from the foot end he should raise it three times.
Then, when the patient has stretched out his limbs and has a pillow, at the heels
he should strike with the fist, and should anoint the body with oil and massage it.

children.text: vedanārtam iti sneho na hi śīghraṃ nivartate
children.translated_text: Thus, for one afflicted with pain, the oil indeed does not return quickly.
If the oil returns quickly, another oil should be applied; oil that does not remain accomplishes no purpose.

children.text: dīptāgniṃ tv āgatasnehaṃ sāyāhne bhojayel laghu
children.translated_text: When the digestive fire is kindled and the oil has come back, he should feed the patient lightly in the evening.

children.text: nivṛttikālaḥ paramas trayo yāmas tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: The utmost time for its return is three <s>yāmas</s>; beyond that,
one should wait for a day and night. After that, by means of fruit suppositories

children.text: tīkṣṇair vā vastibhiḥ kuryād yatnaṃ snehanivṛttaye ||
children.translated_text: or sharp enemas, one should make an effort to bring the oil back.
If, because of excessive dryness, it does not come back and does not produce disorders such as stiffness,

children.text: upekṣetaiva hi tato 'dhyuṣitaś ca niśāṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: one should simply disregard it. Then, after it has stayed overnight, he should drink

children.text: prātar nāgaradhānyāmbhaḥ koṣṇaṃ kevalam eva vā
children.translated_text: warm water with dry ginger and coriander in the morning, or simply warm water alone.

children.text: anvāsayet tṛtīye 'hni pañcame vā punaś ca tam ||
children.translated_text: One should administer <s>anuvāsana</s> to him again on the third or fifth day,
or according as the oil is digested. Therefore, for those whose <s>māruta</s> is extremely aggravated,
for those habituated to exercise, those with strong digestive fire, and those who are dry, it may be given every day.
Thus, when the channels have been cleansed by three or four oil administrations and the body is oleated,

children.text: nirūhaṃ śodhanaṃ yuñjyād asnigdhe snehanaṃ tanoḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should apply a purifying <s>nirūha</s>; in one not oleated, oleation of the body is required.

children.text: pañcame 'tha tṛtīye vā divase sādhake śubhe
children.translated_text: Then on the fifth or the third day, on a successful and auspicious day,
At midday, when the sun has turned somewhat, after the offering and auspicious rites have been performed,
having examined a person who has been anointed, sudated, and freed of waste, and who is not excessively hungry,
and having carefully considered the person, the <s>doṣa</s>, the medicine, and the other factors,

children.text: vastiṃ prakalpayed vaidyas tadvidyair bahubhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: the physician, together with many who know that science, should prepare the <s>vasti</s> (medicated enema).
He should decoct twenty <s>palas</s> of the substance and eight fruits.

children.text: tataḥ kvāthāc caturthāṃśaṃ snehaṃ vāte prakalpayet
children.translated_text: Then, from that decoction, he should prescribe fat amounting to one fourth in a case of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: pitte svasthe ca ṣaṣṭhāṃśam aṣṭamāṃśaṃ kaphe 'dhike ||
children.translated_text: In <s>pitta</s>, and in a healthy person, it should be one sixth; when <s>kapha</s> is excessive, one eighth.

children.text: sarvatra cāṣṭamaṃ bhāgaṃ kalkād bhavati vā yathā
children.translated_text: In every case the paste is an eighth part, or otherwise as needed,
so that the <s>vasti</s> is neither too thin nor too thick; and there should be one <s>pala</s> of jaggery.

children.text: madhupaṭvādiśeṣaṃ ca yuktyā sarvaṃ tad ekataḥ
children.translated_text: The remaining ingredients, beginning with honey and salt, should all be combined according to judgment.
Warmed by the steam of a pot of hot water and beaten together with a churner,
it should be put into the <s>vasti</s> bladder and introduced into the anus, being neither too hot nor too cold,

children.text: nātisnigdhaṃ na vā rūkṣaṃ nātitīkṣṇaṃ na vā mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: neither too unctuous nor dry, neither too sharp nor mild,
neither too thin nor too thick, neither deficient nor excessive in quantity, neither bland nor too salty.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ tadvad amlaṃ ca paṭhanty anye tu tadvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Other experts also teach the same rule regarding sourness.
One should make the dose three <s>palas</s> each for the fat and the honey,
half a <s>karṣa</s> of <s>māṇimantha</s>, and, in a healthy person, two <s>palas</s> of paste.
For all the remaining liquids one should prescribe ten <s>palas</s>.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ lavaṇaṃ snehaṃ kalkaṃ kvātham iti kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Honey, salt, fat, paste, and decoction, in that order,
should be poured in for <s>nirūha</s> enemas; this is the rule for compounding them.

children.text: uttāno dattamātre tu nirūhe tanmanā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after the <s>nirūha</s> has been given, the patient should lie supine and keep his mind on it.
With a pillow placed under him, and when the urge has arisen, he should evacuate while squatting.

children.text: āgatau paramaḥ kālo muhūrto mṛtyave param ||
children.translated_text: For its return, the utmost time is one <s>muhūrta</s>; beyond that limit it may lead to death.
In that case one should prepare an enema that promotes downward movement, made with fat, alkali, urine, and sour substances,
and quickly administer another <s>vasti</s>, unctuous, sharp, and hot.
Or one should prescribe a fruit suppository, fomentation, frightening, and similar measures.

children.text: svayam eva nivṛtte tu dvitīyo vastir iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: But when it has returned by itself, a second <s>vasti</s> is desired.
A third and even a fourth may be given, or as many as are needed until there is good <s>nirūha</s> evacuation.

children.text: viriktavac ca yogādīn vidyād yoge tu bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: As with a purged patient, one should know the proper and other effects; when the effect is proper, one should feed him,
after he has bathed in warm water, with thin rice and meat soup of dry-land animals.

children.text: vikārā ye nirūḍhasya bhavanti pracalair malaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The disorders that arise in one treated with <s>nirūha</s>, because the wastes have been stirred up,
come to rest when he has been sprinkled with pleasantly warm water and has eaten.
Then, if he is again afflicted by <s>vāta</s>, he should at once be given an <s>anuvāsana</s> enema.
Its proper, deficient, and excessive effects are like those of a person who has drunk <s>sneha</s> (fat).

children.text: kiñcitkālaṃ sthito yaś ca sapurīṣo nivartate ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>sneha</s> remains for a short time and then returns together with feces,
with the wind moving downward, that is a successful <s>anuvāsana</s>.

children.text: ekaṃ trīn vā balāse tu snehavastīn prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: In <s>balāsa</s> conditions one should prescribe one or three unctuous enemas,

children.text: pañca vā sapta vā pitte navaikādaśa vānile
children.translated_text: five or seven in <s>pitta</s>, and nine or eleven in <s>anila</s>.

children.text: punas tato 'py ayugmāṃs tu punar āsthāpanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, after these, one should use odd numbers; after that comes <s>āsthāpana</s>.
For <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>anila</s>, the food should be taken respectively with pulse soup, milk, and meat soup.
For <s>anila</s>, a single unctuous <s>vasti</s>, joined with a decoction of <s>vāta</s>-subduing drugs, <s>trivṛt</s>, and rock salt,
should be sweet, sour, hot, and accompanied by meat soup.
For <s>pitta</s>, two preparations, with decoctions of the <s>nyagrodhādi</s> group and with the <s>padmakādi</s> group and sugar,
should be sweet and cold, with ghee, milk, sugarcane juice, and honey.
For <s>kapha</s>, three preparations, with decoction of the <s>āragvadhādi</s> group and with the <s>vatsakādi</s> group,
should be dry, with honey and cow urine, sharp, hot, and pungent.

children.text: trayas te saṃnipāte 'pi doṣān ghnanti yataḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: These three also destroy the <s>doṣas</s> in <s>saṃnipāta</s>, because they act on them in sequence.

children.text: tribhyaḥ paraṃ vastim ato necchanty anye cikitsakāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore some physicians do not approve a <s>vasti</s> beyond three.

children.text: na hi doṣaś caturtho 'sti punar dīyeta yaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: For there is no fourth <s>doṣa</s> in relation to which another would be given.
One should devise <s>vasti</s> in three ways: for stirring up, for purifying,

children.text: tridhaiva kalpayed vastim ity anye 'pi pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: and, in order, for pacifying the <s>doṣas</s>; so others also declare.
All this should be measured according to the strength of the <s>doṣa</s>, the medicine, and the other factors.
But one should not discontinue treatment without considering the signs of proper <s>nirūha</s>.

children.text: prāk sneha ekaḥ pañcānte dvādaśāsthāpanāni ca
children.translated_text: One unctuous enema comes first, five at the end, and twelve <s>āsthāpana</s> enemas,
together with their <s>anuvāsana</s> enemas; this course is said to comprise thirty <s>vastis</s>.

children.text: kālaḥ pañcadaśaiko 'tra prāk sneho 'nte trayas tathā
children.translated_text: In the <s>kāla</s> course there are fifteen: one preliminary unctuous enema, and three likewise at the end.
Six are interposed among five <s>vastis</s>; in the <s>yoga</s> course, however, there are eight <s>vastis</s>.

children.text: trayo nirūhāḥ snehāś ca snehāv ādyantayor ubhau
children.translated_text: There are three <s>nirūhas</s> and unctuous enemas, with two unctuous enemas at the beginning and the end.
One should not make a habit of only an unctuous enema or only a <s>nirūha</s>.
From unctuous enemas come excitation and injury to the digestive fire; from <s>nirūhas</s> there is danger from <s>marut</s> (wind).

children.text: tasmān nirūḍhaḥ snehyaḥ syān nirūhyaś cānuvāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one who has received <s>nirūha</s> should be oleated, and one who has received <s>anuvāsana</s> should be treated with <s>nirūha</s>.
Thus, by the method of oleation and purification, <s>vasti</s> therapy conquers all three <s>doṣas</s>.
A <s>sneha</s> administered in the small dose used for drinking fat

children.text: mātrāvastiḥ smṛtaḥ snehaḥ śīlanīyaḥ sadā ca saḥ
children.translated_text: is regarded as a <s>mātrāvasti</s>; it should always be practiced.
It may be regularly used by children, the aged, travelers, load-bearers, women, and those attached to exertion and anxious thought,
by those broken by <s>vāta</s>, the weak, those of little digestive fire, and by kings, lords, and people accustomed to comfort.
It destroys <s>doṣas</s>, requires no strict regimen, strengthens, releases stool, and is easy.
In diseases of the bladder and in disorders of women affecting the vagina, womb, and uterus,
after purification by two or three <s>āsthāpana</s> enemas, one should administer an <s>uttaravasti</s>.
Measured by the patient's own fingers, its nozzle should be twelve finger-breadths long,
round, like a cow's tail, and furnished with raised rims at the base and middle,
with a tip admitting a mustard seed, smooth, and made of gold or the like,
firm, and resembling the stalks of <s>kunda</s>, <s>aśvamāra</s>, and <s>sumanas</s> flowers.

children.text: tasya vastir mṛdulaghur mātrā śuktir vikalpya vā
children.translated_text: Its bladder should be soft and light; the dose may be a <s>śukti</s>, or otherwise as determined.
Then, for this patient after he has bathed and eaten, according to the procedure for an unctuous <s>vasti</s>,
For one sitting straight and comfortably on a soft seat level with the knees,

children.text: hṛṣṭe meḍhre sthite carjau śanaiḥ srotoviśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: when the penis is stimulated and held straight, for the purification of the channels,

children.text: sūkṣmāṃ śalākāṃ praṇayet tayā śuddhe anusevani
children.translated_text: one should slowly introduce a fine probe; when it has been cleared by that, along the perineal seam,

children.text: āmehanāntaṃ netraṃ ca niṣkampaṃ gudavat tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the nozzle should be inserted up to the end of the urinary passage, steadily, as in the anus. Then,
when the oil within has been pressed in, the procedure of an oil enema is beneficial.

children.text: vastīn anena vidhinā dadyāt trīṃś caturo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: By this method one should administer three or even four <s>bastis</s>.
All the remaining procedure for it should be considered just as for an <s>anuvāsana</s> enema.

children.text: strīṇām ārtavakāle tu yonir gṛhṇāty apāvṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: For women, however, at the time of menstruation the vagina receives it because it is open.

children.text: vidadhīta tadā tasmād anṛtāv api cātyaye
children.translated_text: Therefore one should administer it then, and also outside the menstrual season in an emergency,
in prolapse and pains of the vagina, in vaginal disorders, and in excessive uterine bleeding.
A nozzle ten finger-breadths long, admitting a mung bean, should be inserted four finger-breadths
in the passage for offspring, and two finger-breadths in the urinary passage.
In disorders of difficult urination, for children it should be one finger-breadth.

children.text: prakuñco madhyamā mātrā bālānāṃ śuktir eva tu ||
children.translated_text: A <s>prakuñca</s> is the middle dose; for children it is only a <s>śukti</s>.
For a woman lying on her back, after properly contracting the thighs,
with the knees raised, one should apply three or four <s>bastis</s> in a day and night.

children.text: vastīṃs trirātram evaṃ ca snehamātrāṃ vivardhayan
children.translated_text: Thus for three nights, increasing the measure of oil,

children.text: tryaham eva ca viśramya praṇidadhyāt punas tryaham ||
children.translated_text: and after resting for three days, one should again administer it for three days.

children.text: pakṣād vireko vamite tataḥ pakṣān nirūhaṇam
children.translated_text: After a fortnight, purgation is given; after emesis, then after fortnights, a decoction enema is given.
One just treated with a decoction enema should receive an oil enema, and one purged should receive it after seven nights.

children.text: yathā kusumbhādiyutāt toyād rāgaṃ haret paṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as cloth removes color from water mixed with safflower and the like,

children.text: tathā dravīkṛtād dehād vastir nirharate malān ||
children.translated_text: so <s>basti</s> draws out impurities from the body when they have been liquefied.

children.text: śākhāgatāḥ koṣṭhagatāś ca rogā marmordhvasarvāvayavāṅgajāś ca
children.translated_text: Diseases located in the branches and located in the bowel, and those arising in vital spots, above the clavicles, or in all the limbs,

children.text: ye santi teṣāṃ na tu kaścid anyo vāyoḥ paraṃ janmani hetur asti ||
children.translated_text: whatever they are, have no cause in their origin greater than <s>vāyu</s>.
Because it brings about the dispersal and gathering of accumulations of feces, phlegm, bile, and other impurities,

children.text: tasyātivṛddhasya śamāya nānyad vaster vinā bheṣajam asti kiñcit ||
children.translated_text: there is no medicine at all, apart from <s>basti</s>, for pacifying that <s>vāyu</s> when it has greatly increased.

children.text: tasmāc cikitsārdha iti pradiṣṭaḥ kṛtsnā cikitsāpi ca vastir ekaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore it is taught as half of treatment; and some hold <s>basti</s> alone to be the whole of treatment,
just as venesection is also so, since it acts as the medicine for blood causing internal and external disorders.
For disorders above the clavicles, <s>nasya</s> is especially approved,

children.text: nāsā hi śiraso dvāraṃ tena tad vyāpya hanti tān ||
children.translated_text: for the nose is the gateway of the head; by that route it pervades it and destroys those disorders.

children.text: virecanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ ca śamanaṃ ca tridhāpi tat
children.translated_text: It is threefold: purgative, nourishing, and pacifying.
Purgative <s>nasya</s> is for headache, heaviness, discharge, and diseases of the throat,
for swelling, goiter, worms, tumors, skin disease, epilepsy, and coryza.
Nourishing <s>nasya</s> is for pain caused by <s>vāta</s>, migraine, and loss of voice,
for dryness of the nose and mouth, obstruction of speech, difficult awakening, and <s>avabāhuka</s>.
Pacifying <s>nasya</s> is for bluish discoloration, facial blemishes, disorders of the hair, and streaks in the eyes.

children.text: yathāsvaṃ yaugikaiḥ snehair yathāsvaṃ ca prasādhitaiḥ
children.translated_text: According to each case, with suitable oils prepared appropriately,
and with pastes, decoctions, and the like, and also with honey, salt, and fermented preparations, the first is to be applied.
The nourishing kind should also be applied with the juice of meat from arid-land animals, with blood, with <s>kha-pura</s>, and the like.

children.text: śamanaṃ yojayet pūrvaiḥ kṣīreṇa salilena vā ||
children.translated_text: The pacifying kind should be applied with the former substances, or with milk or water.

children.text: marśaś ca pratimarśaś ca dvidhā sneho 'tra mātrayā
children.translated_text: Here oily <s>nasya</s> is of two kinds by quantity: <s>marśa</s> and <s>pratimarśa</s>.

children.text: kalkādyair avapīḍas tu sa tīkṣṇair mūrdharecanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But <s>avapīḍa</s>, made with pastes and the like, when sharp, is a purgation of the head.
Insufflation is purgative powder; one should apply it with the breath from the mouth,
through a tube six finger-breadths long, open at both ends and filled with the medicine.

children.text: sa hi bhūritaraṃ doṣaṃ cūrṇatvād apakarṣati
children.translated_text: Because it is in powder form, it draws out a much larger quantity of <s>doṣa</s>.
From a drop that falls after dipping and lifting up two joints of the index finger,

children.text: yāvat patatyasau bindur daśāṣṭau ṣaṭ krameṇa te
children.translated_text: the measures for <s>marśa</s>, in order as superior, middle, and inferior, are ten, eight, and six such drops.

children.text: marśasyotkṛṣṭamadhyonā mātrās tā eva ca kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Those same measures, in that order, are the superior, middle, and inferior doses of <s>marśa</s>.

children.text: bindudvayonāḥ kalkāder yojayen na tu nāvanam
children.translated_text: For paste and similar preparations one should use two drops fewer; but nasal instillation should not be applied
to those who have drunk water, liquor, poison, or oil, or who wish to drink,
to those who have eaten, have bathed the head, wish to bathe, or have had bloodletting,
to those with recent coryza, those afflicted by natural urges, women recently delivered, and those with dyspnea or cough,
to those who have undergone purification, to those who have been given <s>basti</s>, and likewise in an unseasonable or bad day,
except in an urgent disease. Now one should apply <s>nasya</s>

children.text: prātaḥ śleṣmaṇi madhyāhne pitte sāyaṃ niśoścale
children.translated_text: in the morning when <s>kapha</s> predominates, at midday when <s>pitta</s> predominates, and in the evening or at night when <s>vāta</s> predominates.
In a regimen for health, however, it is used in the forenoon in autumn and spring,

children.text: śīte madhyaṃdine grīṣme sāyaṃ varṣāsu sātape
children.translated_text: at midday in the cold season, in the evening in summer, and when there is sunlight in the rains.
When the head is overcome by <s>vāta</s>, in hiccup, in <s>apatānaka</s>,

children.text: manyāstambhe svarabhraṃśe sāyaṃ prātar dine dine
children.translated_text: in stiffness of the neck and loss of voice, it should be done evening and morning every day;

children.text: ekāhāntaram anyatra saptāhaṃ ca tad ācaret ||
children.translated_text: elsewhere every other day, and it should be carried out for a week.
For one whose head has been oiled and fomented and who has first completed the necessary acts,
lying in a windless place, one should again foment the region above the clavicles.
Then, with the body supine and straight and the hands and feet extended,
with the feet slightly raised and the head slightly lowered,
one should close one nostril and pour into the other alternately,
using medicine warmed in hot water, through a tube or with a cotton swab.
When it has been administered, one should massage the soles of the feet, shoulders, hands, ears, and other parts.

children.text: śanair ucchidya niṣṭhīvet pārśvayor ubhayos tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The patient should slowly loosen and spit it out, then on both sides.

children.text: ā bheṣajakṣayād evaṃ dvis trir vā nasyam ācaret
children.translated_text: Thus, until the medicine is exhausted, one should perform <s>nasya</s> two or three times.
In fainting, one should sprinkle with cold water, avoiding the head.
At the end of purgative <s>nasya</s>, oil should be given with regard to the <s>doṣas</s> and other factors.

children.text: nasyānte vākśataṃ tiṣṭhed uttāno dhārayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of <s>nasya</s>, one should remain supine for the time of one hundred words, and then hold
smoke, after inhaling it, and lukewarm-water mouthfuls for cleansing the throat.
When properly oleated, there is easy breathing, sleep, waking, and acuity of the senses.
When it is too dry, there is stiffness of the eyes, dryness, and a feeling of emptiness in the nose, mouth, and head.
When it is too oily, there are excessive itching, heaviness, salivation, dislike of food, and coryza.
When it has purged well, there are lightness of the eyes and purity of the mouth and voice.
When it has purged badly, the disease increases; when it has purged excessively, there is emaciation.
<s>Pratimarsha</s> should be used for the wounded, the emaciated, children, the old, and people of delicate constitution.
It may be used even in unseasonable weather and rain, but it is not approved in severe coryza.
Nor is it approved when liquor has been drunk, when the hearing is weak, when the head is polluted by worms,
or when the <s>doṣas</s> are excessive and already stirred up, for it is given in a small dose.
After sleep at night, after the day's meal, after vomiting, daytime sleep, travel, fatigue, and sexual intercourse,
after oiling the head, gargling, urination, collyrium, and defecation,
and after tooth-cleaning and laughing, this two-drop <s>pratimarsha</s> should be applied.

children.text: pañcasu srotasāṃ śuddhiḥ klamanāśas triṣu kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In five applications there is cleansing of the channels; in three, removal of fatigue, successively.
In five there is strength of sight; after that come firmness of the teeth and pacification of <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Nasya</s> is not to be given to one under seven years old or beyond eighty years.
Smoke is not for one under eighteen, and a mouthful rinse is not for one under five.
Purification is not for one under ten, nor for one who has passed seventy.
But <s>pratimarsha</s>, like <s>basti</s>, is commended from birth until death.

children.text: marśavacca guṇān kuryāt sa hi nityopasevanāt ||
children.translated_text: It produces the benefits of <s>marsha</s>, because it is used constantly.

children.text: na cātra yantraṇā nāpi vyāpadbhyo marśavad bhayam
children.translated_text: And here there is no strict restraint, nor any fear of complications as there is with <s>marsha</s>.

children.text: tailam eva ca nasyārthe nityābhyāsena śasyate ||
children.translated_text: For the purpose of <s>nasya</s>, only oil is recommended for daily practice.
Because the head is the seat of <s>kapha</s>, other fats are not recommended for a healthy person.
If, in <s>marsha</s> and <s>pratimarsha</s>, there were no distinction of acting quickly or slowly,

children.text: marśe ca pratimarśe ca viśeṣo na bhaved yadi
children.translated_text: nor superiority or inferiority in their qualities,

children.text: ko marśaṃ saparīhāraṃ sāpadaṃ ca bhajet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then who would resort to <s>marsha</s>, with its restrictions and its dangers?
In the same way one should explain what are called <s>acchapāna</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, and staying in a hut, in wind, or in sun,
and also <s>anuvāsana-basti</s> and <s>mātrā-basti</s>.
In the sixfold <s>nasya</s> procedure, one should eat <s>śāli</s> rice and barley with soups made from <s>paṭola</s>, mung beans, eggplant, small radish,
and meat of animals from arid lands.
One should decoct <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>jalada</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, <s>jalada</s>, bark, <s>sevya</s>, <s>gopī</s>, <s>hima</s>,
<s>dārvī</s> bark, licorice, <s>plava</s>, <s>aguru</s>, <s>varī</s>, the plant called <s>puṇḍra</s>, bilva, and lotus,

children.text: dhāvanyau surabhiṃ sthire kṛmiharaṃ pattraṃ truṭīṃ reṇukām
children.translated_text: the two <s>dhāvanī</s>s, <s>surabhi</s>, the two <s>sthirā</s>s, <s>kṛmihara</s>, leaf, <s>truṭi</s>, <s>reṇukā</s>,

children.text: kiñjalkaṃ kamalād balāṃ śataguṇe divye 'mbhasi kvāthayet ||
children.translated_text: lotus filament, and <s>balā</s>, in one hundred times as much pure water.

children.text: tailād rasaṃ daśaguṇaṃ pariśeṣya tena tailaṃ paceta salilena daśaiva vārān
children.translated_text: Leaving a decoction ten times the quantity of the oil, one should cook the oil with it, and then ten times again with water.

children.text: pāke kṣipecca daśame samam ājadugdhaṃ nasyaṃ mahāguṇam uśantyaṇutailam etat ||
children.translated_text: At the tenth cooking one should add an equal quantity of goat's milk; physicians consider this <s>aṇutaila</s> a nasal medicine of great virtue.
Those habituated to <s>nasya</s> become firm and full, with clear skin on the shoulders, neck, face, and chest,
with strong senses, and without premature gray hair.
To prevent the arising of disorders above the clavicles produced by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,

children.text: ucchedāya ca jātānāṃ pibed dhūmaṃ sadātmavān ||
children.translated_text: and to eradicate them when they have arisen, a self-controlled person should always drink smoke.

children.text: snigdho madhyaḥ sa tīkṣṇaśca vāte vātakaphe kaphe
children.translated_text: It is oily, moderate, and sharp; it should be applied for <s>vāta</s>, for <s>vāta-kapha</s>, and for <s>kapha</s> respectively.
It is not to be used for those afflicted by <s>raktapitta</s>, those who have been purged, or those with abdominal disease or urinary disorder.
Nor for those with <s>timira</s>, upward-moving wind, distension, <s>rohiṇī</s>, or those who have been given <s>basti</s>,
nor for those who have eaten fish, liquor, curds, milk, honey, fat, or poison.
Nor when the head has been injured, in pallor-disease, or after staying awake at night.
Smoke taken at a wrong time or in excess causes <s>raktapitta</s>, blindness, deafness, thirst, fainting, intoxication, and delusion.

children.text: dhūmo 'kāle 'tipīto vā tatra śīto vidhir hitaḥ
children.translated_text: In that case a cooling regimen is beneficial.
After sneezing, yawning, defecation, urination, sexual intercourse, and surgical operation,

children.text: hāsasya dantakāṣṭhasya dhūmam ante piben mṛdum
children.translated_text: and after laughing and tooth-cleaning, one should drink mild smoke at the end.
At these times, and after night-sleep, food, and nasal instillation, one should drink the moderate kind.
After sleep, <s>nasya</s>, collyrium, bathing, and vomiting, one should drink purgative smoke.
One should make the smoking tube straight, of the same material as a <s>basti</s> nozzle, and with three chambers.
Its root and tip should admit a thumb and a jujube-stone respectively.
For the sharp, oleating, and moderate kinds, respectively,
its measure should be three, four, and five sets of eight finger-breadths, according to the smoker's own measure.
Sitting upright, intent on it, with the mouth open, one should use it in three rounds.

children.text: pidhāya chidram ekaikaṃ dhūmaṃ nāsikayā pibet
children.translated_text: Closing one nostril at a time, one should drink the smoke through the nose.
When a <s>doṣa</s> lodged in the nose and head is stirred up, one should first drink it through the nose,
but for the purpose of stirring it up through the mouth; the reverse is done when it is in the throat.
One should expel the smoke only through the mouth; through the nose it harms the sight.

children.text: ākṣepamokṣaiḥ pātavyo dhūmas tu tris tribhis tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: The smoke should be drunk by drawing in and releasing, three times in each of three rounds.

children.text: ahnaḥ pibet sakṛt snigdhaṃ dvir madhyaṃ śodhanaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: In a day one should drink the oily smoke once, the moderate smoke twice, and the purifying smoke at most three or four times when it is mild.

children.text: triścatur vā mṛdau tatra dravyāṇyaguru guggulu
children.translated_text: There the substances are <s>aguru</s>, guggulu, <s>musta</s>, <s>sthauṇeya</s>, <s>śaileya</s>, <s>nalada</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>vālaka</s>,
as ingredients for the unctuous preparation.
<s>Varāṅga</s>, <s>kauntī</s>, licorice, bilva pith, cardamom, sand,
<s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, resin of <s>sarja</s>, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, madana, and <s>plava</s>,

children.text: śallakī kuṅkumaṃ māṣā yavāḥ kundurukas tilāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>śallakī</s>, saffron, black gram, barley, kunduruka, and sesame,

children.text: snehaḥ phalānāṃ sārāṇāṃ medo majjā vasā ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the oil of fruits and piths, fat, marrow, muscle-fat, and ghee are also used.
For pacifying smoke, use <s>śallakī</s>, lac, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, lotus, blue lotus,
the barks of banyan, udumbara, aśvattha, plakṣa, and lodhra, and sugar,
licorice, <s>suvarṇatvak</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, and red licorice.
For the sharp smoke, use fragrant substances other than <s>kuṣṭha</s> and tagara, <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, turmeric,
the ten roots, <s>manohvā</s>, orpiment, lac, white-flowered plants, and the three fruits.
Sharp aromatic substances form the group for purgation of the head.
A reed twelve finger-breadths long should be kept in water for a day and night.
With the smoking medicines ground to a paste, one should coat it in this way five times.
The wick should become as thick as a thumb and barley-shaped in the middle.
That substance, dried in the shade, freed of its inner pith, and anointed with oil as appropriate,
should be used for drinking smoke after being placed in the smoking tube and singed by fire.
One should place a tube ten finger-breadths long in the opening of a covered pair of saucers.

children.text: kāsaḥ śvāsaḥ pīnaso visvaratvaṃ pūtir gandhaḥ pāṇḍutā keśadoṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Cough, dyspnea, coryza, hoarseness, foul smell, pallor, disorders of the hair,

children.text: karṇāsyākṣisrāvakaṇḍvartijāḍyaṃ tandrā hidhmā dhūmapaṃ na spṛśanti ||
children.translated_text: discharge from the ears, mouth, and eyes, itching, pain, dullness, drowsiness, and hiccup do not affect one who drinks smoke.
<s>Gaṇḍūṣa</s> (holding a mouthful) is of four kinds: oleating, pacifying, cleansing,
and healing. Among these, the first three are to be applied in the three conditions beginning with <s>vāta</s>.
The last removes wounds. Here the oleating kind is made with fats prepared with sweet, sour, and salty substances;
the pacifying kind is made with bitter, astringent, and sweet medicines.
The cleansing kind is made with bitter, pungent, sour, salty, and hot substances; the healing kind, again,
with astringent and bitter ones. In these, oil, milk, honey-water,

children.text: śuktaṃ madyaṃ raso mūtraṃ dhānyāmlaṃ ca yathāyatham
children.translated_text: sour ferment, wine, meat broth, urine, and sour grain-water are used as appropriate,

children.text: kalkair yuktaṃ vipakvaṃ vā yathāsparśaṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: mixed with pastes or cooked, according to the required contact.
In tooth sensitivity, looseness of the teeth, and oral disease caused by <s>vāta</s>,
lukewarm or cold water with sesame paste is beneficial.
For the regular holding of <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s>, oil or meat broth may be used.
In suppuration accompanied by heat and burning, in wounds arising from external causes,

children.text: viṣe kṣārāgnidagdhe ca sarpir dhāryaṃ payo 'thavā
children.translated_text: and in poisoning and burns from alkali or fire, ghee or milk should be held.
It quickly produces clarity and joins together wounds in the mouth.
Holding a honey <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s> pacifies burning and thirst.
Sour grain-water removes bad taste, impurity, and bad smell in the mouth.
That same liquid, without salt and cold, is supreme for removing dryness of the mouth.
A <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s> of alkaline water quickly breaks up an accumulation of <s>kapha</s>.
By mouthfuls of lukewarm water, lightness of the mouth is produced.
In a windless place, in sunlight, with shoulders and neck fomented and massaged,
one should hold the <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s> without swallowing, with the face slightly raised,
until the mouth is full of <s>kapha</s>, or until fluid flows from the nose and eyes.
Diseases of the neck, head, ears, mouth, and eyes, salivation, throat disorders, dryness of the mouth,
nausea, drowsiness, anorexia, and coryza are especially curable by taking <s>kavaḍa</s> (a mouthful for chewing or gargling).
Paste, thick extract, and powder: <s>pratisāraṇa</s> (rubbing in the mouth) is threefold.
One should use it in <s>kapha</s> disorders, with the medicines prescribed for <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s>.
Facial application is threefold: it removes <s>doṣas</s>, removes poison, and improves complexion.
A warm one is praised for <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>; in the remaining cases it should be extremely cold.
Its thickness has three measures: one quarter, one third, and one half of a finger-breadth.

children.text: aśuṣkasya sthitis tasya śuṣko dūṣayati chavim
children.translated_text: It should remain while not dry; when dry, it spoils the complexion.
One should moisten it and remove it, and afterwards perform an oil massage.
One should avoid sleeping by day, speaking, fire, sun, grief, and anger.
It is not to be applied in coryza, indigestion, after <s>nasya</s>, or in stiffness of the jaw,

children.text: arocake jāgarite sa tu hanti suyojitaḥ
children.translated_text: nor in anorexia or after staying awake. But when properly applied it destroys
untimely gray hair, blemishes, wrinkles, darkness, and bluish discoloration.
Kernels of <s>kola</s>, root of <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>śābara</s>, and white mustard,

children.text: siṃhīmūlaṃ tilāḥ kṛṣṇā dārvītvaṅ nistuṣā yavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: root of <s>siṃhī</s>, black sesame, bark of <s>dārvī</s>, and hulled barley,
roots of <s>darbha</s>, <s>hima</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>miśi</s>, and rice grains,
<s>kumuda</s>, <s>utpala</s>, <s>kalhāra</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>candana</s>,
<s>kālīyaka</s>, sesame, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>tagara</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
<s>tālīśa</s>, <s>gundrā</s>, <s>puṇḍrāhva</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, <s>nata</s>, and <s>aguru</s>:
thus six facial pastes, stated by half-verses, are remembered for the six seasons beginning with winter.
For those accustomed to facial application, the sight becomes firm,
and the face is unfaded, smooth, and like a lotus.
Oil for the head is fourfold: massage, pouring, an oil-soaked pad, and <s>basti</s>.
One should know it to have many benefits, increasing successively with each later form.
Among these, massage should be applied in dryness, itching, and impurity,
while pouring is used for <s>arūṃṣikā</s>, piercing pain of the head, burning, suppuration, and wounds.
The oil-soaked pad is used for falling hair, cracking, burning sensation,
and stiffness of the eyes; <s>basti</s> is used in numbness, facial paralysis, and sleeplessness,
in dryness of the nose and mouth, dimness of vision, and severe disease of the head.

children.text: vidhis tasya niṣaṇṇasya pīṭhe jānusame mṛdau
children.translated_text: Its procedure is as follows: the patient sits on a soft stool knee-high,
with the body cleansed, anointed, and fomented, at the end of the day. A cow or buffalo
leather band, twelve finger-breadths wide and fitted to the head,
should be fastened up to the level of the ear-joints, with the forehead wrapped in cloth.
Having bound it with a cloth braid, one should seal it with black-gram paste.

children.text: tato yathāvyādhi śṛtaṃ snehaṃ koṣṇaṃ niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should pour in warm fat cooked according to the disease.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ keśabhuvo yāvad aṅgulaṃ dhārayecca tam
children.translated_text: It should be held up to one finger-breadth above the roots of the hair,
until the mouth and nose become moist: for ten, eight, or six thousand <s>mātrās</s> in <s>vāta</s> and the following conditions,
and for one thousand when there is no pain. One should massage the shoulders and other parts.
For one from whom the oil has been released, the regimen lasts at most seven days.
One should hold a filling in the ear while massaging the root of the ear.

children.text: rujaḥ syān mārdavaṃ yāvan mātrāśatam avedane ||
children.translated_text: In pain, it is held until softness occurs; when there is no pain, for one hundred <s>mātrās</s>.
The measure called a <s>mātrā</s> is remembered as the time in which the fingertip

children.text: nimeṣonmeṣakālena samaṃ mātrā tu sā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: passes around the right kneecap, equal to the time of closing and opening the eyes.
Oil for the head conquers falling, whiteness, and tawny discoloration of the hair, splitting of the head, and disorders of <s>vāta</s>;
it produces clarity of the senses and strength of the voice, jaw, and head.
At the beginning of all eye diseases, <s>āścyotana</s> (eye drops) is beneficial.
It removes pain, pricking, itching, rubbing sensation, tears, burning, and redness.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ vāte kaphe koṣṇaṃ tacchītaṃ raktapittayoḥ
children.translated_text: It should be hot in <s>vāta</s>, warm in <s>kapha</s>, and cold in disorders of blood and <s>pitta</s>.
For one staying in a windless place, the eye should be opened with the left hand;
with the other hand, using a hanging cotton wick from a shell, at the small aperture of the eye,

children.text: daśa dvādaśa vā bindūn dvyaṅgulād avasecayet ||
children.translated_text: one should sprinkle ten or twelve drops from a distance of two finger-breadths.
Then, after wiping with a soft cloth, in disorders of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,
one should gently foment it with another cloth soaked in warm water.
Eye-sprinkling that is too hot and sharp causes pain, redness, and destruction of sight;
but if it is too cold, it produces piercing pain, stiffness, and aches,
astringency of the eyelids, rubbing, and great difficulty in opening the eye.
If it is too little, it causes increase of the disorder, irritation, and failure of proper discharge.
When a medicine placed in the eye has gone to the channels of the joints, head, nose, and mouth,
it turns away the upward-moving impurities from the eye.
Now <s>añjana</s> (collyrium) is to be used when the body has been purified and the impurity is located only in the eye,
when signs of maturity are present, marked by slight swelling, excessive itching, and sliminess,
when there is mild rubbing, tearing, and redness in the eye, and when the contamination is thick,
and when the eye is afflicted by <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, blood, and especially by <s>māruta</s>.
<s>Añjana</s> is threefold: scraping, healing, and clarifying the sight.
Among these, scraping collyrium is made with astringent, sour, pungent, and hot substances;
healing collyrium is made with bitter drugs, and clarifying collyrium with sweet and cooling ones.
When the eye has been scorched by sharp collyrium, that clarifying collyrium,
when applied, receives the name <s>pratyañjana</s> (counter-collyrium).
A rod ten finger-breadths long, thin in the middle and with bud-shaped tips,
is approved; for scraping it should be copper, for healing made of black iron,

children.text: aṅgulī ca suvarṇotthā rūpyajā ca prasādane ||
children.translated_text: and for clarifying, the finger, or one made of gold or silver, may be used.
Pellet, concentrated extract, and powder are exactly the three preparations of collyrium;

children.text: gurau madhye laghau doṣe tāṃ krameṇa prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: one should apply them respectively when the <s>doṣa</s> is heavy, moderate, and light.
For a pellet the measure is that of a <s>hareṇu</s> seed; for a concentrated extract, that of a <s>vella</s> seed.

children.text: tīkṣṇasya dviguṇaṃ tasya mṛdunaś cūrṇitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: For a sharp preparation that measure is doubled, and likewise for a mild powdered one.

children.text: dve śalāke tu tīkṣṇasya tisras taditarasya ca
children.translated_text: For a sharp powder two rod-measures are used, and for the other kind three.

children.text: niśi svapne na madhyāhne mlāne noṣṇagabhastibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should not be applied at night, during sleep, at midday, or when the eyes are faded by hot rays;
for <s>doṣas</s>, increased, oppressed, and liquefied, would become a cause of eye disease.

children.text: prātaḥ sāyaṃ ca tacchāntyai vyabhre 'rke 'to 'ñjayet sadā ||
children.translated_text: To calm them, therefore, one should always apply collyrium morning and evening, when the sky is cloudless and the sun is present.

children.text: vadantyanye tu na divā prayojyaṃ tīkṣṇam añjanam
children.translated_text: Others say, however, that sharp collyrium should not be applied by day,
because the eye, weakened by purgation, sinks when exposed to the sun.

children.text: svapnena rātrau kālasya saumyatvena ca tarpitā
children.translated_text: Nourished by sleep at night and by the gentleness of the time,

children.text: śītasātmyā dṛg āgneyī sthiratāṃ labhate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fiery eye, being accustomed to coolness, regains stability again.
But when <s>balāsa</s> is excessively aggravated, or in a disease requiring scraping,

children.text: kāmam ahnyapi nātyuṣṇe tīkṣṇam akṣṇi prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: one may apply sharp collyrium to the eye even by day, provided it is not excessively hot.

children.text: aśmano janma lohasya tata eva ca tīkṣṇatā
children.translated_text: Metal has its origin from stone, and from that very source comes its sharpness;
by that same means there is also injury to the radiance of the eye.

children.text: na rātrāvapi śīte 'ti netre tīkṣṇāñjanaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Even at night, in excessive cold, sharp collyrium is not beneficial for the eye;
it would fail to make the stagnant <s>doṣa</s> flow out and would produce itching, dullness, and the like.
One should not apply collyrium to one who is frightened, has vomited, has been purged, has eaten, or is troubled by natural urges,
nor to one who is angry, feverish, exhausted, suffering from eye or head pain, overcome by grief, or keeping vigil,
nor before the sun has been seen, after bathing the head, or after smoke or liquor has been taken,
nor in indigestion, after being heated by fire or sun, after sleeping by day, or when thirsty.
Collyrium that is too sharp, too mild, scanty, excessive, thin, thick, or rough,
or excessively cold or hot, should not be applied.
Then, half-closing the sight, one should slowly move it within;
when the eyelids have been anointed, one should move them slightly. In this way the collyrium
spreads quickly if sharp, and one should not open and close the eyes,

children.text: niṣpīḍanaṃ ca vartmabhyāṃ kṣālanaṃ vā samācaret ||
children.translated_text: nor squeeze the eyelids, nor wash them.
When the agitation from the medicine has passed and the eye is at ease,
then one should wash it with waters suitable to the disease, the <s>doṣa</s>, and the season.
The right eye should then be cleansed with the right thumb, the left with a cloth,
grasping the upper eyelid; the other eye should be cleansed with the left hand.
A <s>doṣa</s> from collyrium that reaches the eyelid would cause diseases; therefore, otherwise,

children.text: kaṇḍūjāḍye 'ñjanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ dhūmaṃ vā yojayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if there is itching or dullness, one should again apply sharp collyrium or smoke therapy.
When the eye is dim, stiff, dry, rough, or injured,
when it is afflicted by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, distorted, with fallen eyelashes or clouded vision,
and when it is affected by difficult opening, vascular irritation, vascular eruption, darkness, or <s>arjuna</s>,
or by <s>syanda</s>, <s>mantha</s>, <s>anyatovāta</s>, <s>vātaparyāya</s>, or <s>śukra</s>,
and when redness, tears, pain, inflammation, and contamination have subsided in the diseased eye,
<s>tarpaṇa</s> should be applied in a windless place, after the head and body have been purified.
In a moderate season, in the morning or evening, while the patient lies supine,
one should make around the eye socket an even rim of barley and black-gram flour,

children.text: dvyaṅguloccāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kṛtvā yathāsvaṃ siddham āvapet
children.translated_text: two finger-breadths high and firm, and pour in ghee prepared as appropriate,
melted in hot water, while the eyes are closed.
In night-blindness, <s>vāta</s>, <s>timira</s>, difficult awakening, and similar conditions, one should use animal fat,

children.text: ā pakṣmāgrād athonmeṣaṃ śanakais tasya kurvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: up to the tips of the eyelashes; then, as the patient slowly opens the eyes,
one should count the measures there: for disease of the eyelid, the junction, the white, the black,

children.text: dṛṣṭau ca kramaśo vyādhau śataṃ trīṇi ca pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: and the sight, respectively, one hundred, three hundred, and five hundred,

children.text: śatāni sapta cāṣṭau ca daśa manthe daśānile
children.translated_text: seven hundred, eight hundred, and ten hundred for <s>mantha</s>; ten hundred also for <s>anila</s>.

children.text: pitte ṣaṭ svasthavṛtte ca balāse pañca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: In <s>pitta</s> one should retain it for six hundred measures, and in a healthy regimen and in <s>balāsa</s> for five hundred.

children.text: kṛtvāpāṅge tato dvāraṃ snehaṃ pātre nigālayet
children.translated_text: Then, making an opening at the outer corner, one should drain the unctuous substance into a vessel,

children.text: pibecca dhūmaṃ nekṣeta vyoma rūpaṃ ca bhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: and the patient should drink smoke; he should not look at the sky or at a bright object.

children.text: itthaṃ pratidinaṃ vāyau pitte tvekāntaraṃ kaphe
children.translated_text: Thus it is to be done daily in <s>vāyu</s> disorders, every other day in <s>pitta</s>, and in <s>kapha</s>...

children.text: svasthe tu dvyantaraṃ dadyād ā tṛpter iti yojayet ||
children.translated_text: For a healthy person, however, one should give it with an interval of two days, and continue it until satisfaction is reached.
Capacity to bear light, normal condition, and a clear, light eye
are the signs of satisfaction; when unsatisfied the opposite occurs, and when over-satisfied there are disorders arising from <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: snehapītā tanur iva klāntā dṛṣṭir hi sīdati
children.translated_text: For vision that has taken in too much unction droops, weary like the body.
Therefore, after <s>tarpaṇa</s>, one should employ <s>puṭapāka</s>, which gives strength to the sight,
in those very ocular disorders stated before.

children.text: sa vāte snehanaḥ śleṣmasahite lekhano hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a <s>vāta</s> condition it is oleating; when <s>kapha</s> is also present, the scraping kind is beneficial.
For weakness of sight, and when <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, or blood is involved, and for a healthy person, the clarifying kind is used.
With the flesh, fat, marrow, and grease of ground-dwelling, predatory, and marshland animals,
ground with milk and with life-promoting drugs, one should prepare the oleating kind.
With the liver and flesh of wild animals and birds, pearl, iron, copper, and rock salt,
with <s>srotoja</s>, conch, sea-foam, and similar substances ground with whey, one prepares the scraping kind.
With the liver, marrow, fat, entrails, heart, and flesh of wild animals and birds,
with sweet drugs and ghee, ground with breast milk and cow's milk, one prepares the clarifying kind.
A separate lump, the size of a <s>bilva</s> fruit, should be made from each of the meat paste and the medicinal paste.
For the oleating and other kinds in sequence, it should be wrapped in leaves of castor, banyan, and lotus,
smeared with clay, and cooked with blazing cow-dung fuel from <s>dhava</s> and <s>dhanvana</s> wood,

children.text: pacet pradīptair agnyābhaṃ pakvaṃ niṣpīḍya tadrasam
children.translated_text: until it has the appearance of fire; when cooked, one should press out its juice,

children.text: netre tarpaṇavad yuñjyācchataṃ dve trīṇi dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: apply it to the eyes as in <s>tarpaṇa</s>, and retain it for one hundred, two hundred, or three hundred counts.
In the scraping, oleating, and final kinds, the first two should be lukewarm and the last cold.

children.text: dhūmapo 'nte tayor eva yogās tatra ca tṛptivat ||
children.translated_text: At the end, inhalation of smoke is for those two alone; the regimen there is as in proper satisfaction.

children.text: tarpaṇaṃ puṭapākaṃ ca nasyānarhe na yojayet
children.translated_text: One should not apply <s>tarpaṇa</s> or <s>puṭapāka</s> to a person unfit for <s>nasya</s>.
For twice as many days as one applies it, the patient should follow a wholesome regimen.
With the eyes bound with <s>mālatī</s> and <s>mallikā</s> flowers, he should spend the night.
By every means one should strive for the strength of the eyes through <s>nasya</s>, <s>añjana</s>, <s>tarpaṇa</s>, and the like;

children.text: dṛṣṭiś ca naṣṭā vividhaṃ jagacca tamomayaṃ jāyata ekarūpam ||
children.translated_text: for when sight is lost, the manifold world becomes one uniform mass of darkness.
That by which various kinds of foreign bodies, revealed in various locations,

children.text: āhartum abhyupāyo yastad yantraṃ yacca darśane ||
children.translated_text: can be extracted, and which serves for seeing them, is called a <s>yantra</s> (instrument).
In the application of knife, alkali, and fire to piles, fistula, and similar conditions,
in protecting the remaining limbs, and likewise in procedures such as <s>basti</s>,
there are <s>ghaṭikā</s>, gourd, horn, <s>jāmbavauṣṭha</s>, and other such instruments;
therefore instruments are varied, with many forms and many functions.

children.text: vikalpya kalpayet buddhyā yathāsthūlaṃ tu vakṣyate
children.translated_text: One should design and fashion them with intelligence; but they will now be described in general terms.
One should make the mouths of instruments like the mouths of animals and birds such as the heron, lion, bear, and crow,

children.text: mukhair mukhāni yantrāṇāṃ kuryāt tatsaṃjñakāni ca
children.translated_text: and should give them names corresponding to those forms.
They are, for the most part, made of iron and eighteen finger-breadths long,
with tips ending in the shape of a lentil, and fastened at the neck with rivets.
One should know these as <s>svastika-yantra</s> instruments, bent like hooks at the base.
With those firm instruments, extraction of foreign bodies attached to bone is intended.
The two <s>saṃdaṃśa</s> forceps, with tips either rivet-fastened or free, are sixteen finger-breadths long,
for drawing out foreign bodies lodged in skin, vessels, sinews, or flesh.
Another, six finger-breadths long, is for removing minute foreign bodies and eyelashes.
The <s>mucuṇḍī</s> has very fine teeth and is ornamented at the base with a <s>rucaka</s> form;
it is for deep wounds, flesh, and the remaining part of an <s>arma</s> growth.
Two instruments, each twelve finger-breadths long, with one or two plates like a fish's palate,
are remembered as palate instruments, for removing foreign bodies from the ear canal.
Tubular instruments are hollow, with one opening or several openings,
for seeing foreign bodies and diseases situated in channels,
for making procedures easy, and also for suction.
Their breadth, circumference, and length should correspond to the channel.
A tube ten finger-breadths long, with half that circumference, is for viewing a foreign body inside the throat.
A tube with five mouth-openings is for grasping the four-eared <s>vāraṅga</s>;
for the two-eared <s>vāraṅga</s>, one with three holes should be made according to that measure,
in accordance with the shape, circumference, and length of the <s>vāraṅga</s> ears.

children.text: nāḍīr evaṃvidhāś cānyā draṣṭuṃ śalyāni kārayet
children.translated_text: One should have other tubes of this kind made for seeing foreign bodies.
A twelve-finger tube, resembling a lotus seed-vessel at the top,
and having four openings, is regarded as a foreign-body dislodger.
For piles, there is an instrument shaped like a cow's teat, four finger-breadths long;
in circumference it is five finger-breadths for men and six for women.

children.text: dvicchidraṃ darśane vyādher ekacchidraṃ tu karmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: It has two openings for seeing the disease, but one opening for the operation.
In its middle is a three-finger aperture, as wide as the belly of the thumb,
and above it a raised circular rim half a finger high.
A similar instrument without a hole, called <s>śamyā</s>, is for pressing piles.
In fistula, one should by all means remove the lip above the opening.
For nasal tumors and piles, there is a one-holed tube two finger-breadths long,
with the circumference of the index finger, like the fistula instrument.
A finger-guard, toothed and made of horn or wood, is four finger-breadths long;
with two holes and shaped like a cow's teat, it is convenient for opening the mouth.
For inspecting wounds of the vagina, there is a hollow instrument in the middle, sixteen finger-breadths long,
secured with a ring, four-walled, and with a mouth like a lotus bud.

children.text: catuḥśalākam ākrāntaṃ mūle tad vikasen mukhe
children.translated_text: When it is pressed by four rods at the base, it opens out at the mouth.
For an instrument six finger-breadths long for anointing and washing tubular wounds,
it is shaped like a <s>basti-yantra</s> at the base, and at the mouth like a thumb or pea,
without a rim at the front, with soft leather fastened at the base.
For fluid in the abdomen, there is a two-doored tube, or else a feather-tube.
Instruments for smoke, <s>basti</s>, and the like have been described as appropriate.
The <s>śṛṅga</s> (horn instrument) should have a mouth three finger-breadths wide; for suction it should be eighteen finger-breadths long.
At its tip it should have a hole the size of a mustard seed, be well bound, and be shaped like a nipple.
The <s>alābu</s> (gourd instrument) should be twelve finger-breadths long, while its circumference is eighteen finger-breadths.
Its round mouth is three or four finger-breadths wide; heated inside, it removes <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and blood.

children.text: tadvad ghaṭī hitā gulmavilayonnamane ca sā
children.translated_text: In the same way the <s>ghaṭī</s> is useful, and it is also useful for dissolving and raising a <s>gulma</s> (abdominal mass).
The instruments called <s>śalākā</s> (probes or rods) have various operations and shapes.
Their measurements are according to use; their operations are chiefly probing.
Two, with mouths like earthworms, remove foreign bodies from the channels.
Two, with mouths like split lentils, should be eight and nine finger-breadths long.
There are six <s>śaṅku</s> instruments; of them, two are sixteen and twelve finger-breadths long.
For pushing aside there are two, ten and twelve finger-breadths long, with mouths like a serpent's hood.
For moving, there are two with mouths like arrow-feathers; for extraction, there are hook-shaped ones.

children.text: nato 'gre śaṅkunā tulyo garbhaśaṅkur iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Bent at the tip and equal to a <s>śaṅku</s>, it is remembered as the <s>garbhaśaṅku</s> (fetal hook).
With that instrument, eight finger-breadths long, one should remove an obstructed fetus from a woman.
The instrument for removing a urinary stone is curved at the front like a serpent's hood.
The instrument for extracting a tooth has a mouth like an arrow-feather and is four finger-breadths long.
Six <s>śalākā</s> rods, furnished with cotton wrappings, are for wiping.
For work near and far in the anus, two are ten and twelve finger-breadths long.
For the nose two are six and seven finger-breadths long, and for the ear two are eight and nine finger-breadths long.
The ear-cleaning instrument has an end like an <s>aśvattha</s> leaf and a mouth like a ladle.
For the <s>śalākā</s> and the <s>jāmbavauṣṭha</s> instruments, three each are used separately for alkali and for fire-cautery.
One should employ thick, fine, and long <s>śalākā</s> rods, and a <s>śalākā</s> for <s>antravardhman</s> (prolapse or enlargement of the bowel).
Its shaft is round in the middle and upper part, and at the base it resembles a half-moon.
With a mouth like half a jujube-stone, it performs cauterization of nasal piles and tumors.
In the sequence of alkaline medicines there are three rods, eight finger-breadths long, with depressed mouths.
Their mouths are equal in size to the nails of the little finger, middle finger, and ring finger.
The respective instruments have been stated in connection with cleansing the penis, applying collyrium, and the like.
Auxiliary instruments are magnet, rope, cloth, stone, and hammer.
Straps, gut-strings, the tongue, hairs, branches, nails, the mouth, and teeth are also auxiliary instruments.

children.text: kālaḥ pākaḥ karaḥ pādo bhayaṃ harṣaś ca tatkriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Time, ripening, the hand, the foot, fear, and joy are also their operative means.
A knower of methods should distinguish them after examining them carefully with expert intelligence.
Striking out, churning, filling, clearing a passage, arranging, extracting, binding, and pressing,
as well as suction, raising, bending down, moving, breaking, turning around, and straightening, are the operations of instruments.

children.text: vivartate sādhvavagāhate ca grāhyaṃ gṛhītvoddharate ca yasmāt
children.translated_text: Because it turns, penetrates well, and, after grasping what is to be grasped, draws it out,

children.text: yantreṣvataḥ kaṅkamukhaṃ pradhānaṃ sthāneṣu sarveṣvadhikāri yacca ||
children.translated_text: therefore among instruments the <s>kaṅkamukha</s> (heron-bill forceps) is foremost, and it is applicable in every site.
Twenty-six cutting instruments, fashioned by good smiths according to rule,
should be capable of cutting hair and are generally six finger-breadths long.
One should have them made well formed, with good edges, and easy to hold.
They should not be misshapen, and should be made of well-smelted, well-sharpened, well-wrought iron.
Their mouths and tips should be properly set, and they should have the color of a blue lotus.
Their forms should match their names, and they should always be kept at hand.
Each should have a blade measuring a half or a fourth of its own total measure.
Generally one should use two or three of them, according to the particular site.
Among them, the <s>maṇḍalāgra</s> has a blade shaped like the nail within the index finger.
It is to be used for scraping and cutting in <s>pothakī</s>, <s>śuṇḍikā</s>, and similar conditions.
The <s>vṛddhipattra</s> is razor-shaped and is used for cutting, splitting, and opening.

children.text: ṛjvagram unnate śophe gambhīre ca tad anyathā ||
children.translated_text: It should have a straight point for an elevated swelling; in a deep swelling it is otherwise.
It has a point bent backward, with a long or short mouth according to its site of application.
The instruments called <s>utpala</s> and <s>adhyardhadhārā</s> are likewise used for splitting and cutting.
The <s>sarpāsya</s>, with a blade half a finger-breadth long, is for cutting piles of the nose and ear.
A smooth probe with an earthworm-like mouth is for investigating a track.
Another, needle-mouthed and with a hole set at the base, is for piercing.
The <s>vetasa</s> is used for puncturing in cases to be drained, as are instruments with mouths like the <s>śarārī</s> and the three-bristled brush.

children.text: kuśāṭā vadane srāvye dvyaṅgulaṃ syāt tayoḥ phalam
children.translated_text: The <s>kuśāṭā</s> is for draining in the mouth; the blades of those two should be two finger-breadths long.

children.text: tadvad antarmukhaṃ tasya phalam adhyardham aṅgulam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, its inward-facing blade is one and a half finger-breadths long.
This half-moon-faced instrument likewise has a blade one and a half finger-breadths long.

children.text: vrīhivaktraṃ prayojya ca tat sirodarayor vyadhe ||
children.translated_text: The rice-grain-mouthed instrument is to be used for piercing veins and the abdomen.
The broad <s>kuṭhārī</s> (axe-shaped instrument) resembles a cow's tooth and has a mouth half a finger-breadth long.
With its upward handle, one should pierce a vein situated above a bone.
The copper <s>śalākā</s> is double-mouthed, with its mouths shaped like <s>kuruvaka</s> buds.
With it one should pierce <s>liṅganāśa</s> (cataract); one should also make an <s>aṅguliśastraka</s> (finger-knife).
Its mouth emerges from a ring, and its blade is half a finger-breadth long.
In application it is the same as the <s>vṛddhipattra</s> or the <s>maṇḍalāgra</s>.
That instrument has a fitted ring of the size of the end joint of the index finger.
It is tied with a thread and is used for cutting and splitting diseases of the throat channel.
For grasping <s>śuṇḍikā</s>, <s>arman</s>, and the like, the hook should have a well-bent mouth.
For cutting bones, the saw is rough-edged and ten finger-breadths long.
It is two finger-breadths wide, fine-toothed, and well fastened to its handle.
For cutting sinews, thread, and hair, the scissors are like ordinary scissors.
The nail instrument is nine finger-breadths long, double-mouthed, and has both curved and straight edges.
It is used for extracting tiny foreign bodies, cutting, splitting, scarification, and scraping.
The tooth-scraper is single-edged, four-cornered, and bound in form on one side.
With it one should clean tartar from the teeth.

children.text: vṛttā gūḍhadṛḍhāḥ pāśe tisraḥ sūcyo 'tra sīvane
children.translated_text: Here, for suturing, there are three needles: round, concealed, and firm at the loop.
For fleshy regions, the instrument should be triangular and three finger-breadths long.
For wounds situated in places with little flesh, on bones, and at joints, it should be two finger-breadths long.
For vital points connected with the cooked and uncooked contents of the stomach and bowel, it should have a rice-grain-shaped mouth and be bent like a bow.
That one is two and a half finger-breadths long; all the round ones are four finger-breadths long.
The <s>kūrca</s> instruments, set on one round base, are seven or eight and well fastened.
It is to be used for pounding in cases of dark discoloration, facial spots, and loss of hair.
The <s>khaja</s> has eight round spikes with half-finger mouths.

children.text: pāṇibhyāṃ mathyamānena ghrāṇāt tena hared asṛk
children.translated_text: When it is churned with the hands, one should remove blood from the nose with it.
The instrument for piercing the earlobes has a mouth like a jasmine bud.
The awl has a circular mouth half a finger wide; its insertion is likewise upward.
It is square, and with it one should pierce a swelling when there is doubt whether it is ripe or unripe.
It is also recommended for a thick earlobe, and for one that has become thickened.
The needle for piercing the ear is hollow for one third of its length and three finger-breadths long.
Leeches, alkali, cautery, glass, stone, nails, and the like
are non-metallic auxiliary instruments; one should arrange them in this way.
Other instruments and the like should also be devised according to practical usefulness and suitable application.
Uprooting, cutting, sewing, probing, scraping, scarifying, and pounding,

children.text: chedyaṃ bhedyaṃ vyadho mantho graho dāhaśca tatkriyāḥ
children.translated_text: incising, splitting, puncturing, churning, grasping, and cauterizing are their actions.
Bluntness, brokenness, thinness, thickness, shortness, excessive length, and crookedness,
and roughness of edge are declared to be the eight defects of surgical instruments.
For cutting, splitting, and scraping, one should hold the instrument between the handle and the blade
with the index finger, middle finger, and thumb, carefully composed.
Instruments for draining are held at the end of the handle with the index finger and thumb.
The rice-mouthed instrument should be held with its handle-end covered in the palm, and with its mouth at the mouth.
Those used for extraction should be held at the root; in other cases, according to ease in the procedure.
The knife-case should be nine finger-breadths wide, dense and firm, and twelve finger-breadths long.
It may be made of linen, leaf, wool, silk, fine cloth, or soft leather.
It should have loops set in place, be well sewn, have inner wool, and contain the surgical instruments.
Its mouth should be covered with a rod, and the instrument-case should be well arranged.
Leeches should be applied for bloodletting in delicate and comfortable patients.
Those born from foul water, fish, frogs, snakes, corpses, decay, and filth,
which are red, white, very black, restless, thick, and slimy,
with variegated rainbow-like upper streaks and hairy bodies,
are poisonous and should be avoided; from them arise itching, suppuration, fever, and dizziness.
In that case treatment that removes poison, <s>pitta</s>, and blood should be done; those born in pure water, however,
are non-poisonous, dark like water-plants, round, and marked with blue upper streaks.
Those whose backs are astringent-colored, whose bodies are slender, and whose bellies are slightly yellow are also such.
But even these should be rejected if, because of improper vomiting and repeated application,

children.text: sīdantīḥ salilaṃ prāpya raktamattā iti tyajet ||
children.translated_text: they become exhausted on reaching water and intoxicated with blood.
Then the other leeches, after being soaked in water mixed with paste of turmeric,
or refreshed again in water, <s>Avantīsoma</s>, or buttermilk,
should be made to attach by means of ghee, earth, breast milk, blood, or a puncture with an instrument.
When they are drinking, with shoulders raised, one should cover them with a soft cloth.
From blood mixed as impure and pure, the leech takes the bad blood first,

children.text: ādatte prathamaṃ haṃsaḥ kṣīraṃ kṣīrodakād iva ||
children.translated_text: as a swan takes milk from a mixture of milk and water.
Leeches pacify abdominal tumors, piles, abscesses, skin disease, gouty disorders, and throat diseases,
as well as eye pain, poison, and erysipelas.

children.text: daṃśasya tode kaṇḍvāṃ vā mokṣayed vāmayecca tām
children.translated_text: When there is piercing pain or itching at the bite, one should release it and make it vomit.
Its mouth should be smeared with pungent oil and gently rubbed with a smooth irritant.

children.text: rakṣan raktamadād bhūyaḥ saptāhaṃ tā na pātayet
children.translated_text: Protecting them again from intoxication with blood, one should not apply those leeches for seven days.
When leeches have properly vomited, their former sharpness and firmness return.

children.text: klamo 'tiyogān mṛtyur vā durvānte stabdhatā madaḥ
children.translated_text: From excessive application there is fatigue or death; from poor vomiting there is rigidity and intoxication.
They should be kept separately, each in a different jar containing clay and water.
Otherwise they may become poisonous through that association, because of putrefaction of saliva and the like.
If the bite is not clean, one should make it bleed with turmeric, jaggery, and honey.
Then one should apply pledgets soaked in ghee washed a hundred times, and cooling pastes.
Because the bad blood has gone out, redness and pain subside immediately.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ calitaṃ sthānāt sthitaṃ raktaṃ vraṇāśaye
children.translated_text: Blood in the wound-site that is impure, displaced from its place, yet remaining there,

children.text: vyamlībhavet paryuṣitaṃ tasmāt tat srāvayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes sour when it has grown stale; therefore one should drain it again.
One should apply a gourd or cupping jar when the blood is vitiated by <s>pitta</s>.
Because these are connected with fire, however, one should use them when it is vitiated by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāyu</s>.

children.text: kaphena duṣṭaṃ rudhiraṃ na śṛṅgeṇa vinirharet
children.translated_text: Blood vitiated by <s>kapha</s> should not be drawn out with a horn.
Because of its clotted state, blood vitiated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> should be drawn out with a horn.

children.text: gātraṃ baddhvopari dṛḍhaṃ rajjvā paṭṭena vā samam
children.translated_text: After binding the limb firmly above with a cord or bandage in an even way,
one should perform scarification, avoiding sinews, joints, bones, and vital points.
The strokes should spread toward the lower part and move upward,

children.text: na gāḍhaghanatiryagbhir na pade padam ācaran ||
children.translated_text: not be too deep, dense, or transverse, and not be made one stroke upon another.
Blood that is clotted and localized should be removed by scarification; blood that is asleep or inert by leeches;
blood that is deep-seated by horns and the like; and blood that is pervasive by venesection.

children.text: pracchānaṃ piṇḍite vā syād avagāḍhe jalaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: Scarification is used when it is massed together; leeches when it is deep-sunk;
gourd, cupping jar, and horn when it is in the skin; the vein itself when the blood is widespread.
The seat of <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s is treated respectively with horn, leech, and gourd.
After the blood has flowed, if through aggravation of <s>vāyu</s> there is swelling with pricking pain and itching,
one should sprinkle that swelling with warm ghee.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the method of venesection.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
Blood is sweet, slightly salty, neither cold nor hot, and not clotted.
It is red like a lotus, an <s>indragopa</s> insect, gold, fire, or the blood of a hare.

children.text: lohitaṃ prabhavaḥ śuddhaṃ tanos tenaiva ca sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: When pure, blood is the origin of the body, and by that very blood the body is sustained.

children.text: tat pittaśleṣmalaiḥ prāyo dūṣyate kurute tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is generally vitiated by <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, and the others; from this it then causes
<s>visarpa</s> (spreading inflammation), <s>vidradhi</s> (abscess), splenic disease, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal masses), depression of the digestive fire, and fever,
diseases of the mouth, eyes, and head, intoxication, thirst, and saltiness in the mouth,
<s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), <s>vātāsra</s>, <s>pittāsra</s>, bitter and sour eructations, and dizziness.
And diseases which, when treated properly with cold, hot, unctuous, dry, and other measures,

children.text: samyak sādhyā na sidhyanti te ca raktaprakopajāḥ
children.translated_text: do not become curable or are not cured, those too arise from aggravation of blood.

children.text: teṣu srāvayituṃ raktam udriktaṃ vyadhayet sirām ||
children.translated_text: In those conditions one should puncture a vein in order to drain the excessive blood.
But one should not do so in those under sixteen years of age, in those past seventy years, or in those whose blood has already been let,
nor in those who have not been oleated or fomented, those who have been excessively fomented, or those suffering from <s>vāta</s> disorders,
nor in pregnant women, puerperal women, those with indigestion, <s>pittāsra</s>, dyspnea, or cough,
nor in those with diarrhea, abdominal disease, vomiting, anemia, or swelling of the whole body,
nor when oil has been drunk, nor while the five purificatory procedures are being applied.

children.text: nāyantritāṃ sirāṃ vidhyen na tiryaṅ nāpyanutthitām ||
children.translated_text: One should not puncture a vein that has not been bound, nor one struck crosswise, nor one that has not risen.
Nor should it be done in excessive cold, heat, wind, or cloud, except in an urgent disease.
In disorders of the head and eyes, one should release a vein in the forehead.
Or one may release one at the outer canthus or near the nose; in ear diseases, one arising from the ear.
In diseases of the nose, one should release the vein situated at the tip of the nose or between the nose and forehead.
In <s>pīnasa</s> (chronic rhinitis) and diseases of the mouth, the veins running to the tongue, lips, jaw, and palate should be opened.
In swellings above the collarbone, the veins situated in the neck, ear, temple, and head should be opened.
In insanity and epilepsy, again, the veins situated in the chest, outer canthus, and forehead should be opened.
Or one should open the vein at the jaw-joint, or generally the vein running between the eyebrows.
In abscess and pain in the side, one should open a vein between the side, armpit, and breast.
In tertian fever, one between the shoulders; in quartan fever, one below the shoulder.
In painful dysentery, one should open the vein situated two finger-breadths from the pelvis.
In diseases of semen and the penis, one in the penis; in <s>galagaṇḍa</s>, one running to the thigh.
In <s>gṛdhrasī</s> (sciatica), one four finger-breadths below the knee or above it.
In <s>apacī</s>, one two finger-breadths below the <s>indravasti</s>, or four finger-breadths above it.
In pain of the thigh, and likewise in <s>kroṣṭukaśīrṣa</s>, one should open a vein above the ankle.
In burning of the feet, <s>khuḍa</s>, tingling, cracked feet, <s>vātakaṇṭaka</s>,

children.text: cipye ca dvyaṅgule vidhyed upari kṣipramarmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>cipya</s>, one should puncture two finger-breadths above the <s>kṣipra-marman</s>.
In <s>viśvācī</s>, one should act as in <s>gṛdhrasī</s>; when the veins stated above are not visible,
one should puncture another vein, free from vital spots, in a place as near as possible.
Now the patient should have an oleated body, all equipment ready, and sufficient strength.
A rite of blessing should have been performed for him, and he should have been fed with unctuous meat-broth and rice.
Having been made to sweat by heat from fire or sun, he should be seated on a seat as high as the knees.
His hairline should be held with a soft band, and his elbows should be placed on his knees.
With both fists wrapped in cloth, he should press the neck firmly.
He should also clench the teeth, cough, and puff out the cheeks.
A man should restrain him from behind, wrapping a cloth around him,
throwing it around the neck and placing the left index finger inside.
This is the method of restraint for veins other than those inside the mouth.
