Then the physician, with the middle finger freed from the thumb,
should tap the vein, once he knows it has risen either by touch or by pressure with the thumb.
He should mark it in the middle with a <s>kuṭhārī</s> held in the left hand,
and, steady at the blade-point, should release the vein in the same way.
Tapping and pressing it, he should puncture it with the rice-tipped instrument.
For the vein near the nose, he should raise the tip of the nose with the thumb.
For the vein beneath the tongue, he should have the tip of the tongue raised and bitten.
When puncturing veins situated in the neck, he should apply restraint above the breasts.
For a patient holding a stone in his hand, with the arm extended and placed on the knee,
he should puncture after rubbing from the belly upward and after an upper band has been tied.
He should puncture a vein of the hand or arm when the elbow is not bent.
After seating the patient comfortably, he should bind the fist with the thumb enclosed.
He should also tie a band four finger-breadths above the place to be punctured.
He should puncture a vein in the sides while the patient is supported by the arms.
When the penis is erect, he should puncture a penile vein; for a leg vein, the knee should not be bent.
For a vein of the foot, the foot should be well placed, and below the knee-joint it should be pressed,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ karābhyām ā gulphaṃ caraṇe tasya copari
children.translated_text: firmly with the hands down to the ankle, and above that foot
the second foot should be slightly bent and mounted; then the procedure is as for the hand.

children.text: baddhvā vidhyet sirām ittham anukteṣvapi kalpayet
children.translated_text: Having bound the vein, he should puncture it in this way; even in cases not mentioned,

children.text: teṣu teṣu pradeśeṣu tat tad yantram upāyavit ||
children.translated_text: the practitioner skilled in means should devise the appropriate restraint in each particular region.
In a fleshy place he should insert the rice-mouthed instrument to the measure of a rice grain.

children.text: yavārdham asthnām upari sirāṃ vidhyan kuṭhārikām ||
children.translated_text: When puncturing a vein over bone, he should insert the <s>kuṭhārikā</s> to half a barley grain.

children.text: samyagviddhā sraveddhārāṃ yantre mukte tu na sravet
children.translated_text: When properly punctured, it flows in a stream; when the restraint is released, it does not flow.
When badly punctured, it flows little and for only a short time; it should be treated with oil and powders.

children.text: saśabdam atividdhā tu sraved duḥkhena dhāryate
children.translated_text: When over-punctured, it flows with a sound and is stopped with difficulty.
Fear, fainting, looseness of the restraint, a blunt instrument, and excessive satiety,
emaciation, agitation, and lack of sweating are causes for blood not flowing.
When the blood does not flow properly, with <s>vellā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>niśā</s>, and <s>nata</s>,
together with house-soot, salt, and oils, he should smear the mouth of the vein.
When it has begun to flow properly, with warm oil and salt applied,

children.text: agre sravati duṣṭāsraṃ kusumbhād iva pītikā
children.translated_text: the vitiated blood flows first, like yellow pigment from safflower.

children.text: samyak srutvā svayaṃ tiṣṭhecchuddhaṃ tad iti nāharet ||
children.translated_text: After it has flowed properly, pure blood stops by itself; one should not draw it out.

children.text: yantraṃ vimucya mūrchāyāṃ vījite vyajanaiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: If fainting occurs, one should release the instrument; after he has been fanned with fans,

children.text: srāvayen mūrchati punas tvaparedyus tryahe 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: one should let the blood flow again. If he faints again, one should do it on the next day, or even after three days.
From <s>vāta</s>, the blood is dark-red, dry, flows swiftly, is clear, and is foamy.
From <s>pitta</s>, it is yellow or blackish, foul-smelling, does not coagulate because of heat, and has a sheen.

children.text: kaphāt snigdham asṛk pāṇḍu tantumat picchilaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: From <s>kapha</s>, the blood is unctuous, pale, stringy, slimy, and thick.
From a combination it has mixed signs; when all three <s>doṣas</s> are involved, it is dirty and turbid.

children.text: aśuddhau balino 'pyasraṃ na prasthāt srāvayet param
children.translated_text: If purification is incomplete, one should not drain more than a <s>prastha</s> of blood, even from a strong man.

children.text: atisrutau hi mṛtyuḥ syād dāruṇā vā calāmayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when too much has flowed out, death may occur, or terrible diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
In that condition, massage with oil, meat broth, milk, and drinking blood are the remedies.

children.text: srute rakte śanair yantram apanīya himāmbunā ||
children.translated_text: When the blood has flowed, one should slowly remove the instrument and wash the mouth of the vein with cold water;
then the opening of the vein should be bandaged with a cloth-strip smeared with oil.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ srāvayed bhūyaḥ sāyam ahnyapare 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: If the blood is not purified, one should let it flow again in the evening or on the following day.
For one whose body has been prepared with oleation, or when the blood is greatly vitiated, this may be done after a fortnight.
For if even a little vitiated blood remains, the disease does not entirely pass away.

children.text: saśeṣam apyato dhāryaṃ na cātisrutim ācaret
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when some remains, it should be kept in check; one should not cause excessive outflow.
One should remove the remainder with horns and similar means, or else bring it to clarity.
By cooling measures, by therapies for <s>pitta</s> and blood, by purifications, and by drying measures,

children.text: duṣṭaṃ raktam anudriktam evam eva prasādayet ||
children.translated_text: one should likewise clarify vitiated blood that has not become excessive.

children.text: rakte tvatiṣṭhati kṣipraṃ stambhanīm ācaret kriyām
children.translated_text: But when the blood does not stop, one should quickly undertake a stopping treatment.
With <s>lodhra</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>pattaṅga</s>, black gram, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and red ochre,
with potsherd, collyrium, linen ash, the milky bark of trees, and sprouts,
one should powder the wound opening; and the patient should drink a cold infusion beginning with <s>padmaka</s>.

children.text: tām eva vā sirāṃ vidhyed vyadhāt tasmād anantaram
children.translated_text: Or one should pierce that same vein near the previous puncture,
or quickly cauterize the opening of the vein with a heated probe.

children.text: unmārgagā yantranipīḍanena svasthānam āyānti punar na yāvat
children.translated_text: As long as the vitiated <s>doṣas</s>, having entered the blood and gone on a wrong path through pressure from the instrument,

children.text: doṣāḥ praduṣṭā rudhiraṃ prapannās tāvaddhitāhāravihārabhāk syāt ||
children.translated_text: do not return again to their own place, so long should the patient observe wholesome food and conduct.

children.text: nātyuṣṇaśītaṃ laghu dīpanīyaṃ rakte 'panīte hitam annapānam
children.translated_text: After blood has been removed, food and drink that are not too hot or too cold, light, and kindling to digestion are beneficial.

children.text: tadā śarīraṃ hyanavasthitāsṛg agnir viśeṣād iti rakṣitavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For then the body has unsettled blood, and the digestive fire especially must be protected.
A man is said to have purified blood when his complexion and senses are clear, when he desires the objects of the senses,
when the impulse of digestion is unobstructed, and when he is comfortable, well nourished, and endowed with strength.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter on the method for removing foreign bodies.
Thus indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
The courses of foreign bodies are fivefold: curved, straight, transverse, upward, and downward.
A wound that is dusky, swollen, painful, and repeatedly discharging blood,
raised up like a bubble, covered with pustules,
and having soft flesh should be understood, in brief, to contain an internal foreign body.
In particular, when a foreign body is in the skin, there is discolored, hard, elongated swelling.

children.text: śopho bhavati māṃsasthe coṣaḥ śopho vivardhate ||
children.translated_text: When it is in the flesh, there is burning and swelling that increases.
There is inability to bear pressure, suppuration, and the path of the foreign body does not heal.
When it is lodged between muscles, the condition is like one that has reached the flesh, but without swelling.
When it is in the network of sinews, there are spasms, inflammation, stiffness, and pains.
In a sinew it is hard to remove; when lodged in a vein, there is distention of the vein.
When it is situated in a channel, there is loss of the channel's own function and qualities.
When it is in an artery, <s>vāta</s> drives out blood mixed with foam.
It comes out with sound, and there is nausea accompanied by pain in the limbs.
When it has reached a bone-joint, there is strong friction and a sense that the bone is full.
When it is in bone, the pains are of many kinds; when it is in a joint, swelling is similar,
and there is cessation of movement. When it is lodged in the abdomen, there is gurgling distention.
There is abdominal swelling, and food, feces, and urine are seen at the mouth of the wound.
One should know a foreign body lodged in a vital spot by the signs of a pierced vital spot.
And in the skin and other sites, one should discern it by the respective discharges.
When it is favorably positioned in persons whose body is purified, it heals.
But through aggravation of <s>doṣas</s>, trauma, and other disturbances, it causes trouble again.
Where the skin is lost, redness, pain, burning, and inflammation arise there through oiling, sweating, and rubbing,
and where ghee melts,

children.text: āśu śuṣyati lepo vā tatsthānaṃ śalyavad vadet ||
children.translated_text: or a plaster dries quickly, one should declare that place to contain a foreign body.
When it is hidden in flesh, after cleansing and through emaciation the flesh becomes slack;

children.text: kṣobhād rāgādibhiḥ śalyaṃ lakṣayet tadvad eva ca ||
children.translated_text: from disturbance, redness, and the like, one should identify the foreign body in the same way.
When it is hidden in muscles, bones, joints, or the abdomen, one should detect it in the bones
by oiling, sweating, bandaging, pressure, and rubbing of the bones.
When it is hidden in a joint, it should likewise be detected as in bone, by extension and flexion.
When it is hidden in sinews, veins, channels, or arteries, on an uneven road
one should place the patient in a chariot yoked with horses and having a broken wheel,

children.text: śīghraṃ nayet tatas tasya saṃrambhācchalyam ādiśet ||
children.translated_text: and drive him swiftly; then, from the disturbance, one should point out the foreign body.
A foreign body hidden in a vital spot has not been described separately, because those spots rest in flesh and the other tissues.

children.text: sāmānyena saśalyaṃ tu kṣobhiṇyā kriyayā saruk ||
children.translated_text: In general, a place containing a foreign body is painful when it is disturbed by an agitating procedure.

children.text: vṛttaṃ pṛthu catuṣkoṇaṃ tripuṭaṃ ca samāsataḥ
children.translated_text: Round, broad, quadrangular, and triangular, in brief,
the shape of an unseen foreign body should be inferred from the form of the wound.
For these, the two methods of extraction are against the course and with the course.
When they are turned toward or away from oneself, one should remove them by the opposite method.
Wherever it is easy to extract, one should cut there and remove one that has gone transversely.
A foreign body lodged in the chest, armpit, groin, or flank should not be driven out by force,

children.text: pratilomam anuttuṇḍaṃ chedyaṃ pṛthumukhaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: nor one that lies against the course, has no projecting tip, is cutting, or has a broad face.
One should not remove a foreign body that destroys the extraction wound, nor one that has become lost and causes no complication.
But one that can be reached by the hand should be removed with the hand itself; another, however,
if visible, should be taken with instruments whose mouths resemble those of a lion, snake, crocodile, armor-joint, crab, or heron.
An invisible one can be grasped according to the position of the wound, wherever possible,
with instruments whose mouths resemble those of a heron, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, vulture, hawk, <s>śarāri</s> bird, or crow.
A foreign body lodged in skin and the like should be removed with forceps; one in a hollow with palate-shaped instruments.

children.text: suṣirasthaṃ tu nalakaiḥ śeṣaṃ śeṣair yathāyatham ||
children.translated_text: One lodged in a hollow channel should be removed with tubes, and the rest with the other instruments as appropriate.

children.text: śastreṇa vā viśasyādau tato nirlohitaṃ vraṇam
children.translated_text: Or, first opening it with a knife, then making the wound free of blood,
one should foment it with ghee and prescribe the regimen for one whose wound has been bound.
A foreign body attached to a vessel or sinew should first be moved with a probe.
A foreign body lodged in the heart, after the patient has been startled with cold water,

children.text: tataḥ sthānāntaraṃ prāptam āharet tad yathāyatham
children.translated_text: when it has reached another location, should then be removed by the suitable method.
If it is hard to pull out along its own path, one should remove it in this same way even by another route.
When it is gripped by bone, one should press the man down with the feet and pull it out.
If that is impossible, when he is firmly held by strong attendants,
and if even then it is impossible, one should bend the <s>vāraṅga</s> with a bowstring,
bind it securely to the ring of the mouth, and act with full attention.
When he is well restrained with a five-branched binding, one should then strike a horse with a whip,
so that, raising its head swiftly, it pulls out the foreign body.

children.text: uddharecchalyam evaṃ vā śākhāyāṃ kalpayet taroḥ
children.translated_text: Or one should arrange the same procedure on the branch of a tree,
and, after fastening the weak <s>vāraṅga</s>, remove the foreign body with cords of <s>kuśa</s> grass.
When the <s>vāraṅga</s> is obstructed by swelling, one should press the swelling out by a proper method.
With a tube struck by a mallet, one should knock it free and remove it when it has protruded.

children.text: taireva cānayen mārgam amārgottuṇḍitaṃ tu yat
children.translated_text: By those same means one should bring into its proper channel what has protruded outside the channel.

children.text: mṛditvā karṇināṃ karṇaṃ nāḍyāsyena nigṛhya vā ||
children.translated_text: One should crush the ear of an eared foreign body, or hold it with the mouth of a tube,
while an earless one, with its mouth open and lying straight, may be removed by a magnet.
A foreign body gone into the large intestine should be removed by purgation.
Vitiated wind, poison, breast-milk, blood, water, and similar substances should be removed by suction.
When a foreign body is in the channel of the throat, one should pass a thread into the throat.

children.text: bisenātte tataḥ śalye bisaṃ sūtraṃ samaṃ haret
children.translated_text: After the foreign body has been caught with a lotus-fiber, one should draw out the lotus-fiber together with the thread.
Or, inserting a probe heated in a tube and made firm in water,
one should draw a lac-made foreign body from the throat with a lac-smeared probe, and a non-lac one otherwise.
With a swallowed hair-ball and liquids, one should draw out a thorn in the throat.
If it is otherwise, with a sudden act, by means of that hair-ball tied with a thread, while the patient vomits,
what cannot be brought out through the mouth or nose should be pushed onward from behind.
A morsel acting as a foreign body should be made to pass down by drinking water or by striking the shoulders.
Minute foreign bodies in eye-wounds should be removed with linen, hair, or water.
One should shake a man whose head is held downward and extended, after filling him with water,
or make him vomit with his face downward, or bury him in a heap of ash.
When the ear is filled with water, one should churn it with the hand; then oil or water

children.text: kṣiped adhomukhaṃ karṇaṃ hanyād vā cūṣayeta vā ||
children.translated_text: should be poured in, the ear turned downward, and it should be struck or sucked out.
When an insect has entered a channel, one should fill the ear with salt water,

children.text: śuktena vā sukhoṣṇena mṛte kledaharo vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or with warm vinegar; when it is dead, the procedure is one that removes moisture.
A foreign body made of lac, or made of metals such as gold and silver, and remaining there for a long time,
is generally melted by the heat born in the body.
But soft reed, wood, horn, bone, tooth, hair, and stone do not melt.
A foreign body of horn, reed, iron, palm-leaf, or wood, even after a long time,
is generally bent or broken apart, for flesh and blood quickly cook it.

children.text: śalye māṃsāvagāḍhe cet sa deśo na vidahyate ||
children.translated_text: If a foreign body is deeply sunk in flesh and that region does not inflame,
then, by massage, fomentation, cleansing, depletion, and nourishing measures,
by sharp poultices, drinks, foods, heavy pressure, knife-marks, and footprints,
one should bring it to suppuration and remove the foreign body by incision, probing, and splitting.
Having considered the many forms of the foreign body, its region, and the instruments,

children.text: tais tairupāyair matimān śalyaṃ vidyāt tathāharet ||
children.translated_text: the intelligent physician should know the foreign body and remove it by those respective methods.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the procedure of surgical operation.
Thus indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
A wound generally arises from suppuration preceded by swelling.

children.text: tam evopacaret tasmād rakṣan pākaṃ prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should treat that swelling itself, carefully guarding against suppuration.
This is done with very cooling pastes and sprinklings, bloodletting, purification, and the like.
A swelling that is mild, with little heat and pain, unripe, of the same color, hard, and fixed,
when it is maturing, becomes discolored, reddened, and stretched like a bladder.
It seems about to burst, has piercing pain, and is accompanied by aching of the limbs and yawning.
It is accompanied by agitation, loss of appetite, burning, heat, thirst, fever, and sleeplessness.
It discharges thick ghee-like fluid and, like a wound, cannot bear touch.
When it is ripe, the force of symptoms is slight: there is withering, pallor, and the formation of wrinkles.
There is depression at the edges, elevation in the middle, and softness of itching, swelling, and the like.
When touched, pus moves within it as water does in a bladder.
Pain arises from wind; burning from bile; swelling from the increase of phlegm.

children.text: rāgo raktācca pākaḥ syād ato doṣaiḥ saśoṇitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Redness comes from blood, and suppuration occurs from the doṣas together with blood.
When suppuration has gone too far, the wound becomes hollow, with thin skin, eaten by the doṣas,
covered with wrinkles, dark-colored, and with its fine body-hairs falling away.

children.text: kaphajeṣu tu śopheṣu gambhīraṃ pākam etyasṛk ||
children.translated_text: But in phlegmatic swellings, the blood reaches a deep suppuration,
so that where the signs of ripeness are indistinct, there is cold swelling,
the skin has its natural color, the pain is slight, and the touch is hard like stone.

children.text: raktapākam iti brūyāt taṃ prājño muktasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should say, without doubt, that this is suppuration of the blood.
In one of little courage, in a weak person, in a child, or when the suppuration is excessively raised,
and when it is situated in a vital spot, joint, or the like, rupture is used; elsewhere, incision.
When an unripe swelling is cut, there are disorders of the veins and sinews and excessive flow of blood;
there is excessive increase of pain, tearing, or erysipelas arising from the wound.
Pus that remains inside again, growing there, together with veins, sinews, blood, and flesh,
quickly burns them, like fire burning dry grass.
The man who cuts what is unripe through ignorance, and the man who neglects what is ripe,
should both be regarded as acting without certainty, like outcast dog-cookers.
Before the operation with the knife, one should feed the patient the food he desires.

children.text: pānapaṃ pāyayen madyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ yo vedanākṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: If he is accustomed to drink and unable to bear pain, one should make him drink strong liquor.

children.text: na mūrchatyannasaṃyogān mattaḥ śastraṃ na budhyate ||
children.translated_text: Because of the association with food he does not faint, and when intoxicated he does not notice the knife.
This does not apply to a patient with obstructed fetus, stone, disease of the mouth, or abdominal disease.
Then, after the instruments have been brought, the physician should set the patient facing east,
restrain him quickly while facing him, and make the incision, avoiding vital points and the like.
With a very sharp knife, in the natural direction, he should cut until pus is seen.
He should withdraw that knife only once; but even when the suppuration is very large,
he should cut it open properly to a breadth of two fingers, at intervals of two or three fingers.
After probing it properly with a probe and examining it well all around,
or with fingers, tubes, or tubular probes, according to the place and according to the cavity,

children.text: yato gatāṃ gatiṃ vidyād utsaṅgo yatra yatra ca
children.translated_text: wherever he knows the tract has gone, and wherever there is a hollow recess,

children.text: tatra tatra vraṇaṃ kuryāt suvibhaktaṃ nirāśayam ||
children.translated_text: there he should make the wound well divided and without a hidden cavity.

children.text: āyataṃ ca viśālaṃ ca yathā doṣo na tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: It should be long and broad, so that the <s>doṣa</s> does not remain there.
Courage, quick action, a sharp knife, absence of sweating and trembling,
and freedom from confusion in the physician are praised in surgical work.
One should cut transversely on the forehead, eyebrows, gums, and collarbone region,
on the abdomen, armpit, orbit of the eye, lip, cheek, throat, and groin.
Elsewhere, because of cutting transversely, there is tearing of veins and sinews.
When the knife has been set down, the patient should be reassured with words and with cold water,
and then the wound should be pressed all around with the fingers.
After washing it with an astringent decoction and removing the water with a cloth,
one should fumigate it with <s>guggulu</s>, <s>aguru</s>, white mustard, asafoetida, and resin of <s>sarja</s>,
together with salt, <s>ṣaḍgrantha</s>, and neem leaves soaked in ghee.
Then, with sesame paste, ghee, honey, and the appropriate medicine,

children.text: digdhāṃ vartiṃ tato dadyāt tairevācchādayecca tām
children.translated_text: one should insert a smeared wick and cover it with those same substances.
Above it one should place a thick pad of meal smeared with ghee,
and then bind it carefully and properly with a bandage.

children.text: pārśve savye 'pasavye vā nādhastān naiva copari ||
children.translated_text: The knot should be on the left side or the right side, not below and not above.
Clean, fine, firm bandages, and pads furnished with wicks,

children.text: dhūpitā mṛdavaḥ ślakṣṇā nirvalīkā vraṇe hitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fumigated, soft, smooth, and free from folds, are beneficial for a wound.
Immediately afterward he should perform protection for the patient, to ward off harmful spirits.

children.text: baliṃ copaharet tebhyaḥ sadā mūrdhnā ca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should also offer an oblation to them, and should always wear on his head
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Guhā</s>, <s>Atiguhā</s>, <s>Jaṭilā</s>, and <s>Brahmacāriṇī</s>,

children.text: vacāṃ chattrām aticchattrāṃ dūrvāṃ siddhārthakān api ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Aticchattrā</s>, <s>Dūrvā</s>, and also white mustard seeds.
After that, he should prescribe for him the conduct taught for the day of oleation.
Sleeping by day produces itching, redness, pain, swelling, and pus in a wound.
When semen is stirred by recollection of women, by touch, or by seeing them,
even without intercourse he incurs the disorders produced by sexual intercourse.
His food, too, should be what is suitable to him: barley, wheat, and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice,
lentils, mung beans, <s>tubarī</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and <s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>,
young radish, eggplant, <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, and <s>vāstuka</s>,
bitter gourd, <s>karkoṭa</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, and bitter fruits,

children.text: saindhavaṃ dāḍimaṃ dhātrī ghṛtaṃ taptahimaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: rock salt, pomegranate, emblic myrobalan, ghee, and water that has been heated and cooled.
Eating a small amount of well-cooked old <s>śāli</s> rice, unctuous and followed by warm water,

children.text: bhuñjāno jāṅgalair māṃsaiḥ śīghraṃ vraṇam apohati
children.translated_text: together with the meats of animals from arid lands, he quickly gets rid of the wound.

children.text: aśitaṃ mātrayā kāle pathyaṃ yāti jarāṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: Food that is eaten in proper measure, at the proper time, and is wholesome is easily digested.
But from indigestion a powerful disturbance of <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s occurs.
From that he incurs swelling, pain, suppuration, burning, and abdominal distension.

children.text: navaṃ dhānyaṃ tilān māṣān madyaṃ māṃsam ajāṅgalam
children.translated_text: He should avoid new grain, sesame seeds, black gram, liquor, meat not from arid-land animals,
milk and sugarcane products, and sour, salty, and pungent things.

children.text: yaccānyad api viṣṭambhi vidāhi guru śītalam
children.translated_text: He should also avoid whatever else is obstructive, burning, heavy, or cold.
This group beginning with new grain produces every <s>doṣa</s> in a wounded person.
Liquor, being sharp, hot, dry, and sour, would quickly damage the wound.
He should be fanned with <s>vāla</s> and <s>uśīra</s>, and the wound should not be disturbed.

children.text: na tuden na ca kaṇḍūyecceṣṭamānaśca pālayet
children.translated_text: He should not pierce it or scratch it, and should protect it while moving about.
Listening to pleasant stories from affectionate elders and twice-born men,
and hopeful for release from disease, he quickly gets rid of the wound.

children.text: tṛtīye 'hni punaḥ kuryād vraṇakarma ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: On the third day one should again perform the wound treatment as before.
On the second day, however, one should not perform washing and the rest in that way.
A wound that is intensely painful and loosened heals only after a long time.

children.text: snigdhāṃ rūkṣāṃ ślathāṃ gāḍhāṃ durnyastāṃ ca vikeśikām
children.translated_text: One should not apply to the wound a wick that is too unctuous, dry, loose, tight, badly placed,

children.text: vraṇe na dadyāt kalkaṃ vā snehāt kledo vivardhate ||
children.translated_text: nor a paste; because of oiliness, moisture increases.
Because of excessive dryness there is cutting of the flesh, severe pain, tearing, and bleeding.
Because of looseness, excessive tightness, and bad placement, there is abrasion of the wound-channel.
A wound with putrid flesh, with a recess, with a tract, and filled with pus
should be cleansed quickly; for the wick has remained inside.

children.text: vyamlaṃ tu pāṭitaṃ śophaṃ pācanaiḥ samupācaret
children.translated_text: But a swelling that has been cut open before it is fully mature should be treated with suppurative measures,
with foods and poultices that are not too opposed to a wound.
One should immediately suture recent wounds that are open and caused by trauma,
fat-born lumps after they have been scraped, and short ear-lobes of the two ears.
On the head, the eye-sockets, the nose, the lips, the cheeks, the ears, the thighs, and the arms,
on the neck, forehead, scrotum, buttocks, penis, anus, abdomen, and similar places,
in deep regions, in fleshy parts, and in immobile parts,
but not in the groin, axilla, and the like, nor in wounds where there is little flesh or movement.
Nor should one suture wounds through which air escapes, wounds containing a foreign body, or those caused by <s>kṣāra</s> (caustic alkali), poison, or fire.
But one may suture after removing loose bone, dried blood, grass, and hair.
Prolapsed and severed flesh should be set back in its own place,

children.text: saṃdhyasthi ca sthite rakte snāyvā sūtreṇa valkalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, when the blood has stopped, joints and bones as well should be sutured with sinew, thread, or bark-fibers.

children.text: sīvyen na dūre nāsanne gṛhṇan nālpaṃ na vā bahu
children.translated_text: One should suture neither far apart nor too close together, taking neither too little tissue nor too much.
Then, after comforting the sufferer, on the wound smeared with honey and melted ghee,
with collyrium, ash of linen cloth, <s>phalinī</s>, fruits of <s>śallakī</s>,
and with <s>lodhra</s> and <s>madhuka</s>, one should apply bandaging and the rest as before.

children.text: vraṇo niḥśoṇitauṣṭho yaḥ kiṃcid evāvalikhya tam
children.translated_text: If a wound has lips without blood, one should scrape it just a little;
when blood has appeared, one should suture it, for blood is the means of its union.

children.text: bandhanāni tu deśādīn vīkṣya yuñjīta teṣu ca
children.translated_text: Bandages should be applied after considering the place and other factors, and among them,
wool, hide, and silk are warming, while linen is cooling.
Those made of cotton-wool, woven fiber, cotton cloth, sinew, and bark are both cooling and warming.
Copper, iron, tin, and lead should be used on wounds with excess fat and <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: bhaṅge ca yuñjyāt phalakaṃ carmavalkakuśādi ca
children.translated_text: and in fracture one should use a splint, as well as leather, bark, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and the like.

children.text: svanāmānugatākārā bandhās tu daśa pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: The bandages, shaped according to their own names, are fifteen:
<s>kośa</s>, <s>svastika</s>, <s>muttolī</s>, <s>cīna</s>, <s>dāma</s>, and <s>anuvellita</s>,
<s>khaṭvā</s>, <s>vibandha</s>, <s>sthagikā</s>, <s>vitāna</s>, <s>utsaṅga</s>, and <s>goṣphaṇa</s>,

children.text: yamakaṃ maṇḍalākhyaṃ ca pañcāṅgī ceti yojayet
children.translated_text: together with <s>yamaka</s>, the one called <s>maṇḍala</s>, and <s>pañcāṅgī</s>; these should be applied.
Among these, one should prescribe the <s>kośa</s> bandage for finger-joints.
The <s>svastika</s> is stated for the ear, axilla, breasts, and also for joints.
One should use the <s>muttolī</s> on the penis, neck, and the like, and the <s>cīna</s> at the outer corners of the eyes.
Likewise the <s>dāma</s> on a constricted part, and the <s>anuvellita</s> specifically on the limbs.

children.text: khaṭvāṃ gaṇḍe hanau śaṅkhe vibandhaṃ pṛṣṭhakodare
children.translated_text: The <s>khaṭvā</s> is used on the cheek, jaw, and temple, and the <s>vibandha</s> on the back and abdomen.
The <s>sthagikā</s> is used on the tips of the thumb, fingers, and penis, and in intestinal swellings.
The <s>vitāna</s> should be applied on broad parts and likewise on the head.
The <s>utsaṅga</s> is used on hanging parts and on the nose, lips, chin, and the like.

children.text: goṣphaṇaṃ saṃdhiṣu tathā yamakaṃ yamike vraṇe
children.translated_text: The <s>goṣphaṇa</s> is used on joints, and the <s>yamaka</s> on a paired wound.
The bandage called <s>maṇḍala</s> is used on a round limb, and the <s>pañcāṅgī</s> above the clavicles.

children.text: yo yatra suniviṣṭaḥ syāttaṃ teṣāṃ tatra buddhimān ||
children.translated_text: A wise physician should bind whichever of these is well fitted in the appropriate place.
He should bind tightly on the thighs, buttocks, axillae, groins, and head;
evenly on the limbs, face, ears, chest, back, flanks, throat, and abdomen;

children.text: samaṃ mehanamuṣke ca netre saṃdhiṣu ca ślatham
children.translated_text: and also evenly on the penis and scrotum, but loosely on the eyes and joints.
In a condition arising from <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, he should bind evenly where a loose bandage would otherwise be used.

children.text: gāḍham eva samasthāne bhṛśaṃ gāḍhaṃ tadāśaye
children.translated_text: Where an even bandage would be used, he should bind tightly; where it is the seat of those doṣas, he should bind very tightly.

children.text: śīte vasante 'pi ca tau mokṣaṇīyau tryahāt tryahāt ||
children.translated_text: In cold weather and also in spring, those bandages should be released every three days.
For conditions arising from <s>pitta</s> and blood, a bandage is considered even in a place where a tight one would be used.
It should be loose where an even one would be used, and in the seat of what should be loose it should not be applied at all.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātas tayor mokṣo grīṣme śaradi ceṣyate
children.translated_text: For those two, release of the bandage is prescribed morning and evening in summer and autumn.
A wound left unbandaged, afflicted by bites, mosquitoes, cold, wind, and the like,
becomes spoiled, and the oily medicine does not remain there for long.

children.text: kṛcchreṇa śuddhiṃ rūḍhiṃ vā yāti rūḍho vivarṇatām ||
children.translated_text: With difficulty it reaches purification or healing, and when healed it becomes discolored.

children.text: baddhas tu cūrṇito bhagno viśliṣṭaḥ pāṭito 'pi vā
children.translated_text: But a bandaged wound, even if crushed, fractured, dislocated, or split,
and even if its sinews and vessels are cut, heals quickly and easily.
It is not pained in any activities, such as rising, lying down, and the like.
A wound with everted lips, swollen up, uneven, hard, and extremely painful

children.text: samo mṛduraruk śīghraṃ vraṇaḥ śudhyati rohati
children.translated_text: is opposed to one that is even, soft, and painless; such a wound cleanses and heals quickly.
For stable wounds with little flesh that do not heal because of dryness,

children.text: pracchādyam auṣadhaṃ pattrair yathādoṣaṃ yathartu ca
children.translated_text: the medicine should be covered with leaves according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to the season.
The leaves should be undigested by age, young, without holes, and well arranged all around.
They should be washed, not rough, and taken from milky trees, birch, <s>arjuna</s>, or <s>kadamba</s>.
The wounds of leprous patients, burns, and the pustules of diabetics,
<s>karṇikā</s> lesions in rat-poisoning, alkali-burns, and poisoned wounds

children.text: bandhanīyā na māṃspāke gudapāke ca dāruṇe ||
children.translated_text: should not be bandaged, nor should severe suppuration of flesh or of the rectum.
Nor should wounds be bandaged when they are disintegrating, painful, burning, or spreading during the swelling stage.

children.text: arakṣayā vraṇe yasmin makṣikā nikṣipet kṛmīn ||
children.translated_text: If, through lack of protection, flies deposit worms in a wound,
then, as they feed, they produce pain, swelling, and a flow of blood.
In that case one should use the <s>surasādi</s> group for washing and filling the wound.
The barks of <s>saptaparṇa</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>rājādana</s>,
made into a paste with cow urine, are a useful plaster, and sprinkling with alkaline water is beneficial.

children.text: pracchādya māṃsapeśyā vā vraṇaṃ tān āśu nirharet
children.translated_text: Or, after covering the wound with a piece of flesh, one should quickly remove those worms.
One who is hurrying should not heal this wound over while it still has <s>doṣa</s> inside,
because with even a small impropriety it becomes disordered again.
Even after it has healed, one should avoid indigestion, exercise, sexual intercourse, and the like,

children.text: harṣaṃ krodhaṃ bhayaṃ cāpi yāvad ā sthairyasaṃbhavāt
children.translated_text: as well as joy, anger, and fear, until firmness has arisen.

children.text: ādareṇānuvartyo 'yaṃ māsān ṣaṭ sapta vā vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This regimen should be followed carefully for six or seven months.

children.text: utpadyamānāsu ca tāsu tāsu vārttāsu doṣādibalānusārī
children.translated_text: When various conditions arise, the physician, following the strength of the <s>doṣa</s> and the other factors,

children.text: tais tairupāyaiḥ prayataścikitsed ālocayan vistaram uttaroktam ||
children.translated_text: should treat them diligently by the respective methods, keeping in view the detailed account stated later.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the method of <s>kṣāra</s> and <s>agni</s> procedures.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
Among all surgical instruments and subsidiary instruments, <s>kṣāra</s> (alkali) is best, because
it performs many procedures such as cutting and splitting, even in difficult places.
Where instruments are painful to apply, and where they have not achieved success,
and in diseases that are extremely difficult, it is also employed even as a drink.
It is to be drunk in hemorrhoids, weak digestive fire, urinary stone, abdominal lump, abdominal enlargement, poisoning, and similar disorders.
It is to be applied directly in moles, leucoderma, external hemorrhoids, skin disease, numbness,
fistula-in-ano, tumors, glandular swellings, bad sinus tracts, wounds, and the like.

children.text: na tūbhayo 'pi yoktavyaḥ pitte rakte cale 'bale ||
children.translated_text: But it should not be used in either form when <s>pitta</s>, blood, or <s>vāta</s> is aggravated, or in a weak patient,
in fever, diarrhea, diseases of the heart or head, anemia, loss of appetite,
eye disease, after purification has been performed, or in swelling of the whole body,
in the timid, pregnant women, menstruating women, and in women whose vaginal passages or fetus are displaced,
when food is undigested, in a child, in an old person, and on arteries, joints, and vital spots,
on young bone, veins, ligaments, suture-lines, the throat, and the navel,
in regions with little flesh, and between the testicles, penis, channels, and nails,
and on the eyes except in eyelid disease, or on a bad day of cold, rain, or heat.
One should take black-nightshade, muṣkaka, śamyāka, plantain, pārijāta,
aśvakarṇa, mahāvṛkṣa, palāśa, āsphota, vṛkṣaka,
indravṛkṣa, arka, pūtīka, naktamāla, aśvamāraka,
kākajaṅghā, apāmārga, agnimantha, agni, and tilvaka,
fresh, with their roots, branches, and other parts, cut into pieces.
Also the four kośātakīs, together with the awns and stalks of barley,
having heaped them up separately on a stone slab in a windless place,
and having put limestone into the heap of muṣkaka, one should set it alight.

children.text: tatas tilānāṃ kutalair dagdhvāgnau vigate pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Then, after burning sesame by the kutala-measure in the fire, when the fire has gone out, separately
one should make ash of the limestone and a droṇa of the other ashes.
Taking the muṣkaka ash as the principal one, in each case in water and cow's urine,

children.text: gālayed ardhabhāreṇa mahatā vāsasā ca tat
children.translated_text: one should filter it with half its weight, and with a large cloth.

children.text: yāvat picchilaraktācchas tīkṣṇo jātas tadā ca tam ||
children.translated_text: When that has become slimy, reddish, clear, and sharp, then
one should take that alkaline filtrate and cook it in an iron vessel, stirring it.
Then, while it is being cooked, those pieces of limestone ash, crystal-sugar-like lime,
oyster shells, milk-cooked shells, conch-shells, and iron slag,
having made them repeatedly fire-colored in an iron vessel, should be quenched in the alkaline solution, one kuḍava in measure.
Having ground them with that very liquid, one should add the admixture.
One should finely powder the dung of cock, peacock, vulture, heron, and pigeon,
together with the bile of quadrupeds and birds, orpiment, realgar, and salts.

children.text: paritaḥ sutarāṃ cāto darvyā tam avaghaṭṭayet ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards one should very thoroughly stir it all around with a ladle.
When it rises up with steaming bubbles and is thick like a linctus,
then, after removing it from the fire, this medium <s>kṣāra</s>, when cool, should be kept in an iron vessel placed in a heap of barley.

children.text: sthāpyo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ kṣāro na tu piṣṭvā kṣipen mṛdau
children.translated_text: This is the medium <s>kṣāra</s>; but for the mild one, one should not grind and add the admixture.
For the sharp one, after quenching, one should remove it and make the admixture as before,
and likewise with lāṅgalikā, dantī, citraka, ativiṣā, vacā,
svarjikā, kanakakṣīrī, hiṅgu, pūtīka sprouts,

children.text: tālapattrī viḍaṃ ceti saptarātrāt paraṃ tu saḥ
children.translated_text: tālapattrī and viḍa. After seven nights it
is the sharp <s>kṣāra</s>, to be used in tumors and similar diseases born of <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, and fat.
In these same diseases when moderate, the medium one is used; another, mild one, is for diseases born of <s>pitta</s>, blood, and the rectum.
When its liquid is depleted, for the sake of strength one should again pour in alkaline water.
<s>Kṣāra</s> should be neither too sharp nor too mild, smooth, slimy, quick-acting, white,

children.text: śikharī sukhanirvāpyo na viṣyandī na cātiruk ||
children.translated_text: having a peak, easy to quench, not causing excessive oozing, and not causing excessive pain.
<s>Kṣāra</s> performs the action of both the knife and fire, with tenfold efficacy.

children.text: ācūṣann iva saṃrambhād gātram āpīḍayann iva ||
children.translated_text: As if sucking up, as if forcefully pressing the limb,
it follows the <s>doṣas</s> everywhere and uproots them from the root.
After performing its action, when the pain has gone, it subsides by itself.
In a disease treatable by <s>kṣāra</s>, after cutting, scraping, or draining it,
one should apply <s>kṣāra</s> with a probe, with the patient's body covered by a cloth.
One should wait for a count of one hundred mātrās; in hemorrhoids, with the opening covered,
one should manipulate the instrument by hand; in eyelid diseases, after turning back the eyelid,
covering the black part with a cotton pad, one should apply it.
In tumors of the nose, the alkaline paste should be thin like a lotus petal.
For a person seated facing the sun, one should raise the tip of the nose

children.text: mātrā vidhāryaḥ pañcāśat tadvad arśasi karṇaje ||
children.translated_text: and hold it for fifty mātrās; the same applies in hemorrhoids of the ear.
Afterwards one should wipe away the <s>kṣāra</s> by cleansing, inspect it,
and, when it is well burnt, smear it with ghee and honey; then with milk, whey, and sour gruel
one should quench it. Thereafter one should anoint it with ghee and apply sweet, cooling pastes.
Foods that cause moisture should be eaten, and foods should be eaten for moistening.

children.text: yadi ca sthiramūlatvāt kṣāradagdhaṃ na śīryate
children.translated_text: But if, because its root is firm, the tissue burnt by <s>kṣāra</s> does not slough off,
then one should apply to it a paste of fermented grain-water, seeds, yaṣṭyāhva, and sesame.
Sesame paste mixed with licorice and smeared with ghee promotes the healing of the wound.
When it is depressed, black like a ripe jambu fruit, that is properly burnt; in the contrary case,
if it is badly burnt, with coppery color, pricking pain, itching, and the like, one should burn it again.
When it is over-burnt, blood flows, and fainting, burning, fever, and similar symptoms occur.
Especially in the rectum there is obstruction of feces and urine, or excessive discharge.
There is impairment of virility, or certainly death from the falling away of the rectum.
In the nose there arises splitting of the nasal bridge and contraction,
and there may be loss of perception of the sense-object; likewise also in the ear and the other organs.

children.text: viśeṣād atra seko 'mlair lepo madhu ghṛtaṃ tilāḥ
children.translated_text: Here especially there should be sprinkling with sour substances, a paste, honey, ghee, and sesame,
and every activity that alleviates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and every cooling procedure.

children.text: amlo hi śītaḥ sparśena kṣāras tenopasaṃhitaḥ
children.translated_text: For sour substance is cool to the touch, and by it <s>kṣāra</s> is counteracted.
It quickly comes to sweetness; therefore one should quench it further with sour substances.
<s>Kṣāra</s> (alkali), used too little or too much, becomes like poison, fire, a weapon, lightning, and death.

children.text: rogān nihanyād acireṇa ghorān sa dhīmatā samyag anuprayuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when properly applied by the intelligent physician, it quickly destroys terrible diseases.

children.text: agniḥ kṣārād api śreṣṭhas taddagdhānām asaṃbhavāt
children.translated_text: Fire is superior even to alkali, because diseases burned by it do not recur,
and because it completes the treatment of those not cured by medicines, alkali, and surgical instruments.
It is applied to the skin, flesh, vessels, sinews, joints, and bones,
in moles, wasting of the limbs, headache, mantha, corns, sesame-like spots, and the like.
Burning of the skin is done with a wick, cow's tooth, sun-crystal, arrow, and similar things,
in hemorrhoids, fistula, tumors, sinus tracts, bad wounds, and the like.
Burning of flesh is done with honey, fat, jambū fruit, lip-shaped metal, molasses, and the like,
in adhesion of the eyelid, bleeding, blue discoloration, improper puncture, and similar cases.
Burning of vessels and the rest is done with those same means. One should not cauterize those forbidden for alkali,
nor those with a foreign body inside, those bleeding, those with ruptured abdominal viscera, or those afflicted by many wounds.
When well burned, it should be anointed with ghee and honey and covered with unctuous, cooling applications.
Its sign, when the blood has stopped, is that it has the sound and lymph-like fluid,
has the appearance of a ripe palmyra fruit or dove, heals well, and is not excessively painful.
In the case of insufficiently burned and excessively burned wounds, everything is as in accidental burns.

children.text: caturdhā tat tu tucchena saha tucchasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: That is fourfold together with the superficial one; the sign of the superficial burn is this:
the skin is greatly discolored and heated, and no blister arises.
A badly burned wound has blisters, burning, and intense heat because of excessive burning.
Hanging of flesh, contraction, burning, fumigating pain,
destruction of vessels and the rest, thirst, fainting, depth of the wound, and death are signs of over-burning.
For a superficial burn, heating by fire and warm medicine should be done.
When the blood is congealed, pain is excessive; when it has melted, the pain becomes slight.

children.text: durdagdhe śītam uṣṇaṃ ca yuñjyād ādau tato himam ||
children.translated_text: In a badly burned wound one should apply both cold and hot at first, and then cold.
When it is properly burned, one should smear it with tavakṣīrī, plakṣa, sandalwood, and red ochre,
together with ghee and amṛtā; afterwards the treatment is as for a bilious abscess.
When it is excessively burned, one should quickly do everything as for bilious erysipelas.

children.text: snehadagdhe bhṛśataraṃ rūkṣaṃ tatra tu yojayet
children.translated_text: When it is burned by fat, a much more drying treatment should be applied there.
Since surgical instruments, alkali, and fire are the supreme weapon of death,

children.text: apramatto bhiṣak tasmāt tān samyag avacārayet ||
children.translated_text: therefore the physician, being attentive, should apply them properly.
This section of the <s>Hṛdaya</s>, like a secret teaching, is completed.

children.text: atrārthāḥ sūtritāḥ sūkṣmāḥ pratanyante hi sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the subtle matters have been stated in aphoristic form, for they are expanded everywhere.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the bodily section on the descent of the embryo.
Thus indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
When semen and menstrual blood are pure, the being, impelled by its own karma and afflictions,
becomes an embryo through the force of proper conjunction, like fire in two fire-sticks.
With subtle great elements in the form of seed and accompanied by the being,
and with elements produced from the mother's nutritive essence, it gradually grows in the womb.
Just as the brilliance of the sun's rays, though blocked by crystal,

children.text: nendhanaṃ dṛśyate gacchat sattvo garbhāśayaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: is not seen moving to fuel, so the being goes to the womb unseen.
Because effects conform to their causes, they have the nature of those causes.
Therefore the being assumes various wombs and forms, like quickly melting metal.

children.text: ata eva ca śukrasya bāhulyāj jāyate pumān
children.translated_text: For this very reason, from the predominance of semen a male is born,

children.text: raktasya strī tayoḥ sāmye klībaḥ śukrārtave punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from that of blood a female, and when the two are equal, a neuter; again, when the semen and menstrual blood
are repeatedly divided by wind, there is multiple offspring, each according to its own division.
Malformed beings and distorted forms are born from vitiated impurities.

children.text: māsi māsi rajaḥ strīṇāṃ rasajaṃ sravati tryaham
children.translated_text: The monthly blood of women, produced from nutritive essence, flows for three days,

children.text: vatsarād dvādaśād ūrdhvaṃ yāti pañcāśataḥ kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: after the twelfth year and up to the fiftieth year, when it reaches cessation.
A woman who has completed sixteen years, united with a man who has completed twenty,

children.text: śuddhe garbhāśaye mārge rakte śukre 'nile hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: when the uterus, passage, blood, semen, wind, and heart are pure,

children.text: vīryavantaṃ sutaṃ sūte tato nyūnābdayoḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: bears a strong son. But from those of fewer years

children.text: rogyalpāyuradhanyo vā garbho bhavati naiva vā ||
children.translated_text: the embryo is diseased, short-lived, unfortunate, or else does not arise at all.
Semen and blood unfit as seed, called corpse-smelling, knotty, pus-like, deficient, and fecal,
should be declared doṣa-produced by their respective marks.
With blood it is corpse-smelling; with phlegm and wind it resembles a knot.
With blood and bile it is pus-like; with wind and bile it is deficient.
These are difficult to cure, but that produced by all three doṣas, resembling urine and feces, is incurable.

children.text: kuryād vātādibhir duṣṭe svauṣadhaṃ kuṇape punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When semen or menstrual blood is vitiated by wind and the other doṣas, one should apply its own medicine; again, in the corpse-smelling type,
one should make the patient drink ghee prepared with dhātakī flowers, khadira, pomegranate, and arjuna,
or else cooked with asana and similar drugs.
In the knot-like type and in pus-like semen, one should use palāśa ash and aśmabhid.
In the deficient type, with parūṣaka, vaṭa, and similar drugs, the treatment is one that produces semen.
When purified, in the feces-like type one should drink ghee prepared with hiṅgu, sevya, and similar drugs.
In knotty menstrual blood one should drink water prepared from pāṭhā, the three pungents, and vṛkṣaka.

children.text: peyaṃ kuṇapapūyāsre candanaṃ vakṣyate tu yat
children.translated_text: In corpse-smelling and pus-like menstrual blood, sandalwood is to be drunk, as will be taught

children.text: guhyaroge ca tat sarvaṃ kāryaṃ sottaravastikam ||
children.translated_text: in the section on diseases of the genitals; all that treatment should be done together with a superior enema.

children.text: śukraṃ śuklaṃ guru snigdhaṃ madhuraṃ bahalaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: Semen suitable for a good embryo is white, heavy, unctuous, sweet, thick, abundant,
and like ghee, honey, or oil; menstrual blood, again,
is like lac-juice or hare's blood, and when washed it becomes stainless.
A healthy couple, with pure semen and menstrual blood and mutually impassioned,
having been made unctuous by fats and male-producing rites, purified, and accustomed to enemas,
should especially treat the man with milk and ghee prepared with sweet medicines,
and should treat the woman with oil, black gram, and bile-promoting substances.
She is thin, with a clear face and quivering hips and breasts;
with loosened eyes and abdomen, and desirous of a man: one should know such a woman to be in her fertile period.

children.text: padmaṃ saṃkocam āyāti dine 'tīte yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: Just as a lotus contracts when the day has passed,

children.text: ṛtāvatīte yoniḥ sā śukraṃ nātaḥ pratīcchati
children.translated_text: so, when the fertile period has passed, that uterus no longer receives semen.
The blood accumulated over the month, at the season again, through the two vessels,

children.text: īṣatkṛṣṇaṃ vigandhaṃ ca vāyur yonimukhān nudet
children.translated_text: slightly dark and without foul smell, wind drives out from the mouth of the vagina.
Then, merely from seeing the menstrual flow, she should think auspicious thoughts for three days,
without cleansing or adornment, lying on a bed spread with darbha grass.
She should eat a little milk-preparation and barley gruel, reducing and purifying the bowels,

children.text: parṇe śarāve haste vā bhuñjīta brahmacāriṇī
children.translated_text: from a leaf, an earthen bowl, or her hand, while observing chastity.
Then on the fourth day, having bathed, wearing white garlands and garments, and being pure,

children.text: icchantī bhartṛsadṛśaṃ putraṃ paśyet puraḥ patim
children.translated_text: desiring a son like her husband, she should look at her husband before her.

children.text: ṛtus tu dvādaśa niśāḥ pūrvās tisro 'tra ninditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fertile period is twelve nights; the first three of these are censured,

children.text: ekādaśī ca yugmāsu syāt putro 'nyāsu kanyakā
children.translated_text: and the eleventh as well. On the even nights there will be a son; on the others, a daughter.
Then the preceptor should perform, according to rule, the rite for obtaining a son;
for a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, who is intent on respectful salutation, it is performed without mantras.

children.text: avandhya evaṃ saṃyogaḥ syād apatyaṃ ca kāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way the union is not barren, and the offspring is as desired.
For good people say that the private union of husband and wife is for the sake of offspring.
Bad offspring, though born in a great lineage, is a firebrand of the family.
Whatever sort of son the two desire, they should think of people of that form and conduct,
and of regions, customs, and dress of that same kind.
At the end of the rite, the man, having eaten rice cooked with ghee, milk, and śāli rice,
should mount the bed first with the right foot, at the astrologer's instruction,

children.text: ārohet strī tu vāmena tasya dakṣiṇapārśvataḥ
children.translated_text: and the woman with the left foot, on his right side.
Having taken food rich in oil and black gram, one should apply this mantra there:

children.text: oṃ āhirasy āyurasi sarvataḥ pratiṣṭhāsi dhātā tvām
children.translated_text: Oṃ, you are the serpent, you are life, you are established on every side. May <s>Dhātṛ</s>

children.text: dadhātu vidhātā tvāṃ dadhātu brahmavarcasā bhaveti
children.translated_text: place you; may <s>Vidhātṛ</s> place you. Be endowed with sacred brilliance.

children.text: brahmā bṛhaspatir viṣṇuḥ somaḥ sūryas tathāśvinau
children.translated_text: May <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and the two <s>Aśvins</s>,

children.text: bhago 'tha mitrāvaruṇau vīraṃ dadatu me sutam ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, give me a heroic son.
Then, having comforted one another, the two should lie together filled with joy.

children.text: uttānā tanmanā yoṣit tiṣṭhed aṅgaiḥ susaṃsthitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The woman should remain on her back, intent on that, with her limbs well arranged;

children.text: tathā hi bījaṃ gṛhṇāti doṣaiḥ svasthānam āsthitaiḥ
children.translated_text: for in that way she receives the seed, with the doṣas remaining in their proper places.

children.text: liṅgaṃ tu sadyogarbhāyā yonyā bījasya saṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sign of immediate conception is the retention of the seed in the vagina,
satisfaction, heaviness, throbbing, and the cessation of semen and blood,
palpitation of the heart, drowsiness, thirst, fatigue, and horripilation.
In the first month the embryo is indistinct; after a week it becomes a gelatinous mass.
Before its manifestation, one should apply puṃsavana rites in this case,
for vigorous human effort even overcomes fate.
Under <s>Puṣya</s>, making a little male figure of gold, silver, or iron,
heating it to the color of fire and quenching it in milk, she should drink a handful of that milk.
Gauradaṇḍa, apāmārga, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, and sairayaka,
ground in water under <s>Puṣya</s>, she should drink singly, in pairs, in threes, or all together.
The root of white bṛhatī with milk should be poured by her into a nostril:
into the right for a son, and into the left if she desires a daughter.
The root of lakṣmaṇā with milk gives birth and stability to a son,
and likewise eight shoots of vaṭa, drunk through the nose or mouth.
She should use life-promoting herbs externally and internally.
The pregnant woman should be attended by her husband and servants with things pleasant and wholesome;
and he should always care for her with fresh butter, ghee, and milk.
She should avoid excessive intercourse, exertion, carrying loads, heavy coverings,
untimely waking and sleep, and hard or excessively high seats,
grief, anger, fear, agitation, and suppression of urges and cravings,
fasting, travel, and sharp, hot, heavy, and constipating food,
red garments, looking into pits and wells, liquor, meat,

children.text: uttānaśayanaṃ yacca striyo necchanti tat tyajet ||
children.translated_text: lying on her back, and whatever else women do not desire.

children.text: tathā raktasrutiṃ śuddhiṃ vastim ā māsato 'ṣṭamāt
children.translated_text: Similarly, until the eighth month, she should avoid bloodletting, purgation, and enema;

children.text: ebhir garbhaḥ sraved āmaḥ kukṣau śuṣyen mriyeta vā ||
children.translated_text: by these the immature embryo may miscarry, dry up in the womb, or die.
From wind-provoking substances the embryo may become hunchbacked, blind, dull, or dwarfish;

children.text: pittalaiḥ khalatiḥ piṅgaḥ śvitrī pāṇḍuḥ kaphātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: from bile-provoking substances, bald, tawny, or leucodermic; from phlegm-producing substances, pale.
One should overcome her diseases with medicines that are mild, pleasant, and not sharp.
In the second month, from the gelatinous mass comes a solid mass, a lump of flesh, or a tumor-like form;

children.text: puṃstrīklībāḥ kramāt tebhyas tatra vyaktasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: from these respectively come male, female, and neuter embryos. When it has become manifest, the signs are:
emaciation, heaviness of the abdomen, fainting, vomiting, and anorexia,
yawning, salivation, languor, and the appearance of the line of hair,
desire for sour things, full breasts with milk and black nipples,
swelling of the feet, burning, and various other cravings.

children.text: mātṛjaṃ hyasya hṛdayaṃ mātuśca hṛdayena tat ||
children.translated_text: For the embryo's heart is maternal, and it is connected with the mother's heart;
therefore a pregnant woman's craving should not be disregarded.
Even what is unwholesome should be given to her, made wholesome, in small amount;
because from thwarting a craving there may be deformity of the embryo or even miscarriage.
In its third month the five bodily parts become manifest:

children.text: mūrdhā dve sakthinī bāhū sarvasūkṣmāṅgajanma ca
children.translated_text: the head, the two thighs, and the arms, and the origin of all the subtle limbs.

children.text: samam eva hi mūrdhādyair jñānaṃ ca sukhaduḥkhayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with the head and the rest, awareness of pleasure and pain also arises.

children.text: garbhasya nābhau mātuśca hṛdi nāḍī nibadhyate
children.translated_text: A vessel is bound between the embryo's navel and the mother's heart,

children.text: yayā sa puṣṭim āpnoti kedāra iva kulyayā ||
children.translated_text: by which it obtains nourishment, like a field by an irrigation channel.
In the fourth month the limbs become distinct, and in the fifth consciousness becomes manifest.
In the sixth month the tendons, vessels, hair, strength, complexion, nails, and skin become distinct.
In the seventh month, complete in all limbs and with all conditions present, the fetus develops.
The <s>doṣas</s>, compressed by the embryo, take refuge in the heart at that time,

children.text: kaṇḍūṃ vidāhaṃ kurvanti garbhiṇyāḥ kikkisāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and cause itching, burning, and <s>kikkisā</s> marks in the pregnant woman.
Fresh butter is beneficial there, prepared with jujube water and sweet herbs,

children.text: siddham alpapaṭusnehaṃ laghu svādu ca bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: as is food that is low in salt and fat, light, and sweet.
One should anoint the thighs, breasts, and abdomen with a paste of sandalwood and uśīra,
mixed with the best blood of the <s>eṇa</s> antelope, deer, and hare.
After oiling her with oil prepared with aśvaghna leaves, one should massage her,
and then sprinkle her with the juices of paṭola, nimba, mañjiṣṭhā, and surasa.
She should also practice cleansing with water of dārvī and madhuka.
In the eighth month <s>ojas</s> circulates repeatedly, in order, between mother and child.

children.text: tena tau mlānamuditau tatra jāto na jīvati
children.translated_text: Because of this they become alternately languid and cheerful; a child born then does not live,
because its <s>ojas</s> is unstable, and the woman too may be in danger.
At this time she should drink milk-gruel with ghee, and for purification an unctuous enema of ghee
prepared with sweet herbs is proper, likewise for old fecal accumulation.
A decoction of dried radish and sour jujube is recommended,
and an enema prepared with a paste of śatāhvā, with oil, ghee, and rock salt.
When even a single day of that month has passed, thereafter it is the time for delivery;

children.text: varṣād vikārakārī syāt kukṣau vātena dhāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the fetus is held in the womb by wind for a year, it causes disorders.
In the ninth month, unctuous rice with meat broth is recommended,
or gruel with much fat, and the unctuous enema previously stated.

children.text: tata eva picuṃ cāsyā yonau nityaṃ nidhāpayet
children.translated_text: From that same preparation one should also place a tampon in her vagina every day.
Cold bath-water containing broken leaves that alleviate wind is beneficial every day.

children.text: niḥsnehāṅgī na navamān māsāt prabhṛti vāsayet
children.translated_text: From the ninth month onward one should not let her remain with her body unoiled.
If milk appears first in the right breast and she first moves on that side,
if she enjoys questions about male names and longings, and sees males in dreams,

children.text: unnate dakṣiṇe kukṣau garbhe ca parimaṇḍale ||
children.translated_text: if the right side of the abdomen is raised and the fetus is round,

children.text: putraṃ sūte 'nyathā kanyāṃ yā cecchati nṛsaṃgatim
children.translated_text: she gives birth to a son; otherwise to a daughter, as also when she desires union with a man
and is fond of dancing, instruments, music, perfumes, and garlands.

children.text: klībaṃ tatsaṃkare tatra madhyaṃ kukṣeḥ samunnatam
children.translated_text: When those signs are mixed, the child is neuter; in that case the middle of the abdomen is raised.

children.text: yamau pārśvadvayonnāmāt kukṣau droṇyām iva sthite ||
children.translated_text: Twins are indicated by the elevation of both sides, with the abdomen set like a trough.

children.text: prāk caiva navamān māsāt sā sūtigṛham āśrayet
children.translated_text: Before the ninth month she should enter the lying-in house,
in an excellent place, furnished with the necessary equipment, on an auspicious day.
There, surrounded by birth-attendants, she should await delivery.
When delivery is today or tomorrow, there are languor, looseness of the abdomen and eyes, fatigue,
heaviness downward, loss of appetite, salivation, and frequent urination,
pain in the thighs, abdomen, waist, back, heart, bladder, and groins,
and splitting pain, piercing pain, throbbing, and discharge in the vagina.
After this comes the occurrence of labor pains, and then the flow of the fetal waters.
Then, when the fetus is ready to be born, she should be adorned with protective and auspicious rites,
holding in her hand a fruit with a male name, well anointed and sprinkled with warm water.

children.text: pāyayet saghṛtāṃ peyāṃ tanau bhūśayane sthitām
children.translated_text: One should make her drink gruel with ghee while she lies on a thin bed on the ground,
with her thighs bent and face upward, her body being anointed again and again.
One should massage below the navel and make her yawn and walk about.
In this way the fetus goes downward; the sign of this is release from the region of the heart.
Having entered the abdomen, the fetus stays above the bladder.
When the labor pains hasten her, one should then place her on a bed.

children.text: atha saṃpīḍite garbhe yonim asyāḥ prasārayet
children.translated_text: Then, when the fetus is being pressed down, one should dilate her vagina,

children.text: mṛdupūrvaṃ pravāheta bāḍham ā prasavācca sā ||
children.translated_text: and she should bear down gently at first, then strongly, until delivery.
One should repeatedly encourage her with the words that a son is being born, and with water and fanning air.
In that way the vital breaths, exhausted by the pain of delivery, return.
If the fetus is retained, one should fumigate the vagina with black snake-sloughs,
and have her hold the root of hiraṇyapuṣpī with her hands and feet.
The same should be done with suvarcalā or viśalyā, and also when the placenta has not fallen.
This procedure should be performed, and likewise one should lift her by the arms and shake her.

children.text: kaṭīm ākoṭayet pārṣṇyā sphijau gāḍhaṃ nipīḍayet
children.translated_text: One should strike her waist with the heel and press the buttocks firmly.

children.text: tālukaṇṭhaṃ spṛśed veṇyā mūrdhni dadyāt snuhīpayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should touch the palate and throat with her braid and place snuhī latex on her head.
With bhūrja, lāṅgalikī, tumbī, snake-skin, kuṣṭha, and mustard,
either singly, in pairs, or all together, one should perform vaginal smearing and fumigation.
Or one should make her drink a paste of kuṣṭha and tālīśa with the clear portion of liquor,
or with horse-gram soup, or with bālbaja wine.
With śatāhvā, mustard, ajājī, śigru, tīkṣṇaka, and citraka,
together with hiṅgu, kuṣṭha, and madana, mustard oil prepared in urine and milk

children.text: tailaṃ siddhaṃ hitaṃ pāyau yonyāṃ vāpyanuvāsanam
children.translated_text: is beneficial as an unctuous enema in the rectum or in the vagina.
A decoction enema, made with a paste of śatapuṣpā, vacā, kuṣṭha, kaṇā, and mustard,
with fat and salt, quickly brings down the placenta.

children.text: tatsaṅge hyanilo hetuḥ sā niryātyāśu tajjayāt ||
children.translated_text: For wind is the cause when it is retained, and it comes out quickly when that is subdued.
A skilled woman should remove it with a hand that has been oiled and with trimmed nails.
When the fetus and placenta have been delivered, she should massage the vagina and the body with oil.
But in the head, bladder, and abdominal pain called <s>makkalla</s>, one should make her drink
well-powdered yavakṣāra with ghee or with warm water,
or grain-water with jaggery, the three pungents, trijāta, and karanja.
Then the woman should care for the child according to the regimen for infant care.

children.text: sūtikā kṣudvatī tailād ghṛtād vā mahatīṃ pibet
children.translated_text: When hungry, the puerperal woman should drink a large dose of oil or ghee
cooked with pañcakola, followed by warm jaggery-water.

children.text: vātaghnauṣadhatoyaṃ vā tathā vāyur na kupyati
children.translated_text: Or [she should use] water boiled with medicines that pacify <s>vāta</s>; in this way <s>vāta</s> does not become aggravated.

children.text: viśudhyati ca duṣṭāsraṃ dvitrirātram ayaṃ kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the corrupted blood is purified. This is the procedure for two or three nights.

children.text: snehāyogyā tu niḥsneham amum eva vidhiṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: But a woman unfit for oleation should follow this same procedure without fat.
After she has drunk it, her abdomen should be wrapped with a bandage smeared with mixed fat.
When it has been digested, after bathing she should drink thin gruel prepared with the previously mentioned medicines.
After three days, [she may take] gruel prepared with a decoction of the group beginning with <s>vidārī</s>.
A gruel rich in fat is beneficial, or, according to what is habitual for her, with milk.

children.text: saptarātrāt paraṃ cāsyai kramaśo bṛṃhaṇaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: After seven nights, gradual nourishing treatment is beneficial for her.
Before twelve days have passed, meat should not be used.
One should treat the puerperal woman with care, for at that time her illness is hard to cure,
because of fetal growth, the pain of delivery, moisture, blood flow, and pressure.
Thus, after a month and a half, she is released from restrictions on food and the like,
and, after menstruation appears again, she is no longer designated a puerperal woman.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the bodily section on disorders of pregnancy.
Thus indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
When a pregnant woman resorts to things that should be avoided, or because of disease,
if bleeding is seen or pain occurs, she should use unctuous and cooling measures externally and internally.
She should apply substances smeared with paste and ghee made from lotus, cooling herbs, and milky-barked trees,
and she should hold moist plugs and cloth-pads in the vagina and by way of the <s>basti</s>.
The woman, anointed with hundred-times-washed ghee, should be immersed in that water.
She should lick milk and ghee with sugar, honey, and filaments of <s>kumuda</s>, <s>kamala</s>, and <s>utpala</s>,
and she should eat <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s> and <s>kaseruka</s>.
She should drink milk prepared with lotus stalk, <s>śālūka</s>, and tender <s>udumbara</s>,
boiled together with <s>śāli</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, the two <s>balā</s>s, <s>madhuka</s>, and sugarcane.
With that milk she should eat red <s>śāli</s> rice, together with honey and sugar.

children.text: rasair vā jāṅgalaiḥ śuddhivarjaṃ cāsroktam ācaret
children.translated_text: Or she may eat it with meat soups of wild animals; and, except for purificatory treatment, the measures stated for bleeding should be performed.
If the pregnancy has not completed three months, one should treat her after declaring the prognosis guarded.
When there is association with <s>āma</s>, cold treatment combined with drying measures is preferred.
Fasting is useful, and [decoctions of] <s>ghana</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>aralu</s>, and <s>dhānyaka</s>,
together with <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, sandalwood, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
boiled in water, are for drinking; grass-grains are to be used as food.
When the <s>āma</s> has been overcome by soups of <s>mudga</s> and the like, unctuous measures and the rest are to be used as before.

children.text: garbhe nipatite tīkṣṇaṃ madyaṃ sāmarthyataḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: When the embryo has fallen, she should drink strong wine according to her strength,
for the purification of the womb cavity and for the forgetting of pain.

children.text: laghunā pañcamūlena rūkṣāṃ peyāṃ tataḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Then she should drink a drying thin gruel made with the light <s>pañcamūla</s>.
A woman who does not drink wine should take thin gruel prepared with a paste of the <s>pañcakaulika</s> group,
with sesame and <s>uddālaka</s> grains in a decoction of the five drugs beginning with <s>bilva</s>.
After miscarriage, this regimen beginning with thin gruel should be followed for just as many days as there were months [of pregnancy].
It is beneficial when light, with little meat soup, fat, and salt, and joined with appetite-kindling substances.
This procedure is for drying up the excess moisture of the <s>doṣa</s>s and tissues.
Afterwards, fats, food, and enemas that strengthen, kindle digestion, and restore vitality are used.
When the embryo has acquired substance and is large, because of vaginal discharge,

children.text: vṛddhim aprāpnuvan garbhaḥ koṣṭhe tiṣṭhati sasphuraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the embryo, failing to grow, remains in the abdomen with movement.

children.text: upaviṣṭakam āhus taṃ vardhate tena nodaram
children.translated_text: They call that condition <s>upaviṣṭaka</s>; because of it, the abdomen does not increase.
Or, because of grief, fasting, drying factors, and the like, or because of excessive vaginal discharge,

children.text: vāte kruddhe kṛśaḥ śuṣyed garbho nāgodaraṃ tu tam
children.translated_text: when <s>vāta</s> is aggravated the emaciated embryo dries up; that is called <s>nāgodara</s>.

children.text: udaraṃ vṛddham apyatra hīyate sphuraṇaṃ cirāt ||
children.translated_text: In that condition, even though the abdomen has enlarged, the movement diminishes after a long time.
For those two conditions, satiation should be given with ghee, milk, and meat soups prepared with nourishing, <s>vāta</s>-pacifying, sweet substances,
and she should be made to eat <s>āmagarbha</s> preparations made with those same substances.
For a well-fed woman, stimulation by carts and mounts should also be done with those same measures.
In the condition called <s>līna</s>, where there is no movement, soups of <s>śyena</s>, <s>gomatsya</s>, <s>utkrośa</s>, and <s>barhija</s>,
rich in ghee, should be given, and also soups made from black gram and radish.

children.text: bālabilvaṃ tilān māṣān saktūṃśca payasā pibet ||
children.translated_text: She should drink tender <s>bilva</s>, sesame, black gram, and roasted flour with milk.

children.text: samedyamāṃsaṃ madhu vā kaṭyabhyaṅgaṃ ca śīlayet
children.translated_text: Or she may take honey with fatty meat, and she should regularly practice massage of the waist.

children.text: harṣayet satataṃ cainām evaṃ garbhaḥ pravardhate ||
children.translated_text: One should constantly gladden her; in this way the embryo grows.

children.text: puṣṭo 'nyathā varṣagaṇaiḥ kṛcchrāj jāyeta naiva vā
children.translated_text: Otherwise, even if nourished, it may be born only with difficulty after years, or not at all.
<s>Udāvarta</s> in a pregnant woman should be overcome very quickly with fats,

children.text: yogyaiśca vastibhir hanyāt sagarbhāṃ sa hi garbhiṇīm
children.translated_text: and should be destroyed with suitable enemas, for it kills the pregnant woman together with the fetus.
When, because of excessive accumulation of <s>doṣa</s>s in the fetus, because of unwholesome conduct, or even because of fate,
the fetus has died, the inside of the abdomen is cold, rigid, distended, and intensely painful.
There is no fetal movement, and there are dizziness, thirst, difficult breathing, and fatigue,
restlessness, fallen eyes, and no arising of labor pains.
For such a woman, after she has been sprinkled with warm water, one should grind [the drugs] and smear the vagina,

children.text: guḍaṃ kiṇvaṃ salavaṇaṃ tathāntaḥ pūrayen muhuḥ
children.translated_text: and repeatedly fill the interior with jaggery, ferment, and salt,
and with the pith of <s>śālmalī</s> and flax made into a paste with ghee.

children.text: mantrair yogair jarāyūktair mūḍhagarbho na cet patet
children.translated_text: If the obstructed fetus does not fall by the mantras and methods stated for the placenta,
then, after asking the ruler's permission, the physician should quickly and carefully remove it.
Having anointed his hand and the vagina with ghee and <s>śālmalī</s> pith,

children.text: hastena śakyaṃ tenaiva gātraṃ ca viṣamaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: with the hand itself, if it is possible, he should deal with the limb that is positioned irregularly,
by drawing, pressing down, squeezing, shifting, lifting, and similar actions.
Having brought it into the natural direction, he should draw it out when it has come straight toward the vagina.
The two obstructed presentations in which the fetus enters the vagina bent, one with hands, feet, and head,

children.text: pādena yonim ekena bhugno 'nyena gudaṃ ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the other bent with one foot in the vagina and the other in the anus,

children.text: viṣkambhau nāma tau mūḍhau śastradāraṇam arhataḥ
children.translated_text: are called <s>viṣkambha</s>; those two obstructed cases require cutting with instruments.
In that case, the procedure with the <s>maṇḍalāgra</s> and <s>aṅguliśastra</s> instruments is recommended.
For the <s>vṛddhipattra</s>, since it has a sharp point, should not be inserted into the vagina.
First, having split open the bones of the head, he should clear them out.
Then, taking firm hold at any one place, the armpit, chest, palate, or chin,
the skilled physician should draw it out with a fetal hook.
But if its head is unbroken, [he should grasp it] at the eye sockets or also at the cheeks;
if it is caught by the shoulder, he should cut off the arm, and if its abdomen is swollen by <s>vāta</s>,

children.text: vidārya koṣṭham antrāṇi bahir vā saṃnirasya ca
children.translated_text: he should open the abdominal cavity and draw the intestines out, or cast them outside,
and likewise when it is caught at the hips; he should split those bones.

children.text: yad yad vāyuvaśād aṅgaṃ sajed garbhasya khaṇḍaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever limb of the fetus becomes stuck, piece by piece, under the control of wind,

children.text: tat tacchittvāharet samyag rakṣen nārīṃ ca yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should cut off that very limb and remove it properly, and should carefully protect the woman.

children.text: garbhasya hi gatiṃ citrāṃ karoti viguṇo 'nilaḥ
children.translated_text: For disordered <s>anila</s> (wind) makes the movement of the fetus varied;
therefore one of considerable intelligence should act with regard to the particular condition.
