children.text: chindyād garbhaṃ na jīvantaṃ mātaraṃ sa hi mārayet
children.translated_text: He should not cut up a living fetus, for that would kill the mother;
but when its life has departed, it should not be neglected for even a moment.
One should abandon a woman with obstructed labor who is afflicted by prolapse or failure of the vaginal closure, makkalla pain, and dyspnea,
and who has foul belching and cold limbs.
Then, if the afterbirth does not fall, the physician should make it fall as before.

children.text: evaṃ nirhṛtaśalyāṃ tu siñced uṣṇena vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: When the foreign body has thus been removed, he should sprinkle her with warm water.
Then, after her body has been anointed, he should place an oil-soaked tampon in the vagina.

children.text: yonir mṛdur bhavet tena śūlaṃ cāsyāḥ praśāmyati ||
children.translated_text: By that the vagina becomes soft and her pain subsides.
From dīpyaka, ativiṣā, rāsnā, hiṅgu, elā, and pañcakola,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ snehena kalkaṃ vā kvāthaṃ vā pāyayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should administer a powder with fat, or a paste, or a decoction, and then have her drink it.
Likewise [he should use] kaṭukā, ativiṣā, pāṭhā, śāka bark, hiṅgu, and tejinī
for the draining of the <s>doṣas</s> and also for the calming of pain.

children.text: trirātram evaṃ saptāhaṃ sneham eva tataḥ pibet
children.translated_text: Thus for three nights; then for a week she should drink only fat,

children.text: sāyaṃ pibed ariṣṭaṃ ca tathā sukṛtam āsavam ||
children.translated_text: and in the evening she should drink ariṣṭa, and likewise a well-prepared āsava.
He should insert tampons with a decoction of śirīṣa and kakubha into the vagina,

children.text: upadravāśca ye 'nye syus tān yathāsvam upācaret ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other complications may arise, he should treat each according to its own method.

children.text: payo vātaharaiḥ siddhaṃ daśāhaṃ bhojane hitam
children.translated_text: Milk cooked with <s>vāta</s>-alleviating drugs is beneficial in food for ten days,
and meat broth for another ten days; after that she should take light, wholesome, small meals.
Intent on sudation and oil massage, she should use fats such as balā oil,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ caturbhyo māsebhyaḥ sā krameṇa sukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and after four months she may gradually enjoy comforts.
Six parts of a decoction of balā root, and the same amount of milk,
with one part of a decoction of yava, kola, kulattha, and daśamūla together,
and one part of oil, with the decoction making fourteen parts,
together with dvimedā, dāru, mañjiṣṭhā, the two kākolīs, and candana,
with śārivā, kuṣṭha, tagara, jīvaka, ṛṣabha, and saindhava,
with kālānusārī, śaileya, vacā, aguru, and punarnavā,
with aśvagandhā, varī, kṣīraśuklā, yaṣṭī, and varā juices,
and with śatāhvā, śūrpaparṇī, elā, tvak, and pattra, ground to a smooth paste:
oil cooked over a gentle fire conquers all disorders of <s>vāta</s>.
It is esteemed for postpartum women, children, and those whose vital points, bones, or milk have been injured or depleted.
It conquers fever, abdominal tumor, graha, insanity, retention of urine, and enlargement of the intestines;
approved by <s>Dhanvantari</s>, it removes diseases of the vagina and wasting.
If the abdomen of a woman who has died at the bladder-opening throbs
at the time of birth, then he should quickly cut it open and extract the child.

children.text: madhukaṃ śākabījaṃ ca payasyā suradāru ca
children.translated_text: Madhuka, śāka seed, payasyā, and suradāru;
aśmantaka, black sesame, tāmravallī, and śatāvarī;
vṛkṣādanī, payasyā, and the creeper with utpala and śārivā;

children.text: anantā śārivā rāsnā padmā ca madhuyaṣṭikā ||
children.translated_text: anantā, śārivā, rāsnā, padmā, and madhuyaṣṭikā;
the two bṛhatīs, kāśmarya, and ghee with the bark of kṣīriśuṅga;
pṛśniparṇī, balā, śigru, śvadaṃṣṭrā, and madhuparṇikā;

children.text: śṛṅgāṭakaṃ bisaṃ drākṣā kaśeru madhukaṃ sitā
children.translated_text: śṛṅgāṭaka, bisa, drākṣā, kaśeru, madhuka, and sugar;
these seven formulations, completed in half-verses and prepared with milk,

children.text: kramāt saptasu māseṣu garbhe sravati yojayet
children.translated_text: should be employed in order in the seven months when there is discharge during pregnancy.
From the roots of kapittha, bilva, bṛhatī, paṭola, sugarcane, and nidigdhikā,

children.text: mūlaiḥ śṛtaṃ prayuñjīta kṣīraṃ māse tathāṣṭame
children.translated_text: one should use milk boiled with them in the eighth month.
In the ninth month [milk should be prepared] with śārivā, anantā, payasyā, and madhuyaṣṭi,

children.text: yojayed daśame māsi siddhaṃ kṣīraṃ payasyayā
children.translated_text: and in the tenth month milk prepared with payasyā should be prescribed,
or else with yaṣṭimadhuka, nāgara, and amaradāru.

children.text: avasthitaṃ lohitam aṅganāyā vātena garbhaṃ bruvate 'nabhijñāḥ
children.translated_text: The ignorant call blood retained in a woman by <s>vāta</s> an embryo;

children.text: garbhākṛtitvāt kaṭukoṣṇatīkṣṇaiḥ srute punaḥ kevala eva rakte ||
children.translated_text: because it has the shape of an embryo, while, when made to flow by pungent, hot, and sharp substances, it is only blood.

children.text: garbhaṃ jaḍā bhūtahṛtaṃ vadanti mūrter na dṛṣṭaṃ haraṇaṃ yatas taiḥ
children.translated_text: Fools say that an embryo has been seized by spirits, because they have not seen its form being carried off by them;

children.text: ojo'śanatvād athavāvyavasthair bhūtair upekṣyeta na garbhamātā ||
children.translated_text: or, because unstable beings feed on <s>ojas</s>, the pregnant mother should not be neglected.
The head, the trunk, the two arms, and the two thighs: in brief,
the body has six limbs; its subsidiary limbs are the eyes, heart, and the rest.

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaḥ kramād guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are the qualities in order
of ether, wind, fire, water, and earth; the latter follow with an increase of one quality.

children.text: tatra khāt khāni dehe 'smin śrotraṃ śabdo viviktatā
children.translated_text: There, from ether come the hollow spaces in this body, hearing, sound, and distinctness;
from wind come touch, skin, and exhalation; from fire, sight, form, and digestion;
from water come the tongue, taste, and moisture; from earth come the nose, smell, bones, and what is earthy.
The soft parts here are maternal: blood, flesh, marrow, anus, and so on;
but the stable parts are paternal: semen, vessels, bones, hair, and the like.

children.text: caitanaṃ cittam akṣāṇi nānāyoniṣu janma ca ||
children.translated_text: Consciousness, mind, the sense faculties, and birth in various wombs are from the conscious principle;

children.text: sātmyajaṃ tv āyur ārogyam anālasyaṃ prabhā balam
children.translated_text: from habituation arise lifespan, health, freedom from laziness, radiance, and strength;

children.text: rasajaṃ vapuṣo janma vṛttir vṛddhir alolatā ||
children.translated_text: from nutritive essence arise the birth of the body, maintenance, growth, and steadiness.
Sāttvika traits are purity, faith in what is sacred, and a mind delighted in bright <s>dharma</s>.
Rājasa traits are excessive speech, pride, anger, deceit, and jealousy.
Tāmasa traits are fear, ignorance, sleep, laziness, and despondency.

children.text: iti bhūtamayo dehas tatra sapta tvaco 'sṛjaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the body is made of the elements. In it, the seven skins arise from blood
as it is being cooked, like the layer of cream from milk.
The moisture between the <s>dhātu</s>s and receptacles, cooked by each one's own heat,
covered by phlegm, sinew, and membrane, is called <s>kalā</s>, like the pith of wood.

children.text: tāḥ sapta sapta cādhārā raktasyādyaḥ kramāt pare ||
children.translated_text: They are seven, and in order the seven supports are remembered: first that of blood, and the others
of <s>kapha</s>, raw matter, <s>pitta</s>, feces, <s>vāyu</s>, and urine.
For women, the uterus is an eighth, located between the receptacle of <s>pitta</s> and that of feces.

children.text: koṣṭhāṅgāni sthitāny eṣu hṛdayaṃ kloma phupphusam
children.translated_text: Within these are situated the organs of the cavity: the heart, kloma, lungs,
liver, spleen, the unduka, the two kidneys, the navel, the dimbas, intestines, and bladder.
The ten abodes of life are the head, the binding of the tongue,

children.text: kaṇṭho 'sraṃ hṛdayaṃ nābhir vastiḥ śukraujasī gudam ||
children.translated_text: the throat, blood, heart, navel, bladder, semen, <s>ojas</s>, and anus.

children.text: jālāni kaṇḍarāś cāṅge pṛthak ṣoḍaśa nirdiśet
children.translated_text: In the limbs one should separately specify sixteen networks and sixteen tendons,
six kūrcas, and seven sutures situated in the penis, tongue, and head.
One should avoid those sutures with the surgical instrument, as well as the four fleshy cords.
There are fourteen aggregations of bones, and twice nine sutures.

children.text: asthnāṃ śatāni ṣaṣṭiś ca trīṇi dantanakhaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: The bones number three hundred and sixty, including teeth and nails.

children.text: dhanvantaris tu trīṇy āha saṃdhīnāṃ ca śatadvayam ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Dhanvantari</s> says there are three hundred, and two hundred joints.
The son of <s>Atri</s> declared two thousand and ten.

children.text: snāvnāṃ navaśatī pañca puṃsāṃ peśīśatāni tu ||
children.translated_text: There are nine hundred sinews; and in men there are five hundred muscles,
while in women there are twenty more, located in the vagina and breasts.

children.text: daśa mūlasirā hṛtsthās tāḥ sarvaṃ sarvato vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ten root-veins, situated in the heart, carry the whole body everywhere,

children.text: rasātmakaṃ vahanty ojas tannibaddhaṃ hi ceṣṭitam
children.translated_text: which has the nature of nutritive fluid and <s>ojas</s>; for activity is bound to that.
Having thick roots and very fine tips, like the spreading lines of a leaf,

children.text: bhidyante tās tataḥ saptaśatāny āsāṃ bhavanti tu
children.translated_text: they divide; from them there come to be seven hundred veins.

children.text: tatraikaikaṃ ca śākhāyāṃ śataṃ tasmin na vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: Among them, in each branch there are one hundred; in that one should not pierce
the vein called Jālandharā and the three that are situated internally.

children.text: ṣoḍaśadviguṇāḥ śroṇyāṃ tāsāṃ dve dve tu vaṅkṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: In the pelvis there are twice sixteen veins; of these, two in each groin

children.text: dve dve kaṭīkataruṇe śastreṇāṣṭau spṛśen na tāḥ
children.translated_text: and two in each kaṭī-kataruṇa are not to be touched with the instrument, making eight.
On the two sides there are sixteen; on each side one upward-going vein should be avoided.
In the back there are twice twelve, on the two sides of the spinal column.

children.text: dve dve tatrordhvagāminyau na śastreṇa parāmṛśet ||
children.translated_text: There two upward-going veins on each side should not be touched with the surgical instrument.
As in the back, so in the abdomen; among them, above the organ of urination,

children.text: romarājīm ubhayato dve dve śastreṇa na spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: on both sides of the line of hair, two and two should not be touched with the instrument.

children.text: catvāriṃśad urasy āsāṃ caturdaśa na vedhayet
children.translated_text: In the chest there are forty of these; fourteen should not be pierced.
At the breast, Rohita, its root, and the heart, there are two each.
There is one in each of the two called Apastambha, and likewise in the two Apālāpas.

children.text: grīvāyāṃ pṛṣṭhavat tāsāṃ nīle manye kṛkāṭike ||
children.translated_text: In the neck, as in the back, among them at Nīlā, Manyā, Kṛkāṭikā,
Vidhura, and the eight Mātṛkās, sixteen in all are to be avoided.
In the two jaws there are sixteen; of these two perform the function of binding the joint.

children.text: jihvāyāṃ hanuvat tāsām adho dve rasabodhane
children.translated_text: In the tongue, as in the jaw, among them two below perceive taste,
and two set speech in motion. In the nose there are twenty-four;

children.text: viṃśatir gandhavedinyau tāsām ekāṃ ca tālugām
children.translated_text: twenty perceive smell, and among them one goes to the palate.
In the two eyes there are fifty-six, performing the action of closing and opening.

children.text: dve dve apāṅgayor dve ca tāsāṃ ṣaḍ iti varjayet
children.translated_text: Two at each outer corner and two others, six of them in all, should be avoided.
There are sixty connected with the nose and eyes; in the forehead, one situated at Sthapanī,

children.text: tatraikāṃ dve tathāvartau catasraś ca kacāntagāḥ
children.translated_text: two likewise at the two Āvartas, and four ending at the hairline:

children.text: saptaivaṃ varjayet tāsāṃ karṇayoḥ ṣoḍaśātra tu ||
children.translated_text: thus seven of them should be avoided. In the two ears there are sixteen here;

children.text: dve śabdabodhane śaṅkhau sirās tā eva cāśritāḥ
children.translated_text: two perceive sound. The same veins are also situated at the two temples,

children.text: dve śaṅkhasaṃdhige tāsāṃ mūrdhni dvādaśa tatra tu ||
children.translated_text: two going to the temple-joints. Of these, in the head there are twelve, and there
one each, separately situated at Utkṣepa, Sīmanta, and Adhipati, should be avoided.
Thus the veins have been described limb by limb for the purpose of classifying those that must not be pierced.
Among them, in the whole body, ninety-eight are entirely unfit to be pierced.

children.text: saṃkīrṇā grathitāḥ kṣudrā vakrāḥ saṃdhiṣu cāśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those that are mingled, knotted, small, crooked, or situated in the joints

children.text: tāsāṃ śatānāṃ saptānāṃ pādo 'sraṃ vahate pṛthak
children.translated_text: make up one quarter of those seven hundred veins; each carries blood separately,

children.text: vātapittakaphair juṣṭaṃ śuddhaṃ caivaṃ sthitā malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: affected by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and also pure blood. Thus situated, the wastes
support the body; otherwise, again, they afflict it.

children.text: tatra śyāvāruṇāḥ sūkṣmāḥ pūrṇariktāḥ kṣaṇāt sirāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them, dusky-red, fine veins that become full and empty in an instant
and pulsate carry blood affected by <s>vāta</s>; those carrying <s>pitta</s>-blood
are warm to the touch, swift-flowing, and blue-yellow. Those carrying <s>kapha</s>, again,

children.text: gauryaḥ snigdhāḥ sthirāḥ śītāḥ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ liṅgasaṃkare
children.translated_text: are pale, unctuous, stable, and cold; when mixed, the signs are mixed.
Hidden, evenly situated, unctuous, Rohiṇī veins carry pure blood.
The <s>dhamanī</s>s, bound to the navel, are twenty-four.
The navel is surrounded by them, like the nave of a wheel by spokes.

children.text: tābhiś cordhvam adhas tiryag deho 'yam anugṛhyate
children.translated_text: By them this body is supported upward, downward, and crosswise.
The channels are the two nostrils, the two ears, the two eyes, the anus, the mouth, and the organ of urination,

children.text: stanau raktapathaś ceti nārīṇām adhikaṃ trayam
children.translated_text: the two breasts and the path of blood; for women there are three additional.
They say the internal <s>srotas</s> that are seats of life are thirteen:
those carrying breath, <s>dhātu</s>s, wastes, water, and food. Through unwholesome conduct

children.text: tāni duṣṭāni rogāya viśuddhāni sukhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: these, when vitiated, lead to disease, and when purified, to well-being.
The <s>srotas</s> have the same color as their own <s>dhātu</s>; they are round, thick, and minute,
and the channels are long in form and like branching networks.

children.text: āhāraś ca vihāraś ca yaḥ syād doṣaguṇaiḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: Food and conduct that are similar to the qualities of the <s>doṣa</s>s,

children.text: dhātubhir viguṇo yaś ca srotasāṃ sa pradūṣakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but incompatible with the <s>dhātu</s>s, are what vitiate the <s>srotas</s>.

children.text: atipravṛttiḥ saṅgo vā sirāṇāṃ granthayo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Excessive flow, obstruction, or even knots in the veins,
or movement along a wrong path, are the signs of vitiation of the <s>srotas</s>.

children.text: bisānām iva sūkṣmāṇi dūraṃ pravisṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: Like lotus fibers, the openings are minute and extend far;

children.text: dvārāṇi srotasāṃ dehe raso yair upacīyate ||
children.translated_text: they are the openings of the <s>srotas</s> in the body, by which <s>rasa</s> is nourished.
When the <s>srotas</s> are pierced, there are stupor, trembling, distension, vomiting, and fever,
delirium, pain, obstruction of feces and urine, or even death.
Therefore, after declaring the case grave, the physician should treat one whose <s>srotas</s> has been pierced,
carefully extracting the foreign body according to the procedure for fresh wounds.

children.text: annasya paktā pittaṃ tu pācakākhyaṃ pureritam
children.translated_text: <s>Pitta</s>, previously described and called <s>pācaka</s>, is the digester of food;
according to the teaching of <s>Ātreya</s>, it is the heat of the <s>doṣa</s>s, <s>dhātu</s>s, wastes, and the rest.
Its seat is called <s>grahaṇī</s> because it receives food;
in the view of <s>Dhanvantari</s>, this same structure is the membrane called <s>pittadharā</s>.
It is situated at the gate of the <s>pakvāśaya</s>, for the nourishment of life, health, vigor, <s>ojas</s>, the elements, <s>dhātu</s>s, and <s>agni</s>,
like a bolt on the path of swallowed food.

children.text: bhuktam āmāśaye ruddhvā sā vipācya nayaty adhaḥ
children.translated_text: Holding the eaten food in the <s>āmāśaya</s>, it digests it and carries it downward;

children.text: balavaty abalā tv annam āmam eva vimuñcati ||
children.translated_text: when strong it does this, but when weak it releases the food while it is still raw.

children.text: grahaṇyā balam agnir hi sa cāpi grahaṇībalaḥ
children.translated_text: The strength of the <s>grahaṇī</s> is indeed <s>agni</s>, and <s>agni</s> too depends on the strength of the <s>grahaṇī</s>;
therefore, when <s>agni</s> is impaired, the <s>grahaṇī</s>, being impaired, produces disease.
In the case of food that nourishes the bodily <s>dhātu</s>s, <s>ojas</s>, strength, complexion, and so on,

children.text: tatrāgnir hetur āhārān na hy apakvād rasādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>agni</s> is the cause; for <s>rasa</s> and the rest do not arise from undigested food.
Food eaten at the proper time is brought into the alimentary tract by <s>prāṇa</s>-wind,
its compact mass broken up by fluids and made soft by unctuousness.
Kindled by <s>samāna</s>, the abdominal <s>agni</s> digests what is situated in the <s>āmāśaya</s>,
just as an external fire cooks water and rice placed in a pot.

children.text: ādau ṣaḍrasam apy annaṃ madhurībhūtam īrayet
children.translated_text: At first, even though the food has the six tastes, it becomes sweet and produces

children.text: phenībhūtaṃ kaphaṃ yātaṃ vidāhād amlatāṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: foamy <s>kapha</s>; then, from burning, it reaches sourness.

children.text: pittam āmāśayāt kuryāc cyavamānaṃ cyutaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It produces <s>pitta</s> dripping from the <s>āmāśaya</s>; then, when it has descended further,

children.text: agninā śoṣitaṃ pakvaṃ piṇḍitaṃ kaṭu mārutam ||
children.translated_text: dried by <s>agni</s>, digested, and compacted, it becomes pungent and produces <s>māruta</s>.
The five heat-principles, earthy, watery, fiery, airy, and also etheric,

children.text: pañcāhāraguṇān svān svān pārthivādīn pacanty anu ||
children.translated_text: successively digest the five qualities of food, each its own, beginning with the earthy.

children.text: yathāsvaṃ te ca puṣṇanti pakvā bhūtaguṇān pṛthak
children.translated_text: And when digested, each nourishes, according to its own nature, the corresponding elemental qualities separately:

children.text: pārthivāḥ pārthivān eva śeṣāḥ śeṣāṃś ca dehagān ||
children.translated_text: the earthy qualities nourish the earthy ones in the body, and the remaining qualities nourish the remaining ones.

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ sāraś ca tat pakvam annaṃ sambhavati dvidhā
children.translated_text: That digested food becomes twofold, waste and essence;

children.text: tatrācchaṃ kiṭṭam annasya mūtraṃ vidyād ghanam śakṛt ||
children.translated_text: there, the liquid waste of food should be known as urine and the dense waste as feces.

children.text: sāras tu saptabhir bhūyo yathāsvaṃ pacyate 'gnibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The essence, however, is further digested by seven <s>agni</s>s, each in its own sequence:

children.text: rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsaṃ māṃsān medas tato 'sthi ca ||
children.translated_text: from <s>rasa</s> comes blood, then flesh; from flesh comes fat, and from that bone.

children.text: asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukrād garbhaḥ prajāyate
children.translated_text: From bone comes marrow, then semen; from semen an embryo is produced.

children.text: kaphaḥ pittaṃ malāḥ kheṣu prasvedo nakharoma ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, wastes in the openings, sweat, nails and hair,
unctuousness of the eyes, skin, and feces, and <s>ojas</s> are, in order, the wastes of the <s>dhātu</s>s.
Thus, through digestion, the <s>dhātu</s>s attain two forms, refined essence and waste.
Because the <s>dhātu</s>s mutually support one another, some say that the succession of <s>dhātu</s>-nourishment

children.text: kecid āhur ahorātrāt ṣaḍahād apare pare ||
children.translated_text: takes place within a day and night; others say within six days, and still others otherwise.
Through the sequence of digestion and the rest, food reaches the state of semen in a month;
but the transformation of food and <s>dhātu</s>s is continuous, like a wheel.
Aphrodisiacs and the like, through their special potency, produce semen and the rest immediately;

children.text: prāyaḥ karoty ahorātrāt karmānyad api bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: other medicine too generally produces its action within a day and night.
The <s>rasa-dhātu</s> is constantly dispersed throughout the body at once
by <s>vyāna</s>, whose proper function is distribution.

children.text: kṣipyamāṇaḥ khavaiguṇyād rasaḥ sajati yatra saḥ
children.translated_text: As it is being sent forth, wherever <s>rasa</s> lodges because of a defect in a channel,

children.text: tasmin vikāraṃ kurute khe varṣam iva toyadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there it produces a disorder, as a rain-cloud produces rain in the sky.
In just this way there may also be local aggravation of the <s>doṣa</s>s;
this has been defined as the action of food, elements, <s>dhātu</s>s, and <s>agni</s>.

children.text: annasya paktā sarveṣāṃ paktṝṇām adhiko mataḥ
children.translated_text: The digester of food is regarded as the chief among all digesters,
for they are rooted in it and have increase and decrease according to its increase and decrease.

children.text: tasmāt taṃ vidhivad yuktair annapānendhanair hitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore one should carefully protect it, according to rule, with suitable and wholesome foods and drinks as fuel;

children.text: pālayet prayatas tasya sthitau hy āyurbalasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for when it is stable, life and strength are stable.
<s>Agni</s> is balanced when <s>samāna</s> remains in its own place, irregular when it has gone on a wrong path,
sharp when overwhelmed by <s>pitta</s>, and dull when oppressed by <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: samo 'gnir viṣamas tīkṣṇo mandaś caivaṃ caturvidhaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>agni</s> is fourfold: balanced, irregular, sharp, and dull.

children.text: yaḥ pacet samyag evānnaṃ bhuktaṃ samyak samas tv asau ||
children.translated_text: The balanced one is that which properly digests food that has been properly eaten.

children.text: viṣamo 'samyag apy āśu samyag vāpi cirāt pacet
children.translated_text: The irregular one digests improperly, even quickly, or else properly only after a long time.

children.text: tīkṣṇo vahniḥ pacec chīghram asamyag api bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: The sharp fire digests food quickly, even when the eating has been improper.

children.text: mandas tu samyag apy annam upayuktaṃ cirāt pacet
children.translated_text: The dull one, however, digests even properly taken food only after a long time,
producing dryness of the mouth, abdominal gurgling, intestinal rumbling, distension, and heaviness.
Bodily strength is threefold: innate, born of time, and produced by regimen.
Among these, innate strength is the natural strength arising from mind and body.

children.text: vayaḥkṛtam ṛtūtthaṃ ca kālajaṃ yuktijaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Strength produced by age and by season is born of time; that produced by regimen, again,
is generated from conduct and diet, and also from combinations that produce vigor.
A region with little water, few trees, and few mountains is <s>jāṅgala</s>, and has few diseases;
the <s>ānūpa</s> region is the opposite of this, while the balanced region is called <s>sādhāraṇa</s>.
Marrow, fat, muscle-fat, urine, <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, feces, blood,
<s>rasa</s>, and water in this body are each said to increase by one <s>añjali</s>.
<s>Ojas</s>, brain-substance, and semen are each separately said to have their own <s>prasṛta</s> measure.

children.text: dvāv añjalī tu stanyasya catvāro rajasaḥ striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But there are two <s>añjali</s>s of breast milk and four of a woman's menstrual blood.

children.text: samadhātor idaṃ mānaṃ vidyād vṛddhikṣayāv ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: This should be known as the measure for one whose <s>dhātu</s>s are balanced; increase and decrease are to be understood from this.
In semen, blood, the pregnant woman's food and activity, the womb, and the season,

children.text: yaḥ syād doṣo 'dhikas tena prakṛtiḥ saptadhoditā ||
children.translated_text: whichever <s>doṣa</s> is predominant, by that the <s>prakṛti</s> (constitution) is said to be sevenfold.
Because of its pervasiveness, quick action, strength, stimulation of the others,
independence, and production of many diseases, among the <s>doṣa</s>s <s>anila</s> (wind) is the strongest.

children.text: prāyo 'ta eva pavanādhyuṣitā manuṣyā doṣātmakāḥ sphuṭitadhūsarakeśagātrāḥ
children.translated_text: Mostly for this very reason, people occupied by wind, being of that <s>doṣa</s>, have cracked, grayish hair and limbs;
they dislike cold, and their steadiness, memory, intellect, activity, affection, sight, and gait are unstable; they talk excessively.
They have little wealth, strength, life, and sleep, and their speech is depressed, obstructed, unsteady, and broken.
They are unbelieving, eat much, are playful, and are very fond of song, laughter, hunting, and gaming or quarrel.
They desire what is sweet, sour, salty, and hot as suitable to them; they are thin and tall in form and make noise as they move.

children.text: na dṛḍhā na jitendriyā na cāryā na ca kāntādayitā bahuprajā vā ||
children.translated_text: They are not firm, not masters of the senses, not noble, and not beloved by beautiful women, nor do they have many children.

children.text: netrāṇi caiṣāṃ kharadhūsarāṇi vṛttāny acārūṇi mṛtopamāni
children.translated_text: Their eyes are rough and gray, round, unattractive, and like those of the dead;

children.text: unmīlitānīva bhavanti supte śailadrumāṃs te gaganaṃ ca yānti ||
children.translated_text: even in sleep they seem to be open, and in dreams they go among mountains, trees, and the sky.
The <s>vāta</s> type are unfortunate, swollen with envy, thievish, and have prominent calf muscles;
they resemble dogs, jackals, camels, vultures, mice, crows, and the like.

children.text: pittaṃ vahnir vahnijaṃ vā yad asmāt pittodriktas tīkṣṇatṛṣṇābubhukṣaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pitta</s> is fire, or born of fire; therefore one in whom <s>pitta</s> is increased has sharp thirst and hunger.
He is fair or yellowish, hot-bodied, copper-colored in hands, feet, and face, brave, proud, tawny-haired, and scanty-haired.
He loves garlands, unguents, and ornaments, is well-conducted, pure, and affectionate toward dependents.

children.text: vibhavasāhasabuddhibalānvito bhavati bhīṣu gatir dviṣatām api ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with wealth, daring, intelligence, and strength, he becomes a refuge for the fearful and even for enemies.
He is intelligent, with relaxed joints, ligaments, and flesh, not pleasing to women, and has little semen and desire.
He is an abode for gray hair, wrinkles, and dark spots, and he eats food that is sweet, astringent, bitter, and cold.
He hates heat, sweats, smells foul, and is given to much excretion, anger, drinking, eating, and jealousy.

children.text: suptaḥ paśyet karṇikārān palāśān digdāholkāvidyudarkānalāṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: When asleep he sees karṇikāra flowers, palāśa flowers, burning quarters, meteors, lightning, the sun, and fires.

children.text: tanūni piṅgāni calāni caiṣāṃ tanvalpapakṣmāṇi himapriyāṇi
children.translated_text: Their eyes are thin, tawny, and restless, with thin and sparse eyelashes, and they love cold.

children.text: krodhena madyena raveś ca bhāsā rāgaṃ vrajanty āśu vilocanāni ||
children.translated_text: Through anger, liquor, and the sun's radiance their eyes quickly become red.
The <s>pitta</s> type have medium lifespan and medium strength, are compact-bodied, and are afraid of hardship;
they resemble tigers, bears, monkeys, cats, and <s>yakṣa</s>s.

children.text: śleṣmā somaḥ śleṣmalas tena saumyo gūḍhasnigdhaśliṣṭasaṃdhyasthimāṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣmā</s> is <s>Soma</s>; one with <s>śleṣma</s> is therefore gentle, with hidden, unctuous, well-knit joints, bones, and flesh.

children.text: kṣuttṛḍduḥkhakleśagharmair atapto buddhyā yuktaḥ sāttvikaḥ satyasaṃdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is not overcome by hunger, thirst, pain, hardship, or heat; he is endowed with intelligence, sāttvika, and true to his promise.
His color is like priyaṅgu, dūrvā grass, reed-stalk, gorocanā, lotus, or gold.
He has long arms, a broad and full chest, a large forehead, and thick dark-blue hair.
Soft-limbed, with a symmetrical, well-proportioned, beautiful body, he has abundant <s>ojas</s>, pleasure, nutritive fluid, semen, sons, and servants.

children.text: dharmātmā vadati na niṣṭhuraṃ ca jātu pracchannaṃ vahati dṛḍhaṃ ciraṃ ca vairam ||
children.translated_text: He is righteous and never speaks harshly; yet he bears hidden enmity firmly and for a long time.
His gait is like that of a noble rutting elephant, and his voice is like a cloud, ocean, drum, or lion.

children.text: smṛtimān abhiyogavān vinīto na ca bālye 'py atirodano na lolaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is mindful, energetic, and modest; even in childhood he is not overly tearful or fickle.

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ kaṭukoṣṇarūkṣam alpaṃ sa bhuṅkte balavāṃs tathāpi
children.translated_text: He eats bitter, astringent, pungent, hot, and dry food in small quantity, and yet he is strong.
His eyes have red corners, are very unctuous, broad, and long, with clear white and black parts and fine lashes.
He has little inclination to speech, anger, drinking, eating, and exertion; he has abundant life and wealth, is farsighted and generous.

children.text: śrāddho gambhīraḥ sthūlalakṣaḥ kṣamāvān āryo nidrālur dīrghasūtraḥ kṛtajñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is faithful, deep, broad-marked, patient, noble, sleepy, slow to act, and grateful.

children.text: ṛjur vipaścit subhagaḥ sulajjo bhakto gurūṇāṃ sthirasauhṛdaś ca
children.translated_text: He is upright, discerning, fortunate, modest, devoted to teachers, and steady in friendship.

children.text: svapne sapadmān savihaṃgamālāṃs toyāśayān paśyati toyadāṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: In dreams he sees water reservoirs with lotuses and rows of birds, and also clouds.
Those of <s>śleṣma-prakṛti</s> are comparable with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, swans, and lordly elephants,
and likewise with lions, horses, cows, and bulls.
Constitutions arising from two <s>doṣa</s>s or from all are to be described when the qualities of the pair or of all arise;
and, by qualities such as purity and belief, one should likewise describe the constitutions composed of the <s>guṇa</s>s.

children.text: vayas tv ā ṣoḍaśād bālaṃ tatra dhātvindriyaujasām
children.translated_text: As for age, up to the sixteenth year one is a child; there the <s>dhātu</s>s, senses, and <s>ojas</s>

children.text: vṛddhir ā saptater madhyaṃ tatrāvṛddhiḥ paraṃ kṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: increase. Up to seventy is middle age; there there is no further increase, and after that there is decline.

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ hastatrayaṃ sārdhaṃ vapuḥ pātraṃ sukhāyuṣoḥ
children.translated_text: Each body, measuring three and a half cubits, is a vessel for happiness and long life,

children.text: na ca yad yuktam udriktair aṣṭābhir ninditair nijaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: provided it is not joined with its own excessive eight censured traits:
hairlessness, darkness, stoutness, tallness, and their opposites.

children.text: susnigdhā mṛdavaḥ sūkṣmā naikamūlāḥ sthirāḥ kacāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hair should be very unctuous, soft, fine, not springing many from one root, and stable.
The forehead should be raised, with closely joined temples, and resemble a half-moon.
The ears should be low and high at the back, large, close-set, and fleshy.
The eyes should have distinct black and white parts, with well-set, thick eyelashes.
The nose should have a raised tip and ample breath, and be full, straight, and even.

children.text: oṣṭhau raktāv anudvṛttau mahatyau nolbaṇe hanū
children.translated_text: The lips should be red and not upturned; the jaws should be large but not protruding.

children.text: mahad āsyaṃ ghanā dantāḥ snigdhāḥ ślakṣṇāḥ sitāḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mouth should be large; the teeth close-set, unctuous, smooth, white, and even.

children.text: jihvā raktāyatā tanvī māṃsalaṃ cibukaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: The tongue should be red, long, and thin; the chin fleshy and large.

children.text: grīvā hrasvā ghanā vṛttā skandhāv unnatapīvarau ||
children.translated_text: The neck should be short, thick, and round; the shoulders raised and full.
The abdomen should be raised, with a hidden navel that turns to the right;
the nails should be thin, red, and raised, and the body unctuous, somewhat coppery, and fleshy.
having long, gapless fingers, with large hands and feet firmly planted,

children.text: gūḍhavaṃśaṃ bṛhat pṛṣṭhaṃ nigūḍhāḥ saṃdhayo dṛḍhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the spinal column hidden, the back broad, and the joints concealed and firm;

children.text: dhīraḥ svaro 'nunādī ca varṇaḥ snigdhaḥ sthiraprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: with a voice that is steady and resonant, and a complexion that is unctuous and of lasting radiance;

children.text: svabhāvajaṃ sthiraṃ sattvam avikāri vipatsv api ||
children.translated_text: with innate, steady <s>sattva</s> that remains unchanged even in misfortunes;
with a body that becomes an ever better field, free from disease from the womb onward,
growing gradually and auspiciously in length, knowledge, and discriminative understanding;
in a body endowed with all these qualities, a hundred autumns

children.text: āyur aiśvaryam iṣṭāś ca sarve bhāvāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: of life, sovereignty, and all desired states are established.
Skin, blood, and the rest, ending with <s>sattva</s>, are eight excellent constituents in successive order;
they have been taught as the essences of embodied beings, for the purpose of knowing the measure of strength.

children.text: sārair upetaḥ sarvaiḥ syāt paraṃ gauravasaṃyutaḥ
children.translated_text: One endowed with all the essences is possessed of supreme dignity;
in all undertakings he is hopeful, enduring, sound-minded, and firm.

children.text: anutsekam adainyaṃ ca sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca sevate
children.translated_text: He experiences pleasure and pain without arrogance and without dejection;

children.text: sattvavāṃs tapyamānas tu rājaso naiva tāmasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one possessed of <s>sattva</s>, though afflicted, is not tormented as the <s>rājasa</s> or <s>tāmasa</s> person is.
Generosity, good conduct, compassion, truthfulness, chastity, and gratitude,
together with friendship, are <s>rasāyana</s>s, a group that increases merit and life-span.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the anatomical division of <s>marma</s>s.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
The <s>marma</s>s are one hundred and seven; of these one should assign eleven

children.text: pṛthak sakthnos tathā bāhvos trīṇi koṣṭhe navorasi ||
children.translated_text: separately to each leg and likewise to each arm, three in the abdomen, and nine in the chest.

children.text: pṛṣṭhe caturdaśordhvaṃ tu jatros triṃśacca sapta ca
children.translated_text: There are fourteen in the back, while above the collar-bones there are thirty-seven.
In the middle of the sole of the foot, on both sides of the middle toe, they speak of
the <s>marma</s> named <s>Talahṛd</s>; when it is pierced, death comes through pain.
The <s>Kṣipra</s>, situated between the big toe and the toes, kills by convulsion.
Two finger-breadths above it is <s>Kūrca</s>, which causes twisting and trembling of the foot.
Below the ankle-joint is <s>Kūrcaśiras</s>, which produces swelling and pain.
At the joint of shank and foot is the ankle, which causes pain, stiffness, and weakness.
In the middle of the shank is <s>Indravasti</s>; it kills through loss of blood.

children.text: jaṅghorvoḥ saṃgame jānu khañjatā tatra jīvataḥ
children.translated_text: At the meeting of shank and thigh is the knee; there, if one survives, lameness results.
Three finger-breadths above the knee is <s>Āṇi</s>, which causes stiffness and swelling of the thigh.
In the middle of the thigh is <s>Urvī</s>; from piercing it, wasting of the leg occurs because of loss of blood.
At the root of the thigh is <s>Lohitākṣa</s>; it destroys one side of the body through loss of blood.
Between the scrotum and the groin is <s>Viṭapa</s>, which causes impotence.

children.text: iti sakthnos tathā bāhvor maṇibandho 'tra gulphavat ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is for the legs; likewise in the arms, the wrist here is like the ankle.

children.text: kūrparaṃ jānuvat kauṇyaṃ tayor viṭapavat punaḥ
children.translated_text: The elbow is like the knee; deformity in them is again like the result from <s>Viṭapa</s>.
Between the axilla and the shoulder is <s>Kakṣādhṛk</s>; there contraction of the arm is produced.
The rectum, bound to the large intestine, is immediately fatal and causes vomiting of feces and flatus.
The urinary bladder is bow-shaped, with little blood and flesh,
with one downward-facing opening; situated in the middle of the pelvis, it immediately destroys life.
Except when it is pierced by a wound from a stone, and even there if the wound is on both sides,
when it is broken on one side and urine drains out, the wound may heal with careful treatment.
The navel, among the body's sites of undigested and digested matter, is the support of all the veins;

children.text: nābhiḥ so 'pi hi sadyoghno dvāram āmāśayasya ca
children.translated_text: it too is immediately fatal, and is also the gateway of the stomach.
The heart, the seat of <s>sattva</s> and the other vital factors, lies in the middle of the breasts, chest, and abdomen.
At the two breasts, two finger-breadths away, one should describe the points called <s>Stana</s>, <s>Rohita</s>, and <s>Mūla</s>.
When these are pierced above or below, the cavity fills respectively with blood or <s>kapha</s>, and the person perishes.
The two <s>Apastambha</s>s, at the sides of the chest, are channels that carry <s>vāta</s>.
Here, when the cavity is filled with blood, the person dies from dyspnea and cough.
Between the spinal column and the chest, and on the sides of those very two,
below the shoulder-peaks, one should know the two <s>marma</s>s called <s>Apālāpa</s>.

children.text: tayoḥ koṣṭhe 'sṛjā pūrṇe naśyed yātena pūyatām
children.translated_text: When their cavity is filled with blood, the person dies once it has gone on to suppuration.
At the sides of the spinal column, situated opposite the hip-crests,
resting on the spine above the buttocks, are remembered the tender pelvic points called <s>Kaṭīkataruṇa</s>.
There, from loss of blood, a person becomes pale and disfigured, and dies.
The two joints on both sides of the spinal column, at the sides of the waist,
on the outer part of the pelvis, are the two <s>marma</s>s called <s>Kukundara</s>.
From wounding them, there is loss of movement in the lower body and loss of tactile sensation.
The two fixed within the flanks, above the hip-crests,
covering the viscera, located in tender bone, are the two buttock-points, <s>Nitamba</s>.
Here swelling in the lower body, weakness, and then death occur.
The two fixed within the flanks, in the middle of the sides of the pelvis,

children.text: tiryag ūrdhvaṃ ca nirdiṣṭau pārśvasaṃdhī tayor vyadhāt ||
children.translated_text: are described as running obliquely upward; these are the two <s>Pārśvasaṃdhi</s>s, and from wounding them,
the cavity becomes filled with blood and an internal bodily disorder arises.
In the straight region from the roots of the breasts, along the veins resting on the spinal column,
are the two <s>Bṛhatī</s>s; when they are pierced, death comes from loss of blood.
Attached to the roots of the arms, on the two sides of the spinal column,
are the shoulder-blades; from wounding them, numbness and wasting of the arms occur.
On both sides of the neck are the tendons between the neck, arms, and head;
connected with the shoulders and the shoulder-seat are the two <s>Aṃsa</s>s, which take away the action of the arms.
On both sides of the windpipe are veins supported by the jaws;

children.text: catasras tāsu nīle dve manye dve marmaṇī smṛte
children.translated_text: there are four of them: two <s>Nīlā</s>s and two <s>Manyā</s>s are remembered as <s>marma</s>s.
When they are wounded, there is loss or alteration of the voice and loss of the knowledge of taste.
On both sides of the windpipe are veins going to the tongue and nose;

children.text: pṛthak catasras tāḥ sadyo ghnantyasūn mātṛkāhvayāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are four separate vessels called <s>Mātṛkā</s>s, and they kill life at once.
The <s>Kṛkāṭikā</s>s are at the joint of the head and neck; there the head becomes unsteady.
Below the ears, in the hollows, are the <s>Vidhura</s>s, which take away hearing.
The two <s>Phaṇā</s>s are on both sides of the nasal passage, following the channels of the ears;
situated inside the throat, when pierced they take away the perception of smell.
Outside the two eyes are the <s>Apāṅga</s>s, below the ends of the tails of the eyebrows;
and above the eyebrows, in the hollows, are the two <s>Āvarta</s>s; in these there is blindness.
Near the ears, at the ends of the forehead, are the two <s>Śaṅkha</s>s, which destroy life at once.
At the hairline above the temples are the two <s>Utkṣepa</s>s, and again <s>Sthapanī</s>

children.text: bhruvor madhye traye 'pyatra śalye jīved anuddhṛte
children.translated_text: is between the eyebrows. In all three of these, if a foreign body remains, one lives;

children.text: svayaṃ vā patite pākāt sadyo naśyati tūddhṛte ||
children.translated_text: or if it falls out by itself after suppuration, one lives, but if it is pulled out, one dies at once.
At the meeting place of the four cavities of the tongue, eyes, nose, and ears
there are four <s>Tālu</s>s, openings of the channels; among the <s>marma</s>s,
one pierced in those called <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> at once abandons life.
In the skull there are five joints, the <s>Sīmanta</s>s, running crosswise and upward.
When these are pierced, one dies through giddiness, madness, and loss of mind.
Inside, at the top of the head, is the meeting of veins and joints;
the hair-whorl there is the <s>marma</s> called <s>Adhipati</s>, and it at once takes away life.

children.text: viṣamaṃ spandanaṃ yatra pīḍite ruk ca marma tat ||
children.translated_text: A place where there is irregular throbbing and pain when pressed is a <s>marma</s>.
It is the conjunction of muscle, bone, ligament, artery, vein, and joint;

children.text: syān marmeti ca tenātra sutarāṃ jīvitaṃ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: therefore it is called a <s>marma</s>, and life is especially established there.
But the description is chiefly a sixfold conception of the <s>marma</s>s in this way;
or, because they are all seats of life in common, the <s>marma</s>s are held to be one.
The ten arising from muscle are those called <s>Indra</s>, <s>Tala</s>, <s>Hṛd</s>, <s>Stanarohita</s>,
the two <s>Śaṅkha</s>s, the <s>Kaṭīkataraṇa</s>s, the two <s>Nitamba</s>s, and the <s>Aṃsaphalaka</s>s.
There are eight in bone; the ligament <s>marma</s>s are twenty-three:
<s>Kūrca</s>, <s>Kūrcaśiras</s>, <s>Apāṅga</s>, <s>Kṣipra</s>, <s>Utkṣepa</s>, <s>Aṃsa</s>, and <s>Vasti</s>.
One should designate <s>Guda</s>, <s>Apastambha</s>, <s>Vidhura</s>, and the <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s>s, nine in all,
as <s>marma</s>s situated in arteries; thirty-seven rest on veins.

children.text: bṛhatyau mātṛkā nīle manye kakṣādharau phaṇau
children.translated_text: The two <s>Bṛhatī</s>s, the <s>Mātṛkā</s>s, <s>Nīlā</s>, <s>Manyā</s>, <s>Kakṣādhara</s>, the two <s>Phaṇā</s>s,
the <s>Viṭapa</s>s, <s>Hṛdaya</s>, <s>Nābhi</s>, the <s>Pārśvasaṃdhi</s>s, and the <s>Stanādhara</s>s,
the two <s>Apālāpa</s>s, <s>Sthapanī</s>, the four <s>Urvī</s>s, and the <s>Lohita</s>s are vein-based.
In joints there are twenty: the two <s>Āvarta</s>s, the two <s>Maṇibandha</s>s, and the two <s>Kukundara</s>s,

children.text: sīmantāḥ kūrparau gulphau kṛkāṭyau jānunī patiḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Sīmanta</s>s, two <s>Kūrpara</s>s, two <s>Gulpha</s>s, two <s>Kṛkāṭikā</s>s, the knees, and <s>Adhipati</s>.
According to others, <s>Guda</s> is a muscle <s>marma</s>, and the <s>Kakṣādhara</s>s likewise are in ligaments.

children.text: viṭapau vidhurākhye ca śṛṅgāṭāni sirāsu tu
children.translated_text: The two <s>Viṭapa</s>s and those called <s>Vidhura</s>, and the <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s>s, are in veins;

children.text: apastambhāvapāṅgau ca dhamanīsthaṃ na taiḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Apastambha</s>s and <s>Apāṅga</s>s are not remembered by them as artery-based.
When a muscle <s>marma</s> is pierced, there is constant flow of blood and the body is like washed flesh;
there is pallor, loss of sensory awareness, and swift death.
In a bone <s>marma</s> there is a clear, broken discharge mixed with marrow, and pain.
In a ligament <s>marma</s> there are extension, convulsion, and stiffness, with especially severe pain,
inability to move, stand, or sit, and either deformity or death.
In an artery-based <s>marma</s>, the blood is noisy, frothy, and hot, and the person loses consciousness.
When a vein <s>marma</s> is pierced, thick, abundant blood flows constantly;
from its loss, death comes with thirst, giddiness, dyspnea, stupor, and hiccup.
In a joint <s>marma</s>, the affected part seems as if scattered with awns, and when healed there is contracture and lameness;
there are loss of strength and activity, wasting, and swelling of the joint.
<s>Nābhi</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Adhipati</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Hṛd</s>, <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, and <s>Vasti</s>,
together with the eight <s>Mātṛkā</s>s, make nineteen that kill immediately.

children.text: saptāhaḥ paramas teṣāṃ kālaḥ kālasya karṣaṇe
children.translated_text: For them the utmost limit of time, when death is delayed, is seven days.
Thirty-three, namely <s>Apastambha</s>, <s>Tala</s>, <s>Hṛd</s>, and the <s>Pārśvasaṃdhi</s>s,
<s>Kaṭītaruṇa</s>, <s>Sīmanta</s>, <s>Stanamūla</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Vasti</s>,
<s>Kṣipra</s>, <s>Apālāpa</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Nitamba</s>, and <s>Stanarohita</s>,
take life after an interval; life lasts for a month or half a month.

children.text: utkṣepau sthapanī trīṇi viśalyaghnāni tatra hi ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>Utkṣepa</s>s and <s>Sthapanī</s>, three in all, kill when the foreign body is removed.
For there <s>vāyu</s> dries up muscle, fat, marrow, and brain matter;
when the foreign body is removed, it issues out with breathing and coughing and takes away life.
The two <s>Phaṇā</s>s, <s>Apāṅga</s>s, <s>Vidhura</s>s, <s>Nīlā</s>s, <s>Manyā</s>s, and <s>Kṛkāṭikā</s>s,
the <s>Aṃsa</s>s, <s>Aṃsaphalaka</s>s, <s>Āvarta</s>s, <s>Viṭapa</s>s, <s>Urvī</s>s, and <s>Kukundara</s>s,
with the knees, <s>Lohitākṣa</s>s, <s>Āṇi</s>s, <s>Kakṣādhara</s>s, <s>Kūrca</s>s, and <s>Kūrpara</s>s,
forty-four in all, cause deformity.
Even these sometimes take life because of the violence of the injury.
The eight <s>Kūrcaśiras</s>, <s>Gulpha</s>s, and <s>Maṇibandha</s>s cause pain.
Among them, the <s>Viṭapa</s>s, <s>Kakṣādhara</s>s, <s>Urvī</s>s, and <s>Kūrcaśiras</s>s
measure twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s; the two <s>Maṇibandha</s>s measure two <s>aṅgula</s>s.

children.text: gulphau ca stanamūle ca tryaṅgulaṃ jānukūrparam
children.translated_text: The two <s>Gulpha</s>s and <s>Stanamūla</s>s, and the knees and elbows, measure three <s>aṅgula</s>s.
<s>Apāna</s>, <s>Vasti</s>, <s>Hṛd</s>, <s>Nābhi</s>, the <s>Nīlā</s>s, <s>Sīmanta</s>s, and <s>Mātṛkā</s>s,
<s>Kūrca</s>, <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, and <s>Manyā</s>, twenty-nine less one from thirty,
have the measure of one's own palm; the remaining ones should be stated as half an <s>aṅgula</s>.
Other authorities accept fifty-six <s>marma</s>s even as small as sesame and rice grains.

children.text: iṣṭāni marmāṇyanyeṣāṃ caturdhoktāḥ sirās tu yāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the veins that have been described in four ways

children.text: tarpayanti vapuḥ kṛtsnaṃ tā marmāṇyāśritās tataḥ
children.translated_text: nourish the whole body; therefore the <s>marma</s>s are dependent on them.
From injury to them, because blood flows excessively and the <s>dhātu</s>s are depleted,
<s>vāta</s>, increased and mobile, spreads intense pains.
<s>Tejas</s>, drawn out from that, produces thirst, wasting, intoxication, and giddiness.
Then death takes the person whose body is sweating, collapsed, and slack.
When a <s>marma</s> has been struck, one should quickly support the limb from the joint.
From cutting the region of a joint, the veins contract; therefore

children.text: jīvitaṃ prāṇināṃ tatra rakte tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: the life of living beings remains there, in the blood; it remains there indeed.
Therefore one may live even when badly wounded in a place that is not a <s>marma</s>, but not in a <s>marma</s>.

children.text: prāṇaghātini jīvet tu kaścid vaidyaguṇena cet ||
children.translated_text: In a life-destroying <s>marma</s>, however, someone may live if this happens through the excellence of the physician,
and because the injury is incomplete; even so, he suffers deformity or disability.
Therefore caustics, poisons, fire, and the like should be carefully avoided at the <s>marma</s>s.
Even a slight injury to a <s>marma</s> generally causes very great distress,

children.text: rogā marmāśrayās tadvat prakrāntā yatnato 'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: and so too do diseases lodged in <s>marma</s>s, even when they have been carefully treated.
Now then, we shall explain the section on the body concerning the recognition of morbid change.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
As a flower is the sign of fruit, smoke of fire, and the rising of clouds of rain,

children.text: yathā bhaviṣyato liṅgaṃ riṣṭaṃ mṛtyos tathā dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: so a <s>riṣṭa</s> is certainly the sign of death that is to come.
All treatments undertaken for one whose span of life remains

children.text: bhavanti bhiṣajāṃ bhūtyai kṛtajña iva bhūbhuji
children.translated_text: become successful, for the prosperity of physicians, like service rendered to a grateful ruler.

children.text: kṣīṇāyuṣi kṛtaṃ karma vyarthaṃ kṛtam ivādhame
children.translated_text: A procedure done for one whose life is exhausted is useless, like an act done for an unworthy man;
it brings disgrace, danger to the body, and loss of one's own interest.
Therefore, now they declare the signs of those whose vital breaths are departing.
A deviation from the normal state has been taught by the wise under the name <s>riṣṭa</s>.

children.text: ariṣṭaṃ nāsti maraṇaṃ dṛṣṭariṣṭaṃ ca jīvitam
children.translated_text: There is no death without an inauspicious sign, and no continued life when such a sign has been seen.
Through lack of skill, one may perceive a <s>riṣṭa</s> where there is none, and fail to perceive one even where there is a <s>riṣṭa</s>.
Some say that it is twofold, because of the distinction between stable and unstable signs.
A semblance of <s>riṣṭa</s> may also arise from an abundance of the <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: sa doṣāṇāṃ śame śāmyet sthāyyavaśyaṃ tu mṛtyave
children.translated_text: It subsides when the <s>doṣa</s>s subside, but a stable one necessarily leads to death.
In form, senses, voice, complexion, reflection, activity, and so forth,
and also in other normal conditions, when there is no apparent cause,

children.text: vikṛtir yā samāsena riṣṭaṃ tad iti lakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: whatever abnormality there is, in brief, one should recognize that as a <s>riṣṭa</s>.
When a person's head-hair and body-hair appear as if anointed, though no oil has been applied,
when his eyes are extremely unsteady, fixed, sunken, or protruding,
crooked, expanded, or contracted, and his brows are contracted or bent downward,
when his vision is confused, deficient, or like that of a mongoose,
dove-colored, coal-red, watering, with disordered eyelashes,
when his nose is excessively open, closed, or covered with eruptions,
when his lip is swollen, cracked, faded, and the lower lip sinks downward,
or the upper lip turns upward, or both become like ripe <s>jambū</s> fruit,
when the teeth have gravel-like deposits, are dark, coppery, blossoming with tartar, or coated with filth,

children.text: sahasaiva pateyur vā jihvā jihmā visarpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: or suddenly fall out, and the tongue is crooked and spreading,

children.text: śūnā śuṣkā guruḥ śyāvā liptā suptā sakaṇṭakā
children.translated_text: swollen, dry, heavy, dusky, coated, numb, or thorny,

children.text: śiraḥ śirodharā voḍhuṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ vā bhāram ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when his head, neck, or back cannot bear its own weight,

children.text: hanū vā piṇḍam āsyasthaṃ śaknuvanti na yasya ca
children.translated_text: and when his jaws cannot manage the morsel that is in his mouth,
when his limbs without cause are heavy or excessively light,

children.text: viṣadoṣād vinā yasya khebhyo raktaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: when blood flows from his bodily openings without poison or <s>doṣa</s> as the cause,
when his organ of urination is raised and his testicles hang far down,

children.text: ato 'nyathā vā yasya syāt sarve te kālacoditāḥ
children.translated_text: or when his condition is otherwise abnormal in these respects: all such persons are driven by Time.
One on whose forehead or at the head of the bladder there appear new vein-lines, or even shapes like a young moon,

children.text: lalāṭe vastiśīrṣe vā ṣaṇ māsān na sa jīvati
children.translated_text: does not live for six months.
For the embodied person on whose body water, like water on a lotus leaf,

children.text: plavate plavamānasya ṣaṇ māsās tasya jīvitam
children.translated_text: floats while he is being bathed, his life is six months.
The man whose veins are greenish and whose hair follicles are closed,
and who longs for sour things, meets death from <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: yasya gomayacūrṇābhaṃ cūrṇaṃ mūrdhni mukhe 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: For one who has a powder like powdered cow dung on the head or even on the face,

children.text: sasnehaṃ mūrdhni dhūmo vā māsāntaṃ tasya jīvitam
children.translated_text: or an oily smoke-like mark on the head, life lasts until the end of a month.

children.text: mūrdhni bhruvor vā kurvanti sīmantāvartakā navāḥ ||
children.translated_text: New partings and whorls that form on the head or on the brows

children.text: mṛtyuṃ svasthasya ṣaḍrātrāt trirātrād āturasya tu
children.translated_text: bring death to a healthy person in six nights, but to a sick person in three nights.

children.text: jihvā śyāvā mukhaṃ pūti savyam akṣi nimajjati ||
children.translated_text: One whose tongue is dusky, whose mouth is foul, and whose left eye sinks,

children.text: khagā vā mūrdhni līyante yasya taṃ parivarjayet
children.translated_text: or on whose head birds settle, should be abandoned.
One whose chest, after he has been bathed and anointed, dries first and very intensely,
while all his limbs are still wet, does not live for half a month.
When natural and unnatural colors suddenly appear together on the body,
and likewise increase and wasting, dryness and oiliness, and the like, they point to death.

children.text: yasya sphuṭeyuraṅgulyo nākṛṣṭā na sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: One whose fingers crack without being pulled does not live.
The same is true when an unprecedented sound arises in his sneezing, coughing, and the like,

children.text: hrasvo dīrgho 'ti vocchvāsaḥ pūtiḥ surabhireva vā ||
children.translated_text: or when his breath is too short, too long, foul-smelling, or even fragrant,
or when his body, washed or unwashed, has a superhuman smell,
or when such a smell is in his excrement, clothes, wounds, and so on; his life lasts until the end of a year.
One whom lice, flies, and the like seek out because of the excessive sweetness of his limbs,

children.text: tyajanti vātivairasyāt so 'pi varṣaṃ na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: or abandon because of excessive bad taste, he too does not live for a year.
When coldness is observed in limbs that are constantly warm,

children.text: śīteṣu bhṛśam auṣṇyaṃ vā svedaḥ stambho 'pyahetukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or intense heat in limbs that are cold, or sweating or stiffness without cause,
one who develops cold eruptions, or who, cold-limbed, feels burning,
and who hates heat while afflicted by cold, is within the domain of the lord of the dead.
One who has heat in the chest and excessive coldness in the belly,

children.text: bhinnaṃ purīṣaṃ tṛṣṇā ca yathā pretas tathaiva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: loose stool and thirst, is just like a dead man.

children.text: mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ niṣṭhyūtaṃ śukraṃ vāpsu nimajjati
children.translated_text: One whose urine, feces, sputum, or semen sinks in water,

children.text: niṣṭhyūtaṃ bahuvarṇaṃ vā yasya māsāt sa naśyati ||
children.translated_text: or whose sputum is many-colored, perishes within a month.

children.text: ghanībhūtam ivākāśam ākāśam iva yo ghanam
children.translated_text: One who sees the sky as if solidified, and a solid mass as if it were sky,

children.text: amūrtam iva mūrtaṃ ca mūrtaṃ cāmūrtavat sthitam ||
children.translated_text: and what is formless as if it had form, and what has form as if it were formless.

children.text: tejasvyatejas tadvacca śuklaṃ kṛṣṇam asacca sat
children.translated_text: radiant things as without radiance, and likewise the opposite, white as black, and unreal as real,
and, though having no eye disease, the moon as many-formed and without its mark,

children.text: jāgrad rakṣāṃsi gandharvān pretān anyāṃśca tadvidhān
children.translated_text: while awake, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, and others of that sort,

children.text: rūpaṃ vyākṛti tat tacca yaḥ paśyati sa naśyati ||
children.translated_text: and the form and appearance of this or that: the person who sees such things perishes.
One who does not see <s>Arundhatī</s> standing near the Seven Seers,

children.text: dhruvam ākāśagaṅgāṃ vā sa na paśyati tāṃ samām ||
children.translated_text: or <s>Dhruva</s>, or the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>, will not see that year.
One who hears the roar of clouds, floods of water, or sounds born from lute, drum, or flute,

children.text: śṛṇotyanyāṃśca yaḥ śabdān asato na sato 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: and other sounds that are not present, or fails to hear even those that are present,

children.text: niṣpīḍya karṇau śṛṇuyān na yo dhukadhukāsvanam
children.translated_text: or who, after pressing his ears, does not hear a throbbing dhuk-dhuk sound,
and likewise one who perceives smells, tastes, and touches in a contrary way,

children.text: sarvaśo vā na yo yaśca dīpagandhaṃ na jighrati
children.translated_text: or not at all in any respect, and one who does not smell the odor of a lamp,
for whom tastes taken properly lead to <s>doṣa</s>, and tastes taken improperly lead to health,

children.text: yaḥ pāṃsuneva kīrṇāṅgo yo 'ṅge ghātaṃ na vetti vā
children.translated_text: one whose limbs seem as if strewn with dust, or who does not feel a blow on the body,

children.text: antareṇa tapas tīvraṃ yogaṃ vā vidhipūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: without severe ascetic practice or yoga performed according to rule,
and one who knows what is beyond the senses: one should predict death for such persons.

children.text: hīno dīnaḥ svaro 'vyakto yasya syād gadgado 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: He whose voice is low, pitiable, indistinct, or even stammering,

children.text: sahasā yo vimuhyed vā vivakṣur na sa jīvati
children.translated_text: or who suddenly becomes bewildered when wishing to speak, does not live.
On seeing weakness of the voice and loss of strength and complexion,

children.text: rogavṛddhim ayuktyā ca dṛṣṭvā maraṇam ādiśet
children.translated_text: and an unreasonable increase of disease, one should predict death.
One speaking in a discordant voice has reached his own death,
and the hearer of this sound should avoid him from afar.
If a person's shadow changes in shape, size, color,

children.text: chāyā vivartate yasya svapne 'pi preta eva saḥ
children.translated_text: or even radiance, even in a dream, he is as good as a dead man.
That shadow which arises from the body in sunlight, a mirror, water, and the like,
in respect of shape and size, is called a reflection; but again,

children.text: varṇaprabhāśrayā yā tu sā chāyaiva śarīragā ||
children.translated_text: that which has color and radiance as its basis, abiding in the body, is the bodily shadow itself.
If a person's reflection is cut off, broken, excessive, confused,

children.text: viśirā dviśirā jihmā vikṛtā yadi vānyathā ||
children.translated_text: headless, two-headed, crooked, distorted, or otherwise abnormal,
one should know him to have reached the end of his life, unless it is produced by some visible cause.
If the pupil in a person's reflected image is not seen by the eyes,
there are varied signs for the five shadows belonging to the five elements beginning with ether.
The ethereal shadow is clear, blue, unctuous, and as if luminous.
The airy one, from <s>vāta</s>, is dusty-red, dusky, ash-dry, and robbed of radiance.
The fiery one is pure red, with blazing lustre, and pleasing to behold.
The watery one is clear like pure beryl, very unctuous, and pleasant.

children.text: sthirā snigdhā ghanā śuddhā śyāmā śvetā ca pārthivī ||
children.translated_text: The earthy one is steady, unctuous, dense, pure, dark, or white.
The airy shadow leads to disease, death, and suffering; the others bring the arising of happiness.

children.text: prabhoktā taijasī sarvā sā tu saptavidhā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Fiery radiance illuminates all; it is remembered as sevenfold.

children.text: raktā pītā sitā śyāvā haritā pāṇḍurāsitā
children.translated_text: Red, yellow, white, dusky, green, pale, and black are its forms.

children.text: tāsāṃ yāḥ syur vikāsinyaḥ snigdhāśca vimalāśca yāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them, those that are expansive, unctuous,
and clear are auspicious; those that are dirty, dry, and contracted bring inauspicious results.
Shadow overlays color; radiance makes color shine forth.

children.text: āsanne lakṣyate chāyā vikṛṣṭe bhā prakāśate
children.translated_text: Shadow is perceived when near; light radiance shines from afar.
No one is without shadow or without radiance, but their distinctions mark
the arising of good and evil for human beings in due time, depending on shadow.
One who creeps along as if scraping his feet, with his shoulders fallen,

children.text: hīyate balataḥ śaśvad yo 'nnam aśnan hitaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: and who constantly loses strength while eating much wholesome food,
one who, eating little, passes much stool and urine, or, eating much, passes little urine and stool,

children.text: yo vālpāśī kaphenārto dīrghaṃ śvasiti ceṣṭate
children.translated_text: or one who, though eating little and afflicted by <s>kapha</s>, breathes long and struggles,

children.text: dīrgham ucchvasya yo hrasvaṃ niḥśvasya paritāmyati ||
children.translated_text: one who, after a long inhalation, exhales briefly and becomes exhausted,

children.text: hrasvaṃ ca yaḥ praśvasiti vyāviddhaṃ spandate bhṛśam
children.translated_text: and one who breathes in short gasps, spasmodically, and trembles violently,
one who tosses his head with difficulty after bending his forearms,
one from whose forehead sweat flows, with loosened joints and ligaments,

children.text: utthāpyamānaḥ saṃmuhyed yo balī durbalo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: one who becomes unconscious when being lifted up, whether strong or weak,

children.text: uttāna eva svapiti yaḥ pādau vikaroti ca
children.translated_text: one who sleeps only lying on his back and moves his feet about,
one who tries to grasp nonexistent things from the bed, seat, wall, and the like,
one who laughs at what is not laughable, becomes bewildered, and licks his lips,
one who licks his upper lip and makes blowing sounds,

children.text: yam abhidravati chāyā kṛṣṇā pītāruṇāpi vā
children.translated_text: one whom a shadow that is black, yellow, or reddish rushes upon,
and those who hate the physician, medicine, drink, food, teacher, and friends,
all these, being under his control, should be known as followers of <s>Samavartin</s>.
If a person's neck, forehead, and heart sweat and are cold,
while the rest of the body region is hot, the gods are his only refuge.
One whose light is minute, whose attention is scattered, whose shadow is bad, and whose mind is always dejected,
for whom the creatures that eat offerings do not consume the offering that has been set out,

children.text: nirnimittaṃ ca yo medhāṃ śobhām upacayaṃ śriyam ||
children.translated_text: or one who without cause attains intelligence, beauty, increase, and prosperity,

children.text: prāpnotyato vā vibhraṃśaṃ sa prāpnoti yamakṣayam
children.translated_text: or falls away from these, reaches the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
If the constitution of a healthy or sick person, made up of virtues and faults,

children.text: yātyanyathātvaṃ prakṛtiḥ ṣaṇ māsān na sa jīvati
children.translated_text: undergoes alteration, he does not live for six months.

children.text: bhaktiḥ śīlaṃ smṛtis tyāgo buddhir balam ahetukam ||
children.translated_text: Devotion, conduct, memory, generosity, intelligence, and strength, without cause:

children.text: ṣaḍ etāni nivartante ṣaḍbhir māsair mariṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: these six depart from one who will die within six months.
A drunken-like gait, speech, trembling, and confusion belong to one who will die within months.
One who does not feel the pain of hair being plucked out dies within six days.

children.text: na yāti yasya cāhāraḥ kaṇṭhaṃ kaṇṭhāmayād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: And if a person's food does not pass down the throat, apart from a disease of the throat,
Servants turn hostile, and a ghost-like appearance is said to arise in him.

children.text: yasya nidrā bhaven nityā naiva vā na sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: One whose sleep is constant, or else entirely absent, does not live.
The face fills with tears, and the feet sweat profusely;
the eyes become agitated in one who is going to the kingdom of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: yaiḥ purā ramate bhāvairaratis tair na jīvati
children.translated_text: A person who feels aversion to the very states in which he formerly delighted does not live;
nor one in whom a disorder with all its symptoms suddenly arises.

children.text: nivartate vā sahasā sahasā sa vinaśyati
children.translated_text: Or if it suddenly ceases, he suddenly perishes.
A fever that is powerful, deep-seated, and long-lasting kills,
with delirious speech, confusion, and dyspnea, a patient who is wasted, swollen, and whose digestive fire is destroyed,
who is not emaciated, whose speech is obstructed, whose eyes are red, and who has pain in the heart.
A dry cough that occurs in the forenoon or even in the afternoon,
in one deprived of strength and flesh and accompanied by a phlegmatic cough, is fatal.
In <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorder), blood that is very red, black, or like the color of a rainbow,
or blood that displays a coppery, yellow, or green appearance,
that has spread out through the hair-pores and sticks in the throat, mouth, and heart,
that does not stain cloth, is foul-smelling, forceful, and excessively abundant, is fatal.
It kills an old person afflicted with pallor, fever, vomiting, cough, swelling, and diarrhea,
or one affected by cough, dyspnea, fever, vomiting, thirst, diarrhea, and swelling.
<s>Yakṣmā</s> (consumption) kills one with pain in the side, distension, vomiting of blood, and heat in the shoulders.
Vomiting is fatal when it is violent, smells of urine and feces, and is speckled with white spots,
when attended by bloody stool, pus, pain, cough, and dyspnea, and when it is persistent.
Thirst kills one wasted by another disease, with the tongue protruding and consciousness lost.
<s>Madātyaya</s> (intoxication disorder) kills one afflicted by excessive cold, wasted, and with a face shining like oil.
Hemorrhoids kill one swollen in the hands, feet, navel, anus, testicles, and mouth,
and tormented by pain in the heart, sides, and limbs, by vomiting, anal inflammation, and fever.
Diarrhea kills when the discharges are like liver, lumps of flesh, meat-washings, or dark liquid,
like oil, ghee, milk, curd, marrow, fat, or wine,
like brain-matter, ink, pus, broth, water, or honey,
excessively red, black, unctuous, foul-smelling, clear or thick, and painful,
variegated, flowing with bodily tissues, without feces or with excessive feces,
stringy, swarmed by flies, streaked, and marked with circular patches,
in a patient whose anal folds have collapsed, whose passage is open, and whose joints and bones ache,
whose anus has prolapsed, whose strength is exhausted, and who passes food just as it was eaten,
with thirst, dyspnea, fever, vomiting, burning, distension, and dysentery.
Urinary stone kills one whose testicles are swollen, whose urine is obstructed, and who is tortured by pain.
<s>Meha</s> (urinary disease) kills one with thirst, burning, eruptions, sloughing of flesh, and diarrhea.
Eruptions located in vital spots, the heart, back, breasts, shoulders, anus, or head,
or situated in the joints, feet, or hands, kill a <s>pramehin</s> (diabetic patient) who has little energy.
And every case accompanied by sloughing of flesh, burning, thirst, stupor, and fever,
with obstruction of vital parts from <s>visarpa</s>, hiccup, dyspnea, giddiness, and fatigue, is fatal.
<s>Gulma</s> (abdominal tumor) kills when its circumference is broad, when it is hard and raised like a tortoise,
bound with veins and attended by fever, vomiting, hiccup, distension, and pain,
with cough, coryza, nausea, dyspnea, diarrhea, and swelling.
Retention of feces and urine, dyspnea, swelling, hiccup, fever, and giddiness,
together with fainting, vomiting, and diarrhea, kill a weak patient with abdominal enlargement.
So too when the eyes are swollen, the genital is crooked, and the thin skin is softened,
and when distension removed by purgation returns again and again.
<s>Pāṇḍuroga</s> (pallor disease) kills one who is edematous and whose eyes and nails appear yellow,
with drowsiness, burning, anorexia, vomiting, fainting, distension, and diarrhea,
and accompanied by many complications; swelling that spreads from the feet kills a man,
swelling from the face kills a woman, and swelling from the abdomen or genitals kills both.
A streaked, discharging swelling kills one with vomiting, fever, dyspnea, and diarrhea.

children.text: jvarātīsārau śophānte śvayathur vā tayoḥ kṣaye
children.translated_text: Fever and diarrhea at the end of swelling, or swelling when those two have subsided,
especially in a weak person, arise for the death of the embodied patient.

children.text: śvayathur yasya pādasthaḥ parisraste ca piṇḍike
children.translated_text: The physician should avoid the patient whose swelling is located in the feet,

children.text: sīdataḥ sakthinī caiva taṃ bhiṣak parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: whose calves have wasted away, and whose thighs are sinking.

children.text: ānanaṃ hastapādaṃ ca viśeṣād yasya śuṣyataḥ
children.translated_text: One whose face, hands, and feet in particular dry up,

children.text: śūyete vā vinā dehāt sa māsād yāti pañcatām ||
children.translated_text: or swell while the rest of the body does not, goes to the state of the five elements within a month.
<s>Visarpa</s> (spreading inflammation) kills when accompanied by cough, discoloration, fever, fainting, and breaking pain in the limbs,
with giddiness, swelling of the mouth, nausea, bodily exhaustion, and diarrhea.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease) kills one whose limbs are falling apart, whose eyes are red, and whose voice is destroyed,
whose digestive fire is weak, who is infested with organisms, and who suffers from thirst and diarrhea.
A <s>vāta</s> disorder kills one with numb skin, a bent body, and suffering from tremor, swelling, and pain.
<s>Vātāsra</s> (gout-like disorder) kills when accompanied by delusion, fainting, intoxication, sleeplessness, and fever.
It is fatal when there is stiffness of the head, anorexia, dyspnea, contractions, eruptions, and sloughing.
Head disease kills through anorexia, dyspnea, delusion, looseness of stool, thirst, and giddiness.
All diseases kill one whose voice, tissues, strength, and digestive fire are exhausted.
Patients with <s>vātavyādhi</s>, epilepsy, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, blood disease, abdominal disease, or consumption,

children.text: gulmī mehī ca tān kṣīṇān vikāre 'lpe 'pi varjayet
children.translated_text: and those with <s>gulma</s> or <s>meha</s>, should be abandoned when wasted, even if the disorder is slight.
Severe loss of strength and flesh, increase of disease, and anorexia,

children.text: yasyāturasya lakṣyante trīn pakṣān na sa jīvati
children.translated_text: when observed in a sick person, mean that he does not live for three fortnights.
Greatly enlarged <s>vātāṣṭhīlā</s> masses, terrible and lodged in the heart,
at once steal the life of one overcome by thirst.

children.text: śaithilyaṃ piṇḍike vāyur nītvā nāsāṃ ca jihmatām ||
children.translated_text: When <s>vāyu</s>, having brought flaccidity to the calves and crookedness to the nose,

children.text: kṣīṇasyāyamya manye vā sadyo muṣṇāti jīvitam
children.translated_text: or having stretched the neck sinews in a wasted person, it at once steals life.
Going between the navel and anus, or taking its seat in the groins,
or, powerful, seizing the anus and heart in a wasted body,

children.text: malān vastiśiro nābhiṃ vibadhya janayan rujam ||
children.translated_text: and obstructing the wastes, bladder, head, and navel while producing pain.
causing pain in the groins, thirst, and looseness of the stool,

children.text: śvāsaṃ vā janayan vāyur gṛhītvā gudavaṅkṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: or producing dyspnea, <s>vāyu</s> (wind) has seized the anus and groins.
When <s>māruta</s> (wind), stretching out the tips of the ribs, has seized the chest
of one who is motionless and whose eyes are stretched wide, it immediately steals away his life.
Sudden burning heat of fever, thirst, fainting, and loss of strength,
and loosening of the joints arise in one who is about to die.

children.text: gosarge vadanād yasya svedaḥ pracyavate bhṛśam
children.translated_text: At the time when the cattle are released, if sweat pours heavily from the face of one
who is tormented by clamminess and fever, his life is hard to preserve.
If eruptions like coral pellets appear on a person's body

children.text: utpadyāśu vinaśyanti na cirāt sa vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: and quickly vanish after arising, he perishes before long.
Blisters like split lentils, likewise resembling coral,
with inward mouths and looking like calluses, destroy the body.
One whose eyes are jaundiced, whose face is full, whose temples have loose flesh,
and who has panic and heat in the limbs should be abandoned.
A wound that suddenly spreads, is chafed, and is lodged in the skin,

children.text: yo vātajo na śūlāya syān na dāhāya pittajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that, though produced by <s>vāta</s> (wind), does not cause pain, or, though produced by <s>pitta</s> (bile), does not cause burning,

children.text: kaphajo na ca pūyāya marmajaśca ruje na yaḥ
children.translated_text: that, though produced by <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), does not form pus, or, though arising in a <s>marma</s> (vital spot), causes no ache,
and in which, though no powder is present, a powder-scattered appearance is suddenly seen,

children.text: rūpaṃ śaktidhvajādīnāṃ sarvāṃs tān varjayed vraṇān
children.translated_text: or the form of a spear, banner, and the like: all such wounds should be rejected.
So too a <s>bhagandara</s> (fistula) that carries feces, urine, and flatus and contains worms.
A sick man who strikes knee against knee, lifts up his feet and lets them fall,

children.text: yo 'pāsyati muhur vaktram āturo na sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: and repeatedly turns his face away does not live.

children.text: dantaiśchindan nakhāgrāṇi taiśca keśāṃs tṛṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Cutting the tips of his nails with his teeth, and with those nails cutting hair and grass,

children.text: bhūmiṃ kāṣṭhena vilikhan loṣṭaṃ loṣṭena tāḍayan ||
children.translated_text: scratching the ground with a piece of wood, and striking a clod with a clod,

children.text: hṛṣṭaromā sāndramūtraḥ śuṣkakāsī jvarī ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: one whose hair stands on end, whose urine is thick, who has a dry cough and fever,

children.text: muhur hasan muhuḥ kṣveḍan śayyāṃ pādena hanti yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who repeatedly laughs, repeatedly hisses, and strikes the bed with his foot,

children.text: muhuśchidrāṇi vimṛśann āturo na sa jīvati
children.translated_text: and who repeatedly touches the bodily openings: that sick man does not live.
For one suddenly afflicted, a disturbance of moles and blemishes points to death.

children.text: mukhe dantanakhe puṣpaṃ jaṭhare vividhāḥ sirāḥ
children.translated_text: Flower-like marks on the mouth, teeth, and nails, and various veins on the belly,
upward breathing, departed bodily warmth, and groin pain from colic:
a wise man should abandon one who cannot obtain relief.
When a person's disorders increase and his natural condition declines,

children.text: sahasā sahasā tasya mṛtyur harati jīvitam
