children.translated_text: death suddenly and repeatedly carries off his life.
When a physician, intending to prepare medicine for a sick man,

children.text: yatamāno na śaknoti durlabhaṃ tasya jīvitam
children.translated_text: strives but cannot do so, that man's life is hard to preserve.
If a medicine that is known, often successful, and properly administered

children.text: na sidhyatyauṣadhaṃ yasya nāsti tasya cikitsitam
children.translated_text: does not take effect for someone, there is no treatment for him.
If, while medicine or food is being prepared for someone, an unexpected reversal

children.text: akasmād varṇagandhādeḥ svastho 'pi na sa jīvati
children.translated_text: of color, smell, and the like suddenly occurs, even if he is healthy he does not live.
If the flame of a fire with fuel goes out in a windless place,

children.text: āturasya gṛhe yasya bhidyante vā patanti vā
children.translated_text: or if, in the sick person's house, vessels break or fall,
and this happens excessively, his life is hard to preserve.

children.text: yaṃ naraṃ sahasā rogo durbalaṃ parimuñcati
children.translated_text: When a disease suddenly leaves a weak man,
<s>Ātreya</s> considers his life to have entered uncertainty.

children.text: kathayen na ca pṛṣṭo 'pi duḥśravaṃ maraṇaṃ bhiṣak
children.translated_text: Even when asked, the physician should not speak of death, which is painful to hear,

children.text: gatāsor bandhumitrāṇāṃ na cecchet taṃ cikitsitum ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of the relatives and friends of one whose life is gone, unless he wishes to treat him.
Because one whose life is gone is attended by messengers of <s>Yama</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and others,
who destroy the powers of medicines, therefore he should be abandoned.
The entire fruit of <s>Āyurveda</s> rests upon knowledge of life span;
therefore a physician should always be attentive to knowledge of <s>riṣṭa</s> (fatal signs).
The death of living beings is observed from the exhaustion of life span, of merit, or of both;
even when these are not exhausted, it is observed among those who do not avoid harmful irregularities.
Now then we shall explain the section of the body doctrine concerning knowledge of messengers and the like.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
For sects, life-stages, and social classes, messengers of the same class lead to success in the undertaking;

children.text: ta eva viparītāḥ syur dūtāḥ karmavipattaye ||
children.translated_text: those same messengers, when contrary, bring failure of the undertaking.
A messenger who is wretched, frightened, hurrying, terrified, harsh, or speaking inauspiciously,
armed with a weapon, carrying a staff, impotent, shaven-headed, or wearing beard or matted hair,
one with an inauspicious name, cruel in action, dirty, or a woman,
many messengers at once, one who is diseased or deformed, or one wearing red garlands and unguents,
one marked with oil and mud, wearing a single garment that is old, discolored, or wet,
one mounted on a donkey, camel, or buffalo, or crushing wood, clods, and the like:

children.text: nānugacched bhiṣag dūtam āhvayantaṃ ca dūrataḥ
children.translated_text: the physician should not follow such a messenger, nor one who summons him from afar.
When there is inauspicious thought or speech at the physician's side, or when he is naked, cutting, or breaking something,
offering into the fire, or setting out rice-balls for the ancestors,
asleep, with hair loose, anointed, weeping, or likewise impure,
then messengers come to the physician on behalf of people who are about to die.
If, in a place or time whose qualities resemble the disorder,

children.text: dūtam abhyāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā nāturaṃ tam upācaret
children.translated_text: the physician sees a messenger arrive, he should not treat that patient.
Touching the navel, nose, mouth, hair, body hair, nails, or teeth,
or the genitals, back, breast, neck, belly, or ring finger,
or cotton, chaff, lead, bone, a skull, a pestle, or a stone,
a broom, winnowing basket, edge of cloth, ash, charcoal, fringe, or husks,
a rope, shoe, balance, noose, or anything else broken or displaced,
after first seeing these, messengers speak for those who are going to die.
Likewise at midnight, at midday, at the two twilights, and on a festival day,
on the sixth, fourth, and ninth lunar days, and at the rising of <s>Rāhu</s> or <s>Ketu</s>, and so on,
under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Pūrvā</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Paitrya</s>, or <s>Nairṛta</s>.
And when a messenger is speaking words concerning the sick person,

children.text: paśyen nimittam aśubhaṃ taṃ ca nānuvrajed bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: if the physician sees an inauspicious omen, he should not follow that messenger.

children.text: tad yathā vikalaḥ pretaḥ pretālaṅkāra eva vā
children.translated_text: That is as follows: a crippled or mutilated person, a corpse, or one adorned like a corpse,

children.text: chinnaṃ dagdhaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ vā tadvādīni vacāṃsi vā ||
children.translated_text: something cut, burned, or destroyed, or words that say such things,

children.text: raso vā kaṭukas tīvro gandho vā kauṇapo mahān
children.translated_text: or a pungent and sharp taste, or a strong corpse-like smell,

children.text: sparśo vā vipulaḥ krūro yad vānyad api tādṛśam ||
children.translated_text: or a broad, harsh touch, or anything else of that kind.

children.text: tat sarvam abhito vākyaṃ vākyakāle 'thavā punaḥ
children.translated_text: If all this occurs around the speech, at the time of the speech, or again

children.text: dūtam abhyāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā nāturaṃ tam upācaret ||
children.translated_text: after seeing the messenger who has arrived, he should not treat that sick person.
Cries of “hā hā,” weeping, loud shouting, abuse, stumbling, and sneezing,
mishaps involving clothes, parasols, or shoes, and the sight of misfortune,
the sinking of shrine-banners and of full vessels,
reports of killing and unwelcome news, and being soiled with ashes or dust,
the path being cut across by snakes, cats, iguanas, lizards, or monkeys,

children.text: dīptāṃ prati diśaṃ vācaḥ krūrāṇāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: and harsh cries of fierce beasts and birds toward a blazing quarter;
the sight of black grain, jaggery, sour gruel, salt, liquor, and hides,
of mustard seed, fat, oil, grass, mud, and fuel,
of eunuchs, cruel men, dog-cook outcastes, and also nets and snares,
of vomit, feces, and what is foul and ugly,
of what is worthless, sexual intercourse, cotton and the like, and an enemy,
and of beds, seats, and vehicles turned upward;
and the inauspicious sight of other things, such as vessels and the like, turned face down.

children.text: puṃsaṃjñāḥ pakṣiṇo vāmāḥ strīsaṃjñā dakṣiṇāḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Birds with male names are auspicious on the left, and those with female names on the right.
Birds and beasts going clockwise are auspicious, but not dogs and jackals in that way.

children.text: ayugmāśca mṛgāḥ śastāḥ śastā nityaṃ ca darśane ||
children.translated_text: Odd-numbered animals are praised, and these are always praised when seen:
the <s>cāṣa</s> bird, the <s>bhāsa</s> bird, the <s>bharadvāja</s> bird, the mongoose, the goat, and the peacock.
The sight of an owl, cat, or lizard is inauspicious in every way.
In mention, the boar, iguana, snake, hare, and <s>jāhaka</s> are praised,
but not when seen or when heard calling; monkeys and bears are otherwise.

children.text: dhanuraindraṃ ca lālāṭam aśubhaṃ śubham anyataḥ
children.translated_text: A rainbow directly in front is inauspicious; in another place it is auspicious.
Vessels full of fire, broken things, and arrows,
curds, unbroken grains, and the like going out, and the auspicious objects to be mentioned below:

children.text: vaidyo mariṣyatāṃ veśma praviśann eva paśyati ||
children.translated_text: the physician sees these as he enters the house of those who are going to die.
Having thus seen what is bad in the messenger and the rest, he should abandon the afflicted person; but otherwise,
with a pure current of compassion, he should treat him carefully.
Curds, unbroken grains, sugarcane, beans, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, honey, and ghee,
barley, collyrium, pitchers, bells, lamps, and lotuses,
<s>dūrvā</s> grass, fresh fish and meat, parched grain, fruits, and foods,
jewels, elephants, full jars, a maiden, and a chariot,
a man who is prospering, deities, and the king,
white flowers, yak-tail fans, garments, and horses,
a conch, a good man, a twice-born man, a turban, an archway, and a <s>svastika</s>,
raised ground and a blazing fire,
pleasant food and drink, and a loaded cart,

children.text: nṛbhir dhenvāḥ savatsāyā vaḍabāyāḥ striyā api ||
children.translated_text: a cow with her calf, a mare, and also a woman accompanied by men,
<s>jīvañjīvaka</s>, <s>sāraṅga</s>, <s>sārasa</s>, and sweet-speaking birds,
geese, <s>śatapattra</s> birds, and also a single tethered animal,
the sight of a golden ornament, a mirror, white mustard seed, and yellow pigment;

children.text: gandhaḥ susurabhir varṇaḥ suśuklo madhuro rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a very fragrant smell, a very white color, and a sweet taste;
the favorable bellowing of a bull, and likewise that of cows;
and auspicious voices of handsome beasts, birds, and men;
the raising of parasols, banners, and flags, and praise;
the sounds of kettledrums, mṛdaṅga drums, and conches, and the sounds of auspicious-day proclamations;
the sounds of Vedic recitation, and a pleasant wind moving clockwise;
on the road and when entering the house, one should know these as signs of recovery.
Thus the omens connected with a messenger have been stated; next they explain dreams.

children.text: svapne madyaṃ saha pretair yaḥ piban kṛṣyate śunā ||
children.translated_text: In a dream, the mortal who drinks liquor together with corpses and is dragged by a dog

children.text: sa martyo mṛtyunā śīghraṃ jvararūpeṇa nīyate
children.translated_text: is quickly carried away by death in the form of fever.
One whose garlands, body, and clothing are red, and who is laughing as he is carried off by a woman,
dies from hemorrhagic <s>pitta</s>; and the one who, by buffaloes, horses, boars, camels, and donkeys,

children.text: yaḥ prayāti diśaṃ yāmyāṃ maraṇaṃ tasya yakṣmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: goes toward the southern quarter, has death from consumption.

children.text: latā kaṇṭakinī vaṃśas tālo vā hṛdi jāyate
children.translated_text: If a thorny creeper, bamboo, or palm tree grows in a person's chest,

children.text: yasya tasyāśu gulmena yasya vahnim anarciṣam ||
children.translated_text: that person soon dies from <s>gulma</s>; and for one whose fire is without flame,
who offers oblations while drenched with ghee and naked, and on whose chest

children.text: padmaṃ sa naśyet kuṣṭhena caṇḍālaiḥ saha yaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: a lotus grows, he perishes from <s>kuṣṭha</s>; the one who drinks with outcastes

children.text: snehaṃ bahuvidhaṃ svapne sa prameheṇa naśyati
children.translated_text: many kinds of unctuous substances in a dream perishes from <s>prameha</s>.

children.text: unmādena jale majjed yo nṛtyan rākṣasaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: The one who, dancing with rākṣasas, sinks in water dies from insanity,

children.text: apasmāreṇa yo martyo nṛtyan pretena nīyate
children.translated_text: and the mortal who is carried off while dancing with a corpse dies from epilepsy.
The one whose vehicle is with donkeys, camels, cats, monkeys, tigers, and pigs,

children.text: yasya pretaiḥ śṛgālair vā sa mṛtyor vartate mukhe
children.translated_text: or with corpses or jackals, is in the mouth of death.
Having eaten cakes and fried pastries, if on waking he vomits the same kind of food,
he does not live; seeing eclipses of the sun and moon leads to eye disease.
Seeing the fall of the sun or moon causes loss of sight.
The growth of bamboo, creepers, and the like on the head, and likewise the dwelling of birds there,
baldness, and being surrounded by crows, vultures, and the like,
as well as association with corpses, piśācas, women, Drāviḍas, Andhras, and cow-eaters,
or being hemmed in among canes, creepers, bamboo, grass, and thorns:
Sleeping in a pit or cremation ground, falling into dust or ashes,
sinking into water, mud, and the like, or being carried off by a swift current;
dancing, instrumental music, and singing; wearing red garlands and garments;
increase of age or limbs, oil-massage, marriage, and shaving of the beard;
eating cooked food with fat or liquor; induced vomiting and purgation;
gain of gold or iron; quarrel, bondage, and defeat;
loss of a pair of shoes, and the feet being stripped of their skin;
excessive joy, and being harshly rebuked by angry ancestors;
the falling, destruction, or breaking of lamps, planets, stars, teeth, deities, and eyes,

children.text: patanaṃ vā vināśo vā bhedanaṃ parvatasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and the splitting of a mountain;
entering a forest with red flowers, a place of sinful deeds,
a pyre, a dense darkness, or one's mother;
falling from a palace, mountain, and the like, and being swallowed by a fish;
the sight of men in ocher garments, inauspicious men, naked men, men bearing staffs,

children.text: raktākṣāṇāṃ ca kṛṣṇānāṃ darśanaṃ jātu neṣyate
children.translated_text: red-eyed men, and black men is never desirable.
A black woman, sinful in face and conduct, with long hair, nails, and breasts,
with faded garlands and clothing, is considered <s>Kālaniśā</s> in a dream.
Because the channels that carry the mind are filled with powerful impurities,

children.text: dṛśyante dāruṇāḥ svapnā rogī yair yāti pañcatām
children.translated_text: terrible dreams appear, by which the sick person goes to the five elements.

children.text: arogaḥ saṃśayaṃ prāpya kaścid eva vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: A healthy person, having come into danger, is released only in some cases.
Seen, heard, experienced, desired, imagined,
future-signifying, and <s>doṣa</s>-born: a dream is considered sevenfold.
Among these, the first five are fruitless; those that follow one's own constitution by day,
that are forgotten, too long, too short, or seen in the first part of the night bear fruit only after a long time.

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ karoti tucchaṃ ca gosarge tadahar mahat
children.translated_text: A trivial dream has trivial effect; one seen at cow-release, on that very day, has great effect.
A bad dream, when not spoiled by further sleep and counteracted by opposite words,
goes to smallness of fruit through gifts, oblations, recitation, and the like.

children.text: akalyāṇam api svapnaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatraiva yaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even after seeing an inauspicious dream, if one there again

children.text: paśyet saumyaṃ śubhaṃ tasya śubham eva phalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: sees a gentle and auspicious one, its result becomes auspicious indeed.

children.text: devān dvijān govṛṣabhān jīvataḥ suhṛdo nṛpān ||
children.translated_text: Whoever sees gods, twice-born men, cows and bulls, living friends, kings,

children.text: sādhūn yaśasvino vahnim iddhaṃ svacchān jalāśayān
children.translated_text: good men, famous men, blazing fire, clear reservoirs,
maidens, boys, fair persons, white-clothed persons, brilliant persons,
a man-eater with blazing body, sprinkled all around with blood,

children.text: yaḥ paśyel labhate yo vā chattrādarśaviṣāmiṣam ||
children.translated_text: or whoever obtains an umbrella, mirror, poison, or meat,
white flowers, clothing, smearing with impure substances, or fruit;
whoever climbs mountains, palaces, fruit-bearing trees, lions, men, or elephants,
rides a cow, horse, or vehicle, and crosses rivers, lakes, or oceans;
going toward the east or north, intercourse with one who should not be approached, a dead person,
escape from confinement, and being congratulated by gods and ancestors;
weeping, rising after a fall, and crushing enemies;

children.text: yasya syād āyurārogyaṃ vittaṃ bahu ca so 'śnute
children.translated_text: for the person who has such a dream, he gains life, health, and much wealth.
When the patient has an entourage furnished with auspicious conduct,
trusting and favorable, and possessing abundant wealth,
when there is conjunction with marks of strength of mind and devotion toward physicians and twice-born men,
and no despondency in treatment, that is the sign of his recovery.
Since birth and death have been properly set forth here,

children.text: śarīrasya tataḥ sthānaṃ śārīram idam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: this section concerning the state of the body is therefore called <s>śārīra</s>.
Now then, we shall explain the causes of all diseases.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: rogaḥ pāpmā jvaro vyādhir vikāro duḥkham āmayaḥ
children.translated_text: Roga, pāpman, jvara, vyādhi, vikāra, duḥkha, and āmaya,
and yakṣman, ātaṅka, gada, and ābādhā are words expressing synonyms.
<s>Nidāna</s>, preliminary signs, manifest signs, relief by suitability,
and pathogenesis: knowledge of diseases is remembered as fivefold.
By the synonyms occasion, cause, seat, condition, origin, and reason,

children.text: nidānam āhuḥ paryāyaiḥ prāgrūpaṃ yena lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: they call it <s>nidāna</s>; that by which a prior sign is perceived is a preliminary sign.
A disease that is about to arise, not yet established in a particular <s>doṣa</s>,

children.text: liṅgam avyaktam alpatvād vyādhīnāṃ tad yathāyatham ||
children.translated_text: has an indistinct sign because of its smallness; that is the preliminary sign of diseases, according to each case.

children.text: tad eva vyaktatāṃ yātaṃ rūpam ityabhidhīyate
children.translated_text: That very thing, when it has become manifest, is called the form or symptom.

children.text: saṃsthānaṃ vyañjanaṃ liṅgaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cihnam ākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Configuration, indication, sign, mark, token, and shape are its terms.
The use of medicines, foods, and regimens that are contrary to the cause and disease,
or that produce an effect contrary to them, and that brings comfort,

children.text: vidyād upaśayaṃ vyādheḥ sa hi sātmyam iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: one should know as the <s>upaśaya</s> of the disease; for it is remembered as what is suitable.
The opposite is non-relief, known as what is unsuitable for the disease.
The production of the disease according to the vitiated <s>doṣa</s>,
and according as it spreads onward, is its <s>saṃprāpti</s>, its birth and course.
That is divided according to number, variation, predominance, strength, and time,

children.text: sā bhidyate yathātraiva vakṣyante 'ṣṭau jvarā iti ||
children.translated_text: as will be stated here, for example: 'there are eight fevers.'
Variation among combined <s>doṣas</s> is the calculation of portions and sub-portions.
One should state the predominance of a disease by independence and dependence.
The distinction of strength and weakness is made by the completeness or partialness of the cause and the rest.
The time of disease is according to the impurity, by night, day, season, and portions of what has been eaten.
Thus the meaning of <s>nidāna</s> has been stated; he will teach it in detail.

children.text: sarveṣām eva rogāṇāṃ nidānaṃ kupitā malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The cause of all diseases is just the aggravated impurities.
And the cause of their aggravation has been stated as the various use of what is unwholesome.

children.text: ahitaṃ trividho yogas trayāṇāṃ prāg udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unwholesomeness is the threefold improper conjunction of the three, as previously explained.
By bitter, hot, astringent, scanty, dry, and measured foods,
by suppression and forced discharge, night-waking, and overly loud speech,
By excessive therapeutic action, fear, grief, worry, exercise, and sexual intercourse,
and in summer, at the ends of day and night, and after digestion, <s>samīraṇa</s> (vāta) becomes aggravated.
<s>Pitta</s> is aggravated by pungent, sour, sharp, hot, and salty things, by anger, and by burning substances,
and in autumn, at midday, at midnight, and at times of burning heat.
By sweet, sour, salty, unctuous, heavy, obstructive, and cold things,
by sitting idle, sleep, comfort, indigestion, daytime sleep, and excessive nourishing,
by insufficient use of emesis and the like, just after eating, and in spring,

children.text: pūrvāhṇe pūrvarātre ca śleṣmā dvandvaṃ tu saṃkarāt ||
children.translated_text: in the forenoon and in the first part of the night, <s>śleṣman</s> is aggravated; paired <s>doṣas</s> arise from combination.
From the blending together of all of them, again, there is <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
And by mixed, undigested, irregular, incompatible food, and by eating before the previous meal is digested,
by spoiled liquor and water, dried greens, and raw radishes,
by oil-cake, earth, barley, beer, and putrid, dried, emaciated meat,
by all such things that produce the three <s>doṣas</s>, and likewise by changes in food,

children.text: ṛtor duṣṭāt purovātād grahāveśād viṣād garāt ||
children.translated_text: by a corrupted season, an easterly wind, possession by planets, poison, and artificial poison,
by spoiled food, proximity to mountains, and planets afflicting one's birth-star,
by various improper applications and by resorting to sinful acts,
in women by irregularity in childbirth, and likewise by improper treatment,
thus, in each disease, the aggravated <s>doṣas</s>, going toward the seats of disease,
quickly enter the <s>rasāyanīs</s> (channels of rasa) and derange the body.
Now then, we shall explain the etiology of fever.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Fever is the lord of diseases, evil, death, the devourer of vitality, and the ender;
it is wrath, the destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, born from the upward eye of <s>Rudra</s>.
At birth and death it is made of delusion; its nature is burning heat, and it is born of misconduct.
Cruel, it exists under various names among many kinds of beings.

children.text: sa jāyate 'ṣṭadhā doṣaiḥ pṛthaṅ miśraiḥ samāgataiḥ
children.translated_text: It arises in eight ways from the <s>doṣas</s>: separately, mixed in pairs, and all combined,

children.text: āgantuśca malās tatra svaiḥ svair duṣṭāḥ pradūṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also as an adventitious fever; there the impurities, vitiated by their respective corrupting factors,
enter the stomach, follow the undigested matter, and obstruct
the channels, driving the digestive fire outward from its place of cooking.
Spreading together with it, heating the whole body,

children.text: kurvanto gātram atyuṣṇaṃ jvaraṃ nirvartayanti te ||
children.translated_text: and making the body intensely hot, they produce fever.

children.text: srotovibandhāt prāyeṇa tataḥ svedo na jāyate
children.translated_text: Because the channels are generally obstructed, sweating then does not occur.
Its prodromal signs are lassitude, discontent, heaviness of the limbs,
bad taste in the mouth, anorexia, yawning, and eyes troubled and watery,
aching of the limbs, indigestion, scant vitality, and excessive sleep,
horripilation, bending of the body, twisting of the calves, and fatigue,
impatience with wholesome advice, and liking for sour, salty, and hot things,

children.text: dveṣaḥ svāduṣu bhakṣyeṣu tathā bāleṣu tṛḍ bhṛśam
children.translated_text: aversion toward sweet foods, and, among children, especially thirst.
Without cause, there is desire and aversion toward sounds, fire, cold, wind, water, shade, and heat;

children.text: icchā dveṣaśca tadanu jvarasya vyaktatā bhavet
children.translated_text: after that, fever becomes manifest.
Irregularity of onset, cessation, agitation, mildness, pain, and heat

children.text: vaiṣamyaṃ tatra tatrāṅge tās tāḥ syur vedanāścalāḥ
children.translated_text: occurs here and there in the limbs, and various shifting pains arise.
In the feet there are numbness, stiffness, twisting of the calves, and weakness;

children.text: viśleṣa iva saṃdhīnāṃ sāda ūrvoḥ kaṭīgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: it is as if the joints were loosened, there is exhaustion in the thighs, and there is gripping pain in the waist.
The back feels as if crushed, and the abdomen as if it were being squeezed.
The bones seem to be cut apart, especially those along the flanks.
There is seizure and pricking of the heart, and the chest feels as if goaded by a driving spur.

children.text: skandhayor mathanaṃ bāhvor bhedaḥ pīḍanam aṃsayoḥ
children.translated_text: There is churning pain in the shoulders, splitting pain in the arms, and pressure in the upper arms.

children.text: aśaktir bhakṣaṇe hanvor jṛmbhaṇaṃ karṇayoḥ svanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is inability to eat, yawning of the jaws, and ringing in the ears,
piercing pain in the temples, pain in the head, and bad taste in the mouth,
or else an astringent taste in the mouth, and non-movement of the wastes.
The skin, mouth, eyes, nails, urine, and feces become dry and reddish.
There are salivation, anorexia, lack of desire for food, indigestion, absence of sweating, and wakefulness,
dryness of the throat and lips, thirst, dryness, vomiting, cough, and dejection,
horripilation in the body-hairs and teeth, trembling, and obstruction of sneezing.
Dizziness, delirium, desire for warmth, and bending of the body occur in fever from <s>anila</s> (vāta).
In fever from <s>pitta</s> there are simultaneous pervasion of the limbs, delirium, and pungency in the mouth,
suppuration of the nose and mouth, desire for cold, dizziness, fainting, intoxication, and restlessness,
loose stools, vomiting of bile, spitting of blood, and sour eructation,
the appearance of red wheals, and yellowness and greenness in the skin and other parts,
sweating, foul smell of the breath, and excessive thirst.
In fever arising from <s>kapha</s> there are especially anorexia, sluggishness, obstruction of the channels, and low intensity,
salivation, sweetness in the mouth, coating in the cardiac region, dyspnea, and coryza,
nausea, vomiting, cough, stiffness, and whiteness in the skin and other parts,
cold eruptions on the limbs, torpor, and urticaria.

children.text: kāle yathāsvaṃ sarveṣāṃ pravṛttir vṛddhireva vā
children.translated_text: All of them begin or increase at the time proper to each.
There is non-relief by the measures stated under the causes, and relief by opposite measures.
When the signs proper to each are combined, fever is also produced by conjunction.
Headache, fainting, vomiting, burning, stupor, dryness of the throat and mouth, restlessness, and splitting pain in the joints,
sleeplessness, thirst, dizziness, horripilation, yawning, and excessive speech are from <s>vāta</s> joined with <s>pitta</s>.
Decrease of heat, anorexia, pain in the joints and head, coryza, dyspnea, cough, and constipation,
coldness, sluggishness, darkness before the eyes, dizziness, and drowsiness are signs of fever produced by <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Irregular cold, stiffness, sweat, and burning, thirst, cough, and activity of <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: mohas tandrā liptatiktāsyatā ca jñeyaṃ rūpaṃ śleṣmapittajvarasya ||
children.translated_text: stupor, drowsiness, and a coated, bitter mouth should be known as the form of fever from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: sarvajo lakṣaṇaiḥ sarvair dāho 'tra ca muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: The fever arising from all <s>doṣas</s> has all the symptoms, and in it there is burning again and again.
Likewise, there is coldness, great sleep, wakefulness by day and by night,

children.text: sadā vā naiva vā nidrā mahāsvedo 'ti naiva vā
children.translated_text: or sleep either always or never, and great sweating, or excessive sweating or none at all;
the undertaking of distorted actions such as singing, dancing, laughing, and the like;
the eyes are tearful, turbid, red, bent, with lashes in disorder,
and there is pain in the calves, flanks, head, joints, and bones, with dizziness;
the ears ring and are painful, and the throat feels as if filled with awns;
the tongue is as though burnt and rough, and the joints of the limbs are heavy and slack;
there is spitting of blood, bile, and phlegm, rolling of the head, and excessive pain;
and there is the appearance of eruptions and patches that are dark and red.
There is pain in the heart, retention of stool, or evacuation in very small quantity or excessively;
oiliness of the mouth, loss of strength, depression of the voice, and delirious speech;
slow maturation of the <s>doṣas</s>, drowsiness, and constant gurgling in the throat.
One should call that condition <s>saṃnipāta</s> and <s>abhinyāsa</s>, with the <s>ojas</s> seized away.
When the <s>doṣa</s> is obstructed, the digestive fire lost, and all its symptoms are complete,

children.text: asādhyaḥ so 'nyathā kṛcchro bhaved vaikalyado 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: it is incurable; otherwise it is difficult to cure, and it may also cause deformity.

children.text: anyacca saṃnipātottho yatra pittaṃ pṛthak sthitam
children.translated_text: There is another fever arising from <s>saṃnipāta</s>, where the <s>pitta</s> remains separately situated

children.text: tvaci koṣṭhe 'thavā dāhaṃ vidadhāti puro 'nu vā ||
children.translated_text: in the skin or in the alimentary tract, and produces burning either first or afterward.

children.text: tadvad vātakaphau śītaṃ dāhādir dustaras tayoḥ
children.translated_text: In the same way, <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> produce cold; when burning and the other symptoms occur, those two are hard to overcome.
There, when cold comes first, after the <s>kapha</s> has been liquefied and dried up by <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: śīte śānte 'mlako mūrchā madas tṛṣṇā ca jāyate
children.translated_text: and the cold has subsided, sourness, fainting, intoxication, and thirst arise.
But when burning comes first, at the end there are drowsiness, spitting, vomiting, and fatigue.
Adventitious fever is fourfold, from injury, contact or possession, curse, and sorcery.
Here, that arising from injury is caused by wounds, cuts, burns, and the like.

children.text: śramācca tasmin pavanaḥ prāyo raktaṃ pradūṣayan
children.translated_text: In that case, and from exertion, <s>pavana</s> (vāta), generally vitiating the blood,
produces a painful fever with pain, swelling, and discoloration.
That due to contact or seizure may be caused by possession by spirits, medicines, poison, anger, fear, grief, or desire.
In this one, when due to a possessing spirit, there is sudden laughter and crying.
When caused by the smell of medicines, there is fainting, headache, vomiting, and sneezing.
From poison there are fainting, diarrhea, darkening of the mouth, burning, and heart disease.

children.text: krodhāt kampaḥ śiroruk ca pralāpo bhayaśokaje
children.translated_text: From anger there are trembling and headache; in that from fear and grief, there is delirious speech.
From desire there are dizziness, anorexia, burning, and loss of shame, sleep, intellect, and steadiness.
In the cases beginning with spirit-possession, there is aggravation of <s>saṃnipāta</s>; in those beginning with fear, aggravation of <s>marut</s> (vāta) among the three;

children.text: kopaḥ kope 'pi pittasya yau tu śāpābhicārajau ||
children.translated_text: in anger there is aggravation of <s>pitta</s>. But the two fevers produced by curse and sorcery
are terrible <s>saṃnipāta</s> fevers and are considered the most unbearable.
In the case of sorcery, when offerings are being made with hostile mantras,

children.text: pūrvaṃ cetas tato dehas tato visphoṭatṛḍbhramaiḥ
children.translated_text: first the mind burns, then the body; then, with eruptions, thirst, and dizziness,
and seized by burning and fainting, his fever increases day by day.

children.text: iti jvaro 'ṣṭadhā dṛṣṭaḥ samāsād vividhas tu saḥ
children.translated_text: Thus fever has been seen as eightfold in brief, but it is manifold:
bodily and mental, mild and sharp, with internal or external seat,
natural and abnormal, curable and incurable, with <s>āma</s> and without <s>āma</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ śarīre śārīre tāpo manasi mānase ||
children.translated_text: In bodily fever, heat first appears in the body; in mental fever, in the mind.
When joined with <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha), because <s>pavana</s> is a carrier of conjunction, there is coldness;
when joined with <s>pitta</s>, there is burning; when mixed, there is a mixed condition. Again, in fever seated internally,
the disorders are more severe: internal agitation and retention of wastes.
When the force is external, the heat is only external, and there is easy curability.
In the rainy season, autumn, and spring, fever is natural through <s>vāta</s> and the others respectively.
Any other is abnormal and difficult to cure; and the natural fever is mostly from <s>anila</s> (vāta).
In the rains, vitiated <s>māruta</s> (vāta), joined with <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha),

children.text: kuryāt pittaṃ ca śaradi tasya cānubalaṃ kaphaḥ ||
children.translated_text: produces fever; in autumn <s>pitta</s> does so, and <s>kapha</s> is its auxiliary force.
Because of its nature and because of the period of emission, there is no danger there from fasting.

children.text: kapho vasante tam api vātapittaṃ bhaved anu ||
children.translated_text: In spring, <s>kapha</s> produces it, and <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> become subsequent auxiliaries to it.
Fever is curable when the patient is strong, the <s>doṣas</s> are slight, and there are no complications.
The incurable type has already been described under the full knowledge of abnormality in every respect.
Sharpness of the complications of fever, absence of weariness, abundant urination,

children.text: na pravṛttir na viḍ jīrṇā na kṣut sāmajvarākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: no evacuation, undigested stool, and no hunger: these are the form of <s>sāma-jvara</s> (fever with undigested matter).
Greater intensity of the fever, thirst, delirium, difficult breathing, and dizziness,
evacuation of wastes, and nausea are the signs that it is being digested.
By the opposites of the undigested state, and by fasting for seven nights, fever reaches the digested state.
Fever is said to be fivefold according to the impurity, time, strength, and weakness.
For the most part it is taught as arising from <s>saṃnipāta</s>, and, more specifically,
as continuous, constant, alternate-day, third-day, and fourth-day fever.
The impurities pervading the channels that carry tissue, urine, and feces,
heating the whole body and increased by similar affected substrates and other factors,
being strong, heavy, obstructive, and especially lodged in <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid),
without any opposing force, produce a continuous fever that is very hard to bear.

children.text: malaṃ jvaroṣmā dhātūn vā sa śīghraṃ kṣapayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: The heat of fever quickly wastes the impurity or the tissues; therefore,
it proceeds in every form according to the purification or impurification of <s>rasa</s> and the rest in sequence.
With <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, respectively, for seven, ten, or twelve days,

children.text: prāyo 'nuyāti maryādāṃ mokṣāya ca vadhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: it generally reaches its limit, either for release or for death.
This is the opinion of <s>Agniveśa</s>; but the recollection of <s>Hārīta</s> is that
the periods are doubled, up to the seventh, and likewise the ninth and eleventh days.

children.text: eṣā tridoṣamaryādā mokṣāya ca vadhāya ca
children.translated_text: This is the limit for the three <s>doṣas</s>, either for release or for death.
Whether purification occurs or not, fever may continue for a long time.
For emaciated persons, those freed from disease, and those who follow wrong diet and conduct,
even a slight <s>doṣa</s>, having obtained strength from one among the affected substrates and the like...
A <s>doṣa</s> with its opposing factor produces an irregular fever, subject to decrease and increase;

children.text: doṣaḥ pravartate teṣāṃ sve kāle jvarayan balī ||
children.translated_text: among them, the powerful <s>doṣa</s> becomes active at its own time, causing fever.
This again subsides according to the strength or weakness of the counteracting force;

children.text: kṣīṇe doṣe jvaraḥ sūkṣmo rasādiṣveva līyate ||
children.translated_text: when the <s>doṣa</s> is diminished, the subtle fever remains hidden in <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues.
Because it is latent, it brings about emaciation, discoloration, dullness, and the like;
because the mouths of the <s>rasa</s>-carrying channels are near and open,

children.text: āśu sarvasya vapuṣo vyāptir doṣeṇa jāyate
children.translated_text: the whole body is quickly pervaded by the <s>doṣa</s>.
Therefore the fever is continuous or constant; from the opposite condition comes the opposite pattern.
An irregular fever has irregular onset, course of activity, timing, and recurrence.

children.text: doṣo raktāśrayaḥ prāyaḥ karoti satataṃ jvaram ||
children.translated_text: A <s>doṣa</s> lodged chiefly in the blood produces constant fever.

children.text: ahorātrasya sa dviḥ syāt sakṛd anyedyurāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: That occurs twice within a day and night; the other, occurring once on the next day, is so based.
In that case it seizes the flesh-carrying channels; in tertian fever, the fat-carrying channels.
From <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s> it takes hold of the head; from <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, of the sacral region;
from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, of the back as well; and that is remembered as occurring with one day between.
Quartan fever occurs when the impurity is situated in any one of fat, marrow, or bone;

children.text: majjastha evetyapare prabhāvaṃ sa tu darśayet ||
children.translated_text: others say it is only when situated in marrow, but that fever displays its own power.

children.text: dvidhā kaphena jaṅghābhyāṃ sa pūrvaṃ śiraso 'nilāt
children.translated_text: It is twofold: through <s>kapha</s> it begins from the legs, and through <s>vāta</s> from the head.
When it has entered both bone and marrow, there is the reverse of quartan fever.

children.text: tridhā dvyahaṃ jvarayati dinam ekaṃ tu muñcati
children.translated_text: In threefold fashion it produces fever for two days and releases the patient for one day.
According to the strength and weakness of the <s>doṣas</s>, born from food, activity, and the like,

children.text: jvaraḥ syān manasas tadvat karmaṇaśca tadā tadā
children.translated_text: fever may arise from the mind in the same way, and from karma, at such and such a time.
By the strength of <s>doṣa</s>, affected tissue, season, day and night, and so on,

children.text: manaso viṣayāṇāṃ ca kālaṃ taṃ taṃ prapadyate
children.translated_text: and by the strength of the mind and its objects, fever comes at its particular time.
Having agitated the tissues, the <s>doṣa</s> becomes latent at the time of release.

children.text: tato naraḥ śvasan svidyan kūjan vamati ceṣṭate
children.translated_text: Then the person breathes hard, sweats, groans, vomits, and writhes;
he trembles and babbles, his limbs hot and cold, his luster destroyed.
Unconscious and afflicted by the rush of fever, he looks as if angry;

children.text: sadoṣaśabdaṃ ca śakṛd dravaṃ sṛjati vegavat ||
children.translated_text: and he forcefully passes liquid stool, noisy and filled with morbid matter.

children.text: deho laghur vyapagataklamamohatāpaḥ pāko mukhe karaṇasauṣṭhavam avyathatvam
children.translated_text: Lightness of the body, the absence of fatigue, confusion, and heat, digestion, clarity in the mouth, sound functioning of the senses, and freedom from pain,

children.text: svedaḥ kṣavaḥ prakṛtiyogi mano 'nnalipsā kaṇḍūśca mūrdhni vigatajvaralakṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: sweating, sneezing, a mind in its natural state, desire for food, and itching on the head are signs that fever has gone.
Now then, we shall explain the etiology of <s>raktapitta</s> and cough.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Through excessive use of extremely hot, sharp, pungent, sour, salty, and other burning substances,
and through grains such as <s>kodrava</s> and <s>uddālaka</s>, and foods combined with those,

children.text: kupitaṃ pittalaiḥ pittaṃ dravaṃ raktaṃ ca mūrchite
children.translated_text: <s>pitta</s>, aggravated by <s>pitta</s>-provoking things, and the fluid blood become disturbed;

children.text: te mithas tulyarūpatvam āgamya vyāpnutas tanum ||
children.translated_text: having reached mutual similarity in form, they spread through the body.

children.text: pittaṃ raktasya vikṛteḥ saṃsargād dūṣaṇād api
children.translated_text: Because <s>pitta</s> is associated with blood in its alteration, and because it vitiates it,
and because it follows its smell and color, it is designated by the term blood.
It arises from the seat of blood, from the spleen and from the liver.
Heaviness of the head, loss of appetite, desire for cold, a smoky sensation, and sour eructation,
vomiting, disgust at what is vomited, cough, dyspnea, dizziness, and fatigue,
a mouth smelling like iron, blood, or raw fish, and loss of voice,
red, yellow, and green coloration in the eyes and other parts,
inability to distinguish blue, red, and yellow colors,
and seeing such colors in dreams occur when this disease is about to arise.
When aggravated, it proceeds upward through the nose, eyes, ears, and mouth, and downward through the penis, vagina, and anus;
and through the hair follicles and all the openings together it flows forth.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ sādhyaṃ kaphād yasmāt tad virecanasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: The upward form is curable because it is due to <s>kapha</s>, since it is treatable by purgation;

children.text: bahvauṣadhaṃ ca pittasya vireko hi varauṣadham
children.translated_text: there are many medicines for <s>pitta</s>, and purgation is its best medicine.

children.text: anubandhī kapho yaśca tatra tasyāpi śuddhikṛt ||
children.translated_text: And the accompanying <s>kapha</s> is also purified by that treatment.
Astringent and sweet remedies too are beneficial for this patient when the phlegm has been purified;

children.text: kimu tiktāḥ kaṣāyā vā ye nisargāt kaphāpahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more, then, are bitter or astringent remedies beneficial, since by nature they remove <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: adho yāpyaṃ calād yasmāt tat pracchardanasādhanam
children.translated_text: The downward form is manageable, because it is due to mobile <s>vāta</s>; it is treatable by emesis.

children.text: alpauṣadhaṃ ca pittasya vamanaṃ na varauṣadham ||
children.translated_text: But there are few medicines for <s>pitta</s>, and vomiting is not its best medicine.

children.text: anubandhī calo yaśca śāntaye 'pi na tasya tat
children.translated_text: And the accompanying mobile <s>vāta</s> is not calmed by that treatment either.

children.text: kaṣāyāśca hitās tasya madhurā eva kevalam ||
children.translated_text: Only astringent remedies that are sweet are beneficial for this patient.
When mixed with <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s> and moving by both paths, it is incurable,
because it cannot be turned back and because there is no medicine for it.

children.text: na hi saṃśodhanaṃ kiṃcid astyasya pratilomagam
children.translated_text: For there is no purificatory treatment for it that moves against its course;
and in <s>raktapitta</s>, purifying treatment against the course is the physician's means of conquest.
Likewise, complete pacification of it is not found in every respect;
for when the <s>doṣas</s> are combined, a pacifying remedy that overcomes all of them is beneficial.
There one should recognize the following of the <s>doṣas</s> as in blood from a vein,
and also the complications; from knowledge of the morbid change, one should attend especially to what predominates among them.

children.text: āśukārī yataḥ kāsas tam evātaḥ pravakṣyati
children.translated_text: Because cough acts quickly, therefore he will now explain that very disease.
Five coughs are remembered: those caused by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, injury, and wasting.
All, if neglected, lead to wasting, and the later ones are successively stronger.
The sign that they are about to arise is itching in the throat and loss of taste.
There is a feeling as though the throat were filled with awns; then <s>vāta</s>, obstructed below,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ pravṛttaḥ prāpyoras tasmin kaṇṭhe ca saṃsajan ||
children.translated_text: moves upward, reaches the chest, and attaches there and in the throat.
Filling the channels of the head, it then seems to toss the limbs upward,

children.text: kṣipann ivākṣiṇī pṛṣṭham uraḥ pārśve ca pīḍayan ||
children.translated_text: to hurl the eyes, and to pain the back, chest, and flanks.
It proceeds through the mouth with a sound like broken bronze.
Because of the difference in causes, or the difference in obstruction of the swift-moving <s>vāyu</s>,
there arises the variation in pain and sound among coughs.
When aggravated by things that provoke <s>vāta</s>, <s>vāta</s> produces dryness of the chest, throat, and mouth,
pain in the heart-region, sides, chest, and head, confusion, agitation, and loss of voice,
and a dry cough with a great, painful, noisy impulse.

children.text: so 'ṅgaharṣī kaphaṃ śuṣkaṃ kṛcchrān muktvālpatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: It is accompanied by horripilation; after dry phlegm is expelled with difficulty, it becomes scanty.
From <s>pitta</s> there are yellow eyes and phlegm, bitterness of the mouth, fever, and dizziness.
There are vomiting of <s>pitta</s> and blood, thirst, hoarseness, a smoky sensation, and sourness,
and, because of the continual force of coughing, the sight of lights as it were.
From <s>kapha</s> there is slight pain in the chest; the head and heart-region are numb and heavy.
There is coating of the throat, weakness, coryza, vomiting, and loss of appetite.
There is horripilation and the discharge of thick, unctuous, white phlegm.
Through such acts of violence as battle and the like, undertaken beyond one's strength,
when there is internal injury in the chest, powerful <s>vāyu</s>, accompanied by <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: kupitaḥ kurute kāsaṃ kaphaṃ tena saśoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: becomes aggravated and produces cough; because of it the phlegm is mixed with blood.

children.text: pītaṃ śyāvaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca grathitaṃ kuthitaṃ bahu
children.translated_text: One spits out much phlegm that is yellow and dark, dry, clotted, and putrid,
with pain in the throat and as if the chest were split open.
It is painful, as if being pierced by sharp needles,
with splitting pain in the joints, fever, dyspnea, thirst, hoarseness, and trembling.
Cooing like a dove and having pain in the side, thereafter

children.text: kramād vīryaṃ ruciḥ paktā balaṃ varṇaśca hīyate ||
children.translated_text: his vigor, taste for food, digestion, strength, and complexion gradually decline.
In one who is wasted, there may be blood in the urine and stiffness of the back and waist.
In a patient with <s>rājayakṣman</s>, the aggravated tissues, with <s>vāyu</s> predominant,

children.text: kurvanti yakṣmāyatanaiḥ kāsaṃ ṣṭhīvet kaphaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: produce cough through the seats of <s>yakṣman</s>; then he spits out phlegm
like foul pus, yellow, fetid, and greenish-red.

children.text: lucyete iva pārśve ca hṛdayaṃ patatīva ca
children.translated_text: The sides seem to be torn apart, and the heart seems to be falling.
There are sudden desires for heat and cold, excessive eating, and loss of strength,
an unctuous and clear face, and eyes that appear splendid and beautiful.
Then all the forms of wasting become manifest in him.
This is the cough born of wasting, destructive of the bodies of the emaciated.

children.text: yāpyo vā balināṃ tadvat kṣatajo 'bhinavau tu tau ||
children.translated_text: For the strong it is manageable, and the injury-born form is the same; but if the two are recent,

children.text: sidhyetām api sānāthyāt sādhyā doṣaiḥ pṛthak trayaḥ
children.translated_text: they may even be cured because support remains. The three that arise separately from the <s>doṣas</s> are curable.

children.text: miśrā yāpyā dvayāt sarve jarasā sthavirasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Mixed forms arising from two <s>doṣas</s> are manageable, as are all forms in an aged person and those due to old age.
Since diseases such as dyspnea, wasting, vomiting, and loss of voice

children.text: bhavantyupekṣayā yasmāt tasmāt taṃ tvarayā jayet ||
children.translated_text: arise from cough when it is neglected, one should therefore overcome it quickly.
Now then, we shall explain the causes of dyspnea and hiccup.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Dyspnea may arise from the increase of cough, or from the previously mentioned provocations of the <s>doṣas</s>,
and also from <s>āma</s>, diarrhea, vomiting, poison, anemia, and fever.
It may arise from dust, smoke, wind, injury to a vital point, or excessively cold water.
The varieties are minor, <s>tamaka</s>, interrupted, great, and, as the fifth, upward dyspnea.
When the movement of <s>pavana</s> is obstructed by <s>kapha</s> and it is lodged everywhere in the body,
it becomes vitiated and vitiates the channels carrying breath, water, and food.
Situated in the chest, it produces dyspnea arising from the stomach.
Its prodrome is pain in the heart-region and sides, reversal of the movement of breath,
abdominal distension, and splitting pain in the temples. There, when impelled by exertion and overeating,

children.text: preritaḥ prerayet kṣudraṃ svayaṃ saṃśamanaṃ marut ||
children.translated_text: the wind, set in motion, produces minor dyspnea, which subsides on its own.

children.text: pratilomaṃ sirā gacchann udīrya pavanaḥ kapham
children.translated_text: Moving against its course through the vessels, <s>pavana</s> stirs up <s>kapha</s>;

children.text: parigṛhya śirogrīvam uraḥ pārśve ca pīḍayan ||
children.translated_text: seizing the head and neck and oppressing the chest and sides,

children.text: kāsaṃ ghurghurakaṃ moham arucim pīnasaṃ tṛṣam
children.translated_text: it causes a rumbling cough, confusion, loss of appetite, coryza, and thirst,
as well as an intense attack of dyspnea that torments the vital breath.

children.text: pratāmyet tasya vegena niṣṭhyūtānte kṣaṇaṃ sukhī
children.translated_text: He is faint with its attack, but after expectoration he is comfortable for a moment.
He breathes with difficulty when lying down, but when seated he attains ease.
His eyes are raised; sweating on the forehead, he is greatly distressed.
His mouth is dry, he breathes again and again, longs for warmth, and trembles.
It is increased by clouds, rain, cold, easterly wind, and phlegm-producing things.

children.text: sa yāpyas tamakaḥ sādhyo navo vā balino bhavet ||
children.translated_text: This <s>tamaka</s> is manageable; if recent, or occurring in a strong person, it may be curable.

children.text: jvaramūrchāyutaḥ śītaiḥ śāmyet pratamakas tu saḥ
children.translated_text: When it is accompanied by fever and fainting and is calmed by cold things, that is <s>pratamaka</s>.
In interrupted dyspnea one breathes in broken breaths, afflicted by pain as if the vital points were being cut.
There is sweating, fainting, abdominal distension, burning in the bladder, and retention.
His gaze is downward, his eyes are unsettled, he is confused, and one eye is blood-red.
His mouth is dry; he talks deliriously, is wretched, has lost his luster, and is unconscious.

children.text: mahatā mahatā dīno nādena śvasiti krathan ||
children.translated_text: With a very great sound he breathes, wretched and groaning.
Heaving upward and agitated, he is like an intoxicated bull at all times.
His knowledge and discernment are lost, and his eyes and face are confused.
He tosses his chest about, urine and feces are obstructed, and his speech is broken.
His throat is dry; repeatedly fainting, he has severe pain in the ears, temples, and head.

children.text: dīrgham ūrdhvaṃ śvasityūrdhvān na ca pratyāharatyadhaḥ
children.translated_text: He breathes long upward breaths, and does not draw the breath back downward.
The passages of his mouth are covered with phlegm, and he is afflicted by the enraged odor-bearing wind.

children.text: ūrdhvadṛg vīkṣate bhrāntam akṣiṇī paritaḥ kṣipan
children.translated_text: With upward gaze he looks about wildly, casting his eyes all around.
As his vital points are being cut, he laments, with speech obstructed.
These may be cured when unmanifest; when manifest, they certainly take life.
Hiccup has the same causes, prodrome, number, nature, and seats as dyspnea.

children.text: hidhmā bhaktodbhavā kṣudrā yamalā mahatīti ca
children.translated_text: Hiccup is said to be food-born, minor, double, great,
and deep. There, <s>marut</s>, oppressed by foods and drinks used hastily and without proper method,
which are dry, sharp, rough, and unsuitable,
produces a painless hiccup, low in sound and following sneezing.

children.text: śamaṃ sātmyānnapānena yā prayāti ca sānnajā
children.translated_text: The one that subsides through suitable food and drink is food-born.

children.text: āyāsāt pavanaḥ kṣudraḥ kṣudrāṃ hidhmāṃ pravartayet ||
children.translated_text: From exertion, a slight <s>pavana</s> (wind) may set in motion a slight hiccup.
It spreads from the root of the collarbones; its impulse is weak and it is gentle.

children.text: vṛddhim āyāsyato yāti bhuktamātre ca mārdavam ||
children.translated_text: It increases in one who is about to exert himself, and becomes mild just after eating.
That which starts after a long time, with paired impulses, when food
is approaching digestion, and which increases during digestion,
shaking the head and neck of one who is bloated and exceedingly thirsty,
with delirious speech, vomiting, diarrhea, disturbed eyes, and yawning,

children.text: yamalā veginī hidhmā pariṇāmavatī ca sā
children.translated_text: is the paired, violent hiccup; it is also called the digestion-related one.
For one whose brows and temples are rigid, and whose eyes are tearful and agitated,

children.text: stambhayantī tanuṃ vācaṃ smṛtiṃ saṃjñāṃ ca muṣṇatī
children.translated_text: stiffening the body, speech, memory, and consciousness, and stealing them away,
blocking the path of food and causing injury to the vital points,
producing backward bending and wasting, the great hiccup arises.
It has a great root, great sound, great force, and great strength.

children.text: pakvāśayād vā nābher vā pūrvavad yā pravartate
children.translated_text: That which arises, as before, from the colon or from the navel,

children.text: tadrūpā sā muhuḥ kuryāj jṛmbhām aṅgaprasāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: having that same character, repeatedly produces yawning and stretching of the limbs.
Among these, one should treat the deep hiccup, marked by a deep resonance.

children.text: ādye dve varjayed antye sarvaliṅgāṃ ca veginīm ||
children.translated_text: The first two should be abandoned, and also the final, violent one when it has all the signs.
All hiccups should be rejected when accumulated in an aged man, in one given to sexual activity,
in one whose body has been wasted by diseases, or in one deprived of food and injured.

children.text: sarve 'pi rogā nāśāya na tvevaṃ śīghrakāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: All diseases may lead to destruction, but none acts so quickly

children.text: hidhmāśvāsau yathā tau hi mṛtyukāle kṛtālayau ||
children.translated_text: as hiccup and dyspnea, for those two have their dwelling at the time of death.
Now then, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>rājayakṣmā</s> and the other disorders.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Associated with many diseases and preceded by many diseases,

children.text: rājayakṣmā kṣayaḥ śoṣo rogarāḍ iti ca smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>rājayakṣmā</s> is remembered also as <s>kṣaya</s> (wasting), <s>śoṣa</s> (drying up), and the king of diseases.

children.text: nakṣatrāṇāṃ dvijānāṃ ca rājño 'bhūd yad ayaṃ purā
children.translated_text: Because this formerly befell the king of the stars and of the twice-born,

children.text: yacca rājā ca yakṣmā ca rājayakṣmā tato mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because it is both royal and a <s>yakṣmā</s>, it is therefore regarded as <s>rājayakṣmā</s>.
It is called <s>kṣaya</s> because it causes wasting of the body and medicines, and because it arises from that.
It is <s>śoṣa</s> because it dries up <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues, and the king of diseases because it rules among them.
Overexertion, suppression of natural urges, depletion of semen, vitality, and unctuousness,
and abandonment of the rules for food and drink: these are its four causes.
By these, aggravated <s>anila</s> (wind) also aggravates <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> everywhere.
Entering the joints of the body and pressing upon them and upon the vessels,
blocking the openings of the channels, or else making them too open,

children.text: sarpann ūrdhvam adhas tiryag yathāsvaṃ janayed gadān ||
children.translated_text: moving upward, downward, and sideways, it produces disorders according to each place.

children.text: rūpaṃ bhaviṣyatas tasya pratiśyāyo bhṛśaṃ kṣavaḥ
children.translated_text: The form of the disease that is about to arise is severe coryza and sneezing,
salivation, sweetness in the mouth, and weakness of digestion and body,
a sense of foulness in vessels, food, drink, and so on, even when they are clean,
and the apparent falling of flies, grass, hair, and the like into food and drink.
There is nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, and loss of strength even in one who eats,
inspection of the hands, swelling of the feet and face, and excessive whiteness of the eyes,
a desire to know the measure of the arms, seeing ugliness in the body,
fondness for women, liquor, and meat, disgust, and covering the head,
excessive growth of nails and hair, and, in dreams, being overcome
by insects, chameleons, snakes, monkeys, wild beasts, and birds,
or climbing upon heaps of hair, bones, husks, ashes, and the like,
seeing empty villages and regions, and water that is drying up,

children.text: jyotir girīṇāṃ patatāṃ jvalatāṃ ca mahīruhām
children.translated_text: and lights and mountains falling, and trees blazing.
Coryza, dyspnea, cough, pain in the shoulders, head, and voice, and loss of appetite occur.
When it is situated above, there are displacement and drying up of feces; when below, vomiting; and when in the alimentary tract,
when it is situated laterally, pain in the sides; when the <s>doṣa</s> is in the joints, fever occurs.
These eleven forms arise in a person with <s>rājayakṣmā</s>.
One should know their complications to be destruction of the throat and pain in the chest,
yawning, aching of the limbs, spitting, weakness of digestion, and foulness of the mouth.
There, from <s>vāta</s>, there is pain in the head and sides, aching in the shoulders and limbs,
destruction of the throat and loss of voice; from <s>pitta</s>, burning in the feet, shoulders, and hands,
diarrhea, vomiting of blood, bad odor of the mouth, fever, and intoxication.
From <s>kapha</s> there are anorexia, vomiting, cough, heaviness of the head and limbs,
salivation, coryza, dyspnea, weakness of the voice, and poor digestive fire.
When the openings of the channels are blocked by the <s>doṣas</s>, because the digestive fire is weak,
and when they are coated and dominated by <s>kapha</s>, and the tissue heat is slight,

children.text: vidahyamānaḥ svasthāne rasas tāṃs tān upadravān
children.translated_text: <s>rasa</s>, being cooked in its own place, produces those various complications,

children.text: kuryād agacchan māṃsādīn asṛk cordhvaṃ pradhāvati ||
children.translated_text: not going on to flesh and the other tissues; and the blood rushes upward.

children.text: pacyate koṣṭha evānnam annapaktraiva cāsya yat
children.translated_text: Food is digested only in the alimentary tract, and whatever digestion of food he has
generally becomes waste from this; it is not at all sufficient for nourishing the tissues.

children.text: raso 'pyasya na raktāya māṃsāya kuta eva tu
children.translated_text: Even his <s>rasa</s> does not become blood; how much less could it become flesh?

children.text: upastabdhaḥ sa śakṛtā kevalaṃ vartate kṣayī ||
children.translated_text: Supported only by feces, the wasting patient continues to live.
One should reject a wasted patient, even if the signs are few, when he cannot bear disease, medicines, or exertion.
Otherwise one should treat him even when all signs are present.

children.text: doṣair vyastaiḥ samastaiśca kṣayāt ṣaṣṭhaśca medasā
children.translated_text: Through the <s>doṣas</s>, separately and together, and as a sixth type through wasting and through fat,

children.text: svarabhedo bhavet tatra kṣāmo rūkṣaścalaḥ svaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is alteration of the voice. In that condition the voice is thin, dry, and unsteady.
A sensation as if the throat were filled with bristles, relieved by unctuous and warm things, is due to <s>anila</s>.
From <s>pitta</s> there is burning in the palate and throat, dryness, and irritation when speaking.

children.text: limpann iva kaphāt kaṇṭhaṃ mandaḥ khurakhurāyate
children.translated_text: From <s>kapha</s>, the voice seems to smear the throat; it is dull and makes a rough rattling sound.

children.text: svaro vibaddhaḥ sarvais tu sarvaliṅgaḥ kṣayāt kaṣet ||
children.translated_text: When caused by all the <s>doṣas</s>, the voice is obstructed and has all the signs; when due to wasting, it is hoarse.
When due to fat, it seems extremely smoky and has the signs of <s>śleṣman</s>.
Here, when the syllables are hard to discern in all cases, and also in the final type, one should reject the patient.
<s>Arocaka</s> (loss of relish) arises from the <s>doṣas</s> lodged in the tongue and heart;
from <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined doṣas), and, as a fifth type, from distress of the mind.
In conditions due to <s>vāta</s> and the others, the mouth is astringent, bitter, and sweet respectively;
when all arise together it is tasteless, and in grief, anger, and the like it is according to the impurity present.

children.text: chardir doṣaiḥ pṛthak sarvair dviṣṭairarthaiśca pañcamī
children.translated_text: Vomiting arises separately from the <s>doṣas</s>, from all of them together, and, as a fifth type, from hated objects.
In every form, the deranged <s>udāna</s> throws the <s>doṣas</s> upward.
In these, nausea, saltiness of the mouth, salivation, and loss of appetite come first.

children.text: nābhipṛṣṭhaṃ rujan vāyuḥ pārśve cāhāram utkṣipet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, causing pain in the navel, back, and sides, throws the food upward.

children.text: tato vicchinnam alpālpaṃ kaṣāyaṃ phenilaṃ vamet
children.translated_text: Then one vomits intermittently, little by little, an astringent and foamy matter,
accompanied by sound and belching, blackish and thin, with difficulty and with force.
It is accompanied by cough, dryness of the mouth, pain in the heart, head, and voice, and fatigue.
From <s>pitta</s>, the vomit resembles alkaline water, smoky, greenish, or yellowish;
it is mixed with blood, sour, pungent, and hot, and accompanied by thirst, fainting, heat, and burning.
From <s>kapha</s>, it is unctuous, thick, cold, and streaked like lattices with threads of phlegm;
it is sweet, salty, abundant, persistent, and produces horripilation.
It is accompanied by swelling of the face, sweetness in the mouth, drowsiness, nausea, and cough.

children.text: sarvaliṅgā malaiḥ sarvai riṣṭoktā yā ca tāṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: When all the impurities are involved there are all the signs; and the type described among fatal signs should be abandoned.
Through seeing, hearing, and other contact with what is putrid, impure, unclean, or hated,

children.text: tapte citte hṛdi kliṣṭe chardir dviṣṭārthayogajā
children.translated_text: when the mind is heated and the heart afflicted, vomiting arises from association with hated objects.
In cases of worms, thirst, <s>āma</s>, and <s>daurhṛda</s> (pregnancy craving), one should examine <s>vāta</s> and the other doṣas themselves.
One should especially declare vomiting worm-born when there are colic, trembling, and nausea,
and also the signs of worm-related heart disease. Five heart diseases are remembered.
Their occurrence arises from the etiological factors stated in the diagnosis of <s>gulma</s>.
By <s>vāta</s>, the heart is tormented with extreme pain, pierced, and seems to burst;

children.text: bhidyate śuṣyati stabdhaṃ hṛdayaṃ śūnyatā dravaḥ
children.translated_text: it feels split, dried, rigid, empty, and unsteady.
There are sudden dejection, sorrow, fear, and intolerance of sound,
trembling, constriction, stupor, obstruction of breath, and little sleep.

children.text: pittāt tṛṣṇā bhramo mūrchā dāhaḥ svedo 'mlakaḥ klamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>pitta</s> there are thirst, dizziness, fainting, burning, sweating, sourness, and fatigue,
vomiting, the smoky sensation of sour <s>pitta</s>, yellowness, and fever.
By <s>śleṣman</s>, the heart is rigid, heavy, and as if containing a stone;
there are cough, depression of digestive fire, spitting, sleepiness, lassitude, loss of appetite, and fever.
With the three <s>doṣas</s> there are all the signs; with worms there is dark discoloration of the eyes,
a sense of entering darkness, nausea, emaciation, itching, and discharge of <s>kapha</s>.
In this condition the heart is constantly as if being split by a saw.

children.text: cikitsed āmayaṃ ghoraṃ taṃ śīghraṃ śīghrakāriṇam
children.translated_text: One should treat that dreadful disease quickly, for it acts swiftly.

children.text: vātāt pittāt kaphāt tṛṣṇā saṃnipātād rasakṣayāt ||
children.translated_text: Thirst arises from <s>vāta</s>, from <s>pitta</s>, from <s>kapha</s>, from <s>saṃnipāta</s>, from depletion of <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhī syād upasargācca vātapitte tu kāraṇam
children.translated_text: and, as a sixth type, from a complication; but in thirst due to <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> lies the causal basis.
For in all forms, their aggravation dries up the watery tissues.
It causes whole-body dizziness, trembling, heat, thirst, burning, and delusion.
The vessels carrying water at the root of the tongue, throat, <s>kloma</s>, and palate
are dried up, and thirst arises; the following are their general signs.
Dryness of the mouth, lack of satisfaction from water, hatred of food, loss of voice,
roughness of the throat, lips, and tongue, protrusion of the tongue, and fatigue occur,
together with delirious speech, disturbance of consciousness, and the diseases described under seizure by thirst.
From <s>māruta</s> there are emaciation, dejection, stabbing pain in the temples, and dizziness of the head,
loss of smell, bad taste in the mouth, and loss of hearing, sleep, and strength.
It increases after drinking cold water; from <s>pitta</s> there are fainting and bitterness of the mouth,
redness of the eyes, constant drying, burning, and excessive smoky sensation.
Aggravated <s>kapha</s> obstructs <s>māruta</s> in the water-carrying channels;

children.text: srotaḥsu sa kaphas tena paṅkavacchoṣyate tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then that <s>kapha</s>, in those channels, is dried up like mud.
The throat feels as if filled with awns; there is sleepiness and sweetness of the mouth,
distension, heaviness of the head, torpor, nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite.
When all are involved, there are all the signs; there is also thirst born of <s>āma</s>,
and that which arises from obstruction of food is caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
When a person exhausted by heat suddenly resorts to cold water,

children.text: ūṣmā ruddho gataḥ koṣṭhaṃ yāṃ kuryāt pittajaiva sā ||
children.translated_text: the heat, being obstructed and having gone into the alimentary tract, produces thirst; that is precisely <s>pitta</s>-born.

children.text: yā ca pānātipānotthā tīkṣṇāgneḥ snehajā ca yā
children.translated_text: The thirst that arises from excessive drinking, that in one with sharp digestive fire, and that produced by unctuousness,
as well as that caused by unctuous, heavy, sour, and salty food, is born of <s>kapha</s>.
Thirst of the wasting type has the symptoms stated for depletion of <s>rasa</s>.
The intense thirst that arises as a complication of another long-lasting disease,

children.text: yā tṛṣṇā jāyate tīvrā sopasargātmikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: such as wasting, urinary disease, fever, and the like, is remembered as the complication type.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>madātyaya</s> and related disorders.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Alcohol is sharp, hot, dry, subtle, sour, pervading, swift-acting, and light;
it is diffusive and clear. Because of this, <s>madya</s> (alcohol) is opposite to <s>ojas</s>.
The qualities beginning with sharpness are also stated for poison; they disturb the mind.
In poison, however, because they act in an intensified manner, they arise for the ending of life.

children.text: tīkṣṇādibhir guṇair madyaṃ mandādīn ojaso guṇān
children.translated_text: By its ten qualities beginning with sharpness, alcohol agitates the ten qualities of <s>ojas</s>, beginning with dullness,

children.text: daśabhir daśa saṃkṣobhya ceto nayati vikriyām ||
children.translated_text: and brings the mind into derangement.

children.text: ādye made dvitīye tu pramādāyatane sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: In the first stage of intoxication, and then in the second, one stands in the sphere of heedlessness;
struck down by wrong imaginings and deluded, one becomes convinced that it is happiness.
Having reached the junction of the middle and highest stages, dominated by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>,

children.text: niraṅkuśa iva vyālo na kiṃcin nācarej jaḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the dull man, like an unrestrained serpent, does everything whatsoever.
This is the ground of blame; this is the abode of bad conduct.
This one thing is the supreme guide to the many paths of misfortune.

children.text: niśceṣṭaḥ śavavacchete tṛtīye tu made sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: In the third stage of intoxication, he lies motionless like a corpse;

children.text: maraṇād api pāpātmā gataḥ pāpatarāṃ daśām ||
children.translated_text: the sinful man has entered a state worse than death.
When a man attached to liquor does not know <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, pleasure and pain, profit and loss, the beneficial and the harmful,

children.text: yad āsakto na jānāti kathaṃ tacchīlayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how could a wise man practice such a habit?

children.text: madye moho bhayaṃ śokaḥ krodho mṛtyuśca saṃśritāḥ
children.translated_text: In liquor dwell delusion, fear, grief, anger, and death,
together with madness, intoxication, fainting, epilepsy, and falling attacks.

children.text: yatraikaḥ smṛtivibhraṃśas tatra sarvam asādhu yat
children.translated_text: Where there is even a single loss of memory, everything there is unwholesome.

children.text: ayuktiyuktam annaṃ hi vyādhaye maraṇāya vā ||
children.translated_text: For food taken in an improper manner leads to disease or to death.
Liquor destroys even the three goals of life, intelligence, firmness, modesty, and the rest.
Strong people, who have eaten, who are great eaters, do not become excessively intoxicated;
nor do those who are unctuous, endowed with good mental strength and youth, accustomed to liquor, and born in such a line,
who have abundant fat and <s>kapha</s>, little <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and firm digestive fire.
Those of the opposite kind become excessively intoxicated, as do those who drink carelessly or in an angry state,
or with liquor that is sour and dry, during indigestion, in excessive quantity, and too much.

children.text: vātāt pittāt kaphāt sarvaiścatvāraḥ syur madātyayāḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>vāta</s>, from <s>pitta</s>, from <s>kapha</s>, and from all of them, there are four kinds of <s>madātyaya</s> (pathological intoxication).

children.text: sarve 'pi sarvair jāyante vyapadeśas tu bhūyasā ||
children.translated_text: All of them arise from all the <s>doṣas</s>, but the naming is according to predominance.
Their common symptoms are severe delusion and pain in the heart region,
looseness of stool, constant thirst, fever of both cooling and heating character, and anorexia;
pain in the head, sides, and bones, trembling, piercing pain in the vital spots, and stiffness of the sacral region;
constriction in the chest, darkness before the eyes, cough, dyspnea, and sleeplessness;
excessive sweating, obstruction, swelling, and mental disturbance;
delirious speech, vomiting, nausea, dizziness, and seeing bad dreams.
In particular, from <s>anila</s> (wind) there are sleeplessness, dyspnea, trembling, and pain in the head;
in dreams he wanders about, leaps up, and speaks with ghosts.
From <s>pitta</s> there are burning, fever, sweating, delusion, diarrhea, thirst, and dizziness;
the body is greenish-yellow, and the eyes and cheeks are red.
From <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha) there are vomiting, nausea, sleep, urticaria, and heaviness of the limbs.

children.text: sarvaje sarvaliṅgatvaṃ muktvā madyaṃ pibet tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the type born of all the <s>doṣas</s>, all the signs occur. For one who, after giving up liquor, drinks it again,
or suddenly takes something else unsuitable, there arise <s>dhvaṃsaka</s> and <s>vikṣaya</s>,
two difficult disorders caused by <s>māruta</s> (wind), especially in a weak person.
In <s>dhvaṃsaka</s> there is spitting of phlegm, dryness of the throat, and excessive sleep;
there is intolerance of sound and drowsiness. In <s>vikṣaya</s> there is severe pain in the limbs and head,

children.text: hṛtkaṇṭharogaḥ saṃmohaḥ kāsas tṛṣṇā vamir jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: disease of the heart and throat, confusion, cough, thirst, vomiting, and fever.

children.text: nivṛtto yas tu madyebhyo jitātmā buddhipūrvakṛt ||
children.translated_text: But one who has withdrawn from liquors, is self-controlled, and acts with deliberate understanding

children.text: vikāraiḥ spṛśyate jātu na sa śārīramānasaiḥ
children.translated_text: is never touched by disorders of body or mind.
For a man devoted to passion, delusion, and unwholesome food, there are three diseases,
arising from obstruction of the channels that carry <s>rasa</s>, blood, and consciousness:
<s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>mūrchā</s> (fainting), and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (collapse), each succeeding one stronger than the preceding.
Here <s>mada</s> is caused by all the <s>doṣas</s>, and also by blood, liquor, and poison.
When it is produced by <s>vāta</s>, the patient has halting, scanty, hurried speech, is restless, and has stumbling movements;
his body is dry, dark, and reddish.
When produced by <s>pitta</s>, he is angry, red-yellow in appearance, and fond of quarrels.
When produced by <s>kapha</s>, his speech is slight and incoherent, he is pale, contemplative, and sluggish.
When produced by the combined <s>doṣas</s>, it has all forms; when produced by blood, the limbs and gaze are rigid.
When produced by liquor there are signs of <s>pitta</s>, with distorted laughter, voice, and limbs;

children.text: viṣe kampo 'tinidrā ca sarvebhyo 'bhyadhikas tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: when produced by poison there is trembling and excessive sleep, and it is more severe than all the others.
One should recognize <s>vāta</s> and the others, when they affect blood and the rest, by the prominence of their symptoms.

children.text: aruṇaṃ kṛṣṇanīlaṃ vā khaṃ paśyan praviśet tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>mūrchā</s> caused by <s>māruta</s>, seeing the sky as red, black, or blue, he enters darkness;

children.text: śīghraṃ ca pratibudhyeta hṛtpīḍā vepathur bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: he quickly awakens, with pain in the heart, trembling, and dizziness,
with emaciation and a dark-reddish complexion.

children.text: pittena raktaṃ pītaṃ vā nabhaḥ paśyan viśet tamaḥ
children.translated_text: When it is caused by <s>pitta</s>, seeing the sky as red or yellow, he enters darkness;
he awakens sweating and afflicted by burning, thirst, and heat.
His stool is loose, his complexion blue-yellow, and his eyes confused with red and yellow.
When it is caused by <s>kapha</s>, seeing the sky as cloud-like, he enters darkness;
he awakens after a long time, with nausea and salivation,
with heavy, motionless limbs, as if covered with a wet hide.
When it has every form through the three <s>doṣas</s>, it is like another epilepsy;
it quickly throws the person down motionless, but without repulsive movements.
When the <s>doṣas</s> in intoxication and fainting have completed their force in embodied beings,
they subside by themselves; <s>saṃnyāsa</s> does not subside without medicines.
The excessively powerful impurities, combined together and lodged in the seats of life,
seize the activity of speech, body, and mind and produce <s>saṃnyāsa</s>.
Because of this, the person becomes like a log of wood, resembling one dead;

children.text: mriyeta śīghraṃ śīghraṃ ceccikitsā na prayujyate ||
children.translated_text: he dies quickly if treatment is not applied quickly.
As in a deep flood of water full of crocodiles one who is wandering is sinking,
so in <s>saṃnyāsa</s> one should quickly turn back a man who is sinking.
When a man is embraced by his own enemies, such as intoxication, pride, anger, and satisfaction,
and by liquor that treats proper and improper as the same and is devoid of reasoning,
but if, after distinguishing strength, time, place, suitability, constitution, companions, disease, and age,

children.text: pravibhajya tadanurūpaṃ yadi pibati tataḥ pibatyamṛtam ||
children.translated_text: he drinks in a manner corresponding to those factors, then he drinks nectar.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids).
Thus spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
Because, like enemies, they pierce living beings as fleshy pegs,
and because they obstruct the anal passage, they are called <s>arśāṃsi</s>.
The <s>doṣas</s>, vitiating skin, flesh, and fat, produce growths of flesh of various forms
at the region of <s>apāna</s> and elsewhere; these are called <s>arśas</s>.
In brief, it is twofold, by the distinction between being congenital and arising later.
There is also the distinction between dry and oozing forms; the <s>guda</s> (anus) is connected with the large intestine.
It measures four and a half finger-breadths; in it there are three folds, each one and a half finger-breadths.

children.text: valyaḥ pravāhiṇī tāsām antar madhye visarjanī ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the inner fold is <s>pravāhiṇī</s>, the middle one is <s>visarjanī</s>,
and the outer one is <s>saṃvaraṇī</s>; outside it, at one finger-breadth, is the lip of the anus.
In measure it is one and a half barley-corns; beyond that are the hairs.
There, the cause of congenital hemorrhoids is injury to the seed of the folds.
The injury to the seed of hemorrhoids comes from misconduct by the mother and father,

children.text: daivācca tābhyāṃ kopo hi saṃnipātasya tānyataḥ
children.translated_text: and also from fate; because through those two there is aggravation of all three <s>doṣas</s>,
therefore they have been declared incurable, as are all diseases born in the family line.
Congenital ones in particular are dry and hard to look at,
