turned inward, pale, and accompanied by terrible complications.
The other kinds are sixfold, according to separate <s>doṣas</s>, combinations, accumulation, and blood.
They are dry from <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, but moist from blood and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: doṣaprakopahetus tu prāg uktas tena sādite
children.translated_text: The causes of aggravation of the <s>doṣas</s> have been stated before; when digestive fire is overcome by them,
and when waste has again accumulated excessively, also because of excessive sexual intercourse,
because of jolting in vehicles, uneven, hard, or cramped seats,
because of rubbing by an enema nozzle, stone, clod, the ground, cloth, and the like,
because of intense contact with cold water, and because of continual excessive straining,
because of holding back the urges for flatus, urine, and feces, or forcing them on,
because of fever, abdominal tumor, diarrhea, <s>āma</s>, <s>grahaṇī</s>, swelling, and anemia,
because of emaciation and irregular exertions, and again, in women,
because of miscarriage of an unripe fetus and pressure from the growth of the fetus,
by such and other causes the <s>apāna</s> wind, being aggravated, takes the feces
and deposits it in the folds of the anus when their substance has become congested;
then hemorrhoids arise. Their prodromal sign is weakness of digestive fire,
constipation, weakness in the thighs, cramping of the calves, dizziness,
weariness in the limbs, swelling of the eyes, and either looseness or retention of feces.
The wind, abundant and obstructed, usually moving below the navel,
comes out with difficulty, with pain, cutting pain, and sound.
There is rumbling in the intestines, distension, emaciation, and many belches,

children.text: prabhūtaṃ mūtram alpā viḍ aśraddhā dhūmako 'mlakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: much urine, little feces, lack of desire for food, a smoky sensation, and sour belching.
There is pain in the head, back, and chest, lassitude, and alteration of complexion,
drowsiness, weakness of the senses, anger, and difficulty in treatment,
and suspicion of disorders such as <s>grahaṇī</s>, anemia, abdominal tumor, and abdominal enlargement.
These same symptoms increase when the ill-named hemorrhoids have arisen.
For <s>apāna</s>, turning back because its downward path is blocked by them,
disturbs the other winds that move through all the senses and the body,
as well as urine, feces, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, the tissues, and their receptacles.
It crushes the digestive fire; consequently, almost every person with hemorrhoids
becomes extremely thin, devoid of energy, wretched, wasted, and very lusterless,
without vigor and bereft of complexion, like a tree infested by living creatures.
He is afflicted by all the complications that have been described, which torment the vital points,
and also by cough, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, dyspnea, and coryza,
by fatigue, breaking pain in the limbs, vomiting, sneezing, swelling, and fever,
and he is troubled by impotence, deafness, darkness of vision, gravel, and urinary stones.
His voice is weak and broken; he broods, repeatedly spits, and has anorexia.
He has pain in all the joints, bones, heart, navel, anus, and groins.
Through the anus there flows mucus resembling the water from washed rice,
and he passes feces intermittently, sometimes bound and sometimes loose, dry or moist, cooked or uncooked,

children.text: pāṇḍu pītaṃ harid raktaṃ picchilaṃ copaveśyate
children.translated_text: pale, yellow, green, red, and slimy.
The anal sprouts that contain much wind are dry and accompanied by tingling.

children.text: mlānāḥ śyāvāruṇāḥ stabdhā viṣamāḥ paruṣāḥ kharāḥ
children.translated_text: They are withered, dusky-red, rigid, uneven, rough, and harsh,
mutually dissimilar, crooked, sharp, and with split openings.
They resemble the fruits of bimbī, karkandhu, date, and cotton,
some have the appearance of kadamba flowers, and some are like mustard seeds.
They produce especially severe pain in the head, sides, shoulders, hips, thighs, and groins,
and they cause sneezing, belching, constipation, catching pain in the heart, and anorexia.
They bring on cough, dyspnea, irregularity of digestive fire, ringing in the ears, and dizziness.
Afflicted by them, the patient passes knotted feces, scanty, noisy, and with straining,
bound up and accompanied by pain, froth, and mucus.
His skin, nails, feces, urine, eyes, and face become blackish.
From the same cause arise abdominal tumors, splenic disease, abdominal enlargement, and <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>.
Those dominated by <s>pitta</s> have blue mouths and a red, yellow, or black appearance.
They ooze thin blood, smell foul, and are thin, soft, and flaccid.
They resemble a parrot's tongue, a piece of liver, or the mouth of a leech.
They cause burning, suppuration, fever, sweating, thirst, fainting, loss of taste, and confusion.
They are hot, and the stool is liquid, blue, hot, yellow, red, and mixed with <s>āma</s>.
The waist becomes slender, and the skin, nails, and so on become green, yellow, and turmeric-colored.
Those in which <s>śleṣman</s> is predominant have large roots, are dense, slightly painful, and white.
They are swollen, enlarged, unctuous, rigid, round, heavy, and firm.
They are slimy, dull, smooth, rich in itching, and pleasant to the touch.
They resemble karīra fruits, jackfruit stones, or the teats of a cow.
They bring heaviness to the groins and cutting pain in the anus, bladder, and navel.
They are accompanied by cough, dyspnea, nausea, salivation, anorexia, and coryza,
and they produce difficult urination, heaviness of the head, and cold fever.
They cause impotence, softness of digestive fire, vomiting, and disorders mostly involving <s>āma</s>.
The feces are rich in fat-like matter and <s>kapha</s>, and are passed with straining.
The pale, unctuous ones and the like do not flow and do not split open.
Those with mixed signs are from a combination of <s>doṣas</s>; from accumulation they have all the characteristics.
Hemorrhoidal growths in the rectum, dominated by blood, are accompanied by the form of <s>pitta</s>.
They resemble shoots of a banyan tree and are like guñjā berries or coral.
When they are excessively vitiated and hot, and are pressed hard by solid feces,
they suddenly discharge blood; and because of its excessive flow,
he becomes frog-like and is afflicted by sufferings arising from loss of blood.
His color, strength, and energy are diminished, his vitality is damaged, and his senses are clouded.
By mung beans, kodo millet, jūrṇa grain, karīra, chickpeas, and the like,

children.text: rūkṣaiḥ saṃgrāhibhir vāyuḥ sve sthāne kupito balī ||
children.translated_text: which are dry and constipating, <s>vāyu</s> (wind), aggravated in its own place and powerful,
blocks the downward-carrying channels and, drying downward,
makes the feces produce a terrible obstruction of flatus, feces, and urine.
Through that, severe pain occurs, spreading through the abdomen, back, heart, and sides,
with distension, twisting of the belly, nausea, and cutting pain.
There is especially pain in the bladder, and swelling like a lump arises;
the wind moves upward, and then vomiting, anorexia, and fever occur.
Heart disease, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, obstruction of urine, and dysentery,
deafness, darkness of vision, dyspnea, headache, cough, and coryza,
mental disturbance, thirst, blood-pitta, abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, and so on,

children.text: te te ca vātajā rogā jāyante bhṛśadāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those various diseases born of <s>vāta</s>, exceedingly severe, arise.
This <s>udāvarta</s> is the supreme complication of the diseases called durnāman, that is, hemorrhoids.
It arises in those whose bowels are overcome by <s>vāta</s>, even without those hemorrhoids.
Those that are congenital, produced by all three <s>doṣas</s>, and those situated in the inner fold,
are incurable; they are only manageable, depending on digestive fire, strength, and the like.
Those born of two <s>doṣas</s>, and those lodged in the second fold,
are said to be difficult to cure, as are those that have lasted a year.
But hemorrhoids that arise in the outer fold, that are dominated by a single <s>doṣa</s>,
and that have not arisen long ago, are easy to cure.
Those in the penis and other places will also be described according to their respective nature; those arising from the navel, however,
have the form of an earthworm's mouth, and are slimy and soft.

children.text: vyāno gṛhītvā śleṣmāṇaṃ karotyarśas tvaco bahiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāna</s>, taking hold of <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), produces an arśas outside the skin.

children.text: kīlopamaṃ sthirakharaṃ carmakīlaṃ tu taṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is like a peg, firm and rough; they know that as a skin tag.
Because of <s>vāta</s> there is pricking pain and roughness; from <s>pitta</s>, blackish redness;
because of <s>śleṣman</s>, it has unctuousness, nodularity, and the same color as the skin.

children.text: arśasāṃ praśame yatnam āśu kurvīta buddhimān
children.translated_text: A wise man should quickly make effort to pacify hemorrhoids,

children.text: tānyāśu hi gudaṃ baddhvā kuryur baddhagudodaram ||
children.translated_text: for they quickly obstruct the rectum and cause baddhagudodara, abdominal disease from rectal obstruction.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of diarrhea and <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder.
Thus, indeed, spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Through the <s>doṣas</s>, separately and together, and from fear and from grief, it is sixfold.
That diarrhea arises especially from drinking too much water.
It arises from emaciating and drying meat, from unsuitable food, from sesame paste and sprouted grains,
from liquor, dry food, excessive food, hemorrhoids, and derangement caused by oleation.
From worms and from suppression of natural urges, <s>anila</s> (wind), aggravated by such factors,
dislodges the water element downward and by that very action destroys the digestive fire.
Having disturbed the bowel and the feces, and bringing the stool to fluidity,
it prepares the way for diarrhea. The sign of that which is about to occur is:
pricking pain in the heart, rectum, and bowel, weakness of the limbs, retention of stool,
distension, and indigestion. In that condition, through <s>vāta</s>, watery feces
are passed in small quantities, with sound and pain, and are obstructed.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ saphenam acchaṃ ca grathitaṃ vā muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are dry, foamy, clear, or clotted, again and again.
Likewise they have the appearance of burnt molasses, with mucus and cutting pain.
The mouth is dry, the anus prolapsed, the hairs bristle, and the patient groans.
Through <s>pitta</s>, the stool is yellow, black, turmeric-colored, or like green grass,
mixed with blood, very foul-smelling, and the patient has thirst, fainting, sweating, and burning.
There is pain, burning of the anus, and a desire for ripening. Through <s>śleṣman</s> it is thick,
slimy, stringy, white, unctuous, unripe, and accompanied by <s>kapha</s>.
It is frequent, heavy, foul-smelling, obstructed, and accompanied by continuous pain.
He is sleepy, languid, averse to food, and passes small quantities with straining.
There is horripilation and nausea, and the bladder, rectum, and abdomen feel heavy.
Even after evacuation he has the sense that it has not been done; the type caused by all <s>doṣas</s> has all the signs.
When the mind is agitated by fear, wind accompanied by <s>pitta</s> liquefies the feces.

children.text: vāyus tato 'tisāryeta kṣipram uṣṇaṃ dravaṃ plavam ||
children.translated_text: Then he has diarrhea quickly, with stool that is hot, liquid, and floating.
They say it has signs equal to <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; the same applies to diarrhea from grief.
In brief, diarrhea is twofold: with <s>āma</s> and without <s>āma</s>.

children.text: sāsṛṅ nirasras tatrādye gauravād apsu majjati
children.translated_text: It may be bloody or bloodless. In the first, because of heaviness,
the foul-smelling stool sinks in water; there are gurgling, obstruction, pain, and salivation.

children.text: viparīto nirāmas tu kaphāt pakvo 'pi majjati
children.translated_text: The type without <s>āma</s> is the opposite; when due to <s>kapha</s>, even digested stool sinks.
For one who is not very diligent with regard to diarrheas, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease
will arise from things used by another person that destroy the digestive fire.

children.text: sāmaṃ śakṛn nirāmaṃ vā jīrṇe yenātisāryate ||
children.translated_text: When, after food is digested, one has diarrhea with stool containing <s>āma</s> or without <s>āma</s>,
that is diarrhea, from excessive flowing, naturally rapid in action.

children.text: sāmaṃ sānnam ajīrṇe 'nne jīrṇe pakvaṃ tu naiva vā ||
children.translated_text: When food is undigested it is with <s>āma</s> and with food; when digested, it is cooked, or not so.

children.text: akasmād vā muhur baddham akasmācchithilaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: When, without apparent cause, it is repeatedly bound, and without apparent cause repeatedly loose,
that is chronic <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder; because of accumulation, it makes one evacuate.

children.text: sa caturdhā pṛthag doṣaiḥ saṃnipātācca jāyate
children.translated_text: It arises in four ways from the separate <s>doṣas</s> and also from their combined aggravation.

children.text: prāgrūpaṃ tasya sadanaṃ cirāt pacanam amlakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its prodromal sign is lassitude, digestion only after a long time, sour belching,

children.text: praseko vaktravairasyam arucis tṛṭ klamo bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: salivation, distaste in the mouth, loss of appetite, thirst, exhaustion, and dizziness.
Distension and tightness of the abdomen, vomiting, ringing in the ears, and gurgling in the intestines occur.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kārśyaṃ dhūmakas tamako jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The general symptoms are emaciation, a smoky sensation, <s>tamaka</s> (oppressive dyspnea), and fever,
fainting, headache, constipation, and swelling of the hands and feet.
There, from <s>anila</s> (wind), there is dryness of the palate, dimness of sight, and ringing in the ears,
with repeated attacks of cholera-like pain and pain in the sides, thighs, groins, and neck.

children.text: raseṣu gṛddhiḥ sarveṣu kṣut tṛṣṇā parikartikā
children.translated_text: There is craving for all tastes, hunger, thirst, and cutting pain,

children.text: jīrṇe jīryati cādhmānaṃ bhukte svāsthyaṃ samaśnute ||
children.translated_text: and distension when the food is digested or is being digested; after eating he attains relief.
He is suspected of <s>vāta</s>-heart disease, <s>gulma</s>, hemorrhoids, splenic disease, and pallor.

children.text: cirād duḥkhaṃ dravaṃ śuṣkaṃ tanvāmaṃ śabdaphenavat ||
children.translated_text: After a long time, with difficulty, he passes stool that is fluid or dry, thin, unripe, noisy, and foamy,
again and again, along with anal pain, dyspnea, and cough.
When caused by <s>pitta</s>, he passes liquid stool with a blue-yellow appearance, or, yellow in appearance, he passes liquid stool,
afflicted by fetid sour belching, burning in the heart and throat, loss of appetite, and thirst.
When caused by <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha), food is digested with difficulty, and there is vomiting and loss of appetite,
coating of the mouth, spitting, cough, nausea, and coryza.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ manyate styānam udaraṃ stimitaṃ guru ||
children.translated_text: He thinks his heart is stiff; the abdomen is inert and heavy.
The belching is corrupt and sweet; there is lassitude and lack of desire for women.
There is passage of heavy stool, broken up and mixed with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and phlegm.
In the type caused by all the <s>doṣas</s>, there is weakness even in one who is not emaciated, and all the signs are mixed together.
The three digestive fires beginning with the irregular one, which have been described in the division of the body,

children.text: te 'pi syur grahaṇīdoṣāḥ samas tu svāsthyakāraṇam
children.translated_text: are also <s>grahaṇīdoṣas</s>; the balanced one, however, is the cause of health.
<s>Vātavyādhi</s>, urinary stone, skin disease, <s>meha</s>, abdominal disease, fistula,
hemorrhoids, and <s>grahaṇī</s>: these eight are great diseases, very hard to cross.
Now therefore we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>mūtrāghāta</s> (urinary obstruction).
So spoke the great seers such as <s>Ātreya</s>.
The bladder, the neck of the bladder, the penis, the waist, the testicles, and the anus
are said to have one connection, resting in the cavity of the pelvic passage.
For although the bladder opens downward, it is filled from the sides
through the mouths of fine urinary vessels, which constantly exude into it.

children.text: yais taireva praviśyainaṃ doṣāḥ kurvanti viṃśatim
children.translated_text: Entering it by those very channels, the <s>doṣas</s> produce twenty
<s>mūtrāghātas</s>, <s>pramehas</s>, and difficult urinations, all based on vital spots.
In dysuria caused by <s>vāta</s>, the patient, with pain in the bladder, groin, and penis, urinates a little at a time, again and again.

children.text: mūtrayed vātaje kṛcchre paitte pītaṃ sadāharuk ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>pitta</s> type, the urine is yellow and always accompanied by burning pain,
or bloody; in the <s>kapha</s> type, there is heaviness and swelling of the bladder and penis.

children.text: sapicchaṃ savibandhaṃ ca sarvaiḥ sarvātmakaṃ malaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The urine is slimy and obstructed; when caused by all the impurities, the disorder has the nature of all of them.
When <s>vāyu</s> covers the mouth of the bladder and dries up

children.text: mūtraṃ sapittaṃ sakaphaṃ saśukraṃ vā tadā kramāt ||
children.translated_text: urine mixed respectively with <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, or semen,
then a terrible stone arises; from <s>pitta</s> it is like the yellow pigment of a cow,

children.text: śleṣmāśrayā ca sarvā syād athāsyāḥ pūrvalakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and every stone is based in <s>śleṣman</s>. Now its preliminary symptoms are these:
distension of the bladder and excessive pain all around the regions near it,
a goat-like smell in the urine, painful urination, fever, and loss of appetite.
The general sign is pain in the navel, perineal raphe, and top of the bladder.
When the stone obstructs the passage, the urine has a broken stream.
When it moves away, he urinates comfortably, the urine being clear and resembling <s>gomedaka</s> gem.
When it is disturbed and causes a wound, the urine is bloody; from exertion there is very severe pain.

children.text: tatra vātād bhṛśārtyārto dantān khādati vepate
children.translated_text: In that condition, from <s>vāta</s>, he is tormented by intense pain, gnashes his teeth, trembles,
rubs the penis, presses the navel, and groans constantly.

children.text: sānilaṃ muñcati śakṛn muhur mehati binduśaḥ
children.translated_text: He passes feces together with flatus and urinates repeatedly, drop by drop.
His stone is dark and rough, as if covered with thorns.
With <s>pitta</s>, the bladder burns, as though being cooked, and is hot.
The stone has the shape of a <s>bhallātaka</s> seed and is red, yellow, or black.

children.text: vastir nistudyata iva śleṣmaṇā śītalo guruḥ
children.translated_text: With <s>śleṣman</s>, the bladder feels as if it is being pierced; it is cold and heavy.
The stone is large, smooth, and honey-colored or white.

children.text: etā bhavanti bālānāṃ teṣām eva ca bhūyasā
children.translated_text: These occur in children, and mostly in them alone.
Because their seat and accumulation are small, they are easy to grasp and remove.
But a semen-stone arises in adults from retention of semen.
When semen has slipped from its place but has not been discharged, <s>anila</s>, in the space between the testicles,
seizes it and dries it up; that dried semen becomes a stone,
causing bladder pain, difficult urination, and swelling of the testicle.
When it has only just arisen, the semen comes forth and dissolves.
But when this space is compressed, gravel forms as from a stone.

children.text: aṇuśo vāyunā bhinnā sā tvasminn anulomage
children.translated_text: Broken into minute pieces by <s>vāyu</s>, it goes out with the urine
when the wind moves in the regular direction; when it moves contrary, it becomes obstructed.

children.text: mūtrasaṃdhāriṇaḥ kuryād ruddhvā vaster mukhaṃ marut
children.translated_text: In a person who holds back urine, <s>marut</s> (wind), blocking the mouth of the bladder,
causes urinary retention, pain, itching, and sometimes, from its own place,
drives the bladder upward, making it distended like a fetus and grossly swollen.
There it produces pain, burning, throbbing, and twisting.

children.text: binduśaśca pravarteta mūtraṃ vastau tu pīḍite
children.translated_text: When the bladder is pressed, urine proceeds drop by drop,
or in a stream; this twofold condition is remembered as <s>vātavasti</s>.
It is hard to overcome; the second form is still harder, because <s>anila</s> is strong.
<s>Vāyu</s>, lodged in the interval between the fecal passage and the bladder,
forms a dense, glandular knot like an <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, immovable and raised.
This is <s>vātāṣṭhīlā</s>, causing distension and obstruction of feces, urine, and flatus.
Disordered <s>anila</s>, coiled in the bladder and intensely painful,
whirls the urine about, with rigidity, twisting, and heaviness.

children.text: mūtram alpālpam athavā vimuñcati śakṛt sṛjan
children.translated_text: Then it releases urine little by little, or while passing feces.
This is <s>vātakuṇḍalikā</s>; but urine that has been held for a long time...

children.text: na nireti vibaddhaṃ vā mūtrātītaṃ tad alparuk
children.translated_text: When the urine does not come out, or is obstructed, that condition is <s>mūtrātīta</s>; it has little pain.
When, through suppression, it is checked and turned upward by <s>vāta</s>,
then the urine fills the abdomen below the navel,
and causes severe pain, distension, indigestion, and retention of stool.
That is <s>mūtrajaṭhara</s>, caused by defect of the aperture or by <s>anila</s> (wind).

children.text: ākṣiptam alpaṃ mūtraṃ tad vastau nāle 'thavā maṇau ||
children.translated_text: A small quantity of urine, drawn back, stays in the bladder, the channel, or the glans,

children.text: sthitvā sravecchanaiḥ paścāt sarujaṃ vātha nīrujam
children.translated_text: and, after remaining there, flows out slowly afterward, either with pain or without pain.
That is <s>mūtrotsaṅga</s>, with broken flow, residual urine, and heaviness of the penis.

children.text: antar vastimukhe vṛttaḥ sthiro 'lpaḥ sahasā bhavet
children.translated_text: Inside, at the mouth of the bladder, a round, fixed, small mass suddenly forms;
that knot, with pain like a urinary stone, is called <s>mūtragranthi</s>.

children.text: mūtritasya striyaṃ yāto vāyunā śukram uddhatam
children.translated_text: In a man who has urinated and gone to a woman, semen, driven up by <s>vāyu</s>,

children.text: sthānāccyutaṃ mūtrayataḥ prāk paścād vā pravartate ||
children.translated_text: is displaced from its place and proceeds before or after he urinates.
Resembling water mixed with ash, that is called <s>mūtraśukra</s>.
When, in persons who are dry and weak, feces is turned upward by <s>vāta</s>,
then it follows the urinary channel, and the urine is mixed with feces.

children.text: mūtraṃ viṭtulyagandhaṃ syād viḍvighātaṃ tam ādiśet ||
children.translated_text: The urine has an odor like feces; that should be identified as <s>viḍvighāta</s>.
When <s>pitta</s>, increased by exercise, sharp and hot foods, travel, exposure to sun, and the like,
is driven by <s>vāyu</s>, with pain and burning in the bladder and genital region,

children.text: mūtraṃ pravartayet pītaṃ saraktaṃ raktam eva vā
children.translated_text: it makes the urine pass yellow, blood-tinged, or entirely bloody,

children.text: uṣṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṛcchrād uṣṇavātaṃ vadanti tam ||
children.translated_text: hot, again and again, and with difficulty; they call that <s>uṣṇavāta</s>.
In one whose body is dry and exhausted, <s>pitta</s> and <s>māruta</s>, lodged in the bladder,
produce painful and burning diminution of urine; it is named accordingly, <s>mūtrakṣaya</s>.

children.text: pittaṃ kapho dvāvapi vā saṃhanyete 'nilena cet
children.translated_text: If <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, or both are condensed by <s>anila</s>,

children.text: kṛcchrān mūtraṃ tadā pītaṃ raktaṃ śvetaṃ ghanaṃ sṛjet ||
children.translated_text: then one passes urine with difficulty, yellow, red, white, and thick.
It has burning and may be the color of powdered <s>rocanā</s> and conch,

children.text: śuṣkaṃ samastavarṇaṃ vā mūtrasādaṃ vadanti tam ||
children.translated_text: or it may be dry and of all colors; they call that <s>mūtrasāda</s>.
Thus the diseases born from non-discharge of urine have been described in detail.
Next, by their causes and signs, those born from excessive discharge will be described.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>prameha</s>.
Thus spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.

children.text: pramehā viṃśatis tatra śleṣmato daśa pittataḥ
children.translated_text: There are twenty <s>pramehas</s>: among them ten arise from <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha), six from <s>pitta</s>,
and four from <s>anila</s>; for them, whatever carries or increases fat, urine, and <s>kapha</s>,
arising from food, drink, and activity, is generally the provoking cause.
Sweet, sour, salty, unctuous, heavy, slimy, and cold substances,
new grain, liquor, meat from marshy animals, sugarcane, jaggery, and milk-products,
delight in staying and sitting in one place, and sleep taken without proper rule,

children.text: vastim āśritya kurute pramehān dūṣitaḥ kaphaḥ
children.translated_text: make vitiated <s>kapha</s>, resorting to the bladder, produce <s>pramehas</s>,
after it has vitiated bodily moisture, sweat, fat, <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid), and flesh.

children.text: pittaṃ raktam api kṣīṇe kaphādau mūtrasaṃśrayam
children.translated_text: When <s>kapha</s> and the others have diminished, <s>pitta</s> too brings blood into the urine as its seat,

children.text: dhātūn vastim upānīya tatkṣaye 'pi ca mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when those tissues are depleted, <s>māruta</s> also carries the bodily constituents to the bladder.
Therefore the <s>mehas</s> born from these are curable, manageable, or to be abandoned,
because their treatment is unequal, and also because their danger is very great.
Their general sign is the passing of abundant, turbid urine.
Although the <s>doṣas</s> and affected tissues are not individually distinct in every case, through the specific nature of their combinations,
difference among the <s>mehas</s> is determined by differences in the urine's color and other qualities.

children.text: acchaṃ bahu sitaṃ śītaṃ nirgandham udakopamam ||
children.translated_text: With <s>udakameha</s>, one urinates a clear, abundant, white, cold, odorless fluid like water,
and it is somewhat turbid and slimy.
With <s>ikṣumeha</s>, the urine is extremely sweet, like sugarcane juice.
With <s>sāndrameha</s>, what is urinated becomes thick when it has stood overnight.
The <s>surāmehī</s> passes urine like liquor, clear above and dense below.
With <s>piṣṭameha</s>, with hairs bristling, the urine is thick and white like flour-water.
The <s>śukramehī</s> passes urine resembling semen, or mixed with semen.
The <s>sikatāmehī</s> passes formed minute impurities shaped like sand grains.
The <s>śītamehī</s> passes very abundant, sweet, extremely cold urine.

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiḥ śanairmehī mandaṃ mandaṃ pramehati
children.translated_text: The <s>śanairmehī</s> urinates slowly, slowly, in a very feeble stream.
With <s>lālāmeha</s>, the urine is slimy and furnished with threads like saliva.
With <s>kṣārameha</s>, in smell, color, taste, and touch it is like alkaline water.
With <s>nīlameha</s>, the urine is bluish; the <s>kālamehī</s> passes urine like ink.
The <s>hāridramehī</s> passes pungent urine resembling turmeric and causing burning.
With <s>māñjiṣṭhameha</s>, it is foul-smelling and like water mixed with madder.
With <s>raktameha</s>, the urine is foul-smelling, hot, salty, and blood-like.

children.text: vasāmehī vasāmiśraṃ vasāṃ vā mūtrayen muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vasāmehī</s> repeatedly urinates fluid mixed with fat, or fat itself.

children.text: majjānaṃ majjamiśraṃ vā majjamehī muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>majjamehī</s> repeatedly urinates marrow, or fluid mixed with marrow.
Like an intoxicated elephant, constantly and without urge,
the <s>hastimehī</s> passes urine containing <s>lasīkā</s> (lymph-like fluid) and with obstruction.

children.text: madhumehī madhusamaṃ jāyate sa kila dvidhā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>madhumehī</s> produces urine like honey; it is indeed of two kinds.
It occurs when <s>vāyu</s> is enraged by tissue-depletion, or when its path is obstructed by <s>doṣas</s>.
When obstructed, it displays signs of the obstructing <s>doṣas</s> without apparent cause.

children.text: kṣīṇaḥ kṣaṇāt kṣaṇāt pūrṇo bhajate kṛcchrasādhyatām
children.translated_text: When depletion is present, as the bladder fills again from moment to moment, it becomes difficult to cure.
In time, all <s>pramehas</s>, if neglected, pass into <s>madhumeha</s>.

children.text: madhuraṃ yacca sarveṣu prāyo madhviva mehati
children.translated_text: And because in all of them one generally urinates something sweet, like honey,
all are also called <s>madhumeha</s>, and because of sweetness pervading the body.
Indigestion, anorexia, vomiting, sleepiness, cough, and coryza
arise as complications of the <s>mehas</s> born from <s>kapha</s>.
Stabbing pain in the bladder and urinary organ, tearing pain in the scrotum, and fever,
burning, thirst, sourness, fainting, and loose stool are complications of those born from <s>pitta</s>.
For those caused by <s>vāta</s>, there are upward movement, tremor, constriction of the heart, and restlessness.

children.text: śūlam unnidratā śoṣaḥ kāsaḥ śvāsaśca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: Pain, sleeplessness, wasting, cough, and dyspnea arise.
The lesions are <s>śarāvikā</s>, <s>kacchapikā</s>, <s>jālinī</s>, <s>vinatā</s>, and <s>alajī</s>,
<s>masūrikā</s>, <s>sarṣapikā</s>, <s>putriṇī</s>, <s>vidārikā</s>,
and <s>vidradhi</s> (abscess): these are the ten <s>piṭikās</s> (eruptive lesions) caused by neglect of <s>prameha</s>.
They arise in joints, vital spots, and fleshy regions.
Raised at the edges, depressed in the middle, dark, moist, and painful,
and having the size and shape of a saucer: such a <s>piṭikā</s> is <s>śarāvikā</s>.
Deep-seated, with pain and piercing sensations, and occupying a large area,
smooth and resembling the back of a turtle: that <s>piṭikā</s> is regarded as <s>kacchapī</s>.
Stiff, with a net of veins, with oily discharge, and having an extensive seat,
full of pain and pricking, and with minute openings: this is <s>jālinī</s>.
With deep pain and moisture, on the back or even on the abdomen,

children.text: mahatī piṭikā nīlā vinatā vinatā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: a large blue <s>piṭikā</s>, bent downward, is known as <s>vinatā</s>.

children.text: dahati tvacam utthāne bhṛśaṃ kaṣṭā visarpiṇī
children.translated_text: When it rises it burns the skin; it is extremely painful and spreads like erysipelas.
With red-black color, excessive thirst, eruptions, burning, delusion, and fever, it is <s>alajī</s>.
<s>Masūrikā</s> is equal in size and shape to a lentil.
Having the size and shape of a mustard seed, ripening quickly, and very painful,
it is <s>sarṣapī</s>, surrounded by <s>piṭikās</s> like mustard seeds.
<s>Putriṇī</s> is large and covered with very many extremely small <s>piṭikās</s>.
Round like a <s>vidārī</s> tuber and hard is <s>vidārikā</s>.
<s>Vidradhi</s> will be described elsewhere; among these, the first three <s>piṭikās</s>,

children.text: putriṇī ca vidārī ca duḥsahā bahumedasaḥ
children.translated_text: as well as <s>putriṇī</s> and <s>vidārikā</s>, are unbearable in people with much fat.
The others, dominated by <s>pitta</s>, are tolerable and arise in people with little fat.
In these, because of <s>meha</s>, an increase of the <s>doṣas</s> occurs according to each case.
Even without <s>prameha</s>, these arise in persons whose fat is vitiated,
and they are not perceived until they have taken possession of their site.
If a person urinates urine that is turmeric-colored or red, devoid of the prodromal signs of <s>meha</s>,

children.text: yo mūtrayen na taṃ mehaṃ raktapittaṃ tu tad viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: they do not regard that as <s>meha</s>; they know it rather as <s>raktapitta</s> (hemorrhagic pitta disorder).
Sweating, body odor, looseness in the limbs, and attachment to the pleasures of bed, seat, and sleep,
coating of the heart region, eyes, tongue, and ears, heaviness of the body, and excessive growth of hair and nails,
liking cold things, dryness of the throat and palate, sweetness in the mouth, and burning in the hands and feet,
and ants running toward the urine: these are the signs of the coming group of <s>meha</s> diseases.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā pramehaṃ madhuraṃ sapicchaṃ madhūpamaṃ syād dvividho vicāraḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>prameha</s> as sweet, slimy, and honey-like, the inquiry is twofold:

children.text: saṃpūraṇād vā kaphasaṃbhavaḥ syāt kṣīṇeṣu doṣeṣvanilātmako vā ||
children.translated_text: it may be <s>kapha</s>-born from overfilling, or, when the <s>doṣas</s> are depleted, it may be of the nature of <s>anila</s> (wind).

children.text: sapūrvarūpāḥ kaphapittamehāḥ krameṇa ye vātakṛtāśca mehāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>kapha</s>- and <s>pitta</s>-forms of <s>meha</s> that have prodromal signs, and those <s>mehas</s> produced by <s>vāta</s> in sequence,

children.text: sādhyā na te pittakṛtās tu yāpyāḥ sādhyās tu medo yadi nātiduṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: are not curable; the <s>pitta</s>-caused ones are manageable, while they are curable if the fat is not too badly vitiated.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>vidradhi</s> (abscess), enlargement, and <s>gulma</s>.
So indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
From foods that are stale, excessively hot, rough, dry, and burning,
from crooked lying postures and movements, and from various factors that vitiate the blood,
a swelling lodged in corrupted skin, flesh, fat, bone, sinew, blood, and tendons,

children.text: yaḥ śopho bahirantar vā mahāmūlo mahārujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether external or internal, with a large root and great pain,

children.text: vṛttaḥ syād āyato yo vā smṛtaḥ ṣoḍhā sa vidradhiḥ
children.translated_text: round or elongated, is remembered as <s>vidradhi</s>; it is of six kinds:

children.text: doṣaiḥ pṛthak samuditaiḥ śoṇitena kṣatena ca ||
children.translated_text: from the <s>doṣas</s> separately, from them combined, from blood, and from injury.
The external one, wherever it occurs on the body, is severe, knotted, and raised.
The internal one is more severe, deep, and dense like a <s>gulma</s>.
It rises up like an anthill and kills quickly, like fire or a weapon.
It may occur in the navel, bladder, liver, spleen, <s>kloman</s>, heart, abdomen, or groin,
in the kidneys, and in the anal region. When from <s>vāta</s>, there is extremely intense pain;
it is dusky-red, slow in arising and ripening, and irregular in form.
It has piercing, cutting, giddiness, distension, throbbing, creeping sensations, and sounds.
From <s>pitta</s>, it is red, coppery, or black, with thirst, delusion, fever, and burning.
It arises and suppurates quickly. From <s>kapha</s>, it is pale and accompanied by itching,
with nausea, coldness, stiffness, yawning, anorexia, and heaviness.
It arises and ripens slowly; from all <s>doṣas</s> together it is mixed.
Here one should distinguish, as appropriate, the symptoms of the external and internal forms.
The external type caused by blood is dark, covered with black blisters, and has intense burning, pain, and fever,
bearing the signs of <s>pitta</s>; likewise, the internal blood-born type occurs only in women.
In a person wounded by blows from knives and the like, or one who behaves unwholesomely after a wound,
the heat of the wound, driven by <s>vāyu</s>, impels <s>pitta</s> together with blood,
and produces a <s>vidradhi</s> with the signs of <s>pitta</s> and blood, having many complications.
Among these, the difference in complications is remembered according to the difference of location.

children.text: nābhyāṃ hidhmā bhaved vastau mūtraṃ kṛcchreṇa pūti ca
children.translated_text: In the navel there is hiccup; in the bladder, urine is passed with difficulty and is putrid;

children.text: śvāso yakṛti rodhas tu plīhnyucchvāsasya tṛṭ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the liver there is dyspnea; in the spleen, obstruction of exhalation and also thirst;
in the <s>kloman</s> there is constriction of the throat; in the heart, seizure of the whole body;

children.text: pramohas tamakaḥ kāso hṛdaye ghaṭṭanaṃ vyathā ||
children.translated_text: in the heart region there are bewilderment, <s>tamaka</s> asthma, cough, striking pain, and distress.
In the abdomen there is pain in the belly, sides, viscera, and shoulders, and gurgling arises in the abdomen;
in the groins there is gripping of the thighs; in the kidneys, pain in the waist and back;
and in the sides there is pain; in the anus, obstruction of flatus.
Their unripe, ripe, and overcooked states should be taught as in swellings.
When ripe above the navel, they discharge through the mouth; below it, through the anus.

children.text: gudāsyān nābhijo vidyād doṣaṃ kledācca vidradhau ||
children.translated_text: One should know a navel-born one as discharging through the anus and mouth; in <s>vidradhi</s>, the <s>doṣa</s> is known also from the discharge.
There, according to each type, treatment is as for a wound; the one born from all <s>doṣas</s> should be avoided.
When ripe and situated in the heart, navel, or bladder, whether it has burst internally or externally, it too should be avoided.
And when it is ripe, suppurating inward from its opening, in an emaciated person, and accompanied by complications...

children.text: evam eva stanasirā vivṛtāḥ prāpya yoṣitām ||
children.translated_text: In just the same way, having reached the opened breast-vessels of women,
a dense swelling may arise in women who have recently given birth or in pregnant women,
in a breast, whether with milk or without milk, with the signs of an external abscess.

children.text: nāḍīnāṃ sūkṣmavaktratvāt kanyānāṃ na sa jāyate
children.translated_text: Because the mouths of the channels are minute, it does not occur in maidens.
When provoked, or when its movement is obstructed, <s>vāyu</s> moves about causing swelling and pain.
Reaching the testicles from the groin and the vessels that carry to the scrotal sac,
it compresses the arteries and produces enlargement of the scrotal sacs.
That disease called <s>vṛddhi</s> is sevenfold: from the <s>doṣas</s>, blood, fat, urine, and intestine.
The urinary and intestinal forms too arise from <s>anila</s>; only the distinction of cause is different.
From <s>vāta</s> it feels like a leather bag filled with air, is dry, and pains without apparent cause.
From <s>pitta</s> it resembles a ripe <s>udumbara</s> fruit and has burning, heat, and suppuration.
From <s>kapha</s> it is cold, heavy, unctuous, itchy, hard, and only slightly painful.
From blood it is covered with black blisters and has the signs of <s>pitta</s>-type enlargement.
Enlargement from fat is like that from <s>kapha</s>, soft, and like a palm fruit.
The urinary type occurs in one habitually retaining urine; when he walks,

children.text: ambhobhiḥ pūrṇadṛtivat kṣobhaṃ yāti saruṅ mṛduḥ
children.translated_text: it is shaken like a leather bag filled with water, soft and painful.
There is difficult urination, and below there is a ring-like swelling of the scrotal sacs.
By foods that aggravate <s>vāta</s>, by immersion in cold water,
by retention of urges, straining, carrying loads, travelling, and movements with uneven posture,
and by other agitations, when <s>pavana</s> is disturbed and deranges a part of the small intestine,
and carries it downward from its own place,
then, lodged at the groin-joint, it causes a gland-like swelling.

children.text: upekṣyamāṇasya ca muṣkavṛddhim ādhmānarukstambhavatīṃ sa vāyuḥ
children.translated_text: If neglected, that <s>vāyu</s> causes enlargement of the scrotum, with distension, pain, and stiffness.

children.text: prapīḍito 'ntaḥ svanavān prayāti pradhmāpayann eti punaśca muktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When pressed, it goes inward with a sound, inflating it, and, when released, it returns again.
This intestinal enlargement is incurable; its form is like <s>vāta</s>-type enlargement.
It is marked as though by a lattice of networks of dry, black and reddish vein-filaments.

children.text: gulmo 'ṣṭadhā pṛthag doṣaiḥ saṃsṛṣṭair nicayaṃ gataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gulma</s> is eightfold: from the separate <s>doṣas</s>, from combined <s>doṣas</s>, and from all of them accumulated together.
The eighth arises in women from disorder of the menstrual blood.
When one has been emaciated by fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and the like, or by therapies such as emesis,
and eats <s>vāta</s>-producing foods, or, while hungry, drinks cold water,
and then takes food, or practices fasting, swimming, and the like,
or undertakes acts that agitate the body, or induces vomiting,

children.text: anudīrṇām udīrṇān vā vātādīn na vimuñcati ||
children.translated_text: or does not release the urges of <s>vāta</s> and the others, whether not yet arisen or already arisen,
or resorts to evacuation therapy without first using oleation and sweating,

children.text: śuddho vāśu vidāhīni bhajate syandanāni vā ||
children.translated_text: or, after being purified, quickly consumes burning foods or fluid-producing foods,

children.text: vātolbaṇās tasya malāḥ pṛthak kruddhā dviśo 'thavā
children.translated_text: then his wastes, dominated by <s>vāta</s>, separately provoked, or in pairs,
or all together, or combined with blood, lying in the great channel,
obstruct the upward and downward pathways and produce, preceded by pain,
a palpable, raised, knot-shaped mass called <s>gulma</s>.
Through emaciation, or through obstruction of the pathway by <s>kapha</s>, feces, and <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: vāyuḥ kṛtāśrayaḥ koṣṭhe raukṣyāt kāṭhinyam āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>vāyu</s>, having made its seat in the abdomen, becomes hard through dryness.
It is independent when vitiated in its own seat, and dependent when in another's seat.
Although formless, because it is compacted it seems to have assumed form.
It is called <s>gulma</s>, and it is located in the bladder, navel, heart, or flanks.
From <s>vāta</s> there are pain in the neck and head, fever, splenic disorder, and intestinal rumbling.

children.text: vyadhaḥ sūcyeva viṭsaṅgaḥ kṛcchrād ucchvasanaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: There is piercing as if by a needle, obstruction of feces, and frequent difficult breathing.

children.text: stambho gātre mukhe śoṣaḥ kārśyaṃ viṣamavahnitā ||
children.translated_text: There is stiffness in the limbs, dryness of the mouth, emaciation, and irregular digestive fire.
The skin and other tissues are dry and dark; and because <s>anila</s> is mobile,
the mass has no fixed shape, place, increase, decrease, or pain.
As if filled with ants, the <s>gulma</s> throbs and is pierced with pain.
From <s>pitta</s> there are burning, sour belching, fainting, loose stools, sweating, thirst, and fever.
The skin and other tissues become yellow, and the <s>gulma</s> cannot bear touch.

children.text: dūyate dīpyate soṣmā svasthānaṃ dahatīva ca ||
children.translated_text: It aches, blazes, is hot, and seems to burn its own seat.
From <s>kapha</s> there are stagnation, loss of appetite, weakness, and cold fever.
There are coryza, lethargy, nausea, cough, and whiteness of the skin and other tissues.
The <s>gulma</s> is deep-seated, hard, heavy, numb, fixed, and only slightly painful.

children.text: svadoṣasthānadhāmānaḥ sve sve kāle ca rukkarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These cause pain chiefly in the abodes of their own <s>doṣas</s> and at their own times.

children.text: prāyas trayas tu dvandvotthā gulmāḥ saṃsṛṣṭalakṣaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The three <s>gulmas</s> arising from paired combinations usually have mixed symptoms.
The one born from all the <s>doṣas</s> has intense pain and burning, suppurates quickly, and is dense and raised.

children.text: so 'sādhyo raktagulmas tu striyā eva prajāyate
children.translated_text: It is incurable; but <s>raktagulma</s> arises only in a woman.

children.text: ṛtau vā navasūtā vā yadi vā yonirogiṇī ||
children.translated_text: If a woman, in her season, or newly delivered, or suffering from a vaginal disorder,

children.text: sevate vātalāni strī kruddhas tasyāḥ samīraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: takes <s>vāta</s>-producing things, her provoked <s>samīraṇa</s>
blocks the menstrual blood that is situated in the vagina each month.
It enlarges the abdomen and manifests signs of pregnancy,
such as nausea, pregnancy-longing, appearance of breast milk, and emaciation.
Gradually, through association with <s>vāyu</s> and because it has a <s>pitta</s>-source,
that blood produces in her complications arising from a <s>vāta</s>-<s>pitta</s> <s>gulma</s>,
such as pain, rigidity, burning, diarrhea, thirst, and fever.
And there is especially severe pain in the uterus, where the vitiated blood is lodged.
There are discharges, foul smell, piercing, throbbing, and pains of the vagina.

children.text: na cāṅgair garbhavad gulmaḥ sphuratyapi tu śūlavān ||
children.translated_text: The <s>gulma</s> does not move with limbs like a fetus, but it is painful.

children.text: piṇḍībhūtaḥ sa evāsyāḥ kadācit spandate cirāt
children.translated_text: That same compact mass in her sometimes, after a long time, quivers.

children.text: na cāsyā vardhate kukṣir gulma eva tu vardhate ||
children.translated_text: Her belly does not grow; only the <s>gulma</s> grows.

children.text: svadoṣasaṃśrayo gulmaḥ sarvo bhavati tena saḥ
children.translated_text: Every <s>gulma</s> is rooted in its own <s>doṣa</s>; therefore it

children.text: pākaṃ cireṇa bhajate naiva vā vidradhiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: comes to suppuration only after a long time, or not at all; but a <s>vidradhi</s>
suppurates very quickly, because it is based in vitiated blood.
Therefore, because it burns and ripens quickly, it is called <s>vidradhi</s>.
When a <s>gulma</s> has an internal seat, there are pains in the bladder, belly, heart, and spleen,
loss of digestive fire, complexion, and strength, and non-movement of the urges.

children.text: ato viparyayo bāhye koṣṭhāṅgeṣu tu nātiruk
children.translated_text: In an external one the opposite occurs; in the organs of the abdomen there is not much pain,
but there is discoloration of the site and a more prominent outward swelling.
Great distension in the abdomen, with rumbling and extremely fierce pain,
caused by obstruction of upward and downward <s>vāta</s>, is called <s>ānāha</s>.
A dense glandular swelling, like an <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, raised upward like an <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>,
has the signs of <s>ānāha</s>; when it is transverse and of that same form, it is <s>pratyaṣṭhīlā</s>.
When <s>vāyu</s>, going from the large intestine to the anus and genitals, causes intense pain,

children.text: tūṇī pratūṇī tu bhavet sa evāto viparyaye ||
children.translated_text: that is <s>tūṇī</s>; <s>pratūṇī</s> is the same condition in the opposite direction from there.
Frequent belching, constipation, inability to feel satisfied, gurgling of the intestines,

children.text: āṭopam ādhmānam apaktiśaktim āsannagulmasya vadanti cihnam ||
children.translated_text: rumbling, distension, and impaired digestion are said to be signs of an approaching <s>gulma</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>udara</s> diseases.
So indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: rogāḥ sarve 'pi mande 'gnau sutarām udarāṇi tu
children.translated_text: All diseases arise when the digestive fire is weak, and abdominal diseases especially so,
from indigestion, impure foods, and the accumulation of wastes.
Having obstructed the tissue-elements above and below, and the water-carrying channels,
and having vitiated <s>prāṇa</s>, digestive fire, and <s>apāna</s>, the wastes enter the skin, flesh, and joints.

children.text: ādhmāpya kukṣim udaram aṣṭadhā tacca bhidyate
children.translated_text: They distend the belly and produce <s>udara</s>; it is divided into eight kinds:
by the separate <s>doṣas</s>, by all of them together, and by spleen, obstruction, injury, and fluid.
Those afflicted by it have dry palates and lips, swollen feet, hands, and abdomen,
lost activity, strength, and appetite, and they are emaciated, with distended bellies.

children.text: syuḥ pretarūpāḥ puruṣā bhāvinas tasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Men become like corpses. The signs that it is impending are these:

children.text: kṣunnāśo 'nnaṃ cirāt sarvaṃ savidāhaṃ ca pacyate ||
children.translated_text: loss of hunger; all food digests only after a long time and with burning;

children.text: jīrṇājīrṇaṃ na jānāti sauhityaṃ sahate na ca
children.translated_text: he does not know whether food is digested or undigested, and cannot tolerate satiety.
He constantly loses strength and becomes breathless even with slight exertion.
There is enlargement, non-elimination of waste, and some swelling of the feet,
pain in the bladder-joint region, tightness, and heaviness even after little food.
Lines arise and the folds disappear on the abdomen; in all abdominal disorders
there are drowsiness, fatigue, retention of feces, and weak digestive fire.
Burning, swelling, distension, and finally the water-born form occur.
All the non-watery forms are reddish, without swelling, and not very heavy.
Latticed with networks of veins, it constantly makes a gurgling sound.

children.text: nābhim antraṃ ca viṣṭabhya vegaṃ kṛtvā praṇaśyati ||
children.translated_text: Pressing upon the navel and intestines, it creates an urge and then disappears.
In the <s>māruta</s> type there are pains in the heart, waist, navel, anus, and groins.

children.text: saśabdo niścared vāyur viḍ baddhā mūtram alpakam ||
children.translated_text: Wind passes out with sound; feces are bound, and urine is scanty.

children.text: nātimando 'nalo laulyaṃ na ca syād virasaṃ mukham
children.translated_text: The digestive fire is not too weak, there is craving, and the mouth is not tasteless.
In <s>vātodara</s>, swelling occurs in the hands, feet, scrotum, and belly,
with pain in the belly, sides, abdomen, waist, and back, and splitting pain in the joints.
There is dry cough, aching of the limbs, heaviness downward, and retention of feces.
The skin and so on are dusky-red, rough, and the swelling grows and diminishes suddenly.
The abdomen is spread with thin black veins and has pricking and splitting pains.
When struck, it makes a sound like an inflated leather bag,
and <s>vāyu</s> moves there in every direction, with pain and sound.

children.text: pittodare jvaro mūrchā dāhas tṛṭ kaṭukāsyatā
children.translated_text: In <s>pittodara</s> there are fever, fainting, burning, thirst, and a bitter taste in the mouth,
dizziness, diarrhea, yellowness in the skin and so on, and the abdomen is greenish.
It is bound with yellow and copper-colored veins, sweaty, hot, and burning.
It smokes, is soft to the touch, ripens quickly, and becomes greatly painful.
In <s>śleṣmodara</s> there are prostration of the limbs, numbness, swelling, and heaviness,
sleepiness, nausea, anorexia, dyspnea, cough, and whiteness in the skin and so on.
The abdomen is motionless, smooth, large, and spread with white lines.
It grows slowly, is hard, cold to the touch, heavy, and stable.
When the three <s>doṣas</s> are provoked by their various aggravating causes, and by impure menstrual blood given by women,
and by artificial poison, chronic poison, and the like, the accumulated wastes, mixed with blood,
reach the abdomen and become deranged, accompanied by wasting, fainting, and dizziness.
They produce a terrible <s>udara</s> marked by the signs of all three <s>doṣas</s> and quick suppuration.
It afflicts especially at the sight or exposure to cold, wind, and clouds.
In one who has overeaten, from agitation caused by travel in vehicles and similar activities,
and from excessive sexual activity, work, travel, vomiting, disease, and emaciation,
the spleen, lodged on the left side, slips from its place and enlarges.

children.text: śoṇitaṃ vā rasādibhyo vivṛddhaṃ taṃ vivardhayet
children.translated_text: Or blood, increased from <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues, may enlarge it.
At first it is excessively hard like an <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>; then it becomes like a tortoise's back.
Growing gradually in the belly, it brings on abdominal enlargement,
together with dyspnea, cough, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, distension, pain, and fever,
and with pallor, fainting, vomiting, burning, and delusion.
It is reddish or discolored, or marked with blue and turmeric-yellow lines.
By pain and <s>ānāha</s> from upward-moving <s>vāta</s>, by delusion, thirst, burning, and fever,
and by heaviness, anorexia, and hardness, one should recognize the wastes there in order.

children.text: plīhavad dakṣiṇāt pārśvāt kuryād yakṛd api cyutam
children.translated_text: Just as the spleen does from the left side, the liver too, displaced from the right side, produces it.
When the anal passage is obstructed by food eaten together with eyelashes or hairs,
by hemorrhoids, by upward-moving <s>vāta</s>, or by other things that smear and block the intestines,
the provoked <s>anila</s>, obstructing feces, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, causes it.
Through that, <s>apāna</s> produces abdominal disease; burning, fever, thirst, and sneezing arise.
There are cough, dyspnea, weakness of the thighs, and pain in the head, heart, navel, and anus.
There is retention of feces, loss of appetite, vomiting, and an abdominal disorder with obstructed wind.
It is firm, bound with rows of blue-red veins, or else without such streaks.
It usually arises above the navel and has the shape of a cow's tail.
If the intestine is pierced by bones and other sharp objects eaten with food, or by overeating,

children.text: bhidyate pacyate vāntraṃ tacchidraiśca sravan bahiḥ
children.translated_text: or if the intestine splits or suppurates, then fluid leaks outward through those perforations.

children.text: āma eva gudād eti tato 'lpālpaṃ saviḍrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At first only undigested matter comes from the anus; then, little by little, it comes with the character of feces.
It has the same smell as a corpse, is slimy, and is yellow-red.
The remainder, filling the abdomen, brings on a dreadful abdominal disease.

children.text: vardhayet tad adho nābherāśu caiti jalātmatām
children.translated_text: It grows below the navel and quickly comes to have the nature of water.
It shows the form of greatly aggravated <s>doṣas</s> and is accompanied throughout by dyspnea, thirst, and dizziness.
This is called <s>chidrodara</s>; others call it <s>parisrāvi</s>.
In one who, after beginning the drinking of unctuous preparations, suddenly drinks unripe water,
or from excessive drinking of water, in one of weak digestion, depleted strength, or extreme emaciation,
<s>anila</s> and <s>kapha</s>, made watery, obstruct the channels of water.
Lodged in the abdomen after leaving their own places, they increase that very water.
Then there is an abdominal disease marked by thirst, discharge from the anus, and pain.
It is accompanied by cough, dyspnea, and loss of appetite, and is spread over with veins of many colors.
It has the touch, sound, agitation, and trembling of a leather bag filled with water.

children.text: dakodaraṃ mahat snigdhaṃ sthiram āvṛttanābhi tat
children.translated_text: That is <s>dakodara</s>: large, smooth, fixed, and with the navel covered over.
In all these, when they are neglected, the <s>doṣas</s>, displaced from their own seats,
become liquid through maturation and liquefy even the joints and the mouths of the channels.
Sweat too, obstructed in the external channels, comes to be situated transversely.

children.text: tad evodakam āpyāyya picchāṃ kuryāt tadā bhavet
children.translated_text: Nourishing that very water, it produces slime; then there arises

children.text: gurūdaraṃ sthiraṃ vṛttam āhataṃ ca na śabdavat ||
children.translated_text: a heavy, firm, round abdomen which, when struck, does not make a resonant sound.

children.text: mṛdu vyapetarājīkaṃ nābhyāṃ spṛṣṭaṃ ca sarpati
children.translated_text: It is soft, devoid of streaks, and, when touched at the navel, it spreads.
That condition arises from water; in it the enlargement of the flanks is still greater.
There is disappearance of the veins and the symptoms stated for watery abdominal disease.
Abdominal disease from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, spleen, combined <s>doṣas</s>, and water

children.text: kṛcchraṃ yathottaraṃ pakṣāt paraṃ prāyo 'pare hataḥ
children.translated_text: is difficult in increasing order; after a fortnight, the remaining cases are generally destroyed.
Every abdominal disease in which water has appeared and which is accompanied by the complications stated as fatal signs
and every abdominal disease present from birth is considered generally the hardest to cure.
In a strong person, when water has not yet arisen and the disease is newly developed, it is curable with effort.
Now then, we shall explain the causes and diagnosis of <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>, swelling, and erysipelas.
So indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
The bodily impurities, with <s>pitta</s> predominant, become aggravated by the aggravating causes already described.

children.text: tatrānilena balinā kṣiptaṃ pittaṃ hṛdi sthitam ||
children.translated_text: There, <s>pitta</s>, situated in the heart, is driven by powerful <s>anila</s>.

children.text: dhamanīr daśa samprāpya vyāpnuvat sakalāṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Reaching the ten arteries, it spreads through the whole body.
It vitiates <s>śleṣman</s>, skin, blood, and flesh, and lodges within.

children.text: tvaṅmāṃsayos tat kurute tvaci varṇān pṛthagvidhān
children.translated_text: Between the skin and the flesh it produces various colors in the skin:
pale, yellow, and green, with pallor predominant among them.

children.text: yato 'taḥ pāṇḍurityuktaḥ sa rogas tena gauravam
children.translated_text: Therefore it is called <s>pāṇḍu</s>; in that disease there is heaviness,
looseness of the bodily tissues, and loss of the qualities of <s>ojas</s>.
Then the patient has little blood and fat, is without substance, and has slackened senses.
His limbs feel as though they were being kneaded, and his heart feels unstable.
The regions around his eyes are swollen; he is exhausted, irritable, spits, and speaks little.
He dislikes food, dislikes cold, has falling hair, and his digestive fire is damaged.

children.text: sannasaktho jvarī śvāsī karṇakṣveḍī bhramī śramī
children.translated_text: His thighs are weak; he is feverish, short of breath, ringing in the ears, dizzy, and fatigued.

children.text: sa pañcadhā pṛthag doṣaiḥ samastair mṛttikādanāt ||
children.translated_text: It is fivefold: from each <s>doṣa</s> separately, from all together, and from eating clay.
Its preliminary symptoms are palpitation of the heart and dryness of the skin,
loss of appetite, yellow urine, absence of sweat, and weak digestive fire.
There are lassitude and fatigue. In the type caused by <s>anila</s>, there is body pain, throbbing, and trembling.
The veins, nails, feces, urine, and eyes are blackish, dry, or reddish.
There are swelling, distension, bad taste in the mouth, drying of the feces, and pain in the side and head.
From <s>pitta</s>, the veins and the rest have a greenish-yellow appearance; there is fever and darkness before the eyes.
There are thirst, sweating, fainting, desire for cold, foul smell, and a pungent taste in the mouth.
There is looseness of stool, sour belching, and burning. From <s>kapha</s>, the veins and the rest are white.
There are drowsiness, a salty taste in the mouth, horripilation, and loss of voice,
as well as cough and vomiting. From the accumulation of all, the signs are mixed and the condition is extremely hard to bear.

children.text: mṛt kaṣāyānilaṃ pittam ūṣarā madhurā kapham
children.translated_text: Clay that is astringent vitiates <s>anila</s>; saline clay vitiates <s>pitta</s>; sweet clay vitiates <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: dūṣayitvā rasādīṃśca raukṣyād bhuktaṃ virūkṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: After vitiating <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues, and because of its dryness drying up what has been eaten,
it fills the channels with undigested material and blocks them, producing the disease as before.
Then there is <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>; the person's navel, feet, mouth, and penis become swollen.

children.text: purīṣaṃ kṛmiman muñced bhinnaṃ sāsṛk kaphaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: He passes feces with worms, broken up, bloody, and mixed with <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: yaḥ pāṇḍurogī seveta pittalaṃ tasya kāmalām ||
children.translated_text: If a patient with <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> consumes things that increase <s>pitta</s>, <s>kāmalā</s> arises in him.
The <s>pitta</s>, lodged in the alimentary tract and the peripheral tissues, burns the blood and flesh and brings it on.
The eyes, urine, skin, nails, face, and stool become yellow like turmeric.
He has burning, indigestion, and thirst; he resembles a frog and his senses are weak.
This may occur in one with excessive <s>pitta</s> even apart from <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.

children.text: upekṣayā ca śophāḍhyā sā kṛcchrā kumbhakāmalā
children.translated_text: When neglected and accompanied by much swelling, it is difficult to cure and is called <s>kumbhakāmalā</s>.
When in <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> there is a green, dusky, and yellow coloration,

children.text: vātapittād bhramas tṛṣṇā strīṣvaharṣo mṛdur jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, with dizziness, thirst, lack of desire for women, and mild fever,
with drowsiness and loss of strength and digestive fire, they call that <s>loḍhara</s>, <s>halīmaka</s>,

children.text: alasaṃ ceti śaṃsanti teṣāṃ pūrvam upadravāḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>alasa</s>. Their complications have been stated first as dominated by swelling.
Therefore that very swelling is now described.
Vitiated <s>vāyu</s>, carrying outward vitiated <s>pitta</s>, blood, and <s>kapha</s> through the external vessels,

children.text: nītvā ruddhagatis tair hi kuryāt tvaṅmāṃsasaṃśrayam ||
children.translated_text: and obstructing their movement with these, produces a raised swelling lodged in the skin and flesh.

children.text: utsedhaṃ saṃhataṃ śophaṃ tam āhur nicayād ataḥ
children.translated_text: Because it is a compact swelling made by accumulation, they therefore call it <s>śopha</s>.
But all such swellings, through differences in cause, have nine distinct forms.

children.text: doṣaiḥ pṛthag dvayaiḥ sarvairabhighātād viṣād api
children.translated_text: They arise from the <s>doṣas</s> singly, in pairs, and all together, and also from trauma and from poison.

children.text: dvidhā vā nijam āgantuṃ sarvāṅgaikāṅgajaṃ ca tam ||
children.translated_text: Or it is twofold, endogenous and adventitious, and it may arise in the whole body or in one limb.
They know it also as threefold through the distinctions of being broad, raised, or knotty.
The general cause of swellings, and especially of those born from <s>doṣas</s>, is as follows:
when a person weakened by illness, therapies, fasting, and the like quickly resorts
to excessive quantities, or in another case to heavy, sour, unctuous, and cold things,
to salty, alkaline, sharp, hot greens and water, and to sleep or wakefulness,
to clay, domestic-animal meat, dried meat, indigestion, exertion, and sexual intercourse,
to travel on foot along a road, or also by a jolting vehicle;
or when dyspnea, cough, diarrhea, hemorrhoids, abdominal enlargement, menorrhagia, and fever,
<s>viṣūcī</s>, <s>alasaka</s>, vomiting, pregnancy, <s>visarpa</s>, anemia,

children.text: anye ca mithyopakrāntās tair doṣā vakṣasi sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and other diseases are wrongly treated, by these causes the <s>doṣas</s> situated in the chest

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ śopham adho vastau madhye kurvanti madhyagāḥ
children.translated_text: produce swelling upward; when in the bladder, they produce it downward; when in the middle, they produce it in the middle.
Those pervading the whole body make a generalized swelling, while those lodged in individual limbs make localized swelling there.
Its premonitory signs are burning distress, distension of the veins, and heaviness of the limbs.
A swelling from <s>vāta</s> is mobile, dry, rough-haired, and reddish black.
It has contraction, throbbing, horripilation, pain, pricking, splitting pain, and numbness.
It arises and subsides quickly; when pressed, being thin, it quickly rises up again.
It is relieved by unctuous warm massage; it is slight at night and great by day.
And in it the skin tingles as though smeared with mustard paste.
From <s>pitta</s>, it has a yellow, red, and blackish appearance and makes the hairs coppery red.
It spreads and subsides quickly, begins first in the middle, and is thin.
It is accompanied by thirst, burning, fever, sweating, burning moisture, intoxication, and dizziness.
It desires cold, loosens the stool, is foul-smelling, intolerant of touch, and soft.
From <s>kapha</s>, it is itchy, with pale hair and skin, hard, cold, and heavy.
It is unctuous, smooth, fixed, congealed, and causes sleepiness, vomiting, and depression of digestive fire.
When pressed it does not rise; it is difficult to pacify, slow to arise, and strong at night.
When cut by <s>kuśa</s> grass, a weapon, or the like, it does not bleed, but after a long time exudes slimy fluid.

children.text: sparśoṣṇakāṅkṣī ca kaphād yathāsvaṃ dvandvajās trayaḥ
children.translated_text: It desires warm touch; such is the swelling from <s>kapha</s>. The three arising from paired <s>doṣas</s> have the respective mixed signs.
From a mixture of causes and symptoms comes the one born of accumulation, having the nature of accumulation.
From trauma, by cutting, splitting, wounds, and the like caused by weapons and so on,
by cold wind, sea wind, or juices produced by <s>bhallātaka</s> and <s>kapikacchu</s>,
and by contact with irritant hairs and awns, a swelling becomes spreading.
It is intensely hot, reddish in appearance, and for the most part marked by the signs of <s>pitta</s>.
The poison-born swelling arises from the crawling contact or urination of poisonous creatures,
and from the fall of fangs, teeth, or nails, even of creatures that are not poisonous.
It arises from contact with garments fouled by feces, urine, semen, and dirty impurities,
from touch of wind from poisonous trees, and from the application or sprinkling of compound poison.
It is soft, mobile, hanging down, rapid, and causes burning and pain.
A new swelling without complications is curable; one otherwise has already been declared incurable.
<s>Visarpa</s> arises, like swelling, from the <s>doṣas</s> and affected tissues, including those beginning with trauma.
They say it has three seats: external, internal, and dependent on both.

children.text: yathottaraṃ ca duḥsādhyās tatra doṣā yathāyatham
children.translated_text: Each later type is harder to cure; there the <s>doṣas</s>, each in its own way,
provoked by their aggravating factors, especially by burning and irritating substances,
spread rapidly in the body: those situated inside move outward,
those situated outside move in the twofold seat, and those in both seats are dual; one should recognize the internally based type by the following signs.
It is known by distress of the vital spots, bewilderment, disruption of the channels,
excessive thirst, and the irregular activity of the natural urges,
and by the rapid collapse of digestive fire and strength; the external type is known from the opposite.
There, from <s>vāta</s>, <s>parīsarpa</s> has pain equal to a <s>vāta</s>-fever.
It has swelling, throbbing, pricking, splitting pain, stretching pain, distress, and horripilation.
From <s>pitta</s>, it is swift-moving, has the signs of a <s>pitta</s>-fever, and is very red.
From <s>kapha</s>, it is accompanied by itching, is unctuous, and has pain like a <s>kapha</s>-fever.
All of them, when neglected, enlarge with blisters bearing the signs of their own <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: te pakvabhinnāḥ svaṃ svaṃ ca bibhrati vraṇalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: When they have ripened and burst, they each display the characteristics of a wound.
From <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, it is accompanied by fever, vomiting, fainting, diarrhea, thirst, and dizziness,
by bone-splitting pain, depression of digestive fire, darkness before the eyes, and anorexia.
It makes the whole body appear as though strewn with blazing coals.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ deśaṃ visarpaśca visarpati bhavet sa saḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever region the <s>visarpa</s> spreads to, that very region

children.text: śāntāṅgārāsito nīlo rakto vāśu ca cīyate ||
children.translated_text: quickly becomes like extinguished charcoal, black, blue, or red, and rapidly enlarges.

children.text: agnidagdha iva sphoṭaiḥ śīghragatvād drutaṃ ca saḥ
children.translated_text: It is covered with blisters as if burned by fire, and because of its quick movement it soon
follows the vital spots; then this <s>visarpa</s>, with <s>vāta</s> extremely strong,

children.text: vyathetāṅgaṃ haret saṃjñāṃ nidrāṃ ca śvāsam īrayet
children.translated_text: torments the body, takes away consciousness and sleep, and drives on dyspnea

children.text: hidhmāṃ ca sa gato 'vasthām īdṛśīṃ labhate na nā ||
children.translated_text: and hiccup; having reached such a state, that person does not survive.
In some cases, overcome by discomfort of the skin while shifting about on the ground, bed, seat, and the like,
and then afflicted by fatigue of mind and body arising from that movement,
he falls into sleep from which he is hard to awaken; this is called <s>agnivisarpa</s>.

children.text: kaphena ruddhaḥ pavano bhittvā taṃ bahudhā kapham ||
children.translated_text: When <s>pavana</s>, obstructed by <s>kapha</s>, breaks that <s>kapha</s> apart in many ways,
or when, in a person with increased blood, it vitiates blood that has entered the skin, vessels, sinews, and flesh,
and has made it take the nature of long, minute, round, thick, and rough forms,
it produces a garland of red nodules, with severe pain and fever.
It is accompanied by difficult breathing, cough, diarrhea, dryness of the mouth, hiccup, vomiting, and dizziness,
and by confusion, discoloration, fainting, breaking pain in the limbs, and collapse of the digestive fire.
Thus this is the <s>granthi-vīsarpa</s> (nodular spreading inflammation), born from provocation of <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s>.
From <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> there are fever, rigidity, sleepiness, stupor, and headache,
lassitude of the limbs, convulsive tossing, delirium, loss of appetite, and dizziness,
fainting, loss of digestive fire, splitting pain in the bones, thirst, and heaviness of the senses.

children.text: āmopaveśanaṃ lepaḥ srotasāṃ sa ca sarpati ||
children.translated_text: There is settling of <s>āma</s> (undigested morbid matter) and coating of the channels, and it spreads.
It usually takes hold in the stomach, seizing one region, and it is not very painful.
It is strewn with pustules that are very yellow, red, and pale.
It is blackish in appearance, dark, unctuous, dirty, swollen, and heavy.
Its suppuration is deep, its heat abundant; when touched it is moist and breaks open.
Its flesh is decomposed like mud, and the groups of tendons and veins are clearly visible.
It smells like a corpse; that <s>vīsarpa</s> they call <s>kardama</s> (mud-like).
The type arising from all <s>doṣas</s> has all symptoms and spreads through all the tissues.

children.text: bāhyahetoḥ kṣatāt kruddhaḥ saraktaṃ pittam īrayan ||
children.translated_text: When, from an external cause, <s>māruta</s> is provoked by a wound and drives <s>pitta</s> together with blood,
it produces <s>vīsarpa</s>, covered with eruptions like horse gram.
It is full of swelling, fever, pain, and burning, and is dark-red.
The three arising from the individual <s>doṣas</s> are curable, and so too are those born from paired <s>doṣas</s> when free from complications.
Those arising from a wound and from all <s>doṣas</s> are incurable, as are all those that have invaded the vital points.
They have decomposed tendons, veins, and flesh, are thoroughly moist, and smell like a corpse.
Now then we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (cutaneous disease), <s>śvitra</s> (depigmentation), and <s>kṛmi</s> (worms or parasites).
Thus indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Through improper food and conduct, especially what is incompatible,
and through sinful acts that are practiced, such as criticizing the good, killing, and stealing another's property,

children.text: pāpmabhiḥ karmabhiḥ sadyaḥ prāktanair veritā malāḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>malas</s> (morbid humors), impelled by evil deeds both immediate and done in the past,
enter the vessels, move sideways, and reach the skin, lymph, blood, and flesh.
They vitiate these, loosen them, and then emerge outward.

children.text: tvacaḥ kurvanti vaivarṇyaṃ duṣṭāḥ kuṣṭham uśanti tat ||
children.translated_text: They produce discoloration of the skin; when corrupted, that condition they call <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: kālenopekṣitaṃ yasmāt sarvaṃ kuṣṇāti tad vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Because, when neglected over time, it consumes the whole body,

children.text: prapadya dhātūn vyāpyāntaḥ sarvān saṃkledya cāvahet ||
children.translated_text: entering the tissues, pervading all of them inwardly, moistening them, and causing them to flow down,
it brings about subtle and very terrible worms, along with sweat, moisture, and putrefaction.
By these, in order, the hair, skin, tendons, vessels, cartilage, and bones are eaten away.
For this reason <s>śvitra</s> is declared to be outside <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: kuṣṭhāni saptadhā doṣaiḥ pṛthaṅ miśraiḥ samāgataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṣṭhas</s> are sevenfold according to the <s>doṣas</s>: separately, in mixtures, and all together.
Although all three <s>doṣas</s> are present in all of them, the designation is according to predominance.

children.text: vātena kuṣṭhaṃ kāpālaṃ pittād audumbaraṃ kaphāt ||
children.translated_text: From <s>vāta</s> comes the <s>kuṣṭha</s> called <s>kāpāla</s>; from <s>pitta</s>, <s>audumbara</s>; from <s>kapha</s>,
the one called <s>maṇḍala</s>, and <s>vicarcī</s>; the one called <s>ṛkṣa</s> arises from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Carma</s>, <s>ekakuṣṭha</s>, <s>kiṭibha</s>, <s>sidhma</s>, <s>alasa</s>, and <s>vipādikā</s>
arise from <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>; from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s> come <s>dadrū</s> and <s>śatāruṣī</s>,
<s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>visphoṭa</s>, <s>pāmā</s>, and <s>carmadala</s>.

children.text: sarvaiḥ syāt kākaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ trikaṃ dadru sakākaṇam
children.translated_text: From all of them there may be <s>kākaṇa</s>. The first triad, <s>dadrū</s> together with <s>kākaṇa</s>,
and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> and <s>ṛkṣajihvā</s>: these seven are the great <s>kuṣṭhas</s>.
Excessively smooth or rough touch, fatigue, absence of sweating, and discoloration,

children.text: dāhaḥ kaṇḍūs tvaci svāpas todaḥ koṭhonnatiḥ śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: burning, itching, numbness in the skin, piercing pain, elevation of wheals, and weariness,
excessive pain in wounds, rapid arising and long persistence,
dryness even when healed, aggravation from even a slight cause,
horripilation, and blackness of the blood are the earliest signs of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
<s>Kāpāla</s> is black and red like a potsherd, dry, numb, rough, and thin,
wide-spread, with uneven borders, and covered with bristling hairs.
It has much pricking pain, little itching, and spreads quickly.
In <s>audumbara</s>, the skin and hair are coppery like a ripe <s>udumbara</s> fruit and are covered with pale veins.
It is thick, with abundant dense moisture and blood, and has much burning and pain.
One should know <s>audumbara</s> by its quick arising, splitting open, and worms.

children.text: sthiraṃ styānaṃ guru snigdhaṃ śvetaraktam anāśugam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍala</s> is fixed, dense, heavy, unctuous, white and red, and does not move quickly.
It is joined together, raised, and has much itching, discharge, and worms.
It has smooth yellowish borders and is perfectly circular.
<s>Vicarcikā</s> is dark, with itchy pustules, and rich in lymphatic exudate.
<s>Ṛkṣajihvā</s> is rough, thin, red at the edge, dark within, and raised.
It has pricking pain, burning, pain, and moisture, and is covered with hard pustules.
Shaped like a bear's tongue, it is called <s>ṛkṣajihvā</s>, and it has many worms.
<s>Carma</s> or <s>ekakuṣṭha</s> is rough to the touch like elephant hide and occupies a large area.
<s>Kiṭibha</s>, again, has no sweating and resembles fish scales.
It is dry, rough to the touch like a callus, itchy, harsh, and black.

children.text: sidhmaṃ rūkṣaṃ bahiḥ snigdham antar ghṛṣṭaṃ rajaḥ kiret ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sidhma</s> is dry, outwardly unctuous, and when rubbed inwardly sheds powder.
It is smooth to the touch, thin, white and coppery, like the flower of <s>daugdhika</s>.
It usually occurs on the upper body and is covered with itchy nodules.
<s>Alasa</s> consists of red lesions; fissures of the hands and feet are <s>vipādikās</s>.
They have severe pain, slight itching, and are covered with inflamed pustules.
<s>Dadrū</s> spreads in long lines like <s>dūrvā</s> grass and has the color of a flax blossom.
It has raised circular lesions, is itchy, and persists continuously.
<s>Śatāru</s> has a thick root, burning and pain, is red and dark, and has many sores.
It is full of moisture and organisms, and most often arises at the joints.
It is red at the edge and pale within, with itching, burning, and pain.
It is raised and covered with red streaks like a lotus petal.
It is dense, abounding chiefly in lymph and blood, and quickly breaks open.
<s>Puṇḍarīka</s> is covered with thin-skinned blisters that are white and reddish.
<s>Visphoṭa</s> consists of eruptions; <s>pāmā</s> has an excess of itching, moisture, and pain.
Its eruptions are minute, dusky-red, numerous, and generally on the buttocks, hands, and elbows.
<s>Sasphoṭa</s> has blisters, cannot bear touch, and is marked by itching, pricking pain, and burning.
<s>Rakta</s> has splitting flakes of skin; <s>kākaṇa</s> has intense burning and pain.

children.text: pūrvaṃ raktaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ ca kākaṇantīphalopamam
children.translated_text: At first it is red and black, resembling the fruit of the <s>kākaṇantī</s>.

children.text: kuṣṭhaliṅgair yutaṃ sarvair naikavarṇaṃ tato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: After that it becomes of many colors and furnished with all the signs of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
By the signs and actions prescribed in the chapter on distinctions of <s>doṣa</s>,
