one should determine the predominance of <s>doṣas</s> in cases of <s>kuṣṭha</s>; one should abandon what is dominated by all the <s>doṣas</s>.
One should also abandon what is described among fatal signs and what is lodged in bone, marrow, or semen.
That which has entered fat is manageable; that which is in a paired condition with <s>pitta</s>, or has entered blood and flesh, is difficult.

children.text: akṛcchraṃ kaphavātāḍhyaṃ tvakstham ekamalaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: That which is rich in <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, located in the skin, and caused by a single impurity is not difficult.
When <s>kuṣṭha</s> is situated in the skin, there are piercing pain, discoloration, and dryness.
When it is in the blood, there are sweating, numbness, and swellings; when it is in the flesh, again,
there are blisters located on the hands and feet, and excessive moisture in the joints.
When it is in fat, there is crookedness, loss of movement of the limbs, and splitting.
When it is in bone and marrow, there is collapse of the nose, redness of the eyes, and loss of voice.
When there is ulceration, there are worms; when it is in semen, there is injury to one's wife and offspring.
And in blood and the following tissues all the symptoms occur in the order previously stated.

children.text: kuṣṭhaikasaṃbhavaṃ śvitraṃ kilāsaṃ dāruṇaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: <s>Śvitra</s>, also called <s>kilāsa</s> and <s>dāruṇa</s>, arises from the same source as <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
It is described as not exuding and as arising from, and lodged in, the three tissues.
From <s>vāta</s> it is dry and reddish; from <s>pitta</s> it is coppery like a lotus petal,
with burning and destroying the hairs; from <s>kapha</s> it is white, dense, heavy,
and itchy. One should assign it successively to blood, flesh, and fat.
Both are recognized by color alone; they are difficult to cure, increasingly so with each later tissue.
A <s>śvitra</s> patch that does not have white hairs, is not thick, is not merged with others, is fresh,
and is not produced by burning with fire is curable; otherwise it should be rejected.
Even if recent, when it has arisen on the genitals, palms, soles, or lips, it should be rejected.
Through contact, sharing food, beds, and the like, diseases generally become transmissible.
All are communicable, especially disorders of the eyes and skin.
Worms are said to be of two kinds, according to the distinction between external and internal.
Because they are born from external dirt, <s>kapha</s>, blood, and feces, they are fourfold.
By name they are twentyfold; among them, the external ones are born from uncleanness.
They are the size, shape, and color of sesame seeds and live in the hair and garments.
They have many feet and are minute; by name they are <s>yūkā</s> and <s>likṣā</s>.
These two kinds produce urticarial patches, pustules, itching, and nodules.
The internal ones have the same causes as <s>kuṣṭha</s>; among them the <s>śleṣma</s>-born especially arise from
sweet foods, molasses, milk, curds, roasted grain flour, and freshly cooked rice.
Those born from feces arise from much feces, grains, leafy vegetables, <s>olaka</s>, and the like.

children.text: kaphād āmāśaye jātā vṛddhāḥ sarpanti sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: Born from <s>kapha</s> in the stomach, when they have increased they crawl everywhere.
Some are broad and like <s>bradhna</s> worms; some resemble earthworms.
Some have the shape of sprouting grain, and some are thin, long, and minute.

children.text: śvetās tāmrāvabhāsāśca nāmataḥ saptadhā tu te ||
children.translated_text: They are white and coppery in appearance; by name they are sevenfold.
They are <s>antrāda</s>, <s>udarāveṣṭa</s>, <s>hṛdayāda</s>, and <s>mahākuha</s>,

children.text: kuravo darbhakusumāḥ sugandhās te ca kurvate ||
children.translated_text: <s>kurava</s>, <s>darbhakusuma</s>, and <s>sugandha</s>; and they cause
nausea, salivation from the mouth, indigestion, and anorexia,
fainting, vomiting, fever, abdominal distension, emaciation, sneezing, and coryza.
The blood-born creatures arise from blood-carrying vessels; they are minute,
footless, round, and coppery, and some are invisible because of their minuteness.
They are <s>keśāda</s>, <s>romavidhvaṃsa</s>, <s>romadvīpa</s>, and <s>udumbara</s>,
six in all, including <s>sahasaurasa</s> and <s>mātara</s>; they have the same action as <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Those arising from feces are produced in the colon and move downward.
When they have increased and turn toward the stomach,
then the belching and exhalation from the mouth follow the smell of feces.
They are broad, round, thin, or stout, and are dusky, yellow, white, or black.
These worms are five by name: <s>kakeruka</s>, <s>makeruka</s>,
<s>sausurāda</s>, those called <s>sulūna</s>, and <s>lelihā</s>; and they produce
looseness of stool, pain, obstruction, emaciation, roughness, and pallor,
horripilation, depression of the digestive fire, and itching of the anus when they emerge.
Now, then, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>vātavyādhi</s> (disorders of <s>vāta</s>),
so said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
<s>Pavana</s>, whether unvitiated or vitiated, is the single cause of benefit and harm
for this whole world, and especially for the body.
He is <s>Viśvakarman</s>, the soul of the universe, having every form, <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: sraṣṭā dhātā vibhur viṣṇuḥ saṃhartā mṛtyurantakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: creator, establisher, sovereign, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, destroyer, death, and end-maker.
Therefore one should always strive carefully to keep it unvitiated.
Its natural and pathological actions were already stated in the knowledge of the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: samāsād vyāsato doṣabhedīye nāma dhāma ca
children.translated_text: In brief, and in detail in the chapter on distinctions of <s>doṣa</s>, its names and seats were stated,
as well as its fivefold course and activity in each case; here its pathological state
is described by division, together with its causes and symptoms.
<s>Vāyu</s> is provoked by excessive use of things that deplete the bodily tissues.

children.text: caran srotaḥsu rikteṣu bhṛśaṃ tānyeva pūrayan
children.translated_text: Moving in empty channels, it strongly fills those very channels.
Or, being powerful, it becomes obstructed after encountering channels filled by other <s>doṣas</s>.
There, when angered in the colon, it causes pain, abdominal distension, and gurgling of the intestines,
obstruction of feces, urinary stone, <s>vardhma</s> swelling, hemorrhoids, and gripping pain of the sacrum, back, and waist.

children.text: karotyadharakāye ca tāṃs tān kṛcchrān upadravān
children.translated_text: It also produces various difficult complications in the lower part of the body.
When it is in the stomach, it causes thirst, vomiting, dyspnea, cough, and <s>viṣūcikā</s>.

children.text: kaṇṭhoparodham udgārān vyādhīn ūrdhvaṃ ca nābhitaḥ
children.translated_text: It causes obstruction of the throat, eructations, and diseases above the navel,
and in the ears and other sense-organs, destruction of the senses; in the skin, cracking and dryness.

children.text: rakte tīvrā rujaḥ svāpaṃ tāpaṃ rāgaṃ vivarṇatām
children.translated_text: In the blood it causes severe pains, numbness, heat, redness, and discoloration;
ulcers, obstruction of food, distaste, emaciation, and dizziness.
When lodged in flesh and fat, it causes nodules full of piercing pain, hard in texture, as well as fatigue,
heaviness of the limbs, excessive pain, stiffness, and a sensation like being struck by fists and clubs.
When situated in bone, it causes severe pain in the thighs, joints, and bones, and loss of strength;
when in marrow, hollowness in the bones, sleeplessness, and continuous pain.

children.text: śukrasya śīghram utsargaṃ saṅgaṃ vikṛtim eva vā
children.translated_text: When in semen, it causes rapid discharge of semen, obstruction, or else deformity;
and similarly of the fetus; when situated in the vessels, it causes distension and emptiness.
Located there, or situated in the sinews, it produces sciatica, extension-spasm, and hunching;
and <s>anila</s> in the joints produces swelling with the touch of a skin-bag filled with air.
It causes painful activity in extension and contraction.
When occupying the whole body, it causes pricking, splitting pain, throbbing, and breaking pain,
stiffening, convulsions, numbness, contraction of the joints, and trembling.

children.text: yadā tu dhamanīḥ sarvāḥ kruddho 'bhyeti muhur muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when, being enraged, it repeatedly invades all the arteries,
then it throws the limbs into spasms; this disease is remembered as <s>ākṣepaka</s>.

children.text: adhaḥ pratihato vāyur vrajann ūrdhvaṃ hṛdāśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>vāyu</s>, obstructed downward, moves upward and enters

children.text: nāḍīḥ praviśya hṛdayaṃ śiraḥ śaṅkhau ca pīḍayan
children.translated_text: the channels based in the heart, afflicting the heart, head, and temples,
it throws the whole body into spasms and bends it like a bow.
Then the patient breathes with difficulty, is stiff, and has loosened, half-closed eyes;
he coos like a pigeon and is unconscious: that is <s>apatantraka</s>.

children.text: sa eva cāpatānākhyo mukte tu marutā hṛdi
children.translated_text: The very same is called <s>apatāna</s>; when <s>marut</s> is released in the heart,
he repeatedly attains health, and again ill-health when it is obstructed.
Arising from miscarriage, arising from excessive bleeding,
or arising from injury, it is indeed the most difficult of all to cure.
When <s>vāta</s>, stiffening the neck-tendons and blocking the arteries,
spreads through the whole body, then the clavicular region is stretched.

children.text: antar dhanurivāṅgaṃ ca vegaiḥ stambhaṃ ca netrayoḥ
children.translated_text: It bends the body inward like a bow during attacks and produces rigidity of the eyes,
yawning, gnashing of the teeth, and vomiting of <s>kapha</s>.
It causes pain in the flanks and seizure of speech, jaw, back, and head.
This is <s>antarāyāma</s>; <s>bāhyāyāma</s> is of the same kind.
Because of outward bending of the body, the head is drawn backward;
the chest is thrust upward there, and the neck is pressed down.
There is discoloration in the teeth and mouth, sweating, and looseness of the limbs.

children.text: bāhyāyāmaṃ dhanuḥṣkambhaṃ bruvate veginaṃ ca tam ||
children.translated_text: They call this rapid <s>bāhyāyāma</s> <s>dhanuḥṣkambha</s>.
When the <s>doṣas</s>, impelled by the provocation of <s>samīraṇa</s>, reach a wound located in a vital spot,

children.text: vyāyacchanti tanuṃ doṣāḥ sarvām ā pādamastakam ||
children.translated_text: they stretch the whole body from feet to head.
This <s>vraṇāyāma</s>, in a thirsty patient with a pale body, is to be rejected.

children.text: gate vege bhavet svāsthyaṃ sarveṣvākṣepakeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: In all forms of <s>ākṣepaka</s>, health returns when the attack has passed.
From excessive scraping of the tongue, eating dry foods, or injury,
aggravated <s>anila</s>, situated at the root of the jaws, dislocates the jaws
and produces an open-mouthed state, or else a closed-mouthed state.
By that there is <s>hanusraṃsa</s>, with difficulty in chewing and speaking.
Situated in the speech-carrying vessels, <s>anila</s> stiffens the tongue;
that is <s>jihvāstambha</s>, through which there is inability in regard to food, drink, and speech.
From carrying weight on the head, excessive laughing and speaking,
fright, facial strain, sneezing, and drawing a harsh bow,
from an uneven pillow and from chewing hard things,

children.text: vāyur vivṛddhas tais taiśca vātalairūrdhvam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>vāyu</s>, increased by those and by various other <s>vāta</s>-provoking factors, takes an upward course.
It makes one half of the face crooked in speech, laughter, and looking;
then his head trembles, speech is obstructed, and the eyes are stiff.
There is shaking of the teeth, loss of voice, loss of hearing, and obstruction of sneezing;

children.text: gandhājñānaṃ smṛter mohas trāsaḥ suptasya jāyate ||
children.translated_text: ignorance of smells, confusion of memory, and terror in sleep arise.
Spittle goes to one side, and one eye closes;
above the clavicle there is severe pain, or also in the lower half of the body.
Some call this <s>ardita</s>; others call it <s>ekāyāma</s>.

children.text: raktam āśritya pavanaḥ kuryān mūrdhadharāḥ sirāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>pavana</s>, taking support in the blood, affects the veins that support the head,

children.text: rūkṣāḥ savedanāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ so 'sādhyaḥ syāt sirāgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: they become dry, painful, and black; that incurable condition is <s>sirāgraha</s>.

children.text: gṛhītvārdhaṃ tanor vāyuḥ sirāḥ snāyūr viśoṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: When <s>vāyu</s> seizes half of the body and dries up the vessels and sinews,
it disables one or the other side, loosening the bonds of the joints.
One complete half of his body becomes inactive and insensible.

children.text: ekāṅgarogaṃ taṃ kecid anye pakṣavadhaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Some know this as <s>ekāṅgaroga</s>; others know it as <s>pakṣavadha</s>.
In the same way, when <s>anila</s> is lodged in the whole body, it is <s>sarvāṅgaroga</s>.
A side struck by pure <s>vāta</s> is considered most difficult to cure;
when mixed with another <s>doṣa</s>, it is difficult, and if caused by wasting it should be rejected.
When its channels are blocked by <s>āma</s>, and it is associated with <s>kapha</s>, <s>marut</s> stiffens the body
and produces <s>daṇḍaka</s>, rigid like a staff, incurable, and with all activity destroyed.
<s>vāyu</s>, situated at the root of the shoulder, contracts the vessels that go there
and produces <s>avabāhuka</s>, which removes the arm's power of movement.
The tendon that runs from the back of the arm toward the palms of the fingers,
and removes the arm's activity, is remembered by the name <s>viśvācī</s>.

children.text: vāyuḥ kaṭyāṃ sthitaḥ sakthnaḥ kaṇḍarām ākṣiped yadā
children.translated_text: When <s>vāyu</s>, situated in the waist, throws the tendon of the leg into spasm,

children.text: tadā khañjo bhavej jantuḥ paṅguḥ sakthnor dvayorapi ||
children.translated_text: then the person becomes lame; if it affects both legs, he is <s>paṅgu</s>.

children.text: kampate gamanārambhe khañjann iva ca yāti yaḥ
children.translated_text: One who trembles when beginning to walk and goes as though limping,
should be known as having <s>kalāyakhañja</s>, with the bindings of the joints loosened.
When cold, hot, liquid, drying, heavy, and oily things have been consumed,
whether after digestion or before digestion, and likewise through exertion, agitation, sleep, and wakefulness,
when <s>āma</s> (undigested morbid matter), together with <s>śleṣman</s>, fat, and <s>pavana</s>, has accumulated excessively
and, overpowering the other <s>doṣa</s>, reaches the thighs,
then, filling the thigh bones within with inactive <s>śleṣman</s>,
it props up the thighs; thereby they become stiff, cold, and without sensation.
They feel as though belonging to someone else, heavy and afflicted with very severe pain,
and are accompanied by brooding, aching of the limbs, rigidity, stupor, vomiting, loss of taste, and fever,
together with sinking of the feet, difficulty in lifting them, and numbness.
This they call <s>ūrustambha</s>; others call it <s>āḍhyavāta</s>.
A swelling born of <s>vāta</s> and blood, situated in the knee-joint and very painful,
should be known as <s>kroṣṭukaśīrṣa</s>; it is large, like the head of a jackal.

children.text: ruk pāde viṣamanyaste śramād vā jāyate yadā
children.translated_text: When pain arises in the foot from stepping unevenly, or from fatigue,

children.text: vātena gulpham āśritya tam āhur vātakaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: through <s>vāta</s> taking hold of the ankle, they call that <s>vātakaṇṭaka</s>.
The tendon extending from the heel toward the toes, when afflicted by <s>māruta</s>,
prevents the lifting of the thigh; that they call <s>gṛdhrasī</s>.
<s>Viśvācī</s> and <s>gṛdhrasī</s> have been described; <s>khalli</s> is present when there is intense pain.

children.text: hṛṣyete caraṇau yasya bhavetāṃ ca prasuptavat ||
children.translated_text: When a person's feet tingle and become as though numb,
that should be recognized as <s>pādaharṣa</s>, arising from the aggravation of <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s>.
<s>Anila</s>, joined with <s>pitta</s> and blood, causes burning in the feet,
especially when walking; one should designate that as <s>pādadāha</s>.
Now then, we shall explain the causes and diagnosis of <s>vātaśoṇita</s>.
So indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
For those who partake of food that is burning, incompatible, and of the various kinds that vitiate the blood,
and who improperly practice sleep, wakefulness, and sexual intercourse,
especially for delicate people who are not accustomed to walking,
when the blood of men has been vitiated by injury and by lack of purification,

children.text: vātalaiḥ śītalair vāyur vṛddhaḥ kruddho vimārgagaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>vāyu</s>, increased by things that aggravate <s>vāta</s> and by cold things, becomes enraged and moves on a wrong path.

children.text: tādṛśaivāsṛjā ruddhaḥ prāk tad eva pradūṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Obstructed by blood of that same kind, it first vitiates that very blood.
They call it, by various names, <s>āḍhyaroga</s>, <s>khuḍa</s>, <s>vātabalāsa</s>, and <s>vātaśoṇita</s>.

children.text: tad āhur nāmabhis tacca pūrvaṃ pādau pradhāvati ||
children.translated_text: It first rushes to the feet.

children.text: viśeṣād yānayānād yaiḥ pralambau tasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Especially through travelling by vehicles and the like, the feet hang down; its impending symptoms are
like those of impending <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and also lassitude and looseness of the limbs.
In the joints of the knees, shanks, thighs, waist, shoulders, hands, feet, and limbs
there are itching, twitching, pricking pain, splitting pain, heaviness, and numbness.
These arise and then disappear, and again repeatedly manifest.
Taking its base at the roots of the feet, and sometimes of the hands as well,

children.text: ākhoriva viṣaṃ kruddhaṃ kṛtsnaṃ dehaṃ vidhāvati
children.translated_text: the enraged condition runs through the whole body like the poison of a rat.

children.text: tvaṅmāṃsāśrayam uttānaṃ tat pūrvaṃ jāyate tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At first it arises superficially, lodged in the skin and flesh.
Then, after some time, it becomes deep and attacks all the bodily tissues.
In the superficial form, accompanied by itching and the other symptoms, the skin is coppery, dusky, or red,
with stretching, severe burning, and heat; in the deep form there is greater preceding pain.
The swelling is knotty and suppurating; <s>vāyu</s>, in the joints, bones, and marrow,
moves within as though cutting, and with force bends them crooked.

children.text: karoti khañjaṃ paṅguṃ vā śarīre sarvataścaran ||
children.translated_text: Moving throughout the body, it makes a person lame or crippled.
When <s>vāta</s> is predominant there are especially severe colic-like pain, twitching, and pricking.
The swelling is dry, blackish, or dusky, and it increases and diminishes.
There is contraction of the arteries, fingers, and joints, rigidity of the limbs, and excessive pain.
There are aversion to cold, no relief from cold applications, stiffness, trembling, and numbness.
When blood is predominant, the swelling is extremely painful, pricking, copper-colored, and tingling.
It is not relieved by either unctuous or dry measures and is accompanied by itching and moisture.

children.text: pitte vidāhaḥ saṃmohaḥ svedo mūrchā madaḥ satṛṭ
children.translated_text: When <s>pitta</s> is predominant there are burning, confusion, sweating, fainting, intoxication-like disturbance, and thirst.

children.text: sparśākṣamatvaṃ rug rāgaḥ śophaḥ pāko bhṛśoṣmatā ||
children.translated_text: There are inability to bear touch, pain, redness, swelling, suppuration, and very great heat.
When <s>kapha</s> is predominant there are rigidity, heaviness, numbness, oiliness, and coldness.

children.text: kaṇḍūr mandā ca rug dvandvasarvaliṅgaṃ ca saṃkare ||
children.translated_text: There is itching and mild pain; when there is combination, there are the signs of two <s>doṣas</s> or of all.
A new case following one <s>doṣa</s> is curable; one born of two <s>doṣas</s> is manageable.

children.text: tridoṣajaṃ tyajet srāvi stabdham arbudakāri ca ||
children.translated_text: One should abandon a three-<s>doṣa</s> case, and one that is discharging, stiff, or producing tumors.
When <s>māruta</s> quickly blocks the path of the blood
and lodges in the branches and joints, the two obstruct one another and, through pains, take away life.
Among the fivefold <s>vāyu</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, aggravated by dryness, exercise, fasting,
overeating, injury, travel, and by the forcing or suppression of urges,
brings about damage to the eyes and other sense organs,
and many diseases such as coryza, facial paralysis, thirst, cough, and dyspnea.
<s>Udāna</s>, deranged by suppressing sneezing, belching, vomiting, and sleep,
and by heavy loads, excessive crying, laughing, and the like, causes diseases:
obstruction of the throat, derangement of the mind, vomiting, anorexia, and coryza,
and also goiter and others, each of them lodged above the clavicles.
<s>Vyāna</s>, vitiated by excessive walking, brooding, play, irregular movements,
incompatible and dry things, fear, joy, grief, and the like,
causes loss of virility, enthusiasm, and strength, swelling, mental agitation, and fever,
diseases of the whole body, pricking pains, horripilation, and numbness of the limbs.

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ visarpam anyāṃśca kuryāt sarvāṅgagān gadān
children.translated_text: It causes <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>visarpa</s>, and other diseases that spread through the whole body.
<s>Samāna</s>, vitiated by irregular, undigested, cold, and mixed foods,
and also by sleeping and waking at improper times and the like,
causes colic, abdominal tumors, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and other diseases born in the large and small intestines.
<s>Apāna</s>, provoked by dry and heavy food, suppression of urges, excessive riding and travelling,
and by overuse of vehicles, mounts, sitting, standing, and walking,
causes difficult diseases located in the colon,
and many disorders such as vitiation of urine and semen, hemorrhoids, and prolapse of the rectum.
One should know every condition of <s>māruta</s> (vāta), when associated with <s>āma</s>, by drowsiness, rigidity, and heaviness,
by unctuousness, anorexia, lassitude, coldness, swelling, and impairment of digestive fire,
by desire for pungent and dry things, and by relief from treatment of that sort.

children.text: yuktaṃ vidyān nirāmaṃ tu tandrādīnāṃ viparyayāt ||
children.translated_text: But one should know it to be free from <s>āma</s> from the opposite of drowsiness and the rest.
Therefore the obstruction of <s>vāyu</s>, with its many varieties, will now be explained.

children.text: liṅgaṃ pittāvṛte dāhas tṛṣṇā śūlaṃ bhramas tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is obstructed by <s>pitta</s>, the signs are burning, thirst, pain, dizziness, and darkness before the eyes.
Pungent, hot, sour, and salty things cause burning, and there is desire for cold.
When it is obstructed by <s>kapha</s>, there are coldness, heaviness, and pain, with marked relief from pungent and similar measures,
and there is desire for fasting, exertion, dry things, and hot things.
When it is obstructed by blood, there is severe burning pain arising between the skin and flesh.

children.text: bhavecca rāgī śvayathur jāyante maṇḍalāni ca
children.translated_text: There is reddish swelling, and circular patches also arise.

children.text: māṃsena kaṭhinaḥ śopho vivarṇaḥ piṭikās tathā ||
children.translated_text: When obstructed by flesh, the swelling is hard and discolored, and pustules likewise appear.

children.text: harṣaḥ pipīlikānāṃ ca saṃcāra iva jāyate
children.translated_text: Horripilation arises, as though ants were moving about.

children.text: calaḥ snigdho mṛduḥ śītaḥ śopho gātreṣvarocakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A mobile, unctuous, soft, cold swelling appears in the limbs, with anorexia.

children.text: āḍhyavāta iti jñeyaḥ sa kṛcchro medasāvṛte
children.translated_text: When obstructed by fat, it should be known as <s>āḍhyavāta</s>, and it is difficult to cure.
When obstructed by bone, the patient welcomes very hot touch and pressure.
The limb is pierced as if by a needle, sinks down, and is afflicted with pain.
When obstructed by marrow, there is bending, yawning, twisting around,

children.text: śūlaṃ ca pīḍyamānena pāṇibhyāṃ labhate sukham
children.translated_text: and pain; when pressed with the hands, the patient obtains comfort.

children.text: śukrāvṛte 'tivego vā na vā niṣphalatāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: When obstructed by semen, there is either excessive urge, no urge, or even fruitlessness.
When wind is obstructed by food, pain arises in the abdomen after eating and subsides when the food is digested.
When obstructed by urine, there is non-passage of urine and distension of the bladder.
When obstructed by feces, there is constipation, and it cuts below in its own place.

children.text: vrajatyāśu jarāṃ sneho bhukte cānahyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unctuous substance quickly undergoes digestion, and after eating the person becomes distended.

children.text: śakṛt pīḍitam annena duḥkhaṃ śuṣkaṃ cirāt sṛjet
children.translated_text: Pressed by the food, he passes feces painfully, dry, and only after a long time.
When <s>vāyu</s> is obstructed by all the bodily tissues, there is pain in the hips, groins, and back.
The wind moves contrary to its course, and the heart is greatly distressed and unwell.

children.text: bhramo mūrchā rujā dāhaḥ pittena prāṇa āvṛte ||
children.translated_text: When <s>prāṇa</s> is obstructed by <s>pitta</s>, there are dizziness, fainting, pain, and burning.
When food is acidly digested there is vomiting; in <s>udāna</s> too there are dizziness and the like.
There is internal burning and loss of vigor; and when <s>vyāna</s> is obstructed, burning is spread everywhere.
There is fatigue and impediment of bodily movement, accompanied by heat and pain.
In <s>samāna</s>, there is impairment of warmth, excessive sweating, aversion, with thirst,

children.text: dāhaśca syād apāne tu male hāridravarṇatā
children.translated_text: and burning; but in <s>apāna</s>, the feces have a turmeric-yellow color.
There is excessive menstrual flow and heat in the vagina, penis, and anus.

children.text: śleṣmaṇā tvāvṛte prāṇe sādas tandrārucir vamiḥ
children.translated_text: But when <s>prāṇa</s> is obstructed by <s>śleṣman</s>, there are lassitude, drowsiness, anorexia, vomiting,
spitting, sneezing, belching, and obstruction of inhalation and exhalation.
In <s>udāna</s>, there is heaviness of the body, anorexia, and obstruction of speech and voice.
There is also loss of strength and complexion; in <s>vyāna</s>, there is stiffness of joints, bones, and speech.

children.text: gurutāṅgeṣu sarveṣu skhalitaṃ ca gatau bhṛśam
children.translated_text: There is heaviness in all the limbs and severe stumbling in gait.
In <s>samāna</s>, the limbs become excessively cold, sweating is absent, and digestive fire is weak.
In <s>apāna</s>, urine and feces are passed together with <s>kapha</s>.
Thus they know the obstruction of <s>vāyu</s> to be of twenty-two kinds.
<s>Prāṇa</s> and the others also obstruct one another in due order.

children.text: sarve 'pi viṃśatividhaṃ vidyād āvaraṇaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: All of that obstruction too should be known as twentyfold.
There is obstruction of inhalation and exhalation, coryza, and stiffness of the head
as well as heart disease and dryness of the mouth, when <s>udāna</s> is obstructed by <s>prāṇa</s>.
When <s>prāṇa</s> is obstructed by <s>udāna</s>, there is wasting of complexion, <s>ojas</s>, and strength.

children.text: diśānayā ca vibhajet sarvam āvaraṇaṃ bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: In this manner the physician should divide all cases of obstruction,

children.text: sthānānyavekṣya vātānāṃ vṛddhiṃ hāniṃ ca karmaṇām
children.translated_text: considering the seats of the <s>vātas</s> and the increase or decrease of their actions.

children.text: prāṇādīnāṃ ca pañcānāṃ miśram āvaraṇaṃ mithaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is mutual mixed obstruction among the five beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>,
and among the mixed conditions of the twelve beginning with <s>pitta</s>, together with those that are themselves mixed.
Likewise, by mixed <s>pitta</s> and the rest and by combinations in many ways,
because of gradations and alternatives, obstruction becomes innumerable.
The attentive physician should identify it by the manifestation of each one's proper symptoms,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiścopaśayād gūḍhām api muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: and, again and again, by gradual relief from suitable treatment, even when it is hidden.

children.text: viśeṣāj jīvitaṃ prāṇa udāno balam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: In particular, life is <s>prāṇa</s>, and <s>udāna</s> is called strength.
From the affliction of those two there is loss of life span and of strength.

children.text: āvṛtā vāyavo 'jñātā jñātā vā vatsaraṃ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Obstructed <s>vāyus</s>, whether unrecognized, or recognized but present for a year,
become difficult to cure even with effort, or are not to be treated.
Abscess, splenic disease, heart disease, abdominal tumor, depression of digestive fire, and the like
arise as complications from neglecting those obstructed <s>vāyus</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of fever.
So said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.

children.text: āmāśayastho hatvāgniṃ sāmo mārgān pidhāya yat
children.translated_text: Since the <s>doṣa</s> associated with <s>āma</s>, located in the stomach, destroys the digestive fire

children.text: vidadhāti jvaraṃ doṣas tasmāt kurvīta laṅghanam ||
children.translated_text: and blocks the channels, producing fever, therefore one should carry out fasting.

children.text: prāgrūpeṣu jvarādau vā balaṃ yatnena pālayan
children.translated_text: In the prodromal signs or at the beginning of fever, one should carefully preserve strength,
for health is founded on strength, and the therapeutic procedure is for the sake of health.

children.text: laṅghanaiḥ kṣapite doṣe dīpte 'gnau lāghave sati
children.translated_text: When the <s>doṣa</s> has been reduced by fasting, the digestive fire is kindled, and lightness is present,

children.text: svāsthyaṃ kṣut tṛḍ ruciḥ paktir balam ojaśca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: health, hunger, thirst, relish, digestion, strength, and <s>ojas</s> arise.
When the impurity is excessive, stirred up, predominantly <s>kapha</s>, and moving,
with nausea, salivation, aversion to food, cough, and <s>viṣūcikā</s>,
when fever associated with <s>āma</s> has arisen, especially in one who has just eaten,

children.text: vamanaṃ vamanārhasya śastaṃ kuryāt tad anyathā ||
children.translated_text: emesis is recommended for one fit for emesis; otherwise it should have the opposite effect.
For dyspnea, diarrhea, stupefaction, heart disease, and irregular fevers,

children.text: pippalībhir yutān gālān kaliṅgair madhukena vā ||
children.translated_text: one should drink boluses mixed with <s>pippalī</s>, or with <s>kaliṅga</s>, or with licorice,
with warm water containing honey, or else with salt,
or with water prepared from leaves of <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>karkoṭa</s>, and <s>vetra</s>.
Or he should employ the emetics prescribed in the <s>Kalpa</s> section, with <s>tarpaṇa</s>, sugarcane juice, or wines,
knowing the distinctions of strength and season.

children.text: kṛte 'kṛte vā vamane jvarī kuryād viśoṣaṇam
children.translated_text: After emesis has been done, or even when it has not been done, a fever patient should undertake drying treatment,
for the digestion and pacification of the <s>doṣas</s> that have risen up.
When food is covered by a <s>doṣa</s>, as fire is by ashes, it is not digested;
therefore fever patients should be made to fast until the <s>doṣas</s> are digested.
When thirsty, in fever arising from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, one should drink warm water little by little;

children.text: tat kaphaṃ vilayaṃ nītvā tṛṣṇām āśu nivartayet ||
children.translated_text: it brings <s>kapha</s> to dissolution and quickly stops thirst.
And by kindling the digestive fire and softening the channels, it purifies them;
it brings about the downward movement of latent <s>pitta</s>, <s>vāta</s>, sweat, feces, and urine.
It removes sleepiness, dullness, and anorexia, and is a support for the vital breaths;
cold water, being opposite to this, increases the aggregation of the <s>doṣas</s>.
Although warm water has such qualities, one should not use it in a condition wholly dominated by <s>pitta</s>,
when <s>pitta</s> is excessive, with scorching pain, burning, confusion, and diarrhea,
in fever arising from poison or wine, in summer, in one wounded or wasted, or in one with bleeding disorder.
For them, water boiled with <s>ghana</s>, sandalwood, dry ginger, <s>parpaṭa</s>, and <s>uśīra</s>,

children.text: śītaṃ tebhyo hitaṃ toyaṃ pācanaṃ tṛḍjvarāpaham
children.translated_text: then cooled, is beneficial; it digests and removes thirst and fever.

children.text: ūṣmā pittād ṛte nāsti jvaro nāstyūṣmaṇā vinā ||
children.translated_text: There is no heat apart from <s>pitta</s>, and no fever without heat;
therefore, when <s>pitta</s> is predominant, one should especially avoid what is unsuitable for <s>pitta</s>,
such as bathing, massage, anointing applications, and the remaining forms of lightening treatment.

children.text: ajīrṇa iva śūlaghnaṃ sāme tīvraruji jvare
children.translated_text: As in indigestion, in a fever with <s>āma</s> and severe pain one should not drink medicine that removes colic,

children.text: na pibed auṣadhaṃ taddhi bhūya evāmam āvahet ||
children.translated_text: for that would bring on still more <s>āma</s>.
For one whose digestive tract is overwhelmed by <s>āma</s>, milk is like the venom of a snake.
In a fever with urticaria, coryza, dyspnea, and pain in the shanks, joints, and bones,
when it is of <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> nature, sweating is recommended; it sets in motion
sweat, urine, feces, and flatus, and makes the digestive fire sharp.
One should follow in every respect the regimen of conduct taught for oleation.

children.text: laṅghanaṃ svedanaṃ kālo yavāgvas tiktako rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fasting, sweating, time, gruel, and bitter taste

children.text: malānāṃ pācanāni syur yathāvasthaṃ krameṇa vā
children.translated_text: are means for digesting the impurities, according to the condition or in sequence.
In fevers from pure <s>vāta</s>, wasting, external causes, and chronicity, fasting

children.text: neṣyate teṣu hi hitaṃ śamanaṃ yan na karśanam
children.translated_text: is not desired; for in these, a pacifying treatment that does not emaciate is beneficial.
There one should know, from the features of fever with <s>āma</s>, that drying has not yet been accomplished,
and in fasting one should consider the knowledge of the two kinds of therapeutic procedure.
But when proper fasting is indicated by its signs, one should treat him with thin gruels,
prepared with the appropriate medicines for each case, beginning with <s>maṇḍa</s>.

children.text: ṣaḍahaṃ vā mṛdutvaṃ vā jvaro yāvad avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: This should be done for six days, or until the fever attains mildness.
His digestive fire is kindled by them as fire is by fuel sticks.
At first he should drink easily digested parched-grain gruel with dry ginger, coriander, and <s>pippalī</s>;
with rock salt, and, if he wants sourness, with pomegranate.
One whose stool is loose, or who has much <s>pitta</s>, should take it cold, with dry ginger and honey.
One with pain in the bladder, flank, or head should take one prepared with <s>vyāghrī</s> and <s>gokṣura</s>.
With <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, blue lotus, and coriander,
it is a sour thin gruel for fever with diarrhea, stimulating digestion and digesting morbid matter.
With the lesser five roots, it is for those with hiccup, pain, dyspnea, and cough;
with the greater five roots, for one afflicted by <s>kapha</s>, cooked with barley.
One whose stool is obstructed should take one made with barley, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>āmalaka</s>;
a gruel fried in ghee, promoting the downward movement of feces and <s>doṣas</s>.
With <s>cavikā</s>, <s>pippalī</s>-root, grapes, <s>āmalaka</s>, and dry ginger,

children.text: koṣṭhe vibaddhe saruji pibet tu parikartini
children.translated_text: when the bowel is obstructed, painful, and cutting, he should drink it.
He should take one made with <s>kola</s>, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, <s>kalaśī</s>, <s>dhāvanī</s>, and <s>śrīphala</s>.
One without sweating or sleep and afflicted by thirst should take one with sugar, <s>āmalaka</s>, and dry ginger;
with sugar, jujube, raisins, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>musta</s>, and sandalwood,
combined with honey, it destroys thirst, vomiting, burning distress, and fever.
One should also make meat broths, pulse soups, and the like with these same gruel-medicines.
In fever arising from wine, in one habituated to wine, and when <s>kapha</s> has entered the seat of <s>pitta</s>,
in summer, or when those two are excessive, and in one afflicted by thirst, vomiting, and burning,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ pravṛtte rakte ca peyāṃ necchanti teṣu tu
children.translated_text: and when blood flows upward, they do not recommend thin gruel in these cases.
Instead he should drink parched-grain <s>tarpaṇa</s> with fever-removing fruit juices or with water,

children.text: pibet saśarkarākṣaudrān tato jīrṇe tu tarpaṇe
children.translated_text: mixed with sugar and honey; then, when the <s>tarpaṇa</s> has been digested,
if hungry, he should eat gruel or cooked rice made from roasted grains,
with watery, lightly salted soups, or with broths from green gram, quail, or goat.

children.text: ityayaṃ ṣaḍaho neyo balaṃ doṣaṃ ca rakṣatā ||
children.translated_text: Thus these six days should be guided while protecting strength and the <s>doṣas</s>.
Then, when the <s>doṣas</s> have ripened through fasting and the like, there is recommended
a decoction that digests or pacifies the remaining <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: tiktaḥ pitte viśeṣeṇa prayojyaḥ kaṭukaḥ kaphe
children.translated_text: A bitter one is especially to be used in <s>pitta</s>, and a pungent one in <s>kapha</s>.
Though a decoction removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, it is not praised
in a new fever; because by obstructing the stool a decoction produces irregular fever,
as well as anorexia, nausea, hiccup, abdominal distension, and the like.
Some say medicine should be given after seven days, others after ten days.
Some say it may be applied when light food has been eaten, but not when <s>āma</s> is abundant.
For one overcome by intense fever, when the surge of the <s>doṣas</s> is arising,
or when the <s>doṣa</s> is very accumulated and causing drowsiness and torpor,
medicine that is not being digested inflames the fever still further.

children.text: mṛdur jvaro laghur dehaścalitāśca malā yadā ||
children.translated_text: When the fever is mild, the body light, and the impurities have moved,
then medicine should be used even for one whose fever is recent.

children.text: mustayā parpaṭaṃ yuktaṃ śuṇṭhyā duḥsparśayāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: One should prepare <s>parpaṭa</s> combined with <s>mustā</s>, or else with <s>śuṇṭhī</s> and <s>duḥsparśā</s>.
Or one should drink <s>pāṭhā</s> and <s>uśīra</s> together with <s>vālaka</s>, cooked as a decoction or made as a cold infusion.
Likewise, one should drink <s>bhūnimba</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>.
These decoctions, which digest the <s>doṣas</s>, are to be applied according to suitability;
they remove fever, anorexia, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, and indigestion.
<s>Kaliṅgaka</s>, the leaf of <s>paṭola</s>, and <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>;
<s>Paṭola</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>;
<s>Paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>mṛdvīkā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and <s>vatsaka</s>;
<s>kirātatiktā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>candana</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>;
<s>Dhātrī</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and honey: these are the endings of the half-verses.
These five are considered pacifying for the five fevers beginning with continuous fever.
In fever caused by <s>vāta</s>, use <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>;
or else <s>pippalī</s> root, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>.

children.text: kanīyaḥ pañcamūlaṃ ca pitte śakrayavā ghanam ||
children.translated_text: In fever caused by <s>pitta</s>, use the lesser <s>pañcamūla</s>, <s>śakrayava</s>, and <s>ghana</s>;
also <s>kaṭukā</s>, with honey; likewise <s>mustā</s> and <s>parpaṭaka</s>,
with <s>dhanvayāsa</s> and <s>bhūnimba</s>. In fever caused by <s>kapha</s>, use the group beginning with <s>vatsaka</s>,
or else <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>gāṅgeyī</s>, <s>śṛṅgavera</s>, and <s>durālabhā</s>.
When pain, obstruction of stool, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s> are combined, one should use medicine that kindles and digests:
<s>abhayā</s>, <s>pippalī</s> root, <s>śamyāka</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and <s>ghana</s>.
<s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and <s>śārivā</s>;
<s>mustā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>hrīvera</s>, <s>padmakesara</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>;
<s>mṛṇāla</s>, <s>candana</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>nīlotpala</s>, and <s>parūṣaka</s>.
An infusion, or a cold infusion, from the group beginning with <s>drākṣā</s>, scented with jasmine flowers,
combined with honey, sugar, and parched grain, conquers fever born of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: jvaraṃ madātyayaṃ chardiṃ mūrchāṃ dāhaṃ śramaṃ bhramam
children.translated_text: intoxication from drink, vomiting, fainting, burning, fatigue, and dizziness,

children.text: ūrdhvagaṃ raktapittaṃ ca pipāsāṃ kāmalām api ||
children.translated_text: upward-moving <s>raktapitta</s>, thirst, and jaundice as well.
Having ground <s>kaṭukā</s>, one should cook it in a new, clean potsherd;
its juice, squeezed out and mixed with ghee, conquers fever and burning.
In <s>kapha-vāta</s>, use <s>vacā</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, and <s>vatsaka</s>;
or a decoction made from <s>chinnodbhava</s>, combined with powder of <s>pippalī</s>.
A decoction of <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>, combined with powder of <s>pippalī</s>,
conquers fever of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, dyspnea, cough, coryza, and colic.
<s>Pathyā</s>, <s>kustumburī</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>kaṭtṛṇa</s>, and <s>parpaṭa</s>,
with <s>kaṭphala</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, and <s>devāhva</s>, together with honey and <s>hiṅgu</s>,
restrains fever of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, expectoration, and pains in the belly, heart, and sides,
as well as throat diseases, swelling of the mouth, cough, and dyspnea.
The group beginning with <s>āragvadha</s>, together with honey, conquers fever of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
so too do <s>tiktā</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>.
<s>Paṭola</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>dhanvayavāsa</s>, and <s>vāsaka</s>;
in fever involving all three <s>doṣas</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, <s>niśā</s>, and <s>ghana</s>;
together with <s>paṭola</s> leaves, <s>nimba</s> bark, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>kaṭukā</s>;
<s>nāgara</s>, <s>pauṣkara</s> root, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>
when there is cough, dyspnea, and pain in the side in fever dominated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
<s>Madhūka</s> flowers, <s>mṛdvīkā</s>, <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
with <s>uśīra</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>kāśmarya</s>, should be prepared as a cold infusion.

children.text: kaṣāyaṃ taṃ piban kāle jvarān sarvān apohati ||
children.translated_text: Drinking that decoction at the proper time removes all fevers.
Likewise, <s>jātī</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and also <s>dhanvayavāsaka</s>;
when the stool is bound, use <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>drākṣā</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and jaggery.
When the medicine has been digested, one should take food beginning with <s>peyā</s>; but one with <s>śleṣman</s> should not,

children.text: peyā kaphaṃ vardhayati paṅkaṃ pāṃsuṣu vṛṣṭivat ||
children.translated_text: for <s>peyā</s> increases <s>kapha</s> like rain turning dust into mud.
Therefore, for those whose bodies are obstructed by <s>śleṣman</s>, one should prescribe even beforehand
light soups made from <s>kulattha</s>, <s>caṇaka</s>, <s>kalāya</s>, and the like,
dry, accompanied by bitter taste, wholesome to the heart, appetizing, and pungent.

children.text: raktādyāḥ śālayo jīrṇāḥ ṣaṣṭikāśca jvare hitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Old red and other <s>śāli</s> rices, and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, are beneficial in fever.
In fever dominated by <s>śleṣman</s>, barley freed from husk and made into cakes is likewise suitable.

children.text: odanas taiḥ sruto dvis triḥ prayoktavyo yathāyatham ||
children.translated_text: Cooked rice from these, with the water poured off two or three times, should be used as appropriate,
according to the strength of the <s>doṣas</s>, the affected tissues, and the rest, and prepared with fever-removing decoctions.
Soups made with light pulses such as <s>mudga</s>, and with <s>kulattha</s>, remove fever.
With <s>kāravellaka</s>, <s>karkoṭa</s>, young radish, and <s>parpaṭa</s>,
with eggplant, <s>nimba</s> flowers, and fruits and sprouts of <s>paṭola</s>,
and with extremely light meats from dry-land animals, broths are beneficial.
They may be prepared with <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>parūṣa</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, <s>drākṣā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and pomegranate,
seasoned with <s>pippalī</s>, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>dhānya</s>, <s>jīraka</s>, and rock salt,
usually combined with sugar and honey, or prepared with or without them.
Palatable relishes cooked in non-sour buttermilk
and clear drinks endowed with digestive power should also be used as after-drinks.

children.text: tāni kvathitaśītaṃ ca vāri madyaṃ ca sātmyataḥ
children.translated_text: Those, and water that has been boiled and cooled, and wine according to habituation,

children.text: sajvaraṃ jvaramuktaṃ vā dinānte bhojayel laghu ||
children.translated_text: should be given as light food at the end of the day, whether fever is present or gone.
At that time, when <s>śleṣman</s> has diminished and heat has increased, the digestive fire is strong;
or food may be given at the proper time, in conformity with region and habituation.

children.text: prāg alpavahnir bhuñjāno na hyajīrṇena pīḍyate
children.translated_text: Eating earlier, when the digestive fire is weak, one is indeed afflicted by indigestion.
After ten days have thus been passed with fasting, drinking decoctions, and wholesome food,

children.text: sarpir dadyāt kaphe mande vātapittottare jvare
children.translated_text: one should give ghee, when <s>kapha</s> is slight, in fever dominated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
When the <s>doṣas</s> are cooked, it is nectar; otherwise it is like poison.
Even after the tenth day has passed, it may increase the complications of fever.
There one should follow the sequence beginning with fasting until <s>kapha</s> has diminished.
Because of weakness of the body and its tissues, chronic fever continues.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ hi tejo jvarakṛt tejasā rūkṣitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: For the heat that produces fever is dry, and for one dried out by that heat
through emesis, sweating, time, water, decoctions, and light food,

children.text: yaḥ syād atibalo dhātuḥ sahacārī sadāgatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that bodily constituent which is very strong, accompanying the disease and always mobile,
ghee is its pacifier, as water is for a blazing house.
It is foremost among remedies that conquer <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and it adapts to processing.
Therefore one should give it all the more, prepared with the proper medicines for each case.

children.text: viparītaṃ jvaroṣmāṇaṃ jayet pittaṃ ca śaityataḥ ||
children.translated_text: By its coolness it conquers the contrary heat of fever and <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: snehād vātaṃ ghṛtaṃ tulyaṃ yogasaṃskārataḥ kapham
children.translated_text: by its unctuousness it conquers <s>vāta</s>, and, through its particular combination and processing, <s>kapha</s> as well.

children.text: pūrve kaṣāyāḥ saghṛtāḥ sarve yojyā yathāmalam ||
children.translated_text: All the decoctions mentioned before, combined with ghee, should be used according to the individual impurity.
A decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>picumanda</s> bark, <s>madhuka</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants,
and an equal amount of <s>sūradala</s>, taken with ghee, removes fever and cough.
Ghee cooked with <s>pippalī</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>dhāvanī</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>amalaka</s>, and <s>tāmalakī</s>,
with <s>bilva</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>himapāla</s>, <s>nisevya</s>, <s>drākṣā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>sthirā</s>,

children.text: ghṛtam āśu nihanti sādhitaṃ jvaram agniṃ viṣamaṃ halīmakam
children.translated_text: quickly destroys fever, irregular digestive fire, and <s>halīmaka</s>,

children.text: aruciṃ bhṛśatāpam aṃsayor vamathuṃ pārśvaśirorujaṃ kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: as well as loss of appetite, intense burning in the shoulders, vomiting, pain in the sides and head, and wasting.

children.text: tailvakaṃ pavanajanmani jvare yojayet trivṛtayā viyojitam
children.translated_text: In fever born of <s>vāta</s> one should use <s>tailvaka</s> ghee with <s>trivṛt</s> omitted.

children.text: tiktakaṃ vṛṣaghṛtaṃ ca paittike yacca pālanikayā śṛtaṃ haviḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a <s>pitta</s> fever, one should use <s>tiktaka</s>, <s>vṛṣa-ghṛta</s>, and ghee cooked with <s>pālanikā</s>.
With one-pala portions of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, rock salt, <s>cavya</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>agni</s>, sea salt, and barley bristles,

children.text: palāṃśakaiḥ kṣīrasamaṃ ghṛtasya prasthaṃ pacej jīrṇakaphajvaraghnam ||
children.translated_text: one should cook a prastha of ghee with an equal amount of milk; it destroys chronic <s>kapha</s> fever.
Fats prepared with the juice and paste of <s>guḍūcī</s>, or of <s>triphalā</s> or <s>vṛṣa</s>,
or with <s>mṛdvīkā</s> and <s>balā</s>, cut off fever.
When the ghee has been digested, one should eat soft meat broth with rice.

children.text: balaṃ hyalaṃ doṣaharaṃ paraṃ tacca balapradam ||
children.translated_text: For strength is fully capable of removing the <s>doṣas</s>, and that food is supremely strength-giving.
Soups made from <s>mudga</s>, <s>kāravella</s>, and the like remove <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>;

children.text: prāyeṇa tasmān na hitā jīrṇe vātottare jvare ||
children.translated_text: therefore, in general, they are not wholesome in chronic fever when <s>vāta</s> is predominant.
They cause colic, upward movement of wind, and obstruction of stool, and they increase fever.

children.text: na śāmyatyevam api cejjvaraḥ kurvīta śodhanam ||
children.translated_text: If the fever still does not subside even in this way, one should undertake purification.

children.text: śodhanārhasya vamanaṃ prāg uktaṃ tasya yojayet
children.translated_text: For one fit for purification, one should employ the emesis that was prescribed earlier,
when the <s>doṣa</s> is lodged in the stomach and the patient is strong, while preserving his strength.

children.text: pakve tu śithile doṣe jvare vā viṣamadyaje
children.translated_text: But when the <s>doṣa</s> is cooked and loosened, in fever or in one produced by poison or liquor,
one should give a bolus made with <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>kesara</s>,
together with sugar and honey, or else the <s>vyoṣādi</s> purgative.
Likewise one may give the juice of grapes and <s>dhātrī</s>, or <s>harītakī</s> together with grapes,

children.text: āragvadhaṃ vā payasā mṛdvīkānāṃ rasena vā
children.translated_text: or <s>āragvadha</s> with milk or with the juice of raisins.

children.text: triphalāṃ trāyamāṇāṃ vā payasā jvaritaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: The fevered patient may drink <s>triphalā</s> or <s>trāyamāṇā</s> with milk.
For those who have been purged, the transitional diet should proceed in order, beginning with thin gruel.
One should always leave alone fecal matter that is being dislodged and agitated by fever.

children.text: pakvo 'pi hi vikurvīta doṣaḥ koṣṭhe kṛtāspadaḥ
children.translated_text: For even when cooked, a <s>doṣa</s> that has taken residence in the bowel may cause disturbance.
Or, when it is moving too much, one should digest it and bring it to restraint.
The faults in restraining undigested matter have been stated in the treatment of the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: pāyayed doṣaharaṇaṃ mohād āmajvare tu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the man who, out of delusion, gives a <s>doṣa</s>-expelling treatment in fever with <s>āma</s> (undigested morbidity),
touches a sleeping black serpent with the tip of his finger.

children.text: jvarakṣīṇasya na hitaṃ vamanaṃ na virecanam ||
children.translated_text: For one wasted by fever, neither emesis nor purgation is wholesome.

children.text: kāmaṃ tu payasā tasya nirūhair vā haren malān
children.translated_text: However, his fecal matter may be removed with milk or with <s>nirūha</s> enemas.
For one accustomed to milk, whose phlegm is depleted and who has burning and thirst,
milk is wholesome when he is afflicted by <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>, even if he has diarrhea.

children.text: tad vapur laṅghanottaptaṃ pluṣṭaṃ vanam ivāgninā ||
children.translated_text: It revives the body, scorched by fasting and heat, like a forest burned by fire

children.text: divyāmbu jīvayet tasya jvaraṃ cāśu niyacchati
children.translated_text: that is revived by divine rain; and it quickly restrains fever.

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ śītam uṣṇaṃ vā tasmāddhāroṣṇam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: Prepared milk, whether cold or hot, or else milk still warm from the udder,
should be used in divided doses at the proper time; used otherwise, it kills the fevered patient.
Milk with dry ginger, dates, raisins, sugar, and ghee,
boiled, cooled, and mixed with honey, destroys thirst, burning, and fever.
Similarly, one may drink it with <s>drākṣā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>kaṇa</s>, and sandalwood,

children.text: caturguṇenāmbhasā vā pippalyā vā śṛtaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: or boiled with four times as much water, or with <s>pippalī</s>.
By drinking milk boiled with <s>pañcamūlī</s>, the fevered patient is freed
from cough, dyspnea, headache, pain in the side, and chronic fever.
Milk boiled with castor root or with young <s>bilva</s> frees one from fever;
or milk warm from the udder should be drunk by one whose wind and stool are obstructed.
For diarrhea with blood and mucus, with thirst, pain, and dysenteric straining,
milk prepared with dry ginger, <s>balā</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>gokaṇṭaka</s>, and jaggery
conquers swelling, obstruction of urine, feces, and flatus, fever, and cough.
Milk prepared with <s>vṛścīva</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>varṣābhū</s> removes fever and swelling.
Milk prepared with the heartwood of <s>śiṃśipā</s> quickly takes away fever.

children.text: nirūhas tu balaṃ vahniṃ vijvaratvaṃ mudaṃ rucim
children.translated_text: A <s>nirūha</s> enema, properly applied, quickly produces strength, digestive fire, freedom from fever, joy, and appetite,

children.text: doṣe yuktaḥ karotyāśu pakve pakvāśayaṃ gate ||
children.translated_text: when the <s>doṣa</s> is cooked and has gone to the large intestine.

children.text: pittaṃ vā kaphapittaṃ vā pakvāśayagataṃ haret
children.translated_text: It removes <s>pitta</s>, or <s>kapha</s> together with <s>pitta</s>, when lodged in the large intestine.

children.text: sraṃsanaṃ trīn api malān vastiḥ pakvāśayāśrayān ||
children.translated_text: A loosening <s>vasti</s> (enema) removes all three wastes that have their seat in the large intestine.
For one whose <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> are depleted, with stiffness in the sacrum, back, and waist,
whose digestive fire is kindled and whose stool is bound, one should apply an <s>anuvāsana</s> oil enema.
With <s>paṭola</s>, leaves of neem, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s>,
with <s>sthirā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>vālaka</s>,
one should make a decoction in milk and half as much water, boiling it until only the milk remains,
and mix it with pastes of <s>musta</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>vatsaka</s>.
Together with honey and ghee, one should administer this as a <s>vasti</s>; it destroys fever.
One should decoct the four <s>parṇinī</s> plants, <s>yaṣṭīphala</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>nṛpadruma</s>,
and make a paste of <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, the fruit of <s>phalinī</s>,
and <s>musta</s>; this <s>vasti</s>, with jaggery, honey, and ghee, removes fever.

children.text: jīvantīṃ madanaṃ medāṃ pippalīṃ madhukaṃ vacām
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: ṛddhiṃ rāsnāṃ balāṃ bilvaṃ śatapuṣpāṃ śatāvarīm ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,

children.text: piṣṭvā kṣīraṃ jalaṃ sarpis tailaṃ caikatra sādhitam
children.translated_text: and having cooked milk, water, ghee, and oil all together with them,
one should give an <s>anuvāsana</s> (unctuous enema) in fever, according to the unctuous substance and according to the impurity.

children.text: ye ca siddhiṣu vakṣyante vastayo jvaranāśanāḥ
children.translated_text: And the <s>bastis</s> (enemas) that will be taught in the sections on accomplishment
as destroying fever, removing headache, heaviness, and <s>śleṣman</s>, and awakening the senses,
one should give in chronic fever as evacuative <s>nasya</s> (nasal medication) that restores relish.
For one whose head is empty it should be unctuous; for one afflicted by burning it should destroy <s>pitta</s>.
One should also prepare inhaled smoke, gargles, and mouthful-retentions according to the <s>doṣa</s>,
removing coryza, bad taste in the mouth, and disorders of the head and throat.
In anorexia one should hold in the mouth the filament of <s>mātuluṅga</s> mixed with ghee and rock salt,
or a paste of <s>dhātrī</s>, grapes, and sugar.
According to what gives relief by contact, with substances prepared as cold or hot,
one should perform massage, anointing, sprinkling, and the like in chronic fever seated in the skin.
One should also use collyria and smokes; the same applies in adventitious fever too.
In burning, one should perform massage with ghee washed a hundred times.
With those several groups taught in the sūtras, sweet, sour, and astringent,
or with <s>dūrvā</s> and the other <s>pitta</s>-destroying drugs taught in the groups beginning with purifiers,
being cool in potency and cold to the touch, made into decoction and paste, one should cook
oil together with milk; by massage it immediately removes burning fever.

children.text: śiro gātraṃ ca taireva nātipiṣṭaiḥ pralepayet
children.translated_text: With those same drugs, not ground too finely, one should plaster the head and body,
and one should apply sprinkling and immersion with their decoction.
Likewise, with sour gruel, water, milk, vinegar, ghee, and the like,
with the sour juices of <s>kapittha</s> and <s>mātuluṅga</s>, and with <s>vidārī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and pomegranate,
or with foam produced from young leaves of <s>badarī</s>, or from <s>ariṣṭaka</s>,
when the body is smeared, burning, pain, bewilderment, vomiting, and thirst subside.
The procedure described as removing <s>pitta</s> in the treatment of the <s>doṣas</s>,

children.text: taṃ ca śīlayataḥ śīghraṃ sadāho naśyati jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when one practices it, quickly destroys fever together with burning.
With substances hot in potency and warm to the touch, with <s>tagara</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and saffron,
with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>sthauṇeya</s>, <s>śaileya</s>, <s>sarala</s>, and <s>amaradāru</s>,
with <s>nakha</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>pura</s>, <s>vacā</s>, strong <s>elā</s> of the two kinds, and <s>coraka</s>,
with <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>surasā</s>, <s>hiṃsrā</s>, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, and mustard,
with the ten roots, <s>amṛtā</s>, the two castor plants, <s>pattūra</s>, and <s>rohiṣa</s>,
with <s>tamālapattra</s>, <s>bhūtīka</s>, <s>śallakī</s>, coriander, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
with <s>miśi</s>, black gram, horse gram, <s>agni</s>, <s>prakīryā</s>, and the two <s>nākulīs</s>,

children.text: anyaiśca tadvidhair dravyaiḥ śīte tailaṃ jvare pacet ||
children.translated_text: and with other substances of that kind, one should cook oil in cold fever.
They should be boiled, made into paste, and combined with <s>surā</s>, <s>sauvīraka</s>, and the like.
With that oil, pleasantly warm, one should massage; and with those drugs well ground one should plaster.

children.text: kavoṣṇais taiḥ parīṣekam avagāhaṃ ca kalpayet
children.translated_text: With those, lukewarm, one should prepare sprinkling and immersion.
The same may also be done with vinegar, cow urine, and whey alone.
The group beginning with <s>āragvadha</s> too is to be used for drinking, massage, and plastering,
as well as the fumigations made from <s>aguru</s> that will be taught in intermittent fever.
One who is to be sweated should make habitual use of fomentations produced with fire and without fire, and of warming medicines and food,
of sleeping in an inner or underground chamber, of rugs, blankets, and woolen covers,
of smokeless, glowing coals, and of laughing and laughter-provoking companions,
of wine with the three pungents, buttermilk, horse gram, rice, and <s>kodrava</s> grain.
A trembling patient should habitually use whatever else also tends to increase <s>pitta</s>.
Beloved women, full-breasted, plump, adorned with playful charm,
and intoxicated with the wine of youth, should embrace him.

children.text: vītaśītaṃ ca vijñāya tās tato 'panayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when he is known to be free from cold, they should remove them again.
By increasing one <s>doṣa</s>, or by reducing the one that is elevated,
or by following the order of the seats of <s>kapha</s>, one should overcome impurities of equal strength.
At the end of <s>saṃnipāta-jvara</s> (fever from all doṣas), at the root of the ear

children.text: śophaḥ saṃjāyate yena kaścid eva vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: there arises a very severe swelling, from which only some person escapes.
One should conquer it quickly by bloodletting and by drinking ghee,
with poultices that remove <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, with nasal therapies, and with mouthful-retentions.
When a person's fever is not pacified by cold, hot, unctuous, dry, and similar treatments,

children.text: śākhānusārī tasyāśu muñced bāhvoḥ kramāt sirām ||
children.translated_text: and follows the branches, one should quickly open a vein in the arms, in due order.

children.text: ayam eva vidhiḥ kāryo viṣame 'pi yathāyatham
children.translated_text: This same procedure should be performed as appropriate in intermittent fever too,
after distinguishing <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>, and also what is stated immediately next.
Decoctions made from <s>paṭola</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>prāṇadā</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>,
in combinations of three, four, or five, destroy intermittent fever.

children.text: yojayet triphalāṃ pathyāṃ guḍūcīṃ pippalīṃ pṛthak
children.translated_text: One should apply <s>triphalā</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>pippalī</s> separately,

children.text: tais tair vidhānaiḥ saguḍaṃ bhallātakam athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: by those various methods, together with jaggery; or else <s>bhallātaka</s>.
On the day when fever is due to arrive, at the beginning one should use either fasting or nourishing treatment.

children.text: prātaḥ satailaṃ laśunaṃ prāgbhaktaṃ vā tathā ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: In the morning, before food, one may take garlic with oil, or likewise ghee.

children.text: jīrṇaṃ tadvad dadhi payas takraṃ sarpiśca ṣaṭpalam
children.translated_text: Similarly, when it has been digested, one may take old curds, milk, buttermilk, and six <s>palas</s> of ghee,
<s>Kalyānaka</s> ghee, <s>pañcagavya</s> ghee, and the ghee called <s>Tikta</s>, prepared with <s>vṛṣa</s>.
Ghee cooked with curds in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>kola</s>, and <s>tarkārī</s>,
with an admixture made from the bark of <s>tilvaka</s>, is supreme in conquering intermittent fever.

children.text: surāṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca yan madyaṃ śikhitittiridakṣajam
children.translated_text: Having freely consumed <s>surā</s>, sharp liquor,
and meat of peacock, partridge, or cock, fatty and hot in potency, together with rice,
one should sleep that day, or else vomit again.

children.text: sarpiṣo mahatīṃ mātrāṃ pītvā vā chardayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, after drinking a large dose of ghee, one should again induce vomiting.
At the onset of fever, one should drink <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>,
<s>trivṛt</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>, after being prepared with oleation and sweating.
As eye-salve for the eyes, <s>manohvā</s>, rock salt, and black pepper should be combined with oil.
A nasal medication should be prepared from fat of <s>vyāghrī</s>, equal in amount to asafoetida, together with rock salt.
Old ghee and lion's fat, likewise with rock salt, should be used.
<s>Palaṅkaṣā</s>, neem leaves, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>harītakī</s>,

children.text: sarṣapāḥ sayavāḥ sarpir dhūpo viḍ vā biḍālajā
children.translated_text: mustard seeds, together with barley, ghee, and fumigation, or cat dung,
with <s>puradhyāma</s>, <s>vacā</s>, resin, neem, <s>arka</s>, agarwood, and deodar:
this unconquered fumigation should be performed in all fevers.
Fumigations, nasal medicines, eye-salves, fright-inducing measures, and those remedies that have been stated for disorders of consciousness,

children.text: daivāśrayaṃ ca bhaiṣajyaṃ jvarān sarvān vyapohati
children.translated_text: as well as medicine relying on divine means, drive away all fevers.
They remove especially irregular fevers, for those are mostly consequent on external causes.

children.text: yathāsvaṃ ca sirāṃ vidhyed aśāntau viṣamajvare
children.translated_text: And according to the case one should puncture a vein if an irregular fever is not pacified.
In fever caused solely by <s>anila</s> (wind), by erysipelas, by eruptions, or by injury,
one should administer drinking of ghee, cooling applications, sprinkling, and eating meat soup,

children.text: kuryād yathāsvam uktaṃ ca raktamokṣādi sādhanam ||
children.translated_text: and the prescribed treatment such as bloodletting, according to the particular case.
In fever produced by <s>grahas</s>, one should use the treatments taught in demonology, such as offerings and mantras.
In fever produced by the smell of herbs, one should use <s>pitta</s>-pacifying treatment; in poisoning, poison-conquering treatment.
With desired and pleasing objects, and with pacification according to the <s>doṣa</s>,
and with discernment of what is wholesome and unwholesome, one should overcome fever born from anger and the like.

children.text: krodhajo yāti kāmena śāntiṃ krodhena kāmajaḥ
children.translated_text: A fever born from anger comes to peace through desire, and one born from desire through anger.
Those arising from fear and grief are pacified by those two, fear and grief; and the other two likewise by their opposites.
For fever arising from a curse, Atharvan rites, or mantras, the procedure is divine therapy.

children.text: te jvarāḥ kevalāḥ pūrvaṃ vyāpyante 'nantaram malaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those fevers are at first unmixed; afterward they become pervaded by the impurities.
Therefore in them one should arrange diet and the like in accordance with the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: na hi jvaro 'nubadhnāti mārutādyair vinā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For fever does not persist unless it is produced in connection with <s>māruta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>.
One should remove the patient's memory of the time of fever by attractive sense-objects.
A mind made tender with compassion and purified destroys every fever.
Until strength has been regained, one should avoid exercise, bathing, and sexual intercourse,
as well as heavy, unsuitable, burning food and whatever else causes fever.

children.text: na vijvaro 'pi sahasā sarvānnīno bhavet tathā
children.translated_text: Even when free from fever, one should not suddenly become an eater of all foods in that way.
For a fever, though it has ceased, quickly kills a weak person.

children.text: sadyaḥ prāṇaharo yasmāt tasmāt tasya viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Since it immediately takes life, therefore especially in its case

children.text: tasyāṃ tasyām avasthāyāṃ tat tat kuryād bhiṣagjitam ||
children.translated_text: the physician should do whatever is suited to each particular condition.
Medicines, jewels, good mantras, worship of the virtuous, teachers, twice-borns, and deities,

children.text: prītikarā manaso viṣayāśca ghnantyapi viṣṇukṛtaṃ jvaram ugram ||
children.translated_text: and sense-objects pleasing to the mind, destroy even the severe fever made by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>raktapitta</s> (blood-pitta).
So said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
One should treat <s>raktapitta</s> that moves upward, occurs in a strong person, has no violent attack, follows a single <s>doṣa</s>, is recent,
appears in an easy season, and is without complications.
One should manage <s>raktapitta</s> that moves downward, and that which follows two <s>doṣas</s>,

children.text: śāntaṃ śāntaṃ punaḥ kupyan mārgān mārgāntaraṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: that which, though pacified again and again, flares up again, and that which passes from one channel to another.
One should abandon as untreatable that which flows excessively, occurs in one with weak digestive fire, involves all three <s>doṣas</s>, and follows both paths.
Having understood the cause, the course, the strength of the impurity and of the patient,
and the condition of place, time, and so on, one should apply treatment in <s>raktapitta</s>.

children.text: laṅghanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vādau śodhanaṃ śamanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, depletion or nourishment, and also purification and pacification, should be used.
When it has arisen from over-nourishment, in a strong patient with abundant <s>doṣa</s>, one should cure it
when it affects the upper part by purgation, but when it goes downward by emesis.
Other cases are treated with pacifying and nourishing measures, after considering what requires depletion and what requires nourishment.
When it proceeds upward, the pacifying tastes are bitter and astringent,
together with fasting for those who drink <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> water without dry ginger.

children.text: adhoge raktapitte tu bṛṃhaṇo madhuro rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in downward <s>raktapitta</s>, the nourishing taste is sweet.

children.text: ūrdhvage tarpaṇaṃ yojyaṃ prāk ca peyā tvadhogate
children.translated_text: In upward movement, a nourishing drink should be administered first; but in downward movement, gruel should be given first.

children.text: aśnato balino 'śuddhaṃ na dhāryaṃ taddhi rogakṛt ||
children.translated_text: In a strong person who is eating, impure blood should not be held back, for it causes disease.
Otherwise one should restrain it quickly, since, like fire, it acts quickly.
With a decoction of <s>trivṛt</s> and <s>śyāmā</s>, and with their paste, together with sugar,

children.text: sādhayed vidhival lehaṃ lihyāt pāṇitalaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: one should prepare a linctus according to rule; then one should lick a palmful of it.

children.text: trivṛtā triphalā śyāmā pippalī śarkarā madhu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, long pepper, sugar, and honey:
this bolus removes upward bleeding, swelling, and fever caused by the combined <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Trivṛt</s> with an equal amount of sugar, likewise joined with a quarter part of long pepper,
is an emetic when combined with emetic fruit; a nourishing drink is taken with sugar and honey.

children.text: sasitaṃ vā jalaṃ kṣaudrayuktaṃ vā madhukodakam ||
children.translated_text: Or water with sugar, or licorice water mixed with honey,

children.text: kṣīraṃ vā rasam ikṣor vā śuddhasyānantaro vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: or milk, or sugarcane juice, is the subsequent regimen for one who has been purified.
According to the case, churned drinks, gruels, and the like should be prescribed while protecting strength.

children.text: mantho jvarokto drākṣādiḥ pittaghnair vā phalaiḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The churned drink mentioned for fever, beginning with grapes, or one made with <s>pitta</s>-pacifying fruits,
or a churned drink with licorice, dates, raisins, <s>parūṣaka</s>, sugar, and water,
or with the five sweet substances, together with fried grain flour mixed with ghee, should be used.
Or, for those with weak digestive fire who desire sourness, it may be sour with pomegranate or emblic myrobalan.
Lotus, blue lotus filaments, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
<s>uśīra</s>, <s>śabara</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, dry ginger, and red sandalwood,
<s>hrīvera</s>, flowers of <s>dhātakī</s>, the middle part of bilva, and <s>durālabhā</s>,
prepared in halves and halves, are drinks; combinations by quarter-parts will now be stated.
<s>Bhūnimba</s>, <s>sevya</s>, <s>jalada</s>, lentils, and also <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>,
<s>vidārigandhā</s>, mung beans, <s>balā</s>, ghee, and <s>hareṇukā</s>,
and meat of animals of dry lands, all cold in potency, should be cooked.

children.text: pṛthak pṛthag jale teṣāṃ yavāgūḥ kalpayed rase ||
children.translated_text: Separately for each of these, one should prepare barley gruel in water or in their broth.
They should be cold and accompanied by sugar and honey; meat broths too should be prepared in the same way.
either slightly sour or not sour, fried in ghee and accompanied by sugar.

children.text: śūkaśimbībhavaṃ dhānyaṃ rakte śākaṃ ca śasyate
children.translated_text: In <s>raktapitta</s>, grains produced from awned cereals and pulses, and vegetables, are recommended
when, in the knowledge of the nature of foods, they have been described as light and cooling.

children.text: pūrvoktam ambu pānīyaṃ pañcamūlena vā śṛtam
children.translated_text: The drinking water previously mentioned should be used, or water boiled with <s>pañcamūla</s> (the five roots),

children.text: laghunā śṛtaśītaṃ vā madhvambho vā phalāmbu vā ||
children.translated_text: or water boiled with the light roots and then cooled, or honey-water, or fruit-water.

children.text: śaśaḥ savāstukaḥ śasto vibandhe tittiriḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Hare with <s>vāstuka</s> greens is praised when there is constipation; partridge, again,
should be cooked in a decoction of <s>udumbara</s> when vāta is excessive.

children.text: plakṣasya barhiṇas tadvan nyagrodhasya ca kukkuṭaḥ
children.translated_text: In the same way peacock should be cooked with <s>plakṣa</s>, and chicken with <s>nyagrodha</s>.

children.text: yat kiṃcid raktapittasya nidānaṃ tacca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is a cause of <s>raktapitta</s>, that should be avoided.
The juice of <s>vāsā</s>, with <s>phalinī</s>, clay, <s>lodhra</s>, collyrium, and honey,
when drunk, pacifies pitta and blood; or the exudation from <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>
does so when combined with sugar and honey, whether taken alone or after being boiled.

children.text: vṛṣaḥ sadyo jayatyasraṃ sa hyasya param auṣadham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣa</s> immediately conquers bleeding, for it is the supreme medicine for this condition.
<s>Paṭola</s>, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, the two sandalwoods, and <s>padmaka</s>,

children.text: lodhro vṛṣas taṇḍulīyaḥ kṛṣṇā mṛn madayantikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>lodhra</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, clay, and <s>madayantikā</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>gopakanyā</s>, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, and <s>madhuyaṣṭikā</s>:
these are three decoctions that remove <s>raktapitta</s>, to be taken with honey and sugar.
Or one may use a very cold decoction of <s>palāśa</s> bark, furnished with sugar.
Or one should lick the expressed liquid of cow or horse dung with honey and ghee.
When the blood is clotted, one should lick dove dung with honey.
And when blood has flowed out excessively, one should drink blood with honey.

children.text: jāṅgalaṃ bhakṣayed vājam āmaṃ pittayutaṃ yakṛt
children.translated_text: Or one should eat the raw, bile-mixed liver of a wild animal as food.
With sandalwood, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>jalada</s>, parched grain, mung beans, long pepper, and barley,
kept overnight in water of <s>balā</s>, a decoction removes <s>raktapitta</s>.
The clear liquid produced from sandalwood, lotus, <s>sevya</s>, clay, and roasted clods,
very cold and with sugar and honey, conquers excessive flow of blood.

children.text: āpothya vā nave kumbhe plāvayed ikṣugaṇḍikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, after crushing pieces of sugarcane in a new jar, one should soak them.

children.text: sthitaṃ tad guptam ākāśe rātriṃ prātaḥ srutaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: That water, kept protected in the open air through the night and strained in the morning,
with honey and adorned with fully opened lotuses, has the same qualities.

children.text: ye ca pittajvare coktāḥ kaṣāyās tāṃśca yojayet
children.translated_text: And the decoctions that were taught for pitta-fever should also be applied.
If, after the digestive fire has been kindled and kapha has been overcome by these various decoctions,

children.text: raktapittaṃ na cecchāmyet tatra vātolbaṇe payaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>raktapitta</s> still does not subside, then, when vāta is predominant, milk should be used.
Goat's milk should be boiled and administered; cow's milk likewise, boiled in five times as much water,
or boiled with the light <s>pañcamūla</s>, together with sugar and honey.
Milk may be boiled separately with <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, grapes, <s>balā</s>, <s>gokṣura</s>, and dry ginger,

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak śṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ saghṛtaṃ sitayāthavā
children.translated_text: each one separately, and given with ghee or with sugar.
Milk boiled with <s>gokaṇṭaka</s> and <s>abhīru</s>, and also with the leafy drugs,
quickly destroys painful bleeding, especially when it moves through the urinary passage.
When it moves through the fecal passage, it is especially beneficial with <s>mocarasa</s>,
with sprouts or shoots of banyan, or also with dry ginger, <s>udīcya</s>, and blue lotus.
Here one should also devise the treatment for bloody diarrhea and piles.

children.text: pītvā kaṣāyān payasā bhuñjīta payasaiva ca
children.translated_text: After drinking the decoctions, one should eat with milk, and drink milk as well.
Or one should administer ghee cooked with these decoction formulas.
Having crushed <s>vṛṣa</s> together with its roots and top,
