one should boil it in eight times as much water, and when one eighth remains, cook ghee with that liquid.
That ghee, containing its flowers, cooled, and mixed with honey, destroys pitta-blood,
as well as pitta-type abdominal tumor, fever, dyspnea, cough, heart disease, and jaundice,
and also dimness of sight, dizziness, erysipelas, and hoarseness of voice.
One should cook ghee in the expressed juice of <s>palāśa</s> stalks, with those stalks placed in it.
With honey, that too destroys blood; likewise ghee prepared with <s>trāyamāṇā</s> does so.
When blood is slimy, accompanied by kapha, clotted, and moving through the throat passage,
one should lick the alkali made from lotus stalk with honey and ghee.
Likewise, separately, alkali made from lotus pollen, <s>śyāmā</s>, and <s>madhūka</s> should be used.
When blood comes through the anus, an enema is especially desired.
When blood comes through the nose, after purification, one should apply nasal instillation and sprinkling.
The decoction formulas stated earlier, infused with milk and sugarcane juice and the like,

children.text: kṣīrādīn sasitāṃs toyaṃ kevalaṃ vā jalaṃ hitaṃ ||
children.translated_text: milk and similar drinks with sugar, or plain water alone, are beneficial.
The juice of pomegranate flowers, of mango stones, or of <s>śādvala</s> grass may be prepared.
And the cooling group should be arranged for poultices, anointments, and the like.
Whatever medicine, external and internal, has been taught for pitta-fever

children.text: raktapitte hitaṃ tacca kṣatakṣīṇe hitaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: is also beneficial in <s>raktapitta</s>, as is whatever is beneficial for the wounded and wasted condition.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>kāsa</s> (cough).
So said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
A cough caused by vāta alone should first be treated with unctuous substances,
with fats prepared with vāta-alleviating drugs, and with unctuous gruels, soups, meat broths, and the like,
with linctuses, fumigations, oil massage, sudation, affusions, and immersions.
When feces and flatus are obstructed, it should be treated with enemas; but when it is accompanied by pitta, with ghee taken after meals,
and with milk; when accompanied by kapha, one should conquer it with unctuous purgatives.
In the decoction of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, prepared separately from thirty palas of each,
a prastha of ghee cooked therein removes vāta-cough and kindles the digestive fire.
With alkali, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, asafoetida, <s>pāṭhā</s>, licorice, and coriander,
two śāṇas of each, together with <s>pañcakola</s>, one should cook a prastha of ghee.
Drunk with thin gruel as its vehicle, after being cooked in a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>,
it removes cough, dyspnea, heart disease, pain in the sides, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, and abdominal tumor.
In a droṇa of water one should boil <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>daśamūla</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
measured at one pala each, together with two kuḍavas of horse gram, jujube, and barley,
and half a tulā of goat meat; with that liquid an āḍhaka of ghee should be prepared.
That, with an equal amount of milk and with life-promoting drugs in pala-measures, properly prepared,
when used in diseases of <s>vāta</s> by drinking, nasal therapy, and enemas,
overcomes the five kinds of cough, shaking of the head, pain in the vagina and groins,
diseases of the whole body and of single limbs, together with splenic disease and upward-moving wind.
A preparation cooked with the decoction and paste of the <s>vidāryādi</s> group is also a conqueror of cough.
With <s>aśoka</s> seed, <s>kṣavaka</s>, <s>jantughna</s>, <s>añjana</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,

children.text: saviḍaiśca ghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ taccūrṇaṃ vā ghṛtaplutam
children.translated_text: and with the <s>viḍa</s> salts, ghee should be cooked; or the powder of those drugs, soaked in ghee,
should be licked, and goat's milk should be drunk afterward by one severely oppressed by cough.

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ nāgaraṃ rāsnā pippalī hiṅgu saindhavam
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, dry ginger, <s>rāsnā</s>, long pepper, asafoetida, rock salt,

children.text: bhārgī kṣāraśca taccūrṇaṃ pibed vā ghṛtamātrayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>bhārgī</s>, and alkali: one should drink this powder with a measure of ghee,
when the cough is due to <s>vāta</s> with kapha, and when dyspnea, hiccup, and digestive fire have been impaired.
One should lick <s>durālabhā</s>, fresh ginger, <s>śaṭhī</s>, raisins, sugar candy,

children.text: lihyāt karkaṭaśṛṅgīṃ ca kāse tailena vātaje
children.translated_text: and <s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s> with oil in a cough caused by <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: duḥsparśāṃ pippalīṃ mustāṃ bhārgīṃ karkaṭakīṃ śaṭhīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>Duḥsparśā</s>, long pepper, <s>mustā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>karkaṭakī</s>, and <s>śaṭhī</s>,
powdered with old jaggery and oil, should be taken as a linctus.

children.text: tadvat sakṛṣṇāṃ śuṇṭhīṃ ca sabhārgīṃ tadvad eva ca ||
children.translated_text: In the same way one may use dry ginger with <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, and likewise with <s>bhārgī</s> in the same manner.
One should also drink <s>kṛṣṇā</s> with warm water and rock salt,

children.text: mastunā sasitāṃ śuṇṭhīṃ dadhnā vā kaṇareṇukām ||
children.translated_text: dry ginger with sugar in whey, or <s>kaṇā</s> and <s>reṇukā</s> with curd.
Or one should drink jujube kernels with wine, curd, or whey,
or else a paste of long pepper, fried in ghee and mixed with rock salt.

children.text: kāsī sapīnaso dhūmaṃ snaihikaṃ vidhinā pibet
children.translated_text: A cough sufferer accompanied by coryza should inhale unctuous medicinal smoke according to rule,
and also the smokes prescribed for hiccup and dyspnea, while taking milk and meat broth as food.
One should feed him with rice, barley, wheat, and sixty-day rice, using broths of domestic, marsh, and aquatic animals,
or with soups of black gram and <s>ātmaguptā</s>, when these are beneficial.
In cough due to <s>vāta</s>, one should drink a gruel cooked with <s>yavānī</s>, long pepper, the middle part of bilva, dry ginger, <s>citraka</s>,
<s>rāsnā</s>, cumin, <s>pṛthakparṇī</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
unctuous, sour, and salty,
destroying pain in the waist, heart, flanks, and abdomen, as well as dyspnea and hiccup.
In the same way one should drink a gruel made in decoction of the ten roots, with <s>pañcakola</s> and jaggery,

children.text: pibet peyāṃ samatilāṃ kṣaireyīṃ vā sasaindhavām ||
children.translated_text: or a milk-gruel with sesame and rock salt.
Or it may be made with fish, fowl, or boar meat, together with ghee and rock salt.
<s>Vāstuka</s>, <s>vāyasī</s> vegetable, and <s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s> are cough-destroying.

children.text: kaṇṭakāryāḥ phalaṃ pattraṃ bālaṃ śuṣkaṃ ca mūlakam
children.translated_text: The fruit and leaf of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, and young and dried radish,
fats such as oils are to be eaten, as are milk, sugarcane juice, and <s>gauḍikā</s>.
One should drink curd, whey, sour gruel, sour fruit-water, and wine.

children.text: pittakāse tu sakaphe vamanaṃ sarpiṣā hitam ||
children.translated_text: But in cough due to <s>pitta</s>, when kapha is present, emesis with ghee is beneficial,
as also with waters decocted with <s>madana</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and licorice,
or with pastes of emetic fruit and licorice, saturated with <s>vidārī</s> juice and sugarcane juice.
In cough due to <s>pitta</s> with thin kapha, one should employ <s>trivṛt</s> mixed with sweet substances
for purgation; when the phlegm is thick, it should be mixed with bitter substances.

children.text: hṛtadoṣo himaṃ svādu snigdhaṃ saṃsarjanaṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: When the <s>doṣa</s> has been removed, one should follow a cold, sweet, and unctuous restorative diet.

children.text: ghane kaphe tu śiśiraṃ rūkṣaṃ tiktopasaṃhitam ||
children.translated_text: But when kapha is thick, it should be cold, dry, and accompanied by bitter substances.
In a <s>pitta</s> cough, a linctus of sugar, emblic myrobalan, honey, raisins, cold infusion, and blue lotus,
with ghee, is beneficial when <s>vāta</s> is present; when kapha is present, it should include <s>abdā</s> and black pepper.
One should lick with honey fifty raisins, thirty long peppers, and a pala of sugar,

children.text: lehayen madhunā gor vā kṣīrapasya śakṛdrasam ||
children.translated_text: or, for one who lives on cow's milk, the juice of cow dung.
A linctus made with cinnamon, cardamom, the three pungents, raisins, long-pepper root, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
with parched grain, <s>mustā</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, emblic myrobalan, and <s>vibhītaka</s>,
together with sugar, honey, and ghee, removes heart disease and cough.
Barley, <s>śyāmāka</s>, and <s>kodrava</s>, with sweet broths of dry-land animals,
soups beginning with mung, and bitter vegetables are beneficial in proper measure.
When the phlegm is thick, bitter linctuses mixed with honey are also beneficial.
When kapha is thin, rice and sixty-day rice should be used with broths and the like.
For a following drink, there may be sugar-water, grape juice, sugarcane juice, or milk.
For a <s>pitta</s> cough, one should prepare meat broths, milk, gruels, and soups
with <s>kākolī</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, the two <s>medā</s>s, <s>vṛṣa</s>, and dry ginger.

children.text: drākṣāṃ kaṇāṃ pañcamūlaṃ tṛṇākhyaṃ ca pacejjale
children.translated_text: One should boil raisins, <s>kaṇā</s>, the five roots called grasses, in water;

children.text: tena kṣīraṃ śṛtaṃ śītaṃ pibet samadhuśarkaram ||
children.translated_text: with that, milk should be cooked, cooled, and drunk with honey and sugar.

children.text: sādhitāṃ tena peyāṃ vā suśītāṃ madhunānvitām
children.translated_text: Or one may take a gruel prepared with that, well cooled and mixed with honey.
<s>Śaṭhī</s>, <s>hrīvera</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, sugar, and dry ginger

children.text: piṣṭvā rasaṃ pibet pūtaṃ vastreṇa ghṛtamūrchitam
children.translated_text: should be ground; one should drink the juice, filtered through cloth and infused with ghee.
<s>Medā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, the fruit of <s>svayaṅguptā</s>, <s>balā</s>,
sugar, <s>jīvaka</s>, mung, <s>māṣaparṇī</s>, and <s>durālabhā</s>
should be made into a paste; one should cook ghee with eight times as much milk by means of that paste.
Used in drinks, food, and linctuses, it conquers cough due to <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: lihyād vā cūrṇam eteṣāṃ kaṣāyam athavā pibet ||
children.translated_text: Or one should lick the powder of these drugs, or drink their decoction.
A patient with kapha cough should first drink the fat that has trickled from a piece of <s>surakāṣṭha</s>
that has been set alight, sprinkled with the three pungents and barley-alkali.

children.text: snigdhaṃ virecayed ūrdhvam adho mūrdhni ca yuktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having been oleated, he should be purged upward, downward, and in the head, as appropriate.

children.text: tīkṣṇair virekair balinaṃ saṃsargīṃ cāsya yojayet ||
children.translated_text: If he is strong, sharp purgative measures should be used, and his subsequent regimen should be arranged.
With foods of barley, mung, and horse gram, hot, dry, pungent, and very sharp,
mixed with <s>kāsamardaka</s>, eggplant, <s>vyāghrī</s>, alkali, and <s>kaṇā</s>,
with broths of dry-land animals and bilva, and with fats from sesame, mustard, and neem,

children.text: daśamūlāmbu gharmāmbu madyaṃ madhvambu vā pibet ||
children.translated_text: he should drink water of the ten roots, hot water, wine, or honey-water.
Or he should drink water in which roots of <s>pauṣkara</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, and <s>paṭola</s> have stood overnight,

children.text: pibed vāri sahakṣaudraṃ kāleṣvannasya vā triṣu ||
children.translated_text: together with honey, at the three times connected with food.
Long pepper, long-pepper root, dry ginger, and vibhītaka,
the ash of peacock and cock feathers, and alkali produced from barley:
viśālā, long-pepper root, trivṛt, and liquids of honey
are three linctuses that remove <s>kapha-kāsa</s> (phlegmatic cough), arranged in half-verses.

children.text: madhunā maricaṃ lihyān madhunaiva ca joṅgakam
children.translated_text: One should lick black pepper with honey, and joṅgaka likewise with honey,
and separately the juices of vyāghrī, vārtāka, and bhṛṅga with honey.
Also the cough-removing juice of horse dung, of surasa, and of black basil,
devadāru, śaṭhī, rāsnā, karkaṭākhyā, and durālabhā,

children.text: pippalī nāgaraṃ mustaṃ pathyā dhātrī sitopalā
children.translated_text: long pepper, dry ginger, musta, pathyā, dhātrī, and sugar candy,
parched grain, sugar candy, ghee, śṛṅgī, and products of dhātrī fruit:
these three linctuses, joined with honey and oil, are used when <s>kapha</s> is attended by <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: dve pale dāḍimād aṣṭau guḍād vyoṣāt palatrayam ||
children.translated_text: Two palas from pomegranate, eight from jaggery, and three palas from the three pungents,
make a preparation that improves taste, kindles digestion, benefits the voice, and conquers catarrh, dyspnea, and cough.
Jaggery, alkali, pungent substances, long pepper, and pomegranate conquer dyspnea and cough.
In order, the measures are two palas, half an akṣa, a karṣa, half an akṣa, and a pala.
One should drink the digestive remedy beginning with pathyā, mentioned in the fever section, together with śṛṅgī.
Or dīpyaka, trivṛt, viśālā, ghana, and pauṣkara,

children.text: sakaṇaṃ kvathitaṃ mūtre kaphakāsī jale 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: together with long pepper, boiled in urine, or even in water, should be used by one with <s>kapha-kāsa</s>.
An akṣa of paste of vaidehī, fried in oil and mixed with sugar candy,
should be given to drink, soaked in horse-gram water; it destroys <s>kapha-kāsa</s>.
In an āḍhaka of decoction of the ten roots, one should cook a prastha of ghee with akṣa-equal portions
of puṣkarāhva, śaṭhī, bilva, surasā, the three pungents, and hiṅgu.
That, with gruel as its after-drink, removes all disorders of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
Ghee prepared with the expressed juice of nirguṇḍī leaves conquers cough.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ rase viḍaṅgānāṃ vyoṣagarbhaṃ ca sādhitam ||
children.translated_text: So too does ghee prepared in the juice of viḍaṅga, with the three pungents inside it.
With the juices of punarnavā, śivāṭikā, saralā, kāsamarda, amṛtā, paṭola, bṛhatī, and phaṇijjaka, joined with milk,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ trikaṭunā ca siddham upayujya saṃjāyate na kāsaviṣamajvarakṣayagudāṅkurebhyo bhayam ||
children.translated_text: ghee prepared with trikaṭu, when used, makes there be no danger from cough, irregular fever, wasting, or rectal sprouts.
In an āḍhaka of juice of kaṇṭakārī, together with its root, fruit, and leaves,
one should cook a prastha of ghee with balā, the three pungents, viḍaṅga, śaṭhī, and pomegranate,
with sauvarcala salt, barley alkali, mūlāmalaka, and pauṣkara,
with vṛścīva, bṛhatī, pathyā, yavānī, citraka, and ṛddhi,
with raisins, cavya, varṣābhū, durālabhā, and sour vetasa,
and with śṛṅgī, tāmalakī, bhārgī, rāsnā, and gokṣuraka as pastes.
That is prescribed in all coughs and in dyspnea and hiccup.
This is kaṇṭakārī ghee, the destroyer of diseases of <s>kapha</s>.
One should cook a tulā of crushed vyāghrī in a vāha of water until an āḍhaka remains.
When it has been filtered, one should add, after powdering, the three pungents, rāsnā, amṛtā, and agnika,
and half-pala portions of śṛṅgī, bhārgī, ghana, granthi, and dhanvayāsa.
One should add sixteen palas of ghee and forty palas
of purified matsyaṇḍikā, and then place it again on the fire.

children.text: darvīlepini śīte ca pṛthag dvikuḍavaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: When it coats the ladle and has cooled, one should add separately two kuḍavas
of long peppers, tavakṣīrī, fresh honey, and new honey.
This linctus conquers <s>gulma</s>, heart disease, piles, dyspnea, and cough.

children.text: śamanaṃ ca pibeddhūmaṃ śodhanaṃ bahale kaphe ||
children.translated_text: One should also drink pacifying smoke; in thick <s>kapha</s>, purifying smoke should be used.
Realgar, lac, licorice, māṃsī, musta, and bark of iṅgudī

children.text: dhūmaṃ kāsaghnavidhinā pītvā kṣīraṃ pibed anu ||
children.translated_text: should be smoked according to the cough-removing rule; after inhaling the smoke, one should drink milk.

children.text: niṣṭhyūtānte guḍayutaṃ koṣṇaṃ dhūmo nihanti saḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of expectoration, warm milk mixed with jaggery should be drunk; that smoke destroys
coughs dominated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, even chronic ones, quickly.
But if <s>tamaka</s> occurs in <s>kapha-kāsa</s> and is connected with <s>pitta</s>,
then one should apply the treatment for <s>pitta-kāsa</s> according to the condition.
When <s>vāta</s> is connected with <s>kapha</s>, one should perform <s>kapha</s>-removing treatment.
When <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> are connected with <s>pitta</s>, one should use <s>pitta</s>-destroying treatment.
In dry cough consisting of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, treatment should be unctuous; in moist cough, drying.

children.text: kāse karma sapitte tu kaphaje tiktasaṃyutam ||
children.translated_text: When cough is accompanied by <s>pitta</s>, the procedure for <s>kapha</s>-born cough should be joined with bitter substances.
When there is an internal wound in the chest, one should immediately drink lac mixed with honey.
When that is digested, one should eat śāli rice with milk, and again with milk mixed with sugar.
If there is pain in the flanks and bladder and little <s>pitta</s> and digestive fire, he should take that lac with liquor.
If his stool is loose, he should take it with musta, ativisā, pāṭhā, and vatsaka.

children.text: lākṣāṃ sarpir madhūcchiṣṭaṃ jīvanīyaṃ gaṇaṃ sitām
children.translated_text: Lac, ghee, beeswax, the life-promoting group, sugar,

children.text: tvakkṣīrīṃ samitaṃ kṣīre paktvā dīptānalaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: and tvakkṣīrī should be cooked together in milk; one whose digestive fire is strong should drink it.
Milk boiled with ikṣvārikā, lotus-fiber knots, lotus filaments, and sandalwood,

children.text: śṛtaṃ payo madhuyutaṃ saṃdhānārthaṃ pibet kṣatī ||
children.translated_text: and mixed with honey, should be drunk by one wounded in the chest for the purpose of healing.

children.text: yavānāṃ cūrṇam āmānāṃ kṣīre siddhaṃ ghṛtānvitam
children.translated_text: Powder of unripe barley, cooked in milk and furnished with ghee,
or roasted-grain flour with sugar and honey should be drunk with milk in fever and burning.
But one afflicted with cough should drink ghee prepared with sweet medicines,
or jaggery water boiled with honey and black pepper is beneficial.

children.text: cūrṇam āmalakānāṃ vā kṣīre pakvaṃ ghṛtānvitam
children.translated_text: Or powder of āmalaka fruits, cooked in milk and furnished with ghee, may be used.
Or long peppers should be administered according to the rasāyana regimen.
A coughing patient with pain in the joints and bones should lick, together with ghee and honey,
madhūka, licorice, grapes, tvakkṣīrī, long pepper, and balā.
The three aromatics, each half a karṣa, long pepper half a pala, sugar,
grapes, madhūka, dates, and palāśa should be made into a fine powder.

children.text: madhunā guṭikā ghnanti tā vṛṣyāḥ pittaśoṇitam
children.translated_text: With honey, these pills, aphrodisiac in effect, destroy <s>pitta</s> and blood disorders,
cough, dyspnea, loss of appetite, vomiting, fainting, hiccup, intoxication, and dizziness,
as well as chest-wound wasting, loss of voice, spleen disease, emaciation, and severe <s>vāta</s> disorders.
as well as bloody spitting, pain in the heart and sides, thirst, and fever.
A person spitting blood should drink powder made from <s>varṣābhū</s>, sugar, and red <s>śāli</s> rice grains,
prepared with grape juice, milk, and ghee.
Or he may drink <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> cooked with milk, <s>madhūka</s>, and licorice.
When blood has issued by each respective path, one should apply the treatment appropriate to it.
When <s>vāta</s> is obstructed, he should eat skin and fat fried in liquor, with rock salt.
One who is emaciated, wasted, wounded in the chest, poor in sleep, and has a keen digestive fire
should eat it with the cream of boiled milk, together with ghee, honey, and sugar.
A wasted, injured, thin person should lick sugar, barley, wheat, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and honey,

children.text: śṛtakṣīrānupānaṃ vā lihyāt kṣīṇaḥ kṣataḥ kṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: with boiled milk as the after-drink.
He should also drink the broth of the flesh of carnivorous animals, fried in ghee,
combined with long pepper and honey, for it increases flesh and blood.
With <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>plakṣa</s>, <s>śāla</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
and with <s>tālamastaka</s>, bark of <s>jambū</s>, <s>priyāla</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,

children.text: sāśvakarṇaiḥ śṛtāt kṣīrād adyāj jātena sarpiṣā ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>aśvakarṇa</s>, from milk boiled with these he should eat cooked <s>śāli</s> rice with the ghee produced from it,
if he has a chest wound and his semen, strength, and faculties are depleted.
For one afflicted by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, when there is splitting pain in the limbs, massage with ghees is prescribed.
And when he is oppressed by <s>mātariśvan</s> (wind), massage with oils that remove <s>anila</s> disorders is recommended.
For pains in the heart and sides, drinking the ghee of the <s>jīvanīya</s> group is proper.
Or one should do whatever removes <s>vāta</s> disorders without opposing <s>pitta</s> and blood.
Ghee cooked in a decoction of licorice and <s>nāgabalā</s>, with an equal amount of milk,
and with pastes of <s>payasyā</s>, long pepper, and <s>vāṃśī</s>, is beneficial in chest injury.

children.text: jīvanīyo gaṇaḥ śuṇṭhī varī vīrā punarnavā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>jīvanīya</s> group, dry ginger, <s>varī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>balā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>svaguptā</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>,

children.text: śṛṅgāṭakaṃ payasyā ca pañcamūlaṃ ca yallaghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, the smaller five roots,
and fruits such as grapes and walnuts, sweet, unctuous, and nourishing:

children.text: taiḥ pacet sarpiṣaḥ prasthaṃ karṣāṃśaiḥ ślakṣṇakalkitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with these, one <s>karṣa</s> each and finely ground into paste, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee,
together with milk, emblic myrobalan, <s>vidārī</s>, sugarcane juice, and goat-meat broth.
When it has cooled, one should mix in half a <s>prastha</s> of honey and half a <s>tulā</s> of powdered sugar,
and half a <s>pala</s> each of pepper, cinnamon bark, cardamom, leaf, and saffron.
After mixing it, one should lick from it a <s>prasṛta</s> dose, according to strength.
This ghee, called <s>Amṛtaprāśa</s>, is nectar for human beings.
It is to be eaten like the essence of ambrosia by one who lives on milk and meat broth.
It nourishes those whose semen is lost, who are injured, wasted, weak, and emaciated by disease,
those attached to women, the thin, and those deficient in complexion and voice.
It removes cough, hiccup, fever, dyspnea, burning, thirst, and <s>asṛkpitta</s> (bleeding-pitta).
It gives sons and removes vomiting, fainting, and disorders of the heart, female generative tract, and urinary tract.
<s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>kaṭtṛṇa</s>,
root of <s>darbha</s>, <s>pṛthakparṇī</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>sthirā</s>:
one should cook one <s>pala</s> of each, and in their decoction with four times as much milk,
with pastes of <s>svaguptā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, raisins, sugar, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, and lotus fiber,
a <s>prastha</s> of ghee, when cooked, removes heart disease and colic caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It removes dysuria, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), piles, cough, consumption, and wasting.
It gives strength and flesh to those exhausted by the bow, women, wine, burdens, and travel.
One should cook ghee in a decoction of eight <s>palas</s> of licorice and a <s>prastha</s> of grapes.

children.text: pippalyaṣṭapale kalke prasthaṃ siddhe ca śītale ||
children.translated_text: With eight <s>palas</s> of long pepper as paste, a <s>prastha</s> of ghee is cooked; when it is cooked and cooled,
one should separately mix in eight <s>palas</s> each of honey and sugar.
With an equal amount of roasted flour, it is beneficial in chest injury, wasting, and blood tumors.
From juices of emblic myrobalan, <s>vidārī</s>, sugarcane, and the <s>jīvanīya</s> drugs, from ghee,
and from cow's and goat's milk, one should cook one <s>prastha</s> of each.
When it is cooked and cooled, one should then add two <s>prasthas</s> of sugar and honey.
It removes <s>yakṣmā</s> (consumption), epilepsy, disorders of <s>pitta</s> and blood, cough, <s>meha</s>, and wasting.
It stabilizes age, promotes longevity, and gives flesh, semen, and strength.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tu pitte 'bhyadhike lihyād vāte 'dhike pibet ||
children.translated_text: But when <s>pitta</s> is predominant, one should lick ghee; when <s>vāta</s> is predominant, one should drink it.
Licked, it cools <s>pitta</s> and, because the amount is small, does not destroy the digestive fire.
Drunk, it overcomes <s>anila</s> and also restrains heat.
For those whose bodies are emaciated, depleted, and thin, these same ghees
should be made thick with powders of bark, <s>kṣīrī</s>, sugar, and parched grain.

children.text: sarpirguḍān samadhvaṃśān kṛtvā dadyāt payo 'nu ca
children.translated_text: Making ghee-jaggery boluses with equal parts honey, one should give them, and milk afterward.

children.text: reto vīryaṃ balaṃ puṣṭiṃ tairāśutaram āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Through them one very quickly obtains semen, vigor, strength, and nourishment.
A <s>tulā</s> of pumpkin, with skin and seeds removed and steamed, should be cooked again,

children.text: ghaṭṭayan sarpiṣaḥ prasthe kṣaudravarṇe 'tra ca kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: stirring it in a <s>prastha</s> of ghee; when it has the color of honey, one should add to it
one hundred <s>palas</s> of sugar candy, two <s>palas</s> each of long pepper and dry ginger, and also cumin.
The three aromatics, coriander, and pepper should each be added in half-<s>pala</s> portions.
When it has been taken off the fire and cooled, one should add honey equal to half the ghee,
churn it with a churning stick, and store it; when used, it destroys
cough, hiccup, fever, dyspnea, <s>raktapitta</s>, chest injury, and wasting.
It produces repair of the chest and gives intelligence, memory, and strength.
This heart-pleasing pumpkin <s>rasāyana</s> was prescribed by the two <s>Aśvins</s>.
One should drink the root of <s>nāgabalā</s>, increased by half-<s>karṣa</s> measures,
to the amount of one <s>pala</s>, with milk for a month, living on milk and eating no solid food.
This regimen is supreme for producing nourishment, lifespan, strength, and complexion.
This is also the regimen for <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, licorice, and <s>viśvauṣadha</s>.
One should cook a <s>tulā</s> of <s>nāgabalā</s> in a <s>droṇa</s> of water until one quarter remains.

children.text: tena kvāthena tulyāṃśaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ ca sādhayet
children.translated_text: With that decoction one should prepare equal parts ghee and milk.
and with half-pala portions of <s>atibalā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>;
with <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>priyāla</s>, and <s>kapikacchu</s>;
with <s>aśvagandhā</s>, sugar, <s>abhīru</s>, the pair of <s>medā</s> herbs, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>;
with <s>kākolī</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>kṣīraśuklā</s>, and the two <s>jīraka</s> seeds;
with lotus stalk, lotus fiber, dates, <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, and <s>kaseruka</s>.
This <s>Nāgabalā</s> ghee conquers disorders of <s>pitta</s> and blood, injury, and wasting,
as well as thirst, dizziness, and burning; it is supremely productive of strength and nourishment.
It improves complexion, promotes longevity and <s>ojas</s> (vital vigor), and destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: upayujya ca ṣaṇ māsān vṛddho 'pi taruṇāyate ||
children.translated_text: After using it for six months, even an old man becomes youthful.
This procedure is for one whose digestive fire is kindled; when it is weak, kindling and digesting measures are required.

children.text: yakṣmoktaḥ kṣatināṃ śasto grāhī śakṛti tu drave ||
children.translated_text: What was prescribed for <s>yakṣman</s> is suitable for those with injury; but when the stool is liquid, a constipating treatment is appropriate.
One should take <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>svayaṅguptā</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>balā</s>,
<s>hastipippalī</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, root of <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
<s>bhārgī</s> and root of <s>puṣkara</s>, each in two-pala portions, together with an āḍhaka of barley,
and one hundred <s>harītakī</s> fruits; these should be cooked in five āḍhakas of water.
When the barley has cooked, that decoction is strained; then that hundred <s>abhayā</s> fruits

children.text: paced guḍatulāṃ dattvā kuḍavaṃ ca pṛthag ghṛtāt ||
children.translated_text: should be cooked after adding a tulā of jaggery and one kuḍava each of ghee,
oil, powdered <s>pippalī</s>, and honey when the preparation has cooked and cooled.

children.text: lehaṃ dve cābhaye nityam ataḥ khāded rasāyanāt ||
children.translated_text: From this <s>rasāyana</s> linctus one should eat two <s>abhayā</s> fruits daily.
It removes wrinkles and gray hair and increases complexion, life span, and strength.
It conquers the five kinds of cough, wasting, dyspnea together with hiccup, and intermittent fever,
as well as urinary disease, abdominal tumor, <s>grahaṇī</s>, piles, heart disease, anorexia, and chronic coryza.
This excellent, auspicious <s>rasāyana</s> was prescribed by <s>Agastya</s>.
<s>Daśamūla</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, the two <s>haridrā</s> herbs, the two <s>pippalī</s> herbs,
<s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>svaguptā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>,
young <s>bilva</s>, the roots of <s>trivṛt</s> and <s>dantī</s>, and the leaf of <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: payasyāṃ kuṭajaṃ hiṃsrāṃ puṣpaṃ sāraṃ ca bījakāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>payasyā</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>hiṃsrā</s>, and the flower and heartwood of <s>bījaka</s>,
<s>boṭa</s>, <s>sthavira</s>, <s>bhallāta</s>, <s>vikaṅkata</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>pūtikarañja</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, <s>candralekhā</s>, and <s>sahācara</s>,
the bark of <s>śobhāñjana</s> and <s>nimba</s>, and <s>ikṣura</s>, each in one-pala portions,
one thousand and one hundred <s>pathyā</s> fruits, and two āḍhakas of barley.
One should cook them in eight times as much water and remove the vessel when the barley is cooked.

children.text: pūte kṣipet sapathye ca tatra jīrṇaguḍāt tulām ||
children.translated_text: When it has been strained, with the <s>pathyā</s> fruits included, one should add a tulā of old jaggery there;
then one prastha each of oil, ghee, and juice of <s>dhātrī</s>;
then one should set it again over a gentle fire and remove it when it coats the ladle.
When it is cool, one should add two prasthas of honey and a kuḍava of <s>pippalī</s>,
and three palas of powdered <s>trijāta</s>; then one should bury it
in grain, placed in an old jar, for a month, and eat it as before.
This <s>rasāyana</s>, taught by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, exceeds the previous one in its qualities.
It is recommended for healthy people, without dietary restriction, in all seasons.

children.text: pālikaṃ saindhavaṃ śuṇṭhī dve ca sauvarcalāt pale ||
children.translated_text: One pala each of rock salt and dry ginger, and two palas of <s>sauvarcala</s>,
one kuḍava each of <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, pomegranate, and leaves of <s>ārjaka</s>,
one caturthikā each of black pepper and <s>ajājī</s>, and two caturthikās of coriander,

children.text: śarkarāyāḥ palānyatra daśa dve ca pradāpayet
children.translated_text: and twelve palas of sugar should be added here.

children.text: kṛtvā cūrṇam ato mātrām annapāneṣu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made this into a powder, one should administer a dose of it in foods and drinks.
It is appetizing, kindles digestion, strengthens, and conquers pain in the side, dyspnea, and cough.

children.text: ekāṃ ṣoḍaśikāṃ dhānyād dve dve cājājidīpyakāt ||
children.translated_text: One sixteenth-measure of coriander, and two each of <s>ajājī</s> and <s>dīpyaka</s>,

children.text: tābhyāṃ dāḍimavṛkṣāmle dvir dviḥ sauvarcalāt palam
children.translated_text: pomegranate and <s>vṛkṣāmla</s> in twice the amount of those two, and two palas of <s>sauvarcala</s>,

children.text: śuṇṭhyāḥ karṣaṃ dadhitthasya madhyāt pañca palāni ca ||
children.translated_text: a karṣa of dry ginger, and five palas from the middle of <s>dadhittha</s>;
that powder should be mixed with sixteen palas of sugar.
This <s>ṣāḍava</s> should be given in foods and drinks as before.
The regimen prescribed for <s>yakṣman</s> is beneficial in <s>kṣata</s>, according to the condition.

children.text: nivṛtte kṣatadoṣe tu kaphe vṛddha uraḥ śiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when the defect of <s>kṣata</s> has ceased, if <s>kapha</s> has increased and the chest and head

children.text: dālyate kāsino yasya sa nā dhūmān pibed imān
children.translated_text: of the coughing man feel as though they are being split, he should inhale these smoke therapies.
On linen well impregnated with pastes of the two <s>medā</s> herbs, the two <s>balā</s> herbs, and <s>yaṣṭī</s>,
one should make a wick and inhale the smoke, followed by <s>jīvanīya</s> ghee.
With <s>manaḥśilā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, bark, <s>kṣīrī</s>, and dry ginger,
the same is done; but the after-drink is water with sugar, sugarcane juice, or jaggery.
Having ground an equal amount of <s>manaḥśilā</s> with a fresh shoot of <s>vaṭa</s>,
one should inhale the smoke with ghee, taking partridge as the following food.

children.text: kṣayaje bṛṃhaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ kuryād agneśca vardhanam ||
children.translated_text: In cough arising from wasting, one should first perform nourishment and increase the digestive fire.
For one with abundant <s>doṣa</s>, one should give a mild purgation accompanied by unction,
with <s>śamyāka</s> and <s>trivṛt</s>, joined with grape juice,
or with a decoction of <s>tilvaka</s> and the fresh juice of <s>vidārī</s>.

children.text: sarpiḥ siddhaṃ pibed yuktyā kṣīṇadeho viśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: A person whose body is wasted should drink properly prepared medicated ghee as purification.

children.text: pitte kaphe dhātuṣu ca kṣīṇeṣu kṣayakāsavān
children.translated_text: A person with wasting cough, when <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and the bodily tissues are depleted,
should drink ghee prepared with <s>karkaṭakī</s>, milk, and the two <s>balā</s> herbs,
or prepared with <s>vidārī</s>, with <s>kadamba</s>, or with young shoots of <s>tāla</s>.
Ghee and milk are used when the urine is discolored and difficult to pass,
when the penis is swollen and painful, and when the anus is affected together with the hips and groins.
He should be given an unctuous enema with light <s>ghṛtamaṇḍa</s> or with <s>miśraka</s>.
After he has been fed with dry-land animal meat, burrow-dwelling animals beginning with <s>vartaka</s>
and then, in sequence, <s>prasaha</s> animals and carnivores should likewise be employed.
Because of their heat and their penetrating, dislodging nature, they loosen <s>kapha</s> from the channels;

children.text: kaphaṃ śuddhaiśca taiḥ puṣṭiṃ kuryāt samyag vahan rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when those channels have been cleared, the nutritive fluid, moving properly, produces nourishment.
With <s>cavikā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>daśamūla</s>, and <s>citraka</s>...
With horse gram, pippalī root, pāṭhā, kola, and barley boiled in water,
and with nāgara, duḥsparśā, pippalī, śaṭhī, and pauṣkara ground up,

children.text: piṣṭaiḥ karkaṭaśṛṅgyā ca samaiḥ sarpir vipācayet ||
children.translated_text: together with karkaṭaśṛṅgī in equal parts, one should cook ghee.

children.text: siddhe 'smiṃścūrṇitau kṣārau dvau pañca lavaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: When this is perfected, the two alkalis and the five salts, powdered,
should be added as appropriate, and a person afflicted by wasting cough should drink a measured dose.
With kāsamarda, abhayā, musta, pāṭhā, kaṭphala, and nāgara,
with pippalī, kaṭurohiṇī, kāśmaryā, and surasa,
each an akṣa in measure, one should cook a prastha of ghee in an āḍhaka of milk and grape juice.
It is auspicious and removes consumption fever, spleen disease, and every cough.
From the leaves, roots, fruits, and sprouts of vṛṣa, vyāghrī, and guḍūcī,
ghee cooked with their juices and pastes destroys cough, fever, and loss of appetite.
Or ghee cooked in twice as much pomegranate juice and joined with vyoṣa,
a man should drink after a meal, mixed with barley alkali.
Or ghee prepared with pippalī and jaggery, mixed with goat's milk, may be used.
These ghees are for increasing the digestive fire in patients with wasting cough.
They are also for purifying the channels of those whose throat and chest are blocked by doṣas.
In a decoction of barley measuring a prastha, one should cook twenty vijayā fruits.

children.text: svinnā mṛditvā tās tasmin purāṇāt ṣaṭpalaṃ guḍāt
children.translated_text: When they are steamed, one should crush them in that liquid and add six palas of old jaggery,
two palas of pippalī, and a karṣa each of manohvā and rasāñjana.

children.text: dattvārdhākṣaṃ paced bhūyaḥ sa lehaḥ śvāsakāsajit
children.translated_text: After adding half an akṣa, one should cook it again; that linctus conquers dyspnea and cough.
Burnt porcupine quills, with ghee, honey, and sugar,
remove dyspnea and cough; or the feet of a peacock may be used with honey and ghee,
or alkali from castor leaves, mixed with vyoṣa, oil, and jaggery.
One should have the patient lick it; or in the same way, alkali produced from surasa and castor leaves.
Or he should lick powder of tryūṣaṇa with old jaggery and ghee.

children.text: padmakaṃ triphalā vyoṣaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ devadāru ca
children.translated_text: Padmaka, triphalā, vyoṣa, viḍaṅga, and devadāru,

children.text: balā rāsnā ca taccūrṇaṃ samastaṃ samaśarkaram ||
children.translated_text: and balā and rāsnā: their powder, all together with an equal amount of sugar,

children.text: khāden madhughṛtābhyāṃ vā lihyāt kāsaharaṃ param
children.translated_text: one should eat, or lick with honey and ghee; it is the supreme remover of cough.
Likewise, powder of marica may be used with ghee, honey, and sugar.
One should hold in the mouth a pill made of pathyā, śuṇṭhī, ghana, and jaggery.
In all cases of dyspnea and cough, or else vibhītaka alone may be used.
A paste of tilvaka leaves, fried in ghee and with sugar,
as a drink or gruel, conquers vomiting, thirst, cough, āma, and diarrhea.
Mung soup, well prepared and cooked in the juice of kaṇṭakārī,
with gaurāmalaka and made sour, is a successful physician for every cough.
In decoctions of medicines that pacify <s>vāta</s>, one should administer milk, soups, and meat juices
from vaiṣkira, prātuda, and baila animals to a patient with wasting cough.

children.text: kṣatakāse ca ye dhūmāḥ sānupānā nidarśitāḥ
children.translated_text: And the smokes, with their accompanying drinks, that were indicated for chest-wound cough,

children.text: kṣayakāse 'pi te yojyā vakṣyate yacca yakṣmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: should also be applied in wasting cough, as also what will be prescribed in <s>yakṣman</s>.

children.text: bṛṃhaṇaṃ dīpanaṃ cāgneḥ srotasāṃ ca viśodhanam
children.translated_text: Nourishing treatment, kindling of the digestive fire, and purification of the channels,
and everything strengthening, used alternately, are praised for patients with wasting cough.
Because wasting cough produced by the combined doṣas is dreadful,
what is beneficial in <s>saṃnipāta</s> is beneficial for it according to the strength of the doṣas.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of dyspnea and hiccup.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Since dyspnea and hiccup have similar causes and related factors, therefore their treatment

children.text: tulyam eva tadārtaṃ ca pūrvaṃ svedairupācaret ||
children.translated_text: is exactly the same; one afflicted by them should first be treated with sudations,

children.text: snigdhair lavaṇatailāktaṃ taiḥ kheṣu grathitaḥ kaphaḥ
children.translated_text: unctuous and anointed with salt and oil. By these, <s>kapha</s> knotted in the channels,
even if firmly stuck, is liquefied; once it has reached the abdomen, it is easily expelled.
There is also softness of the channels and downward movement of <s>marut</s>.

children.text: svinnaṃ ca bhojayed annaṃ snigdham ānūpajai rasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he has been sweated, he should be fed unctuous food with the meat juices of marshland animals,

children.text: dadhyuttareṇa vā dadyāt tato 'smai vamanaṃ mṛdu
children.translated_text: or it may be given with the upper part of curds; then one should give him mild emesis,
especially when there is cough, nausea, cardiac constriction, or loss of voice.
It should be mixed with pippalī, rock salt, and honey, and should not oppose <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: nirhṛte sukham āpnoti sa kaphe duṣṭavigrahe ||
children.translated_text: When the corrupt, embodied <s>kapha</s> has been removed, he obtains comfort.
And when the channels have been purified, <s>anila</s> moves unobstructed.
In abdominal distention, upward movement of vāta, and tamaka dyspnea, with citron and sour vetasa,
food joined with hiṅgu, pīlu, and viḍa should promote downward movement.

children.text: sasaindhavaṃ phalāmlaṃ vā koṣṇaṃ dadyād virecanam ||
children.translated_text: Or one should give a warm purgative with rock salt and sour fruits.
For these arise from aggravation of prāṇa whose course is obstructed by <s>kapha</s>.
Therefore, for purifying its path, cleansing upward and downward is beneficial.
Just as water, when its path is obstructed, surges up much more violently,

children.text: yathā tathānilas tasya mārgam asmād viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: so too does <s>anila</s>; therefore one should clear its path.

children.text: aśāntau kṛtasaṃśuddher dhūmair līnaṃ malaṃ haret
children.translated_text: If there is no pacification after purification has been done, one should remove the hidden impurity with smokes.
Turmeric leaf, castor root, lac, and realgar,
together with devadāru, valā, and māṃsī: grinding these, one should prepare a smoking wick.

children.text: tāṃ ghṛtāktāṃ pibeddhūmaṃ yavān vā ghṛtasaṃyutān ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared it with ghee, he should inhale the smoke; or barley grains joined with ghee may be used,

children.text: madhūcchiṣṭaṃ sarjarasaṃ ghṛtaṃ vā guru vāguru
children.translated_text: or beeswax, sarja resin, ghee, or guru and aguru,

children.text: candanaṃ vā tathā śṛṅgaṃ vālān vā snāva vā gavām ||
children.translated_text: or sandalwood, likewise horn, or the hairs or sinews of cows,
or the hides, horns, and hooves of bear, iguana, antelope, and black antelope,

children.text: gugguluṃ vā manohvāṃ vā śālaniryāsam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or guggulu, manohvā, or śāla resin,

children.text: śallakīṃ gugguluṃ lohaṃ padmakaṃ vā ghṛtāplutam
children.translated_text: or śallakī, guggulu, iron, or padmaka, soaked in ghee.
Those who must necessarily be sweated, even those otherwise unsuitable for sweating, for a moment
one should foment with pleasant warm sprinklings of sugar, milk, and unctuous substances,
and with utkārikā poultices and the medicines stated in the chapter on sudation,

children.text: uraḥ kaṇṭhaṃ ca mṛdubhiḥ sāme tvāmavidhiṃ caret
children.translated_text: using mild measures on the chest and throat; when there is āma, one should follow the āma regimen.
When one sees <s>vāta</s> (wind) driven upward by excessive treatment, one should use wind-subduing measures,
and bring it to calm with unctuous meat juices and the like, not too hot, and with oil massage.
For in those whose <s>kapha</s> has not been stirred up, who have not been sweated, and who are weak, because of purificatory treatment

children.text: vāyur labdhāspado marma saṃśoṣyāśu hared asūn
children.translated_text: the wind, having found a place, dries up the vital points and quickly takes away life.
Therefore one should pacify, in such patients, by astringent decoctions, linctuses, fats, and the like,
hiccup and dyspnea connected with wasting, injury, diarrhea, bleeding <s>pitta</s>, and burning,
using measures that are sweet, unctuous, cooling, and similar.
In a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>daśamūla</s>, meat broths of wild animals may be prepared,
and soups with <s>śigru</s>, eggplant, <s>kāsaghna</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, and radish,
with shoots of <s>nimba</s>, <s>kulaka</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and citron,
with <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, the middle part of <s>bilva</s>, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>,
and with <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>kulattha</s> boiled in water; such should be the soup.
Likewise there may be gruel with <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and the rest, <s>balā</s>, green gram, and <s>citraka</s>,
or a thin gruel made with <s>citraka</s>, cumin, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, and <s>sauvarcala</s> salt,
or with <s>daśamūla</s>; it removes the pain of cough, dyspnea, and hiccup.
With <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
with crab, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>capalā</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, and <s>amṛtauṣadha</s>,

children.text: pibet kaṣāyaṃ jīrṇe 'smin peyāṃ taireva sādhitām
children.translated_text: one should drink a decoction; when that is digested, one should take gruel prepared with those same ingredients.
One should eat <s>śāli</s> rice, sixty-day rice, wheat, barley, green gram, and <s>kulattha</s>,
for the calming of cough, cardiac constriction, side pain, hiccup, and dyspnea.
One should drink barley flour soaked with the milk of tender <s>arka</s> shoots and mixed with honey,
stirred into a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s> and the like.
In food one should use alkali, asafoetida, ghee, <s>viḍa</s> salt, and pomegranate,
together with <s>pauṣkara</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, citron, sour <s>vetasa</s>,
or one should drink a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>, or else of deodar.
A person with hiccup and dyspnea who is thirsty may drink the upper liquid of <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor.
With long pepper, long-pepper root, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>jantughna</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
ground into paste and smeared inside, one should pour buttermilk into a ghee vessel after the paste has dried there.
When kept for a month, that buttermilk kindles digestion and conquers dyspnea and cough.

children.text: pāṭhāṃ madhurasāṃ dāru saralaṃ ca niśi sthitam
children.translated_text: One should drink <s>pāṭhā</s>, sweet-tasting <s>dāru</s>, and <s>sarala</s>, kept overnight
in the upper liquid of liquor, with a little salt, in a measure of one <s>prasṛta</s>.
Or one may take <s>bhārgī</s> and dry ginger with warm water, or alkali mixed with pepper.
Or one should administer <s>bāṣpikā</s>, ground with its own decoction and stirred up.
The fresh juice of <s>saptaparṇa</s>, or of the flowers of <s>śirīṣa</s>,
mixed with honey and pepper, is for hiccup and dyspnea when accompanied by <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
A cake should be made with <s>tugā</s>, black pepper, honey, fried grain, ghee, and dry ginger,
when <s>pitta</s> is associated; but when wind is associated,
it should be prepared with hedgehog and hare meat, pepper, ghee, and porcupine blood.
Milk combined with <s>suvarcalā</s> juice, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and ghee
should be drunk after a meal of <s>śāli</s> rice when wind and <s>pitta</s> are associated.
Or goat's milk cooked with four times as much water, with jaggery and dry ginger, should be drunk.
Long-pepper root, licorice, jaggery, and the liquid from cow and horse dung,
mixed with honey and ghee, should be licked; they remove hiccup, catarrh, and cough.
One may lick, one by one with honey, the liquid from the dung of cow, elephant, horse, boar, camel, donkey, sheep, or goat,
or, when there is much phlegm, one may drink it.
One with dyspnea in whom <s>kapha</s> is excessive should likewise lick ash produced from the hide, hair, bones, hooves, and horns of quadrupeds,
and similarly the ash of <s>vājigandhā</s>.
Or one may take <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>pauṣkara</s>, and emblic myrobalan, or <s>pauṣkara</s> with pepper,
or red ochre, collyrium, and black pepper, or the fresh juice of wood apple.
Or with the juice of wood apple one may take emblic myrobalan, rock salt, and long pepper;
or with ghee and honey, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>uṣaṇa</s>, and long pepper;
or jujube, parched grain, emblic myrobalan, grapes, long pepper, and dry ginger;
or jaggery, oil, turmeric, grapes, pepper, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>uṣaṇa</s>.
One should drink the powders of linctus-medicines with meat juice, water, wine, or sour liquids.
<s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>surasā</s>, bark, the two cardamoms, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
<s>caṇḍā</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, iron, <s>bhārgī</s>, dry ginger, and <s>vālaka</s>,
the plant called <s>karkaṭa</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, black pepper, <s>nāgakesara</s>, and <s>coraka</s>,
made into a powder with twice as much sugar and used as desired,
removes pain in the side, fever, and cough, and is supreme for removing hiccup and dyspnea.
A powder of <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>caṇḍā</s>, <s>vālaka</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
with eight times as much sugar, is supreme for removing hiccup and dyspnea.

children.text: tulyaṃ guḍaṃ nāgaraṃ ca bhakṣayen nāvayeta vā
children.translated_text: One may eat equal parts jaggery and dry ginger, or use as a nasal medicine

children.text: laśunasya palāṇḍor vā mūlaṃ gṛñjanakasya vā ||
children.translated_text: the root of garlic, onion, or carrot.

children.text: candanād vā rasaṃ dadyān nārīkṣīreṇa nāvanam
children.translated_text: Or one should give the juice of sandalwood as a nasal instillation with coconut milk,
or fly excrement with breast milk or with the juice of lac dye.

children.text: sasaindhavaṃ ghṛtācchaṃ vā siddhaṃ stanyena vā ghṛtam
children.translated_text: Or one may use clear ghee with rock salt as a nasal medicine, or ghee cooked with breast milk.

children.text: kalkitair madhuradravyais tat piben nāvayeta vā ||
children.translated_text: With sweet substances ground into paste, one should drink that ghee or use it nasally.
One should take it once hot and once cold, alternately, with sugar and honey.

children.text: tadvat payas tathā siddham adhobhāgauṣadhair ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise milk, and ghee cooked with medicines acting on the lower part of the body, may be used.
With pepper, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, alkali, <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, asafoetida, and <s>coraka</s>,
together with <s>kāyastha</s>, one should cook ghee in whey and the juice of <s>daśamūla</s>.

children.text: tat pibej jīvanīyair vā lihyāt samadhu sādhitam
children.translated_text: One should drink that, or lick ghee prepared with the life-promoting drugs and honey.
<s>Tejovatī</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, long pepper, <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,
<s>bhūtika</s>, <s>pauṣkara</s> root, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>śaṭhī</s>,
the two salts, <s>tāmalakī</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and a piece of <s>bilva</s>,

children.text: vacā pattraṃ ca tālīśaṃ karṣāṃśais tair vipācayet
children.translated_text: <s>vacā</s>, leaf, and <s>tālīśa</s>: with these, in one-<s>karṣa</s> portions, one should cook

children.text: hiṅgupādair ghṛtaprasthaṃ pītam āśu nihanti tat ||
children.translated_text: a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with quarter portions of asafoetida; when drunk, it quickly destroys
<s>śākhānila</s> disorders, piles, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, hiccup, and pain in the heart and sides.
One should drink ghee with half a portion of alkali, or else with something pungent.
Or one may use <s>Dhānvantara</s> ghee, <s>Vṛṣa</s> ghee, <s>Dādhika</s>, or the preparation beginning with <s>hapuṣā</s>.
Sudden sprinkling with cold water, fright, startling movements, fear, and grief,
as well as joy, jealousy, holding the breath, and bites by insects, are beneficial.
Whatever removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, is hot, and makes <s>vāta</s> move downward,

children.text: tat sevyaṃ prāyaśo yacca sutarāṃ mārutāpaham
children.translated_text: that should generally be used, and especially whatever dispels <s>māruta</s>.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bṛṃhaṇe hyalpaḥ śakyaśca prāyaśo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For all these disorders, nourishing therapy is usually manageable even in a small measure;
but in pacifying treatment there should not be excessive depletion, and strong wasting treatment is usually impracticable.
Therefore one should treat them mostly with pacifying and nourishing measures.
Cough, dyspnea, wasting, vomiting, and hiccup are also treated with one another's medicines.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>rājayakṣmā</s> and related disorders.
So indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
For a strong patient with <s>yakṣmā</s>, having abundant <s>doṣas</s>, after oiling and sweating,

children.text: ūrdhvādho yakṣmiṇaḥ kuryāt sasnehaṃ yanna karśanam ||
children.translated_text: one should perform purification upward and downward, with unctuousness, in such a way that it does not cause emaciation.
He should be made to vomit with milk combined with emetic fruit, or with a sweet meat broth,
or with a gruel containing ghee and prepared with emetic substances.
For purgation one should give <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, and <s>nṛpadruma</s>,
combined with sugar, honey, and ghee, or with milk or nourishing drink,
or joined with the juices of grapes, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and meat.
When the bowel has been purified, one should apply a regimen that nourishes and kindles digestion.
Foods and drinks should be pleasing to the heart, <s>vāta</s>-relieving, and light.
Rice, sixty-day rice, wheat, barley, and mung beans, properly prepared warm,

children.text: ājaṃ kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ māṃsaṃ kravyānmāṃsaṃ ca śoṣajit
children.translated_text: as well as goat's milk, ghee, meat, and the meat of carnivorous animals, overcome wasting.
The flesh of crows, owls, wolves, panthers, cattle, horses, mongooses, snakes,
vultures, <s>bhāsa</s> birds, donkeys, and camels is beneficial when served in disguise.

children.text: jñātaṃ jugupsitaṃ taddhi chardiṣe na balaujase ||
children.translated_text: For when it is recognized as repulsive, it produces vomiting, not strength and vigor.
Deer and similar meats are suitable when <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> predominate; animals of the <s>prasaha</s> class and the like are suitable when <s>vāta</s> predominates.
They are wholesome when made into <s>vesavāra</s> relish and prepared in broths and similar dishes.
They should be fried in mustard oil or in ghee, as appropriate,
made juicy, soft, and unctuous, and seasoned with pungent substances.
Soups prepared from radish and horse gram are also beneficial in the same way.
One should drink fatty goat-meat broth with <s>pippalī</s>, barley, horse gram, and dry ginger,

children.text: sadāḍimaṃ sāmalakaṃ snigdham ājaṃ rasaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: with pomegranate and emblic myrobalan.
By that, the six disorders beginning with <s>pīnasa</s> turn back.
One should especially drink old wine, which cleanses the channels.
When <s>pitta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s> are involved, mead, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and clear <s>vāruṇī</s> are particularly useful.
Or one may use water prepared with <s>pañcamūla</s> or with <s>tāmalakī</s>,
or with the four leafy drugs, or with coriander and dry ginger.
With that, the careful physician should arrange for him clean food that is agreeable.
Ghee cooked with <s>daśamūla</s>, milk, or meat broth,
with <s>balā</s> as its paste, should be prescribed, or else with the meat broth of carnivorous animals.

children.text: sakṣaudraṃ payasā siddhaṃ sarpir daśaguṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: Or ghee cooked with milk ten times its quantity should be used together with honey.

children.text: jīvantīṃ madhukaṃ drākṣāṃ phalāni kuṭajasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvantī</s>, licorice, grapes, the fruits of <s>kuṭaja</s>,

children.text: puṣkarāhvaṃ śaṭhīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ vyāghrīṃ gokṣurakaṃ balām ||
children.translated_text: <s>puṣkarāhva</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, black pepper, <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
blue lotus, <s>tāmalakī</s>, <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, and <s>durālabhā</s>:
having made these into a paste, one should cook ghee; it is the supreme remover of the king of diseases.
Ghee prepared with dates, raisins, licorice, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
together with <s>pippalī</s>, removes hoarseness, cough, dyspnea, and fever.

children.text: daśamūlaśṛtāt kṣīrāt sarpir yad udiyān navam
children.translated_text: The fresh ghee that rises from milk boiled with <s>daśamūla</s>,
with <s>pippalī</s> and honey, is the best awakener of the voice.
It removes pain in the head, flanks, and shoulders, and removes cough, dyspnea, and fever.

children.text: pañcabhiḥ pañcamūlair vā śṛtād yad udiyād ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Or the ghee that rises from milk boiled with the five sets of five roots,
cooked in the decoction of the five <s>pañcamūlas</s> with four times as much milk,

children.text: siddhaṃ sarpir jayatyetad yakṣmaṇaḥ saptakaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: that ghee conquers the sevenfold <s>yakṣmā</s> and gives strength.
One should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with six <s>palas</s> of <s>pañcakola</s> and barley alkali,
with an equal quantity of milk; it cleanses the channels.
It conquers <s>gulma</s>, fever, abdominal disease, splenic disease, <s>grahaṇī</s>, anemia, and <s>pīnasa</s>,
as well as dyspnea, cough, weakness of digestion, swelling, and upward-moving <s>vāta</s>.
In water decocted with <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, and <s>varṣābhū</s>,
ghee containing <s>jīvantī</s> and <s>pippalī</s>, and cooked with milk, conquers wasting.
So too ghee from milk boiled with <s>aśvagandhā</s>, together with sugar-water.
One should cook a <s>tulā</s> of ordinary meat in two <s>droṇas</s> of water.
When one eighth remains, one should prepare a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with that and with life-promoting drugs measured by the <s>pala</s>.
This removes disorders of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
This meat-ghee, drunk by itself or combined with meat broth,
conquers cough, dyspnea, loss of voice, wasting, and pain in the heart and flanks.
Cardamom, wild celery, <s>triphala</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, the three pungents, and <s>citraka</s>,
and the heartwoods obtained from <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>gāyatrī</s>, <s>śāla</s>, and <s>bīja</s>,
as well as <s>bhallātaka</s> and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, each measured separately at eight <s>palas</s>,
should be cooked in sixteen times as much water until one sixteenth remains.

children.text: punas tena ghṛtaprasthaṃ siddhe cāsmin palāni ṣaṭ
children.translated_text: Again, with that decoction one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee; when it is prepared,

children.text: tavakṣīryāḥ kṣipet triṃśat sitāyā dviguṇaṃ madhu ||
children.translated_text: one should add six <s>palas</s> of <s>tavakṣīrī</s>, thirty of sugar, and twice as much honey.

children.text: ghṛtāt trijātāt tripalaṃ tato līḍhaṃ khajāhatam
children.translated_text: Then three <s>palas</s> of the three aromatics are added to the ghee, and the mixture is beaten with a churner and licked.
With milk as the after-drink, taken in the morning, it is an unrestricted <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: medhyaṃ cakṣuṣyam āyuṣyaṃ dīpanaṃ hanti cācirāt
children.translated_text: It benefits intelligence, eyesight, and lifespan, kindles digestion, and quickly destroys
<s>meha</s>, <s>gulma</s>, wasting disease, anemia, and fistula-in-ano.

children.text: ye ca sarpirguḍāḥ proktāḥ kṣate yojyāḥ kṣaye 'pi te
children.translated_text: And the ghee-jaggery preparations that were prescribed for chest injury should be used also in wasting.
Bark, cardamom, long pepper, <s>kṣīrī</s>, and sugar should be taken in successively doubled quantities.
Powdered and eaten, or licked with honey and ghee,
they benefit the voice and destroy cough, consumption, dyspnea, pain in the side, and <s>kapha</s>.
Especially in this loss of voice, one should apply nasal therapy, therapeutic smoking, and the like.
Even there, when it is caused by <s>vāta</s>, one should drink, warm and after a meal,
ghee cooked with the fresh juices of <s>kāsamardaka</s>, <s>vārtākī</s>, and <s>mārkava</s>;

children.text: sādhitaṃ kāsajit svaryaṃ siddham ārtagalena vā ||
children.translated_text: it conquers cough and benefits the voice, or the same may be prepared with <s>ārtagala</s>.
Or one may use paste of jujube leaves, fried in ghee and mixed with rock salt,
or oil cooked with <s>madhuka</s>, grapes, long pepper, <s>kṛminut</s>, blue lotus,
and the root of <s>haṃsapadī</s>; one should pour it into the nose.
He should eat rice with jaggery and ghee, with warm water as the after-drink,

children.text: aśnīyāt pāyasaṃ caivaṃ snigdhaṃ svedaṃ niyojayet
children.translated_text: and also milk-rice; in this way he should employ unctuous fomentation.
When it arises from <s>pitta</s>, he should drink ghee followed by boiled and cooled milk,
prepared with decoction and paste of shoots of latex-bearing trees and mixed with honey.
He should also eat milk-rice made with licorice and ghee.
Ghee prepared with <s>balā</s>, <s>vidārigandhā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>,

children.text: siddhaṃ salavaṇaṃ sarpir nasyaṃ svaryam anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>madhuka</s>, with salt, is the unsurpassed nasal remedy for improving the voice.
<s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, long pepper, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>balā</s>,

children.text: sādhitaṃ kṣīrasarpiśca tat svaryaṃ nāvanaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: cooked with milk and ghee, make an excellent voice-improving nasal instillation.
He should lick the powder of sweet drugs soaked with honey and ghee.
In the <s>kapha</s>-born condition, eating dry food, he should drink pungent drugs with urine.
He should lick <s>kaṭphala</s>, emblic myrobalan, and <s>vyoṣa</s>, moistened with oil and honey,
or <s>vyoṣa</s>, alkali, <s>agni</s>, <s>cavikā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, and honey.
He should drink barley gruel made with <s>kaṇā</s> and <s>dhātrī</s> in the two fats.

children.text: bhuktvādyāt pippalīṃ śuṇṭhīṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vā vamanaṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: After eating he should take long pepper and dry ginger, or resort to sharp emesis.
One whose voice has been injured by speaking loudly
should drink milks boiled with sweet drugs and mixed with sugar and honey.
When there is anorexia, varied food made agreeable with wholesome adjuncts is beneficial.
External and internal cleansing, calming of the mind, and pleasant medicine are beneficial.
At the two proper times he should chew a tooth-cleaning twig, and with mouth-washes

children.text: kaṣāyaiḥ kṣālayed āsyaṃ dhūmaṃ prāyogikaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: of astringent decoctions he should rinse the mouth and drink the habitual therapeutic smoke.
Tablets of <s>tālīśa</s> powder, with camphor and sugar candy,
and those called <s>Śaśāṅkakiraṇa</s>, are especially appetite-producing things to be eaten.
There, in anorexia caused by <s>vāta</s>, he should drink with clear wine a powder
made from <s>hareṇu</s>, black pepper, <s>kṛmijit</s>, grapes, rock salt, and dry ginger,
together with cardamom, <s>bhārgī</s>, barley-alkali, and asafoetida, or he may take it with ghee.
Or he should vomit with water containing <s>vacā</s>; when it is from <s>pitta</s>, with jaggery-water.
Or he should lick sugar, ghee, the best salt, and honey.
When it is from <s>kapha</s>, he should vomit with neem-water; water of <s>dīpyaka</s> and <s>āragvadha</s>
is for drinking, as are sharp <s>ariṣṭas</s> with honey and <s>mādhavas</s> with honey.
He should also drink the previously mentioned powder beginning with <s>hareṇu</s> with hot water.
Cardamom, bark, <s>nāgakusuma</s>, pungent pepper, long pepper, and dry ginger,
made into a powder with each part successively increased and with an equal amount of sugar,
destroy salivation, anorexia, diseases of the heart, side, cough, dyspnea, and throat.
<s>Yavānī</s>, <s>tintiḍīka</s>, sour <s>vetasa</s>, dry ginger, pomegranate,

children.text: kṛtvā kolaṃ ca karṣāṃśaṃ sitāyāśca catuḥpalam
children.translated_text: and <s>kola</s> should each be made one <s>karṣa</s>; sugar should be four <s>palas</s>.
Coriander, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, cumin, and cinnamon should each be half a <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: pippalīnāṃ śataṃ caikaṃ dve śate maricasya ca
children.translated_text: There should be one hundred long peppers and two hundred black peppers.

children.text: cūrṇam etat paraṃ rucyaṃ hṛdyaṃ grāhi hinasti ca ||
children.translated_text: This powder is supremely savory, pleasing to the heart, absorbent, and it destroys
constipation, cough, disorders of the heart, side, spleen, piles, and <s>grahaṇī</s>.
<s>Tālīśapattra</s>, black pepper, dry ginger, and excellent long pepper,
in successively increasing quantities, with bark and cardamom each in half-parts,
make a savory, kindling powder, with sugar eight times the amount of <s>kaṇā</s>.
It removes cough, dyspnea, anorexia, vomiting, spleen disease, and pain in the heart and side;
it cures anemia, fever, and diarrhea, and it moves obstructed <s>vāta</s> downward.
For salivation, barley soaked overnight in water of alkali from <s>arka</s> and <s>amṛtā</s>

children.text: praseke kalpitān saktūn bhakṣyāṃścādyād balī vamet ||
children.translated_text: should be made into parched flour; one should eat foods made from it, and, if strong, should vomit.

children.text: kaṭutiktais tathā śūlyaṃ bhakṣayej jāṅgalaṃ palam
children.translated_text: He should also eat roasted meat of wild animals, seasoned with pungent and bitter substances,
and dry, very light foods, followed by broths such as chickpea soup.
When, because of excessive salivation from <s>śleṣman</s>, <s>vāyu</s> drives the <s>śleṣman</s> out,
the wise physician should overcome that salivation from <s>kapha</s> with warm unctuous measures alone.

children.text: pīnase 'pi kramam imaṃ vamathau ca prayojayet
children.translated_text: In <s>pīnasa</s> also, and in vomiting, he should employ this procedure.
Especially in <s>pīnasa</s>, he should habitually use massage, oleation, and fomentation.
With unctuous lumps of <s>utkārikā</s> on the head, side, throat, and other parts,
he should use salty, sour, pungent, and hot soups combined with fat.
For pains in the head, shoulder, and side, he should act according to the rule for the doṣa.
Well-prepared poultices with the flesh of aquatic and marsh animals
are desired there, together with the four fats; they are also recommended when doṣas are combined.
A paste with <s>nata</s>, licorice, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and sandalwood is used;
likewise with <s>balā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, sesame, and with ghee, <s>madhuka</s>, and blue lotus,
and with <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>kṛṣṇagandhā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, and <s>vidārī</s>.
Nasal instillations, therapeutic smoking, and oleations after meals are useful,
as are oils suitable for massage and, above all, enema therapy.

children.text: śṛṅgādyair vā yathādoṣaṃ duṣṭam eṣāṃ hared asṛk
children.translated_text: Or, according to the doṣa, one should remove the vitiated blood from these parts by horns and similar means.
A poultice with <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and sandalwood, together with ghee, is best,
or one with <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, madder, and saffron soaked in ghee,
or with oil cooked with the banyan group, and with ghee washed one hundred times.
<s>Abhyaṅga</s> (oil massage), sprinkling with milk, and also sprinkling with <s>madhuka</s>-water are recommended.
Because the digestive fire is generally impaired, he passes diarrhea with mucus.
For him, the medicines prescribed for <s>atisāra</s> (diarrhea) and <s>grahaṇī</s> are beneficial.
One should carefully preserve the stool of a patient with <s>rājayakṣman</s> as he dries up.
For one afflicted by loss of all the tissues, his strength is strength based on feces.

children.text: māṃsam evāśnato yuktyā mārdvīkaṃ pibato 'nu ca ||
children.translated_text: When he eats meat alone in the proper manner and afterward drinks <s>mārdvīka</s> wine,
and does not suppress the natural urges, <s>yakṣman</s> finds no opening.
He should drink <s>surā</s> with its scum, <s>mārdvīka</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>s, <s>sīdhu</s>, and <s>mādhava</s> drinks,
as appropriate, as after-drinks while eating meats.
That is for releasing obstruction of the channels and for nourishing strength and <s>ojas</s>.
One should immerse him, well anointed, in tubs of oil, milk, and water.

children.text: uttīrṇaṃ miśrakaiḥ snehair bhūyo 'bhyaktaṃ sukhaiḥ karaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he has come out, anointed again with mixed fats, with gentle hands

children.text: mṛdnīyāt sukham āsīnaṃ sukhaṃ codvartayet param
children.translated_text: one should comfortably knead him as he sits at ease, and then rub him pleasantly.
<s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>śatavīryā</s>, and <s>vikasā</s> together with <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
<s>vidārī</s>, mustard seeds, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, rice grains, and flaxseed,

children.text: māṣāṃs tilāṃśca kiṇvaṃ ca sarvam ekatra cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: <s>māṣa</s> beans, sesame seeds, and yeast: all of these should be powdered together.
Barley flour, three times as much, should be mixed with curds and honey.
This rubbing powder should be prepared; it gives nourishment, complexion, and strength.
With a paste of white mustard and with bathing herbs, he
should bathe in waters comfortable for the season, prepared with life-promoting herbs.
He should resort to perfumes, garlands, and other ornaments, which destroy misfortune.
The sight of friends and hearing of song, instrumental music, and festivals,
<s>basti</s>s, milk, ghee, and good habits regarding wine and meat,
and each <s>daivavyapāśraya</s> measure taught in the Atharvan tradition are praised.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of vomiting, heart disease, and thirst.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Vomiting generally arises from agitation in the stomach; therefore, what is beneficial

children.text: laṅghanaṃ prāg ṛte vāyor vamanaṃ tatra yojayet ||
children.translated_text: at first is fasting, except in that due to <s>vāyu</s>; in such a case one should employ emesis.
For one who is strong, has abundant <s>doṣa</s>, and vomits much continually,

children.text: tato virekaṃ kramaśo hṛdyaṃ madyaiḥ phalāmbubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, in gradual order, one should give purgation pleasing to the heart, with wines and fruit waters,

children.text: kṣīrair vā saha sa hyūrdhvaṃ gataṃ doṣaṃ nayatyadhaḥ
children.translated_text: or with milk; for it leads downward the <s>doṣa</s> that has gone upward.

children.text: śamanaṃ cauṣadhaṃ rūkṣadurbalasya tad eva tu ||
children.translated_text: For one who is dry and weak, however, the medicine should be pacifying.

children.text: pariśuṣkaṃ priyaṃ sātmyam annaṃ laghu ca śasyate
children.translated_text: Food that is dry, agreeable, wholesome, and light is recommended.

children.text: upavāsas tathā yūṣā rasāḥ kāmbalikāḥ khalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too are fasting, soups, meat juices, <s>kāmbalika</s>s, and <s>khala</s>s,
vegetables, linctuses, foods to be eaten, <s>rāga</s>s, <s>ṣāḍava</s>s, and drinks,
dry and varied edibles, fruits, bathing, and rubbing.
Pleasant fragrances born from scented fruits, flowers, foods, and drinks are also recommended.
Sprinkling cold water on the mouth immediately after eating

children.text: hanti mārutajāṃ chardiṃ sarpiḥ pītaṃ sasaindhavam
children.translated_text: destroys vomiting caused by <s>māruta</s>; ghee drunk with rock salt,
somewhat warm, is especially useful when there is cough and palpitation of the heart.
Or ghee rich in <s>vyoṣa</s> and the three salts, or cooked with pomegranate juice, may be used.
Or milk boiled with dry ginger, curds, and coriander, with an equal amount of water,
or soup of <s>vaiṣkira</s> birds, clearly mixed with rock salt and ghee and made sour with fruit,
and unctuous food prepared with dry ginger, curds, and pomegranate,
warm and with salt, is beneficial here; so too is unctuous purgation.
In vomiting due to <s>pitta</s>, for purgation, <s>trivṛt</s> with fresh grape and sugarcane juices

children.text: sarpir vā tailvakaṃ yojyaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca śleṣmadhāmagam
children.translated_text: or <s>tailvaka</s> ghee should be applied; and when increased <s>pitta</s> has gone to the seat of <s>śleṣman</s>,

children.text: ūrdhvam eva haret pittaṃ svādutiktair viśuddhimān ||
children.translated_text: one who has been purified should draw that <s>pitta</s> out upward with sweet and bitter substances.

children.text: piben manthaṃ yavāgūṃ vā lājaiḥ samadhuśarkarām
children.translated_text: He should drink <s>mantha</s> or gruel made with parched grain, with honey and sugar,
and should eat <s>śāli</s> and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with sauces made from <s>mudga</s> and dry-land meat.
He should drink very cold water produced from clods roasted in an earthen vessel,
or water kept overnight together with <s>mudga</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and coriander.

children.text: drākṣārasaṃ rasaṃ vekṣor guḍūcyambu payo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Or he may drink grape juice, sugarcane juice, <s>guḍūcī</s>-water, or milk.
A decoction made from tender shoots of <s>jambu</s> and mango, <s>uśīra</s>, and shoots and aerial roots of <s>vaṭa</s>,

children.text: kvāthaḥ kṣaudrayutaḥ pītaḥ śīto vā viniyacchati
children.translated_text: drunk cold with honey, restrains

children.text: chardiṃ jvaram atīsāraṃ mūrchāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ ca durjayām ||
children.translated_text: vomiting, fever, diarrhea, fainting, and hard-to-conquer thirst.

children.text: dhātrīrasena vā śītaṃ piben mudgadalāmbu vā
children.translated_text: Or one should drink cold <s>dhātrī</s> juice, or water from split <s>mudga</s>.
The marrow of <s>kola</s>, sugar, parched grain, <s>mākṣika</s> mineral, and <s>kaṇāñjana</s>

children.text: lihyāt kṣaudreṇa pathyāṃ vā drākṣāṃ vā badarāṇi vā
children.translated_text: one should lick with honey; or else <s>pathyā</s>, grapes, or badara fruits.
In vomiting due to <s>kapha</s>, one should make him vomit with <s>nimba</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>piṇḍīta</s>, and mustard,
combined with warm water; and one should make a weak patient fast.
He should drink a cold decoction of the <s>āragvadhādi</s> group, mixed with honey,
or repeated <s>mantha</s>s made with barley impregnated with anti-vomiting medicines.

children.text: kaphaghnam annaṃ hṛdyaṃ ca rāgāḥ sārjakabhūstṛṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Food that reduces <s>kapha</s> and is pleasing to the heart is beneficial, as are <s>rāga</s>s with <s>sārjaka</s> and <s>bhūstṛṇa</s>.
Realgar, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, and black pepper, licked with the juice of <s>bījapūraka</s>,
or with the honeyed juice of <s>kapittha</s>, conquers vomiting.

children.text: khādet kapitthaṃ savyoṣaṃ madhunā vā durālabhām
children.translated_text: He should eat <s>kapittha</s> with <s>vyoṣa</s>, or <s>durālabhā</s> with honey.
He should lick black pepper, <s>coca</s>, cardamom, cow-dung juice, and honey.
Vomiting caused by disliked objects comes to pacification through agreeable treatment.
Vomiting caused by worms is conquered by physicians through the treatments stated for worms and heart disease,
and the remaining varieties, as well as the diseases produced by them, should be treated according to each case.

children.text: chardiprasaṅgena hi mātariśvā dhātukṣayāt kopam upaityavaśyam
children.translated_text: For, when vomiting persists, <s>mātariśvan</s> is necessarily aggravated because of depletion of the tissues.
Therefore, in this condition, one should carry out the procedure described for excessive emesis: checking and nourishing.
Ghee, jaggery, meat broth, and medicated ghees prepared with <s>kalyāṇaka</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and life-promoting drugs,

children.text: payāṃsi pathyopahitāni lehāśchardiṃ prasaktāṃ praśamaṃ nayanti ||
children.translated_text: as well as milks combined with <s>pathyā</s> and linctuses, bring persistent vomiting to quiet.
In heart disease caused by <s>vāta</s>, one should drink oil mixed with whey, <s>sauvīra</s>, or buttermilk,
warm and with salt; it conquers <s>gulma</s>, distension, and pain.

children.text: tailaṃ ca lavaṇaiḥ siddhaṃ samūtrāmlaṃ tathāguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Oil cooked with salts, cow urine, and sour liquids has the same property.

children.text: bilvaṃ rāsnāṃ yavān kolaṃ devadāruṃ punarnavām
children.translated_text: Having boiled <s>bilva</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, barley, jujube, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: kulatthān pañcamūlaṃ ca paktvā tasmin pacejjale ||
children.translated_text: horse gram and <s>pañcamūla</s> in water, one should cook oil in that water.

children.text: tailaṃ tan nāvane pāne vastau ca viniyojayet
children.translated_text: That should be used for nasal therapy, drinking, and enema.
Ghee boiled with dry ginger, <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, salts, <s>kāyasthā</s>, asafoetida, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
and with <s>pathyā</s>, conquers pain in the flank and heart and <s>gulma</s>.
A <s>prastha</s> of ghee cooked with two <s>palas</s> of <s>sauvarcala</s> salt and fifty <s>pathyās</s>
conquers heart disease, dyspnea, and <s>gulma</s>.
Pomegranate, black salt, dry ginger, asafoetida, and <s>amlavetasa</s>
make an excellent powder that destroys <s>apatantraka</s>, heart disease, and dyspnea.
<s>Puṣkarāhva</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, dry ginger, citron root, and <s>abhayā</s>,
drunk after being made into a paste and combined with alkali, ghee, sour liquid, and salt,
remove cutting pain and colic; a warm decoction has the same property.
A preparation made with wild celery, salt, alkali, <s>vacā</s>, cumin, and <s>auṣadha</s>,
with <s>pūtidāru</s>, <s>bījāhva</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
and with <s>pañcakola</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, jaggery, <s>bījāhva</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
made into a paste with <s>vāruṇī</s>, fried in the two fats, and mixed with salt,
should be eaten for pains of the heart, flank, and uterus, and for <s>gulma</s> and abdominal disease.

children.text: snigdhāśceha hitāḥ svedāḥ saṃskṛtāni ghṛtāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Here unctuous fomentations are beneficial, as are processed ghees.

children.text: laghunā pañcamūlena śuṇṭhyā vā sādhitaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: When thirsty, one should drink water cooked with light <s>pañcamūla</s> or with dry ginger,

children.text: vāruṇīdadhimaṇḍaṃ vā dhānyāmlaṃ vā pibet tṛṣi ||
children.translated_text: or <s>vāruṇī</s>, curd whey, or grain-sour gruel.
When the heart is affected by <s>māruta</s> with constriction, stiffness, pain, and <s>āma</s>,
this is the treatment; but when there is fluidity, constriction, and fainting, meat broths are beneficial.
They should be rich in fat, from partridge, <s>krauñca</s>, peacock, quail, and fowl.
A person with heart disease should drink <s>balā</s> oil, or <s>sukumāraka</s>,
or the excellent <s>mahāsneha</s> cooked a hundred times with licorice.
