One should cook <s>mahāsneha</s> with <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
with <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and the three pungents.
With one quarter curd and with sour liquids as obtainable, it is to be used;
it nourishes, builds bulk, gives strength, and destroys <s>vāta</s> heart disease.
In <s>vāta</s>-type heart disease, when the digestive fire is bright and fluid constriction is present, beneficial are
milk, curd, jaggery, ghee, and the meat of aquatic and marsh animals.
These same things are to be avoided in all the other four kinds of heart disease,
and even in the <s>vāta</s> type when it is associated with stiffness, dullness, and <s>āma</s>.
But when <s>kapha</s> is connected with it, one should apply dry and hot treatment.
In the <s>pitta</s> type, purgation suited to the heart should be combined with grapes, sugarcane juice, sugar, honey, and <s>parūṣaka</s>.

children.text: yukto vireko hṛdyaḥ syāt kramaḥ śuddhe ca pittahā ||
children.translated_text: Once the patient is purified, the regimen should be <s>pitta</s>-pacifying.
The external and internal cleansing taught for injury, <s>pitta</s> disorder, and fever should also be used.
One should drink a paste of <s>kaṭvī</s> and licorice with sugared water.
<s>Śreyasī</s>, sugar, grapes, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and blue lotus,
with <s>balā</s>, dates, <s>kākolī</s>, and the two <s>medās</s>, are cooked
in buffalo ghee with milk; this destroys <s>pitta</s> heart disease.
<s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s>, licorice, lotus fiber knots, and <s>serukā</s>,
together with dry ginger and moss: with these one should cook ghee with milk.

children.text: śītaṃ samadhu tacceṣṭaṃ svāduvargakṛtaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: It is best used cold and with honey, as is ghee prepared from the sweet group.

children.text: vastiṃ ca dadyāt sakṣaudraṃ tailaṃ madhukasādhitam
children.translated_text: One should also give an enema with honey, and oil cooked with licorice.
In one arising from <s>kapha</s>, after fomentation, one should cause vomiting with water of <s>picumanda</s> and <s>vacā</s>.
He should eat horse gram, soup of desert animals, strong liquor, and barley.
He should drink a powder of <s>vacā</s>, asafoetida, the two salts, and dry ginger,
with cardamom, wild celery, <s>kaṇā</s>, and barley alkali, taking warm water with it.
Likewise he may take it with sour drinks from fruits and grains, horse-gram soup, urine preparations, and <s>āsava</s>.
And he should drink a decoction of <s>puṣkarāhva</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, dry ginger, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>,
and likewise a decoction of <s>abhayā</s>, dry ginger, <s>mādrī</s>, <s>pītadru</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s>.
In a decoction of <s>rohītaka</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, and <s>arjuna</s>,
with <s>palāśa</s> and banyan, a linctus prepared with powder of the three pungents and <s>trivṛt</s>,
and followed by warm water as the after-drink, removes disorders of <s>kapha</s>.
One should drink the ghees and various alkalis prescribed for <s>śleṣma-gulma</s>.
Or here one should apply <s>śilājatu</s> or <s>brāhma rasāyana</s>,
or <s>āmalaka</s> linctus, or the preparation made by <s>Agastya</s>.

children.text: syācchūlaṃ yasya bhukte 'ti jīryatyalpaṃ jarāṃ gate
children.translated_text: For one whose pain occurs after eating, when only a little digestion has taken place,
it is pacified by <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kṛmijit</s>, the two salts, and <s>tilvaka</s>,
with <s>devadāru</s> and <s>ativiṣā</s>; he should drink the powder with hot water.

children.text: yasya jīrṇe 'dhikaṃ snehaiḥ sa virecyaḥ phalaiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one whose pain is greater when the food is digested, he should be oleated and then purged with fruits;

children.text: jīryatyanne tathā mūlais tīkṣṇaiḥ śūle sadādhike
children.translated_text: and likewise, when pain is constantly excessive while food is digesting, with sharp roots.
Generally <s>anila</s>, its movement obstructed, becomes aggravated when it has entered the stomach;
for that, downward-moving treatment should be done with purification, fasting, and digestives.
In heart disease caused by worms, every worm-destroying medicine is appropriate.
In thirst disorders, a method that mostly reduces <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> is recommended;
in all of them it should be cooling externally and internally, and both pacifying and cleansing.

children.text: divyāmbu śītaṃ sakṣaudraṃ tadvad bhaumaṃ ca tadguṇam
children.translated_text: Rainwater, cold and mixed with honey, and likewise terrestrial water possessing the same qualities,
cooled with heated clods, potsherds, sand, and the like,

children.text: saśarkaraṃ vā kvathitaṃ pañcamūlena vā jalam
children.translated_text: or water boiled with sugar, or with <s>pañcamūla</s>, may be used.
A <s>mantha</s> drink prepared with <s>darbha</s> as the first ingredient and with flour of parched grain is recommended.
So too a cool <s>vāṭya</s>, made with unripe barley and furnished with sugar and honey,
and a <s>yavāgū</s> gruel made from <s>śāli</s> rice, likewise, and from old <s>kodrava</s> grain.
Food should be cooked with cold water and with substances of cooling potency.
Milk sprinkled with icy water, together with sugar and honey, is also suitable.
So are broths of wild animals that are not sour or salty and have been fried in ghee,
and likewise soups of <s>mudga</s> and the like, combined with life-promoting juices.

children.text: nasyaṃ kṣīraghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ śītairikṣos tathā rasaḥ
children.translated_text: As nasal therapy, milk and ghee cooked with cooling substances are used; so too sugarcane juice.
Cooling gargles, as taught in the <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>, are beneficial.
Pastes and other applications prescribed for burning fever are useful, along with freedom from exertion and pleasing the mind.
So too are the sight and recollection of great rivers, lakes, and the like.
In thirst arising from <s>vāta</s>, curds with jaggery are praised.
Cooling, nourishing meat broths are also praised, and water prepared with the <s>vidāryādi</s> group.
In thirst born of <s>pitta</s>, the juice of ripe <s>udumbara</s> mixed with sugar is recommended.
Or its decoction may be taken cold; likewise water prepared with the <s>śārivādi</s> group.
With groups of that kind one should prepare cold decoctions with sugar and honey,
and likewise with sweet medicines and with milky trees.
Citron, grapes, <s>vaṭa</s>, and tender shoots of <s>vetasa</s>,

children.text: mūlāni kuśakāśānāṃ yaṣṭyāhvaṃ ca jale śṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the roots of <s>kuśa</s> and <s>kāśa</s>, and licorice should be boiled in water.

children.text: jvaroditaṃ vā drākṣādi pañcasārāmbu vā pibet
children.translated_text: Or one should drink the <s>drākṣādi</s> preparation taught under fever, or the five-essence water.
In thirst arising from <s>kapha</s>, emesis should be done with water of neem blossoms.
One should drink water prepared with <s>bilva</s>, <s>āḍhakī</s>, <s>pañcakola</s>, and the five <s>darbha</s> grasses,

children.text: jalaṃ pibed rajanyā vā siddhaṃ sakṣaudraśarkaram ||
children.translated_text: or water cooked with turmeric, together with honey and sugar.
One should also use <s>mudga</s> soup with the three pungents, <s>paṭolī</s>, and neem leaves,
barley food, and sharp mouthfuls, nasal medicines, and linctuses.
For all thirst arising from <s>āma</s>, treatment that destroys it is desired, and so too emesis.
This is done with the three pungents, <s>aruṣkara</s>, <s>vacā</s>, sour fruits, hot water, and whey.

children.text: annātyayān maṇḍam uṣṇaṃ himaṃ manthaṃ ca kālavit
children.translated_text: When thirst follows missing a meal, one who knows the proper time should drink warm <s>maṇḍa</s> or cold <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: tṛṣi śramān māṃsarasaṃ manthaṃ vā sasitaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: When thirst comes from fatigue, one should drink meat broth or <s>mantha</s> with sugar.
When it comes from the heat of the sun, one should drink <s>mantha</s> with sugar and flour made from barley and <s>kola</s>.
He should also anoint all his limbs with sesame oilcake and sour gruel.

children.text: śītasnānācca madyāmbu pibet tṛṇmān guḍāmbu vā
children.translated_text: When thirst comes from a cold bath, the thirsty person should drink wine-water or jaggery-water.
When it comes from wine, after bathing he should drink wine diluted by half with water and mixed with sour and salty substances.
For one made thirsty by unctuousness and an overly sharp digestive fire, naturally cold water is proper.

children.text: snehād uṣṇāmbvajīrṇāt tu jīrṇān maṇḍaṃ pipāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when thirst follows unctuous food, hot water, or indigestion, after digestion the thirsty person should drink <s>maṇḍa</s>.
When thirsty after unctuous food, he should drink jaggery-water as cold as snow.
When thirsty from heavy and similar foods, he should drink hot water and then vomit it up.
In thirst born of wasting, every strengthening medicine beneficial in wasting should be used.
For the thin, weak, and dry, milk is suitable, or else goat-meat broth.
For thirst accompanied by upward-moving <s>vāta</s>, milk boiled with remedies that remove wasting and cough is suitable.
In thirst arising as a complication of disease, grain-water with sugar and honey

children.text: pāne praśastaṃ sarvā ca kriyā rogādyapekṣayā
children.translated_text: is praised as a drink; all treatment should be applied with regard to the underlying disease and other factors.

children.text: tṛṣyan pūrvāmayakṣīṇo na labheta jalaṃ yadi ||
children.translated_text: If a thirsty person, depleted by a previous illness, does not obtain water,

children.text: maraṇaṃ dīrgharogaṃ vā prāpnuyāt tvaritaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: then he quickly meets with death or a long-lasting disease.
Therefore one should first overcome his thirst with suitable foods, drinks, and medicines.
When that has been conquered, another disease too can be treated.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>madātyaya</s> and related conditions.
Thus indeed said the great seers such as <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: yaṃ doṣam adhikaṃ paśyet tasyādau pratikārayet
children.translated_text: Whichever <s>doṣa</s> one sees to be predominant, one should first counteract that.
When the <s>doṣas</s> are equal in <s>madātyaya</s>, treatment should proceed according to the sequence of the seats of <s>kapha</s>.
For <s>madātyaya</s> generally extends through <s>pitta</s> and <s>māruta</s>.
The disease that arises from drinking too little, wrongly, or excessively
is pacified by that very wine, when the same wine is drunk properly.
Because wine resembles poison; and poison, when its action has become excessive,
through association with sharp and similar qualities, requires another poison.
By wine that is sharp, hot, sour, burning, and drunk in excessive measure,
the moist food-essence is burnt and becomes alkaline.
This produces intoxication, thirst, delusion, fever, internal burning, and confusion.
When <s>vāta</s> is obstructed in the channels by a <s>doṣa</s> agitated by wine,
it causes very severe pains in the head, bones, and joints.
When the fault of digested or undigested wine is present, and there is appetite and lightness,

children.text: yaugikaṃ vidhivad yuktaṃ madyam eva nihanti tān ||
children.translated_text: wine itself, properly combined and administered according to rule, destroys those disorders.

children.text: kṣāro hi yāti mādhuryaṃ śīghram amlopasaṃhitaḥ
children.translated_text: For alkali quickly turns sweet when joined with sourness.

children.text: madyam amleṣu ca śreṣṭhaṃ doṣaviṣyandanād alam ||
children.translated_text: And wine is the best among sour substances, sufficient for liquefying the <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇoṣṇādyaiḥ purā proktair dīpanādyais tathā guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: By the sharp, hot, and other qualities previously stated, and likewise by qualities that kindle digestion,
and because it is habituated to him, that very wine is the supreme restorer of balance among his tissues.
For seven days or eight nights one should carry out the remedy for excessive drinking.
Within this length of time, the drink that has gone onto a wrong path is digested.

children.text: paraṃ tato 'nubadhnāti yo rogas tasya bheṣajam
children.translated_text: After that, whatever disease remains attached should receive its own remedy.
Having completed the treatment for <s>pānātyaya</s>, one should apply that remedy as appropriate.

children.text: tatra vātolbaṇe madyaṃ dadyāt piṣṭakṛtaṃ yutam
children.translated_text: There, when <s>vāta</s> is predominant, one should give wine made from flour and combined with
citron, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, <s>kola</s>, pomegranate, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
<s>yavānī</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, the three pungents, the three salts, and fresh ginger,
with spit-roasted meat, <s>harītakī</s>, and unctuous parched-grain flour.
Warm, unctuous, sour, and salty broths of fatty meat are beneficial.
<s>rāga</s> and <s>ṣāḍava</s> preparations seasoned with the pulps of mango and <s>āmrātaka</s> are useful.
Soft, varied preparations of wheat and <s>māṣa</s>, pleasing to the mouth, are also suitable.
containing moist ginger, fresh ginger, <s>kulmāṣa</s>, fermented sour gruel, meat, and the like.
It should be fragrant, salty, cool, and wholesome; or clear <s>vāruṇī</s> wine may be used.
There may be fresh juice from pomegranate, or a decoction from the lesser <s>pañcamūla</s>,
and also from dry ginger and coriander; whey, sour vinegar-water, or clear sour <s>kāñjika</s>.
Massage with oil, rubbing, bathing, warmth, and a thick covering should be used,
as well as thick incense made from <s>aguru</s> and a paste of <s>aguru</s> and saffron.
Beloved women endowed with breasts, thighs, and hips, with youthful, warm-limbed bodies,
are appropriate for cheerful embracing and for massages.

children.text: pittolbaṇe bahujalaṃ śārkaraṃ madhu vā yutam ||
children.translated_text: When <s>pitta</s> is predominant, wine should be mixed with much water, sugar, or honey,
and with juices made from pomegranate, dates, <s>bhavya</s>, grapes, and <s>parūṣaka</s>.

children.text: suśītaṃ sasitāsaktu yojyaṃ tādṛk ca pānakam ||
children.translated_text: It should be very cold and combined with sugar and <s>saktu</s>; a similar <s>pānaka</s> drink should be employed.
Or wine mixed with decoctions from the sweet group and with honey may be used.
He should eat <s>śāli</s> and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with meat of hare, antelope, and <s>kapiñjala</s> bird,
with soups of <s>satīna</s>, green gram, emblic myrobalan, <s>paṭolī</s>, and pomegranate.
If <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> are greatly stirred up, a man afflicted with thirst and burning should vomit them out,
after drinking cold water, or wine mixed with abundant sugarcane juice,

children.text: drākṣārasaṃ vā saṃsargī tarpaṇādiḥ paraṃ hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or grape juice. In a mixed condition, nourishing preparations and the like are especially beneficial.
In that way his digestive fire is kindled, digesting the remaining <s>doṣas</s> and food.
In cough with blood-streaked sputum, and in pains of the side and breast,
and in thirst accompanied by burning and nausea in the heart and chest,
one should use the juice of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>bhadramustā</s>, or else of <s>paṭola</s>,
together with fresh ginger, followed by a meal of partridge.
When he is extremely thirsty because <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> are greatly aggravated,
one should give cold grape juice as a drink, since it moves the <s>doṣas</s> downward.
When that is digested, he should eat with a sweet-sour soup of goat meat.

children.text: tṛṣyalpaśaḥ piben madyaṃ madaṃ rakṣan bahūdakam
children.translated_text: When thirsty he should drink wine little by little, guarding against intoxication, with plenty of water.
Or he may drink water prepared with <s>musta</s>, pomegranate, and parched grain, or water boiled with <s>parṇinī</s>,

children.text: pāṭalyutpalakandair vā svabhāvād eva vā himam
children.translated_text: or with <s>pāṭalī</s> and blue-lotus tubers, or water that is naturally cold.
When, from excessive drinking, the watery bodily element is depleted and heat is aggravated,
the man whose throat, palate, and lips are dry, and who thrusts out his tongue and struggles,
should be made to drink water as much as he wishes, while touched by the midnight breeze.
The juice of <s>kola</s>, pomegranate, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, <s>cukrīkā</s>, and <s>cukrikā</s>,
the five-sour mouth-application, immediately restrains thirst.
When the heat of drink has reached the skin, intensified by <s>pitta</s> and blood,
and produces terrible burning, then a very cooling regimen is required.

children.text: aśāmyati rasais tṛpte rohiṇīṃ vyadhayet sirām
children.translated_text: If it is not pacified after he has been satisfied with juices, one should pierce the <s>rohiṇī</s> vein.
One should overcome a <s>śleṣman</s>-predominant condition by emesis and fasting; he should drink
cold water prepared with any one of dry ginger, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>udīcya</s>, or <s>duḥsparśā</s>.
When he is free from undigested matter and hungry at the proper time, he should be made to drink a preparation with much honey,

children.text: śārkaraṃ madhu vā jīrṇam ariṣṭaṃ sīdhum eva vā
children.translated_text: or old sugar-wine, old honey-wine, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, or <s>sīdhu</s>,
combined with dry nourishing flour and with <s>yavānī</s> and dry ginger.
He should be fed barley or wheat with soup, thin and in a small quantity,
with a hot, sour, pungent, bitter horse-gram soup and a little ghee,
or with soups of dried radish and of goat or animals that roam in arid land,
together with sour <s>vetasa</s>, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and pomegranate.
It should contain abundant dry ginger, black pepper, and slices of fresh green ginger,
be moistened with sour juices such as citron juice, roasted, and without watery liquid.
<s>Karīra</s>, <s>karamarda</s>, and the like, appetizing and richly seasoned,
with distinct <s>aṣṭāṅga-lavaṇa</s> and various pounded relishes, may be used.

children.text: yathāgni bhakṣayan māṃsaṃ mādhavaṃ nigadaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: Eating meat according to his digestive power, he should drink sound <s>mādhava</s> wine.
Sugar, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, cumin, <s>tintiḍīka</s>, sour <s>vetasa</s>,
cinnamon bark, cardamom, and black pepper in half-portions make the beneficial <s>aṣṭāṅga-lavaṇa</s>.
In <s>kapha</s>-predominant <s>madātyaya</s>, it clears the channels and produces digestive fire.
By dry and hot rubbing, friction, bathing, food, and fasting,

children.text: sakāmābhiḥ saha strībhir yuktyā jāgaraṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: and by judicious wakefulness together with women he desires,
<s>kapha</s>-predominant <s>madātyaya</s> quickly subsides.

children.text: yad idaṃ karma nirdiṣṭaṃ pṛthag doṣabalaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: This treatment has been prescribed separately according to the strength of each <s>doṣa</s>.
In the tenfold combined condition, and even in residual states, one should adapt that treatment.
With cinnamon bark, <s>nāgapuṣpa</s>, long pepper, black pepper, cumin, and coriander,
and with <s>parūṣaka</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, cardamom, and <s>surāhva</s>, together with sugar,
a heart-pleasing drink with citron juice, cooled under the moon,
should be drunk in all cases of <s>madātyaya</s>; it is tasty and kindles the digestive fire.

children.text: nāvikṣobhya mano madyaṃ śarīram avihanya vā ||
children.translated_text: Wine does not produce <s>madātyaya</s> without disturbing the mind

children.text: kuryān madātyayaṃ tasmād iṣyate harṣaṇī kriyā
children.translated_text: or harming the body; therefore a gladdening treatment is desired.
If the disorder from wine does not subside even after purification, pacification, and other measures,

children.text: na cecchāmyet kaphe kṣīṇe jāte daurbalyalāghave
children.translated_text: when <s>kapha</s> is depleted and weakness and lightness have arisen,
then, for one scorched by wine and dominated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: grīṣmopataptasya taror yathā varṣaṃ tathā payaḥ
children.translated_text: milk is like rain to a tree oppressed by summer heat.

children.text: madyakṣīṇasya hi kṣīṇaṃ kṣīram āśveva puṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For milk quickly nourishes the man depleted by wine,

children.text: ojas tulyaṃ guṇaiḥ sarvair viparītaṃ ca madyataḥ
children.translated_text: and also <s>ojas</s>, being similar in all its qualities and opposite to wine.

children.text: payasā vihate roge bale jāte nivartayet ||
children.translated_text: When the disease has been overcome by milk and strength has arisen, one should discontinue
the use of milk and gradually take wine little by little,
so that he is not touched by complications arising from wasting and collapse.

children.text: tayos tu syād ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ vastayo bṛṃhaṇāḥ śivāḥ
children.translated_text: For those two, ghee, milk, and nourishing enemas are auspicious,
as are massage, rubbing, bathing, and food and drink that conquer <s>vāta</s>.
For one who drinks wine properly, no disease arising from wine occurs.

children.text: ato 'sya vakṣyate yogo yaḥ sukhāyaiva kevalam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore its regimen will be described, which is solely for happiness.

children.text: āśvinaṃ yā mahat tejo balaṃ sārasvataṃ ca yā
children.translated_text: That great power of the <s>Aśvins</s>, and that <s>Sārasvata</s> strength which...

children.text: dadhātyaindraṃ ca yā vīryaṃ prabhāvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca yā ||
children.translated_text: Wine bears the vigor of <s>Indra</s>, and it has the potency of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: astraṃ makaraketor yā puruṣārtho balasya yā
children.translated_text: It is the weapon of <s>Makaraketu</s>, and it is the aim attained by strength.

children.text: sautrāmaṇyāṃ dvijamukhe yā hutāśe ca hvayate ||
children.translated_text: It is invoked in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, in the mouth of twice-born priests, and in the sacrificial fire.
It arose from the great ocean, filled with all medicinal herbs, when it was being churned by gods and asuras,
together with <s>Śrī</s>, the moon, and nectar.
In forms such as <s>madhu</s>, <s>mādhava</s>, <s>maireya</s>, <s>sīdhu</s>, <s>gauḍa</s>, and <s>āsava</s>,

children.text: madaśaktim anujjhantī yā rūpair bahubhiḥ sthitā ||
children.translated_text: it remains in many shapes, never abandoning its power of intoxication.

children.text: yām āsvādya vilāsinyo yathārthaṃ nāma bibhrati
children.translated_text: Having tasted it, amorous women bear their name in its true sense.
Even a woman of good family, after drinking it, becomes excited in mind and carries away,
with limbs as though embraced by <s>Anaṅga</s>, even the mind of a sage somewhere.
With threats from brows furrowed like breaking waves, it wins over the mind of a proud woman.

children.text: ekaṃ prasādya kurute yā dvayorapi nirvṛtim
children.translated_text: By pleasing one person, it brings satisfaction to both.
When groups of apsarases rejoice at obtaining warriors as they desire,

children.text: tṛṇavat puruṣā yuddhe yām āsvādya tyajantyasūn
children.translated_text: men, after tasting it, cast away their lives in battle as though they were grass.
Even after practicing it for a long time in its many kinds and many forms,
one continually resorts to it with an intense rush of joy, as if it were the first time.
On seeing it, one is not overwhelmed by grief, agitation, displeasure, or fear.
No gathering, great festival, or garden outing shines without it.

children.text: smṛtvā smṛtvā ca bahuśo viyuktaḥ śocate yayā ||
children.translated_text: When separated from it, a person grieves, remembering it again and again.

children.text: aprasannāpi yā prītyai prasannā svarga eva yā
children.translated_text: Even when not clear it gives pleasure; when clear it is like heaven itself.
With it dwelling in the heart, one would think even <s>Indra</s> poor.
Its taste of happiness cannot be described; it is known only by oneself in the highest degree.
Thus, in its varied states, it imitates a beloved woman.
It becomes dearer than the very beloved, especially to the one who loves it.

children.text: yā prītir yā ratir vā vāg yā puṣṭiriti ca stutā ||
children.translated_text: It is praised by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and humans
as pleasure, delight, speech, nourishment, and by other names.

children.text: pānapravṛttau satyāṃ tu tāṃ surāṃ vidhinā pibet ||
children.translated_text: But when one has begun to drink, one should drink that <s>surā</s> (wine) according to rule.
Those diseases arising from fat, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> do not occur

children.text: vidhiyuktād ṛte madyād ye na sidhyanti dāruṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which, apart from properly used <s>madya</s> (alcohol), are terrible and cannot be cured.

children.text: asti dehasya sāvasthā yasyāṃ pānaṃ nivāryate
children.translated_text: There is a condition of the body in which drinking is prohibited,
except for alcohol expressly prescribed and prepared with various medicines.
How can meat from marshy or dry-land animals, even when prepared according to rule,

children.text: madyaṃ sahāyam aprāpya samyak pariṇamet katham ||
children.translated_text: be properly digested if it does not obtain alcohol as an aid?
And in the use of garlic, which destroys very severe disorders of <s>vāta</s>,
how much benefit would there be if it were separated from alcohol and meat?
In extracting a hidden foreign body, and in operations with the knife, alkali, or fire,
a man who has drunk alcohol comfortably endures the physician's bold procedures.
For kindling the digestive fire, pleasing the taste, and dispelling grief and fatigue,
there is nothing else superior to it that produces health, strength, and nourishment.

children.text: rakṣatā jīvitaṃ tasmāt peyam ātmavatā sadā
children.translated_text: Therefore one who has self-control should always drink it while protecting life,
for it supports the welfare of oneself and dependents and is the supreme means for <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: snātaḥ praṇamya suravipragurūn yathāsvaṃ vṛttiṃ vidhāya ca samastaparigrahasya
children.translated_text: After bathing, bowing to the gods, brahmins, and teachers, and arranging the proper livelihood and affairs of the whole household,
he should then go to the drinking place, sprinkled with fragrant water and situated near the dining pavilion.
Then, on a beautifully spread and lovely couch, accompanied by friends, servants, and women,
he should listen to his own fame, raised beyond the ordinary world by bands of storytellers and bards.

children.text: vilāsinīnāṃ ca vilāsaśobhi gītaṃ sanṛtyaṃ kalatūryaghoṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: He should hear the graceful song of charming women, accompanied by dance and by the sounds of lutes and drums,
echoing with girdle strings, tinkling little bells, and pet birds at play.
His beloved women should have their bodies covered with varied ornaments born of gems and gold, and with fine linen garments marked by moist, multicolored patterns;
with their restless glances like startled deer, they should be capable of disturbing even the minds of sages.
From the excessive weight produced by breasts and hips, they should be languid and stirred by excited attention to their lord,
bearing an unsteady movement that acts like a spell for alluring the minds of young men.
Intoxicated with the wine of youth and possessed by playful grace,
slender women should carry it about all at once, here and there.
It should be cooled by very cool breezes from palm-leaf fans and lotus leaves;

children.text: darśane 'pi vidadhad vaśānugam svāditaṃ kim uta cittajanmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if even at the sight of it it makes the mind-born god obedient, how much more when it is tasted?
It should be perfumed with mango juice, camphor, and musk, attended by bright jasmine,

children.text: sphāṭikaśuktigataṃ sataraṅgaṃ kāntam anaṅgam ivodvahad aṅgam ||
children.translated_text: set in crystal and mother-of-pearl vessels, rippling, charming, and bearing a body like bodiless <s>Anaṅga</s>.

children.text: tālīśādyaṃ cūrṇam elādikaṃ vā hṛdyaṃ prāśya prāg vayaḥsthāpanaṃ vā
children.translated_text: First he should eat a pleasing powder beginning with <s>tālīśa</s>, or one beginning with cardamom, or a life-preserving tonic;

children.text: tatprārthibhyo bhūmibhāge sumṛṣṭe toyonmiśraṃ dāpayitvā tataśca ||
children.translated_text: then, after having it given mixed with water to those who desire it on a well-cleaned spot of ground,
he should remain firm and mindful, always acting with nothing deficient or excessive,
and should arrange everything with suitable service and attendance.
He should drink the wine like the face of a beloved woman, its beauty increased by the reflection of conquered, fully opened dark lotus eyes,
and with its fragrance drawing a swarm of bees.

children.text: pītvaivaṃ caṣakadvayaṃ parijanaṃ saṃmānya sarvaṃ tato gatvāhārabhuvaṃ puraḥ subhiṣajo bhuñjīta bhūyo 'tra ca
children.translated_text: After drinking two cups in this way and honoring all the attendants, he should then go to the dining place and eat in the presence of a good physician; there again,

children.text: māṃsāpūpaghṛtārdrakādiharitair yuktaṃ sasauvarcalair dvis trir vā niśi cālpam eva vanitāsaṃvalganārthaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: with meat, cakes, ghee, fresh ginger, and greens mixed with <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, he may drink two or three times at night, or only a little, for the purpose of amorous play with a woman.

children.text: rahasi dayitām aṅke kṛtvā bhujāntarapīḍanāt pulakitatanuṃ jātasvedāṃ sakampapayodharām
children.translated_text: In private, having placed his beloved on his lap, her body thrilled, perspiring, and her breasts trembling from the pressure between his arms,

children.text: yadi sarabhasaṃ sīdhor vāraṃ na pāyayate kṛtī kim anubhavati kleśaprāyaṃ tato gṛhatantratām ||
children.translated_text: If a capable man does not swiftly drink a round of <s>sīdhu</s>, what does he experience thereafter except household life, full of hardship?
The cup, made more fragrant by contact with the face of a lovely-bodied woman,
as if it were a ruby jewel in liquid form, bearing the form of wine,

children.text: bhavati ratiśrameṇa ca madaḥ pibato 'lpam api
children.translated_text: and intoxication, even from drinking a little, arising together with the fatigue of love-play,

children.text: kṣayam ata ojasaḥ pariharan sa śayīta param ||
children.translated_text: should be enjoyed; avoiding depletion of <s>ojas</s>, he should then sleep soundly.

children.text: itthaṃ yuktyā piban madyaṃ na trivargād vihīyate
children.translated_text: Drinking wine in this way, according to proper method, one is not deprived of the three aims of life,
and one obtains the highest pleasure in this insubstantial world.
This enjoyment of wealth is desirable even to the gods.

children.text: anyathā hi vipatsu syāt paścāt tāpendhanaṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, in misfortunes, wealth becomes fuel for later remorse.
A man who has possessions but lacks enjoyment is censured as merely a possessor of enjoyments.
This extremely miserly man was created by fate as a guardian of treasure.

children.text: tasmād vyavasthayā pānaṃ pānasya satataṃ hitam
children.translated_text: Therefore drinking in due order is always wholesome for one who drinks,
after he has conquered the independence of the senses that are greedy for their objects.

children.text: vidhir vasumatām eṣa bhaviṣyadvasavas tu ye
children.translated_text: This is the rule for wealthy men; but those who are to become wealthy in the future

children.text: yathopapatti tair madyaṃ pātavyaṃ mātrayā hitam ||
children.translated_text: should drink wine as occasion allows, in a wholesome measure.

children.text: yāvad dṛṣṭer na saṃbhrāntir yāvan na kṣobhate manaḥ
children.translated_text: Only so long as there is no confusion of sight and the mind is not disturbed,

children.text: tāvad eva virantavyaṃ madyād ātmavatā sadā ||
children.translated_text: so long, and no further, should a self-possessed man always desist from wine.
One dominated by <s>vāta</s> should drink after being prepared with oil massage, rubbing, bathing, garments, incense, and unguents,
and with unctuous, warm foods.
One of <s>pitta</s> constitution, prepared with many kinds of cooling treatment

children.text: paittiko bhāvitaścānnaiḥ piban madyaṃ na sīdati ||
children.translated_text: and with sweet, unctuous, cold foods, does not sink down when drinking wine.
One of <s>kapha</s> constitution should drink with treatments that are not cold, after eating barley and wheat,

children.text: ślaiṣmiko dhanvajair māṃsair madyaṃ māricikaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: together with meats of desert animals and peppery substances.

children.text: tatra vāte hitaṃ madyaṃ prāyaḥ paiṣṭikagauḍikam
children.translated_text: Among these, for <s>vāta</s>, wine made from flour or molasses is generally beneficial;
for <s>pitta</s>, honey-wine mixed with water; for <s>kapha</s>, grape wine, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and <s>mādhava</s> wine.
One of <s>kapha</s> constitution should drink wine before eating, one of <s>pitta</s> constitution after the meal,

children.text: vātikas tu piben madhye samadoṣo yathecchayā ||
children.translated_text: but one of <s>vāta</s> constitution should drink in the middle of the meal; one with balanced <s>doṣa</s>s may drink as he wishes.
In states of intoxication, treatment that removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> is generally recommended, and also in fainting;
but everywhere one should especially take <s>pitta</s> into account.
Cold plasters, gems, sprinklings, breezes from fans,
sugar, the juices of grapes, sugarcane, dates, and <s>kāśmarya</s>, and milk;
milk cooked with the sweet group, meat juices and soups with pomegranate;

children.text: ṣaṣṭikāḥ śālayo raktā yavāḥ sarpiśca jīvanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, red <s>śāli</s> rice, barley, ghee, and vitalizing therapy are beneficial.
<s>Kalyāṇaka</s> ghee, <s>mahātikta</s> ghee, <s>ṣaṭpala</s> ghee, or <s>agnika</s> taken with milk,
or long peppers, or <s>śilāhva</s>, should be used according to the method of rejuvenation therapy.
Or <s>triphalā</s> should be administered with ghee, honey, and sugar.
When the urges are persistent, obstruction of the mouth and nose is beneficial.

children.text: pibed vā mānuṣīkṣīraṃ tena dadyācca nāvanam
children.translated_text: Or he should drink human milk, and with it one should administer nasal medication.
Or he should lick lotus stalk, lotus fiber, and <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, together with <s>abhayā</s>, mixed with honey.

children.text: durālabhāṃ vā mustaṃ vā śītena salilena vā
children.translated_text: Or he should drink <s>durālabhā</s> or <s>musta</s> with cold water,
or black pepper, the marrow of <s>kola</s> seeds, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>nāgakesara</s>.
Ghee cooked in the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, or with a decoction of <s>pathyā</s>,
should be used, and one should carry out treatment as already stated, according to the manifestation of the strength of the <s>doṣa</s>s.

children.text: pañca karmāṇi ceṣṭāni secanaṃ śoṇitasya ca
children.translated_text: The five purificatory actions are recommended, as is letting of blood,
supporting the mind, knowledge, and absence of greed for sense objects.
These should be applied when intoxications have become excessive and in cases of fainting.
In cases caused by poison, the sharp treatment prescribed for collapse and the anti-poison treatment should be used.

children.text: āśu prayojyaṃ saṃnyāse sutīkṣṇaṃ nasyam añjanam
children.translated_text: In collapse, very sharp nasal medication, collyrium,
smoke, insufflation, and pricking with needles in the spaces between the nails should be applied quickly,
as well as pulling of the hair, burning, and bites by teeth and scorpions,
pouring pungent and sour substances into the mouth, and rubbing with <s>kapikacchu</s>.
When he has risen and regained consciousness, he should drink garlic juice,
and eat citron filaments with <s>vyoṣa</s> and salt.
For the cleansing of the channels, he should eat light food followed by sharp and hot substances.
With startling acts, reminders, and the hearing and sight of dear things,
with strong sounds of song and instruments, and with the practice of exercise,
with purgations, emetics, smokes, and letting of blood,
one should treat him continually because of the fear of recurrence.
His mind must also be protected, since it is the cause of dissolution.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of hemorrhoids.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
At a suitable time, in ordinary weather, with the sky clear, a hemorrhoid patient who is not very weak,
whose bowel has been purified, and who has eaten a light, small, downward-moving meal,
clean, with auspicious rites performed, having passed feces and urine, and free from pain,
should be supported on a bed, a plank, or in another man's lap,
with the front of the body upward, supine, the anus evenly facing the sun,
and the region of the hips raised. Then, with a restraining cloth,

children.text: sakthnoḥ śirodharāyāṃ ca parikṣiptam ṛju sthitam
children.translated_text: he should be bound around the thighs, head, and neck, and kept straight,
held by attendants, with the anus anointed with ghee.
Then the physician should gently insert into his anus, straight and comfortably,
a straight instrument anointed with ghee; then, after seeing it by making him strain,
when the hemorrhoid has entered the instrument, the physician should press it with a probe wrapped in cloth,
and burn it according to the prescribed procedure.
If it is moist, he should burn it with alkali alone; the other kind with alkali or fire.
Or, if it is large and the patient strong, after cutting it out and removing the instrument from the patient,
he should place him, with anus and hips well anointed, in a tub bath.
Then, while he is staying in a windless chamber, one should prescribe his regimen.
Thus one should treat each one separately, at intervals of a week.

children.text: prāg dakṣiṇaṃ tato vāmam arśaḥ pṛṣṭhāgrajaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: First the one on the right, then the one on the left, and after that the posterior and anterior <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids).
For a person with many hemorrhoids, when they have been well cauterized, <s>vāta</s> moves downward in its proper course.
There is relish for food, sharpness of the digestive fire, health, and the arising of complexion and strength.
But in pain of the bladder region, one should apply below the navel a smooth paste made from
<s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>surabhi</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>loha</s>, and the drug called <s>amarāhvaya</s>.
In obstruction of feces and urine, for sprinkling and immersion baths,
one should use <s>varaṇa</s>, <s>ālambuṣa</s>, <s>airaṇḍa</s>, <s>gokaṇṭaka</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>;
with <s>suṣavī</s> and <s>surabhī</s> as well, one should apply a warm decoction.

children.text: sasneham athavā kṣīraṃ tailaṃ vā vātanāśanam ||
children.translated_text: Or one should use milk mixed with fat, or oil that destroys <s>vāta</s>.
One should employ food that loosens the stool, and unctuous substances that destroy <s>vāta</s> and kindle digestion.
Next, for protruding anal piles of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> origin, where cautery is not to be used,
which are accompanied by stiffness, itching, pain, and swelling, one should anoint the anal nodules
and sprinkle them with oil prepared with root of <s>bilva</s>, <s>agnika</s>, alkali, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>;
or with oil containing the fat of snake, cat, camel, or boar.

children.text: svedayed anu piṇḍena dravasvedena vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward one should foment them with a bolus, or again with liquid fomentation,
or with little boluses of flour of roasted grain, made unctuous with oil and ghee,

children.text: rāsnāyā hapuṣāyā vā piṇḍair vā kārṣṇyagandhikaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or with boluses of <s>rāsnā</s> or <s>hapuṣā</s>, or with fragrant black substances.
Root of <s>arka</s>, leaves of <s>śamī</s>, human hair, a snake's slough,
cat skin, and ghee make a fumigation beneficial for <s>arśas</s>.
Likewise <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>surasā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and ghee,
and the soft net-like material of <s>jīmūta</s> seeds ground with sour grain gruel:
when it is smeared on and dried in the shade, it becomes a suppository that destroys anal growths.
Or one may use a linctus of <s>jīmūta</s> with its network and root, combined with alkali.
A suppository made with seeds of <s>guñjā</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> has the same effect.
Likewise there is a paste of fresh turmeric with latex of <s>snuhī</s>, and similarly with substances ground in cow urine:
cock dung, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, turmeric, and fruits of <s>guñjā</s>;
also <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>halinī</s>, and bones of <s>vāraṇa</s>, ground with latex of <s>snuhī</s>;
<s>kulīraśṛṅgī</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>āruṣkara</s>, and blue vitriol;
seeds produced from the root of <s>śigru</s>, and leaves from <s>aśvaghna</s> and <s>nimba</s>;
together with root of <s>pīlu</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>hiṅgu</s>.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s>, seeds of <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, rock salt, and jaggery,
latex of <s>arka</s>, latex of <s>sudhā</s>, and <s>triphalā</s> form an application.
Latex of <s>arka</s>, the stalk of <s>sudhā</s>, and shoots of bitter bottle-gourd,

children.text: karañjo bastamūtraṃ ca lepanaṃ śreṣṭham arśasām
children.translated_text: <s>karañja</s>, and goat urine make the best application for <s>arśas</s>.
An application with drugs suitable for an oil enema, and with those beginning with <s>pippalī</s>, is also approved.
With these same medicines one should also prepare oils for anointing.
Through fumigation, application, and anointing, the anal sprouts discharge
the accumulated vitiated blood; after that the patient becomes comfortable.
If they do not discharge, one should draw blood from the swollen and hard <s>arśas</s>
again and again, using leeches, a surgical instrument, needles, and a brush.
For when the blood is vitiated, the disease is not pacified by cold, hot, unctuous, or dry measures.

children.text: rakte duṣṭe bhiṣak tasmād raktam evāvasecayet
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the blood is vitiated, the physician should drain blood alone.
That which is produced from cow's milk dusted with powder of <s>vahni</s>,

children.text: pibaṃs tam eva tenaiva bhuñjāno gudajān jayet
children.translated_text: drinking that very thing and eating with that same thing, one overcomes anal piles.
Drinking the powder of the roots of <s>kovidāra</s> with churned curd or buttermilk,

children.text: aśnan jīrṇe ca pathyāni mucyate hatanāmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: and eating wholesome foods after it has digested, one is freed from the disease called by the ill-omened name.
One afflicted by anal swelling and pain, with weak digestion, should drink the <s>gaulmika</s> preparations,
the compounds beginning with <s>hiṅgu</s>, or buttermilk after food; or he should eat jaggery with <s>harītakī</s>.
Or with buttermilk he should drink <s>pathyā</s>, <s>vellā</s>, <s>agni</s>, and bark of <s>kuṭaja</s>,
or <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>magadhā</s>, <s>jyotiḥ</s>, and <s>sūraṇa</s> grown up through bamboo.
Or, with warm water, he should drink the three salts, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
combined with <s>bilva</s> and <s>kapittha</s>, or with <s>mahauṣadha</s> and <s>viḍa</s> salt.
With <s>aruṣkara</s> or <s>yavānī</s>, one should administer a nourishing drink of buttermilk.
Or one should give <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>citraka</s> combined with buttermilk.
For a month he should eat fruits of <s>pīlu</s> with buttermilk as the accompanying drink.

children.text: pibed aharahas takraṃ niranno vā prakāmataḥ
children.translated_text: Or he should drink buttermilk day after day, either without food or as much as desired.
For one whose body and digestive fire are extremely sluggish, one should prescribe buttermilk alone

children.text: saptāhaṃ vā daśāhaṃ vā māsārdhaṃ māsam eva ca
children.translated_text: for seven days, ten days, half a month, or a full month.
The physician, knowing the patient's strength, the season, and the disorder, should administer buttermilk.
In the evening he may give a lickable preparation of parched-grain flour with buttermilk.

children.text: jīrṇe takre pradadyād vā takrapeyāṃ sasaindhavām ||
children.translated_text: Or, when the buttermilk has been digested, he may give a salted buttermilk gruel.
After that, he should take rice cooked with buttermilk, made unctuous, with buttermilk as the accompanying drink.

children.text: yūṣai rasair vā takrāḍhyaiḥ śālīn bhuñjīta mātrayā ||
children.translated_text: Or he should eat a measured amount of <s>śāli</s> rice with soups or meat juices rich in buttermilk.
Buttermilk is of three kinds: dry, with half its fat removed, and that from which the ghee has not been removed.
Knowing the <s>doṣa</s>, digestive fire, and strength, one should apply these three kinds accordingly.
Anal piles do not grow again when struck down by buttermilk.
For when it is poured out, it burns up even a tuft of grass on the ground.

children.text: srotaḥsu takraśuddheṣu raso dhātūn upaiti yaḥ
children.translated_text: When the channels have been purified by buttermilk, the nutritive fluid that reaches the bodily tissues

children.text: tena puṣṭir balaṃ varṇaḥ paraṃ tuṣṭiśca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: produces nourishment, strength, complexion, and supreme satisfaction.
And a hundred disorders of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣma</s> are driven away.
Buttermilk churned in a vessel smeared with fruits of the small and large <s>bṛhatī</s>,
kept overnight, should be drunk by those who desire the destruction of anal piles.
With <s>dhānya</s>, <s>upakuñcikā</s>, <s>ājājī</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, and the two <s>pippalī</s>s,
with <s>kāravī</s>, <s>granthika</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>yavānaka</s>,
powdered and placed in a ghee vessel, buttermilk is fermented so that it is not too sour.
One should drink mature <s>takrāriṣṭa</s> as desired, when it has a distinct sour and pungent taste.
It kindles digestion, improves relish, benefits the complexion, and causes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> to move downward.
It destroys swelling, itching, and pain of the anus, and increases strength.
One should grind the bark of the root of <s>citraka</s> and smear a jar with it.

children.text: takraṃ vā dadhi vā tatra jātam arśoharaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: Buttermilk or curd that has formed there should be drunk; it removes hemorrhoids.
The same procedure also applies with <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>āsphotā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>pañcakola</s>.
With pasted <s>gajakaṇā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>kāravī</s>, and <s>pañcakola</s>,
and with <s>tumburu</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, coriander, and the pith of <s>bilva</s>, one should prepare
fruit-sour gruels, mixed-fat preparations, soups, meat broths, and the like.
Water and ghee cooked with these very medicines become digestive stimulants.
This is the procedure for those whose stool is loose; now it will be stated for those whose feces are hard.

children.text: snehāḍhyaiḥ saktubhir yuktāṃ lavaṇāṃ vāruṇīṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: He should drink salty <s>vāruṇī</s> mixed with flour cakes rich in fat.
Or he should take salty buttermilk, <s>sīdhu</s>, grain-sour gruel, or <s>vāruṇī</s>,
before food, fried in mixed fat and sprinkled with flour cakes.
He should eat tender leaves of <s>karañja</s>, which move <s>vāta</s> and feces downward.
Or he should take <s>nāgara</s> with jaggery, <s>pāṭhā</s>, or jaggery, alkali, and ghee.
Or he should eat <s>harītakī</s> soaked in cow urine, or mixed with jaggery.
Two hundred <s>pathyā</s> fruits should be cooked in a <s>droṇa</s> of urine until the urine is consumed.

children.text: pakvāt khādet samadhunī dve dve hanti kaphodbhavān
children.translated_text: From what has been cooked he should eat two fruits at a time, together with honey; this destroys disorders born of <s>kapha</s>:
hemorrhoids, skin disease, swelling, abdominal tumors, urinary disease, abdominal enlargement, and worms,
as well as glandular swellings, tumors, scrofula, obesity, anemia, and disorders rich in <s>vāta</s>.
Whoever drinks a paste of the root of <s>ajaśṛṅgī</s> with goat urine,
while eating jaggery and eggplant, has his anal sprouts quickly disappear.

children.text: śreṣṭhārasena trivṛtāṃ pathyāṃ takreṇa vā saha ||
children.translated_text: He should eat <s>trivṛt</s> with the juice of excellent <s>ārā</s>, or <s>pathyā</s> together with buttermilk,
or <s>pathyā</s> mixed with long pepper, fried in ghee, and combined with jaggery.
Or he should eat a downward-moving preparation containing <s>trivṛt</s> and <s>dantī</s>.

children.text: hate gudāśraye doṣe gudajā yānti saṃkṣayam
children.translated_text: When the fault lodged in the anus has been eliminated, anal diseases subside.
Buttermilk combined with pomegranate juice, cumin, <s>yavānī</s>, jaggery, and <s>nāgara</s>,
or with <s>pāṭhā</s>, causes <s>vāta</s> and feces to move downward.
Or he should drink <s>sīdhu</s> made from jaggery, or else with <s>citraka</s> and <s>mahauṣadha</s>,
or liquor combined with <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>sauvarcala</s> salt.
Having increased long peppers by tens, ten at a time, and taken two <s>picu</s>s of sesame seeds,
he should drink them with milk; he obtains strength of body and digestive fire.
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, combined even with any one of <s>duḥsparśaka</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>yavānī</s>,
or <s>nāgara</s>, destroys the pain of hemorrhoids.
One should cook half a <s>prastha</s> of <s>abhayā</s> bark in a <s>vaha</s> of water,
a <s>prastha</s> of <s>dhātrī</s>, and ten <s>palas</s> of <s>kapittha</s>; then, half as much
of <s>viśālā</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, black pepper, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>elā</s>, and <s>vālukā</s>,

children.text: dvipalāṃśaṃ pṛthak pādaśeṣe pūte guḍāt tule
children.translated_text: two <s>palas</s> each separately; when a quarter remains and it has been strained,

children.text: dattvā prasthaṃ ca dhātakyāḥ sthāpayed ghṛtabhājane ||
children.translated_text: one should add a <s>tulā</s> of jaggery and a <s>prastha</s> of <s>dhātakī</s>, and store it in a vessel smeared with ghee.

children.text: pakṣāt sa śīlito 'riṣṭaḥ karotyagniṃ nihanti ca
children.translated_text: After a fortnight, when used habitually, that <s>ariṣṭa</s> kindles the digestive fire and destroys
hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, anemia, skin disease, abdominal enlargement, poisoning, and fever,
as well as swelling, splenic disease, heart disease, abdominal tumor, consumption, vomiting, and worms.
One should cook <s>dantī</s>, <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>varā</s>, and <s>agnika</s>, each one <s>pala</s>, in a <s>droṇa</s> of water.

children.text: pālikān pādaśeṣe tu kṣiped guḍatulāṃ param
children.translated_text: When a quarter remains, one should add a full <s>tulā</s> of jaggery.

children.text: pūrvavat sarvam asya syād ānulomitaras tvayam ||
children.translated_text: Everything for this is as before, but this preparation is more strongly downward-moving.
One should cook a <s>prastha</s> of <s>durālabhā</s> in a <s>droṇa</s> of water, together with one <s>prasṛta</s> each
of <s>dantī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>amalaka</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>.
When it has been reduced to a quarter, one should add one hundred measures of sugar, and the rest is as before.
But the jar should be smeared with <s>phalinī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>cavyā</s>, barley, and honey.

children.text: prāgbhaktam ānulomyāya phalāmlaṃ vā pibed ghṛtam
children.translated_text: For downward movement, he should drink fruit-sour ghee before food,
or ghee cooked with <s>cavya</s> and <s>citraka</s>, combined with barley alkali and jaggery,
or ghee cooked with long-pepper root, with jaggery, alkali, and <s>nāgara</s>.
Or ghee prepared with long pepper, long-pepper root, coriander, pomegranate,
and curd removes obstruction of <s>vāta</s>, feces, and urine.
One should cook ghee with three times as much water of <s>palāśa</s> alkali,
with an added paste beginning with <s>vatsaka</s>; it removes hemorrhoids and is an excellent digestive stimulant.
With <s>pañcakola</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, alkali, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>viḍa</s> salt, and rock salt,
with <s>pāṭhā</s>, coriander, black pepper, and <s>bilva</s>, one should prepare ghee in curd.
It quickly conquers pain of the anus and groins,
dysentery, prolapse of the anus, painful urination, and discharge.
With <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>ajamodā</s>, coriander, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>pañcakola</s>,
with <s>bilva</s>, in curd and in four times as much juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s>,
cooked ghee destroys abdominal distension, painful urination, and dysentery,
as well as pain from prolapse of the anus, hemorrhoids, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, and <s>vāta</s> disorders.
Sour, well-prepared meat soups of peacock, partridge, quail,
fowl, or quail-like birds should be given when feces and flatus are retained.
Tender shoots of <s>vāstukā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, tamarind, and the like,

children.text: anyacca kaphavātaghnaṃ śākaṃ ca laghu bhedi ca
children.translated_text: and other light, laxative vegetables that reduce <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>,

children.text: sahiṅgu yamake bhṛṣṭaṃ siddhaṃ dadhisaraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: should be fried in mixed fat with asafoetida and cooked together with the cream of curd.
They should be mixed with coriander and <s>pañcakola</s>, both ground with pomegranate water,
with tender shoots of fresh ginger and pieces of fresh ginger,
and made fragrant by pleasant charcoal smoke.
Rich in cumin, black pepper, <s>viḍa</s> salt, and <s>sauvarcala</s> salt,
for a dry patient with predominant <s>vāta</s>, weak digestive fire, and bound feces,
one should prepare accompaniments to red <s>śāli</s> rice, like vegetable dishes, and meat soups
of cow, monitor lizard, goat, and camel, especially of carnivorous animals.

children.text: madirāṃ śārkaraṃ gauḍaṃ sīdhuṃ takraṃ tuṣodakam ||
children.translated_text: Liquor, sugar liquor, <s>gauḍa</s>, <s>sīdhu</s>, buttermilk, and water prepared from grain-husks,

children.text: ariṣṭaṃ mastu pānīyaṃ pānīyaṃ vālpakaṃ śṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>ariṣṭa</s>, whey, drinking water, or a little water boiled
with grain, with grain and dry ginger, or with <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>,
taken at the end of the meal or in the middle, promotes the downward movement of <s>vāta</s> and feces.
For when feces, flatus, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s> move downward properly and are clear,
hemorrhoids in the anus subside, and the digestive fire increases.
For those who are afflicted by upward movement, and those who have been made extremely dry,
whose <s>vāta</s> moves in reverse and who are distressed by pain, an oil enema is desired.

children.text: pippalīṃ madanaṃ bilvaṃ śatāhvāṃ madhukaṃ vacām ||
children.translated_text: Long pepper, <s>madana</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, licorice, <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ śaṭhīṃ puṣkarākhyaṃ citrakaṃ devadāru ca
children.translated_text: <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, the drug called <s>puṣkara</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>:
after grinding these, oil should be cooked with twice as much milk.
That is the best oil enema for hemorrhoids with obstructed <s>vāta</s>.
Prolapse of the anus, pain, difficulty in urination, dysenteric straining,
weakness of the waist, thighs, and back, distension situated in the groin,
a slimy discharge, swelling in the anus, and obstruction of <s>vāta</s> and feces,
and frequent rising to pass stool: all this it conquers by means of oil enema.
Or one should apply a decoction enema made with <s>pañcamūla</s> and milk,
together with urine, fat, and salt, and mixed with pastes beginning with <s>phala</s>.

children.text: atha raktārśasāṃ vīkṣya mārutasya kaphasya vā ||
children.translated_text: Now, in bleeding hemorrhoids, after observing whether there is association of <s>vāta</s>

children.text: anubandhaṃ tataḥ snigdhaṃ rūkṣaṃ vā yojayeddhimam
children.translated_text: or of <s>kapha</s>, one should then apply cooling treatment, either unctuous or dry.

children.text: śakṛcchyāvaṃ kharaṃ rūkṣam adho niryāti nānilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the feces goes downward dark, hard, and dry, and wind does not pass,

children.text: kaṭyūrugudaśūlaṃ ca hetur yadi ca rūkṣaṇam
children.translated_text: and there is pain in the waist, thighs, and anus, and if desiccation is the cause,

children.text: tatrānubandho vātasya śleṣmaṇo yadi viṭ ślathā ||
children.translated_text: there the association is of <s>vāta</s>. But if the feces is loose because of <s>śleṣman</s>,

children.text: śvetā pītā guruḥ snigdhā sapicchaḥ stimito gudaḥ
children.translated_text: white, yellow, heavy, unctuous, and slimy, and the anus is sluggish,
one should know the cause to be unctuousness and heaviness; and the signs of blood are to be understood according to their own nature.

children.text: duṣṭe 'sre śodhanaṃ kāryaṃ laṅghanaṃ ca yathābalam
children.translated_text: When the blood is vitiated, purification should be performed, and fasting or lightening according to strength.

children.text: yāvacca doṣaiḥ kāluṣyaṃ srutes tāvad upekṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: So long as there is impurity in the discharge because of the <s>doṣa</s>s, one should wait.
For the purpose of digesting the <s>doṣa</s>s and kindling the digestive fire,
and also for restraining the blood, one should treat especially with bitter substances.

children.text: yat tu prakṣīṇadoṣasya raktaṃ vātolbaṇasya vā
children.translated_text: But blood in a patient whose <s>doṣa</s>s are diminished, or in one in whom <s>vāta</s> is predominant,
should be managed with suitable fats in drinking, anointing, and enemas.

children.text: yat tu pittolbaṇaṃ raktaṃ gharmakāle pravartate
children.translated_text: But blood in which <s>pitta</s> is predominant, which flows in the hot season,

children.text: stambhanīyaṃ tad ekāntān na ced vātakaphānugam ||
children.translated_text: must certainly be checked, unless it is accompanied by <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
When the blood is accompanied by <s>kapha</s>, one should drink a cooked preparation of dry ginger and <s>kuṭaja</s> bark;
or <s>kirātatiktaka</s>, dry ginger, <s>dhanvayāsa</s>, and red sandalwood;
or the barks of <s>dārvī</s>, neem, and <s>sevya</s>, or bark produced from pomegranate;
or <s>kuṭaja</s> bark and fruit, <s>tārkṣya</s>, honey, and <s>ghuṇavallabhā</s>;
or he should drink <s>mayūraka</s> ground with rice-water.
One should boil a <s>tulā</s> of fresh <s>kuṭaja</s> bark in rainwater.
When the bark has lost its sap, into the decoction one should add, reduced to fine powder,
equal handful portions of <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, and <s>mocarasa</s>.
With these, and with <s>śakrayava</s>, after it has been filtered, and after smearing the ladle,

children.text: paktvāvalehaṃ līḍhvā ca taṃ yathāgnibalaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: one should cook it into a linctus; after licking it, one should drink according to the strength of one's digestive fire.

children.text: peyāṃ maṇḍaṃ payaśchāgaṃ gavyaṃ vā chāgadugdhabhuk
children.translated_text: The patient should take thin gruel, scum of boiled rice, goat's milk, or cow's milk, while living on goat's milk.
This linctus quickly pacifies bloody diarrhea and disorders arising in the anus.

children.text: balavad raktapittaṃ ca sravad ūrdhvam adho 'pi vā
children.translated_text: It also pacifies strong <s>raktapitta</s> flowing either upward or downward.
One should boil a <s>tulā</s> of <s>kuṭaja</s> bark in a <s>droṇa</s> of water until one eighth remains.
Having made a paste, one should add to it <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s> and the three pungents,
the two <s>lodhra</s>s, <s>mocarasa</s>, <s>balā</s>, and pomegranate bark,
<s>bilva</s>, <s>karkaṭikā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, and <s>dhātakī</s> flowers,
each measured at one <s>pala</s>, and ten <s>pala</s>s of <s>kuṭaja</s> bark itself.

children.text: triṃśat palāni guḍato ghṛtāt pūte ca viṃśatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after filtering, thirty <s>pala</s>s of jaggery and twenty of ghee should be added.

children.text: tat pakvaṃ lehatāṃ yātaṃ dhānye pakṣasthitaṃ lihan ||
children.translated_text: When it has been cooked to the state of a linctus and kept for a fortnight in grain, one should lick it.
It restrains all hemorrhoids, disorders of <s>grahaṇī</s>, dyspnea, and cough.
<s>Lodhra</s>, sesame, <s>mocarasa</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, sandalwood, and blue lotus
should be given to drink with goat's milk, and <s>śāli</s> rice should be fed with that same milk.
<s>Yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>anantā</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, milk, and <s>moraṭa</s>,
with sugar and honey, should be drunk with cold water, or with that milk.
Or <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, and bark of <s>śālmalī</s>,
together with <s>himakesara</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and <s>sevya</s>, may be taken with rice-water.
<s>Yavānī</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, dry ginger, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,
as a powder, are beneficial when the stool is loose, when there is pain, and when excessive bleeding has begun.
Ghee cooked with <s>dugdhikā</s> and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s> is recommended.
Or else ghee cooked with <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s> bark and fruit, and blue lotus,
together with saffron, or with alkali of barley and the expressed juice of pomegranate,
or butter used repeatedly with sugar and lotus filaments,
or together with sesame, restrains bleeding hemorrhoids.
Goat butter, ghee, milk, and meat, and meat from animals of dry land,

children.text: anamlo vā kadamlo vā savāstukaraso rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: meat soup without sourness or with only slight sourness, along with the juice of <s>vāstuka</s>,

children.text: raktaśāliḥ saro dadhnaḥ ṣaṣṭikas taruṇī surā
children.translated_text: red <s>śāli</s> rice, the liquid part of curds, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, young liquor,
and fresh scum of liquor are supreme medicine for bleeding.
Onion, used in thin gruel, soups, meat soups, and the like, or even by itself,

children.text: sa jayatyulbaṇaṃ raktaṃ mārutaṃ ca prayojitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: conquers severe bleeding and <s>māruta</s> when administered.
When blood has flowed out excessively, the hemorrhoids generally become predominant in <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: arśāṃsi tasmād adhikaṃ tajjaye yatnam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should make special effort to conquer that condition.
Having seen that blood and <s>pitta</s> are strong, and that <s>kapha</s> and <s>anila</s> are weak,
Cold measures should by all means be carried out for its pacification.

children.text: na ced evaṃ śamas tasya snigdhoṣṇais tarpayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: If, in this way, its alleviation does not occur, then one should nourish him with unctuous and warm things,
with meat broths, and with lukewarm ghees applied in the manner of <s>avapīḍaka</s>.
One may also sprinkle him with lukewarm oil, milk, and ghee as desired.
The roots of <s>yavāsa</s>, <s>kuśa</s>, and <s>kāśa</s>, and the flower of <s>śālmali</s>,
and sprouts of <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, and <s>aśvattha</s>, two <s>pala</s>s in measure each:
one should cook these in three <s>prastha</s>s of water and one <s>prastha</s> of milk.

children.text: kṣīraśeṣe kaṣāye ca tasmin pūte vimiśrayet
children.translated_text: When the milk and decoction remain, after straining that, one should mix in
<s>mocarasa</s> made into a paste, <s>samaṅgā</s>, sandalwood, and blue lotus,

children.text: priyaṅguṃ kauṭajaṃ bījaṃ kamalasya ca kesaram
children.translated_text: <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>kauṭaja</s> seed, and the filaments of lotus.
This <s>picchābasti</s> (mucilaginous enema), prepared with ghee, honey, and sugar, is ready.
It removes <s>pravāhikā</s> (dysenteric straining), rectal prolapse, bleeding, and fever.
With <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s> and white lotus, and likewise with <s>mocarasa</s> and the others,
oil cooked with twice as much milk should be given as an <s>anuvāsana</s> (unctuous enema).
<s>Madhuka</s>, blue lotus, <s>lodhra</s>, water, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and sandalwood,
<s>cavikā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, alkali, and <s>yavāgraja</s>,

children.text: dārvītvaṅ nāgaraṃ māṃsī citrako devadāru ca ||
children.translated_text: the bark of <s>dārvī</s>, dry ginger, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>:
ghee cooked with these in the fresh juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s> conquers all three <s>doṣa</s>s.
It should be given for hemorrhoids, diarrhea, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, anemia, fever, and anorexia,
for difficult urination, rectal prolapse, distension in the bladder, and straining,
for mucous discharge and pain of hemorrhoids; it is a supreme medicine.
One should alternately apply sweet and sour, and cold and hot, measures,
always taking digestive fire and strength into account; thus one overcomes the diseases caused by hemorrhoids.
After anointing a patient afflicted with <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of wind) with oils that remove chill and fever,

children.text: susnigdhaiḥ svedayet piṇḍair vartim asmai gude tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should foment him with well-unctuous boluses; then, for him, in the anus, a suppository
anointed, resembling his own thumb in size, and causing downward movement,
should be given, made with the fruits of <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>nīlinī</s>,
powdered, with the two salts, and combined with jaggery and cow urine.
In the same way it may be made with <s>māgadhikā</s>, <s>rāṭha</s>, house soot, and mustard.

children.text: eteṣām eva vā cūrṇaṃ gude nāḍyā vinirdhamet
children.translated_text: Or one may blow the powder of these same substances into the anus through a tube.

children.text: tadvighāte sutīkṣṇaṃ tu vastiṃ snigdhaṃ prapīḍayet ||
children.translated_text: If that is obstructed, he should force in a very sharp, unctuous enema.
That will set straight his rectal channels and the movement of feces, urine, and wind.
If the condition recurs again, he should be purged with unctuous purgatives that remove <s>vāta</s>,
and should also receive an unctuous enema, for obstruction of wind and feces arises from dryness.
<s>Tripaṭu</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>aruṣkara</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
coarsely crushed, moistened with fat and urine, should be cooked without smoke
in the joint of two earthen dishes sealed with clay; this alkali is called <s>Kalyāṇaka</s>.

children.text: sa pītaḥ sarpiṣā yukto bhakte vā snigdhabhojinā
children.translated_text: Taken with ghee, or in food by one eating unctuous food,
it destroys <s>udāvarta</s>, constipation, hemorrhoids, <s>gulma</s> masses, anemia, abdominal disease, and worms,
urinary retention, urinary stone, swelling, heart disease, and <s>grahaṇī</s> disorders,
as well as urinary disease, spleen pain, distension, dyspnea, and cough.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca kuryād yat proktam arśasāṃ gāḍhavarcasām
children.translated_text: And one should do everything that has been prescribed for hemorrhoids with hard stool.

children.text: droṇe 'pāṃ pūtivalkadvitulam atha pacet pādaśeṣe ca tasmin
children.translated_text: In a <s>droṇa</s> of water one should cook two <s>tulā</s>s of <s>pūtivalka</s>; when a quarter remains in that,
eighty <s>pala</s>s of jaggery should be added, and eight <s>pala</s>s of finely powdered <s>vyoṣa</s>.

children.text: etan māsena jātaṃ janayati paramām ūṣmaṇaḥ paktiśaktiṃ
children.translated_text: When matured in a month, this produces supreme digestive power from its heat.
Made into a sour ferment and promoting downward movement, it conquers diseases of the anus, spleen, <s>gulma</s>, and abdomen.
One should cook one <s>tulā</s> of <s>pūtikarañja</s> bark, and two roots each of <s>citraka</s> and <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>,

children.text: droṇatraye 'pi caraṇāvaśeṣe pūte śataṃ tatra guḍasya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: in three <s>droṇa</s>s; when a quarter remains, after straining it, one should add one hundred <s>pala</s>s of jaggery.
Also one <s>pala</s> each, finely powdered, of <s>trijāta</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>granthika</s>, pomegranate, and <s>aśmabheda</s>,
<s>pura</s>, <s>puṣkaramūla</s>, coriander, <s>cavya</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, fresh ginger, and sour <s>vetasa</s>.
When it has cooled, it should be combined with twenty <s>pala</s>s of honey, and with fresh grapes, citron, and fresh ginger,

children.text: yuktaṃ kāmaṃ gaṇḍikābhis tathekṣoḥ sarpiḥpātre māsamātreṇa jātam ||
children.translated_text: and, as desired, with <s>gaṇḍikā</s>s and also sugarcane; placed in a ghee vessel, it matures in about a month.

children.text: cukraṃ krakacam ivedaṃ durnāmnāṃ vahnidīpanaṃ paramam
children.translated_text: This sour preparation is like a saw for the so-called hemorrhoids, and is an excellent kindler of digestive fire.
It destroys anemia, chronic poisoning, abdominal disease, <s>gulma</s>, spleen disease, distension, stone, and dysuria.
A <s>droṇa</s> of <s>pīlu</s> juice, filtered through cloth and placed in a ghee vessel,
should be mixed with two-<s>pala</s> quantities of <s>madā</s>, <s>madhuphala</s>, dates, and <s>dhātrī</s> fruit,
with <s>pāṭhā</s>, fresh <s>durālabhā</s>, sour <s>vidula</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, cinnamon bark, cardamom, and <s>ullaka</s>,
and with one-<s>pala</s> quantities of <s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>kola</s>, clove, <s>vella</s>, <s>capalā</s> root, and <s>agnika</s>.

children.text: guḍapalaśatayojitaṃ nivāte nihitam idaṃ prapibaṃśca pakṣamātrāt
children.translated_text: This, combined with one hundred <s>pala</s>s of jaggery and kept where there is no wind, when drunk for just a fortnight,

children.text: niśamayati gudāṅkurān sagulmān analabalaṃ prabalaṃ karoti cāśu ||
children.translated_text: quiets rectal sprouts together with <s>gulma</s> masses, and quickly makes the power of digestion strong.
Ten <s>pala</s>s each of the ten roots, <s>kumbha</s>, the two <s>pāṭhā</s>s, <s>arka</s>, <s>ghuṇavallabha</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s>,

children.text: dagdhe srute 'nu kalaśena jalena pakve pādasthite guḍatulāṃ palapañcakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: having been burned, strained, and then cooked with one pitcher of water until a quarter remains, should receive one <s>tulā</s> of jaggery and five <s>pala</s>s more.

children.text: dadyāt pratyekaṃ vyoṣacavyābhayānāṃ vahner muṣṭī dve yavakṣārataśca
children.translated_text: One should add two handfuls each of <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>vahni</s>, and <s>yavakṣāra</s>.

children.text: darvīm ālimpan hanti līḍho guḍo 'yaṃ gulmaplīhārśaḥkuṣṭhamehāgnisādān ||
children.translated_text: This jaggery, licked when it coats the ladle, destroys <s>gulma</s>, spleen disease, hemorrhoids, skin disease, urinary disorders, and weakness of digestion.

children.text: toyadroṇe citrakamūlatulārdhaṃ sādhyaṃ yāvat pādadalastham athedam
children.translated_text: In a <s>droṇa</s> of water, half a <s>tulā</s> of <s>citraka</s> root should be boiled until it stands at a quarter; then this,

children.text: aṣṭau dattvā jīrṇaguḍasya palāni kvāthyaṃ bhūyaḥ sāndratayā samam etat ||
children.translated_text: after eight <s>pala</s>s of old jaggery have been added, should again be boiled until it is equally thick.
The electuary, sprinkled with powders of <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>varāṅga</s>, <s>kṛmiripu</s>, <s>dahana</s>, and cardamom,

children.text: jayati gudajakuṣṭhaplīhagulmodarāṇi prabalayati hutāśaṃ śaśvad abhyasyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When used constantly, it conquers hemorrhoids, skin disease, splenic enlargement, abdominal tumors, and abdominal diseases, and it strengthens the digestive fire.
With jaggery, <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), <s>varā</s>, <s>vella</s>, sesame, <s>aruṣkara</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: arśāṃsi hanti guṭikā tvagvikāraṃ ca śīlitā ||
children.translated_text: a pill, when regularly used, destroys hemorrhoids and disorders of the skin.
Having coated a tuber of <s>sūraṇa</s> with clay and baked it in fire like a closed baking,
one should eat it with oil and salt for the removal of the so-called bad-named disease, hemorrhoids.
Take black pepper, long pepper, dry ginger, and <s>citraka</s>, gathered in successively increasing portions,
combine them with <s>sūraṇa</s> in four times the amount of <s>śikhi</s>, and make jaggery pills that cut off hemorrhoids.

children.text: cūrṇīkṛtāḥ ṣoḍaśa sūraṇasya bhāgās tato 'rdhena ca citrakasya
children.translated_text: Sixteen parts of <s>sūraṇa</s>, powdered, and then half as much <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: mahauṣadhād dvau maricasya caiko guḍena durnāmajayāya piṇḍī ||
children.translated_text: two parts of <s>mahauṣadha</s> (dry ginger), and one of black pepper, made into a lump with jaggery, serve for conquering hemorrhoids.
A powder made with <s>pathyā</s>, dry ginger, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>vella</s>, and <s>agni</s>, with an equal amount of sugar,

children.text: vaḍabāmukha iva jarayati bahugurvapi bhojanaṃ cūrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: digests even abundant heavy food like the submarine fire of the mare's mouth.
Jaggery pills made with <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>vahni</s>, and grains of <s>apāmārga</s>,
together with <s>bhūnimba</s>, rock salt, and jaggery, destroy hemorrhoids.
If you wish to crush the growths at the anus, drink for seven days the best salt, <s>vahni</s>, <s>kaliṅga</s>, barley,

children.text: piba saptadinaṃ mathitāluḍitān yadi marditum icchasi pāyuruhān ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>ciribilva</s> and great <s>picumanda</s>, stirred into buttermilk.

children.text: śuṣkeṣu bhallātakam agryam uktaṃ bhaiṣajyam ārdreṣu tu vatsakatvak
children.translated_text: For dry hemorrhoids, <s>bhallātaka</s> is said to be the foremost medicine; for moist ones, the bark of <s>vatsaka</s>.

children.text: sarveṣu sarvartuṣu kālaśeyam arśaḥsu balyaṃ ca malāpahaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In all hemorrhoids, in all seasons, <s>kālaśeya</s> is strengthening and removes fecal obstruction.

children.text: bhittvā vibandhān anulomanāya yan mārutasyāgnibalāya yacca
children.translated_text: Whatever food, drink, or medicine breaks obstructions, promotes the downward movement of <s>vāta</s>, and strengthens the digestive fire,

children.text: tad annapānauṣadham arśasena sevyaṃ vivarjyaṃ viparītam asmāt ||
children.translated_text: that should be used by a patient with hemorrhoids; whatever is the opposite of this should be avoided.
Hemorrhoids, diarrhea, and disorders of the <s>grahaṇī</s> are generally causes of one another.

children.text: sanne 'nale santi na santi dīpte rakṣed atas teṣu viśeṣato 'gnim ||
children.translated_text: They occur when the digestive fire is depressed and do not occur when it is blazing; therefore, in these conditions one should especially protect the fire.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of diarrhea.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
For diarrhea for the most part has a connection with the stomach.
Since it has destroyed the digestive fire, fasting is beneficial at first in that condition, even when it is caused by <s>vāta</s>.
One should make a patient with diarrhea vomit when he is afflicted by colic, distension, and salivation.
The <s>doṣa</s>s that have accumulated and are overwhelmed by spoiled, undigested food
are ready to produce diarrhea; in such cases mere non-interference is the treatment.
When they are strongly stirred up and flowing forth, since they are by nature mobile,

children.text: na tu saṃgrahaṇaṃ yojyaṃ pūrvam āmātisāriṇi
children.translated_text: one should not first apply a restraining treatment in diarrhea with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter),
especially when it causes distension, heaviness, pain, and torpor.
When the <s>doṣa</s> is obstructed, <s>prāṇadā</s> is life-giving, because it sets it in motion.
A patient with a moderate amount of <s>doṣa</s> should drink the following drugs, dried and well boiled in water:
<s>Bhūtika</s>, long pepper, dry ginger, <s>vacā</s>, coriander, and <s>harītakī</s>;
or <s>bilva</s>, <s>dhanikā</s>, <s>musta</s>, dry ginger, and <s>vālaka</s>;
or <s>viḍa</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>kṛmijit</s>, and dry ginger;
or dry ginger, <s>ghana</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>mādrī</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, and asafoetida.
For patients with diarrhea whose <s>doṣa</s> is slight, fasting is recommended.
Or one should have him drink water boiled with <s>vacā</s> and <s>prativiṣā</s>, or with <s>musta</s> and <s>parpaṭaka</s>,
or with <s>hrīvera</s> and dry ginger.
At the proper meal time, when he has grown thin with hunger, one should first feed him light food.

children.text: tathā sa śīghraṃ prāpnoti rucim agnibalaṃ balam
children.translated_text: In this way he quickly obtains relish, strength of digestive fire, and bodily strength.
According to what is suitable for him, one should treat him with buttermilk, with <s>avantisoma</s>, with barley gruel, or with a nourishing drink,
or else with liquor or honey.
Afterwards one should prepare foods with substances that are absorbent, kindling, and digestive.

A gruel beneficial when <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> are predominant is sour with pomegranate and cooked with young <s>bilva</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, coriander, asafoetida, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, and pomegranate,
with <s>palāśa</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, cumin, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>viḍa</s>, and rock salt,
with light <s>pañcamūla</s>, with <s>pañcakola</s>, with <s>pāṭhā</s>,
and with <s>śāliparṇī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>.
Such pomegranate-sour gruel is beneficial when <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> are predominant.
Prepared with <s>abhayā</s>, root of long pepper, and <s>bilva</s>, it promotes the downward movement of <s>vāta</s>.
A patient with diarrhea who has obstructed stool, abundant <s>doṣa</s>, and a blazing digestive fire
should be purged with decoctions of <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>.

children.text: peyāṃ yuñjyād viriktasya vātaghnair dīpanaiḥ kṛtām
children.translated_text: After he has been purged, one should prescribe gruel prepared with <s>vāta</s>-subduing and kindling substances.
But when the <s>āma</s> has matured and the digestive fire is blazing, if he evacuates
stool that is foamy, slimy, painful, obstructed, and passed again and again,
a little at a time, with little impurity, either without fecal matter or with straining,
he should drink dry ginger with jaggery, mixed with curds, oil, ghee, and milk.
Or he should eat jujube fruits steamed with jaggery and oil.
When hungry, he should be fed with vegetables prepared to firm the stool, with abundant fats and also with meat soups
prepared with curds and pomegranate.

children.text: śālyodanaṃ tilair māṣair mudgair vā sādhu sādhitam
children.translated_text: He may take <s>śāli</s> rice well cooked with sesame, black gram, or green gram,
or with the juices of <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>mūlakapotā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, or <s>svastika</s>,
or of <s>sūṣā</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>karkāru</s>, <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, or <s>cirbhaṭa</s>,
or of <s>upodakā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, or <s>vāstuka</s>,
or also with the juices of <s>suvarcalā</s>, <s>cuñcu</s>, or <s>loṇikā</s>.
