It may also be taken with the meat soups of tortoise, quail, <s>lopāka</s>, peacock, partridge, or chicken.
With <s>bilva</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>akṣibhaiṣajya</s>, flowers of <s>dhātakī</s>, and dry ginger,
buttermilk gruel, as well as curd-based gruel, conquers mature diarrhea.
With <s>kapittha</s>, <s>kacchurā</s>, <s>phañjī</s>, <s>yūthikā</s>, banyan, and <s>śelu</s>,
and with the shoots of pomegranate, hemp, cotton, and silk-cotton trees,
a paste of unripe <s>bilva</s> fruits, together with an equal amount of sesame paste,

children.text: dadhnaḥ saro 'mlaḥ sasnehaḥ khalo hanti pravāhikām ||
children.translated_text: made into a sour, fatty relish with the whey of curds, cures <s>pravāhikā</s> (dysenteric straining).
Black pepper, <s>dhanikā</s>, cumin, <s>tintiḍīka</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>viḍa</s>...
Pomegranate, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>pañcakola</s>;
barley awns, and the inner pulp of <s>kapittha</s>, mango, and rose-apple, together with <s>dīpyaka</s>;

children.text: piṣṭaiḥ ṣaḍguṇabilvais tair dadhni mudgarase guḍe ||
children.translated_text: when these are ground, with six times as much <s>bilva</s>, and cooked in curds, mung-bean broth, jaggery,

children.text: snehe ca yamake siddhaḥ khalo 'yam aparājitaḥ
children.translated_text: and the combined fats, this preparation called <s>khala</s> is invincible.
It kindles appetite, digests, absorbs, is appetizing, and destroys <s>bimbiśī</s>.
With pastes of jujubes and young <s>bilva</s>, and of <s>śāli</s> rice and barley,
and of mung beans, black gram, and sesame, one should prepare a grain soup.
Fried all together in the combined fats, with curds and the essence of pomegranate,
with that one should feed <s>śāli</s> rice to a patient whose stool is depleted and whose mouth is dry.

children.text: dadhnaḥ saraṃ vā yamake bhṛṣṭaṃ saguḍanāgaram
children.translated_text: Or the liquid part of curds, fried in the combined fats, with jaggery and <s>nāgara</s>,

children.text: surāṃ vā yamake bhṛṣṭāṃ vyañjanārthaṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: or liquor fried in the combined fats, should be used as a condiment.

children.text: phalāmlaṃ yamake bhṛṣṭaṃ yūṣaṃ gṛñjanakasya vā
children.translated_text: Fruit-acid fried in the combined fats, or soup of <s>gṛñjanaka</s>,

children.text: bhṛṣṭān vā yamake saktūn khāded vyoṣāvacūrṇitān ||
children.translated_text: or roasted <s>saktu</s> in the combined fats, sprinkled with the three pungents, may be eaten.
Likewise, well-cooked black gram may be eaten, followed by the scum of ghee.
Or a well-cooked and filtered broth prepared from the entrails of a goat or sheep
should be cooked sour with pomegranate juice, with coriander, fat, and <s>nāgara</s>.
Eating red <s>śāli</s> rice with it and drinking that broth,
one is quickly freed from disorders caused by depletion of stool.
One may lick young <s>bilva</s>, jaggery, oil, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>,
when <s>vāta</s> is obstructed, with pain and <s>pravāhikā</s>.
One should drink <s>śābara</s> bark, <s>dhātakī</s> flowers, and jujube leaves,
soaked in the liquid of curds, honey, and <s>kapittha</s> juice.
But one whose <s>vāta</s> and stool are obstructed, with severe pain and <s>pravāhikā</s>,
with blood and mucus and afflicted by thirst, is fit to be satisfied with milk.
Milk poured over the combined fats, or warm fresh from the udder, should be administered;
or else milk boiled with castor root or with young <s>bilva</s>.
Boiling twenty <s>musta</s>s in milk with three times as much water,

children.text: kṣīrāvaśiṣṭaṃ tat pītaṃ hanyād āmaṃ savedanam
children.translated_text: until only the milk remains, that, drunk, destroys painful <s>āma</s>.

children.text: pippalyāḥ pibataḥ sūkṣmaṃ rajo maricajanma vā ||
children.translated_text: For one drinking the fine powder of <s>pippalī</s> or that produced from pepper,
even long-persistent <s>pravāhikā</s> quickly disappears.
When the condition has no <s>āma</s>, the patient is pained by colic and emaciated by fasting and the like,
and the bowel is dry, one should, considering the digestive fire, make him drink ghee with alkali.
Oil cooked in the scum of curds and liquor and in the decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>,
with rock salt and <s>pañcakola</s>, immediately removes pain.

children.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ śuṇṭhyāḥ palair dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ granthyagnisaindhavāt ||
children.translated_text: With six <s>pala</s>s of dry ginger, and two <s>pala</s>s each of <s>granthi</s>, <s>agni</s>, and rock salt,
one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil with curds; it removes the pain of evacuation.
Taken together, meat, milk, and ghee conquer retention of stool and colic.
Oil, used for drinking, unctuous enema, and massage, acts in another way;

children.text: taddhi vātajitām agryaṃ śūlaṃ ca viguṇo 'nilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for it is foremost among remedies that conquer <s>vāta</s>, and pain is vitiated <s>anila</s>.
<s>Vāta</s> is mobile, pervasive, inflamed by pressing upon other tissues, and moving into its own seat.
Oil, when applied with proper reasoning, gives supreme relief even to one with weak digestive fire.
When stool is exhausted, when the other <s>doṣa</s>s have fallen from their own places, and when the one hero, <s>vāta</s>, is driven on,

children.text: ko niṣṭanan prāṇiti koṣṭhaśūlī nāntarbahistailaparo yadi syāt ||
children.translated_text: what groaning person with abdominal colic can live unless he is devoted to oil internally and externally?
For pain and prolapse of the anus one should employ ghee cooked with milk,

children.text: rase kolāmlacāṅgeryor dadhni piṣṭe ca nāgare
children.translated_text: in the juice of jujube and sour <s>cāṅgerī</s>, in curds, and with <s>nāgara</s> ground as paste.
Combining it with those same sour substances and with finely levigated pastes,
of coriander, the pungents, <s>viḍa</s> salt, <s>ajājī</s>, <s>pañcakola</s>, and pomegranate,
or one should apply an unctuous enema cooked with <s>daśamūla</s>,
or with <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>vacā</s>, or <s>citraka</s>.
In <s>pravāhaṇa</s> (straining), anal prolapse, obstruction of urine, and stiffness of the lower back,
oil or ghee boiled with sweet and sour substances is an <s>anuvāsana</s> enema.

children.text: praveśayed gudaṃ dhvastam abhyaktaṃ sveditaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: The fallen anus, anointed, fomented, and softened, should be inserted,
and one should make a sling-bandage with leather having a hole in the middle.
A decoction of the larger <s>pañcamūla</s> should be cooked in milk,
and also a mouse with its entrails removed; with that and with <s>vāta</s>-conquering pastes,

children.text: tailaṃ paced gudabhraṃśaṃ pānābhyaṅgena taj jayet ||
children.translated_text: one should cook oil, and by drinking and massage it will conquer anal prolapse.

children.text: paitte tu sāme tīkṣṇoṣṇavarjyaṃ prāg iva laṅghanam
children.translated_text: But in the pitta type with <s>āma</s>, as before, fasting is used while sharp and hot things are avoided.
A thirsty patient should drink <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> water with <s>bhūnimba</s> and <s>śārivā</s>.
For one who is hungry, food beginning with thin gruel that kindles the digestive fire is beneficial.
With the <s>bṛhatyādi</s> group, <s>abhīru</s>, the two <s>balā</s>s, and <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>,
when an accompanying condition persists, one should administer a drink with honey and rice-water.
<s>Kuṭaja</s> fruit ground together with bark and with <s>ghuṇapriya</s>,
or <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s> seed and bark, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>granthika</s>, and dry ginger,
or a decoction made from <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>udīcya</s>, and <s>musta</s>,
or from <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, turmeric, <s>indrayava</s>, and <s>tārkṣya</s>,
or <s>ativiṣā</s>, dry ginger, <s>musta</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s> with honey;
having boiled a <s>pala</s> of <s>vatsaka</s> seed, he should drink the liquid.

children.text: yo rasāśī jayecchīghraṃ sa paittaṃ jaṭharāmayam ||
children.translated_text: A person who lives on that broth quickly conquers a pitta-type abdominal disease.
Or he should drink a decoction of <s>musta</s> in this way, mixed with honey,
or the cold preparation of the stalk of <s>śālmalī</s>, with honey.
<s>Kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>;
<s>kaṭaṅkaṭerī</s>, <s>hrīvera</s>, the pith of <s>bilva</s>, and <s>durālabhā</s>;
sesame, <s>mocarasa</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, lotus, and blue lotus;
<s>nāgara</s>, <s>dhātakī</s> flowers, pomegranate bark, and blue lotus;
these formulations, stated in half-verses, are to be taken with honey and rice-water.
A decoction of <s>niśā</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>elā</s> conquers matured diarrhea.
The groups beginning with <s>lodhra</s>, <s>ambaṣṭhā</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s> should similarly be drunk separately.
With bark of <s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, and pomegranate shoots,
one should prepare thin gruel, thick gruel, and sour gruel, with curds and pomegranate.
Likewise one should prepare them with the piths of <s>dadhittha</s>, <s>bilva</s>, mango, and <s>jambū</s>.
Goat's milk should be administered when the condition is free from <s>āma</s>; if there is not pacification by it,

children.text: doṣādhikyān na jāyeta balinaṃ taṃ virecayet ||
children.translated_text: because of excess of the <s>doṣa</s>s, one should purge that strong patient.
Or one who passes stool and blood alternately
should drink a decoction of <s>palāśa</s> fruit, or one combined with milk.

children.text: tato 'nu koṣṇaṃ pātavyaṃ kṣīram eva yathābalam
children.translated_text: After that, warm milk alone should be drunk according to one's strength.
When the fecal matter has been driven out by it, the abdominal disorder subsides.
Or purifying <s>trāyamāṇā</s> may be used in the same way as <s>palāśa</s>.
If pain continues while the gradual restorative diet is being carried out,
then, once the <s>doṣa</s>s have flowed out, one should quickly give him an unctuous enema according to his digestive fire.
With <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>varī</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>,
ghee cooked with a quarter part of oil and with milk is an unctuous enema.
If the diarrhea is still not calmed in this way, a <s>picchā-basti</s> is supremely beneficial.
Having wrapped the moist stalks of <s>śālmalī</s> with wet <s>kuśa</s> grasses,
and having smeared them with black clay, one should steam them over a cow-dung fire.
When the clay is dry, one should crush them; then a lump of that, the size of a fist,
should be rubbed into a <s>prastha</s> of milk, filtered, and then used as an evacuative enema.
Afterward it should be followed with <s>nata</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s> paste, ghee, honey, and oil.

children.text: snāto bhuñjīta payasā jāṅgalena rasena vā ||
children.translated_text: After bathing, the patient should eat with milk or with meat broth from animals of dry land.
This enema quickly conquers pitta-type diarrhea, fever, swelling, abdominal tumors, disorders of <s>vāta</s>, blood, and <s>grahaṇī</s>,
and also the excessive flow caused by purgation and evacuative enema.
A <s>phāṇita</s> preparation made from <s>kuṭaja</s> also destroys all diarrheas,
when combined with the <s>vatsaka</s> group and the <s>ambaṣṭhā</s> group, and mixed with honey.
When diarrhea is painless, free from <s>āma</s>, with the digestive fire kindled, even if bloody and long-standing,
and of various colors, one should treat it with <s>puṭapāka</s> preparations.
From a ball of bark of the long-stalked tree, enclosed in leaves of <s>śrīparṇī</s>,

children.text: mṛlliptād agninā svinnād rasaṃ niṣpīḍitaṃ himam ||
children.translated_text: smeared with clay and steamed by fire, the expressed juice, cooled,
the patient with diarrhea should drink, combined with honey or with sugar.
In the same way one should prepare it with the barks of milk-exuding trees and with their shoots.
Bark of <s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, mixed with ghee and steamed by the heat of water,
when combined with honey, quickly destroys even a strong diarrhea.
But one who has pitta-type diarrhea and again consumes pitta-provoking substances
has his <s>pitta</s> produce bloody diarrhea, accompanied by thirst and fever,

children.text: dāruṇaṃ gudapākaṃ ca tatra chāgaṃ payo hitam
children.translated_text: and a terrible suppuration of the anus; in that case goat's milk is beneficial,
boiled with lotus, blue lotus, <s>samaṅgā</s>, and <s>mocarasa</s>.
Or it may be boiled with <s>śārivā</s>, <s>yaṣṭi</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>, or with shoots produced by banyan and similar trees.
With honey and sugar it is beneficial for drinking, for food, and for sprinkling the anus.
Likewise, meat broths and the like that are not sour, with ghee added, are beneficial in drinks and foods,
as is soup of <s>kāśmarya</s> fruit, slightly sour and with sugar.
In goat's milk diluted with half water, with <s>hrīvera</s>, blue lotus, and dry ginger,
a gruel accompanied by juice of <s>pṛśniparṇī</s> destroys bloody diarrhea.
Before food, or else, one should lick fresh butter mixed with honey and sugar.
When the bleeding is strong, goat's blood itself, or that of a deer, fried in ghee, is useful.
With milk as the after-drink, living on milk, one may take ghee produced from milk for three days,
or, eating broth of <s>kapiñjala</s>, one obtains health while licking it.
Having drunk a paste of <s>śatāvarī</s> with milk, while eating milk foods,

children.text: raktātīsāraṃ hantyāśu tayā vā sādhitaṃ ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: one quickly destroys bloody diarrhea, or else with ghee prepared with that plant.
With <s>lākṣā</s>, dry ginger, <s>vaidehī</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and bark of <s>dārvī</s>,
ghee cooked together with <s>indrayava</s>, and followed by thin gruel and rice-water,
quickly conquers diarrhea, even if severe and caused by all three <s>doṣa</s>s.
Black clay, conch shell, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, honey, blood, and rice-water
conquer bleeding; so too does <s>priyaṅgu</s> mixed with rice-water and honey.
A paste of black sesame seeds, with sugar as a fifth part,

children.text: ājena payasā pītaḥ sadyo raktaṃ niyacchati
children.translated_text: drunk with goat's milk, immediately restrains the blood.
Having drunk sandalwood with sugar and honey in rice-water,
one is freed from burning, thirst, faintness, and the flow of blood.

children.text: gudasya dāhe pāke vā sekalepā hitā himāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is burning or suppuration of the anus, cold sprinklings and applications are beneficial.
When blood is passed little by little, repeatedly, and with pain,

children.text: yadā vibaddho vāyuśca kṛcchrāccarati vā na vā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>vāyu</s> is obstructed and moves with difficulty, or does not move at all,
then one should prepare for him the <s>picchā-basti</s> described earlier.
Having crushed the leaves of <s>śiṃśipā</s> and <s>kovidāra</s>,
one should cook barley in their decoction, together with ghee and milk.
When mucus flows, when there is prolapse of the anus, or when there are pains from straining,
a <s>picchā-basti</s> should be applied; it restores strength to one injured and wasted.
And an unctuous enema should be made with ghee cooked with <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>.

children.text: raktaṃ viṭsahitaṃ pūrvaṃ paścād vā yo 'tisāryate
children.translated_text: For one who passes blood mixed with feces first or afterward,
one should prepare <s>śatāvarī</s> ghee for licking.
Freshly churned new butter, licked with half as much sugar
and a quarter part honey, quickly conquers that disorder in one who eats wholesome food.
Having pounded the shoots of <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, and <s>aśvattha</s>, one should soak them

children.text: ahorātraṃ jale tapte ghṛtaṃ tenāmbhasā pacet ||
children.translated_text: for a day and night in hot water; with that water one should cook ghee.
Mixed with half as much sugar, it should be licked with a quarter part honey.

children.text: adho vā yadi vāpyūrdhvaṃ yasya raktaṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: or downward, or also upward, in one from whom blood flows.
In diarrhea caused by <s>kapha</s>, the treatment described for <s>vāta</s> should be done, especially the digestion of <s>āma</s>.
When this is associated with it, he should drink a preparation cooked for kindling the digestive fire:
<s>bilva</s>, <s>karkaṭikā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>prāṇadā</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>,
or <s>vacā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>bhūtīka</s>, coriander, and <s>amaradāru</s>;
or else root of long pepper, the two kinds of long pepper, and <s>citraka</s>.
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>agnivatsaka</s>, <s>granthi</s>, bitter substances, dry ginger, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>,
whether boiled as a decoction or ground as a paste, are medicine for diarrhea caused by <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> salt, <s>vacā</s>, the three pungents, asafoetida, <s>prativiṣā</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>,
powdered, should be drunk by one afflicted with <s>kapha</s>-diarrhea together with warm water.
Having licked the middle pulp of <s>kapittha</s> with the three pungents, honey, and sugar,
or <s>kaṭphala</s> mixed with honey, one is freed from abdominal disease.

children.text: kaṇāṃ madhuyutāṃ līḍhvā takraṃ pītvā sacitrakam ||
children.translated_text: Having licked long pepper mixed with honey, or drunk buttermilk with <s>citraka</s>,
or having eaten young <s>bilva</s> fruits, one drives away disease of the abdomen.
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>mocarasa</s>, <s>ambhoda</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and dry ginger
will destroy even very difficult diarrhea when taken with jaggery and buttermilk.
With <s>yavānī</s>, root of long pepper, the four aromatics, and dry ginger,
with black pepper, <s>agnija</s>, parched grain, cumin, coriander, and <s>sauvarcala</s> in equal parts,
with threefold quantities of <s>vṛṣāmla</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, long pepper, <s>bilva</s>, pomegranate, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
with sixfold sugar and eightfold <s>kapittha</s>, a powder is made.
This powder conquers diarrhea, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, wasting, abdominal tumors, throat diseases,
cough, dyspnea, weakness of digestive fire, piles, catarrh, and anorexia.
One <s>karṣa</s> of <s>tavakṣīrī</s> and two <s>karṣa</s>s of the four aromatics,
with <s>yavānī</s>, coriander, cumin, <s>granthi</s>, and the three pungents, each one <s>pala</s>,
eight <s>pala</s>s of pomegranate and an equal amount of sugar, when made together,
has the qualities of the eightfold <s>kapittha</s> powder; this is the <s>dāḍimāṣṭaka</s> powder.
According to the condition, it should be eaten with relishes and the like described for diarrhea caused by <s>vāta</s>.
A relish containing <s>viḍaṅga</s>, black pepper, <s>kapittha</s>, and dry ginger,
sour with <s>cāṅgerī</s>, buttermilk, jujube, and sour substances, conquers <s>kapha</s>-diarrhea.

children.text: kṣīṇe śleṣmaṇi pūrvoktam amlaṃ lākṣādi ṣaṭpalam
children.translated_text: When the <s>kapha</s> has diminished, one should give the previously mentioned sour <s>lākṣādi ṣaṭpala</s>,
or old ghee mixed with the liquid portion of barley gruel.
When there is obstruction by <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, or even when <s>kapha</s> is flowing excessively,
or when there is pain or <s>pravāhikā</s> (dysenteric straining), a slimy enema is recommended.
It should contain <s>vacā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, long pepper, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, dill, and salt,
with <s>bilva</s> oil, or with oil cooked with <s>vacā</s> and the other drugs.
Repeated warm oil enemas are beneficial for one afflicted by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
When <s>kapha</s> has diminished and the rectum has been weakened by long-lasting diarrhea,
<s>vāta</s>, strong and situated in its own place, inevitably arises.

children.text: sa balī sahasā hanyāt tasmāt taṃ tvarayā jayet ||
children.translated_text: Being powerful, it can kill suddenly; therefore one should conquer it quickly.
After <s>vāta</s>, one should conquer <s>pitta</s>; after <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: jayet pūrvaṃ trayāṇāṃ vā bhaved yo balavattamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, among the three, whichever is strongest should be conquered first.

children.text: bhīśokābhyām api calaḥ śīghraṃ kupyatyatas tayoḥ
children.translated_text: The mobile <s>vāta</s> is quickly aggravated also by fear and grief; therefore for those two
one should perform <s>vāta</s>-pacifying treatment, along with gladdening and reassurance.

children.text: yasyoccārād vinā mūtraṃ pavano vā pravartate
children.translated_text: For one in whom urine or wind passes without evacuation of stool,
when his digestive fire is bright and his bowel is light, his abdominal disease is pacified.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>grahaṇī-doṣa</s>.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
A <s>doṣa</s> lodged in the <s>grahaṇī</s> should be treated as in indigestion,
and its <s>āma</s> should be digested by the method taught for diarrhea.
At meal time one should administer barley gruel and similar foods mixed with <s>pañcakola</s> and the like,
and again foods that are pungent and light, together with formulations that kindle digestion.

children.text: dadyāt sātiviṣāṃ peyām āme sāmlāṃ sanāgarām
children.translated_text: When there is <s>āma</s>, one should give a drink with <s>ativiṣā</s>, sour and containing dry ginger.
For drinking, one should give water, buttermilk, liquor, and the like as prescribed for diarrhea.
For those with <s>grahaṇī-doṣa</s>, buttermilk is wholesome because it kindles digestion, is absorbent, and is light,
and because, being sweet in its post-digestive effect, it does not vitiate <s>pitta</s>.
Because it is astringent, hot, diffusive, and dry, it is beneficial in <s>kapha</s>.
For <s>vāta</s>, fresh buttermilk is not burning, because it is sweet, sour, and dense.
From four <s>prastha</s>s of sour substances, three <s>pala</s>s of the three pungents,
four <s>pala</s>s of salts, and eight <s>pala</s>s of sugar,
one should make a powder and sprinkle it into vegetables, soups, rice, relishes, and the like.
It removes cough, indigestion, anorexia, dyspnea, heart disease, pallor, splenic disease, and abdominal tumors.
One should drink a cooked preparation of dry ginger, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>musta</s>, which removes <s>āma</s>,
or its paste with hot water, or dry ginger, or else <s>abhayā</s>,
with rock salt, or <s>vacā</s> and related drugs in the same way, or else with liquor.
When there is <s>āma</s> in the stool together with straining, he should drink it with pomegranate water.
One should grind salt with <s>viḍa</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and dry ginger.
When <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> are accompanied by <s>āma</s> and cause pain in the bowel, it should be taken with warm water.
<s>Kaliṅga</s>, asafoetida, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>sauvarcala</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>
should be drunk with hot water in vomiting, heart disease, and colic.
A powder of <s>pathyā</s>, <s>sauvarcala</s>, and cumin, combined with black pepper,
long pepper, dry ginger, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, and the two <s>bṛhatī</s>s,
<s>citraka</s>, <s>kauṭaja</s>, alkali, and also the five salts,
when powdered, should be drunk with curds, liquor, its clear upper liquid, warm water, or sour gruel.
It is for increasing the digestive fire and is supreme for removing <s>vāta</s> from the bowel.

children.text: paṭūni pañca dvau kṣārau maricaṃ pañcakolakam ||
children.translated_text: The five salts, the two alkalis, black pepper, <s>pañcakola</s>,
<s>dīpyaka</s>, and asafoetida, made into pills with citron juice,
or with jujube and pomegranate water, are supremely digestive and kindling.
Of <s>tālīśapattra</s>, <s>cavikā</s>, and black pepper, one <s>pala</s> each;
of long pepper and its root, two <s>pala</s>s each; of dry ginger, three <s>pala</s>s.
<s>Caturjāta</s> and <s>uśīra</s>, one <s>karṣa</s> each, should be finely powdered.

children.text: guḍena vaṭakān kṛtvā triguṇena sadā bhajet ||
children.translated_text: Having made pills with three times as much jaggery, one should always use them.
Wine, soup, meat broth, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, whey, gruel, and milk are the accompanying drinks.
For vomiting, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, pain in the side, and heart pain in people of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> constitution,
and for fever, swelling, pallor, abdominal tumor, after-effects of drinking, and hemorrhoids,
as well as for salivation, coryza, dyspnea, and cough, it is used for their cessation.
In that same preparation, when there is obstruction of feces, one should give <s>abhayā</s> in place of dry ginger.
And in vomiting and the like when caused by <s>pitta</s>, the pills should be combined with four times as much sugar.

children.text: pakvena vaṭakāḥ kāryā guḍena sitayāpi vā
children.translated_text: The pills should be made with cooked jaggery, or else with sugar,

children.text: paraṃ hi vahnisaṃparkāl laghimānaṃ bhajanti te ||
children.translated_text: for by contact with fire they become especially light.
Now, in this <s>grahaṇī</s> disease caused by <s>māruta</s> when the undigested matter has matured,
the physician should have the patient drink ghee combined with digestive-kindling drugs, little by little.
When the digestive fire has been somewhat kindled, if feces, urine, and wind are obstructed,

children.text: dvyahaṃ tryahaṃ vā saṃsnehya svinnābhyaktaṃ nirūhayet ||
children.translated_text: he should be oleated for two or three days, then fomented and anointed, and given a decoction enema.
After that, when <s>anila</s> has been pacified, with castor oil, ghee, or <s>tailvaka</s> oil,
along with alkali, one should purge him when the <s>doṣa</s>s have loosened.
When his channels have been cleansed and dried, and when the stool is bound, one should give him an oil enema
with oil prepared with digestive-kindling, sour, and <s>vāta</s>-subduing substances.

children.text: nirūḍhaṃ ca viriktaṃ ca samyak cāpyanuvāsitam
children.translated_text: When he has been given a decoction enema, purged, and also properly given an oil enema,
and has resumed light food, one should again make him practice taking ghee.
With <s>pañcamūla</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, root of long pepper, and rock salt,
with <s>rāsnā</s>, the two alkalis, cumin, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>śaṭhī</s>, ghee is prepared,
using vinegar, the fresh juice of citron and of fresh ginger,
and of dried radish, sour jujube, <s>cukrikā</s>, and pomegranate,
with buttermilk, whey, the clear part of liquor, <s>sauvīraka</s>, and grain-wash water,

children.text: kāñjikena ca tat pakvam agnidīptikaraṃ param ||
children.translated_text: and also with sour gruel. Cooked thus, it is supreme for kindling the digestive fire.
It removes colic, abdominal tumor, abdominal enlargement, dyspnea, cough, <s>anila</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
Or one should give ghee cooked with the juice of <s>bījapūraka</s>.
Oil cooked with these same drugs is for anointing and removes disorders of the mobile <s>vāta</s> principle.
Or one may drink the powder of these medicines with pleasant warm water.

children.text: vāte śleṣmāvṛte sāme kaphe vā vāyunoddhate
children.translated_text: When <s>vāta</s> is covered by <s>śleṣman</s> together with <s>āma</s>, or when <s>kapha</s> has been stirred up by <s>vāyu</s>,

children.text: agner nirvāpakaṃ pittaṃ rekeṇa vamanena vā ||
children.translated_text: one should remove the <s>pitta</s> that extinguishes the digestive fire, by purgation or by emesis.
Then, with bitter, light, absorbent, digestive-kindling, and non-burning substances,

children.text: annaiḥ saṃdhukṣayed agniṃ cūrṇaiḥ snehaiśca tiktakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should kindle the digestive fire with foods, powders, and bitter fats.
<s>Paṭola</s>, neem, <s>trāyantī</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>tiktaka</s>, and <s>parpaṭa</s>,
bark and fruit of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, fruit of <s>madhuśigru</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
bark of <s>dārvī</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>musta</s>, and sandalwood,
<s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay leaf, and deodar,

children.text: cūrṇitaṃ madhunā lehyaṃ peyaṃ madyair jalena vā
children.translated_text: powdered, should be licked with honey or drunk with alcoholic drinks or with water.
It destroys heart disease, pallor, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, abdominal tumor, colic, anorexia, and fever,
as well as jaundice, <s>saṃnipāta</s>, and diseases of the mouth.
Equal parts of <s>bhūnimba</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and <s>indrayava</s>,
two parts of <s>citraka</s> and sixteen parts of <s>vatsaka</s> bark should be powdered.
Drunk with jaggery and cold water, it removes <s>grahaṇī doṣa</s> and abdominal tumor.
It conquers jaundice, fever, pallor, urinary disease, anorexia, and diarrhea.
Dry ginger, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,

children.text: kuṭajatvakphalaṃ tiktā dhātakī ca kṛtaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: bark and fruit of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, and <s>dhātakī</s>, made into powder,
are prescribed with honey and rice-water in <s>grahaṇī</s> disease caused by <s>pitta</s>,
and also in dysenteric straining, hemorrhoids, pain in the rectum, and bleeding disorders.
Sandalwood, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, and <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>,
<s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>sphoṭā</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, and <s>aṭarūṣaka</s>,
<s>paṭola</s>, fig, aśvattha, banyan, plakṣa, and kapitāna,

children.text: kaṭukāṃ rohiṇīṃ mustāṃ nimbaṃ ca dvipalāṃśakān
children.translated_text: <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>musta</s>, and neem, each two <s>palas</s>,

children.text: droṇe 'pāṃ sādhayet tena pacet sarpiḥ picūnmitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be boiled in a <s>droṇa</s> of water; with that decoction one should cook ghee with paste-measures,
including <s>kirātatiktā</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>māgadhikā</s>, and blue lotus.

children.text: pittagrahaṇyāṃ tat peyaṃ kuṣṭhoktaṃ tiktakaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: That should be drunk in <s>pitta</s>-type <s>grahaṇī</s>, as also the <s>tiktaka</s> ghee taught in the treatment of skin disease.
When <s>grahaṇī</s> is vitiated by <s>śleṣman</s>, after strong emesis has been performed,
one should gradually increase the digestive fire with pungent, sour, salty, and alkaline substances.
With <s>pañcakola</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, coriander, <s>pāṭhā</s>, fragrant <s>palāśa</s>,
and with preparations strongly infused with citron, one should prepare gruel and the like.
A <s>droṇa</s> of <s>madhūka</s> flowers, and half as much <s>viḍaṅga</s>,
half as much <s>citraka</s>, and likewise an <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>bhallātaka</s>,
together with eight <s>palas</s> of <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, should be boiled in three <s>droṇas</s> of water.
When boiled down to one <s>droṇa</s> and cooled, it should be combined with half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of honey.
After it has been scented with cardamom, lotus-stalk, agarwood,

children.text: kumbhe māsaṃ sthitaṃ jātam āsavaṃ taṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: and sandalwood, it should stand in a jar for a month; when it has become an <s>āsava</s>, one should administer it.
This stimulates the <s>grahaṇī</s>, is nourishing, and removes disorders of <s>pitta</s> and blood.
It destroys wasting disease, skin disease, leucoderma, and urinary disorders.
The fresh juice of <s>madhūka</s> flowers should be boiled until reduced by half.
When cooled and combined with a quarter part of honey, it should be stored as before.

children.text: tat piban grahaṇīdoṣān jayet sarvān hitāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: A person who drinks that, while eating wholesome food, conquers all <s>grahaṇī</s> disorders.
In the same way, one should drink fermented juices of grapes, sugarcane, and dates.
Asafoetida, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>mādrī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, <s>gokṣura</s>,
and <s>pañcakola</s>, each one <s>karṣa</s>, with the five salts, each one <s>pala</s>,
should be pounded in two <s>kuḍavas</s> of ghee and oil and in two <s>prasthas</s> of curds.
It should be decocted over the fire until the liquid has been absorbed into the clay vessel.
Then it should be burnt in a closed, smoky fire, powdered, and drenched with ghee.

children.text: pibet pāṇitalaṃ tasmiñ jīrṇe syān madhurāśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should drink a palmful of it; when it has been digested, he should take sweet food.
It destroys all disorders of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, and also poison and artificial poison.
One should burn <s>bhūnimba</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>parpaṭa</s>;
with buffalo urine, and drink it; it increases the digestive fire.

children.text: dve haridre vacā kuṣṭhaṃ citrakaḥ kaṭurohiṇī ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>haridrā</s>s, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,
and <s>mustā</s>: an alkali prepared with goat's urine is a stimulant of the digestive fire.
Four <s>pala</s>s from the stalk of <s>sudhā</s>, three <s>pala</s>s of the three salts,

children.text: vārtākakuḍavaṃ cārkād aṣṭau dve citrakāt pale
children.translated_text: a <s>kuḍava</s> of eggplant, eight <s>pala</s>s from <s>arka</s>, and two <s>pala</s>s of <s>citraka</s>:
after burning these with the juice of eggplant, the pills are to be taken after meals.
They quickly digest the food that has been eaten and are beneficial for cough, dyspnea, and piles.
They also pacify <s>viṣūcikā</s> (cholera-like illness), catarrh, and heart disease.
<s>Mātuluṅga</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, the three pungents, and <s>harītakī</s>,
the alkalis called <s>svarjikā</s> and <s>yāvaśūka</s>, and the five salts:
that powder, drunk with warm water, increases strength, complexion, and digestive fire.

children.text: ślaiṣmike grahaṇīdoṣe savāte tair ghṛtaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: In a <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder that is phlegmatic and accompanied by <s>vāta</s>, one should cook ghee with these.
The <s>Dhānvantara</s>, <s>Ṣaṭpala</s>, <s>Bhallātaka-ghṛta</s>, and <s>Abhayā-ghṛta</s> preparations are also applicable.
One should take substances produced from <s>viḍa</s>, <s>kāca</s>, <s>uṣa</s> salt, <s>svarjikā</s>, and <s>yāvaśūka</s>,

children.text: saptalāṃ kaṇṭakārīṃ ca citrakaṃ caikato dahet
children.translated_text: and burn <s>saptalā</s>, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, and <s>citraka</s> together.
In half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of this strained alkali, repeated seven times,
one should cook an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee; it is to be drunk for increasing the strength of the digestive fire.
When there is an accumulation of <s>doṣa</s>s, one should apply the five procedures, according to the patient's strength.
In phlegmatic salivation with weak digestive fire, a dry, bitter kindling treatment should be used.
For a thin person, when <s>kapha</s> rises, oily and dry measures should be used alternately.
For one whose body is wasted, emaciated, and depleted, the kindling treatment should be combined with unctuous substances.
For one with abundant <s>pitta</s>, the kindling treatment should be bitter and joined with sweet substances.
For one with abundant <s>vāta</s>, fat joined with sour and salty substances is recommended.
One should know fat itself to be the supreme means for kindling a weak digestive fire.
Even very heavy food is not able to extinguish a fire that has been fed with fat.

children.text: yo 'lpāgnitvāt kaphe kṣīṇe varcaḥ pakvam api ślatham ||
children.translated_text: When, because of weak digestive fire and depleted <s>kapha</s>, a person passes stool that is cooked but loose,

children.text: muñcet paṭvauṣadhayutaṃ sa pibed alpaśo ghṛtam
children.translated_text: he should drink ghee little by little, mixed with sharp medicines.
By that, <s>samāna</s>, brought into its own channel and set to its own function,

children.text: samāno dīpayatyagnim agneḥ saṃdhukṣako hi saḥ
children.translated_text: kindles the digestive fire, for it is what fans the digestive fire.
And a person who passes feces with difficulty because of its hardness

children.text: sa ghṛtaṃ lavaṇair yuktaṃ naro 'nnāvagrahaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: should drink ghee mixed with salts before taking food.

children.text: raukṣyān mande 'nale sarpis tailaṃ vā dīpanaiḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: When the digestive fire is weak because of dryness, he should drink ghee or oil with kindling substances.
When it is weak because of excessive drinking of fats, alkalis, powders, <s>āsava</s>s, and <s>ariṣṭa</s>s should be used.
But when it is due to <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of wind), evacuative and unctuous enemas should be employed.
When the digestive fire is weak because the <s>doṣa</s>s are excessively increased, after purification one should follow the dietary regimen.
For one freed from disease but with weak digestive fire, ghee alone is the kindling remedy.
When one is exhausted from travel, fasting, and emaciation, one should feed him barley gruel with ghee.

children.text: annāvapīḍitaṃ balyaṃ dīpanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Taken along with food, it gives strength, kindles the digestive fire, and nourishes.
But men who have become wasted, depleted, and thin through a long continuation of the condition
should be fed with sour meat soups of <s>prasaha</s> animals, carnivorous creatures.
Because they are light, hot, pungent, and cleansing, they quickly kindle the digestive fire.
And because their flesh is built up from meat, they greatly increase strength.
With fats, <s>āsava</s>, liquor, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, powders, decoctions, and wholesome foods,
properly used, the strength of the body and of the digestive fire increases.
Just as an external fire, blazing on a log, grows through resinous fuel,
so the fire in the gut grows through foods containing fat.
The bodily digestive fire is not kindled by not eating, nor by overeating.
It is like a fire without fuel, or a small fire covered over by wind and fuel.

children.text: yadā kṣīṇe kaphe pittaṃ svasthāne pavanānugam
children.translated_text: When, after <s>kapha</s> has been depleted, <s>pitta</s>, remaining in its own place and followed by <s>pavana</s>,
increases the digestive fire, then that fire, accompanied by wind,

children.text: paktvānnam āśu dhātūṃśca sarvān ojaśca saṃkṣipan
children.translated_text: quickly cooks the food and all the tissues, and contracts the <s>ojas</s>.

children.text: mārayet syāt sa nā svastho bhukte jīrṇe tu tāmyati ||
children.translated_text: It may kill; that person is not healthy, and when the meal has been digested he languishes.
Thirst, cough, burning, fainting, and the like are diseases arising from excessive digestive fire.
That excessive digestive fire should be brought to calm with foods and drinks that are heavy, unctuous, mild, dense, cold, and stable,
as a blazing fire is calmed with water.
Food should be brought to him again and again, even when the previous food is undigested,
so that, finding an interval without fuel, it does not destroy him.
He should eat <s>kṛśarā</s>, oily milk pudding, flour preparations, and products made from jaggery,
as well as the well-nourished flesh of aquatic and marsh-dwelling animals.
Especially he should eat smooth fish, and those that live in still water.
He should eat well-fattened sheep meat; it checks excessive digestive fire.

children.text: payaḥ sahamadhūcchiṣṭaṃ ghṛtaṃ vā tṛṣitaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: When thirsty, he should drink milk together with beeswax, or else ghee.
He may take wheat flour with milk, drenched in abundant ghee,
or fats mixed with the soup of marsh animals, excluding oil.
Or milk cooked with <s>śyāmā</s> and <s>trivṛt</s> should be given as a purgative,
repeatedly removing <s>pitta</s>, with milk pudding as the follow-up meal.

children.text: yat kiṃcid guru medyaṃ ca śleṣmakāri ca bhojanam
children.translated_text: Whatever food is heavy, fatty, and productive of <s>śleṣman</s>,

children.text: sarvaṃ tad atyagnihitaṃ bhuktvā ca svapanaṃ divā ||
children.translated_text: all of that is beneficial in excessive digestive fire; and after eating, sleeping by day is beneficial.
The digestive fire digests food; when deprived of food, it digests the <s>doṣa</s>s.
When the <s>doṣa</s>s are depleted it digests the tissues, and when the tissues are depleted, life itself.

children.text: etat prakṛtyaiva viruddham annaṃ saṃyogasaṃskāravaśena cedam
children.translated_text: 'This food is incompatible by its very nature, and this one through combination and preparation':

children.text: ityādi avijñāya yatheṣṭaceṣṭāścaranti yat sāgnibalasya śaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: not knowing such matters, people act as they please; the result depends on the power of the digestive fire.

children.text: tasmād agniṃ pālayet sarvayatnais tasmin naṣṭe yāti nā nāśam eva
children.translated_text: Therefore one should protect the digestive fire by every effort; when it is lost, a person goes only to destruction.

children.text: doṣair graste grasyate rogasaṃghair yukte tu syān nīrujo dīrghajīvī ||
children.translated_text: When it is seized by the <s>doṣa</s>s, one is seized by hosts of diseases; but when it is properly balanced, one is free from illness and long-lived.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>mūtrāghāta</s> (urinary obstruction).
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
In painful urination caused by <s>vāta</s>, the body below the navel should be anointed with <s>vāta</s>-pacifying oil,
and the body should be fomented with very unctuous boluses, affusions, and immersions.
With <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>balā</s>, castor, barley, <s>abhīru</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
with horse gram, jujube, <s>pattūra</s>, <s>vṛścīva</s>, and <s>upalabhedaka</s>,
oil, ghee, and the fats of boar and bear, cooked with their decoctions and pastes,
and prepared with the five salts, when drunk, are supreme removers of pain.
These substances should also be used in drinks and food, and likewise in bolus poultices and applications,

children.text: saha tailaphalair yuñjyāt sāmlāni snehavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: together with castor fruits, sour substances, and unctuous materials.
One should drink liquor rich in <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, which removes urinary pain.
In the <s>pitta</s> type, one should use cooling affusion, anointing paste, and immersion.
One should drink <s>varī</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, together with <s>kaseruka</s>,
and the five roots called grasses, cooked and mixed with honey and sugar.
<s>Vṛṣaka</s>, the seeds of cucumber, <s>ervāru</s>, and <s>laṭvā</s>, and saffron,
when drunk with raisin-water, remove all forms of <s>mūtrāghāta</s>.
Or one may drink the seeds of <s>ervāru</s>, licorice, and <s>dārvī</s> with rice-washing water,

children.text: toyena kalkaṃ drākṣāyāḥ pibet paryuṣitena vā ||
children.translated_text: or the paste of raisins with water, or with water that has stood overnight.
In the type caused by <s>kapha</s>, one should practice emesis, fomentation, and food that is sharp, hot, and pungent,

children.text: yavānāṃ vikṛtīḥ kṣāraṃ kālaśeyaṃ ca śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: preparations of barley, alkali, and <s>kālaśeya</s> liquor.
One should drink finely powdered cardamom with liquor, or with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit,
or a mixture of crane bone, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, cardamom, and the three pungents, with honey and urine.
Or one should administer the fresh juice of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, mixed with honey,
or <s>śitivāraka</s> seed, finely powdered, with buttermilk.
<s>Dhava</s>, <s>saptāhva</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s>,
together with <s>kembuka</s>, cardamom, and <s>karañja</s>, should be cooked and prepared with honey.

children.text: tair vā peyāṃ pravālaṃ vā cūrṇitaṃ taṇḍulāmbunā
children.translated_text: With these one may drink thin gruel, or powdered coral with rice-washing water,
or alkali of <s>pāṭalā</s> with oil, strained seven times.
From <s>pāṭalī</s>, barley-awns, <s>pāribhadra</s>, and also sesame,
one should prepare liquor in alkaline water, combined with bark, cardamom, and dry ginger.

children.text: pibed guḍopadaṃśān vā lihyād etān pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: One should drink these, or lick them separately with jaggery as an accompaniment.
In a condition arising from the combination of all <s>doṣa</s>s, all this is beneficial according to the state of the disease.
It is also beneficial in a recently arisen stone and in disorders beginning with <s>vāta</s> in the bladder.
<s>Aśmarī</s> (urinary stone) is regarded as a terrible disease, comparable to death.
When recent it is curable by medicines; when fully grown it requires cutting.
In its preliminary symptoms, the procedure beginning with oleation is recommended.
<s>Pāṣāṇabheda</s>, <s>vasuka</s>, <s>vaśira</s>, <s>aśmantaka</s>, and <s>varī</s>,
<s>kapotavaṅkā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>bhallūka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>kacchaka</s>,
<s>vṛkṣādanī</s>, the fruit of <s>śāka</s>, the two <s>vyāghrī</s>s, <s>guṇṭha</s>, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>,

children.text: yavāḥ kulatthāḥ kolāni varuṇaḥ katakāt phalam ||
children.translated_text: barley, horse gram, jujubes, <s>varuṇa</s>, and <s>kataka</s> fruit:
ghee cooked in the decoction of these, with an addition of the <s>ūṣakādi</s> group,

children.text: bhinatti vātasambhūtāṃ tat pītaṃ śīghram aśmarīm ||
children.translated_text: when drunk, quickly breaks up a stone produced by <s>vāta</s>.
One should drink the root paste of <s>gandharvahasta</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>gokṣuraka</s>, and <s>ikṣurāta</s>,
with sweet curds; it breaks stones.

children.text: kuśaḥ kāśaḥ śaro guṇṭha itkaṭo moraṭo 'śmabhit
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, reed, <s>guṇṭha</s>, <s>itkaṭa</s>, <s>moraṭa</s>, and <s>aśmabhit</s>,
<s>darbha</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>vārāhī</s>, rice root, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>,
<s>bhallūka</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>pattūra</s> with <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>,

children.text: punarnave śirīṣaśca teṣāṃ kvāthe paced ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>punarnavā</s>s, and <s>śirīṣa</s>: in their decoction one should cook ghee,
with the paste of the seeds of cucumber and the other gourds, and with blue lotus,
<s>madhuka</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>; that breaks a <s>pitta</s>-stone.
The <s>varuṇādi</s> group, the two groups that pacify <s>vāta</s>, cardamom, <s>hareṇukā</s>,
<s>guggulu</s>, black pepper, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>citraka</s>, together with <s>surāhvaya</s>:
with these made into a paste, and with the <s>ūṣakādi</s> group added,

children.text: bhinatti kaphajām āśu sādhitaṃ ghṛtam aśmarīm ||
children.translated_text: ghee prepared from them quickly breaks a stone born of <s>kapha</s>.
One should also prepare remedies with alkalis, milk, barley gruel, and the like, each with its own appropriate substances,
and with fruits produced from <s>picuka</s>, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>kataka</s>, <s>śāka</s>, and blue lotus.
Drunk with warm water and jaggery, these are supreme for making urinary gravel fall.
The bones of <s>krauñca</s>, camel, and donkey, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>tālapattrikā</s>,
<s>ajamodā</s>, the root of <s>kadamba</s>, and <s>viśva</s>, the universal medicine,
when drunk with liquor or hot water, break up gravel.
Powder of <s>nṛtyakuṇḍaka</s> seeds, mixed with honey,
when drunk for seven days with ewe's milk, causes a stone to fall.
A decoction made from <s>śigru</s> root, taken lukewarm, also causes a stone to fall.
The alkali produced from sesame, <s>apāmārga</s>, plantain, <s>palāśa</s>, and barley
should be drunk with sheep's urine in cases of gravel and stones.
Or one should drink the root of <s>kapotavaṅkā</s> alone with liquor and similar vehicles,
or drink milk cooked with it, when afflicted by pains.
Or one may drink milk cooked with <s>harītakī</s> stones, or cooked with <s>punarnavā</s>.
While eating milk-rice, one may take the root of <s>barhiśikhā</s> with rice-washing water.
In the conditions of <s>mūtrāghāta</s>, one should apply treatment by distinction; likewise also in the remaining disorders.
Water, milk, or ghee cooked with the <s>bṛhatyādi</s> group,

children.text: toyaṃ payo vā sarpir vā sarvamūtravikārajit ||
children.translated_text: with <s>gokṣura</s> doubled, conquers all urinary disorders.
<s>Devadāru</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, licorice, and <s>harītakī</s>
should be drunk with liquor, milk, or water in all forms of <s>mūtrāghāta</s>.

children.text: rasaṃ vā dhanvayāsasya kaṣāyaṃ kakubhasya vā
children.translated_text: Or one may drink the juice of <s>dhanvayāsa</s>, or the decoction of <s>kakubha</s>.
or <s>triphalā</s> ground with pleasant water and mixed with rock salt.
Or he should take gruel prepared in a decoction of <s>vyāghrī</s> and <s>gokṣuraka</s>, together with <s>phāṇita</s> (thickened sugarcane syrup),
or in a decoction of the <s>vīratarādi</s> group, or even in the meat-juice of a cock.
Or he should eat <s>śilājatu</s> impregnated with the <s>vīratarādi</s> group,

children.text: madyaṃ vā nigadaṃ pītvā rathenāśvena vā vrajet ||
children.translated_text: or, after drinking harmless wine, he should travel by chariot or by horse.
Through the shaking caused by swift motion, his urinary stone slips downward.
And in every way the <s>vīratarādi</s> group is to be employed.

children.text: rekārthaṃ tailvakaṃ sarpir vastikarma ca śīlayet
children.translated_text: For purgation he should use <s>tailvaka</s> ghee, and he should practice enema therapy.
But especially, after cleansing, he should use urethral enemas for a seminal stone.
By those, when the urinary passage is strong, there is purification of the receptacle of semen.

children.text: pumān sutṛpto vṛṣyāṇāṃ māṃsānāṃ kukkuṭasya ca ||
children.translated_text: For that purpose a man, well satisfied with aphrodisiac meats and with cock's meat,
being desirous, may freely have intercourse with women who are desirous and who give exhilaration.
If the disease is not pacified by these accomplished measures, then the physician,
after informing the king, should properly undertake the surgical instrument.

children.text: akriyāyāṃ dhruvo mṛtyuḥ kriyāyāṃ saṃśayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Without action death is certain; with action there may be uncertainty.
This is so even for a physician who is assured and whose operations have often succeeded.
Then, when the patient has been oleated, purified, and slightly emaciated,
with his body anointed and sweated, fasting, and with auspicious rites performed,
he should be made to recline in the lap of a man seated on a board reaching to the knees,
with the front part of his body upward, supine, seated on a cloth cushion.
Then, when his knees and elbows have been flexed, he should be firmly bound with cloth,
together with the assisting attendant, and he should be reassured.

children.text: nābheḥ samantād abhyajyād adhas tasyāśca vāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The physician should anoint all around his navel and below it on the left side,
and, after rubbing with the fist, should press until the stone has moved downward.
Then, having oiled the index and middle fingers and having lengthened the nails,
he should insert the two fingers into the left side of the anus along the perineal seam.
Having reached the stone by strength and effort between the anus and penis,
and having made the bladder free from folds and not stretched out,
he should press upward with the fingers until the foreign body becomes raised like a knot.

children.text: śalyaṃ syāt sevanīṃ muktvā yavamātreṇa pāṭayet
children.translated_text: Avoiding the seam, he should incise by the measure of a barley grain.

children.text: aśmamānena na yathā bhidyate sā tathāharet ||
children.translated_text: He should draw it out whole with a serpent-mouth instrument, in such a way that it is not broken because of the size of the stone.

children.text: samagraṃ sarpavaktreṇa strīṇāṃ vastis tu pārśvagaḥ
children.translated_text: For women, however, the bladder lies to the side,
since it is connected with the uterus; therefore the instrument should be placed as if on the lap.

children.text: nyased ato 'nyathā hyāsāṃ mūtrasrāvī vraṇo bhavet
children.translated_text: Otherwise, indeed, a wound discharging urine would occur in them.
And in a man too, because of cutting the urinary channel, this may occur in a single way.

children.text: vastibhedo 'śmarīhetuḥ siddhiṃ yāti na tu dvidhā
children.translated_text: Rupture of the bladder, caused by a stone, can be cured when single, but not when double.
When the foreign body has been removed, he should immerse the patient in a tub of warm water.

children.text: tathā na pūryate 'sreṇa vastiḥ pūrṇe tu pīḍayet
children.translated_text: In that way the bladder is not filled with blood; but if it becomes filled, he should press it.
Then he should pour water from milky trees into the end of the penis for purification of the urine.
He should cause him to take jaggery to satiety; with the wound smeared with honey and ghee, he should drink

children.text: dvau kālau saghṛtāṃ koṣṇāṃ yavāgūṃ mūtraśodhanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: warm gruel with ghee at the two meal times, prepared with urine-purifying drugs,
for three days; for ten days he should eat a little boiled rice with milk rich in jaggery.
After that he should eat with sour fruit juices and meat broths of animals that range in dry land.
After washing the wound with a decoction of milky trees, he should apply a paste
made from <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, licorice, and eye-medicines.
For anointing the wound he should cook oil with these same substances, together with turmeric.
For ten days he should sweat him; after seven nights, when the urine follows its own path,
but if the urine does not pass, he should cauterize the stone-wound with fire.
When it has returned to its own channel, he should treat him chiefly with sweet substances.

children.text: taṃ vastibhir na cārohed varṣaṃ rūḍhavraṇo 'pi saḥ
children.translated_text: He should not mount vehicles for a year, even when the wound has healed.
He should not swim in water, nor mount mountains, elephants, horses, trees, women, or chariots.
The urine- and semen-carrying channels, the bladder, the testicles, the perineal seam, the anus,
the urinary stream, and the vagina: these eight are to be avoided by the surgical instrument.
Now therefore we shall explain the treatment of <s>prameha</s> (urinary disease).
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
For a strong man suffering from <s>meha</s>, one should first perform emesis and purgation,
after oleation with oils made from mustard, <s>āriṣṭa</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>akṣa</s>, and <s>karañja</s>,
or with a fat cooked as appropriate with the <s>trikaṇṭakādi</s> group,
with an added paste of <s>musta</s>, <s>devāhva</s>, and dry ginger.
Then he should give an evacuative enema with a decoction of the <s>surasādi</s> group.

children.text: nyagrodhādes tu pittārtaṃ rasaiḥ śuddhaṃ ca tarpayet ||
children.translated_text: But one afflicted with <s>pitta</s>, after being purified, should be nourished with juices of the <s>nyagrodhādi</s> group.
Urinary obstruction, pain, abdominal tumor, wasting, and the like arise from depletion.
Thereafter, to guard against accompanying disorders, palliative measures should be employed.
For one who is not fit for purification, those same remedies should be given to drink in all forms of <s>meha</s>.
In the morning he should take turmeric soaked in the juice of <s>dhātrī</s>, with honey added,
or <s>dārvī</s>, <s>surāhva</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>musta</s>, boiled in water,
or <s>citraka</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, and <s>kaliṅga</s>, together with honey,

children.text: madhuyuktaṃ guḍūcyā vā rasam āmalakasya vā
children.translated_text: or the juice of <s>guḍūcī</s> or of <s>āmalaka</s>, mixed with honey.
For <s>kapha</s>, there are three decoctions with honey: of <s>lodhra</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>toyada</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s>; of <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and <s>dhanvana</s>;
and of <s>gāyatrī</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>kṛmihṛd</s>, and <s>dhava</s>.
For <s>pitta</s>, there are three decoctions with honey: of <s>uśīra</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and sandalwood; of <s>paṭola</s>, neem, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>;
and of <s>lodhra</s>, <s>ambu</s>, <s>kālīyaka</s>, and <s>dhātakī</s>.
According to the condition, with these he should prepare drink, food, and steepings of barley and wheat,
and fats in forms of <s>prameha</s> in which <s>vāta</s> is predominant.
Preparations of barley, such as cakes, roasted flour, and pellets, are beneficial.
Or grains produced from the dung of elephants and horses, or those born from bamboo,
grass-grains, pulses such as <s>mudga</s>, and old <s>śāli</s> rice together with <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice are suitable.
<s>Śrīkukkuṭa</s>, sour <s>khalaka</s> made from sesame and mustard oil-cake,
<s>kapittha</s>, <s>tinduka</s>, and <s>jambū</s>, and the <s>rāga</s> and <s>ṣāḍava</s> preparations made from them, are suitable.

children.text: tiktaṃ śākaṃ madhu śreṣṭhā bhakṣyāḥ śuṣkāḥ sasaktavaḥ
children.translated_text: Bitter greens, honey as the best sweetener, and dry eatables with roasted barley-meal should be eaten.
Meat of dry-land animals, roasted on a spit and well dried, and <s>ayaskṛti</s> are also suitable.
Old honey-based <s>ariṣṭa</s> and <s>āsava</s>, and <s>sīdhu</s> produced from cooked juice,
as well as water from the heartwood of <s>asana</s> and related trees, <s>darbha</s> water, and honey-water, should be used.
Barley that has been scented by soaking overnight in a decoction of <s>varā</s> and dried during the day

children.text: yaveṣu sukṛtān saktūn sakṣaudrān sīdhunā pibet ||
children.translated_text: should be made into well-prepared roasted meal, mixed with honey, and drunk with <s>sīdhu</s>.
The flowers of <s>śāla</s>, <s>saptāhva</s>, <s>kampilla</s>, <s>vṛkṣaka</s>, <s>akṣa</s>, <s>kapittha</s>,
and <s>rohītaka</s> should be finely powdered and eaten with honey.
In prameha caused by <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, one should drink it with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s>, or else,
with <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>, turmeric, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>somavalka</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>arjuna</s>,
with <s>padmaka</s>, <s>aśmantaka</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, sandalwood, agarwood, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
and with <s>paṭola</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>mādrī</s>, and <s>bhallātaka</s>, one should cook the medicated fat.

children.text: tailaṃ vātakaphe pitte ghṛtaṃ miśreṣu miśrakam
children.translated_text: Oil is used when <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> predominate, ghee when <s>pitta</s> predominates, and a mixture for mixed conditions.
<s>Daśamūla</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>surāhva</s>, the two kinds of <s>punarnavā</s>,
the roots of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>bhūkadamba</s>, <s>aruṣkara</s>,

children.text: karañjau varuṇān mūlaṃ pippalyāḥ pauṣkaraṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>karañja</s> trees, the root of <s>varuṇa</s>, and whatever root of <s>pippalī</s> and <s>pauṣkara</s> is used,
each separately in the amount of ten <s>palas</s>, and three <s>prasthas</s> of barley, jujube, and horse-gram,
should be boiled in eight times as much water until one quarter remains.
With that decoction, and with the paste of the two <s>pippalī</s>s, <s>cavya</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>nicula</s>, and <s>rohiṣa</s>,
together with <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>kampilla</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, and <s>viśva</s>, one should prepare

children.text: prasthaṃ ghṛtāj jayet sarvāṃs tan mehān piṭikā viṣam
children.translated_text: one <s>prastha</s> of ghee; it conquers all those pramehas, pustules, poisoning,
pallor, abscess, abdominal tumor, hemorrhoids, wasting disease, swelling, toxic abdominal disease,

children.text: śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ vamiṃ vṛddhiṃ plīhānaṃ vātaśoṇitam
children.translated_text: dyspnea, cough, vomiting, enlargement, splenic disease, <s>vātaśoṇita</s>,
skin disease, insanity, and epilepsy; this is the <s>Dhānvantara</s> ghee.
<s>Lodhra</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>nakha</s>, and <s>plava</s>,
<s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kramuka</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and <s>agnika</s>,
the two <s>viśālā</s>s, the four aromatics, <s>bhūnimba</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,

children.text: yavānīṃ pauṣkaraṃ pāṭhāṃ granthiṃ cavyaṃ phalatrayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>yavānī</s>, <s>pauṣkara</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>granthi</s>, <s>cavya</s>, and the three fruits,
each one <s>karṣa</s>, should be placed in a water-jar; when one quarter remains after boiling and it has been strained and cooled,

children.text: dvau prasthau mākṣikāt kṣiptvā rakṣet pakṣam upekṣayā ||
children.translated_text: two <s>prasthas</s> of honey should be added, and it should be kept undisturbed for a fortnight.
This <s>lodhrāsava</s> restrains prameha, hemorrhoids, leucoderma, skin disease, anorexia, worms,
pallor, disorder of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, and obesity.
One should prepare twenty <s>palas</s> each of the <s>asana</s> group,

children.text: dvivahe 'pāṃ kṣipet tatra pādasthe dve śate guḍāt ||
children.translated_text: in two <s>vahas</s> of water; when it has been reduced to a quarter, two hundred <s>palas</s> of jaggery should be added.
Half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of honey and one-<s>pala</s> quantities of the <s>vatsaka</s> group, made into paste, should also be added.
That should be placed in a firm ghee-vessel smeared with honey and powdered <s>pippalī</s>,
sealed with lac, and buried in a heap of barley.
Thin plates of sharp iron, heated many times in khadira charcoal, should be plunged into it
until the iron has been consumed.

children.text: ayaskṛtiḥ sthitā pītā pūrvasmād adhikā guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This matured <s>ayaskṛti</s>, when drunk, has qualities superior to the preceding preparation.

children.text: rūkṣam udvartanaṃ gāḍhaṃ vyāyāmo niśi jāgaraḥ
children.translated_text: Dry and strong rubbing, physical exercise, staying awake at night,
and whatever else destroys <s>śleṣman</s> and fat are beneficial both externally and internally.
After drinking a <s>tulā</s> of mineral-born <s>śilājatu</s>, thoroughly infused with heartwood waters,
and while eating <s>śāli</s> rice with broths of wild animals, using only that heartwood water,
one overcomes all pramehas, even when they have many complications,
as well as scrofulous swellings, tumors, nodules, obesity, skin disease, fistula,
worms, elephantiasis, and swellings; this is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
A poor man, without umbrella or footwear and following a sage's mode of life,

children.text: yojanānāṃ śataṃ yāyāt khaned vā salilāśayān
children.translated_text: should travel a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, or should dig reservoirs of water.
Or, living on cow dung and urine, he should wander only together with cows.
One who is emaciated should be built up with medicines and foods that do not increase fat or urine.
Pustules such as <s>śarāvikā</s> should be treated in the same way as swellings.

children.text: apakvā vraṇavat pakvās tāsāṃ prāgrūpam eva ca
children.translated_text: When unripe they should be treated like swellings, and when ripe like wounds; their prodromal signs are the same as those already stated.
For drinking, water from milky trees and goat's urine are recommended.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ ca śodhanaṃ prāyo durvirecyā hi mehinaḥ
children.translated_text: Strong purification is generally prescribed, for those suffering from prameha are difficult to purge.
For wound-healing, oil should be prepared with the <s>elādi</s> group.
For rubbing, however, an astringent preparation should be made with the <s>aragvadhādi</s> group.
Sprinkling should be done with the <s>asanādi</s> group, and drink and food with the <s>vatsakādi</s> group.
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, and <s>kaṇṭakārikā</s>,
<s>saptāhva</s>, the root of <s>kauṭaja</s>, <s>somavalka</s>, and <s>nṛpadruma</s>,
should be powdered and licked with honey; the powder called <s>navāyasa</s> is used in the same way.
One who has fallen into <s>madhumeha</s>, having been abandoned by physicians,
and is afflicted by prameha, should eat a <s>tulā</s> of <s>śilājatu</s> and become renewed.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of abscess and enlargement.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Every unripe abscess should be treated just like a swelling,

children.text: pratataṃ ca hared raktaṃ pakve tu vraṇavat kriyā ||
children.translated_text: and blood should be removed repeatedly; when it has ripened, the treatment is like that for a wound.
A <s>vāta</s>-type wound, washed with waters of the five roots,
should be smeared with the <s>bhadrādi</s> group, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and sesame, with salt predominating.
After purifying it with <s>traivṛta</s> joined with purgative substances,
one should heal it with <s>traivṛta</s> itself, prepared with the <s>vidārī</s> group.
For a <s>pitta</s>-type wound, after it has been washed with milky-tree water, one should smear it with <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and sesame,
and with ghee cooked with <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>.
One should bring it to healing with payasyā, the two niśās, excellent yaṣṭī, and milk,
or again a <s>kapha</s>-born one with the shoots, bark, and fruits of the nyagrodhādi group.
After washing it with the āragvadhādi group, one should smear it with parched grain meal, kumbha, niśā, sesame,
kulatthikā, dantī, trivṛt, śyāmā, agni, and tilvaka,
together with rock salt and cow's urine; one should prepare a healing oil.
In one arising from blood or from an external cause, the procedure should be as for a <s>pitta</s>-abscess.
For an unripe <s>vidradhi</s> arising internally,
one should drink in the forenoon a decoction of the varuṇādi group with a counter-addition of the ūṣakādi group.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ virecanadravyaiḥ siddhaṃ tābhyāṃ ca pāyayet
children.translated_text: One should also give him ghee cooked with purgative drugs and with those two groups,

children.text: nirūhaṃ snehavastiṃ ca tābhyām eva prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: and prepare both an evacuative enema and an unctuous enema with those very groups.
Madhuśigru, used in drink, food, and external application,
with added ingredients according to the <s>doṣa</s>, destroys an unripe <s>vidradhi</s>.
Trāyantī, triphalā, nimba, kaṭukā, and madhuka, in equal measure,
and four parts each of trivṛt and paṭola root separately,

children.text: masūrān nistuṣād aṣṭau tatkvāthaḥ saghṛto jayet
children.translated_text: with eight parts of husked lentils: their decoction, taken with ghee, conquers
<s>vidradhi</s>, <s>gulma</s>, <s>vīsarpa</s>, burning, confusion, intoxication, and fever,
as well as thirst, fainting, vomiting, heart disease, disorders of <s>pitta</s> and blood, skin disease, and jaundice.
A kuḍava of trāyamāṇā is to be boiled in eight times as much water.
From that liquid, from fresh juice of dhātrī, from milk, and from ghee, take a kuḍava each.
Add a paste, one karṣa each, of tiktā, trāyantī, and dhanvayāsaka,
with mustā, tāmalakī, vīrā, jīvantī, sandalwood, and utpala.

children.text: paced ekatra saṃyojya tad ghṛtaṃ pūrvavad guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cooking these together produces a ghee with the same virtues as before.
Drākṣā, madhūka, kharjūra, vidārī, together with śatāvarī,
parūṣaka fruits, and triphalā: in their decoction one should cook ghee,
combined with milk, sugarcane juice, dhātrī extract, and a paste of prāṇadā.
When cooled, with one quarter each of sugar and honey, it has the same virtues as before.
One should remove blood with a horn and the other instruments, or by a vein close to the affected place.
When a <s>vidradhi</s> in the abdomen is cooking and bulges outward,
having recognized it, one should apply a poultice when the pain has become fixed there and the mass has localized,
when the adjacent side becomes numb from pressure, and when burning and the other signs are slight.

children.text: pakvaḥ syād vidradhiṃ bhittvā vraṇavat tam upācaret
children.translated_text: When it is ripe, one should open the <s>vidradhi</s> and treat it like a wound.
This too is the sign of a ripened internal <s>vidradhi</s>:

children.text: pakvaḥ srotāṃsi sampūrya sa yātyūrdhvam adho 'thavā
children.translated_text: when ripe, it fills the channels and moves upward or downward.
If that <s>doṣa</s> begins to discharge by itself, the physician should let it alone while the patient eats wholesome food,

children.text: daśāhaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā rakṣan bhiṣag upadravāt
children.translated_text: for ten or twelve days, protecting him from complications.
If the moisture does not flow properly, one should give him varuṇādi with warm water to drink,

children.text: pāyayen madhuśigruṃ vā yavāgūṃ tena vā kṛtām
children.translated_text: or madhuśigru, or a thin gruel made with it.
Food with soups produced from barley, kola, and horse gram is also recommended.
After ten days, according to strength, one should purify him with trāyantī ghee or with tailvaka ghee.

children.text: śodhayed balataḥ śuddhaḥ sakṣaudraṃ tiktakaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: When purified, he should drink tiktaka ghee with honey.
In every respect one should treat this according to the <s>doṣa</s>, as one treats <s>gulma</s>.
And in all states and in all <s>vidradhi</s>s one should use guggulu,

children.text: kaṣāyair yaugikair yuñjyāt svaiḥ svais tadvacchilājatu
children.translated_text: combined with suitable decoctions, each appropriate to its case; likewise also śilājatu.

children.text: pākaṃ ca vārayed yatnāt siddhiḥ pakve hi daivikī ||
children.translated_text: One should carefully prevent suppuration, for once it is ripe, success depends on fate.
Moreover, because it quickly causes tearing and burning, it is called <s>vidradhi</s>.
And when diabetes is present, one should consider the treatment of <s>prameha</s>.

children.text: stanaje vraṇavat sarvaṃ na tvenam upanāhayet
children.translated_text: For one arising in the breast, everything is as in wound treatment, but one should not apply a poultice to it.
One should open it while protecting the milk-carrying ducts and the dark nipple area.
And in all its stages, beginning with the unripe state, one should milk out that breast.
In a mobile <s>vṛddhi</s>, after oleating the patient with fats, one should cleanse him with trivṛt,
using fats such as kauśāmra, tilvaka, castor oil, sukumāra, and miśraka.
Then one should administer an evacuative enema with decoctions, pastes, and fats that subdue <s>anila</s>.
After feeding him with meat soup, one should then give an unctuous enema with yaṣṭī oil.
Sweating and external applications should be <s>vāta</s>-subduing; when it is ripe, after opening it one should use wound treatment.
In <s>vṛddhi</s> arising from <s>pitta</s> and blood, whether unripe or ripe, as appropriate,

children.text: śophavraṇakriyāṃ kuryāt pratataṃ ca hared asṛk ||
children.translated_text: one should perform the procedures for swelling and wounds, and should continually remove blood.
In a phlegmatic one, he should drink a paste made from pītadāru with cow's urine.
Except for dissolving measures, the procedure for a <s>śleṣman</s>-granthi is beneficial for it.

children.text: pakve ca pāṭite tailam iṣyate vraṇaśodhanam
children.translated_text: When it has ripened and been opened, an oil for cleansing wounds is desired,
cooked with sumanas, aruṣkara, aṅkolla, and saptaparṇa,
and also with paṭola, nimba, rajanī, viḍaṅga, and kuṭaja.
For one born from fat, after it has been well fomented with the surasādi group ground in urine,
or with drugs for head-purgation, while avoiding the phalasevanī vessel,
one should split it with the vṛddhi knife; when the fat has been properly removed,
the wound should be rubbed with mākṣika, kāsīsa, and rock salt,
and it should be sutured. For its anointing, an application should be used to purify the fat,
made with manaḥśilā, elā, sumanas-granthi, and bhallātaka.

children.text: tailam ā vraṇasaṃdhānāt snehasvedau ca śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: Until the wound closes, one should use this oil, and should regularly employ unction and sweating.
A urine-born swelling, after being fomented with unctuous substances and wrapped with a cloth bandage,
should be punctured below the perineal raphe, and one should drain it as in abdominal fluid.
The wound, bound with a small bag, should be healed. In one caused by intestine,
if it has not reached the scrotal sac, the treatment is as for <s>vāta-vṛddhi</s>.
One should cook a tulā of punarnavā, and likewise ten palas each
of daśamūla, payasyā, aśvagandhā, castor, and śatāvarī,
together with two darbhas, śara, kāśa, sugarcane root, and poṭagala,
in a vāha of water; when one eighth remains, add thirty palas of jaggery.

children.text: prastham eraṇḍatailasya dvau ghṛtāt payasas tathā
children.translated_text: One should take one <s>prastha</s> of castor oil, and two each of ghee and milk likewise,
and should add two-<s>pala</s> portions each of <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, its root, and rock salt,
as well as licorice, raisins, <s>yavānī</s>, and dry ginger.
Cooked with these, it is the preparation called Sukumāra, a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) for delicate people.
It imposes no strict restraint regarding things otherwise to be avoided, such as wind, sun, travel, riding, and the like.
It is to be used by delicate persons, by the wealthy, and by those whose life is comfortable,
by men who are husbands of groups of women; it destroys misfortune and discord,
and, when used at all times, gives beauty, grace, and nourishment.
It is best in <s>vardhma</s> (inguinal or scrotal swelling), abscess, <s>gulma</s>, piles, and pains of the vagina, penis, and wind,
and also in swelling, abdominal disease, lameness or pain of the foot, splenic disease, and constipation.
If <s>vardhma</s> does not come to rest through oleation, purgation, and unctuous enemas,

children.text: vastikarma puraḥ kṛtvā vaṅkṣaṇasthaṃ tato dahet ||
children.translated_text: then, after first performing enema therapy, one should cauterize the lesion situated in the groin.
For the purpose of blocking the path of <s>marut</s> (wind), one should burn it with fire in a curve shaped like a half-moon.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhasyopari snāva pītaṃ tantusamaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: The yellow tendon-like band that is like a thread and lies above the big toe,

children.text: utkṣipya sūcyā tat tiryag dahecchittvā yato gadaḥ
children.translated_text: one should lift with a needle and burn crosswise after cutting it, on the side where the disease is.
Then the other side is treated likewise; others say that one should cauterize from the ring finger.

children.text: gulme 'nyair vātakaphaje plīhni cāyaṃ vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>gulma</s> produced by <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, and also in splenic disease, this same procedure is remembered by others.
It is done from the little finger and ring finger, and in <s>viśvācī</s> according to the side on which the disease lies.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>gulma</s>.
So indeed spoke the great seers, beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
A <s>vātika gulma</s>, with feces and wind obstructed, is intensely painful,
and arises from dry and cold causes; it should be treated with oils used for diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
For one who has been made unctuous by drinking, food, unctuous enema, and massage, one should apply sweating therapy,
especially in distention, pain, stiffness, and obstruction of feces.

children.text: srotasāṃ mārdavaṃ kṛtvā jitvā mārutam ulbaṇam
children.translated_text: After softening the channels and overcoming the excessive <s>māruta</s> (wind),

children.text: bhittvā vibandhaṃ snigdhasya svedo gulmam apohati ||
children.translated_text: sweating therapy, in one who has been oleated, breaks the obstruction and removes the <s>gulma</s>.
Drinking fat is beneficial in <s>gulma</s>, especially when it is above the navel;
when it is located in the colon, enema is beneficial, and when it rests in the abdomen, both are beneficial.
When the digestive fire is kindled in vātika <s>gulma</s>, and when wind and feces are obstructed,
one should give nourishing foods and drinks that are unctuous and hot.
Again and again, drinking of fat, decoction enemas, and unctuous enemas
should be employed in <s>gulma</s> born of <s>vāta</s>, while guarding against <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: vastikarma paraṃ vidyād gulmaghnaṃ taddhi mārutam
children.translated_text: One should know enema therapy to be the supreme destroyer of <s>gulma</s>,

children.text: svasthāne prathamaṃ jitvā sadyo gulmam apohati ||
children.translated_text: for, after first conquering <s>māruta</s> in its own place, it removes <s>gulma</s> at once.
Therefore <s>gulma</s>s made of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>
become pacified when decoction enemas and unctuous enemas are applied repeatedly.
With asafoetida, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, the three pungents, <s>viḍa</s> salt, pomegranate, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
with <s>puṣkara</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, coriander sour gruel, vetasa, alkali, and <s>citraka</s>,
with <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, cardamom, fermented liquor, and curd,
one should prepare ghee for patients with <s>vātagulma</s>; it removes colic and distention.
With <s>hapuṣā</s>, pepper, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>pañcakola</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,

children.text: sājājīsaindhavair dadhnā dugdhena ca rasena ca ||
children.translated_text: with <s>ajājī</s> and rock salt, and with curd, milk, and meat broth,

children.text: dāḍimān mūlakāt kolāt pacet sarpir nihanti tat
children.translated_text: one should cook ghee from pomegranate, radish, and jujube; that destroys
<s>vātagulma</s>, abdominal disease, distention, and pain in the flanks, heart, and abdomen,
as well as disorders of the vagina, piles, faults of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, cough, dyspnea, anorexia, and fever.

children.text: daśamūlaṃ balāṃ kālāṃ suṣavīṃ dvau punarnavau ||
children.translated_text: One should cook <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kālā</s>, <s>suṣavī</s>, and the two <s>punarnavā</s>s,
<s>pauṣkara</s>, castor, <s>rāsnā</s>, aśvagandhā, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>śaṭhī</s>,
and also two-<s>pala</s> measures of <s>gandhapalāśa</s>, in one <s>droṇa</s> of water.

children.text: yavaiḥ kolaiḥ kulatthaiśca māṣaiśca prāsthikaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: It is to be cooked together with barley, jujube, horse gram, and black gram, each in one-<s>prastha</s> quantity.
In this decoction, together with a vessel of curd, one should thoroughly cook one <s>prastha</s> of ghee.
It should be joined with the fresh juices produced from pomegranate, <s>āmrāta</s>, and citron,
and likewise with husk-water, coriander sour gruel, vinegar, and substances finely ground into paste:
<s>bhārgī</s>, <s>tumburu</s>, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>granthi</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>agni</s>, and coriander,
<s>yavānaka</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, sour vetasa, white cumin, and cumin,
<s>ajājī</s>, asafoetida, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>kāravī</s>, and <s>vṛṣakoṣaka</s>,
<s>nikumbha</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>ebha</s>, long pepper, <s>vella</s>, and pomegranate,
<s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, cucumber, <s>airvāru</s> seeds, <s>hiṃsrā</s>, and <s>aśmabhedaka</s>,
<s>miśi</s>, the two alkalis, <s>surasa</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>nīlinī</s>, and fruits.
That curd-based ghee, furnished with <s>trikaṭu</s> and the three salts, removes

children.text: rogān āśutarān pūrvān kaṣṭān api ca śīlitam ||
children.translated_text: the preceding diseases very quickly, even when they are difficult, if it is taken habitually.
It also removes epilepsy, disease, insanity, urinary obstruction, and disorders of <s>anila</s> (wind).
