With the three pungents, triphalā, coriander, <s>cavikā</s>, <s>vella</s>, and <s>citraka</s>
made into a paste, ghee cooked with milk destroys <s>vātagulma</s>.
One should take one <s>tulā</s> of garlic bulbs, and separately five-<s>pala</s> portions
of the great <s>pañcamūla</s>, and cook them in half a <s>bhāra</s> of water.
When a quarter remains, one should take half as much pomegranate juice, liquor,
coriander sour gruel, and curd, and also pastes in half-<s>pala</s> portions each:
the three pungents, triphalā, asafoetida, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>cavya</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s>.
Together with sour vetasa, rock salt, and deodar, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee from them.
That is supreme, conquering every disorder of <s>vātagulma</s>.

children.text: ṣaṭpalaṃ vā pibet sarpir yad uktaṃ rājayakṣmaṇi
children.translated_text: Or one may drink the six-<s>pala</s> ghee that was prescribed in the treatment of <s>rājayakṣman</s>.

children.text: prasannayā vā kṣīrārthaḥ surayā dāḍimena vā ||
children.translated_text: Or, in place of milk, clear liquor, liquor, or pomegranate juice may be used,

children.text: ghṛte mārutagulmaghnaḥ kāryo dadhnaḥ sareṇa vā
children.translated_text: or the essence of curd may be prepared in the ghee that destroys <s>mārutagulma</s>.

children.text: vātagulme kapho vṛddho hatvāgnim aruciṃ yadi ||
children.translated_text: If, in <s>vātagulma</s>, increased <s>kapha</s>, having impaired the digestive fire,

children.text: hṛllāsaṃ gauravaṃ tandrāṃ janayed ullikhet tu tam
children.translated_text: produces anorexia, nausea, heaviness, and drowsiness, then one should make the patient vomit it.
In cases of colic, distention, and obstruction, after recognizing the seat as containing fat or needing oleation,
decoctions, powders, and pills should be employed together with ghee-based medicines.
With <s>kola</s>, pomegranate, warm water, buttermilk, wine, sour <s>kāñjika</s>,

children.text: maṇḍena vā pibet prātaścūrṇānyannasya vā puraḥ
children.translated_text: or with thin rice gruel, he should drink the powders in the morning, or before food.
Powders of citron, repeatedly steeped in its juice,
should be made into especially effective pills for <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Hiṅgu</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, <s>paśugandhā</s>, pomegranate, <s>dīpyaka</s>, coriander, and <s>pāṭhā</s>,
with <s>puṣkaramūla</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>agni</s>, the pair of alkalis, the three salts, and the three pungents;
this powder, with cumin, <s>cavya</s>, <s>tintiḍīka</s>, and the sour <s>vetasa</s>, destroys
pains of the heart, sides, bladder, sacrum, vagina, and anus, arising from <s>vāyu</s>, <s>āma</s>, and <s>kapha</s>;

children.text: kṛcchrān gulmān vātaviṇmūtrasaṅgaṃ kaṇṭhe bandhaṃ hṛdgrahaṃ pāṇḍurogam
children.translated_text: difficult <s>gulmas</s>, retention of flatus, feces, and urine, constriction in the throat, seizure of the heart, and anemia;
aversion to food, spleen disease, hemorrhoids, hiccup, enlargement, distension, dyspnea, cough, and weakness of digestive fire.
Salt, <s>yavānī</s>, <s>dīpyaka</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and dry ginger are to be increased successively,
with <s>harītakī</s> equal to all of them together; this powder is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, fire itself.

children.text: trikaṭukam ajamodā saindhavaṃ jīrake dve samadharaṇaghṛtānām aṣṭamo hiṅgubhāgaḥ
children.translated_text: The three pungents, <s>ajamodā</s>, rock salt, the two cumin seeds, equal <s>dharaṇa</s> measures, and <s>hiṅgu</s> as the eighth part,

children.text: prathamakavaḍabhojyaḥ sarpiṣā samprayukto janayati jaṭharāgniṃ vātagulmaṃ nihanti ||
children.translated_text: taken with ghee as the first morsel of food, kindles the digestive fire and destroys <s>vātagulma</s>.

A powder of <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>ugrā</s>, <s>viḍa</s>, dry ginger, cumin, <s>vijayā</s>, and the drugs called <s>vāṭya</s>, with the roots of <s>kumbha</s> and <s>nikumbha</s>, increased successively in parts,

children.text: pītaḥ koṣṇajalena koṣṭhajarujo gulmodarādīn ayaṃ śārdūlaḥ prasabhaṃ pramathya harati vyādhīn mṛgaughān iva ||
children.translated_text: drunk with lukewarm water, is a tiger: it violently crushes and removes intestinal pains, <s>gulma</s>, <s>udara</s>, and other diseases, like herds of deer.
For those who drink powders of rock salt, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s> with slightly warm water,
the mass of diseases born from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> comes to destruction, as if pierced by arrows.
Leaves of <s>pūtīka</s>, <s>gajacirbhaṭa</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>vahni</s>, and the three pungents, arranged in layers with a covering of salt,
should be burned, powdered, and used with curd whey in <s>gulma</s>, <s>udara</s>, swelling, anemia, and anal disorders.

children.text: hiṅgutriguṇaṃ saindhavam asmāt triguṇaṃ ca tailam airaṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgu</s> in triple quantity, rock salt triple that, castor oil triple that,
and garlic juice triple that destroy <s>gulma</s>, <s>udara</s>, hernia, and pain.
Citron juice, <s>hiṅgu</s>, pomegranate, <s>viḍa</s> salt, and rock salt
should be drunk with the clear portion of liquor; it removes the pain of <s>vātagulma</s>.

children.text: śuṇṭhyāḥ karṣaṃ guḍasya dvau dhautāt kṛṣṇatilāt palam ||
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> of dry ginger, two of jaggery, and one <s>pala</s> of washed black sesame:
eating these powdered together, with warm milk as after-drink, one should overcome
vāta-related heart disease, <s>gulma</s>, piles, uterine pain, and retention of feces.
A patient with <s>vātagulma</s> should drink castor oil with clear liquor

children.text: śleṣmaṇyanubale vāyau pitte tu payasā saha ||
children.translated_text: when <s>vāyu</s> has <s>kapha</s> as a secondary force; but when <s>pitta</s> is involved, he should take it with milk.

children.text: vivṛddhaṃ yadi vā pittaṃ saṃtāpaṃ vātagulminaḥ
children.translated_text: If <s>pitta</s> has increased, or if there is burning in a patient with <s>vātagulma</s>,
he should be purged with oily agents that move the bowels downward.
If burning continues even after this, his blood should be let.
One should prepare four <s>palas</s> of clean, dried garlic
in milk and water eight times its quantity, and cook it until only the milk remains.
That milk quickly cures <s>vātagulma</s>, <s>udāvarta</s>, sciatica, intermittent fever,

children.text: hṛdrogaṃ vidradhiṃ śoṣaṃ sādhayatyāśu tat payaḥ
children.translated_text: heart disease, abscess, and wasting disease.
Oil, clear liquor, cow urine, <s>āranāla</s>, and <s>yavāgraja</s>,

children.text: gulmaṃ jaṭharam ānāhaṃ pītam ekatra sādhayet
children.translated_text: drunk together, cure <s>gulma</s>, abdominal enlargement, and distension.
A decoction of <s>citraka</s>, <s>granthika</s>, castor, and dry ginger is supremely beneficial
for pain, distension, and constipation, with <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>viḍa</s> salt, and rock salt.
The roots of <s>puṣkara</s> and castor, <s>yavadhanva</s>, and <s>yavāsaka</s>,
boiled in water and drunk, remove burning and pain in the abdomen.
The root of what is called <s>vāṭyā</s>, castor, and <s>darbha</s>, with <s>dāru</s> and <s>mahauṣadha</s>,
drunk after being decocted in water, conquers pain in the belly, back, and shoulders.
A patient with <s>vātagulma</s> should drink <s>śilājatu</s> with milk, or with a decoction of abundant <s>pañcamūla</s>;

children.text: vātagulmī pibed vāṭyam udāvarte tu bhojayet
children.translated_text: but in <s>udāvarta</s> he should be fed <s>vāṭya</s>.

children.text: snigdhaṃ paippalikair yūṣair mūlakānāṃ rasena vā ||
children.translated_text: If feces and wind are obstructed, he should eat unctuous food with long-pepper soups, or with radish juice,
or he should eat <s>yāvaka</s> with warm milk.
Or he should eat <s>kulmāṣas</s>, rich in fat and chiefly salty.
For one with retained waste matter, ghee should be given with <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, and <s>kampillaka</s>,
together with <s>viḍa</s> salt, alkali, and dry ginger.
One should cook <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>,

children.text: paced viḍaṅgaṃ vyāghrīṃ ca pālikāni jalāḍhake ||
children.translated_text: <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>vyāghrī</s>, one <s>pala</s> each, in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water.
When one-eighth of the decoction remains, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee in it,
combined with a <s>prastha</s> of curds and one <s>pala</s> of the latex of <s>sudhā</s>.
Then one should give one <s>pala</s> of the ghee mixed with the scum of rice gruel.
When it has been digested and the patient has been properly purged, he should be fed meals with meat broth.
This <s>Nīlinīghṛta</s> destroys <s>gulma</s>, skin disease, <s>udara</s>, facial discoloration, edema, anemia, and fever,
leucoderma, spleen enlargement, and madness.
Fowl, peacocks, partridges, <s>krauñca</s> birds, and quails,
<s>śāli</s> rice, wine, and ghee are the treatment for <s>vātagulma</s>.

children.text: mitam uṣṇaṃ dravaṃ snigdhaṃ bhojanaṃ vātagulminām
children.translated_text: For patients with <s>vātagulma</s>, food should be moderate, warm, liquid, and unctuous.

children.text: samaṇḍā vāruṇī pānaṃ taptaṃ vā dhānyakair jalam ||
children.translated_text: For drink, <s>vāruṇī</s> with its scum, or water heated with coriander, is suitable.
When a <s>paittika gulma</s> has arisen from unctuous and hot causes, purgation is beneficial.
The juice of grapes, <s>abhayā</s>, and jaggery, or <s>kampillaka</s> mixed with honey, should be used quickly.
Also the regimen taught in the <s>Kalpa</s> section and in the section on blood-pitta applies; but again, for <s>gulma</s> produced by dry and hot causes,

children.text: paraṃ saṃśamanaṃ sarpis tiktaṃ vāsāghṛtaṃ śṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the best pacifying remedy is ghee: bitter ghee, or ghee cooked with <s>vāsā</s>,
in a decoction of the group called <s>tṛṇapañcaka</s>, or with the <s>jīvanīya</s> group.

children.text: śṛtaṃ tenaiva vā kṣīraṃ nyagrodhādigaṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: or milk boiled with that very substance, or with the <s>nyagrodhādi</s> group.
Even there, in an urgent case, the physician should quickly employ <s>sraṃsana</s> (mild downward evacuation),
with ghee prepared with purgative drugs, or also with milk.
He should cook one <s>prastha</s> of ghee with the juices of <s>āmalaka</s> and sugarcane.

children.text: pathyāpādaṃ pibet sarpis tat siddhaṃ pittagulmanut ||
children.translated_text: He should drink that prepared ghee with a quarter part of <s>pathyā</s>; it removes <s>pittagulma</s>.

children.text: pibed vā tailvakaṃ sarpir yaccoktaṃ pittavidradhau
children.translated_text: Or he should drink <s>tailvaka</s> ghee, which was taught in the treatment of pitta-type abscess.

children.text: drākṣāṃ payasyāṃ madhukaṃ candanaṃ padmakaṃ madhu ||
children.translated_text: For the pacification of <s>pittagulma</s>, he should drink grapes, <s>payasyā</s>, licorice, sandalwood, <s>padmaka</s>, and honey
with rice-wash water.
Two <s>palas</s> of <s>trāyamāṇā</s> should be boiled in two <s>prasthas</s> of water.
When one eighth remains, it should be strained, made lukewarm, and drunk with an equal amount of milk.

children.text: pibed upari tasyoṣṇaṃ kṣīram eva yathābalam ||
children.translated_text: After it, he should drink only warm milk, according to his strength.
By that, when the doṣas have been expelled, the pitta-type <s>gulma</s> subsides.

children.text: dāhe 'bhyaṅgo ghṛtaiḥ śītaiḥ sājyair lepo himauṣadhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In burning, there should be anointing with cooling ghees, and a paste of cooling herbs mixed with ghee.
There should be contact with lotus leaves and with vessels containing water that is kept moving.
When there are preliminary signs of burning, pain, and weakness of the digestive fire,
he should remove blood repeatedly, especially in <s>pittagulma</s>.

children.text: chinnamūlā vidahyante na gulmā yānti ca kṣayam ||
children.translated_text: When their root has been cut, the <s>gulmas</s> do not become inflamed and go to wasting away.

children.text: raktaṃ hi vyamlatāṃ yāti tacca nāsti na cāsti ruk
children.translated_text: For the blood becomes excessively sour; when that is not present, pain too is not present.
When the doṣas have been removed, the patient is withered, nourished with broths of animals from dry land,
and has regained composure but still has residual pain, he should again be made accustomed to ghee.
If, because blood and pitta have increased excessively, or because treatment cannot be obtained,
the <s>gulma</s> is tending toward suppuration, every treatment is as for a pitta-type abscess.
<s>Śāli</s> rice, cow's and goat's milk, <s>paṭolī</s>, meat of dry-land animals, and ghee,

children.text: dhātrī parūṣakaṃ drākṣā kharjūraṃ dāḍimaṃ sitā
children.translated_text: <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>parūṣaka</s>, grapes, dates, pomegranate, and sugar
are to be eaten; for drinking, water boiled with <s>balā</s> and the <s>bṛhatyādi</s> group is suitable.
In a <s>śleṣma</s>-born case, he should first induce emesis; if the patient is not fit for emesis, he should make him fast.
Then he should kindle the digestive fire with combinations that are bitter, hot, and pungent,
and with the <s>hiṅgvādi</s> group, together with double alkali, asafoetida, and sour <s>vetasa</s>.

children.text: nigūḍhaṃ yadi vonnaddhaṃ stimitaṃ kaṭhinaṃ sthiram ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>gulma</s> is hidden or raised up, inactive, hard, fixed,
and accompanied by abdominal distension and the like, he should sweat it and then reduce it.
Ghee with alkali and pungent drugs should be drunk by those suffering from <s>kaphagulma</s>,
with <s>vyosa</s>, alkali, salt, asafoetida, <s>viḍa</s>, and pomegranate.
Ghee boiled with the ten roots quickly conquers <s>kaphagulma</s>.
Two <s>palas</s> of <s>bhallātaka</s> and <s>pañcamūla</s> measuring one <s>pala</s>

children.text: alpaṃ toyāḍhake sādhyaṃ pādaśeṣeṇa tena ca ||
children.translated_text: should be boiled in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water until a quarter remains; with that,
he should cook an equal amount of ghee and an equal amount of milk, using pastes in one-<s>akṣa</s> measures
of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, asafoetida, rock salt, barley-awn alkali, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>viḍa</s>,
together with <s>dvīpī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, licorice, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and dry ginger.
This <s>bhallātaka</s> ghee is supreme for removing <s>kaphagulma</s>.
It conquers diseases of the spleen, pallor, dyspnea, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, and cough.

children.text: tato 'sya gulme dehe ca samaste svedam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: After that, in his <s>gulma</s> and over the whole body, he should perform fomentation.
In every case of <s>gulma</s>, when the patient has first been prepared with oleation and sweating,

children.text: yā kriyā kriyate yāti sā siddhiṃ na virūkṣite ||
children.translated_text: whatever treatment is performed succeeds; it does not succeed in one who has been dried out.
When the body has been oiled and sweated and the <s>gulma</s> has become loose,
he should apply the cupping vessel as prescribed, and when it has taken hold he should remove it.

children.text: vastrāntaraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā bhindyād gulmaṃ pramāṇavit
children.translated_text: Then, placing a layer of cloth between, one who knows the proper measure should break up the <s>gulma</s>.
He should press it with <s>vimārga</s>, <s>ajapada</s>, or a mirror, according to what is available.

children.text: pramṛjyād gulmam evaikaṃ na tvantrahṛdayaṃ spṛśet
children.translated_text: He should rub only the <s>gulma</s> itself, but should not touch the intestines or the heart.
After smearing it with sesame, castor, flax, and mustard seeds,
he should then foment the <s>śleṣmagulma</s> with pleasantly warm iron vessels.

children.text: evaṃ ca visṛtaṃ sthānāt kaphagulmaṃ virecanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the <s>kaphagulma</s> has thus moved from its place, he should cleanse it with purgatives
and with unctuous enemas made with the ten roots.
He should cook one-<s>pala</s> portions of long pepper, <s>āmalaka</s>, grapes, and the <s>śyāmādi</s> group
with a <s>prastha</s> each of castor oil and ghee, in six times as much milk.

children.text: siddho 'yaṃ miśrakaḥ sneho gulmināṃ sraṃsanaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: This prepared mixed fat is beneficial as a downward evacuant for those with <s>gulma</s>.
It is like nectar in enlargement, abscess, pain, and diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
Or he should drink <s>nīlinī</s> ghee in a dose of two <s>palas</s>,
and likewise the one called <s>sukumāra</s>, or other ghees for abdominal disorders.
In a <s>droṇa</s> of water he should cook twenty-five <s>palas</s> of <s>dantī</s>,

children.text: citrakasya tathā pathyās tāvatīs tadrase srute
children.translated_text: and the same amount of <s>citraka</s> and <s>pathyā</s>; when that decoction has been strained,

children.text: dviprasthe sādhayet pūte kṣiped dantīsamaṃ guḍam ||
children.translated_text: he should boil it down to two <s>prasthas</s>, strain it, and add jaggery equal to the <s>dantī</s>.
He should add four <s>palas</s> of oil and powdered <s>trivṛt</s>.

children.text: kaṇākarṣau tathā śuṇṭhyāḥ siddhe lehe tu śītale ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, he should add a <s>karṣa</s> each of <s>kaṇā</s> and dry ginger; when the electuary is cooked and cooled,
he should add honey equal to the oil, and a quarter part of the four aromatics.
Eating one <s>harītakī</s> with one <s>pala</s> of this electuary,
a properly oiled person is comfortably purged of a <s>prastha</s> of doṣa and becomes free from illness.
<s>Dantīharītakī</s> preparations destroy <s>gulma</s>, heart disease, piles, swelling, abdominal distension, poison-abdomen,
skin disease, nausea, anorexia, spleen disease, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and irregular fever.
They also destroy pallor together with jaundice.
Powder of <s>trivṛt</s>, well impregnated with the liquid latex of <s>sudhā</s>,
when licked in a <s>karṣa</s> dose with honey and ghee, produces good purgation.
He should drink one of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, alkali, and <s>guggulu</s>

children.text: gomūtreṇa pibed ekaṃ tena guggulum eva vā ||
children.translated_text: with cow's urine, or with that he may drink <s>guggulu</s> alone.
He should apply evacuative enemas taught in <s>Kalpasiddhi</s>, which destroy <s>gulma</s>.
A large, well-rooted, hard, inactive, heavy mass
He should overcome a <s>gulma</s> hidden in flesh by means of <s>kṣāra</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and cauterization,
after allowing rest on alternate days, at intervals of two days, or else for three days.
Intent on increasing or reducing according to the strength of the body and of the <s>doṣas</s>,
he should employ <s>kṣāras</s> in conditions joined with piles, urinary stone, and <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, when kapha is predominant.
<s>Devadāru</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and <s>pañcakola</s>,
the two called <s>svarjikā</s> and <s>yāvaśūka</s>, together with <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>upakuñcikā</s>,
<s>kuṣṭha</s> and <s>sarpasugandhā</s>, each in two-<s>akṣa</s> portions, and the five salts
in one-<s>pala</s> portions, powdered and drenched with oil, fat, curds, and ghee,

children.text: ghaṭasyāntaḥ pacet pakvam agnivarṇe ghaṭe ca tam
children.translated_text: should be cooked inside a pot; when it is cooked and the pot has become fire-colored,
he should take that <s>kṣāra</s> and drink it with milk, ghee, buttermilk, wine, and the like.
<s>Gulma</s>, <s>udāvarta</s>, <s>vardhman</s>, piles, abdominal enlargement, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, and worms,
epilepsy, artificial poison, insanity, diseases of the womb and semen, and urinary stones:
this alkali-antidote pacifies them, and also poison from mice and snakes.
In those who eat sweet and unctuous foods, meat broth, milk, and ghee, it cuts through <s>śleṣman</s>;
breaking it up from its seat, <s>kṣāra</s>, because of its alkalinity, drains it downward.
When digestive fire is weak and there is anorexia, for those eating suitable food together with fat and wine,
he should prescribe the stated <s>āsavas</s> and <s>ariṣṭas</s> for clearing the channels.

children.text: śālayaḥ ṣaṣṭikā jīrṇāḥ kulatthā jāṅgalaṃ palam ||
children.translated_text: Old <s>śāli</s> and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, horse gram, and meat of animals from dry land,
sprouts of <s>ciribilva</s>, <s>agnimantha</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, and <s>varuṇa</s>,
<s>śigru</s>, young <s>bilva</s>, and both tender and dry radish,
citron, asafoetida, sour <s>vetasa</s>, alkali, pomegranate,

children.text: vyoṣaṃ takraṃ ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ bhaktaṃ pānaṃ tu vāruṇī ||
children.translated_text: <s>vyoṣa</s>, buttermilk, ghee, oil, food, and, as drink, <s>vāruṇī</s> wine,
grain-sour gruel, whey, and buttermilk powdered with <s>yavānī</s> and <s>viḍa</s>,

children.text: pañcamūlaśṛtaṃ vāri jīrṇaṃ mārdvīkam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: water boiled with the five roots, or old grape wine,
and beer prepared with long pepper, long-pepper root, <s>citraka</s>, cumin, and rock salt,
quickly conquers <s>gulma</s>, as does <s>jagala</s> mixed with it.
If a <s>śleṣmika gulma</s> does not subside through emetics, fasts, sweats, drinking ghee, purgatives,
enemas, alkalis, <s>āsavas</s>, <s>ariṣṭas</s>, pills, and wholesome foods,

children.text: ślaiṣmiko baddhamūlatvād yadi gulmo na śāmyati
children.translated_text: because its root is firmly bound,

children.text: tasya dāhaṃ hṛte rakte kuryād ante śarādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, after drawing blood, he should at the end perform cautery on it with reeds and the like.
Then the physician, placing a cloth between himself and the <s>gulma</s> all around,
should avoid the navel, bladder, intestines, heart, and line of hair,
and touch it, not too firmly, with a burning reed,
or with iron, with wood kindled from the fire-stick, or with wood of <s>tinduka</s>.

children.text: tato 'gnivege śamite śītair vraṇa iva kriyā
children.translated_text: After the force of the fire has subsided, cooling treatment should be applied as in a wound.
But when <s>āma</s> is involved, he should kindle the digestive fire with thin gruels and the like after fasting,

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ kuryāt kramaṃ miśraṃ miśradoṣe ca kālavit
children.translated_text: and, when there is a mixed <s>doṣa</s> condition, one who knows the proper time should apply each respective regimen in combination.
For a woman whose time of delivery has passed, when a <s>gulma</s> arises from blood,
he should give an unctuous purgative after her body has been oiled and sweated.
In a sesame decoction, a drink furnished with ghee, jaggery, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and powder of <s>bhārgī</s>

children.text: pānaṃ raktabhave gulme naṣṭe puṣpe ca yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: is used in blood-born <s>gulma</s> and when a woman's menstrual flow has ceased.
A powder made from <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, bark of <s>karañja</s>, <s>granthikā</s>, and <s>amaradāru</s>,
drunk with a decoction of sesame, removes the pain of <s>gulma</s>.
Two vessels of <s>palāśa</s> alkali and two vessels each of oil and ghee
should be cooked, and a dose that produces loosening of the <s>gulma</s> should be administered.
If it does not break open in this way, he should administer vaginal purgation.

children.text: kṣāreṇa yuktaṃ palalaṃ sudhākṣīreṇa vā tataḥ
children.translated_text: He should insert minced meat mixed with alkali, or with the latex of <s>sudhā</s>,

children.text: tābhyāṃ vā bhāvitān dadyād yonau kaṭukamatsyakān ||
children.translated_text: or pungent fish well impregnated with those two into the vagina.
Or he should give <s>naktaka</s> well impregnated with the bile of boar and fish,

children.text: kiṇvaṃ vā saguḍakṣāraṃ dadyād yonau viśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: or yeast with jaggery and alkali, in the vagina for purification.
He should have her lick an alkali that removes <s>raktapitta</s>, together with honey and ghee,
and he should prescribe garlic, strong liquor, and fish for her.
An enema with milk, cow urine, alkali, and the ten roots
is beneficial, breaking up <s>gulma</s> when the blood is not flowing.
When the flow has begun, after her body has been anointed with the two fats, it should be disregarded.

children.text: rasaudanas tathāhāraḥ pānaṃ ca taruṇī surā ||
children.translated_text: Her food should be rice with meat broth, and her drink fresh beer.
But when the blood flows excessively, treatments that remove <s>raktapitta</s> should be performed.
For a woman afflicted by pain from <s>vāta</s>, all measures removing <s>vāta</s> should again be used,
and in abdominal distension and the like, those that remove <s>udāvarta</s> and <s>balāsa</s>, each as appropriate.
Now then we shall explain the treatment of abdominal disease.
Thus, indeed, said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Abdominal disease arises from excessive accumulation of the <s>doṣas</s>
and from obstruction of the channels; therefore one should purge this patient regularly.

children.text: pāyayet tailam airaṇḍaṃ samūtraṃ sapayo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: He should make him drink castor oil with urine, or also with milk,

children.text: māsaṃ dvau vāthavā gavyaṃ mūtraṃ māhiṣam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or for one or two months he should drink cow urine, or buffalo urine.
Or he should live on cow's milk, or follow a regimen of camel's milk,
especially when beset by burning, abdominal distension, excessive thirst, and fainting.
For dry patients with much <s>vāta</s>, who desire cleansing of the <s>doṣas</s>,
he should prescribe oleating ghees that destroy abdominal enlargement.
The <s>Ṣaṭpala</s> preparation is cooked with the water of the ten roots and two <s>āḍhakas</s> of whey;
with three <s>palas</s> of dry ginger, a <s>prastha</s>, and likewise an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee and oil,
having cooked this with whey, he should drink it; it removes all abdominal diseases,
and it is supremely beneficial also in <s>gulma</s> produced by kapha and <s>māruta</s>.

children.text: caturguṇe jale mūtre dviguṇe citrakāt pale
children.translated_text: In four times as much water and twice as much urine, with one <s>pala</s> of <s>citraka</s> as paste,

children.text: kalke siddhaṃ ghṛtaprasthaṃ sakṣāraṃ jaṭharī pibet ||
children.translated_text: a <s>prastha</s> of ghee cooked with alkali should be drunk by a patient with abdominal enlargement.
Or he should be made to drink ghee cooked with the water of barley, jujube, horse gram,

children.text: surāsauvīrakābhyāṃ ca siddhaṃ vā pāyayed ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and the five roots, and with beer and <s>sauvīraka</s>.

children.text: ebhiḥ snigdhāya saṃjāte bale śānte ca mārute
children.translated_text: When by these measures the patient has been made unctuous, strength has arisen, and <s>māruta</s> has become quiet,
and when the seat of the <s>doṣas</s> has loosened, one should give the purgation prescribed in the <s>Kalpa</s> section.

children.text: paṭolamūlaṃ triphalāṃ niśāṃ vellaṃ ca kārṣikam
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> each of root of <s>paṭola</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>niśā</s>, and <s>vella</s>,
with portions of <s>kampilla</s>, <s>nīlinī</s>, and <s>kumbha</s> in two-, three-, and fourfold quantities respectively,

children.text: pibet saṃcūrṇya mūtreṇa peyāpūrvaṃ tato rasaiḥ
children.translated_text: should be powdered and drunk with urine, preceded by thin gruel; then, after purgation, with meat soups
from animals of dry land one should eat, and for six days afterward drink milk.

children.text: śṛtaṃ pibed vyoṣayutaṃ pītam evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should repeatedly drink it boiled and mixed with <s>vyoṣa</s> after it has been taken in this way.
This powder destroys all abdominal diseases, even those in which water has already accumulated.

children.text: gavākṣīṃ śaṅkhinīṃ dantīṃ tilvakasya tvacaṃ vacām
children.translated_text: He should drink <s>gavākṣī</s>, <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, bark of <s>tilvaka</s>, and <s>vacā</s>
with the waters of <s>karkandhu</s>, grapes, and <s>kola</s>, or with urine or <s>sīdhu</s> liquor.
<s>Yavānī</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>dhānya</s>, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>upakuñcikā</s>,
<s>kāravī</s>, root of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
<s>citraka</s>, <s>ajājikā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, and the three fruits,

children.text: dvau kṣārau pauṣkaraṃ mūlaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ lavaṇapañcakam ||
children.translated_text: the two alkalis, root of <s>pauṣkara</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and the five salts,

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ ca samāṃśāni dantyā bhāgatrayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: together with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, in equal parts, and also three parts of <s>dantī</s>,
twice as much <s>trivṛt</s> and <s>viśālā</s>, and four times as much <s>sātalā</s>:
this powder, called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, removes whole groups of diseases.
Diseases do not increase after obtaining it, just as demons do not thrive before <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
It should be drunk with buttermilk by those with abdominal disease, and with jujube water by those with <s>gulma</s>;
with <s>surā</s> in distensive <s>vāta</s>, and with clear liquor in diseases of <s>vāta</s>;
with the watery part of curds in obstruction of feces, and with pomegranate water by patients with piles;
with sour <s>vṛkṣāmla</s> in cutting pain, and with warm water in indigestion.
In fistula, pallor, cough, dyspnea, constriction of the throat,
heart disease, disorder of <s>grahaṇī</s>, skin disease, weak digestive fire, and fever,
in fang-poison, root-poison, poison-abdomen, and artificial disorder,
this purgative should be drunk by one whose bowel has been made unctuous, according to what is suitable.
One should powder <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>kāñcanakṣīrī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, fruit of <s>nīlinī</s>,

children.text: trāyantīṃ rohiṇīṃ tiktāṃ sātalāṃ trivṛtāṃ vacām ||
children.translated_text: <s>trāyantī</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>sātalā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
with rock salt, black salt, and <s>pippalī</s>.
It should be drunk with pomegranate water, <s>triphalā</s> water, meat broth, urine, or pleasant warm water.
This is to be drunk in all <s>gulma</s> disorders, in spleen disease, and in all abdominal diseases,
in white leprosy, skin diseases, indigestion, wasting, and irregular digestive fire,
in swelling, piles, pallor, jaundice, and <s>halīmaka</s>;
by purgation it quickly brings <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> into order.
One should drink, as a powder, <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>nicula</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, the two alkalis, the five salts,
and <s>citraka</s>, together with ghee; it removes abdominal disease and <s>gulma</s>.
As before, after cleansing, the emaciated patient should drink milk at intervals,

children.text: kārabhaṃ gavyam ājaṃ vā dadyād ātyayike gade ||
children.translated_text: whether camel's, cow's, or goat's milk; in an urgent illness it should be given.
For the purpose of purgation, especially for weak patients, one should use fats alone.
An <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee mixed with a <s>prastha</s> of fine powder of <s>harītakī</s>
should be melted over the fire and churned with a churner in a barley vessel.

children.text: nidhāpayet tato māsād uddhṛtaṃ gālitaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Then it should be stored away; after a month it is taken out, strained, and cooked
with a decoction of <s>harītakī</s> and with sour curds added.
By drinking, this destroys abdominal disease, <s>gara</s> poison, <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, abdominal distension, <s>gulma</s>, and abscess,

children.text: hantyetat kuṣṭham unmādam apasmāraṃ ca pānataḥ
children.translated_text: and also skin disease, insanity, and epilepsy.
The ghee that arises from cow's milk mixed with the latex of <s>snuk</s>, boiled, cooled, and churned with a churner,
when cooked with the latex of <s>snuk</s>, has the same properties.
Curds made from a <s>droṇa</s> of milk together with half a <s>prastha</s> of latex of <s>sudhā</s>

children.text: jātaṃ mathitvā tatsarpis trivṛtsiddhaṃ ca tadguṇam
children.translated_text: should be churned; the ghee obtained from it, cooked with <s>trivṛt</s>, has the same properties.
Likewise, one should drink a <s>prastha</s> of prepared ghee cooked in eight times as much milk,
with a paste of one <s>pala</s> of <s>snuk</s> latex and six <s>palas</s> of <s>trivṛt</s>.

children.text: eṣāṃ cānu pibet peyāṃ rasaṃ svādu payo 'thavā ||
children.translated_text: After these, he should drink thin gruel, meat soup, sweet milk, or something similar.
When the ghee has been digested and he has been purged, he should drink warm water prepared with dry ginger,

children.text: pibed ambu tataḥ peyāṃ tato yūṣaṃ kulatthajam ||
children.translated_text: then thin gruel, and after that soup made from horse gram.

children.text: pibed rūkṣas tryahaṃ tvevaṃ bhūyo vā pratibhojitaḥ
children.translated_text: Being kept dry for three days in this way, and then fed again,
he should drink ghee again and again in this very sequence.
A skilled physician should prepare these medicated ghees
for the pacification of <s>gulma</s>, <s>gara</s> disorders, and abdominal diseases.
Or he may drink ghee prepared with paste of <s>pīlu</s>, which breaks abdominal distension,

children.text: tailvakaṃ nīlinīsarpiḥ snehaṃ vā miśrakaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: or <s>tailvaka</s>, <s>nīlinī</s> ghee, or a mixed unctuous preparation.
When the <s>doṣas</s> have been removed, the patient with abdominal disease should gradually eat light boiled <s>śāli</s> rice
as a regular diet, for the cessation of the drying up caused by the <s>doṣas</s>.
Or he may take a thousand <s>harītakīs</s> with cow's urine, followed by milk,
or a thousand <s>pippalīs</s> well impregnated with the latex of <s>snuk</s>.
Or he may use the increasing dose of <s>pippalī</s>, live on milk, or take <s>śilājatu</s>,

children.text: tadvad vā gugguluṃ kṣīraṃ tulyārdrakarasaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: or similarly <s>guggulu</s>, and milk in equal quantity with fresh ginger juice.
Or he should drink a paste of <s>citraka</s> and <s>amaradāru</s> with milk,
properly for a month, and likewise <s>hastipippalī</s> and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>.

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ citrako dantī cavyaṃ vyoṣaṃ ca taiḥ payaḥ
children.translated_text: Having drunk milk with pastes, each the size of a <s>kola</s>, of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>dantī</s>,

children.text: kalkaiḥ kolasamaiḥ pītvā pravṛddham udaraṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>cavya</s>, and <s>vyoṣa</s>, he should conquer even an advanced abdominal enlargement.
Or for a month he should eat food accompanied by <s>snuhī</s> latex and ghee,
or a gruel-cake made from <s>pathyā</s> and <s>kaṇā</s> steeped in the latex of <s>snuk</s>.
If <s>samīraṇa</s> causes pain in the side, obstruction, and constriction of the heart,

children.text: yadi kuryāt tatas tailaṃ bilvakṣārānvitam pibet ||
children.translated_text: then he should drink oil combined with alkali of <s>bilva</s>,
or oil cooked with alkalis made separately from <s>ṭuṇṭuka</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and sesame stalks,
and from banana, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>tarkārī</s>.

children.text: kaphe vātena pitte vā tābhyāṃ vāpyāvṛte 'nile
children.translated_text: When <s>anila</s> is obstructed by <s>kapha</s>, by <s>pitta</s>, or by both of them,
For a strong patient, castor oil combined with the appropriate medicines is beneficial.
With <s>devadāru</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>hastipippalī</s>, and <s>śigru</s>,
together with <s>aśvakarṇa</s> and cow's urine, he should smear the abdomen externally.
With decoctions of <s>vṛścikālī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, dry ginger, <s>pañcamūla</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>varṣābhū</s>, grain, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and with urines, he should sprinkle it.
When the abdomen has been purged, has become languid, and has been sweated with <s>śālvaṇa</s> and the like,

children.text: vāsasā veṣṭayed evaṃ vāyur nādhmāpayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should wrap it with cloth; in this way <s>vāyu</s> will not distend it again.

children.text: suviriktasya yasya syād ādhmānaṃ punareva tam
children.translated_text: If distension should arise again in one who has been well purged,
he should treat him with unctuous decoction enemas containing sour and salty substances.
Or, when obstructed <s>vāyu</s> distends a man,
sharp enemas with alkali and cow's urine are recommended for him.

children.text: iti sāmānyataḥ proktāḥ siddhā jaṭhariṇāṃ kriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the proven treatments for those with abdominal disease have been stated in general.
Now, in <s>vātodara</s>, he should give a strong patient ghee cooked with the <s>vidāryādi</s> group to drink.
Then, when he has been oleated and his limbs sweated, he should purge him,
repeatedly, with this <s>tailvaka</s> ghee or with mixed ghee.
When the graduated diet has been completed, he should administer milk for strength,

children.text: prāg utkleśān nivartyaṃ ca bale labdhe kramāt payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and before it produces nausea it should be withdrawn; when strength has been regained, milk should be given gradually,
or soups and meat broths, mildly sour and salty, so that the digestive fire is increased.
If it is accompanied by <s>udāvarta</s>, he should again oleate and sweat the patient and then administer a non-unctuous enema,
with a <s>daśamūla</s> enema furnished with a sharp downward-acting ingredient,
or with oil of sesame and <s>urubūka</s>, cooked with sour substances that subdue <s>vāta</s>.
When there is throbbing, convulsion, and pain in the joints, bones, flanks, back, and sacral region,
and when the patient is dry, with stool and wind obstructed but digestive fire strong, he should administer an unctuous enema.
For one not fit for purgation, palliative measures such as enemas, milk, and ghee are used.
In a <s>pitta</s> condition, he should oleate a strong patient with ghee cooked with sweet drugs,
and purge him with ghee cooked with <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>tribhaṇḍī</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>.
After that, a decoction enema rich in sugar, honey, and ghee is beneficial for him,
made with a decoction of the <s>nyagrodhādi</s> group; and an unctuous enema cooked with that is also beneficial.
But a weak patient should first be treated with unctuous enemas and then purified with milk enemas.

children.text: jāte cāgnibale snigdhaṃ bhūyo bhūyo virecayet
children.translated_text: When digestive strength has arisen, after oleation he should be purged again and again
with milk containing paste of <s>trivṛt</s>, or with milk cooked with <s>urubūka</s>,
or with <s>āragvadha</s> cooked together with <s>sātalā</s> and <s>trāyamāṇā</s>.
If <s>kapha</s> is present, this should be with cow's urine; if <s>vāta</s> is present, with bitter ghee.
He should take food with milk prepared with any one of these, or with milk cooked with the <s>vidāryādi</s> group,
and his abdomen should be poulticed with milk-rice.

children.text: punaḥ kṣīraṃ punar vastiṃ punareva virecanam
children.translated_text: Again milk, again an enema, and again purgation:

children.text: krameṇa dhruvam ātiṣṭhan yattaḥ pittodaraṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: steadily following this sequence with care, he should surely conquer <s>pittodara</s>.
In a <s>kapha</s> condition, after oleating him with ghee cooked with the <s>vatsakādi</s> group,
he should sweat the strong patient and purge him with ghee prepared with the latex of <s>snuk</s>.
He should restore him with foods containing pungent and alkaline substances that remove <s>kapha</s>.
After that, a decoction enema rich in urine, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and oil is beneficial for him,
made with a decoction of the <s>muṣkakādi</s> group; and an unctuous enema cooked with that is also beneficial.
His food should be taken with milk prepared with <s>vyoṣa</s>, or with soup of horse gram.
When there is heaviness, anorexia, nausea, weak digestive fire, or addiction to liquor,
he should give <s>ariṣṭas</s> and alkalis in a <s>kapha</s> abdomen that is congealed and firm.
Asafoetida, <s>upakulyā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, the two <s>niśās</s>,
<s>bhallātaka</s>, fruit of <s>śigru</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>tiktaka</s>, <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: śuṇṭhīṃ mādrīṃ ghanaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ saralaṃ paṭupañcakam
children.translated_text: dry ginger, <s>mādrī</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>sarala</s>, and the five salts
should be crushed and burned, like the four fats mixed with curds,
without letting smoke escape; then he should drink an amount of this alkali equal to a cat's paw,
with liquor, the watery part of curds, warm water, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, <s>surā</s>, or <s>āsava</s>.

children.text: udaraṃ gulmam aṣṭhīlāṃ tūṇyau śophaṃ viṣūcikām
children.translated_text: It destroys abdominal disease, <s>gulma</s>, <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, the two kinds of <s>tūṇī</s>, swelling, <s>viṣūcikā</s>,
spleen disease, heart disease, diseases arising in the anus, and <s>udāvarta</s>.
By drinking <s>ariṣṭa</s>, cow's urine, medicinal powders, and <s>ayaskṛti</s>,
and by drinking oil with alkali, he should conquer <s>kaphodara</s> in a weak patient.
The abdomen should be poulticed with mustard, ferments, and seeds of radish,
made into a paste; frequent sweating should also be applied here.
In <s>saṃnipātodara</s>, if the patient's strength and digestive fire are not greatly exhausted,
he should undertake this treatment after giving a guarded prognosis, in accordance with the predominance of the <s>doṣas</s>.
Oil produced from <s>dantī</s>, <s>dravantī</s>, and fruits is also recommended for drinking,
especially when treatment has ceased to work in an abdominal disease involving all three <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: dadyād āpṛcchya tajjñātīn pātuṃ madyena kalkitam
children.translated_text: After informing his relatives, he should give him to drink, mixed with liquor,
the root obtained from <s>kākādanī</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, and <s>karavīraka</s>.
Or he should give a plant poison, mixed with drink and food,

children.text: yasmin vā kupitaḥ sarpo vimuñcati phale viṣam ||
children.translated_text: or the fruit in which an enraged snake has released its venom.
By that, the mass of <s>doṣas</s> in him, fixed, hidden, and moving by a wrong path,
is split by the swiftly agitating poison and moves outward.
In this way he either becomes free from poison, or passes on to another body.

children.text: hṛtadoṣaṃ tu śītāmbusnātaṃ taṃ pāyayet payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when the <s>doṣas</s> have been removed, he should bathe him with cold water and make him drink milk,

children.text: peyāṃ vā trivṛtaḥ śākaṃ māṇḍūkyā vāstukasya vā
children.translated_text: or thin gruel, or vegetables of <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>māṇḍūkī</s>, or <s>vāstuka</s>.
He may eat <s>kālaśāka</s> or what is called barley-greens, prepared in its own juice.
Without sourness, salt, or fat, whether cooked or uncooked, and eating no grain,

children.text: māsam ekaṃ tataścaiva tṛṣitaḥ svarasaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: for one month he should do this; then, when thirsty, he should drink its fresh juice.

children.text: evaṃ vinirhṛte śākair doṣe māsāt paraṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: When the <s>doṣa</s> has thus been drawn out by vegetables, after a month
the physician should administer camel's milk to the weak patient.
In <s>plīhodara</s>, according to the <s>doṣa</s>, after the patient has been oleated and sweated,
and after he has eaten with curds, one should open a vein in the left arm.

children.text: labdhe bale ca bhūyo 'pi snehapītaṃ viśodhitam
children.translated_text: When strength has been regained, again, after the patient has drunk unctuous substances and has been purified,
he should likewise make him drink alkali produced from sea-shell with milk.
He may use an acidic extract from <s>naktamāla</s>, enriched with powder of <s>viḍa</s> and <s>kaṇā</s>,
or a decoction of <s>śobhāñjana</s>, combined with rock salt and <s>agnikaṇā</s>.
He should use <s>hiṅgvādi</s> powder and alkali-ghee according to the patient's strength.
A powder should be made of equal parts <s>pippalī</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, and <s>dantī</s>, with twice as much <s>abhayā</s>,
joined with a half part of <s>viḍa</s>; this powder should be drunk with hot water.

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ citrakaṃ saktūn saghṛtān saindhavaṃ vacām ||
children.translated_text: He should take <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>citraka</s>, roasted grain flour with ghee, rock salt, and <s>vacā</s>,
burn them in an earthen pan, and drink them with milk; this removes <s>gulma</s> and spleen disease.
If the spleen is bandaged with jujube leaves mixed with oil and thoroughly crushed,

children.text: musalena pīḍito 'nu ca yāti plīhā payobhujo nāśam
children.translated_text: and then pressed with a pestle, it comes to destruction in one who lives on milk.
Prepared stems of <s>rohītaka</s>, cut into pieces and placed in water together with <s>abhayā</s>,
should be steeped in urine; after standing for seven nights, that liquid should be drunk.
It removes jaundice, spleen disease, <s>gulma</s>, piles, worms, urinary disease, and abdominal disease.
Taking twenty-five <s>palas</s> of <s>rohītaka</s> bark,
one should prepare a decoction together with two <s>prasthas</s> of jujubes.

children.text: pālikaiḥ pañcakolais tu taiḥ samastaiśca tulyayā
children.translated_text: With one-<s>pala</s> portions of the five pungent drugs, and with all of them together,
and with an equal amount of ground <s>rohītaka</s> bark, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee.
When administered, this quickly pacifies enlargement of the spleen.
Oil cooked with alkali from plantain stalks, sesame stalks, and <s>kṣuraka</s>

children.text: tailaṃ pakvaṃ jayet pānāt plīhānaṃ kaphavātajam
children.translated_text: conquers, when drunk, spleen disease born of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
If it is not pacified, he should apply cauterization by fire according to the method for <s>gulma</s>.
When the spleen has not reached a slimy, watery state and <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> are predominant,
but in a pitta-born case, life-promoting ghees and milk enemas are prescribed.
Bloodletting, purification, and drinking milk are also recommended.

children.text: yakṛti plīhavat karma dakṣiṇe tu bhuje sirām ||
children.translated_text: For disease of the liver, the treatment is as for the spleen; but the vein to be opened is in the right arm.
For a patient with <s>baddhodara</s> who has been fomented, he should give a decoction enema
mixed with urine and sharp medicines, with oil and salt, together with an unctuous enema.
He should also give foods that move downward and a sharp purgative,
and whatever treatment removes upward movement and pacifies <s>vāta</s> should be performed for him.
Except for fomentation, <s>chidrodara</s> should be treated like abdominal disease of <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: jātaṃ jātaṃ jalaṃ srāvyam evaṃ tad yāpayed bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: Whatever water appears should be drained as it appears; in this way the physician should manage it palliatively.
At the beginning, in <s>udakodara</s>, he should apply remedies that remove the morbid water,
combined with urine, sharp in action, and containing various alkalis.
He should care for that patient with foods that kindle digestion and destroy <s>kapha</s>.
He should strain the alkali of goat dung in urine and cook it over fire.
When it becomes thick, he should add, powdered, one <s>karṣa</s> each of
<s>pippalī</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, dry ginger, and the five salts,
<s>nikumbha</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, and <s>viṣāṇikā</s>,
<s>svarjikākṣāra</s>, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>sātalā</s>, and the alkali from barley awns.
He should make pills the size of jujube fruits from this and then soak them in <s>sauvīraka</s>.
He should drink them in persistent swelling and in advanced <s>udakodara</s>.
If there is no pacification by these medicines in the three conditions beginning with <s>baddhodara</s>,
the physician should use the knife, when requested by the afflicted patient, his relatives, and the king.
When the body has been oleated and fomented, in cases of bound or wounded intestines, below the navel,
he should incise the abdomen, leaving four fingerbreadths on the left side.
The incision should be four fingerbreadths in length; through it he should draw out the intestines,
inspect them, and remove hair, fecal coating, stones, and the like.
When there is a perforation, he should extract the foreign body and cleanse the intestinal discharge.
He should have ants bite the perforation, and when they have taken hold, he should remove them.
Then, guiding the body and the intestines from the head downward, he should place the intestines back in their proper position.

children.text: aktāni madhusarpirbhyām atha sīvyed bahir vraṇam ||
children.translated_text: After anointing them with honey and ghee, he should then suture the external wound.
Next he should smear it with black earth mixed with licorice and bind it.
Staying out of the wind and living on milk, the patient should then remain in a vat of oil.
When there is water in the abdomen, after the patient has been anointed with oils that pacify <s>vāta</s>
and fomented with hot water up to the armpits, with the abdomen wrapped in cloth,
he should pierce a finger's breadth at the place indicated for the bound and perforated abdominal conditions.

children.text: nidhāya tasmin nāḍīṃ ca srāvayed ardham ambhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Placing a tube there, he should drain off half of the water.

children.text: athāsya nāḍīm ākṛṣya tailena lavaṇena ca
children.translated_text: Then, drawing out the tube, with oil and salt

children.text: vraṇam abhyajya baddhvā ca veṣṭayed vāsasodaram ||
children.translated_text: he should anoint the wound, bind it, and wrap the abdomen with cloth.

children.text: tṛtīye 'hni caturthe vā yāvad ā ṣoḍaśaṃ dinam
children.translated_text: On the third or fourth day, up to the sixteenth day,

children.text: tasya viśramya viśramya srāvayed alpaśo jalam ||
children.translated_text: after intervals of rest, he should drain the water little by little.
He should wrap the slack abdomen more tightly with cloth.
When the water has flowed out, after fasting, the patient should drink thin gruel without fat or salt.

children.text: syāt kṣīravṛttiḥ ṣaṇmāsāṃstrīn peyāṃ payasā pibet
children.translated_text: He should live on milk for six months; for three months he should drink gruel with milk,
and for another three months he should eat with milk, or with meat soup soured by fruit.
Then, in small quantities, he should eat well-cooked <s>śyāmāka</s> and <s>kodrava</s>, without fat or salt.
Careful in this way, within a year he should conquer <s>jalodara</s>.
Restrained regarding forbidden things, moderate even in what is prescribed, and self-controlled,
he should be treated so, since every abdominal disease is generally produced by an aggregate of doṣas.
Therefore a treatment that pacifies <s>vāta</s> and the other doṣas is recommended everywhere.

children.text: vahnir mandatvam āyāti doṣaiḥ kukṣau prapūrite ||
children.translated_text: The digestive fire becomes weak when the belly is filled with doṣas.

children.text: tasmād bhojyāni bhojyāni dīpanāni laghūni ca
children.translated_text: Therefore the foods to be eaten should be digestive-kindling and light,
with <s>pañcamūla</s>, slightly sour and salty, unctuous, and pungent.

children.text: bhāvitānāṃ gavāṃ mūtre ṣaṣṭikānāṃ ca taṇḍulaiḥ
children.translated_text: With grains of <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice that have been impregnated with cow's urine,

children.text: yavāgūṃ payasā siddhāṃ prakāmaṃ bhojayen naram ||
children.translated_text: one should cook <s>yavāgū</s> in milk and feed the person as much as he desires.
And afterward he should drink sugarcane juice for the subsiding of abdominal disorders.

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ sthānaṃ vrajantyeṣāṃ vātapittakaphās tathā ||
children.translated_text: In this way <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> return to their own respective places.
He should avoid what is excessively hot, sour, or salty, dry, constipating, cold, or heavy,
as well as jaggery, preparations made with oil, vegetables, and water both for drinking and for immersion bathing.
He should also avoid exertion, travel on the road, daytime sleep, and riding in vehicles.
For drinking, buttermilk that is not too clear, thick, or sweet is recommended.
In a <s>vāta</s> condition it should have <s>kaṇā</s> and salt; in a <s>pitta</s> condition, <s>uṣaṇa</s> and sugar;
in a <s>kapha</s> abdominal disorder, it should have <s>yavānī</s>, rock salt, <s>ajājī</s>, honey, and <s>vyoṣa</s>.
In an abdominal disorder caused by accumulation of all the <s>doṣas</s>, it should be combined with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, alkali, and salts.
For spleen disease it should be combined with honey, oil, <s>vacā</s>, dry ginger, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and rock salt.
But when the spleen is obstructed, it should be used with <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, salt, and <s>ajājī</s>.
In a perforated abdominal disorder it should be taken with <s>kṛṣṇā</s> and honey; in a watery abdomen, as with <s>vyoṣa</s>.
For those suffering from heaviness, anorexia, abdominal distension, weak digestive fire, and diarrhea,
buttermilk becomes like nectar for those afflicted by <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: prayogāṇāṃ ca sarveṣām anu kṣīraṃ prayojayet
children.translated_text: After all these applications, milk should be administered.
It brings firmness to all the bodily tissues, gives strength, and removes associated <s>doṣas</s>.
For those whose bodies have been wasted by medicines, milk itself becomes like nectar.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
A patient with <s>pāṇḍu</s> should first drink ghee called <s>Kalyāṇaka</s>,
or <s>Pañcagavya</s> ghee, <s>Mahātikta</s> ghee, or ghee cooked with the <s>āragvadhādi</s> group.

children.text: dāḍimāt kuḍavo dhānyāt kuḍavārdhaṃ palaṃ palam
children.translated_text: One <s>kuḍava</s> of pomegranate, half a <s>kuḍava</s> of coriander, and one <s>pala</s> each
of <s>citraka</s> and fresh ginger, along with half a <s>pala</s> of long pepper, should be made into a paste.
With these pastes, twenty <s>palas</s> of ghee are cooked in one <s>āḍhaka</s> of water.
This prepared ghee removes disorders of the heart, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, <s>gulma</s>, piles, spleen disease, and affliction from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
It stimulates digestion, destroys dyspnea and cough, and moves obstructed <s>vāta</s> downward.
It is also recommended for women who have painful childbirth and for barren women.

children.text: snehitaṃ vāmayet tīkṣṇaiḥ punaḥ snigdhaṃ ca śodhayet
children.translated_text: When oleated, the patient should be made to vomit with sharp medicines; then, oleated again, he should be purified
many times with milk mixed with urine, or with milk alone.
An <s>añjali</s> of <s>kāśmarya</s> soaked in warm juice of <s>dantī</s> fruit,

children.text: drākṣāñjaliṃ vā mṛditaṃ tat pibet pāṇḍurogajit ||
children.translated_text: or an <s>añjali</s> of grapes crushed in it, should be drunk; that conquers <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.

children.text: mūtreṇa piṣṭāṃ pathyāṃ vā tatsiddhaṃ vā phalatrayam
children.translated_text: Or he may drink <s>pathyā</s> ground with urine, or the three fruits prepared with that urine.
<s>Svarṇakṣīrī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>bhadradāru</s>, and <s>mahauṣadha</s>,

children.text: gomūtrāñjalinā piṣṭaṃ śṛtaṃ tenaiva vā pibet
children.translated_text: ground with an <s>añjali</s> of cow's urine, or boiled in that same urine, should be drunk.

children.text: sādhitaṃ kṣīram ebhir vā pibed doṣānulomanam ||
children.translated_text: Or he may drink milk prepared with these; it causes the <s>doṣas</s> to move downward.

children.text: mūtre sthitaṃ vā saptāhaṃ payasāyorajaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: Or he should drink iron powder kept in urine for seven days, taking it with milk.

children.text: jīrṇe kṣīreṇa bhuñjīta rasena madhureṇa vā ||
children.translated_text: When the milk has been digested, he should eat with milk or with sweet meat broth.
After being purified in both ways, he should lick <s>pathyā</s> softened with honey and ghee.
<s>Viśālā</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>dāru</s>, and <s>kaliṅgaka</s>,
each in portions of one <s>karṣa</s>, with two <s>picus</s> of <s>mūrvā</s> and half-<s>karṣa</s> portions of <s>ghuṇapriyā</s>,

children.text: pītvā taccūrṇam ambhobhiḥ sukhair lihyāt tato madhu ||
children.translated_text: should be taken as a powder with agreeable waters; afterward he should lick honey.

children.text: pāṇḍurogaṃ jvaraṃ dāhaṃ kāsaṃ śvāsam arocakam
children.translated_text: That conquers <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>, fever, burning, cough, dyspnea, anorexia,
<s>gulma</s>, abdominal distension, <s>āmavāta</s>, and <s>raktapitta</s>.
A decoction of <s>vāsā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>kaṭvī</s>, <s>bhūnimba</s>, and neem bark,
mixed with honey, destroys <s>pāṇḍu</s>, disorders of <s>pitta</s> and blood, and jaundice.
Iron powder equal in amount to <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>mustā</s>
should be powdered and administered with buttermilk, honey, ghee, or warm water.
It destroys jaundice, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, heart disease, skin disease, piles, and urinary disorders.
Jaggery, dry ginger, <s>maṇḍūra</s>, and sesame should be taken in equal measures,
and twice as much long pepper should be added; this pill should be given to a patient with <s>pāṇḍu</s>.

children.text: tāpyaṃ dārvyās tvacaṃ cavyaṃ granthikaṃ devadāru ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s>, bark of <s>dārvī</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>granthika</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,
together with the group of nine beginning with <s>vyoṣa</s>, should be powdered; then twice as much
<s>maṇḍūra</s>, black like collyrium, is added, and all of it is put into cow's urine eight times its quantity,
which has been cooked separately until it is fit for forming pills.

children.text: prakṣipya vaṭakān kuryāt tān khādet takrabhojanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should make pills from it, and the patient should eat them while taking buttermilk as food.
These <s>maṇḍūra</s> pills are life-giving for patients with <s>pāṇḍu</s>.
They pacify skin diseases, chronic fever, swelling, stiffness of the thighs, and anorexia,

children.text: arśāṃsi kāmalāṃ mehān plīhānaṃ śamayanti ca
children.translated_text: as well as piles, jaundice, urinary disorders, and disease of the spleen.
<s>Tāpya</s>, mountain resin, silver dross, and iron dross should each be taken in five-<s>pala</s> portions.
They are combined with one-<s>pala</s> portions of <s>citraka</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>.
Powdered and mixed with eight <s>palas</s> of sugar, they are softened with honey.

children.text: pāṇḍurogaṃ viṣaṃ kāsaṃ yakṣmāṇaṃ viṣamaṃ jvaram
children.translated_text: They especially destroy <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>, poisoning, cough, consumption, irregular fever,
skin diseases, chronic fever, urinary disorder, swelling, dyspnea, and anorexia;
above all, they destroy epilepsy, jaundice, and disorders born in the anus.
With <s>kauṭaja</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, neem, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>ghana</s>, and dry ginger,
the ingredients are impregnated for ten days with their juices, or with two or three times as much juice.
Eight <s>palas</s> of <s>śilājatu</s> and the same quantity of white sugar are used.
<s>Tvakkṣīrī</s>, long pepper, <s>dhātrī</s>, and the drug called <s>karkaṭa</s> are each measured at one <s>pala</s>.
One <s>pala</s> is taken from the fruit and root of <s>nidigdhī</s>, and the three aromatics are added in suitable measure.
With three <s>palas</s> of honey, he should make boluses equal to an <s>akṣa</s> in size.
After eating them, he should drink pomegranate water, milk, bird broth, meat broth, water, <s>surā</s>, or <s>āsava</s>,

children.text: tān bhakṣayitvānupiben niranno bhukta eva vā
children.translated_text: either while fasting or after he has eaten.
These wholesome boluses, removing all <s>doṣas</s>, destroy <s>pāṇḍu</s>, skin disease, fever, spleen disease, asthma, emaciation, and fistula,
disorders of the heart, urine, putrid semen, digestive fire, wasting, poison, and abdominal disease,
cough, bloody vaginal discharge, <s>pittāsṛk</s>, swelling, <s>gulma</s>, and diseases of the throat,
as well as urinary disorder, scrotal enlargement, and dizziness.
One <s>prastha</s> of grapes, one <s>prastha</s> of <s>kaṇā</s>, half a <s>tulā</s> of sugar,

children.text: dvipalaṃ madhukaṃ śuṇṭhīṃ tvakkṣīrīṃ ca vicūrṇitam
children.translated_text: and two <s>palas</s> each of <s>madhuka</s>, dry ginger, and <s>tvakkṣīrī</s> should be powdered.
Having put that into a <s>droṇa</s> of the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit, he should cook it to the consistency of an electuary.
When it has cooled, he should lick a palmful of it, mixed with a <s>prastha</s> of honey.
It checks <s>halīmaka</s>, <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> (anemia-like pallor disease), and <s>kāmalā</s> (jaundice).
Water prepared with the lesser five roots is recommended for drinking and in food.
For those suffering from <s>pāṇḍu</s> and <s>kāmalā</s>, the juice of raisins and <s>āmalaka</s> is recommended.
Thus the treatment used by the physician in <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> has been stated in general terms.

children.text: vikalpya yojyaṃ viduṣā pṛthag doṣabalaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: The learned physician should apply it with variations, separately according to the strength of the <s>doṣas</s>.
In a disorder arising from <s>vāta</s>, it should be predominantly unctuous; in a <s>pitta</s> disorder, bitter and cooling.
In a <s>kapha</s> disorder it should be pungent, drying, and heating; in one involving all three <s>doṣas</s>, it should be mixed.

children.text: mṛdaṃ niryāpayet kāyāt tīkṣṇaiḥ saṃśodhanaiḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: First, he should drive the clay out of the body by sharp purificatory measures.

children.text: balādhānāni sarpīṃṣi śuddhe koṣṭhe tu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: But when the bowel has been purified, he should administer ghees that build strength.
<s>Vyoṣa</s>, <s>bilva</s>, the two <s>rajanīs</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>dvipunarnava</s>,
<s>mustā</s>, iron rust, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,

children.text: vṛścikālī ca bhārgī ca sakṣīrais taiḥ śṛtaṃ ghṛtam
children.translated_text: together with <s>vṛścikālī</s> and <s>bhārgī</s>: ghee cooked with these and milk
quickly pacifies all disorders caused by clay.
In the same way, with saffron, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, milk, and <s>śādvala</s>,
when there is a craving for clay, he should give clay processed with these, in order to create aversion to clay.
This may also be done with <s>vellā</s>, <s>agni</s>, neem blossoms, <s>pāṭhā</s>, or <s>mūrvā</s>.
The medicine should be chosen according to the particular kind of clay and the <s>doṣas</s> affected by it.
In <s>kāmalā</s>, one should use what pacifies <s>pitta</s> and is not opposed to <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.
A <s>prastha</s> of ghee, cooked in the juice of one hundred <s>pathyā</s> fruits with a paste of fifty <s>pathyā</s> stalks,
cures <s>gulma</s>, <s>kāmalā</s>, and <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.
He should give <s>āragvadha</s>, together with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, in an amount the size of a <s>bilva</s>,
with the juice of sugarcane, or of <s>vidārī</s>, or of <s>āmalaka</s>; it removes <s>kāmalā</s>.
Or he should drink paste of <s>nikumbha</s> with twice as much jaggery, mixed with cold water.

children.text: kumbhasya cūrṇaṃ sakṣaudraṃ traiphalena rasena vā
children.translated_text: Or he should use powder of <s>kumbha</s> with honey, or with the juice of <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: triphalāyā guḍūcyā vā dārvyā nimbasya vā rasam ||
children.translated_text: or the juice of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, or neem.
Morning after morning, he should administer these with honey to one afflicted by <s>kāmalā</s>.
A collyrium made from <s>niśā</s>, red ochre, and <s>dhātrī</s> removes <s>kāmalā</s>.

children.text: tilapiṣṭanibhaṃ yas tu kāmalāvān sṛjen malam
children.translated_text: But when a person with <s>kāmalā</s> passes stool resembling sesame paste,
his <s>pitta</s>, whose path is blocked by <s>kapha</s>, should be conquered by remedies that remove <s>kapha</s>.
Through dry, cold, heavy, and sweet things, through exercise, and through restraint of strength,

children.text: kaphasaṃmūrchito vāyur yadā pittaṃ bahiḥ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: when <s>vāyu</s>, overwhelmed by <s>kapha</s>, drives <s>pitta</s> outward,
then the man's eyes, urine, and skin become yellow, while his feces become white.
He becomes affected with gurgling, obstruction, and heaviness in the heart.
Weakness, poor digestion, pain in the sides, hiccup, dyspnea, anorexia, and fever follow.
Gradually, when the <s>pitta</s> is scant and lodged in the branches of the body, he should treat him as follows.
He should feed him with dry, pungent, and sour meat juices of peacock, partridge, and cock,
and with soups made from dried radish and from horse gram.
Very sour, sharp, pungent, salty, and hot substances are also recommended.
He should lick <s>vyoṣa</s> with the juice of citron and other suitable vehicles.

children.text: svaṃ pittam eti tenāsya śakṛd apyanurajyate
children.translated_text: By this, his own <s>pitta</s> returns, and even his feces become colored again.
<s>Vāyu</s> too becomes pacified, together with complications such as gurgling.
When his complications have ceased, the regimen for <s>kāmalā</s> should be applied to him.
In <s>kumbhakāmalā</s>, he should drink <s>śilājatu</s> with cow's urine,

children.text: māsaṃ mākṣikadhātuṃ vā kiṭṭaṃ vātha hiraṇyajam
children.translated_text: or <s>mākṣika</s> mineral for a month, or else slag produced from gold.
For one with <s>halīmaka</s>, after oleation with buffalo ghee cooked with fresh <s>guḍūcī</s> juice and milk,
he should drink <s>trivṛt</s> with <s>dhātrī</s> juice.
When purged by that, he should eat sweet food that pacifies <s>pitta</s> and <s>anila</s>.

children.text: drākṣālehaṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ sarpīṃṣi madhurāṇi ca
children.translated_text: He should also make use of the raisin electuary mentioned earlier and sweet ghees.
He should regularly take sustaining milk enemas, together with unctuous enemas.
He should drink formulas of raisin <s>ariṣṭa</s> as appropriate, to increase the digestive fire.
A skilled physician should also use <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>abhayāleha</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>balā</s>
with milk, according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to the patient's strength,
in cases of <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>; and he should apply the course of treatment described for swelling.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>śvayathu</s> (swelling).
So said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
In <s>śvayathu</s> caused by the <s>doṣas</s>, spreading everywhere through the whole body, first,

children.text: sāme viśoṣito bhuktvā laghu koṣṇāmbhasā pibet ||
children.translated_text: when there is <s>āma</s>, the patient, after being dried out and after eating light food, should drink with lukewarm water
<s>nāgara</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, and <s>uṣaṇa</s>,
or else <s>vijayā</s>, dry ginger, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>punarnava</s>.
Or, when the <s>doṣas</s> are abundant, he should take <s>navāyasa</s> for purification, and <s>harītakī</s> with urine.
With a decoction of <s>varā</s>, he may take <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, iron preparation, and <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>.
Or, in the same way, he may take <s>guggulu</s>, or mineral pitch born from the mountain.
One with weak digestion, whose stool is obstructed by <s>āma</s>, heaviness, and irregularity, should habitually use
buttermilk mixed with <s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and honey, and <s>guḍābhayā</s>.
Or, in the same way, he may take jaggery and dry ginger with buttermilk as the after-drink.
Or he may take fresh ginger with an equal amount of jaggery, increasing by half a <s>prakuñca</s>,
up to a maximum of five <s>palas</s>, for a month, while eating soup, milk, and meat broth.
This regimen conquers <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, hemorrhoids, swelling, <s>prameha</s>, dyspnea, catarrh, <s>alasaka</s>, indigestion,

children.text: sakāmalāśoṣamanovikārān kāsaṃ kaphaṃ caiva jayet prayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>kāmalā</s>, wasting, mental disorders, cough, and <s>kapha</s> itself.

children.text: ghṛtam ārdrakanāgarasya kalkasvarasābhyāṃ payasā ca sādhayitvā
children.translated_text: After cooking ghee with the paste and juice of fresh ginger and dry ginger, and with milk,
even one overwhelmed by swelling, sneezing, abdominal disease, and weakness of digestion becomes free from disease by drinking it.
When free from <s>āma</s>, with fecal impurity bound, a person afflicted by <s>śvayathu</s> should drink
milk cooked with <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: mūtraṃ gor vā mahiṣyā vā sakṣīraṃ kṣīrabhojanaḥ
children.translated_text: or the urine of a cow or buffalo mixed with milk, while living on a milk diet.
For seven days, or for a month, there should be a regimen of camel's milk.
One should take <s>yavānaka</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, and the <s>pañcakola</s> group,
pepper, pomegranate, <s>pāṭhā</s>, coriander, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
and young <s>bilva</s>, each in one-<s>karṣa</s> portions, and cook them in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water.
A <s>prastha</s> of ghee cooked with that destroys swelling, piles, <s>gulma</s>, and <s>meha</s>.
Or ghee may be prepared from curds containing <s>citraka</s>, mixed with that buttermilk,

children.text: pakvaṃ sacitrakaṃ tadvad guṇair yuñjyācca kālavit ||
children.translated_text: and cooked together with <s>citraka</s>; one who knows the proper time should use it likewise for these properties.
The <s>Dhānvantara</s>, <s>Mahātikta</s>, <s>Kalyāṇa</s>, and <s>Abhayā</s> ghee preparations may also be used.
In a bronze vessel one should cook one hundred <s>pathyā</s> fruits in a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>.

children.text: dattvā guḍatulāṃ tasmin lehe dadyād vicūrṇitam
children.translated_text: After adding a <s>tulā</s> of jaggery to that electuary, one should add, in powdered form,
<s>trijātaka</s>, <s>trikaṭuka</s>, and a little substance produced from barley awns.

children.text: prasthārdhaṃ ca hime kṣaudrāt tan nihantyupayojitam
children.translated_text: When it is cool, one should add half a <s>prastha</s> of honey; used in this way, it destroys
advanced swelling, fever, <s>meha</s>, <s>gulma</s>, wasting, <s>āmavāta</s>, acid disorder, and blood-pitta,
as well as discoloration, disorders of urine, flatus, and semen, dyspnea, anorexia, spleen disease, poisoning, and abdominal disease.
Old barley and rice food cooked in <s>daśamūla</s> water
is beneficial in swelling when eaten in small quantity, with little salt and little fat.
Soups of mung beans and horse gram, containing alkali, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>,
and likewise meat soups from wild animals, tortoise, iguana, and porcupine are beneficial.
For drinking, non-sour churned curds and medicated liquors are also beneficial.
With cumin, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, caraway, <s>pauṣkara</s>, and <s>agni</s>,
with the pith of <s>bilva</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s>, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, and measured <s>badara</s>,
a thin gruel made with ghee and oil, properly roasted, is supremely beneficial
for those with swelling, diarrhea, heart disease, <s>gulma</s>, piles, weak digestion, and <s>meha</s>.
A similar preparation made from <s>pāṭhā</s> cooked with <s>pañcakola</s> has the same properties.
With <s>śaileya</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>sthauṇeya</s>, <s>reṇukā</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
with <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, <s>nakha</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
with <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>māgadhikā</s>, wild coriander, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, and <s>vālaka</s>,
and with <s>caturjātaka</s>, <s>tālīśa</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and fragrant <s>palāśa</s>,

children.text: kuryād abhyañjanaṃ tailaṃ lepaṃ snānāya tūdakam ||
children.translated_text: one should prepare an oil for massage, a paste, and water for bathing.
Or bathing may be done with water cooked with <s>nimba</s>, <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>naktamāla</s>, and <s>arka</s>.
In swelling confined to one limb, with <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>karavīraka</s>, and <s>kiṃśuka</s>,
with <s>viśālā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>nalikā</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,
with <s>hiṃsrā</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>mādrī</s>, <s>tālaparṇī</s>, and <s>jayantī</s>,
with <s>sthūlakākādanī</s>, <s>śālanākulī</s>, and <s>vṛṣaparṇī</s>,
and with <s>vṛddhi</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, and <s>hastikarṇa</s>, a comfortably warm paste is beneficial.
Now, in swelling arising from <s>vāta</s>, one should drink <s>trivṛt</s> for half a month.

children.text: tailam eraṇḍajaṃ vātaviḍvibandhe tad eva tu ||
children.translated_text: In obstruction of <s>vāta</s> and feces, castor oil should be used in just the same way.

children.text: prāgbhaktaṃ payasā yuktaṃ rasair vā kārayet tathā
children.translated_text: One should administer it before food, combined with milk or with meat soups.
Likewise, one should apply sudations and massages that pacify <s>vāta</s>; when it affects one limb, again a paste
should be made with citron, <s>agnimantha</s>, dry ginger, <s>hiṃsrā</s>, and the herb called <s>marā</s>.

children.text: paitte tiktaṃ pibet sarpir nyagrodhādyena vā śṛtam ||
children.translated_text: In a pitta condition, one should drink bitter ghee, or milk cooked with the <s>nyagrodhādi</s> group
for thirst, burning, and faintness; pastes and massages should be cooling.
<s>Paṭola</s> root, <s>trāyantī</s>, licorice, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>,

children.text: dāru dārvī himaṃ dantī viśālā niculaṃ kaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>dāru</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>hima</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, <s>nicula</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>:
a decoction of these, drunk with ghee, destroys internal heat, thirst, and dizziness,
as well as <s>saṃnipāta</s>, <s>visarpa</s>, swelling, burning, poisoning, and fever.
When the condition arises from <s>śleṣman</s>, one should drink oil prepared with the <s>āragvadhādi</s> group.
When the channels are obstructed, the digestive fire is weak, there is anorexia, and the bodily interior is sluggish,
one should habitually use alkaline powders, <s>āsava</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, urine, and buttermilk.
Black pepper, old oil-cake, bark of <s>śigru</s>, sand, and flax
should be used for smearing and rubbing, made into a paste with urine and comfortably warm.
Bathing should be done in urine and water cooked with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
or with horse gram and dry ginger; <s>caṇḍāguru</s> is used for anointing.
<s>Kālājaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>bastagandhā</s>, <s>hayāhvayā</s>,
and <s>ekaiṣīkā</s> make a paste for swelling affecting a single limb.
In a mixed-doṣa condition one should perform purification and bloodletting according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to the affected site.
The treatment should be based on the force of the aggravated <s>doṣa</s>.
Cumin, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>pañcakola</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and turmeric, drunk with warm water,

children.text: śophaṃ tridoṣaṃ cirajaṃ pravṛddhaṃ nighnanti bhūnimbamahauṣadhe ca ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>bhūnimba</s> and <s>mahauṣadha</s>, destroy swelling that is tridoṣic, chronic, and advanced.
The two <s>amṛtā</s>s, <s>śivātikā</s>, <s>surakāṣṭha</s>, with <s>pura</s> and cow's urine,
remove swelling, abdominal enlargement, skin disease, anemia, worms, <s>meha</s>, upward-moving <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: iti nijam adhikṛtya pathyam uktaṃ kṣatajanite kṣatajaṃ viśodhanīyam
children.translated_text: Thus the regimen has been stated with reference to intrinsic swelling; in swelling caused by injury, the blood from injury should be purified.
For swelling caused by poison, treatment against poison is desired, along with bleeding, cold applications, ghee, pastes, sprinkling, and purifying measures.
A patient with swelling should avoid meat from domestic, aquatic, and marshy animals, weak meat, dried vegetables, and food made of sesame,

children.text: gauḍaṃ piṣṭānnaṃ dadhi salavaṇaṃ vijjalaṃ madyam amlam
children.translated_text: jaggery liquor, flour preparations, curds, salty food, waterless preparations, and sour liquor,

children.text: dhānā vallūraṃ samaśanam atho gurvasātmyaṃ vidāhi
children.translated_text: parched grain, dried meat, eating incompatible foods together, and heavy, unsuitable, or burning foods,

children.text: svapnaṃ cārātrau śvayathugadavān varjayen maithunaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: as well as sleeping at improper times and sexual intercourse.
Now therefore we shall explain the treatment of <s>visarpa</s>.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
At the very beginning, in cases of <s>visarpa</s>, fasting and drying measures are beneficial,

children.text: raktāvaseko vamanaṃ virekaḥ snehanaṃ na tu ||
children.translated_text: as are bloodletting, emesis, and purgation, but not oleation.
A vomitive that destroys <s>visarpa</s> is the fruit taken with licorice and <s>indrayava</s>,
or combined with <s>paṭola</s>, long pepper, and sprouts of <s>nimba</s>,

children.text: rasena yuktaṃ trāyantyā drākṣāyās traiphalena vā
children.translated_text: mixed with the juice of <s>trāyantī</s>, or with that of grapes, or with a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
For purgation, <s>trivṛt</s> powder is used with milk or with ghee.
When the <s>doṣa</s> has gone into the <s>koṣṭha</s> (alimentary tract), purification should especially be applied.
For one who is not fit for purification, when the <s>doṣa</s> is slight, palliative treatment with <s>candana</s> and <s>utpala</s> should be used.
Or one may use <s>musta</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>paṭola</s>, or simply the group beginning with <s>paṭola</s>.
Or <s>śārivā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>musta</s>, boiled in water, may be used.
<s>Durālabhā</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s> should be cooked,
and a person suffering from thirst and <s>visarpa</s> should drink it, either cooked down or as a cold decoction.
Likewise <s>dārvī</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>masūra</s>, and <s>triphala</s>,
together with <s>nimba</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, and <s>trāyantī</s>, decocted and tempered with ghee, may be used.

children.text: śākhāduṣṭe tu rudhire raktam evādito haret
children.translated_text: But when the blood is vitiated in the branches, he should remove blood first of all.
For moist corruption of the skin, flesh, and sinews arises from the moist corruption of the blood.
When there is no <s>āma</s>, when <s>śleṣman</s> is diminished, and when <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> predominate,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tiktaṃ mahātiktaṃ śṛtaṃ vā trāyamāṇayā ||
children.translated_text: bitter ghee, <s>mahātikta</s> ghee, or ghee cooked with <s>trāyamāṇā</s> is beneficial.
After the blood has been removed and the internal <s>doṣas</s> have been purified, when it has gone into the skin, flesh, and joints,
external treatments such as applications should be used for the immediate pacification of <s>visarpa</s>.
<s>Śatāhvā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>vārāhī</s>, <s>vaṃśa</s>, <s>ārtagala</s>, <s>dhānyaka</s>,

children.text: surāhvā kṛṣṇagandhā ca kuṣṭhaṃ cālepanaṃ cale ||
children.translated_text: <s>surāhvā</s>, <s>kṛṣṇagandhā</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s> are a paste for the moving type.
For <s>pitta</s>, the <s>nyagrodhādi</s> group is used, and similarly the group beginning with <s>padma</s> and <s>utpala</s>.
