Young shoots of <s>nyagrodha</s>, combined with the inner pith of plantain,
and knots of lotus-rhizome make a paste, soaked in hundred-times-washed ghee.

children.text: padminīkardamaḥ śītaḥ piṣṭaṃ mauktikam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: Cold lotus mud may be used, or powdered pearl.

children.text: śaṅkhaḥ pravālaṃ śuktir vā gairikaṃ vā ghṛtānvitam
children.translated_text: Conch, coral, shell, or red ochre may also be used, mixed with ghee.
<s>Triphala</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, and <s>karavīraka</s>,
with reed roots and <s>anantā</s>, form a paste that removes <s>śleṣman</s>-type <s>visarpa</s>.
<s>Dhava</s>, <s>saptāhva</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>kuraṇṭaka</s>,
together with <s>musta</s> and <s>āragvadha</s>, make a paste, or the group beginning with <s>varuṇa</s> may be used.
The leaves of <s>āragvadha</s>, bark produced from <s>śleṣmātaka</s>,
<s>indrāṇīśāka</s>, <s>kākāhvā</s>, and flowers of <s>śirīṣa</s> may also be used.
With these same medicines he should prepare sprinklings, wound treatments, massages, ghee preparations, pastes, and powders, as appropriate.
For <s>vāyu</s>, pastes made from these very drugs should contain abundant ghee.
When it is located in the seat of <s>kapha</s> and accompanied by <s>āma</s>, or when it is located in the seat of <s>pitta</s>,
applications that are neither cold nor hot are beneficial and dry; in blood-and-<s>pitta</s> conditions they should be mixed with ghee.
They should be very cold, thin, and placed beneath a thin cloth.

children.text: yojyāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe 'nye 'nye mandavīryās ta eva ca
children.translated_text: Different applications should be used again and again, moment by moment, and those same ones should be mild in potency.
When the <s>doṣas</s> are combined, a combined form of this treatment is recommended.
He should smear the burning area with hundred-times-washed ghee, or with that alone.
He should sprinkle it with cool ghee-scum, with licorice water,
with sugar-water, rainwater, milk, or sugarcane juice.
For drinking, application, and sprinkling, <s>mahātikta</s> is supremely beneficial.
In the type called <s>granthi</s>, after properly performing the blood-and-<s>pitta</s>-removing treatment as prescribed,
the desired treatment is one that removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>anila</s>, including lump fomentation and poulticing.
But in the pain of <s>granthi-visarpa</s>, he should sprinkle with warm oil
cooked with <s>daśamūla</s>, or likewise with urines or with water.
Or he should smear it with <s>kṛṣṇagandhā</s> ground into a pleasantly warm paste,
with bark of <s>naktamāla</s>, with dried radishes, or with <s>kali</s>.
<s>Dantī</s>, root-bark of <s>citraka</s>, latexes of <s>sudhā</s> and <s>arka</s>, jaggery,
the kernel of <s>bhallātaka</s>, and <s>kāsīsa</s> make a paste that could split even a stone.
How much more, then, will it split a gland lodged in the external channel and arisen from <s>kapha</s>?
With these medicines he should break up even a gland that has remained for a long time.
This may also be done with soups of radishes and horse gram, mixed with alkali and pomegranate,
with wheat foods or barley foods, together with <s>sīdhu</s>, honey, and sugar,
or with <s>vāruṇī</s> scum mixed with honey and the juice of citron,
and with administrations of <s>triphala</s> and of <s>pippalī</s> combined with honey,
with administrations of <s>devadāru</s> and <s>guḍūcī</s>, and also of mineral pitch,
with administrations of <s>musta</s>, <s>bhallāta</s>, and parched grain, and also of honey.
It may be treated with fumigations, purgations of the head, and the previously taught remedies that break up <s>gulma</s>,
and with pressure from heated iron, gold, salt, stone, and the like.

children.text: ābhiḥ kriyābhiḥ siddhābhir vividhābhir bale sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: If, despite these various proven procedures, the patient remains strong
and the gland, hard as stone, still does not subside,

children.text: athāsya dāhaḥ kṣāreṇa śarair hemnāpi vā hitaḥ
children.translated_text: then cauterization with alkali, with sharp instruments, or even with gold is beneficial for it.

children.text: pākibhiḥ pācayitvā vā pāṭayitvā tam uddharet ||
children.translated_text: Or, after maturing it with suppurating agents, he should open it and extract it.
He should repeatedly let out its blood when it has become excited.
Then, after the blood has again been removed, medicine that conquers <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> should be used.
When it has become wet through cauterization and suppuration, external and internal treatment should be as for a wound.
Oil prepared with <s>dārvī</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>kampilla</s> is beneficial for the wound.
But in a condition dominated by <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, ghee prepared with fresh juice of <s>dūrvā</s> is beneficial.
All the other procedures stand on one side, and bloodletting stands on the other.
For <s>visarpa</s> does not arise without mixture; it arises together with blood and <s>pitta</s>.
Blood itself is its support; therefore one should remove blood repeatedly.

children.text: na ghṛtaṃ bahudoṣāya deyaṃ yan na virecanam
children.translated_text: Ghee that is not purgative should not be given to a person with many <s>doṣas</s>.
For the <s>doṣa</s>, obstructed by it, would cook the skin, blood, and flesh.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
One should first treat every person with <s>kuṣṭha</s> by administering unctuous drink.

children.text: tatra vātottare tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ vā sādhitaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: There, when <s>vāta</s> predominates, oil or ghee properly prepared is beneficial.
With <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>eraṇḍa</s>, <s>śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, and <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,
with <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>durālabhā</s>,

children.text: parpaṭaṃ trāyamāṇāṃ ca palāṃśaṃ pācayed apām
children.translated_text: and with one <s>pala</s> each of <s>parpaṭa</s> and <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, one should cook it in water.
with that, when only one eighth remains from two <s>āḍhakas</s>, and likewise with the drugs measured by one <s>karṣa</s> each:
<s>trāyantī</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>bhūnimba</s>, <s>kaliṅga</s>, <s>kaṇa</s>, and sandalwood.

children.text: sarpiṣo dvādaśapalaṃ pacet tat tiktakaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: One should cook twelve <s>palas</s> of ghee; that <s>Tiktaka</s> overcomes
<s>kuṣṭha</s> of pitta origin, <s>parīsarpa</s>, eruptions, burning, thirst, and dizziness,
itching, pallor disease, swellings, foul sinus wounds, and scrofulous swellings,
blisters, abscesses, abdominal masses, swelling, insanity, and intoxication too,
heart disease, blindness, dark facial patches, <s>grahaṇī</s>, white leprosy, and jaundice,
fistula-in-ano, epilepsy, abdominal disease, excessive uterine discharge, and poison,
hemorrhoids, bleeding disorder, and other pitta-born diseases that are hard to cure.
<s>saptacchada</s>, <s>parpaṭaka</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: triphalā padmakaṃ pāṭhā rajanyau śārive kaṇe ||
children.translated_text: <s>triphala</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, the two <s>rajanīs</s>, the two <s>śārivās</s>, and the two <s>kaṇās</s>,
<s>nimba</s>, sandalwood, licorice, <s>viśālā</s>, <s>indrayava</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>,
<s>kirātatiktaka</s>, <s>sevya</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>paṭola</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, and <s>dhanvayāsaka</s>:
with these, in eight times as much water and twice as much <s>āmalakī</s> juice,
ghee cooked to completion is regarded as <s>Mahātikta</s>, superior in qualities to the bitter ghee.
When <s>kapha</s> predominates, ghee cooked with <s>nimba</s>, <s>saptāhva</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, pungent drugs, <s>vacā</s>, <s>śāla</s>, <s>priyāla</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s>, is used.
In all cases he should drink oils of <s>āruṣkara</s>, <s>tauvara</s>, and mustard,
or ghee as the unctuous substance, cooked with <s>kṛmijit</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, and <s>bhallātaka</s>.
Ghee cooked a hundred times with the root of <s>āragvadha</s>,

children.text: piban kuṣṭhaṃ jayatyāśu bhajan sakhadiraṃ jalam
children.translated_text: when drunk while taking water with <s>khadira</s>, quickly overcomes <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
With these same fats, according to the case, external anointing is also beneficial.

children.text: snigdhasya śodhanaṃ yojyaṃ visarpe yad udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: For a patient who has been oleated, purification should be applied as taught for <s>visarpa</s>.
One should also release his veins on the forehead, hands, and feet.
In a minor <s>kuṣṭha</s> case, scarification is used, and horns and similar instruments as appropriate.
At intervals one should nourish him with anti-<s>kuṣṭha</s> unctuous preparations.
For a <s>kuṣṭha</s> patient whose blood has been let, who has been purged, and whose bowel is empty,

children.text: prabhañjanas tathā hyasya na syād dehaprabhañjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>vāta</s>, the breaker, does not then become a breaker of his body.
Ghee cooked with decoction and paste of <s>vāsā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and <s>karañja</s>
is called <s>Vajraka</s>; it removes <s>visarpa</s>, fever, jaundice, bleeding disorder, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
With <s>triphala</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, the two <s>kaṇṭakārīs</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, and <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>,
together with <s>vacā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>agnika</s>, and <s>pāṭhā</s>, each in a <s>picu</s> portion, and a handful of fresh <s>vajra</s> milk,

children.text: piṣṭaiḥ siddhaṃ sarpiṣaḥ prastham ebhiḥ krūre koṣṭhe snehanaṃ recanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: a <s>prastha</s> of ghee cooked with these ground substances is both oleation and purgation for a hard bowel.
That, called <s>Mahāvajraka</s>, destroys difficult <s>kuṣṭha</s>, white leprosy, splenic disease, scrotal swelling, stone, and abdominal masses.

children.text: dantyāḍhakam apāṃ droṇe paktvā tena ghṛtaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: Having cooked half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>dantī</s> in a <s>droṇa</s> of water, one should cook ghee with that decoction.
When drunk with a <s>pala</s> of <s>dhāmārgava</s>, it purifies both upward and downward.
One should cook a <s>tulā</s> of <s>āvartakī</s> in a <s>droṇa</s> until one eighth remains.
In the decoction of its roots one should thoroughly cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee.

children.text: pītvā tad ekadivasāntaritaṃ sujīrṇe bhuñjīta kodravam asaṃskṛtakāñjikena
children.translated_text: After drinking that every other day, when it has been well digested, he should eat <s>kodrava</s> with unseasoned sour gruel,

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ kilāsam apacīṃ ca vijetum icchan icchan prajāṃ ca vipulāṃ grahaṇaṃ smṛtiṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: wishing to conquer <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kilāsa</s>, and scrofula, and desiring abundant offspring, retention, and memory.
For an ascetic, the fat of <s>lelītaka</s> mixed with honey and jasmine juice
destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s>; or equal ghee may be used with decoction of <s>gāyatrī</s> and <s>asana</s>.
<s>śāli</s> rice, barley, wheat, <s>koradūṣa</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
<s>mudga</s>, lentils, pigeon peas, bitter vegetables, and meat of animals from dry land
prepared with <s>varā</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>āruṣkara</s>,
wines containing medicines, and churned buttermilk with <s>indurājī</s>,
are wholesome food and drink in <s>kuṣṭha</s>, but sour, salty, and hot things are not.
He should especially avoid curds, milk, jaggery, marshy meat, sesame, and black gram.
Roots of <s>paṭola</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>viśālā</s>, separately in three parts, reduced by three <s>śāṇas</s>,

children.text: syus trāyamāṇā kaṭurohiṇī ca bhāgārdhike nāgarapādayukte ||
children.translated_text: with <s>trāyamāṇā</s> and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> in half portions, and with a quarter part of dry ginger:

children.text: etat palaṃ jarjaritaṃ vipakvaṃ jale pibed doṣaviśodhanāya
children.translated_text: one should drink one <s>pala</s> of this, crushed and cooked in water, for purification of the doṣas.
When it is digested, he should take old <s>śāli</s> rice with soups of dry-land deer and birds.

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ kilāsaṃ grahaṇīpradoṣam arśāṃsi kṛcchrāṇi halīmakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: With a six-night course, this destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kilāsa</s>, disorder of <s>grahaṇī</s>, hemorrhoids, difficult urinary disease, and <s>halīmaka</s>,
as well as pain in the heart and bladder, and intermittent fever.
Three <s>palas</s> each of the essence of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>, and three <s>palas</s> from <s>kumbha</s>,

children.text: guḍasya ca dvādaśa māsam eṣa jitātmanāṃ hantyupayujyamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with twelve <s>palas</s> of jaggery, when used for a month by self-controlled people, destroys
<s>kuṣṭha</s>, white leprosy, dyspnea, cough, abdominal disease, hemorrhoids, urinary disorders, splenic disease, glandular swellings, pain, worms, and abdominal masses.

children.text: siddhaṃ yogaṃ prāha yakṣo mumukṣor bhikṣoḥ prāṇān māṇibhadraḥ kilemam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇibhadra</s> the <s>yakṣa</s> is said to have taught this perfected formula for a mendicant seeking liberation.
<s>bhūnimba</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>triphala</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and the two <s>kaṇās</s>,
<s>mūrvā</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, the two <s>niśās</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, bitter <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
and <s>kaliṅga</s> and <s>vacā</s>, equal in amount, with each following item twice the preceding one:
one should lick these powdered with <s>dantī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and <s>brāhmī</s>, with honey and ghee.
That medicine is supreme for <s>kuṣṭha</s>, urinary disorders, and numbness.
Or he should lick <s>varā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇā</s> with oil, ghee, and honey.
A decoction of <s>vṛkṣaka</s> containing the paste of <s>kākodumbarikā</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>abdā</s>, and <s>vyoṣa</s>,
when drunk, destroys all skin diseases.
In a decoction of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>nṛpataru</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>asana</s>, and <s>saptaparṇa</s>,
one should eat <s>abhayā</s> fruits cooked with honey and ghee; they destroy <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
A bark decoction of <s>dārvī</s>, <s>khadira</s>, and <s>nimba</s> destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
A decoction is made with <s>niśottamā</s>, neem, <s>paṭola</s> root, bitter drugs, <s>vacā</s>, red ochre, and <s>yaṣṭikā</s>;

children.text: kṛtaḥ kaṣāyaḥ kaphapittakuṣṭhaṃ susevito dharma ivocchinatti ||
children.translated_text: when properly used, it cuts off <s>kapha</s>- and <s>pitta</s>-type <s>kuṣṭha</s>, as <s>dharma</s> cuts off evil.

children.text: ebhireva ca śṛtaṃ ghṛtam ukhyaṃ bheṣajair jayati mārutakuṣṭham
children.translated_text: Ghee cooked with these very medicines is declared to conquer <s>māruta</s>-type <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
In the same way, one should separately prepare medicines with <s>khadira</s>, neem, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and the two <s>rajanī</s> herbs.
Urine mixed with <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>vahni</s>, <s>ghuṇeṣṭā</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and <s>indrayava</s>, or warm water,

children.text: kuṣṭhī pītvā māsam aruk syād gudakīlī mehī śophī pāṇḍurajīrṇī kṛmimāṃśca ||
children.translated_text: when drunk for a month by one with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, makes him free from sores; it also benefits one with hemorrhoids, <s>prameha</s>, swelling, pallor, indigestion, and worms.

A powder is made from <s>lākṣā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>madhurasa</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>dvīpī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>pratyakpuṣpī</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s> herbs, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, and <s>aṭarūṣa</s>,

children.text: raktā nimbaṃ surataru kṛtaṃ pañcamūlyau ca cūrṇaṃ pītvā māsaṃ jayati hitabhug gavyamūtreṇa kuṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: with red arsenic, neem, <s>surataru</s>, and the two sets of five roots; drunk for a month with cow's urine by one eating wholesome food, it conquers <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
<s>Niśā</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, dry ginger, <s>vella</s>, <s>tauvara</s>, together with <s>vahni</s> and <s>tāpya</s>, are increased successively,

children.text: gavāmbupītaṃ vaṭakīkṛtaṃ tathā nihanti kuṣṭhāni sudāruṇānyapi ||
children.translated_text: made into pills and drunk with cow's urine; in that form they destroy even very severe kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
A pill prepared from <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>uttamā</s>, sesame, <s>aruṣkara</s>, ghee, honey, and sugar candy

children.text: guṭikā rasāyanaṃ kuṣṭhajicca vṛṣyā ca saptasamā ||
children.translated_text: is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenant), conquers <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and is aphrodisiac for seven years.
Pills made with <s>candraśakalā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>rajanī</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>tuvara</s> seed, <s>aruṣkara</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>,
apparently mixed with a portion of jaggery, when habitually used, destroy all kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
A bolus of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, good <s>dvīpī</s>, boar-like <s>harītakī</s>,
together with <s>lāṅgalī</s>, black sesame, <s>opakulyā</s>, and jaggery, destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
A licked preparation containing <s>śaśāṅkalekhā</s>, the essence of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>hutāśamūla</s>,

children.text: sāyomalā sāmalakā satailā kuṣṭhāni kṛcchrāṇi nihanti līḍhā ||
children.translated_text: with iron slag, <s>āmalaka</s>, and oil, destroys difficult kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> when it is licked.
A bolus made from <s>pathyā</s>, sesame, and jaggery, with <s>aruṣkara</s>, conquers <s>kuṣṭha</s>,
or one made from jaggery, <s>aruṣkara</s>, <s>jantughna</s>, and <s>somarājī</s> does so.
A <s>khadira</s> powder containing <s>viḍaṅga</s>, mountain resin, honey, and ghee,
eaten by one who keeps to moderate, wholesome food, destroys <s>kiṭibha</s>, <s>śvitra</s>, and <s>dadrū</s>.
One who licks sugar, oil, worm-destroying drugs, <s>dhātrī</s>, iron slag, and <s>pippalī</s>
conquers all kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, even those that are extremely grave.

children.text: mustaṃ vyoṣaṃ triphalā mañjiṣṭhā dāru pañcamūle dve
children.translated_text: <s>Musta</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>dāru</s>, the two groups of five roots,
<s>saptacchada</s>, neem bark, <s>viśālā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>mūrvā</s>
are made into a powder, combined with nine parts of <s>tarpaṇa</s> and an equal part of honey.
Regularly eaten, this practical preparation removes <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
It destroys swelling with pallor, <s>śvitra</s>, derangement of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, hemorrhoids,
scrotal swelling, fistula, eruptions, itching, wheals, and glandular swellings.
In a <s>rasāyana</s> regimen one should habitually use <s>tuvara</s> seeds,
<s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>vākucikā</s>, <s>vahnimūla</s>, and what is called <s>śilā</s>.

children.text: iti doṣe vijite 'ntastvaksthe śamanaṃ bahiḥ pralepādi hitam
children.translated_text: Thus, when the internal <s>doṣa</s> lodged in the skin has been conquered, pacifying treatment is useful externally, such as applications of pastes.

children.text: tīkṣṇālepotkliṣṭaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ hi vivṛddhim eti maline dehe ||
children.translated_text: For <s>kuṣṭha</s> aggravated by sharp applications increases in an impure body.
For kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> with firm, hard circular patches, sweating with boluses is beneficial.

children.text: svinnotsannaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ śastrair likhitaṃ pralepanair limpet ||
children.translated_text: When the raised <s>kuṣṭha</s> has been sweated, it should be scraped with instruments and smeared with pastes.

children.text: yeṣu na śastraṃ kramate sparśendriyanāśaneṣu kuṣṭheṣu
children.translated_text: In those cases of <s>kuṣṭha</s> where the instrument does not work because the sense of touch has been destroyed,

children.text: teṣu nipātyaḥ kṣāro raktaṃ doṣaṃ ca visrāvya ||
children.translated_text: alkali should be applied after letting out blood and the <s>doṣa</s>.

children.text: lepo 'tikaṭhinaparuṣe supte kuṣṭhe sthire purāṇe ca
children.translated_text: In very hard, rough, numb, fixed, and chronic <s>kuṣṭha</s>, a paste should be applied
with poisons, after the patient has drunk antidote, accompanied by mantra, and followed by antidotes.
Kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> that are rigid, intensely numb, without sweating, and itchy
should be rubbed with dry cow-dung, foam, and instruments, and then smeared.

children.text: mustā triphalā madanaṃ karañja āragvadhaḥ kaliṅgayavāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Musta</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, and <s>kaliṅgayava</s>,
with <s>saptāhva</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, and white mustard, make a bath.

children.text: eṣa kaṣāyo vamanaṃ virecanaṃ varṇakas tathodgharṣaḥ
children.translated_text: This decoction serves for emesis, purgation, restoring complexion, and rubbing,
and it overcomes skin blemishes, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and swelling, and destroys <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.
From the roots of oleander, neem, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
a decoction in urine, thick enough to coat a ladle, destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> when used as a paste.
A paste made from the root of white oleander, the fruit of <s>kuṭaja</s> and <s>karañja</s>, the bark of <s>dārvī</s>,
and shoots of jasmine is established as removing <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Bark and flowers of <s>śirīṣa</s>, cotton plant, leaves of <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>,

children.text: piṣṭā ca kākamācī caturvidhaḥ kuṣṭhahā lepaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and pounded <s>kākamācī</s> make four kinds of paste that remove <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
With <s>vyoṣa</s>, mustard, <s>niśā</s>, house soot, barley awns, salt, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>,
a superior paste made as pills of the size of a jujube, with half a portion of poison, removes <s>śvitra</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: nimbaṃ haridre surasaṃ paṭolaṃ kuṣṭhāśvagandhe suradāru śigruḥ
children.translated_text: Neem, the two <s>haridrā</s> herbs, <s>surasa</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, <s>śigru</s>,

children.text: sasarṣapaṃ tumburudhānyavanyaṃ caṇḍā ca cūrṇāni samāni kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: with mustard, <s>tumburu</s>, coriander, wild plants, and <s>caṇḍā</s>, should be made into equal powders.

children.text: tais takrapiṣṭaiḥ prathamaṃ śarīraṃ tailāktam udvartayituṃ yateta
children.translated_text: With these, ground in buttermilk, one should first try to rub down the body after it has been anointed with oil.

children.text: tathāsya kaṇḍūḥ piṭikāḥ sakoṭhāḥ kuṣṭhāni śophāśca śamaṃ vrajanti ||
children.translated_text: Then that person's itching, eruptions with wheals, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and swellings come to pacification.
<s>Musta</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>āsaṅga</s>, <s>kaṭaṅkaṭerī</s>, green vitriol, <s>kampillaka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>lodhra</s>,
fragrant stone, <s>sarjarasa</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>manaḥśilā</s>, and the bark of oleander
should be made into powders and applied as dusting powder to a body that has been anointed with oil.

children.text: dadrūḥ sakaṇḍūḥ kiṭibhāni pāmā vicarcikā ceti tathā na santi ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>dadrū</s> with itching, <s>kiṭibha</s>, <s>pāmā</s>, and <s>vicarcikā</s> cease to exist.
A paste of mustard cooked in the fire of chaff on a swollen <s>snuhī</s> stem

children.text: lepād vicarcikāṃ hanti rāgavega iva trapām ||
children.translated_text: destroys <s>vicarcikā</s> by application, just as the force of passion destroys shame.

children.text: manaḥśilāle maricāni tailam ārkaṃ payaḥ kuṣṭhaharaḥ pradehaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s>, <s>āla</s>, peppers, oil, <s>arka</s> latex, and milk make an application that removes <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Likewise, <s>karañja</s> and <s>prapunāṭa</s> seeds, together with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, are ground with cow's urine.
With <s>guggulu</s>, pepper, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, mustard, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>sarjarasa</s>, and <s>mustā</s>,
with <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, <s>alagandha</s>, <s>manaḥśilā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>kampilla</s>,
and with both kinds of turmeric, when these are mixed with <s>cakrika</s> oil

children.text: dinakarakarābhitaptaiḥ kuṣṭhaṃ ghṛṣṭaṃ ca naṣṭaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and heated by the rays of the sun, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, when rubbed with them, is destroyed and disappears.
Pepper, <s>tamāla</s> leaf, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, together with <s>manaḥśilā</s> and <s>kāsīsa</s>,

children.text: tailena yuktam uṣitaṃ saptāhaṃ bhājane tāmre ||
children.translated_text: mixed with oil and kept for seven days in a copper vessel:
<s>sidhma</s> anointed with that goes away after seven days in one who takes heat treatment,

children.text: māsān navaṃ kilāsaṃ snānena vinā viśuddhasya ||
children.translated_text: and new <s>kilāsa</s> after a month in one who has been purified, without bathing.
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> oil cooked in water filtered seven times through <s>mayūraka</s> alkali
destroys <s>sidhma</s> when used for anointing.
The root of <s>vāyasajaṅghā</s>, leaves of <s>vamanī</s>, and seed from radish,
made into a paste with buttermilk on a Tuesday, is known as effective for removing <s>sidhma</s>.

children.text: jīvantī mañjiṣṭhā dārvī kampillakaṃ payas tuttham
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>kampillaka</s>, milk, and <s>tuttha</s>:

children.text: eṣa ghṛtatailapākaḥ siddhaḥ siddhe ca sarjarasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this preparation of ghee and oil is cooked, and when it is ready, <s>sarjarasa</s>

children.text: deyaḥ samadhūcchiṣṭo vipādikā tena naśyati hyaktā
children.translated_text: should be added along with honey and beeswax; <s>vipādikā</s>, when smeared with it, is indeed destroyed.
<s>Carma</s>, <s>ekakuṣṭha</s>, <s>kiṭibha</s>, and <s>alasaka</s> also become pacified.

children.text: mūlaṃ saptāhvāt tvak śirīṣāśvamārād arkān mālatyāścitrakāsphotanimbāt
children.translated_text: The roots of <s>saptāhvā</s>, the barks of <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>aśvamāra</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>āsphoṭa</s>, and <s>nimba</s>,

children.text: bījaṃ kārañjaṃ sārṣapaṃ prāpunāṭam śreṣṭhā jantughnaṃ tryūṣaṇaṃ dve haridre ||
children.translated_text: the seeds of <s>karañja</s>, mustard, and <s>prapunāṭa</s>, <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>jantughna</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and the two turmerics:

children.text: tailaṃ tailaṃ sādhitaṃ taiḥ samūtrais tvagdoṣāṇāṃ duṣṭanāḍīvraṇānām
children.translated_text: oil cooked with these together with urine is sufficient, by anointing, for the destruction of skin disorders, foul sinus wounds,
and conditions arising from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>vāta</s>; it is <s>vajraka</s>, as powerful as a thunderbolt.
With <s>eraṇḍa</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, <s>ghana</s>, <s>nīpa</s>, <s>kadamba</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>kampilla</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, and <s>suravāruṇī</s>,
with <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>aruṣkara</s>, <s>surāhva</s>, <s>suvarṇadugdhā</s>, <s>śrīveṣṭa</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, <s>śilā</s>, salt, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>viśva</s>,
and with equal quantities of the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, the cooked oil is remembered as <s>mahāvajra</s>.
It has properties surpassing <s>vajraka</s> and destroys <s>śvitra</s>, hemorrhoids, and glandular swellings.
Oil cooked with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>aśvamāra</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>arka</s>, urine, <s>snuhī</s> latex, and rock salt

children.text: tailaṃ siddhaṃ viṣāpaham abhyaṅgāt kuṣṭhajit param ||
children.translated_text: removes poison and is supreme for conquering <s>kuṣṭha</s> by anointing.
Pungent oil cooked with <s>sikthaka</s>, cinnabar, <s>puratuttha</s>, and substances born of <s>tārkṣya</s>
quickly eradicates <s>kacchū</s> and <s>vicarcikā</s>.

children.text: lākṣā vyoṣaṃ prāpunāṭaṃ ca bījaṃ saśrīveṣṭaṃ kuṣṭhasiddhārthakāśca
children.translated_text: Lac, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>prapunāṭa</s> seed, <s>śrīveṣṭa</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and white mustard,

children.text: takronmiśraḥ syāddharidrā ca lepo dadrūṣūkto mūlakotthaṃ ca bījam ||
children.translated_text: together with turmeric mixed with buttermilk, form a paste for ringworm; radish seed is also prescribed there.
<s>Citraka</s>, <s>śobhāñjana</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,

children.text: khadiro dhavaśca lepaḥ śyāmā dantī dravantī ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>khadira</s> and <s>dhava</s>, and also <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>dravantī</s>, are pastes.
Lac, <s>rasāñjana</s>, cardamom, and <s>punarnavā</s> are also pastes for those with <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Mixed with curd whey in quarter portions, six such pastes are taught as destroying <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
Water plants, <s>vāpya</s>, iron, saffron filaments, leaves, floating plants, sandalwood, and lotus fibers,
in successively increasing parts, make a prepared ointment for <s>kuṣṭha</s> dominated by <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
In cases of burning <s>kuṣṭha</s>, anointing should be done with bitter ghees and washed ghees,
and with oils combined with sandalwood, licorice, white lotus, and blue lotus.

children.text: klede prapatati cāṅge dāhe visphoṭake ca carmadale
children.translated_text: When there is moisture, falling away of body parts, burning, blisters, and cracking of the skin,
cool applications and sprinklings, puncturing and purgation, and bitter ghee are indicated.
<s>Khadira</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>kṛmijit</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, and <s>madhuparṇī</s>,
used internally and externally together with cow's urine, remove worms and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
In <s>kuṣṭha</s> where <s>vāta</s> predominates, ghee is used; where <s>śleṣman</s> predominates, emesis is used.
Where <s>pitta</s> predominates, removal of blood and purgation are to be done first.
The pastes for <s>kuṣṭha</s> are applied to those from whom the disorders of blood and <s>doṣa</s> have been removed,
and whose internal channels have been purified; for them there is immediate success.

children.text: doṣe hṛte 'panīte rakte bāhyāntare kṛte śamane
children.translated_text: When the <s>doṣa</s> has been removed, the blood taken away, internal and external pacification performed,

children.text: snehe ca kālayukte na kuṣṭham ativartate sādhyam ||
children.translated_text: and oleation done at the proper time, curable <s>kuṣṭha</s> does not persist.
A <s>kuṣṭhin</s> with many <s>doṣas</s> should be purified repeatedly, while his vital strength is carefully protected.

children.text: doṣe hyatimātrahṛte vāyur hanyād abalam āśu ||
children.translated_text: For if the <s>doṣas</s> are removed in excessive measure, <s>vāyu</s> can quickly kill the weakened person.
He should undergo emesis every fortnight, and downward evacuations month by month.

children.text: śuddhir mūrdhni syāt trirātrāt trirātrāt ṣaṣṭhe ṣaṣṭhe māsyasṛṅmokṣaṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Purification of the head should occur every third night, and bloodletting every sixth month.

children.text: yo durvānto durvirikto 'thavā syāt kuṣṭhī doṣairuddhatair vyāpyate 'sau
children.translated_text: A <s>kuṣṭhin</s> who has been improperly vomited or improperly purged is overcome by agitated <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: niḥsaṃdehaṃ yātyasādhyatvam evaṃ tasmāt kṛtsnān nirhared asya doṣān ||
children.translated_text: Without doubt he reaches incurability in this way; therefore all his <s>doṣas</s> should be removed completely.
Devotion to vows, self-restraint, service of observances and disciplines, renunciation, cultivation of good conduct, worship of brahmins, gods, and teachers, and friendliness toward all beings,
and worship of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śivasuta</s>, <s>Tārā</s>, and the sun uproot <s>kuṣṭha</s>, whose impurity and sin have become manifest.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>śvitra</s> and worms.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: kuṣṭhād api bībhatsaṃ yacchīghrataraṃ ca yātyasādhyatvam
children.translated_text: That which is even more repulsive than <s>kuṣṭha</s> and goes more quickly toward incurability

children.text: śvitram atas tacchāntyai yateta dīpte yathā bhavane ||
children.translated_text: is <s>śvitra</s>; therefore one should strive for its pacification as for a house that is blazing.

children.text: saṃśodhanaṃ viśeṣāt prayojayet pūrvam eva dehasya
children.translated_text: Especially one should first apply purification of the body.

children.text: śvitre sraṃsanam agryaṃ malayūrasa iṣyate saguḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>śvitra</s>, the foremost laxative is considered to be <s>malayū</s> juice with jaggery.
After drinking that, with his body anointed, according to his strength he should expose himself to the heat of the sun's rays.

children.text: seveta viriktatanus tryahaṃ pipāsuḥ pibet peyām ||
children.translated_text: With his body purged, for three days, when thirsty, he should drink thin gruel.

children.text: śvitre 'ṅge ye sphoṭā jāyante kaṇṭakena tān bhindyāt
children.translated_text: In <s>śvitra</s> (white leprosy), the blisters that arise on the limb should be pierced with a thorn.

children.text: sphoṭeṣu niḥsruteṣu prātaḥ prātaḥ pibet tridinam ||
children.translated_text: When the blisters have drained, he should drink, morning after morning, for three days:

children.text: malayūm asanaṃ priyaṅguṃ śatapuṣpāṃ cāmbhasā samutkvāthya
children.translated_text: <s>malayū</s>, <s>asana</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, well decocted in water,
or <s>pālāśa</s> alkali, according to his strength, mixed with <s>phāṇita</s>.
Having drunk a paste of <s>indurājikā</s> with a decoction of the bark of <s>phalgu</s> and <s>akṣa</s> trees,

children.text: pītvoṣṇasthitasya jāte sphoṭe takreṇa bhojanaṃ nirlavaṇam ||
children.translated_text: while staying warm, when blisters have appeared, he should take food with buttermilk, without salt.

children.text: gavyaṃ mūtraṃ citrakavyoṣayuktaṃ sarpiḥkumbhe sthāpitaṃ kṣaudramiśram
children.translated_text: Cow urine mixed with <s>citraka</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>, placed in a ghee jar and mixed with honey:

children.text: pakṣād ūrdhvaṃ śvitriṇā peyam etat kāryaṃ cāsmai kuṣṭhadiṣṭaṃ vidhānam ||
children.translated_text: after a fortnight this should be drunk by one with <s>śvitra</s>; for him the procedure prescribed for <s>kuṣṭha</s> should also be performed.

children.text: mārkavam athavā khāded bhṛṣṭaṃ tailena lohapātrastham
children.translated_text: Or he should eat <s>mārkava</s> roasted with oil in an iron vessel,
and then drink milk boiled with <s>bījaka</s>, for the destruction of <s>śvitra</s>.
The shoots of <s>pūtīka</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>vyādhighāta</s>, and <s>snuhī</s>, and those of <s>jāti</s>, ground in urine,
by application destroy <s>śvitra</s>, hemorrhoids, ringworm, scabies, wheals, and corrupt sinus wounds.

children.text: dvaipaṃ dagdhaṃ carma mātaṅgajaṃ vā śvitre lepas tailayukto variṣṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: The burnt hide of a leopard, or of an elephant, made into a paste with oil, is best for <s>śvitra</s>.

children.text: pūtiḥ kīṭo rājavṛkṣodbhavena kṣāreṇāktaḥ śvitram eko 'pi hanti ||
children.translated_text: Even by itself, a foul insect smeared with alkali produced from <s>rājavṛkṣa</s> destroys <s>śvitra</s>.

children.text: rātrau gomūtre vāsitān jarjarāṅgān ahni chāyāyāṃ śoṣayet sphoṭahetūn
children.translated_text: Things that produce blisters, bruised in body, should be soaked at night in cow urine and dried by day in the shade.

children.text: evaṃ vārāṃs trīṃs tais tataḥ ślakṣṇapiṣṭaiḥ snuhyāḥ kṣīreṇa śvitranāśāya lepaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Doing this three times, then grinding them finely with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, makes a paste for destroying <s>śvitra</s>.
A paste of soot produced from a black snake, liquefied with <s>akṣa</s> oil,

children.text: śikhipittaṃ tathā dagdhaṃ hrīveraṃ vā tadāplutam ||
children.translated_text: or peacock bile, and likewise burnt <s>hrīvera</s> soaked in it, may be used.
A <s>kuḍava</s> of <s>avalguja</s> seed, mixed with a quarter part of <s>haritāla</s>,

children.text: mūtreṇa gavāṃ piṣṭaḥ savarṇakaraṇaṃ paraṃ śvitre ||
children.translated_text: ground with cow urine, is supreme for restoring the natural color in <s>śvitra</s>.

children.text: kṣāre sudagdhe gajaliṇḍaje ca gajasya mūtreṇa parisrute ca
children.translated_text: When alkali from elephant dung has been well burnt and filtered with elephant urine,

children.text: droṇapramāṇe daśabhāgayuktaṃ dattvā paced bījam avalgujānām ||
children.translated_text: in a <s>droṇa</s> measure, with a tenth part added, one should add seed of <s>avalguja</s> and cook it.

children.text: śvitraṃ jayeccikkaṇatāṃ gatena tena pralimpan bahuśaḥ praghṛṣṭaṃ
children.translated_text: When it has become sticky, by repeatedly smearing it on well-scraped <s>śvitra</s>, one may overcome the disease,

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ maṣaṃ vā tilakālakaṃ vā yad vā vraṇe syād adhimāṃsajātam ||
children.translated_text: whether it is <s>kuṣṭha</s>, a mole, a black spot, or excess flesh arising in a wound.
<s>Bhallātaka</s>, the roots of <s>dvīpī</s>, <s>sudhā</s>, and <s>arka</s>, <s>guñjā</s> fruit, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and conch powder,

children.text: tutthaṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ lavaṇāni pañca kṣāradvayaṃ lāṅgalikāṃ ca paktvā ||
children.translated_text: <s>tuttha</s> with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, the five salts, the two alkalis, and <s>lāṅgalikā</s> should be cooked

children.text: snugarkadugdhe ghanam āyasasthaṃ śalākayā tad vidadhīta lepam
children.translated_text: in the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, in an iron vessel, until thick; with an iron rod one should make it into a paste.

children.text: kuṣṭhe kilāse tilakālakeṣu maṣeṣu durnāmasu carmakīle ||
children.translated_text: It is used on <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kilāsa</s>, black spots, moles, hemorrhoids, and skin tags.
Through purification, bloodletting, drying regimens, and the eating of parched meal,
<s>śvitra</s> subsides only in someone whose evil karma has been exhausted.
In abdominal worms, after oleation and sweating with jaggery, milk, fish, and the like,
when the worms and <s>kapha</s> have been stirred up, and after that night has been comfortably passed,
one should decoct the <s>surasādi</s> group in urine until half the water remains.
That decoction, combined with a paste of <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>agāla</s>, and <s>kṛmijit</s>,
together with oil and <s>svarjikākṣāra</s>, should then be administered as an enema on the following day.

children.text: tasminn eva nirūḍhaṃ taṃ pāyayeta virecanam ||
children.translated_text: On that very day, when he has been given a decoction enema, one should make him drink a purgative:
paste of <s>trivṛt</s>, stirred in a decoction of <s>phala</s> and <s>kaṇā</s>.
Then, when he has been cleansed above and below, one should carry out a regimen containing <s>pañcakola</s>.
There should be sprinkling with decoctions of substances that are pungent, bitter, and astringent,
and, at the proper time, one should then give him an oil enema with <s>viḍaṅga</s> oil.
For worms located in the head, one should apply the procedure taught in the treatment of head diseases,
and food should be predominantly bitter and pungent, with little unctuousness.
With <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, black pepper, root of long pepper, and <s>śigru</s>,
and with <s>svarjikākṣāra</s>, he should drink gruel cooked in buttermilk.
He should drink the juice separately from <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>kiṇihī</s>, <s>pāribhadra</s>, and <s>kembuka</s>,
or separately from <s>palāśa</s> seed, <s>pattūra</s>, or <s>pūtikā</s>.

children.text: sakṣaudraṃ surasādīn vā lihyāt kṣaudrayutān pṛthak
children.translated_text: Or he should lick the <s>surasādi</s> substances separately, mixed with honey.
A person with worms should lick, with honey, horse-dung powder that has been impregnated one hundred times with a decoction of <s>viḍaṅga</s>,

children.text: kṛmimān madhunā lihyād bhāvitaṃ vā varārasaiḥ
children.translated_text: or powder impregnated with the juices of <s>varā</s> and the like.

children.text: śirogateṣu kṛmiṣu cūrṇaṃ pradhamanaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: For worms in the head, that same powder is also to be used as an insufflation.
With shoots of <s>ākhukarṇī</s>, well ground and mixed with flour,

children.text: paktvā pūpalikāṃ khādeddhānyāmlaṃ ca pibed anu ||
children.translated_text: one should cook small cakes and eat them, and afterward drink sour grain gruel.
Or he may drink thin buttermilk with <s>pañcakola</s> and salt.
The same procedure applies also with shoots of <s>nīpa</s>, <s>mārkava</s>, and <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
Or one should prepare foods from doughs mixed with <s>viḍaṅga</s> powder.
<s>Āruṣkara</s> oil, joined with grains of <s>viḍaṅga</s> in half measure and kept in the sun,

children.text: dinam āruṣkaraṃ tailaṃ pāne vastau ca yojayet
children.translated_text: for one day, should be used for drinking and for enema.
In the same way one should separately prepare oils from <s>surāhva</s> and <s>sarala</s> resin.
For worms born from feces, one should especially give enemas and purgatives.
For those born from <s>kapha</s>, head-purgation, emesis, and palliative treatment are used.
For those born from blood, one should perform the remedy from the treatment of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
And for those that eat the hair, the procedure for <s>indralupta</s> is to be applied here.

children.text: kṣīrāṇi māṃsāni ghṛtaṃ guḍaṃ ca dadhīni śākāni ca parṇavanti
children.translated_text: One who wishes to get rid of worms should avoid milks, meats, ghee, jaggery,

children.text: samāsato 'mlān madhurān rasāṃśca kṛmīñ jihāsuḥ parivarjayeta ||
children.translated_text: curds, leafy vegetables, and, in brief, sour and sweet tastes.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>vāta</s> disorders.
Thus spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
At the outset one should treat pure <s>vāyu</s>, unobstructed by any support, with oleating substances,
and then the patient with drinks of ghee, animal fat, marrow, and oil.
When he has become weary from oleation, one should let him recover, and again oleate him with milk,
with soups, or with the juices of domestic, aquatic, and marsh-dwelling animals, combined with <s>sneha</s>.
One should also use milk-rice and <s>kṛsara</s>, with sour and salty ingredients, and with oil enemas,
with nasal therapies, nourishing measures, and very unctuous foods; after that one should induce sweating.
The patient should be well anointed again and again with oily preparations such as <s>śaṃkara</s> and the like.

children.text: snehāktaṃ svinnam aṅgaṃ tu vakraṃ stabdhaṃ savedanam ||
children.translated_text: For a limb that is oiled and sweated, even if crooked, stiff, and painful,

children.text: yatheṣṭam ānāmayituṃ sukham eva hi śakyate
children.translated_text: can very easily be bent as desired.
Even dry pieces of wood, when treated with oleation and sweating,

children.text: śakyaṃ karmaṇyatāṃ netuṃ kimu gātrāṇi jīvatām
children.translated_text: can be brought into workability; how much more the limbs of living beings?
Tingling, pricking pain, ache, tension, swelling, stiffness, constriction, and the like
quickly subside in one who has been sweated, and softness also arises.
And <s>sneha</s>, when applied, quickly nourishes the dried-up <s>dhātus</s>,
and increases his strength, digestive power, nourishment, and vital breaths.

children.text: asakṛt taṃ punaḥ snehaiḥ svedaiśca pratipādayet ||
children.translated_text: One should repeatedly bring him under treatment with oleations and sweatings,
for when the alimentary tract is softened by <s>sneha</s>, diseases of <s>anila</s> do not remain there.
If, because it is accompanied by <s>doṣa</s>, it is not pacified by this procedure,
one should purify him with mild medicines combined with <s>sneha</s>.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tilvakasiddhaṃ vā sātalāsiddham eva vā ||
children.translated_text: He may drink ghee prepared with <s>tilvaka</s>, or else ghee prepared with <s>sātalā</s>,
or castor oil with milk, auspicious and removing the <s>doṣas</s>.
For fecal matter accumulated by unctuous, sour, salty, hot, and similar foods

children.text: sroto baddhvānilaṃ rundhyāt tasmāt tam anulomayet
children.translated_text: blocks the channels and obstructs <s>anila</s>; therefore one should direct it downward.
A weak person who is not fit for purgation should be treated with decoction enemas,

children.text: dīpanaiḥ pācanīyair vā bhojyair vā tadyutair naram
children.translated_text: or with appetizing and digestive medicines, or with foods combined with those.
When he has been purified and the digestive fire has risen, oleation and sweating are again beneficial.
When <s>vāyu</s> is located in the stomach, after emesis and after the patient has been fed again,
one should administer <s>Ṣaḍdharaṇa</s>, or the <s>Vacādi</s> preparation, with warm water.
When the digestive fire has been kindled, the subsequent procedure is that for a purely <s>vātika</s> condition.
When it is situated in the region of the navel, fish cooked with <s>bilva</s> and unripe <s>bilva</s> fruits are prescribed;
below the navel, enema treatment is praised, as is <s>avapīḍaka</s>.
When it is in the alimentary tract, alkaline powders and the like, which digest and kindle appetite, are beneficial.
When it is in the heart, milk cooked with <s>sthirā</s> is beneficial; when it is in the head, a head-enema is used.

children.text: snaihikaṃ nāvanaṃ dhūmaḥ śrotrādīnāṃ ca tarpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Oleating nasal medication, fumigation, and nourishment of the ears and other sense organs are prescribed.
When it is lodged in the skin, sweating, massage, protection from wind, and agreeable food are beneficial.
When it is in the blood, cooling applications, purgation, and bloodletting are prescribed.
When it is in flesh and fat, purgation, decoction enema, and pacifying measures are used.
When it has entered bone and marrow, one should conquer it by external and internal oleations.
When it is in semen, delight and food that produces strength and semen are beneficial.

children.text: vibaddhamārgaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu śukraṃ dadyād virecanam ||
children.translated_text: But when one sees that the pathway of semen is obstructed, one should give purgation.

children.text: viriktaṃ pratibhuktaṃ ca pūrvoktāṃ kārayet kriyām
children.translated_text: After the patient has been purged and fed again, one should perform the procedure stated earlier.

children.text: garbhe śuṣke tu vātena bālānāṃ ca viśuṣyatām ||
children.translated_text: For a fetus dried up by <s>vāta</s>, and for children who are wasting away,
milk cooked with sugar, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and <s>madhuka</s> is for raising them up.
When it has reached the tendons, joints, and vessels, oleation, cauterization, and poulticing are used.
When there is contraction, massage should be done with oil cooked with black gram and rock salt.
When blood has flowed, a paste of house soot, salt, and oil should be applied.
For a numb limb that is constricted by bandaging, poulticing should be done.
Now, one afflicted by <s>apatanaka</s>, whose eyes have not drooped and who is without tremor,
whose penis is not stiff, who is without sweat, and who is free from outward arching,
and who does not strike against the bed, should be treated quickly.
There, first of all, when his limbs have been well oleated and sweated, sharp nasal medication
should be employed to purify the channels; after that he should drink clear ghee.
It should be cooked with decoction of the <s>Vidāryādi</s> group, curd, milk, and meat juices.

children.text: nātimātraṃ tathā vāyur vyāpnoti sahasaiva vā ||
children.translated_text: It should not be in excessive quantity; in that way <s>vāyu</s> does not spread suddenly.
One should decoct horse gram, barley, jujube, and the <s>Bhadradārvādi</s> group,
together with the meat of marsh-dwelling animals, and with sour liquids and also milk.
Adding a counter-ingredient from the sweet group, one should cook a <s>mahāsneha</s>.
Administered through sprinkling, massage, immersion baths, food, drink, nasal therapy, and oil enema,

children.text: sa hanti vātaṃ te te ca snehasvedāḥ suyojitāḥ
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>vāta</s>; and those oleations and sweatings, when well applied, do the same.
Between attacks one should repeatedly purge his head
with sharp <s>avapīḍa</s> and <s>pradhamana</s> nasal therapies that remove phlegm.

children.text: śvasanāsu vimuktāsu tathā saṃjñāṃ sa vindati
children.translated_text: When the breathing passages have been freed, he thereby regains consciousness.
When mobile <s>vāta</s> is excessive, ghee prepared with <s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, and <s>vyoṣa</s> is used.

children.text: palāṣṭakaṃ tilvakato varāyāḥ prasthaṃ palāṃśaṃ gurupañcamūlam
children.translated_text: One should take eight palas of <s>tilvaka</s>, a prastha of <s>varā</s>, one pala each of the heavy five roots,

children.text: sairaṇḍasiṃhītrivṛtaṃ ghaṭe 'pāṃ paktvā pacet pādaśṛtena tena ||
children.translated_text: with castor, <s>siṃhī</s>, and <s>trivṛt</s>, boil them in a jar of water, and, when a quarter remains, cook with that decoction

children.text: dadhnaḥ pātre yāvaśūkāt tribilvaiḥ sarpiḥprasthaṃ hanti tat sevyamānam
children.translated_text: a prastha of ghee in a vessel of curd, with barley awns and three <s>bilvas</s>; when used, it destroys
corrupted <s>vātās</s> situated in one limb or the whole body, disorders of the female genital tract, <s>gulma</s>, scrotal swelling, and abdominal enlargement.
The procedure should be understood in the same way as for <s>tilvaka</s> also in the cases of <s>ramyaka</s> and <s>aśoka</s>.
This treatment should be performed in <s>apatanaka</s> caused by pure <s>vāta</s>.
When the <s>doṣas</s> are mixed, a mixed treatment should be used; when <s>kapha</s> is involved, after powdering
<s>tumburu</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, asafoetida, <s>pauṣkara</s>, and the three salts,
one should drink them with barley-decoction water in heart and flank pain and in <s>apatantraka</s>.
Or one may drink asafoetida, <s>sauvarcala</s>, dry ginger, pomegranate, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
and what has been taught for heart disease due to <s>śleṣma</s> and <s>pavana</s> is also recommended.
For the two kinds of <s>āyāma</s>, external and internal, the treatment is as for <s>ardita</s>;
one should also lie in a vat of oil. Of these, the internal form is very difficult to overcome.
A patient whose teeth and face are discolored, whose limbs hang loose, whose consciousness is lost,
and who sweats while suffering from <s>dhanuskambha</s>, does not live for ten nights.
If the attacks are otherwise, and mild, he may live, but bent, dull-witted,
lame, with a contracted arm, hemiplegic, crippled, or otherwise impaired.
When the jaw has slipped, the jaws, after being oiled and sweated, should be brought back to their proper place.
A skilled physician should raise the chin when the mouth is open,
and bend it down when it is closed; the remaining treatment should be done as for <s>ekāyāma</s>.
In stiffness of the tongue, treatment for <s>vāta</s> should be carried out according to the condition.
In <s>ardita</s>, there should be nasal instillation, oil on the head, and nourishing treatment for the ears and eyes.
When there is swelling, emesis is used; when burning and redness are present, venesection is used.
In <s>pakṣāghāta</s>, oleation joined with oleaginous substances and then purgation are useful.
In <s>avabāhu</s>, nasal therapy is beneficial, as is an oily drink taken after meals.

children.text: ūrustambhe tu na sneho na ca saṃśodhanaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: But in <s>ūrustambha</s>, oleation is not beneficial, nor is evacuative purification.
Because kapha, <s>āma</s>, and fat are abundant, measures that reduce them should therefore be applied judiciously.
One should use dry treatment, and barley, <s>śyāmāka</s> millet, and <s>kodrava</s> millet
are recommended with unsalted greens, a little oil, and water boiled with them.
The patient should drink honey-water and <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and eat meat of wild animals without ghee.
<s>Vatsakādi</s>, <s>haridrādi</s>, or <s>vacādi</s>, together with rock salt,
should be drunk with warm water in <s>āḍhyavāta</s>, or else <s>ṣaḍdharaṇa</s> should be used.
Or he should lick with honey a paste made from <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and <s>ghana</s>;
or, with honey, a paste produced from <s>cavya</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>suradāru</s>.

children.text: mūtrair vā śīlayet pathyāṃ gugguluṃ girisaṃbhavam ||
children.translated_text: Or he should regularly use <s>pathyā</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, and mountain-born resin with urine.
Eating equal parts of <s>guggulu</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>,
one conquers all diseases born from fat, kapha, <s>āma</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.
In this way the wind-principle, when overrun by kapha and accompanied by fat, is pacified.
One should apply fomentations, affusions, and dry rubbings combined with alkali and urine.
One should also smear him with <s>karañja</s> fruits and mustard, rich in urine,
or with roots of <s>arka</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, and neem, together with <s>surāhva</s>.
These may be combined with honey, mustard, baked brick powder, and earth from an anthill.
For the sake of reducing kapha, one should also set him to exercise when he can bear it.
He should cross stretches of dry land and, according to his strength, have intercourse with women.

children.text: sthiratoyaṃ saraḥ kṣemaṃ pratisroto nadīṃ taret ||
children.translated_text: He should swim across a safe pond of still water and a river against the current.
When kapha and fat have been reduced in this condition, one should introduce oleation and the other therapies.
For the remaining disorders also, treatment should be undertaken after considering the site, the affected tissues, and the other factors.

children.text: sahacaraṃ suradāru sanāgaraṃ kvathitam ambhasi tailavimiśritam
children.translated_text: If one drinks <s>sahacara</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>, decocted in water and mixed with oil,
then, though the movement of the body has been afflicted by <s>vāta</s>, one becomes able to go quickly or slowly at will.
One should grind <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>mahauṣadha</s>, <s>dvīpī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
and cook ghee with them; it is the supreme remover of vāta diseases.

children.text: nimbāmṛtāvṛṣapaṭolanidigdhikānāṃ bhāgān pṛthak daśa palān vipaced ghaṭe 'pām
children.translated_text: One should separately cook ten-pala portions of neem, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, and <s>nidigdhikā</s> in a jar of water.

children.text: aṣṭāṃśaśeṣitarasena punaśca tena prasthaṃ ghṛtasya vipacet picubhāgakalkaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the decoction has been reduced to one eighth, one should again cook one <s>prastha</s> of ghee with it and with paste ingredients in <s>picu</s> portions.
These are <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, <s>gajopakulyā</s>, the two alkalis, <s>nāgara</s>, <s>niśā</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>cavya</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>,
together with <s>tejovatī</s>, <s>marica</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>dīpyaka</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>aruṣkara</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and the root of <s>kaṇā</s>.
There should also be <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>viṣā</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, and five purified pala-portions of <s>guggulu</s>.

children.text: tat sevitaṃ vidhamati prabalaṃ samīraṃ saṃdhyasthimajjagatam apyatha kuṣṭham īdṛk ||
children.translated_text: When taken, this preparation scatters powerful <s>samīra</s> (vāta), even when lodged in the joints, bones, and marrow, and also such <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
It also removes sinus ulcers, tumors, fistulas, glandular swellings, all disorders above the clavicle, abdominal masses, rectal disorders, and <s>meha</s>,
as well as consumption, loss of appetite, dyspnea, chronic rhinitis, cough, swelling, heart disease, anemia, intoxication, abscess, and <s>vātarakta</s>.
In milk decocted with <s>balā</s> and <s>bilva</s>, one should cook the scum of ghee.

children.text: tasya śuktiḥ prakuñco vā nasyaṃ vāte śirogate ||
children.translated_text: A <s>śukti</s> or a <s>prakuñca</s> of it is nasal therapy when <s>vāta</s> is located in the head.
In the same way, fat obtained from crocodile, fish, tortoise, and owl should be prepared.
It should be used especially when <s>mātariśvan</s> (vāta) is unmixed.

children.text: jīrṇaṃ piṇyākaṃ pañcamūlaṃ pṛthak ca kvāthyaṃ kvāthābhyām ekatas tailam ābhyām
children.translated_text: Having separately decocted old oil-cake and <s>pañcamūla</s>, one should cook oil with both decoctions together,

children.text: kṣīrād aṣṭāṃśaṃ pācayet tena pānād vātā naśyeyuḥ śleṣmayuktā viśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: using an eighth part of milk; by drinking it, vāta disorders perish, especially those joined with kapha.
In a decoction of a <s>tulā</s> of <s>prasāriṇī</s>, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil with an equal amount of milk,
using pastes of the two <s>medā</s> herbs, <s>miśi</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>kucandana</s>.
The paste should also include <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, the pair of <s>kākolī</s> herbs, and <s>amaradāru</s>.
All of it should be cooked; it destroys every disease of <s>māruta</s> (vāta).
One should take a <s>tulā</s> of <s>sahacara</s>, complete with root and branches, together with <s>daśamūla</s>,

children.text: palāni pañcāśad abhīrutaśca pādāvaśeṣaṃ vipaced vahe 'pām ||
children.translated_text: and fifty palas of <s>abhīru</s>, and cook them in a <s>vāha</s> of water until one quarter remains.
In that decoction, with one-pala portions of <s>sevya</s>, <s>nakha</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>hima</s>, <s>elā</s>, <s>spṛk</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>nalikā</s>, <s>ambu</s>, and <s>śilāja</s>,
and with <s>lohita</s>, <s>analada</s>, <s>loha</s>, <s>surāhva</s>, <s>kopanā</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>turuṣka</s>, and <s>nata</s>,

children.text: tulyakṣīraṃ pālikais tailapātraṃ siddhaṃ kṛcchrāñchīlitaṃ hanti vātān
children.translated_text: one should prepare a vessel of oil with an equal quantity of milk. When perfected and regularly used, it destroys difficult vāta disorders,
including those marked by tremor, convulsion, stiffness, wasting, and the like, as well as abdominal masses, insanity, chronic rhinitis, and diseases of the female genital tract.
Or, in the juice of a <s>tulā</s> of <s>sahacara</s>, one should cook an <s>āḍhaka</s> of oil,
adding ten palas of root paste and four times as much milk.
Or else the paste may be made from <s>nata</s>, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>surāhva</s>,
together with <s>elā</s>, <s>nalada</s>, <s>śaileya</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, and red sandalwood.
When this is cooked, one should add eighteen palas of powdered sugar,

children.text: bheḍasya saṃmataṃ tailaṃ tat kṛcchrān anilāmayān ||
children.translated_text: and the oil approved by <s>Bheḍa</s>; that oil conquers difficult disorders of <s>anila</s> (<s>vāta</s>),
such as <s>vātakuṇḍalikā</s>, insanity, abdominal tumors, scrotal swellings, and the like.
One hundred palas of <s>balā</s>, a quarter part of <s>chinnaruhā</s>, and <s>rāsnā</s> in an eighth part
should be boiled in one hundred āḍhakas of water, until the decoction remains as a hundredth part.
With curd-whey, sugarcane extract, and sour fermented liquid, and with an āḍhaka of oil in equal portions,
one should cook it, together with half as much goat's milk, using these pastes measured by the pala:
<s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, cardamom, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and sandalwood;
<s>padmaka</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>, and <s>hareṇu</s>;
licorice, <s>surasā</s>, <s>vyāghranakha</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>;
<s>palāśa</s> resin, musk, <s>nalikā</s>, and nutmeg husks;
<s>spṛkkā</s>, saffron, <s>śaileya</s>, jasmine, <s>kaṭuphala</s>, and <s>ambu</s>;
bark, <s>kunduruka</s>, camphor, <s>turuṣka</s>, and <s>śrīnivāsaka</s>;
clove, <s>nakha</s>, <s>kaṅkola</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>;
<s>sthauṇeya</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>dhyāma</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>madanaka</s>, and <s>plava</s>,
together with <s>nāgakesara</s>. When it is cooked and removed from the fire, one should add here

children.text: pattrakalkaṃ tataḥ pūtaṃ vidhinā tat prayojitam
children.translated_text: a paste of leaves; then, after it has been strained, when used according to rule,

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ jvaraṃ chardiṃ mūrchāṃ gulmakṣatakṣayān ||
children.translated_text: it removes cough, dyspnea, fever, vomiting, fainting, abdominal tumors, wasting from injury,
enlargement of the spleen, emaciation, epilepsy, and misfortune.
This excellent <s>balātaila</s> is destructive of diseases of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: pāne nasye 'nvāsane 'bhyañjane ca snehāḥ kāle samyag ete prayuktāḥ
children.translated_text: When these oleations are properly used at the right time for drinking, nasal therapy, oil enema, and massage,

children.text: duṣṭān vātān āśu śāntiṃ nayeyur vandhyā nārīḥ putrabhājaśca kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: they quickly bring vitiated <s>vātas</s> to pacification and make barren women bear sons.

children.text: snehasvedair drutaḥ śleṣmā yadā pakvāśaye sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>śleṣman</s>, liquefied by oleation and sweating, is lodged in the large intestine,

children.text: pittaṃ vā darśayed rūpaṃ vastibhis taṃ vinirjayet ||
children.translated_text: or when <s>pitta</s> shows its signs, one should overcome it with <s>bastis</s> (enemas).
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
In a person with <s>vātaśoṇita</s>, after oleation, one should repeatedly let blood,
a little at a time, protecting <s>vāyu</s>, according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to strength.
In pain, redness, pricking pain, and burning, one should remove it with leeches;
when it is accompanied by tingling, itching, pain, and burning, with horns and gourds.

children.text: pracchānena sirābhir vā deśād deśāntaraṃ vrajat
children.translated_text: Or one should remove it by scarification or by the veins, as it moves from one region to another.

children.text: aṅgaglānau tu na srāvyaṃ rūkṣe vātottare ca yat ||
children.translated_text: But when there is exhaustion of the limbs, or when the patient is dry and <s>vāta</s> is predominant, it should not be made to flow,
for because of depletion of blood, <s>vāyu</s> would cause deep swelling, rigidity, tremor, disorders of sinews and vessels,
lassitude, and other conditions arising from <s>vāta</s>.
But after oleating him, one should purge him with oily purgatives.
In <s>vātarakta</s> where <s>vāta</s> is predominant, one should have him drink old ghee.
Ghee cooked with equal parts of <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
along with small mustard seeds and milk, removes <s>vātarakta</s>.
Or one should drink ghee cooked with waters of raisins and <s>madhūka</s>, together with sugar candy,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ pibet tathā kṣīraṃ guḍūcīsvarase śṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and likewise milk boiled in the fresh juice of <s>guḍūcī</s>.

children.text: tailaṃ payaḥ śarkarāṃ ca pāyayed vā sumūrchitam
children.translated_text: Or one should make him drink oil, milk, and sugar, well processed together.
Milk boiled with <s>balā</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, the ten roots, and <s>pīlu</s>,
and with <s>śyāmā</s>, castor, and <s>sthirā</s>, destroys pain from <s>vāta</s>.
Milk fresh and warm from the udder, or mixed with urine, moves the <s>doṣas</s> downward.
In a <s>pitta</s> condition, after cooking <s>varī</s>, bitter drugs, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>,

children.text: pibed ghṛtaṃ vā kṣīraṃ vā svādutiktakasādhitam ||
children.translated_text: he should drink ghee or milk prepared with sweet and bitter substances.
A man with abundant <s>doṣa</s> should drink castor oil with milk as a course of treatment,
for the purpose of purgation; when it has been digested, his food should be rice with milk.
Or one should give him a decoction of <s>abhayā</s> fried in ghee,
or powder of <s>trivṛt</s> with milk as the after-drink, or with grape juice.

children.text: nirhared vā malaṃ tasya saghṛtaiḥ kṣīravastibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Or one should remove his fecal matter with milk <s>bastis</s> containing ghee,
for there is no treatment for <s>vātarakta</s> equal to <s>basti</s>.
This is especially so in pains of the anus, flanks, thighs, joints, bones, and abdomen.
When <s>kapha</s> is predominant, he should drink a decoction of <s>mustā</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, and turmeric,

children.text: sakṣaudraṃ triphalāyā vā guḍūcīṃ vā yathā tathā
children.translated_text: with honey; or one of <s>triphala</s>, or <s>guḍūcī</s>, in whatever suitable manner.
After he has drunk oleation as appropriate and has been made to vomit, one should gently dry him.
<s>Triphala</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, leaves, cardamom, bark, <s>kṣīrī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
<s>viḍaṅga</s>, root of long pepper, <s>romaśā</s>, <s>vṛṣaka</s>, and bark,
<s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>lāṅgalikī</s>, and <s>cavya</s> should be ground in equal parts.

children.text: kalye liptvāyasīṃ pātrīṃ madhyāhne bhakṣayed idam ||
children.translated_text: At dawn, after smearing an iron vessel with it, he should eat this at midday.
It is beneficial in <s>vātāsra</s>, even when all <s>doṣas</s> are involved, and is supreme when there is colic.
A decoction of <s>kokilākṣaka</s>, drunk by one who eats its greens,
restrains <s>vātarakta</s> as the practice of compassion restrains anger.

children.text: pañcamūlasya dhātryā vā rasair lelītakīṃ vasām ||
children.translated_text: With the juices of <s>pañcamūla</s> or of <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>lelītakī</s> and fat

children.text: khuḍaṃ surūḍham apyaṅge brahmacārī piban jayet
children.translated_text: when drunk by a celibate patient conquers <s>khuḍa</s>, even when it is well rooted in a limb.

children.text: ityābhyantaram uddiṣṭaṃ karma bāhyam ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Thus internal treatment has been stated; next comes external treatment.
Oil boiled in an āḍhaka of <s>āranāla</s>, with a quarter part of <s>sarjarasa</s>,
and churned in abundant water, is supreme for removing pain from fever and burning.
Combined with equal parts of beeswax and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, with <s>sarjarasa</s> and <s>śārivā</s>,
that <s>piṇḍataila</s>, through massage, removes the pain of <s>vātarakta</s>.
Milk boiled with the ten roots immediately wards off pain.
For a condition mainly of <s>anila</s> (<s>vāta</s>), sprinkling is likewise done with warm ghee,
or one should sprinkle with the four oleaginous substances cooked with sweet drugs.
One afflicted by rigidity, convulsions, and pain should be sprinkled with warm liquids; but when there is burning, with cold ones.
In the same way, one should use cow's, sheep's, and goat's milk mixed with oil,
with decoctions of the life-promoting drugs or of the lesser <s>pañcamūla</s>.
Grape juice, sugarcane juice, wines, whey from curds, and sour <s>kañjika</s>,
and water with rice, honey, and sugar are recommended for sprinkling.
Beloved, sweet-speaking women, whose hands and breasts are moist with sandalwood,

children.text: sparśaśītāḥ sukhasparśā ghnanti dāhaṃ rujaṃ klamam ||
children.translated_text: cool to the touch and pleasant to touch, remove burning, pain, and fatigue.

children.text: sarāge saruje dāhe raktaṃ hṛtvā pralepayet
children.translated_text: When there is burning with redness and pain, after drawing off blood one should apply a paste
made with <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and sandalwood.
With sugar candy, <s>erakā</s>, parched meal, lentils, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
the paste removes pain, burning, <s>vīsarpa</s>, redness, and swelling.
A fatty <s>kṛśara</s> and mung-bean milk-rice, cooked with <s>vāta</s>-alleviating drugs,
and a poultice made from cakes of sesame and mustard are pain-relieving applications.
Aquatic, <s>prasaha</s>, and marshland animals and birds, well prepared,
joined with life-promoting herbs and fat, may be used in a poultice.
They remove stiffness, piercing pain, ache, contraction, swelling, and seizing of the limbs.
Fat cooked with life-promoting herbs, together with milk, or muscle fat may also be used.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ sahacarān mūlaṃ jīvantī chāgalaṃ payaḥ
children.translated_text: Ghee, root of <s>sahacara</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and goat's milk,

children.text: lepaḥ piṣṭās tilās tadvad bhṛṣṭāḥ payasi nirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or a paste of ground sesame seeds, similarly roasted and cooled in milk, may be used as a paste.
One should make a paste of <s>kṣumā</s> ground with milk, or of castor fruits,
for the purpose of relieving pain, or of <s>śatāhvā</s> when <s>vāta</s> is excessive.
Ghee cooked with urine, alkali, and liquor is beneficial for massage.

children.text: siddhaṃ samadhu śuktaṃ vā sekābhyaṅge kaphottare ||
children.translated_text: Or fermented sour liquid prepared with honey is useful for sprinkling and massage when <s>kapha</s> predominates.
House soot, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, and the two <s>rajanī</s>s
make a paste that removes pain in <s>vātarakta</s> when <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> predominate.
Likewise the seed of <s>madhuśigru</s>, combined with sour grain-gruel, is beneficial.
After it has been applied for a short time, one should sprinkle with sour liquids when <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> predominate.
A superficial condition should be treated with pastes, massage, sprinkling, and immersion baths;
a deep condition should be treated with purgation, decoction enemas, drinking of fats, and similar measures.
Where <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> predominate, pastes and the like should be warm; there, with cold measures,
there comes an increase of burning, swelling, pain, itching, and obstruction through stagnation.
Where <s>pitta</s> and blood predominate in <s>vātarakta</s>, pastes and the like should be cold;
with hot measures there arise scorching, burning pain, redness, sweating, and splitting.
One should take one hundred <s>pala</s>s of <s>madhuyaṣṭī</s> in decoction, reduced to one quarter,
and cook an <s>āḍhaka</s> of oil with an equal quantity of milk and with pastes measured by the <s>pala</s>:
<s>sthirā</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>abhīru</s>, and sandalwood,
<s>lohahaṃsapadī</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, the two <s>medā</s>s, and <s>madhuparṇī</s>,
<s>kākolī</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
<s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, bark, leaves, <s>nakha</s>, and <s>vāla</s>,
<s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>indrī</s>, and <s>vitunnaka</s>.
Used in four ways, it removes <s>vātāsṛk</s>, <s>pitta</s>, burning, fever, and distress.
One should cook oil with a decoction and paste of <s>balā</s>, with an equal quantity of milk.
That oil, cooked a hundred or a thousand times, removes <s>vātāsṛk</s> and diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
It is the foremost <s>rasāyana</s>, a clarifier of the senses,
life-giving, nourishing, good for the voice, and destructive of disorders of semen and blood.

children.text: kupite mārgasaṃrodhān medaso vā kaphasya vā
children.translated_text: When <s>anila</s> is aggravated through obstruction of its pathway by fat or by <s>kapha</s>,
or through excessive increase, oleation and nourishing therapy are not recommended at the beginning.
After first doing there what was prescribed for <s>āḍhyavāta</s>, then, for <s>vātaśoṇita</s>,
one should administer oleating medicine and whatever purifies the blood.
When <s>prāṇa</s> and the other <s>vāta</s>s are aggravated simultaneously, the treatment described for each disease,

children.text: yathāsannaṃ ca bhaiṣajyaṃ vikalpyaṃ syād yathābalam ||
children.translated_text: and the one nearest at hand, should be selected according to the patient's strength.
When a condition with <s>āma</s> has been brought to freedom from <s>āma</s> by sweating, fasting, and digestives,
and by dry pastes, sprinklings, and the like, one should use measures that overcome pure <s>vāta</s>.
Wasting, convulsion, contraction, stiffness, numbness, trembling,
dislocation of the jaw, facial paralysis, lameness, paralysis of the limbs, and <s>khuḍavāta</s>,
dislocation of joints, hemiplegia, and diseases lodged in fat, marrow, and bone:

children.text: ete sthānasya gāmbhīryāt sidhyeyur yatnato navāḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of the depth of their location, these may be cured with effort if they are new.
Therefore one should overcome these when they are new, in strong patients, and without complications.

children.text: vāyau pittāvṛte śītām uṣṇāṃ ca bahuśaḥ kriyām ||
children.translated_text: When <s>vāyu</s> is covered by <s>pitta</s>, one should repeatedly apply cold and hot treatment

children.text: vyatyāsād yojayet sarpir jīvanīyaṃ ca pāyayet
children.translated_text: in alternation, and should give life-promoting ghee to drink.

children.text: dhanvamāṃsaṃ yavāḥ śālir virekaḥ kṣīravān mṛduḥ ||
children.translated_text: Meat of arid-land animals, barley, <s>śāli</s> rice, and a mild purgative with milk are suitable.
There should be enemas with milk, and milk infused with <s>pañcamūla</s> and <s>balā</s>,
and, at the proper time, oil enemas with oils prepared with sweet herbs.
Sprinkling should be done with <s>yaṣṭīmadhu</s>, <s>balā</s>, oil, ghee, and milk,
or with a decoction of <s>pañcamūla</s>, or with cold water.
When <s>kapha</s> covers it, foods made of barley and animals and birds of dry country are suitable,
along with sharp sudations, decoction enemas, emesis, and purgation.
Old ghee and oil made from sesame and mustard are beneficial.
When it is mixed with <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, one should first conquer <s>pitta</s>.
When it is mixed with blood, one should carry out the therapy for <s>vātaśoṇita</s>.
When it is covered by flesh, sudation, massage, meat soups, milk, and fat are beneficial.
In <s>āḍhyavāta</s>, the physician should use treatment that overcomes <s>prameha</s>, fat, and <s>vāta</s>.
When it is in bone and marrow, <s>mahāsneha</s> is used; when it is covered by semen, the previously stated treatment applies.
When it is covered by food, digestive, emetic, appetite-kindling, and light measures are used.
When it is covered by urine, diuretics, sudations, and upper enemas are used.
When it is in feces, castor oil and unctuous, evacuating enemas are used.
Whatever is not opposed to <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and whatever directs <s>vāta</s> downward,
that should be done quickly even when <s>Mātariśvan</s> is covered in every location.
It should also be non-clogging, unctuous, and a means of cleansing the channels.
Sustaining enemas are generally sweet and accompanied by oil enemas.
After examining which strength is greater, one should administer a mild purgative.
The use of all <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) preparations is praised,
especially that of <s>śilāhva</s>, and of purified <s>guggulu</s> with milk.
Or the <s>Bhārgava</s> linctus is used in the same way, taken with eleven parts of sugar.

children.text: apāne tvāvṛte sarvaṃ dīpanaṃ grāhi bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: But when <s>apāna</s> is obstructed, every medicine should kindle digestion and be absorbent,
promote the downward movement of <s>vāta</s>, and cleanse the urinary bladder.
Thus, in brief, the treatment of the obstructed forms has been stated.

children.text: prāṇādīnāṃ bhiṣak kuryād vitarkya svayam eva tat
children.translated_text: For <s>prāṇa</s> and the others, the physician should himself reason out and apply that treatment.
He should direct <s>udāna</s> upward, and guide <s>apāna</s> downward.

children.text: samānaṃ śamayed vidvāṃs tridhā vyānaṃ tu yojayet
children.translated_text: The learned physician should pacify <s>samāna</s>, while he should set <s>vyāna</s> to work in three ways.
<s>Prāṇa</s> must be protected more than the other four, for the body's continuance depends on its stability.

children.text: svaṃ svaṃ sthānaṃ nayed evaṃ vṛtān vātān vimārgagān
children.translated_text: In this way he should lead the obstructed <s>vātas</s> that have gone into wrong channels back to their own proper places.
And every obstruction, except one combined with <s>pitta</s> and blood,
is overcome by garlic, when it is habitually taken according to the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen.
When <s>pitta</s> obstructs, treatment should remove <s>pitta</s> and guide <s>vāta</s> downward.
When blood obstructs, the same applies, along with whatever medicine has been taught for <s>khuḍa</s>.
Various <s>rasāyana</s> remedies that remove blood, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>vāta</s> are also used.
As prescribed according to the cause, this is the proper treatment.
This is the section called the fruit of <s>Āyurveda</s>, because it destroys pain immediately.
<s>Cikitsita</s> (treatment), <s>hita</s> (beneficial measure), <s>pathya</s> (proper regimen), <s>prāyaścitta</s> (remedial expiation), and <s>bhiṣagjita</s> (the physician's cure),

children.text: bheṣajaṃ śamanaṃ śastaṃ paryāyaiḥ smṛtam auṣadham ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>bheṣaja</s>, <s>śamana</s>, and <s>śasta</s>, are remembered as synonyms for <s>auṣadha</s> (medicine).
Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparations for emesis.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
For emesis, <s>madana</s> is best; for purgation, the root of <s>trivṛt</s> is best.
But for any other drug, superiority is always determined by the particular disease.
Having gathered fruits that are neither too pale nor too green,
on a day under an auspicious asterism, in the interval between spring and summer,
one should wipe them, place them in a <s>kuśa</s>-lined basket, tie it up, and smear it
with cow dung; then one should place the basket in the middle of grain.
When, through being wrapped in <s>kuśa</s>, they have become soft and have a honey-sweet smell,
they should be taken out after eight days have passed and then dried in the sun.
Then, from those well-dried fruits, one should remove the fruit-pippalīs,
rub them with curds, honey, ghee, and sesame paste, and dry them again.
Then, after storing them well protected, one should use them at the proper time for the procedure.
Then, taking a dose from them, crushing it coarsely, one should steep it

children.text: śarvarīṃ madhuyaṣṭyā vā kovidārasya vā jale
children.translated_text: for a night in water of <s>madhuyaṣṭi</s> or of <s>kovidāra</s>,

children.text: karbudārasya bimbyā vā nīpasya vidulasya vā ||
children.translated_text: or in water of <s>karbudāra</s>, <s>bimbī</s>, <s>nīpa</s>, or <s>vidula</s>,
or else in water of <s>śaṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>sadāpuṣpī</s>, or <s>pratyakpuṣpī</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pibet kaṣāyaṃ taṃ prātar mṛditagālitam ||
children.translated_text: Then in the morning he should drink that decoction after it has been rubbed and filtered.

children.text: sūtroditena vidhinā sādhu tena tathā vamet
children.translated_text: By the procedure stated in the <s>Sūtra</s> section, he should vomit well with it.
In fever caused by <s>śleṣman</s>, catarrh, <s>gulma</s>, and internal abscesses,
one should especially induce vomiting until bile is seen.
Or powder of the fruit-pippalīs, impregnated with their own decoction,
with one third as much <s>triphala</s> powder, should be drunk with water of <s>kovidāra</s> and the other plants
by one suffering from fever, anorexia, <s>ṣṭheva</s>, glandular swelling, <s>apacī</s>, tumor, or abdominal disease.
When <s>pitta</s> has gone to the seat of <s>kapha</s>, that same powder is taken with water of <s>jīmūta</s> and the other plants.
In burning of the heart and downward bleeding, milk boiled with those pippalīs is used.
