Or <s>kṣaireyī</s> is used in vomiting from <s>kapha</s>, excessive salivation, and <s>tamaka</s> asthma;
or the upper part of curds, or curds produced from milk boiled with those pippalīs, is used.
Ghee prepared with the decoction and paste of <s>phala</s> and the other drugs, or ghee from milk prepared with them,
is an emetic when the digestive fire is overpowered by <s>kapha</s>, or when the body is drying out.
Or the expressed juice of the fruit pulp, boiled according to the procedure for <s>bhallātaka</s>,

children.text: ā darvīlepanāt siddhaṃ līḍhvā pracchardayet sukham ||
children.translated_text: and cooked until it coats the ladle, should be licked; then one vomits easily.
That linctus should be added to chewable and eatable foods, and its decoctions should be used.
A decoction made from fruit pulp, with an admixture of <s>vatsaka</s> and the other drugs,
combined with a decoction of either <s>nimba</s> or <s>arka</s>, checks
all diseases born from over-nourishment, even when they are deeply rooted.
With fine powders of <s>rāṭha</s> flowers and fruits, a garland should be thoroughly dried,
and, after being satisfied with gruel-water and the like, a comfortable man should smell it and vomit easily.

children.text: evam eva phalābhāve kalpyaṃ puṣpaṃ śalāṭu vā
children.translated_text: In just this way, when the fruit is unavailable, the flower or the unripe fruit may be prepared,
and <s>jīmūta</s> and the other drugs should be prepared like <s>phala</s>; but <s>jīmūta</s> in particular
should be used for patients with fever, dyspnea, cough, hiccup, and similar disorders.

children.text: payaḥ puṣpe 'sya nirvṛtte phale peyā payaskṛtā ||
children.translated_text: When its flower has ceased and the fruit has formed, milk prepared with it should be drunk.
When it is hairy, the skin of boiled milk is used; when it is hairless, the upper part of curds is used.
When it has become greenish-yellow, sour curd formed in boiled milk is used.
Or, after steeping it in the scum of <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor, one should drink it crushed and filtered.
This is for anorexia caused by <s>kapha</s>, cough, pallor, and <s>rājayakṣman</s> (consumption).
This same preparation should also be made for <s>tumbī</s> and <s>kośātakī</s>.
Of fully ripened, dry fruits that grow on vines,
a person afflicted by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> should drink a <s>śukti</s> measure of the powder with milk.

children.text: dve vā trīṇyapi vāpothya kvāthe tiktottamasya vā ||
children.translated_text: Or, having crushed two or three fruits in a decoction of <s>tiktottama</s>,
or having steeped them in a decoction of any one among the nine beginning with <s>āragvadha</s>,

children.text: vimṛdya pūtaṃ taṃ kvāthaṃ pittaśleṣmajvarī pibet ||
children.translated_text: the patient with fever from <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> should drink that decoction, rubbed and strained.
One may drink paste or powder of <s>jīmūta</s> with cold water

children.text: jvare paitte kavoṣṇena kaphavātāt kaphād api ||
children.translated_text: in <s>pitta</s> fever, but with lukewarm water in fever from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, or from <s>kapha</s> alone.
For one suffering from cough, dyspnea, poison, vomiting, and fever, and emaciated by <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: ikṣvākur vamane śastaḥ pratāmyati ca mānave ||
children.translated_text: <s>ikṣvāku</s> is praised for emesis, and also when a person is fainting.
When it has neither fruit nor flower, a preparation cooked with its young shoots
In fever caused by <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, one should administer milk when <s>pitta</s> is predominant.

children.text: hṛtamadhye phale jīrṇe sthitaṃ kṣīraṃ yadā dadhi
children.translated_text: When milk left inside a fruit whose middle has been removed has, after it has matured, become curds,

children.text: syāt tadā kaphaje kāse śvāse vamyaṃ ca pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: then, in cough and dyspnea caused by <s>kapha</s>, one should give it to drink as an emetic.
Or the middle of the fruit with whey; one afflicted by pallor, skin disease, or poison

children.text: tena takraṃ vipakvaṃ vā pibet samadhusaindhavam ||
children.translated_text: should drink buttermilk cooked with it, or mixed with honey and rock salt.
After impregnating the seed with goat's milk, he should drink it, or with that same milk,
in poisoning, <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, glandular swellings, goiter, and <s>ślīpada</s>.
Or he should drink a <s>mantha</s> with roasted flour moistened with the juice of <s>tumbī</s>,
in fever born of <s>kapha</s>, cough, throat diseases, and anorexia.

children.text: gulme jvare prasakte ca kalkaṃ māṃsarasaiḥ pibet
children.translated_text: In <s>gulma</s> and in persistent fever he should drink the paste with meat broths;

children.text: naraḥ sādhu vamatyevaṃ na ca daurbalyam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: in this way a man vomits properly and does not incur weakness.
A garland dusted with the dried juices of <s>tumbī</s> fruit, together with its flowers,
when smelled, makes one vomit, if one is accustomed to pleasant and refined fragrances.
In cough, <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, and poisoning, when <s>vāta</s> is lodged in the seat of <s>śleṣman</s>,
and when <s>kapha</s> is located in the throat and mouth, and in disorders produced by accumulation of <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: dhāmārgavo gadeṣviṣṭaḥ sthireṣu ca mahatsu ca
children.translated_text: <s>dhāmārgava</s> is desired, especially in diseases that are fixed and severe.
<s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>kapikacchū</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>kākolī</s>, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>mahāmedā</s>, and <s>madhūlikā</s>:
separate linctuses made from their powders, combined with powder of <s>dhāmārgava</s>,
melted with honey and sugar, are recommended for cough and burning in the heart.
Their after-drink should be pleasant water when <s>kapha</s> is accompanied by heat from <s>pitta</s>.
Its paste with a soup of coriander and <s>tumburu</s> removes poison.

children.text: bimbyāḥ punarnavāyā vā kāsamardasya vā rase ||
children.translated_text: In the juice of <s>bimbī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, or <s>kāsamarda</s>,

children.text: ekaṃ dhāmārgavaṃ dve vā mānase mṛditaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: one should crush one or two <s>dhāmārgava</s> fruits on a stone and drink it.
Or one should take ghee produced from milk boiled with that, cooked with the fruits and other drugs.
<s>Kṣveḍa</s>, being extremely pungent, sharp, and hot, is praised in deep-seated conditions,
in skin disease, pallor disease, spleen disease, swelling, <s>gulma</s>, poisoning, and the like.
In a decoction of the six beginning with the fruits, marshy meat

children.text: kośātakyā samaṃ siddhaṃ tadrasaṃ lavaṇaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: is cooked together with <s>kośātakī</s>; one should drink that broth with salt.
Or the fruits and other drugs, with long pepper in equal amount, are cooked in the juice of <s>kṣveḍa</s>.

children.text: kṣveḍakvāthaṃ pibet siddhaṃ miśram ikṣurasena vā ||
children.translated_text: One should drink a prepared decoction of <s>kṣveḍa</s>, or one mixed with sugarcane juice.
<s>Kauṭaja</s> is honored for delicate patients when <s>pitta</s>, blood, and <s>kapha</s> are increased,

children.text: jvare visarpe hṛdroge khuḍe kuṣṭhe ca pūjitam ||
children.translated_text: in fever, erysipelas, heart disease, <s>khuḍa</s>, and skin disease.
With water of mustard seeds or <s>madhūka</s>, or with salt water,
one should give <s>kauṭaja</s> seed to drink, or combined with <s>kṛśara</s>.
Or, for seven days, one should separately give that powder smeared with the milk of <s>arka</s> to drink,
with waters of the fruit, <s>jīmūtaka</s>, <s>ikṣvāku</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>.
Thus the outline of preparations of the chief emetic medicines has been stated.
With this seed, the wise physician should also devise other preparations.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparation of purgatives.
So indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
<s>Trivṛt</s> is astringent and sweet, dry, and pungent in post-digestive effect;
it pacifies <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and, because of its dryness, aggravates <s>anila</s> (<s>vāta</s>).
Now, combined with medicines that remove <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>,
and obtaining special preparation, it becomes a conqueror of every disease.

children.text: dvidhā khyātaṃ ca tanmūlaṃ śyāmaṃ śyāmāruṇaṃ trivṛt
children.translated_text: Its root is known in two forms: dark <s>trivṛt</s> and dark-red <s>trivṛt</s>.
Of the two, that called <s>trivṛt</s> is superior, harmless, and easy in action.

children.text: sukumāre śiśau vṛddhe mṛdukoṣṭhe ca taddhitam
children.translated_text: It is beneficial for delicate patients, children, the elderly, and those with soft bowels;
it causes fainting, confusion, and irritation and scratching of the heart and throat.
The dark variety, because it acts sharply and quickly, is therefore also recommended

children.text: krūre koṣṭhe bahau doṣe kleśakṣamiṇi cāture ||
children.translated_text: for a patient with hard bowels, abundant <s>doṣa</s>, and the ability to endure distress.
One should take a root that has gone deep, is smooth, and has spread neither too transversely nor irregularly,

children.text: gṛhītvā visṛjet kāṣṭhaṃ tvacaṃ śuṣkāṃ nidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: discard the woody core, and preserve the dried bark.
Then, at the proper time, one should drink the powder with a little dry ginger and rock salt
in diseases of <s>vāta</s>, with sour liquids; in <s>pitta</s> conditions, with ghee, sugar, and honey;
with milk, grapes, sugarcane, <s>kāśmarya</s>, and the best juices of the sweet group;
in <s>kapha</s> disorders, with the juice of <s>pīlu</s>, urine, wine, sour gruel, and <s>kāñjika</s>;
and with powders beginning with <s>pañcakola</s>, properly combined with <s>kapha</s>-removing substances.
A cold preparation with sugar, made from paste and decoction of <s>trivṛt</s>,
combined with honey and the three aromatics, is a pleasant purgative linctus.
<s>Ajagandhā</s>, <s>tavakṣīrī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, sugar, and <s>trivṛt</s>,
powdered and licked with honey and ghee, make one purge well.
This is for one afflicted by fever of all <s>doṣas</s>, rigidity, thirst, burning, and pain.
One should smear the inside of a section of sugarcane, split in two, with <s>trivṛt</s>;

children.text: ekīkṛtya ca tat svinnaṃ puṭapākena bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: then, after joining it together and cooking it by the covered-pit method, one should eat it.
<s>Nīlī</s>, equal to <s>bhṛṅga</s> and cardamom, together with those amounts of <s>trivṛt</s>, and sugar:
one should drink the powder as a nourishing drink with fruit juice, honey, and roasted flour.
In diseases arising from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and in those with weak digestive fire,
it is a harmless purgative for delicate persons.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s>, rice grains, <s>varā</s>, barley awns, long pepper, and <s>trivṛt</s>,
each in half the quantity of the preceding one, when licked with honey, ghee, or jaggery,
clears away <s>gulma</s>, spleen disease, abdominal disease, cough, <s>halīmaka</s>, anorexia,
and many other disorders caused by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s>, root of long pepper, <s>triphala</s>, coriander, <s>citraka</s>,
black pepper, <s>indrayava</s>, cumin, long pepper, and elephant long pepper,
<s>dīpyaka</s> and the five salts, separately powdered, each one <s>karṣa</s> in measure,
and parts of sesame oil and <s>trivṛt</s> powder, each measuring eight <s>palas</s>,
along with three <s>prasthas</s> of juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit and half a <s>tulā</s> of jaggery...

children.text: paktvā mṛdvagninā khādet tato mātrām ayantraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After cooking it over a gentle fire, he should eat the proper dose, without strict restraint thereafter.
It destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s>, piles, jaundice, abdominal tumors, urinary disorders, abdominal enlargement, and fistula,
as well as <s>grahaṇī</s> disease and anemia; it also promotes the begetting of a male child.

children.text: guḍaḥ kalyāṇako nāma sarveṣv ṛtuṣu yaugikaḥ
children.translated_text: This preparation is called <s>Guḍa-kalyānaka</s>; it is suitable in all seasons.
<s>Vyoṣa</s>, <s>trijātaka</s>, <s>ambhoda</s>, <s>kṛmighna</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>trivṛt</s>,

children.text: sarvaiḥ samā samasitā kṣaudreṇa guṭikāḥ kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: all in equal parts, with an equal amount of sugar, are made into pills with honey.
They are recommended for painful urination, fever, vomiting, cough, wasting, dizziness, and consumption,
for burning, anemia, and weak digestive fire, and also in all poisons.
This formula, called <s>Avipatti</s>, is praised for patients with <s>pitta</s> disorders.
<s>Trivṛt</s>, seed of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>,
combined with honey and grape juice, are the purgative for the rainy season.
<s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, sugar, <s>udīcya</s>, and sandalwood,
with raisin-water, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and <s>sātalā</s>, are used at the passing of the clouds, in autumn.

children.text: trivṛtāṃ citrakaṃ pāṭhām ajājīṃ saralaṃ vacām
children.translated_text: In winter one should drink, with hot water, a powder of <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>ajājī</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: svarṇakṣīrīṃ ca hemante cūrṇam uṣṇāmbunā pibet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>.
In summer, <s>trivṛt</s> with an equal amount of sugar is the purgative.
<s>Trivṛt</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>sātalā</s>, <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,

children.text: svarṇakṣīrīṃ ca saṃcūrṇya gomūtre bhāvayet tryaham
children.translated_text: and <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s> should be powdered and steeped in cow urine for three days.
This is an all-season formula, removing feces and <s>doṣas</s> in those who have been oleated.
<s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>durālabhā</s>, <s>hastipippalī</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>,
<s>nīlinī</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, and <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, well powdered together,
are recommended at all times even for dry patients, with meat juice, ghee, or hot water,
in patients with fever, heart disease, <s>vātāsṛj</s>, <s>udāvarta</s>, and the like.
<s>Rājavṛkṣa</s> is especially wholesome, being mild, sweet, and cooling,

children.text: bāle vṛddhe kṣate kṣīṇe sukumāre ca mānave ||
children.translated_text: for a child, an old person, one wounded, one emaciated, and a delicate person.
Because it is gentle and harmless, <s>caturaṅgula</s> in particular should be employed.
At fruiting time one should gather its mature fruit.
One should place a load of those good fruits in sand,
remove them after seven nights, and then dry them in the sun.

children.text: tato majjānam uddhṛtya śucau pātre nidhāpayet
children.translated_text: Then, after extracting the pulp, one should keep it in a clean vessel.
One should give it with grape juice to a patient afflicted by burning and <s>udāvarta</s>.
It may safely be given to a child from four years old up to twelve years old,
or one should have him drink a cold decoction of the pulp of <s>caturaṅgula</s>.
It may be combined separately with the whey of curds, the scum of liquor, or juice of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit,

children.text: sauvīrakeṇa vā yuktaṃ kalkena traivṛtena vā ||
children.translated_text: or with <s>sauvīraka</s>, or with the paste of <s>trivṛt</s>.

children.text: dantīkaṣāye tanmajjño guḍaṃ jīrṇaṃ ca nikṣipet
children.translated_text: One should put old jaggery and that pulp into a decoction of <s>dantī</s>,

children.text: tam ariṣṭaṃ sthitaṃ māsaṃ pāyayet pakṣam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: and have the fermented <s>ariṣṭa</s>, after standing for a month or even a fortnight, drunk.
After taking the bark of the root of <s>tilvaka</s> and discarding the outer bark, one should use the inner bark,

children.text: viśoṣya cūrṇayitvā ca dvau bhāgau gālayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: dry it, powder it, and then sift two parts.
With a decoction of <s>lodhra</s> itself one should impregnate a third part with that,

children.text: kaṣāye daśamūlasya taṃ bhāgaṃ bhāvitaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again impregnate that treated part in a decoction of the ten roots.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ cūrṇaṃ punaḥ kṛtvā tataḥ pāṇitalaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: When it is dry, one should again make it into powder and then drink a palmful,
with whey, urine, the scum of liquor, or water of <s>kola</s> and <s>dhātrī</s> fruits.
A linctus cooked with decoction and paste of <s>tilvaka</s>, with sugar,

children.text: saghṛtaḥ sādhito lehaḥ sa ca śreṣṭhaṃ virecanam ||
children.translated_text: and with ghee, is an excellent purgative.

children.text: sudhā bhinatti doṣāṇāṃ mahāntam api saṃcayam
children.translated_text: <s>Sudhā</s> breaks up even a great accumulation of <s>doṣas</s>,
but because it can quickly cause severe collapse, one should not prescribe it in such cases.
It should not be prescribed when the bowel is soft, or for the weak, a child, an old person, or one with chronic illness.
It is to be prescribed for those with abdominal tumors, abdominal enlargement, poison, skin disease, and diabetes,
and for anemia, latent poison, swelling, and derangement of mind caused by disturbed <s>doṣas</s>.
The best <s>sudhā</s> is covered with many sharp thorns.

children.text: dvivarṣāṃ vā trivarṣāṃ vā śiśirānte viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: It should be two or three years old, especially at the end of the cold season.

children.text: tāṃ pāṭayitvā śastreṇa kṣīram uddhārayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After cutting it with a knife, one should draw out the latex.

children.text: bilvādīnāṃ bṛhatyor vā kvāthena samam ekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: The latex of <s>sudhā</s> should be mixed, one by one, in equal measure with a decoction of the <s>bilva</s> group or of the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants,
and then dried over embers.
After making a pill, one should drink it with whey, urine, liquor, and the like.
The nine beginning with <s>trivṛt</s>, along with <s>varā</s>, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, and <s>sātalā</s>,
after being steeped for seven days in the latex of <s>snuk</s>, should be drunk with juice or with ghee.
Likewise <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>uttamā</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, and <s>agni</s> should be taken with jaggery-water.
The fruit of <s>śaṅkhinī</s> should be taken when it is not too dry and has been freed from its husk,
and likewise the root of <s>saptalā</s>; these two are sharp and diffusive.
One should prescribe them in phlegmatic diseases, abdominal enlargement, poison, swelling, and the like.
A bolus of the two, of one <s>akṣa</s> in measure, should be combined with wine and salt.
It should be used in heart disease caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, and likewise also in abdominal tumor.
The root produced by <s>dantī</s> and <s>dravantī</s> is thick and firm like an elephant's tusk,
coppery-dark in color, sharp, hot, quick-acting, and diffusive.
It is heavy, aggravates <s>vāta</s>, and liquefies <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
Smeared with honey and <s>pippalī</s>, it should be steamed wrapped in clay and <s>darbha</s>,
and dried in gentle sunlight; fire and sun thereby remove its diffusive force.
One should drink it with whey, wine, buttermilk, <s>pīlu</s> juice, or fermented preparations,
if the body is clogged, or if one has abdominal tumor, urinary disease, abdominal enlargement, or poison.
With broths of cow, game, or goat it is used for anemia, intestinal worms, and fistula.
Ghee prepared with its decoction and paste, and also with juice of the ten roots,
conquers <s>visarpa</s>, abscess, <s>alajī</s>, <s>kakṣā</s>, and burning.
Oil, however, conquers abdominal tumor, urinary disease, piles, constipation, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>māruta</s>.
The great fat preparation removes obstruction of feces, semen, and <s>vāta</s>, and pains caused by <s>anila</s>.
These nine, beginning with <s>trivṛt</s>, are the foremost agents in purgation.
<s>Harītakī</s> also should be prepared according to the method prescribed for <s>trivṛt</s>.

children.text: guḍasyāṣṭapale pathyā viṃśatiḥ syāt palaṃ palam ||
children.translated_text: In eight <s>pala</s>s of jaggery there should be twenty <s>pathyā</s> fruits, and one <s>pala</s> each
of <s>dantī</s> and <s>citraka</s>, and ten each of <s>pippalī</s> and <s>trivṛt</s>.
After preparing boluses, one should eat one on every tenth day.
One should drink warm water afterward and eat all of them according to this rule.
These require no special regimen and are destroyers of all diseases.
They are especially beneficial for <s>grahaṇī</s>, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, itching, urticaria, and piles.
By combinations of conjunction, separation, timing, and processing,
one may make even a small amount have great effect and a large amount have little action.
With <s>tvak</s>, <s>kesara</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, pomegranate, cardamom, sugar, honey, and citron,

children.text: madyena taistaiśca mano'nukūlair yuktāni deyāni virecanāni ||
children.translated_text: purgatives should be given mixed with wine and with those various things that are agreeable to the mind.
Now then we shall explain the successful management of complications of emesis and purgation.
Thus spoke the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
An emetic drunk by one with soft bowels, or by one who is hungry and has little <s>kapha</s>,
or one that is too sharp, too cold, or too small in quantity, or drunk during indigestion or by a weak person,
goes downward; in that case the intended result is lost and the wastes are stirred up.

children.text: vāmayet taṃ punaḥ snigdhaṃ smaran pūrvam atikramam ||
children.translated_text: One should make him vomit again after oleating him, remembering the earlier mistake.
In a person with indigestion and much phlegm, purgation goes upward.
If it is too sharp, hot, salty, unpalatable, or excessive in amount,

children.text: tatra pūrvoditā vyāpat siddhiśca na tathāpi cet
children.translated_text: there the complication and the successful treatment are as stated before; but if it is still not so,
and it remains in the receptacle, then a third dose should not be administered,
except when the medicine is harmless because it is habitual, pleasing, or otherwise safe.
For a body that has not been oleated and sweated, an old, dry medicine,

children.text: doṣān utkleśya nirhartum aśaktaṃ janayed gadān
children.translated_text: after agitating the <s>doṣa</s>s but being unable to expel them, produces diseases:

children.text: vibhraṃśaṃ śvayathuṃ hidhmāṃ tamaso darśanaṃ tṛṣam ||
children.translated_text: displacement, swelling, hiccup, seeing darkness, thirst,
cramp in the calves, itching, lassitude of the thighs, and discoloration.
Or, in one who has been oleated and sweated, too little medicine, when the digestive fire is strong and the medicine has been digested,

children.text: śītair vā stabdham āme vā samutkleśyāharanmalān
children.translated_text: or medicine checked by cold things, or medicine in the presence of <s>āma</s>, after agitating the wastes but not carrying them off,

children.text: tān eva janayed rogān ayogaḥ sarva eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: would produce those very diseases. This entire condition is under-action.
After anointing him with oil and salt and sweating him with bed-sudation and mixed sudations,
one should give a decoction enema, feed him with arid-land meat soups, and administer an oil enema
with a proper dose of oil prepared with <s>phala</s>, <s>māgadhikā</s>, and <s>dāru</s>.
When he is oleated with unctions that remove <s>vāta</s>, one should again cleanse him with a sharp medicine.
For a person with many <s>doṣa</s>s, dryness, weak digestive fire, and <s>udāvarta</s>, too little medicine,
after agitating the <s>doṣa</s>s, blocks the channels by means of them,
and greatly distends the region of the navel, causing pain in the back, flanks, and head.
It also causes dyspnea and a severe obstruction of feces, urine, and flatus.
Massage, sudation, suppositories, and the like, together with decoction enemas and oil enemas,
indeed every procedure that removes <s>udāvarta</s>, is recommended for one who is distended.
A well-prepared gruel with <s>pañcamūla</s>, alkali of barley, <s>vacā</s>, <s>bhūtika</s>, and rock salt
removes colic, constipation, and abdominal distension.
One should drink <s>pippalī</s>, pomegranate, alkali, asafoetida, dry ginger, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
together with rock salt, with wines, or with ghee and warm water.
In dysenteric straining, discharge, pain, and cutting pain,
when a person who has drunk the medicine restrains the urges, <s>māruta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s,

children.text: kupitā hṛdayaṃ gatvā ghoraṃ kurvanti hṛdgraham
children.translated_text: being aggravated and having gone to the heart, cause a dreadful seizure of the heart.
With hiccup, pain in the flanks, distress, wretchedness, salivation, and disturbance of the eyes,
he bites his tongue, loses consciousness, and grinds his teeth.

children.text: na gacched vibhramaṃ tatra vāmayed āśu taṃ bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: There the physician should not become confused; he should quickly make him vomit.
One who has fainted from <s>pitta</s> should be treated with sweet substances, and one fainting from <s>kapha</s> with pungent substances.
Then with digestives one should digest the remaining <s>doṣa</s> in him.
And one should gradually increase his bodily fire and his strength.
For one whose heart is oppressed by <s>pavana</s> because he has vomited excessively,
one should give unctuous, sour, and salty things; in <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> conditions the treatment is otherwise.
Through suppression of the urges in one who has drunk the medicine, or through <s>kapha</s>,
<s>māruta</s>, being obstructed, or in one who has been over-cleansed, seizes the limbs,
with stiffness, trembling, pricking pain, lassitude, twisting pain, distress, and splitting pain.
There every <s>vāta</s>-removing measure, beginning with oleation and sudation, is recommended.
A very sharp medicine given to one who is hungry and has soft bowels,
after swiftly removing feces, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, causes the fluid bodily tissues to flow out.
In that over-action, the remaining medicine should be made to be vomited out with sweet substances.
For excessive emesis a mild purgative is proper, and for excessive purgation a mild emetic.
And one should check him with very cold sprinklings, immersions, and the like.
He should drink a churned drink with collyrium, sandalwood, <s>uśīra</s>, goat's blood, and sugar water,
together with parched-grain flour; it is the supreme remedy for over-action.
But in excessive emesis, after being sprinkled with cold water,
he should drink a churned drink with fruit juices, ghee, honey, and sugar.
When there is severe vomiting with belching,
one should have him lick, mixed with honey, a powder of <s>mūrvā</s>, coriander, and <s>musta</s>, with <s>madhūka</s> and collyrium.
When the tongue has gone inward in one who is vomiting, mouthfuls
that are unctuous, sour, salty, pleasing to the heart, and soups and meat juices are beneficial.
Other people should eat sour fruits in front of him.
But when the tongue has come out, one should smear it with a paste of sesame and grapes and replace it.
In disorders of seized speech and of <s>anila</s>,

children.text: yavāgūṃ tanukāṃ dadyāt snehasvedau ca kālavit ||
children.translated_text: one who knows the proper time should give thin gruel prepared with ghee and meat, and also oleation and sudation.
Because of over-action, the medicine carries off blood, which is life itself.
That is called the taking of life, because it takes away life.

children.text: śune kākāya vā dadyāt tenānnam asṛjā saha
children.translated_text: One should give food together with that blood to a dog or to a crow.
According as it is eaten or not eaten, one should declare it to be living blood, or <s>pitta</s> impelled by medicine.

children.text: śuklaṃ vā bhāvitaṃ vastram āvānaṃ koṣṇavāriṇā
children.translated_text: Or a white cloth, after being soaked in it and then washed with lukewarm water,

children.text: prakṣālitaṃ vivarṇaṃ syāt pitte śuddhaṃ tu śoṇite ||
children.translated_text: becomes discolored when it is <s>pitta</s>, but remains clean when it is blood.
For a patient tormented by thirst, fainting, and stupor, one should perform treatment even up to the point of death,
treatment that destroys <s>raktapitta</s> and diarrhea and quickly protects his life.
He should drink the fresh blood of living deer, cattle, buffaloes, or goats,
for the restoration of life; for that quickly reaches the living principle.

children.text: tad eva darbhamṛditaṃ raktaṃ vastau niṣecayet
children.translated_text: That same blood, rubbed with <s>darbha</s> grass, should be injected into the bladder or enema apparatus.
Milk boiled with <s>śyāmāka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, and <s>uśīra</s>,
mixed with the clear part of ghee and <s>añjana</s>, may be applied as a cold enema,
or a very cold mucilaginous enema, or an oil-enema with the clear part of ghee.
A prolapsed rectum should be made firm with astringent decoctions and then inserted back.
One who is unconscious should be made to hear sounds such as <s>Sāman</s> chanting, flute, and song.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the varieties of <s>basti</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: balāṃ guḍūcīṃ triphalāṃ sarāsnāṃ dvipañcamūlaṃ ca palonmitāni
children.translated_text: One should cook one <s>pala</s> each of <s>balā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and the two <s>pañcamūla</s> groups,

children.text: aṣṭau phalānyardhatulāṃ ca māṃsācchāgāt paced apsu caturthaśeṣam ||
children.translated_text: eight fruits, and half a <s>tulā</s> of goat meat in water, until one quarter remains.
After it is strained, with pastes of <s>yavānī</s> fruit, <s>bilva</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>ghana</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>,

children.text: kalkair guḍakṣaudraghṛtaiḥ satailair yuktaḥ sukhoṣṇo lavaṇānvitaśca ||
children.translated_text: joined with jaggery, honey, ghee, and oil, pleasantly warm and furnished with salt,

children.text: vastiḥ paraṃ sarvagadapramāthī svasthe hito jīvanabṛṃhaṇaśca
children.translated_text: this <s>basti</s> is supreme, churning away all disease; it is wholesome for the healthy, life-giving, and nourishing.

children.text: vastau ca yasmin paṭhito na kalkaḥ sarvatra dadyād amum eva tatra ||
children.translated_text: And in any <s>basti</s> for which no paste is stated, this very paste should always be added there.
The juice of the two <s>pañcamūla</s> groups, mixed with something sour, together with goat meat and the previously mentioned paste,
and joined with the three fats, is taught as the foremost decoction-enema, removing all disorders of <s>anila</s>.
From <s>balā</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, the minor <s>pañcamūla</s>, <s>trāyantikā</s>, castor, and barley, when well cooked,

children.text: prastho rasācchāgarasārdhayuktaḥ sādhyaḥ punaḥ prasthasamaḥ sa yāvat ||
children.translated_text: one <s>prastha</s> of decoction, combined with half as much goat broth, should again be prepared until it equals one <s>prastha</s>.
It should be joined with pastes of <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>ghana</s>, and with oil, ghee, honey, and rock salt.

children.text: syād dīpano māṃsabalapradaśca cakṣurbalaṃ copadadhāti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It becomes appetite-kindling and gives flesh and strength; it also immediately bestows strength on the eyes.

children.text: eraṇḍamūlāt tripalaṃ palāśāt tathā palāṃśaṃ laghupañcamūlam
children.translated_text: Three <s>pala</s>s of castor root, one <s>pala</s> of <s>palāśa</s>, and likewise one <s>pala</s> each of the minor <s>pañcamūla</s>,
<s>rāsnā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>chinnaruhā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,
and eight fruits should be boiled in two <s>āḍhaka</s>s of water until one eighth remains.
In this, <s>vacā</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s> seed, and <s>musta</s>,
well ground, together with <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s>, in a measure of one <s>akṣa</s>, and mixed with a portion of salt, should be added.
With honey, oil, and urine added, that scraping and appetite-kindling <s>basti</s> conquers
pain in the shanks, thighs, feet, sacrum, back, abdomen, heart, and genitals, heaviness, constipation,
<s>gulma</s>, urinary stone, scrotal swelling, <s>grahaṇī</s>, disorders arising from the anus, and all those diseases born of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Milk boiled with <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, sandalwood, lotuses, and blue lotuses is excellent.
Made very cold and mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee, it destroys diseases of <s>pitta</s> and is life-restoring.

children.text: rāsnāṃ vṛṣaṃ lohitikām anantāṃ balāṃ kanīyastṛṇapañcamūlyau
children.translated_text: <s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>lohitikā</s>, <s>anantā</s>, <s>balā</s>, the smaller and the grass <s>pañcamūla</s> groups,
<s>gopāṅganā</s>, sandalwood, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>, each in half-<s>pala</s> quantities,

children.text: niṣkvāthya toyena rasena tena śṛtaṃ payo 'rdhāḍhakam ambuhīnam
children.translated_text: should be decocted with water; with that decoction, half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of milk should be boiled until the water is gone.
With <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>varī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, and <s>serukā</s>,
with sugar candy, <s>jīvaka</s>, lotus pollen, <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, blue lotus, and white lotus,
with <s>lodhra</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>madhuyaṣṭikā</s>, <s>nāgāhva</s>, <s>muñjātaka</s>, and sandalwood,

children.text: piṣṭair ghṛtakṣaudrayutair nirūhaṃ sasaindhavaṃ śītalam eva dadyāt
children.translated_text: all ground and mixed with ghee and honey, one should administer a cold decoction-enema with rock salt.

children.text: pratyāgate dhanvarasena śālīn kṣīreṇa vādyāt pariṣiktagātraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it has returned, the patient, with his body sprinkled, should eat <s>śāli</s> rice with arid-land meat soup or with milk.
It destroys burning, diarrhea, morbid discharge, bleeding <s>pitta</s>, heart disease, anemia, and intermittent fever,
as well as <s>gulma</s>, urinary obstruction, jaundice, and the like: all diseases produced by <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Kośātakī</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>aśvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>arka</s>, and <s>pāṭhā</s>,

children.text: paktvā kulatthān bṛhatīṃ ca toye rasasya tasya prasṛtā daśa syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>kulattha</s> and <s>bṛhatī</s>, should be cooked in water; there should be ten <s>prasṛta</s>s of that decoction.

children.text: tān sarṣapailāmadanaiḥ sakuṣṭhair akṣapramāṇaiḥ prasṛtaiśca yuktān
children.translated_text: These, joined with mustard, cardamom, <s>madana</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, each in an <s>akṣa</s> measure, and with <s>prasṛta</s>s

children.text: kṣaudrasya tailasya phalāhvayasya kṣārasya tailasya ca sārṣapasya ||
children.translated_text: of honey, oil, the oil called <s>phala</s>, alkali, and mustard oil,
should be given as a decoction-enema to one suffering from <s>kapha</s> disease, weak digestion, and aversion to food.

children.text: vakṣye mṛdūn snehakṛto nirūhān sukhocitānāṃ prasṛtaiḥ pṛthak tu ||
children.translated_text: I shall describe mild decoction-enemas that produce unctuousness, for those accustomed to comfort, each by <s>prasṛta</s> measures.
Now I shall describe these decoction-enemas for delicate persons, mild because of oleation,

children.text: karmaṇā viplutānāṃ ca vakṣyāmi prasṛtaiḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and also for those worn out by procedures, each according to <s>prasṛta</s> measures.

children.text: kṣīrād dvau prasṛtau kāryau madhutailaghṛtāt trayaḥ
children.translated_text: Two <s>prasṛta</s>s should be made from milk, and three from honey, oil, and ghee.
Churned with a churning-stick, this <s>basti</s> destroys <s>vāta</s> and produces strength and complexion.
There is one <s>prasṛta</s> each of oil, clear wine, honey, and ghee,

children.text: bilvādimūlakvāthād dvau kaulatthād dvau sa vātajit ||
children.translated_text: two of decoction of <s>bilva</s> and the other roots, and two of <s>kulattha</s> decoction; this conquers <s>vāta</s>.
From the waters of <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>bhūtīka</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>saptacchada</s>,
one <s>prasṛta</s> of each, and likewise one of ghee, forms a <s>basti</s> furnished with mustard paste.
That five-bitter <s>basti</s> removes <s>abhiṣyanda</s>, worms, skin disease, and <s>prameha</s>.
Four <s>prasṛtas</s> each of oil, cow urine, whey, sour liquid, and <s>kāñjika</s>,
with mustard seeds ground into them, break up retention of feces and abdominal distension.
Of <s>payasyā</s>, sugarcane, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, honey, and ghee,
one <s>prasṛta</s> of each, with paste of <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, makes a <s>basti</s> that produces virility.

children.text: siddhavastīn ato vakṣye sarvadā yān prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: From here I shall describe the accomplished <s>bastis</s>, which one may employ at all times:
free from danger, rich in benefits, increasing strength and nourishment, and pleasant.

children.text: madhutaile same karṣaḥ saindhavād dvipicur miśiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Honey and oil in equal amount, one <s>karṣa</s> of rock salt, and two <s>picus</s> of <s>miśi</s>,
with a decoction of castor root: this <s>nirūha</s> is the <s>mādhutailika</s>.
It is a rejuvenant and removes urinary disease, hemorrhoids, worms, <s>gulma</s>, and intestinal enlargement;
and this same one, with <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s>, benefits the eyes and conquers bleeding disorders.
A <s>yāpana</s> with paste of <s>ghana</s>, honey, oil, meat juice, and ghee
conquers pain in the anus, knees, thighs, testicles, bladder, and penis.
One should prepare a <s>yāpana</s> from <s>prasṛta</s> measures of ghee, honey, fat, and oil,
together with half an <s>akṣa</s> of rock salt and half a <s>pala</s> of <s>hapuṣā</s>.
A decoction of castor root, honey, oil, and rock salt:
this, with <s>vacā</s> and long pepper fruit, is the <s>yuktaratha</s> <s>basti</s>.
That decoction, with honey, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, asafoetida, and rock salt,

children.text: suradāru ca rāsnā ca vastir doṣaharaḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: as well as <s>suradāru</s> and <s>rāsnā</s>, is an auspicious <s>basti</s> that removes the <s>doṣas</s>.
A decoction of the five roots, oil, <s>māgadhikā</s>, and honey,
with rock salt and <s>madhuka</s>, is remembered as the accomplished <s>basti</s>.
One should cook the two sets of five roots, the fruits of <s>triphala</s>, and bilva fruits
in cow urine, and with that add ground <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, and <s>toyada</s>,
together with fruits, honey and oil, alkali, and salt.
This <s>basti</s>, joined with them, is honored in diseases of <s>kapha</s>, anemia, and cholera-like illness,
in obstructions of semen and wind, and in distension of the bladder.
<s>Mustā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, castor, <s>balā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>āragvadha</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>trāyamāṇā</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,
the minor group of five roots, one <s>pala</s> each, and eight <s>madana</s> fruits:
one should cook these in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water, and, when a quarter remains, strain it.
Mixed with two <s>prasthas</s> of milk, it should again be cooked until only the milk remains.
With one and a quarter measures of dry-land animal meat juice, ghee, honey, and rock salt,
and with pastes of <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>kaliṅgaka</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,
this pleasantly warm <s>basti</s> increases flesh, digestive fire, strength, and semen.
It destroys blood-vāta disease, stupor, urinary disease, hemorrhoids, <s>gulma</s>, and retention of feces and urine,
irregular fever, erysipelas, scrotal swelling, abdominal distension, and dysentery,
pains in the groin, thighs, hips, abdomen, neck, ears, and head.
It also destroys uterine bleeding, insanity, swelling, cough, stones, and <s>kuṇḍala</s> disorders.
It benefits the eyes, grants sons, is the king of <s>yāpana</s> bastis, and is a rejuvenant.
With broth of light, wholesome game animals and with water of <s>daśamūla</s>,
and with pastes of <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>miśi</s>, and <s>gāṅgeyī</s>, it is supremely pacifying to <s>vāta</s>.
The <s>nirūha</s>, furnished with the great unctuous substances, is also exceedingly aphrodisiac.
A peacock, excluding feathers, bile, intestines, feet, feces, and beak,
together with one <s>pala</s> of the light five roots,
should be cooked in milk and water until only the milk remains, with ghee and honey.
That, containing pastes of <s>vidārī</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, and <s>phala</s>,
is a <s>basti</s> with a little salt added, and it produces supreme strength and semen.
This preparation should be made separately also with partridges and the like,
among all <s>viṣkira</s>, <s>pratuda</s>, and <s>prasaha</s> birds.
Likewise it may be made with aquatic creatures and with fish, but without milk.
The flesh of iguana, mongoose, cat, porcupine, and <s>kondura</s>,

children.text: pṛthag daśapalaṃ kṣīre pañcamūlaṃ ca sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: ten <s>palas</s> of each separately, should be cooked in milk with the five roots.
That milk, furnished with pastes of <s>phala</s> and <s>vaidehī</s> and with two salts,
with sugar, oil, honey, and ghee, is a <s>basti</s> to be used as a rejuvenant.
For those whose chests are strained by exercise and whose faculties, strength, and <s>ojas</s> are depleted,
for those with obstructed semen, feces, and urine and with disorders of <s>khuḍavāta</s>,
and for those whose bodies are broken and worn down by jolting from elephants, horses, and chariots,
it brings renewed youth and is an excellent aphrodisiac treatment.
Food should be eaten with milk prepared with <s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>uccaṭā</s>, and sugarcane,
and unctuous preparations, prepared without restriction from the accomplished drugs, should be prescribed.
Unctuous <s>bastis</s> that destroy the <s>doṣas</s>, together with their regimen, will now be described.
<s>Daśamūla</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>guḍūcī</s>, castor, <s>bhūtīka</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>vṛṣaka</s>, and <s>rohiṣa</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>sahacara</s>, and <s>kākanāsā</s>, each one <s>pala</s>,
and barley, black gram, flaxseed, jujube, and horse gram, each measured by a <s>prasṛta</s>,

children.text: vahe vipācya toyasya droṇaśeṣeṇa tena ca ||
children.translated_text: should be cooked in a <s>vaha</s> of water until one <s>droṇa</s> remains; with that decoction
one should cook an <s>āḍhaka</s> of oil with pastes of life-promoting herbs, each one <s>pala</s>.
This is the <s>anuvāsana</s>; it removes all disorders of <s>vāta</s>.
Likewise, the fat of marsh-dwelling animals should be prepared with life-promoting herbs.
Oil cooked with <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>ciribilva</s>, and sour substances is for <s>samīraṇa</s>.
And ghee heated with fire-colored rock salt conquers <s>anila</s>.

children.text: jīvantīṃ madanaṃ medāṃ śrāvaṇīṃ madhukaṃ balām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
<s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>kākanāsā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>svaguptā</s>, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, the herb called <s>karkaṭa</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>vacā</s>:
after grinding these, one should cook oil and ghee in four times as much milk.
It is nourishing, destroys <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, and increases strength, semen, and digestive fire.
This <s>anuvāsana</s> removes disorders of menstrual blood and semen and promotes the birth of sons.

children.text: saindhavaṃ madanaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ śatāhvā niculo vacā ||
children.translated_text: Rock salt, <s>madana</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, <s>nicula</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
<s>hrīvera</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s>,

children.text: nāgaraṃ puṣkaraṃ medā cavikā citrakaḥ śaṭhī ||
children.translated_text: dry ginger, <s>puṣkara</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>cavikā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>śaṭhī</s>...
<s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>hareṇu</s>, <s>nīlinī</s>, and <s>sthirā</s>,

children.text: bilvājamodacapalā dantī rāsnā ca taiḥ samaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>bilva</s>, <s>ajamodā</s>, <s>capalā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>rāsnā</s>: with these in equal parts,

children.text: sādhyam eraṇḍatailaṃ vā tailaṃ vā kapharoganut
children.translated_text: castor oil may be prepared, or an oil that removes diseases of <s>kapha</s>.
That oil enema quickly destroys <s>vardhma</s>, <s>udāvarta</s>, <s>gulma</s>, hemorrhoids, spleen disease, <s>meha</s>, and severe <s>māruta</s> (<s>vāta</s>),

children.text: ānāham aśmarīṃ cāśu hanyāt tad anuvāsanam
children.translated_text: as well as abdominal distension and stone.
Oil prepared with <s>pañcamūla</s>, or else with the <s>bilvādi</s> group,

children.text: kaphaghnaṃ kalpayet tailaṃ dravyair vā kaphaghātibhiḥ
children.translated_text: should be prepared as an oil that removes <s>kapha</s>, or with substances that destroy <s>kapha</s>.
In a <s>kapha</s> condition, an oil enema is prepared with sour fruits in eightfold quantity.
When a mild enema has become inert, another sharp enema is desired.

children.text: tīkṣṇair vikarṣite snigdho madhuraḥ śiśiro mṛduḥ ||
children.translated_text: When sharp substances have drawn the morbid matter out, the next should be unctuous, sweet, cold, and mild.
Sharpness is produced by urine, <s>pīlu</s>, <s>agni</s>, salt, alkali, and mustard.
At the proper time, mildness should be produced with milk, ghee, and the like.
An enema applied after distinguishing strength, season, disease, <s>doṣa</s>, and constitution,

children.text: svaiḥ svair auṣadhavargaiḥ svān svān rogānnivartayati ||
children.translated_text: with its respective classes of medicines, removes its respective diseases.
For those afflicted by heat, one should consider cold enemas; for those afflicted by cold, comfortably warm ones,
and administer enemas combined with medicines suitable for those conditions.
One should not give nourishing enemas in diseases that require purification,

children.text: medasvino viśodhyā ye ca narāḥ kuṣṭhamehārtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor to corpulent people who require purification, nor to men afflicted with skin disease and <s>meha</s>.
One should not give purificatory enemas to those who are wasted, wounded, weak, fainted, thin, dry, or already cleansed,
nor to those whose life is bound up with retained <s>doṣas</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the successful management of complications of <s>basti</s>.
So indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
When applied to a body that has not been oleated or fomented, or to a person with heavy bowels,
if it is cold, has too little unctuous substance, salt, medicine, or dose, or is too thick,

children.text: vastiḥ saṃkṣobhya taṃ doṣaṃ durbalatvād anirharan
children.translated_text: the enema agitates that <s>doṣa</s>, but because of weakness it does not expel it.
It produces under-action; from that there is retention of <s>vāta</s>, urine, and feces.
There are pains in the navel and bladder, burning, oppression in the heart, and swelling in the rectum,
itching, lumps, discoloration, restlessness, and weakness of the digestive fire.
Of the two decoctions prescribed earlier for a middling <s>doṣa</s> in diarrhea,

children.text: uṣṇasya tasmād ekasya tatra pānaṃ praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: drinking one of them warm is recommended in that condition.

children.text: phalavartyas tathā svedāḥ kālaṃ jñātvā virecanam
children.translated_text: Fruit suppositories, fomentations, and, after judging the time, purgation should also be used.
An enema containing <s>bilva</s> root, <s>trivṛt</s>, deodar, barley, <s>kola</s>, and horse gram,
with wine and other liquids and with urine, together with the pastes prescribed before, should bring it down.
When an enema that is properly applied but weak in potency is given to one full of <s>doṣas</s>, dry, or with a hard bowel,
it is covered by the <s>doṣas</s>, its path is blocked, and it obstructs <s>samīraṇa</s> (<s>vāta</s>).
That misdirected wind causes distension and pain in the vital points,
burning in the rectum and bowel, and pain in the testicles and groins.
It obstructs the heart with pains and runs this way and that.
In that case, when his limbs have been well anointed and fomented, one should apply a suppository.
There should be a decoction enema of the <s>bilvādi</s> group, containing <s>pīlu</s>, mustard, and urine,
and an oil enema prepared with <s>sarala</s> and deodar.
If a person suppresses the urges, or if he is driven by excessive <s>vāta</s>,
or if the enema lacks oiliness, salt, and warmth, or is small and has too little medicine,
or if it is mild, it is thrown upward by <s>māruta</s> and comes out through the mouth and nose,
producing fainting, nausea, thirst, burning, and the like.
Seeing his disorder of fainting, one should sprinkle his face with cool water.

children.text: vyajed ā klamanāśācca prāṇāyāmaṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: One should fan him until the exhaustion ceases, and make him perform breath control.
One should rub his back, flanks, and abdomen with warm hands while he faces downward.
Lifting him by the hair, one should shake him, and frighten him with snakes and fanged creatures,
with weapons, firebrands, and royal officers; for in that way the enema goes downward.

children.text: pāṇivastrair galāpīḍaṃ kuryān na mriyate tathā
children.translated_text: One should compress his throat with hands or cloth, but not so that he dies.
For, when <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>udāna</s> are checked, <s>apāna</s>, whose path is better established,
quickly draws the enema downward.
One should also make him drink a paste of <s>kuṣṭha</s> and <s>kramuka</s> combined with sour liquid.
Because of its heat, sharpness, and flowing quality, it makes that enema move downward for him.
Or a paste of <s>trivṛt</s> and <s>pathyā</s> with cow urine is for downward movement.
When it is situated in the colon and the patient has been fomented, a decoction enema of <s>daśamūla</s>
should be prescribed with barley, <s>kola</s>, and horse gram, cooked with urine.
Or the enema may be prepared with cow-urine decoctions containing <s>amṛtā</s> and bamboo shoots,
with bark and leaves of <s>pūtikarañja</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, deodar, and <s>rohiṣa</s>.
It should contain oil, jaggery, rock salt, and a paste of purgative medicines.
When it is lodged in the chest, an enema prepared with <s>bilvādi pañcamūla</s> is used.

children.text: śiraḥsthe nāvanaṃ dhūmaḥ pracchādyaṃ sarṣapaiḥ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: When it is lodged in the head, nasal medication and smoke are used; the head should be covered with mustard.
An enema that is excessively hot, sharp, sour, or thick, or one applied to a person who has been over-fomented,

children.text: alpe doṣe mṛdau koṣṭhe prayukto vā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: or used again and again when the <s>doṣa</s> is slight and the bowel is soft,
comes to be over-action and causes pain in the belly.
It has the same form and treatment as excessive purgation.
An enema that is alkaline, sour, sharp, hot, and salty, or one given to a person of <s>pitta</s> constitution,

children.text: gudaṃ dahan likhan kṣiṇvan karotyasya parisravam
children.translated_text: burns, scrapes, and injures his rectum, and causes a discharge.

children.text: sa vidagdhaṃ sravatyasraṃ varṇaiḥ pittaṃ ca bhūribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He discharges digested blood and <s>pitta</s> of many colors.
Again and again, with excessively violent urges, he repeatedly falls into confusion.
There, treatment that checks blood-pitta and diarrhea is recommended.
In burning and similar symptoms, he should drink paste of <s>trivṛt</s> with raisin water.
For that, after carrying off <s>pitta</s>, feces, and <s>vāta</s>, conquers burning and the other symptoms.
When purified, he should drink cold rice gruel with sugar.
One should prescribe the diet used for someone over-purged, whose feces have been depleted.
with black-gram soup, with <s>kulmāṣa</s>, with a drink, or else with curds or liquor.

children.text: siddhir vastyāpadām evaṃ snehavastes tu vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus is the successful management of disorders of <s>basti</s>; now that of <s>snehavasti</s> will be stated.

children.text: śīto 'lpo vādhike vāte pitte 'tyuṣṇaḥ kaphe mṛduḥ
children.translated_text: When it is cold or too little in increased <s>vāta</s>, too hot in <s>pitta</s>, and mild in <s>kapha</s>,
or when given after excessive eating, when there is accumulation of feces, or when the patient has little strength,
the unctuous substance, obstructed by these, does not return, because it is overpowered.
By stiffness, sinking of the thighs, distension, fever, pain, and aching of the limbs,
together with pain in the sides and griping, one should know that the unctuous enema is obstructed by <s>vāyu</s>.
One should expel it properly with <s>nirūha</s> enemas that are unctuous, sour, salty, and hot, with <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>pītadru</s>, and oils,
prepared with <s>sauvīraka</s>, liquor, <s>kola</s>, horse gram, and barley,
and with urine and the drugs of the <s>pañcamūla</s> group.

children.text: tābhyām eva ca tailābhyāṃ sāyaṃ bhukte 'nuvāsayet
children.translated_text: With those same two oils one should give an <s>anuvāsana</s> in the evening, after the patient has eaten.
By thirst, burning, redness, confusion, discoloration, darkness before the eyes, and fever,

children.text: vidyāt pittāvṛtaṃ svādutiktais taṃ vastibhir haret
children.translated_text: one should know it to be obstructed by <s>pitta</s>; one should remove it with enemas that are sweet and bitter.
By drowsiness, cold fever, languor, salivation, anorexia, and heaviness,
and by fainting and exhaustion, one should know that the unctuous enema is obstructed by <s>śleṣman</s>.
One should expel it with astringent, bitter, and pungent enemas, prepared with liquor and urine,
mixed with <s>phalataila</s> and made sour.
By vomiting, fainting, anorexia, exhaustion, pain, sleepiness, and aching of the limbs,
together with signs of <s>āma</s> and burning, one should know it to be obstructed by overeating.
Digestion should be promoted with decoctions and powders of pungent and salty substances.

children.text: mṛdur virekaḥ sarvaṃ ca tatrāmavihitaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: A mild purgation, and everything prescribed for <s>āma</s> in that condition, is beneficial.
By obstruction of feces, urine, and wind, distress, heaviness, distension, and catching pain in the heart,
having recognized the unctuous enema as obstructed by feces, one should use unction and sudation, along with suppositories,
and properly expel it by the prescribed method with <s>nirūha</s> enemas prepared with <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and similar drugs, together with <s>anuvāsana</s>,
and also by a procedure that removes <s>udāvarta</s>.
When the unctuous enema is introduced into the rectum of one who has not eaten, whose anus is swollen,
or who has eaten only the measure of thin gruel, it rushes forth by force, unobstructed.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ kāyaṃ tataḥ kaṇṭhād ūrdhvebhyaḥ khebhya etyapi ||
children.translated_text: Then it may go upward through the body, even from the throat to the openings above.
A <s>nirūha</s> prepared with urine, <s>śyāmā</s>, and <s>trivṛt</s>, containing barley, <s>kola</s>, and horse gram,
and an <s>anuvāsana</s> with oil prepared from these, should be given.
If it comes from the throat, one should suppress it by measures producing stiffness, throat-constriction, and purgation,
and by therapies that check vomiting.

children.text: nāpakvaṃ praṇayet snehaṃ gudaṃ sa hyupalimpati
children.translated_text: One should not introduce the unctuous enema before digestion is complete, for it coats the rectum.
Then it causes pain, confusion, itching, and swelling; here the treatment is as follows:

children.text: tīkṣṇo vastis tathā tailam arkapattrarase śṛtam
children.translated_text: a sharp <s>basti</s>, and oil cooked in the juice of <s>arka</s> leaves.

children.text: anucchvāsya tu baddhe vā datte niḥśeṣa eva vā ||
children.translated_text: When it is given while the patient has not exhaled, or when the nozzle is bound, or when it is administered without remainder,
the disturbed <s>vāyu</s>, having entered, may produce colic and pricking pain.
In that case there should be massage, fomentation of the rectum, and foods that subdue <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: drutaṃ praṇīte niṣkṛṣṭe sahasotkṣipta eva vā
children.translated_text: When it is inserted hastily, pulled out, or suddenly jerked upward,
there may be stiffness, pain, and splitting distress in the waist, rectum, shanks, thighs, and bladder.
In that case the food should subdue <s>vāta</s>, and there should be sudation, massage, and enemas.
When it is released in the middle while being pressed, <s>anila</s>, checked in the rectum,
being strong, produces pain in the chest and head, debility, and pain in the thighs.
In that case the enema should contain urine and fruits of the <s>bilva</s> group, <s>śyāmā</s>, and the like.
When it is pressed too forcefully, it remains in the bowel or comes up to the throat.

children.text: tatra vastir virekaśca galapīḍādi karma ca ||
children.translated_text: In that case there should be an enema and purgation, and procedures such as compression of the throat.
A person purified by emesis and the other evacuative therapies, whose body, strength, and digestive fire are emaciated,

children.text: yathāṇḍaṃ taruṇaṃ pūrṇaṃ tailapātraṃ yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: should be protected carefully by the physician from every improper regimen, like a young egg or like a full vessel of oil.
The physician should guard him carefully from every fault in conduct.
After that he should give sweet and pleasant foods, then the sour and salty tastes,
then again the sweet and bitter, and after that the astringent and pungent.
By the alternating use of tastes mutually opposed to one another, and of unctuous and dry substances,

children.text: vyatyāsād upayogena kramāt taṃ prakṛtiṃ nayet
children.translated_text: he should gradually bring that patient back to his natural condition.
When he can bear everything and has steady strength, he should be understood to have returned to normal.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparation of substances.
Thus, indeed, said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: dhanve sādhāraṇe deśe same sanmṛttike śucau
children.translated_text: In a dry or ordinary region, on level, clean ground with good soil,
free from cremation grounds, shrines, temples, pits, and anthills,
soft, with water flowing clockwise, covered with <s>kuśa</s> and <s>rohiṣa</s> grasses,
untilled by a plough, not trodden down, and not overborne by stronger trees,
a medicinal plant born there, furnished with color, taste, and the other proper qualities, is recommended.
It should not have been eaten by creatures, burned by forest fire, or spoiled by corrupting factors,
and should have been duly served by the elements, shade, sunlight, water, and so on, according to the season.
It should be deep-rooted with a great root, and situated toward the northern direction.
Then a person of auspicious conduct, faithful, clean, and fasting,

children.text: gṛhṇīyād auṣadhaṃ susthaṃ sthitaṃ kāle ca kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: should gather the healthy medicine and prepare it at the proper time.
It should be used fresh with its juice; if that is not available, it should not be more than a year old,
except in the case of jaggery, ghee, honey, grain, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>.

children.text: payo bāṣkayaṇaṃ grāhyaṃ viṇmūtraṃ tacca nīrujām
children.translated_text: Milk should be taken from a <s>bāṣkayaṇa</s> cow; feces and urine should be from healthy animals,
and marrow, bile, horns, hooves, and the like from animals of vigorous age and strength.
There are five sources of decoctions: the tastes other than salty.

children.text: rasaḥ kalkaḥ śṛtaḥ śītaḥ phāṇṭaśceti prakalpanā ||
children.translated_text: The preparations are juice, paste, boiled decoction, cold infusion, and hot infusion.
Thus the decoctions are fivefold; the preceding one in each case is stronger than the following.
That which flows, when pressed through cloth, from something freshly uprooted and pounded,

children.text: svarasaḥ sa samuddiṣṭaḥ kalkaḥ piṣṭo dravāplutaḥ
children.translated_text: is called fresh juice; paste is what has been ground and moistened with liquid.

children.text: cūrṇo 'plutaḥ śṛtaḥ kvāthaḥ śīto rātriṃ drave sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Powder is unmoistened; boiled decoction is <s>kvātha</s>; cold infusion is what has stood overnight in liquid.
But a <s>phāṇṭa</s> infusion, freshly expressed and strained,

children.text: yuñjyād vyādhyādibalatas tathā ca vacanaṃ muneḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be employed, in determining its measure, according to the disease and the patient's strength; and so too is the sage's statement:

children.text: mātrāyā na vyavasthāsti vyādhiṃ koṣṭhaṃ balaṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no fixed rule for dosage; having considered the disease, the bowels, strength, age,

children.text: ālocya deśakālau ca yojyā tadvacca kalpanā ||
children.translated_text: as well as place and time, the preparation should be applied accordingly.

children.text: madhyaṃ tu mānaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ svarasasya catuḥpalam
children.translated_text: The middle measure prescribed for fresh juice is four <s>pala</s>s.

children.text: peṣyasya karṣam āloḍyaṃ tad dravasya palatraye ||
children.translated_text: One <s>karṣa</s> of what is to be ground should be mixed in three <s>pala</s>s of that liquid.
A decoction should be made from one <s>pala</s> of substance with half a <s>prastha</s> of water, reduced until one quarter remains.

children.text: śītaṃ pale palaiḥ ṣaḍbhiścaturbhis tu tato 'param ||
children.translated_text: For a cold infusion, one <s>pala</s> is prepared with six <s>pala</s>s of water, and another kind with four.
But when no measure is stated for cooking a medicated fat, the paste, fat, and liquid should be used increased fourfold.
Again, <s>Śaunaka</s> teaches this:
When a fat is cooked with pure water, decoction, and fresh juice in order,

children.text: kalkasya yojayed aṃśaṃ caturthaṃ ṣaṣṭham aṣṭamam ||
children.translated_text: one should add the paste in portions of one fourth, one sixth, and one eighth.

children.text: pṛthak snehasamaṃ dadyāt pañcaprabhṛti tu dravam
children.translated_text: Separately, beginning with five times the fat, one should add the liquid equal to the fat.
When the paste is no longer taken up by the fingers, and when the fat on the fire makes no sound,
and when color and the other qualities are perfected, then one should quickly remove it.
For ghee, the sign is the subsiding of foam; for oil, its arising.

children.text: lehasya tantumattāpsu majjanaṃ saraṇaṃ na ca
children.translated_text: For a linctus, there is threadiness, sinking in water, and no spreading.
Cooking is of three kinds: mild, smooth, and rough-smooth.
It is mild when the residue is like paste; smooth when it resembles <s>madana</s> fruit.

children.text: kiṃcit sīdati kṛṣṇe ca vartyamāne ca paścimaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The last stage is when it sinks a little, becomes black, and can be rolled into a wick.

children.text: dagdho 'ta ūrdhvaṃ niṣkāryaḥ syād āmas tvagnisādakṛt
children.translated_text: Beyond this it is burned and should be discarded; if undercooked, it weakens the digestive fire.

children.text: mṛdur nasye kharo 'bhyaṅge pāne vastau ca cikkaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The soft preparation is for nasal therapy, the rough for massage, and the smooth for drinking and enema.

children.text: śāṇaṃ pāṇitalaṃ muṣṭiṃ kuḍavaṃ prastham āḍhakam
children.translated_text: One should know the measures <s>śāṇa</s>, palmful, fistful, <s>kuḍava</s>, <s>prastha</s>, <s>āḍhaka</s>,
<s>droṇa</s>, and <s>vaha</s> successively as each four times the previous one.

children.text: dviguṇaṃ yojayed ārdraṃ kuḍavādi tathā dravam
children.translated_text: Fresh substances should be used in double quantity, and liquids beginning with the <s>kuḍava</s> in the same way.
Water should be used for grinding and mixing, and in fat-cooking where no liquid is stated.

children.text: kalpayet sadṛśān bhāgān pramāṇaṃ yatra noditam
children.translated_text: Where no measure is stated, one should prepare equal parts.
A medicine whose preparation is not specified should be made into a paste.

children.text: aṅgānuktau tu mūlaṃ syād aprasiddhau tad eva tu
children.translated_text: When the part is not stated, the root should be used; when the plant is not well known, that same rule applies.

children.text: dvau śāṇau vaṭakaḥ kolaṃ badaraṃ draṃkṣaṇaśca tau ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>śāṇa</s>s are a <s>vaṭaka</s>, <s>kola</s>, <s>badara</s>, and <s>draṃkṣaṇa</s>; those two are equivalent.
<s>Akṣa</s>, <s>picu</s>, palmful, <s>suvarṇa</s>, and <s>kavaḍagraha</s>
mean a <s>karṣa</s>, also called <s>biḍālapadaka</s>, <s>tinduka</s>, and <s>pāṇimānikā</s>.
These are different words for the same meaning: <s>śukti</s>, <s>aṣṭamikā</s>, and <s>picu</s>;

children.text: palaṃ prakuñco bilvaṃ ca muṣṭirāmraṃ caturthikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>pala</s>, <s>prakuñca</s>, <s>bilva</s>, fistful, <s>āmra</s>, and <s>caturthikā</s>.

children.text: dve pale prasṛtas tau dvāvañjalis tau tu mānikā
children.translated_text: Two <s>pala</s>s are a <s>prasṛta</s>; two of those are an <s>añjali</s>, and those two are a <s>mānikā</s>.

children.text: āḍhakaṃ bhājanaṃ kaṃso droṇaḥ kumbho ghaṭo 'rmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āḍhaka</s>, vessel, <s>kaṃsa</s>, <s>droṇa</s>, jar, pot, and <s>armaṇa</s> are equivalent terms.

children.text: tulā palaśataṃ tāni viṃśatir bhāra ucyate
children.translated_text: A <s>tulā</s> is one hundred <s>pala</s>s; twenty of these are called a <s>bhāra</s>.
The earth is for the most part covered by the <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Vindhya</s> mountains.

children.text: saumyaṃ pathyaṃ ca tatrādyam āgneyaṃ vaindhyam auṣadham ||
children.translated_text: The former provides gentle and wholesome medicines, the <s>Vindhya</s> fiery ones.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the care of children.
Thus indeed spoke the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
As soon as a child is born, one should cleanse it of the fetal covering with rock salt and ghee,
and then sprinkle the infant, wearied by the strain of birth, with <s>balā</s> oil.
One should make stones sound near its ear-root,

children.text: athāsya dakṣiṇe karṇe mantram uccārayed imam ||
children.translated_text: and then recite this mantra into its right ear:
From limb after limb you have arisen; from the heart you are born.

children.text: ātmā vai putranāmāsi saṃjīva śaradāṃ śatam ||
children.translated_text: You are indeed the self called son; live for a hundred autumns.
You are one of a hundred years and a hundred lifespans; obtain long life.
May the constellations, the quarters, night, and day protect you.
When the child is settled, one should tie the navel cord with a thread at four finger-breadths,
cut it above that, and suspend it around the neck.

children.text: nābhiṃ ca kuṣṭhatailena secayet snāpayed anu
children.translated_text: One should anoint the navel with <s>kuṣṭha</s> oil, and then bathe the child
with a decoction of milky trees or with water scented with all perfumes.
It should be warm, made so by immersing heated silver and gold.
Then, with the right index finger, one should raise the palate and swaddle the child.
On the head one should place a pad soaked with oil, and administer something to be swallowed,
the size of a <s>hareṇu</s>, consecrated with a mantra for intelligence, lifespan, and strength.
Paste of <s>aindrī</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, with ghee and honey,
or powdered gold, <s>vacā</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, and <s>pathyā</s>,
should be licked with honey and ghee; or else powder of gold and <s>dhātrī</s> may be used.
Then one should make the child vomit the fetal fluid with ghee containing rock salt.
One should have the birth rites performed according to the <s>Prājāpatya</s> rule.
Because the channels located in the heart are open from birth,

children.text: tṛtīye 'hni caturthe vā strīṇāṃ stanyaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: women's breast milk begins to flow on the third or fourth day.
Therefore, on the first day, three times a day, one should feed the infant honey and ghee
mixed with <s>anantā</s> and purified by mantra.

children.text: dvitīye lakṣmaṇāsiddhaṃ tṛtīye ca ghṛtaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the second day, ghee prepared with <s>lakṣmaṇā</s> should be given, and on the third day ghee alone.
Before the infant has been allowed the breast,
one should administer fresh butter equal to the child's own palm, with breast milk as the after-drink, at two times.
The child should drink its mother's own milk, for that is sufficient for bodily growth.
If that is unavailable, two wet nurses should be appointed, both affectionate.
They should be without deformity, celibate, and similar in complexion and constitution,
free from illness, of middle age, with living children, and not greedy.
They should be carefully cared for with wholesome food and conduct.
Grief, anger, fasting, and exertion are causes of the loss of breast milk.
For breast milk, wines other than <s>sīdhu</s> and the meat juices of marshland animals are prescribed.
Milk and milk-producing herbs promote breast milk; grief and the like have the opposite effect.
For a woman who has eaten incompatible food, who is hungry, or whose mind is disturbed,
and for a pregnant woman whose bodily constituents are vitiated, the breast milk becomes disease-producing for the infant.

children.text: stanyābhāve payaśchāgaṃ gavyaṃ vā tadguṇaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: When breast milk is absent, the child should drink goat's milk, or cow's milk of similar qualities,
mixed with sugar and boiled with the lesser <s>pañcamūla</s>, or with the two <s>sthirā</s> herbs.
On the sixth night especially, after protective and offering rites have been performed,

children.text: jāgṛyur bāndhavās tasya dadhataḥ paramāṃ mudam ||
children.translated_text: his relatives should keep vigil, filled with the greatest joy.
When the tenth day is complete, according to the rites proper to his family,
one should perform the mother's rising from the birth chamber and the honored naming of the child.
He should wear on his limbs <s>manaḥśilā</s>, <s>rocana</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and sandalwood.
The name should be joined with the lunar mansion and its deity, or with a kinsman, and have corresponding syllables.
Then, by the signs stated in the distinctions of constitution, an intelligent physician
should examine the child's life-span, placing his head toward the east or the north.
Pillows, bedding, and garments should be clean, washed, without folds, and soft,
and they should be fumigated with substances that repel <s>rakṣas</s> beings.
A slaughtered crow, combined with <s>trivṛt</s>, is also recommended for fumigation.
The child should always wear auspicious jewels made from the horns of living rhinoceros and similar animals.
He should wear excellent herbs such as <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>aindrī</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>

children.text: hastābhyāṃ grīvayā mūrdhnā viśeṣāt satataṃ vacām ||
children.translated_text: on the hands, neck, and head, and especially <s>vacā</s>, at all times.
It produces long life, intelligence, memory, and health, and protects thoroughly against harmful spirits.
In the sixth, seventh, or eighth month, on an auspicious day, when the child is free from illness,
the physician should pierce the ears in the cold season, while the child sits in the nurse's lap and is comforted.

children.text: prāg dakṣiṇaṃ kumārasya bhiṣag vāmaṃ tu yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a boy he should pierce the right ear first, but for a girl the left.

children.text: dakṣiṇena dadhat sūcīṃ pālīm anyena pāṇinā
children.translated_text: Holding the needle in his right hand and the ear-lobe with the other hand,
he should pierce at the middle of the ear-seat, slightly toward the cheek.
At the natural opening, covered only by a thin membrane and made visible by the sun's rays,
properly marked with steady ghee and with lac dye,

children.text: vidhyed daivakṛte chidre sakṛd evarju lāghavāt
children.translated_text: he should pierce once only, straight and lightly, in the opening made by nature.

children.text: nordhvaṃ na pārśvato nādhaḥ sirās tatra hi saṃśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should not pierce upward, sideways, or downward, for blood vessels are situated there.
If black spots, vital points, or blood vessels are pierced, redness, pain, and fever arise,
with swelling, burning, agitation, stiffness of the neck, and convulsions.
For these, after distinguishing each disorder, he should quickly apply the appropriate treatment.

children.text: sthāne vyadhān na rudhiraṃ na rugrāgādisaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the piercing is in the proper place, there is no bleeding and no occurrence of pain, redness, and the like.
He should insert an oil-smeared thread drawn through the needle,
and sprinkle it with fresh oil; likewise, with a thicker awl,
he should pierce the ear-lobe of a child eating wholesome food, after first moving it about, if it is too thick.

children.text: vartis tryahāt tato rūḍhaṃ vardhayeta śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After three days he should replace it with a wick; when it has healed, he should enlarge it little by little.
Then, when the child's teeth have appeared, he should gradually wean him from the breast

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ yojayet kṣīram annaṃ ca laghu bṛṃhaṇam ||
children.translated_text: and give the milk mentioned earlier, along with light and nourishing food.
For a child without breast milk, a nourishing sweet ball should be prepared
with kernels of <s>priyāla</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, honey, parched grain, and sugar candy.
An appetite-kindling preparation is made with tender <s>bilva</s>, cardamom, sugar, parched grain, and roasted barley-meal.
A binding preparation is made with <s>dhātakī</s> flowers, sugar, parched grain, and nourishing gruel.
One should overcome the child's diseases with gentle medicines that do not cause distress.
Except in an urgent disease, one should especially avoid purgation.

children.text: trāsayen nāvidheyaṃ taṃ trastaṃ gṛhṇanti hi grahāḥ
children.translated_text: One should not frighten him when he is disobedient, for when frightened he is seized by <s>grahas</s>.
One should protect him from drafts through clothing, from contact with others, and from fasting.
Ghee cooked with <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>siddhārthaka</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, rock salt,
and <s>kaṇā</s>, when drunk, promotes speech, intelligence, and memory.
It promotes long life, destroys evil and <s>rakṣas</s> beings, and removes spirit-induced madness.
<s>Vacā</s>, <s>indulekhā</s>, <s>maṇḍūkī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
along with <s>brahmasomā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>brāhmī</s>, should be made into pastes, one <s>pala</s> each.
With these eight ingredients one should cook one <s>prastha</s> of ghee with four times as much milk.
When drunk, it brings good fortune and long life, and produces speech, intelligence, memory, and understanding.
The <s>Sārasvata</s> ghee is prepared with goat's milk, <s>abhayā</s>, the three pungents, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>ugrā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and rock salt;
it produces speech, intelligence, memory, and digestive fire.
Ghee cooked with <s>vacā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>śaṭhī</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>vellā</s>, <s>nāgara</s>,

children.text: apāmārgeṇa ca ghṛtaṃ sādhitaṃ pūrvavad guṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>apāmārga</s> has the same qualities as before.
Gold, white <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>arkapuṣpī</s> with <s>kāñcanā</s>,

children.text: hema matsyākṣakaḥ śaṅkhaḥ kaiḍaryaḥ kanakaṃ vacā
children.translated_text: gold, <s>matsyākṣaka</s>, conch, <s>kaiḍarya</s>, gold again, and <s>vacā</s>
are the four linctuses stated by quarters, soaked in honey and ghee.
Licked for a year, they are auspicious and produce physique, intelligence, strength, and complexion.
With <s>vacā</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, rock salt, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
and with <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and cumin, speech is purified when these are licked with ghee.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the prevention and treatment of diseases of children.
Thus indeed spoke the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
The child is said to be of three kinds: one maintained on milk, one on solid food, and one on both.
Health comes from these two when they are unvitiated; from them when vitiated, disease arises.

children.text: yad adbhirekatāṃ yāti na ca doṣairadhiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: Milk that becomes one with water and is not occupied by the <s>doṣas</s>

children.text: tad viśuddhaṃ payo vātād duṣṭaṃ tu plavate 'mbhasi ||
children.translated_text: is pure; but when vitiated by <s>vāta</s>, it floats on water.
It is astringent, frothy, dry, and causes obstruction of feces and urine.
When vitiated by <s>pitta</s>, it is hot, sour, and pungent, has yellow streaks in water, and causes burning.

children.text: kaphāt salavaṇaṃ sāndraṃ jale majjati picchilam
children.translated_text: When vitiated by <s>kapha</s>, it is slightly salty, thick, sinks in water, and is slimy.
From combination there are mixed signs; when all three signs are present, it is due to <s>sannipāta</s>.
When used, it produces those diseases according to the respective signs.

children.text: śiśos tīkṣṇam abhīkṣṇaṃ ca rodanāllakṣayed rujam ||
children.translated_text: From sharp and repeated crying one should infer pain in the infant.

children.text: sa yaṃ spṛśed bhṛśaṃ deśaṃ yatra ca sparśanākṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever region he touches intensely, and wherever he cannot bear being touched,

children.text: tatra vidyād rujaṃ mūrdhni rujaṃ cākṣinimīlanāt ||
children.translated_text: there one should know the pain to be; pain in the head is known from closing of the eyes.
Pain in the chest is indicated by pressing the tongue, lips, teeth, breath, and fists,
and pain in the abdomen by constipation, vomiting, biting at the breast, and rumbling of the intestines,
also by distension, bending of the back, and lifting up of the belly.
Pain in the bladder and private parts is indicated by retention of feces and urine, fright, and looking about in the directions.

children.text: atha dhātryāḥ kriyāṃ kuryād yathādoṣaṃ yathāmayam
children.translated_text: Then one should perform treatment for the wet nurse according to the <s>doṣa</s> and according to the disease.

children.text: tatra vātātmake stanye daśamūlaṃ tryahaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: When the breast milk is of a <s>vāta</s> nature, she should drink <s>daśamūla</s> for three days,
or <s>agni</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
