together with <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>vṛścikālī</s>, <s>kaṇa</s>, and <s>oṣaṇa</s>.
After that she should drink any ghee that removes disorders of <s>vāta</s>,

children.text: anu cācchasurām evaṃ snigdhāṃ mṛdu virecayet ||
children.translated_text: and then clear liquor; in this way, after she has been made unctuous, she should be gently purged.
Then enema therapy should be performed, along with fomentation and other measures that dispel <s>anila</s>.
The child should lick ghee mixed with powder of <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>ajamodā</s>, <s>sarala</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,

children.text: bālo lihyād ghṛtaṃ tair vā vipakvaṃ sasitopalam
children.translated_text: or ghee cooked with those drugs and with sugar candy.
When it is spoiled by <s>pitta</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>abhīru</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>candana</s>,
boiled as a decoction with <s>śārivā</s>, should be drunk by both the wet nurse and the child.
Or she may use <s>triphalā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>bhūnimba</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,
or the groups beginning with <s>śārivā</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, and <s>padmaka</s> respectively.
Ghees prepared with these, and purgation that removes <s>pitta</s>, are also to be used.
Cooling massages, anointings, and the like should be applied. In the case of a <s>śleṣman</s> condition, however,
one should make the child drink ghee combined with <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s> and rock salt,
or rock salt and <s>pippalī</s>, ground and mixed with honey.
Then one should smear the breasts, and the child's gum coverings, with <s>rāṭhapuṣpa</s> paste.

children.text: sukham evaṃ vamed bālaḥ tīkṣṇair dhātrīṃ tu vāmayet
children.translated_text: In this way the child will vomit easily; but the wet nurse should be made to vomit with sharp medicines.
Then, when mixed disorder is present, she should drink a decoction of the group beginning with <s>musta</s>.
Likewise she may use <s>tagara</s>, <s>pṛthvīkā</s>, <s>suradāru</s>, and <s>kaliṅgaka</s>,
or <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>musta</s>, <s>ṣaḍgranthā</s>, and the <s>pañcakola</s> group.
When the breast milk is polluted by all three <s>doṣas</s>, foul-smelling, immature, and like water,
the stool is passed as obstructed, clear, broken, and foamy.

children.text: śakṛn nānāvyathāvarṇaṃ mūtraṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ ghanam
children.translated_text: The feces has various pains and colors, and the urine is yellow, white, or thick.
Fever, loss of appetite, thirst, vomiting, dry eructation, and yawning arise,
as do aching of the limbs, tossing of the limbs, intestinal rumbling, trembling, and dizziness.
Inflammations of the nose, eyes, mouth, and the like also occur; they call that disease
<s>kṣīrālasaka</s>, a very dreadful and dangerous condition.
In that case one should quickly treat both the wet nurse and the child by emesis.

children.text: vihitāyāṃ ca saṃsargyāṃ vacādiṃ yojayed gaṇam
children.translated_text: And, when the prescribed mixed condition has been addressed, one should employ the group beginning with <s>vacā</s>,
or the group beginning with <s>niśā</s>, or <s>mādrī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, bitter drugs, <s>ghana</s>, and <s>āmaya</s>.
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>devāhva</s>, and <s>śārivā</s>,
together with <s>musta</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, and <s>indrayava</s>, are supreme removers of defects in breast milk.
If a complication persists, the physician who knows the proper time should counteract it according to the disease.
The eruption of teeth is also a cause of all diseases,
especially of fever, diarrhea, cough, vomiting, and headache,
and of conjunctival discharge, <s>pothakī</s>, and <s>visarpa</s>.
When the backs of cats break, when crests arise in peacocks,

children.text: dantodbhede ca bālānāṃ na hi kiṃcinna dūyate ||
children.translated_text: and when teeth erupt in children, there is truly nothing that does not suffer pain.
There the physician should distinguish according to <s>doṣa</s>, disease, aggravation, and danger,
and, after also considering place, time, and the other factors, should apply the treatment he has mastered.

children.text: ta eva doṣā dūṣyāśca jvarādyā vyādhayaśca yat
children.translated_text: Since the same <s>doṣas</s>, the same affected tissues, and the same diseases such as fever are involved,

children.text: atas tad eva bhaiṣajyaṃ mātrā tvasya kanīyasī ||
children.translated_text: the medicine is therefore the same; only its dose is smaller for the child.
Because of delicacy, small body size, and not yet eating all foods,
children are always unctuous from the use of ghee and milk.

children.text: sadyas tān vamanaṃ tasmāt pāyayen matimān mṛdu
children.translated_text: Therefore a wise physician should at once make them drink a mild emetic.
He should make a child satisfied with breast milk vomit, and also one who takes milk and milk-food,
after making him drink thin gruel; for one who eats solid food, the gruel should be combined with ghee.
When enema is appropriate, he should use it along with purgation; in place of a full oil enema, a small oil enema should be used.

children.text: yuñjyād virecanādīṃs tu dhātryā eva yathoditān
children.translated_text: But purgation and the other procedures should be applied to the wet nurse herself as stated above.
<s>Mūrvā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>kola</s>, bark of <s>jambū</s>, <s>dāru</s>, and mustard,
together with <s>pāṭhā</s>, licked with honey, are supreme removers of defects in breast milk.
One should rub the gum line with the powder together with honey,
or with a powder made from <s>pippalī</s>, <s>dhātakī</s> flowers, and <s>dhātrī</s> fruit.
Powder of <s>lāva</s>, <s>tittiri</s>, and <s>vallūra</s>, moistened with flower juice,
quickly makes the mouths of children like those with tooth filaments.
Ghee cooked with <s>vacā</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>ghana</s>,
and sweet substances is effective when teeth are being born.
<s>Rajanī</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>śreyasī</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants,
<s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, and <s>śatāhvā</s>, licked with honey and ghee,
is excellent for kindling the digestive seat and for directing <s>māruta</s> downward.
It removes diarrhea, fever, dyspnea, jaundice, pallor, and cough,
and is esteemed in all diseases of the child, giving strength and complexion.
With <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>, the two <s>balā</s> plants,
<s>mahāsahā</s>, <s>kṣudrasahā</s>, green gram, <s>bilva</s>, and unripe <s>bilva</s> fruit,
and with cotton fruits, boiled in water, ghee should be cooked, combined with milk and whey.
This quickly destroys the various diseases arising from the eruption of teeth.
It was composed by the elder <s>Kāśyapa</s> for illnesses occurring during teething.
In diseases connected with teething, one should not restrain or over-treat the child excessively,
for the diseases subside by themselves when the teeth have emerged.
For a child who has excessive day-sleep, cold water, and phlegmatic breast-milk,
when the channels that carry rasa are blocked by <s>kapha</s>,
loss of appetite, nasal catarrh, fever, and cough arise.
Thereafter the child wastes away, with an oily, pale-white face and eyes.
For one who is wasting, in loss of appetite and the like, one should administer <s>saindhava</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>śārṅgeṣṭā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>girikadambaka</s>,
with honey and ghee.
Also powdered <s>pañcakola</s> combined with <s>aśokarohiṇī</s>,
or powder of <s>badarī</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, and <s>dhātrī</s>, quickly mixed with ghee.
Half a <s>prastha</s> of ghee cooked with <s>sthirā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s>s, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>nata</s>,
and with <s>nicula</s>, <s>utpala</s>, <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, and <s>musta</s>, each one <s>kārṣa</s>,

children.text: siddhaṃ prasthārdham ājyasya srotasāṃ śodhanaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: is an excellent cleanser of the channels.
A ghee containing <s>siṃhī</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>surasā</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s> has the same qualities.
A ghee prepared with <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>utpala</s>, and <s>candana</s>,
as well as <s>tālīśa</s> and <s>śārivā</s>, overcomes consumption.
Ghee prepared with pastes of <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>madhūlikā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>devadāru</s>,
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
together with <s>śūrpaparṇī</s> and <s>viḍaṅga</s>,
in a decoction of a hare's head, is supremely nourishing for one who is wasting.
Oil cooked with <s>vacā</s>, <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>kāyasthā</s>, and <s>coraka</s>,
and with goat's urine and liquor, is useful for anointing.
One <s>prastha</s> of oil equal in quantity to lac juice, and four times as much whey,
with equal parts of <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>niśā</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>kauntī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>abda</s>, and <s>candana</s>,
together with <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>,

children.text: siddhaṃ lākṣādikaṃ nāma tailam abhyañjanād idam
children.translated_text: when cooked, is this oil called <s>Lākṣādika</s>; by anointing,
it strengthens and removes fever, wasting, insanity, dyspnea, epilepsy, and <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>rākṣasa</s>s, and <s>bhūta</s>s, and is also recommended for pregnant women.
One should make a child lick <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, and <s>pippalī</s> with honey,
or <s>ativiṣā</s> alone, when he is afflicted by cough, fever, and vomiting.

children.text: pītaṃ pītaṃ vamati yaḥ stanyaṃ taṃ madhusarpiṣā ||
children.translated_text: A child who vomits breast-milk every time after drinking it
should be made to lick the juice of two <s>vārtākī</s> fruits and <s>pañcakola</s>, with honey and ghee.
In the same way he should lick <s>pippalī</s>, the five salts, <s>kṛmijit</s>, and <s>pāribhadraka</s>,

children.text: tadvallihyāt tathā vyoṣaṃ maṣīṃ vā romacarmaṇām
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>vyoṣa</s>, or the ash of hair and skin,
obtained from a porcupine, hedgehog, iguana, bear, or peacock.
Ghee cooked with milk in the decoction produced from <s>khadira</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>tālīśa</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>candana</s>
checks vomiting.

children.text: sadanto jāyate yas tu dantāḥ prāg yasya cottarāḥ
children.translated_text: But when a child is born with teeth, or when his upper teeth come first,

children.text: kurvīta tasminn utpāte śāntiṃ taṃ ca dvijātaye ||
children.translated_text: one should perform a pacification for that portent, and should give that child, together with a fee, to a twice-born man,

children.text: dadyāt sadakṣiṇaṃ bālaṃ naigameṣaṃ ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: and worship <s>Naigameṣa</s>.
Aggravated <s>kapha</s> in the flesh of the palate produces <s>tālukaṇṭaka</s>.
Because of it, a depression of the palate-region appears in the head.
There is falling of the palate, aversion to the breast, difficult drinking, and liquid stool,
thirst, itching in the mouth, eye-pain, difficulty holding up the neck, and vomiting.
In that condition, after lifting up the palate, one should rub it with <s>yavakṣāra</s> and honey.
Likewise one should rub the palate with <s>kaṇā</s>, dry ginger, cow-dung juice, and rock salt.
Ginger, turmeric, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>, ground with shoots of the banyan,

children.text: baddhvā gośakṛtā liptam kukūle svedayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: should be tied up, smeared with cow dung, and steamed in hot chaff; then

children.text: rasena limpet tālvāsyaṃ netre ca pariṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: one should smear the palate and mouth with the juice, and sprinkle the eyes.
Having drunk a paste of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, mixed with honey,
with breast-milk, the child is freed from <s>tālukaṇṭaka</s>.
From coating by feces, or from sweating, there arises in the anus a copper-colored sore, born of blood and <s>kapha</s>,
internal, itchy, and attended by many complications.
Some call this <s>mātṛkādoṣa</s>; others call it <s>ahipūtana</s>.

children.text: pṛṣṭhārur gudakuṭṭaṃ ca kecicca tam anāmikam ||
children.translated_text: Some call it <s>pṛṣṭhāru</s>, <s>gudakuṭṭa</s>, or <s>anāmika</s>.
In that condition the nurse's milk should be purified with medicines that remove <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
Cooled boiled water, mixed with cold water, should be used as the intervening drink.
With that, and with <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s> together with honey, one should smear the sore.
After washing it with a decoction of <s>triphala</s>, <s>badarī</s>, and <s>plakṣa</s> bark,
one should apply <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>ala</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,
ground in sour liquids, or sprinkle them on in powdered form.
Alternatively, very finely powdered <s>yaṣṭī</s>, conch shell, <s>sauvīraka</s>, and collyrium may be used,
or <s>śārivā</s> and conch-navel, or the bark of <s>asana</s>.
When redness and itching are intense, one should cause bloodletting with a leech.
Everything that conquers a <s>pitta</s>-type sore is recommended in <s>gudakuṭṭaka</s>.
Ghee cooked with <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vella</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s>s, <s>musta</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
with <s>bilva</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and <s>vṛścikālī</s>,
when licked in the proper dose, frees one from diseases arising from clay.

children.text: vyādher yadyasya bhaiṣajyaṃ stanas tena pralepitaḥ
children.translated_text: For whatever disease there is a particular medicine, the breast should be smeared with that medicine,

children.text: sthito muhūrtaṃ dhauto 'nu pītas taṃ taṃ jayed gadam ||
children.translated_text: left for a moment, then washed; when the child drinks afterward, it overcomes that particular disease.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the prevention of child-seizing grahas.
Thus, indeed, said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
In ancient times, for the protection of <s>Guha</s>, they were fashioned by the Trident-bearing Lord:
five grahas in male form and seven grahas in female form.
<s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, the one called <s>Meṣa</s>, the Dog-graha, and the one named <s>Pitṛ</s>;
<s>Śakuni</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Śītapūtanā</s>, <s>Dṛṣṭipūtanā</s>,
<s>Mukhamaṇḍitikā</s>, likewise <s>Revatī</s> and <s>Śuṣkarevatī</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ grahīṣyatāṃ rūpaṃ pratataṃ rodanaṃ jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those about to be seized by them, continual crying and fever are the general signs,
as are fright, yawning, movements of the eyebrows, and dejection.
Foaming at the mouth, discharge, upward-looking eyes, biting of the lips and teeth, and wakefulness;
crying, cooing, aversion to breast milk, and alteration of the voice;
and sudden scratching all around, with the nails, of the limbs of his own nurse.
There, with discharge from one eye, he repeatedly tosses his head;
one side is stricken, his limbs are rigid, he is sweaty, and his neck is bent down.
He gnashes his teeth, hates the breast, becomes frightened, and cries in a distorted voice.

children.text: vakravaktro vaman lālāṃ bhṛśam ūrdhvaṃ nirīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: With a crooked mouth, vomiting saliva, he gazes intensely upward.
The child is agitated, smells of fat and blood, has clenched fists, and passes stool.
One eye, cheek, and brow tremble, and both eyes are reddened.

children.text: skandārtas tena vaikalyaṃ maraṇaṃ vā bhaveddhruvam
children.translated_text: He is afflicted by <s>Skanda</s>; through him deformity or death will certainly occur.
Loss of consciousness, frequent pulling out of the hair, bending of the neck,
and, when he yawns with the body bent down, the passing of feces and urine;
foamy vomiting, upward gaze, dancing movements of the hands, brows, and feet;
biting the breast and his own tongue, agitation, fever, and wakefulness;
and a smell of pus and blood: these are the signs of <s>Skandāpasmāra</s>.
Distension, twitching of the hands and feet, and foamy vomiting;
thirst, clenching of the fists, diarrhea, weakness of voice, and discoloration;
cooing, groaning, vomiting, cough, hiccup, and wakefulness;
biting the lips, contraction and stiffness of the limbs, and a goat-like smell;

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ nirīkṣya hasanaṃ madhye vinamanaṃ jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: looking upward and laughing, bending in the middle, fever,
fainting, and swelling of one eye: this is the form of <s>Naigameṣa-graha</s>.
Trembling, bristling of the body hair, sweating, and closing the eyes;
stretching outward, biting the tongue, and making sounds inside the throat;
running, a fecal smell, and crying like a dog occur in <s>Śunī</s>.

children.text: romaharṣo muhus trāsaḥ sahasā rodanaṃ jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Horripilation, repeated fright, sudden crying, fever,
cough, diarrhea, vomiting, yawning, thirst, and the smell of a corpse;
convulsion and tossing of the limbs, wasting, stiffness, and discoloration;
clenching of the fists and discharge from the eyes occur in a child with <s>Pitṛgraha</s>.
Slackness of the limbs, diarrhea, and sores on the tongue, palate, and throat;

children.text: sphoṭāḥ sadāharukpākāḥ saṃdhiṣu syuḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: blisters with burning, pain, and suppuration repeatedly arise in the joints.

children.text: niśyahni pravilīyante pāko vaktre gude 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: They suppurate and liquefy by night and day, and there may also be suppuration in the mouth or anus.
Fear, a bird-like smell, and fever occur in <s>Śakuni-graha</s>.

children.text: pūtanāyāṃ vamiḥ kampas tandrā rātrau prajāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Pūtanā</s> there are vomiting, tremor, drowsiness, and wakefulness at night;
hiccup, abdominal distension, looseness of stool, thirst, and retention of urine;
slack limbs with bristling body hair, and a foul smell like that of a crow.
In <s>Śītapūtanā</s> there are tremor, crying, and looking sideways;
thirst, gurgling in the intestines, diarrhea, and a fetid smell like fat.
One side becomes cold and the other hot.
In <s>Andhapūtanā</s> there are vomiting, fever, cough, and little sleep;
looseness, discoloration, and foul odor of the feces, and wasting of the body;
weakness of sight, severe pain, itching, the appearance of pustules, and swelling;
hiccup, agitation, aversion to the breast, discoloration, and a sharp voice;
trembling, a fishy smell, or else a sour smell.
In <s>Mukhamaṇḍitā</s>, the hands, feet, and face become attractive;
the abdomen is covered with dark-looking veins, and there is fever.
There is anorexia, languishing of the limbs, and a smell like cow urine.
In <s>Revatī</s> there is blackish-blue coloration and rubbing of the ears, nose, and eyes;
cough, hiccup, twitching of the eyes, crookedness of the mouth, and redness;

children.text: bastagandho jvaraḥ śoṣaḥ purīṣaṃ haritaṃ dravam ||
children.translated_text: a goat-like smell, fever, and wasting; the feces become green and liquid.
In <s>Śuṣkarevatī</s> there arises, in order, wasting of the whole body,
falling of the hair, aversion to food, weakness of voice, and discoloration;
feces of various colors, and knots and veins in the abdomen;
crying, a vulture-like smell, and long persistence.

children.text: udare granthayo vṛttā yasya nānāvidhaṃ śakṛt ||
children.translated_text: If a child has round knots in the abdomen and feces of many kinds,

children.text: jihvāyā nimnatā madhye śyāvaṃ tālu ca taṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: with the tongue depressed in the middle and the palate dark, one should abandon him.
The child who wastes away although eating many kinds of food,
seized by thirst and with emaciated eyes, is killed by <s>Śuṣkarevatī</s>.
The desire for violence, sexual pleasure, or worship is the cause of seizure by a <s>graha</s>.

children.text: tatra hiṃsātmake bālo mahān vā srutanāsikaḥ
children.translated_text: When it is violent in nature, whether the patient is a child or an adult, his nose runs;
his tongue is wounded, he makes loud noises, is miserable, and has tearful eyes.
He becomes discolored, weak in speech, and foul-smelling.

children.text: kṣāmo mūtrapurīṣaṃ svaṃ mṛdnāti na jugupsate ||
children.translated_text: Emaciated, he smears his own urine and feces and feels no disgust.

children.text: hastau codyamya saṃrabdho hantyātmānaṃ tathā param
children.translated_text: Raising his hands in agitation, he strikes himself and also another person.
Likewise he may do so with weapons, sticks, and the like, or he may enter a blazing fire.

children.text: apsu majjet patet kūpe kuryād anyacca tadvidham
children.translated_text: He may sink in water, fall into a well, or do something else of that kind.
He develops thirst, burning, delusion, and vomiting of pus,

children.text: raktaṃ ca sarvamārgebhyo riṣṭotpattiṃ ca taṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: blood from all channels, and fatal signs; one should abandon him.
Fond of solitude, women, sexual pleasure, conversation, perfumes, garlands, and ornaments,
cheerful and peaceful, he is hard to cure when afflicted by one desiring sexual pleasure.
Miserable, rubbing his face, with dry lips, throat, and palate,
he looks about suspiciously, cries, broods, and falls into dejection.
Even when he longs for food, he does not eat much of the food that is given.
One should know him to be seized by one desiring offerings; he is easily treated.
One should overcome the one wishing to kill by oblations empowered with perfected mantras.
But the other two should be treated according to their desire, by gifts of sexual pleasure, offerings, and the like.

children.text: atha sādhyagrahaṃ bālaṃ vivikte śaraṇe sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Now a child seized by a curable <s>graha</s>, staying in a secluded shelter,
in a place sprinkled and swept three times a day, with fire always present,
strewn with ash, flowers, leaves, seeds, food, and mustard,
purified of evil by a lamp burning with demon-destroying oil,
and served by attendants who abstain from sexual intercourse, wine, and meat,
the child, anointed with old ghee and sprinkled with pleasant water
boiled with <s>balā</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>vaijayantī</s>, and <s>nṛpadruma</s>,
with <s>pāribhadraka</s>, <s>kaṭvaṅga</s>, <s>jambū</s>, <s>varuṇa</s>, and <s>kaṭtṛṇa</s>,
with <s>kapotavaṅkā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, and <s>madhuśigru</s>,
with <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>mahāśvetā</s>, <s>kapittha</s>, and milky trees,
and with <s>kadamba</s> and <s>karañja</s>, should be fumigated after bathing.
With skins of leopard, tiger, snake, lion, and bear, mixed with ghee,
with <s>pūtidaśāṅga</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>bhallāta</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s>,
together with <s>kuṣṭha</s> and ghee, the fumigation releases all grahas.
Mustard seeds, neem leaves, the root of <s>aśvakhurā</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
birch bark, and ghee make a fumigation that wards off all grahas.
With <s>anantā</s>, mango stone, <s>tagara</s>, black pepper, and the sweet group,

children.text: śṛgālavinnā mustā ca kalkitais tair ghṛtaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: and with <s>śṛgālavinnā</s> and <s>mustā</s>, one should cook ghee from their paste,
joined with decoction of <s>daśamūla</s> and milk; that is supreme for conquering grahas.
From a decoction of the two <s>rāsnā</s>s, <s>aṃśumatī</s>, the elder five roots, <s>balā</s>, and <s>ghana</s>,
one should cook ghee with pastes of <s>śārivā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
<s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>dāru</s>,

children.text: sagranthikaiḥ sendrayavaiḥ śiśos tat satataṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: along with <s>granthika</s> and <s>indrayava</s>; that is always beneficial for a child,
removing all diseases and grahas, kindling digestion, and giving strength and complexion.
With <s>śārivā</s>, <s>surabhi</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and mustard,
and with <s>vacā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>surasa</s>, one should cook ghee.
It destroys all grahas when drunk and when used for anointing.
Cow horn, hide, hair, snake slough, and the dung of a <s>vṛṣadaṃśa</s>,
neem leaves, ghee, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>madana</s>, and the two <s>bṛhatī</s>s,
cotton seed, barley, goat hair, <s>devāhva</s>, and mustard,
peacock feathers, <s>śrīvāsa</s>, chaff-hair, and <s>rāmaṭha</s>,
steeped in goat urine in an earthen pot and finely powdered,
are beneficial as fumigation in all spirit-afflictions and in intermittent fever.

children.text: ghṛtāni bhūtavidyāyāṃ vakṣyante yāni tāni ca
children.translated_text: And the ghees that will be taught in <s>Bhūtavidyā</s>

children.text: yuñjyāt tathā baliṃ homaṃ snapanaṃ mantratantravit ||
children.translated_text: should likewise be used, as well as offering, oblation, and bathing, by one skilled in mantra and tantra.
Bark and leaves of <s>pūtikarañja</s>, from the milky trees and also from <s>barbarā</s>,
and from <s>tumbī</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, <s>araluka</s>, <s>śamī</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and <s>kapittha</s>:

children.text: utkvāthya toyaṃ tad rātrau bālānāṃ snapanaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: boiling these, that water is auspicious at night for bathing children.
Even after the departure of a graha, one should treat the complications, according to their difficulty,
with the medicines taught in the section on preventing children's diseases.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on knowledge of spirits.
Thus indeed spoke the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
One should observe in a person knowledge, discernment, speech, activity, strength, and manliness:
where these are non-human, there one should call it a <s>bhūtagraha</s>.
By the form, nature, language, gait, and other actions of the being,
whichever one he imitates, one should declare him possessed by that one.
It is of eighteen kinds, according to divisions such as gods and <s>dānava</s>s.
The cause of its attachment is either immediate or done previously,
especially an error of judgment, born from desire and the like.
Having lost <s>dharma</s>, vows, and proper conduct, he transgresses even those worthy of reverence.
Even gods and others strike down that sinful, self-injuring person
who has broken bounds; grahas strike where there is an opening.
An opening is the undertaking of sinful acts, the ripening of unwanted karma,
staying alone in an empty place, or in cremation grounds and the like at night,
being naked, reviling the teacher, and improper indulgence in sexual pleasure,
worshipping deities and the like while impure, and contact with another's puerperal impurity,
and defective performance of homa, mantra, offering, and worship;
in short, transgression of the conduct taught beginning with daily regimen.
The gods seize a person on the bright first and thirteenth lunar days;
<s>dānava</s> grahas on the bright thirteenth and dark twelfth;

children.text: gandharvās tu caturdaśyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ coragāḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>gandharva</s>s on the fourteenth, and serpents again on the twelfth;
the lords of wealth on the fifth, bright seventh, and eleventh;
<s>brahmarākṣasa</s>s on the bright eighth, fifth, and full-moon days;
<s>rakṣas</s>es, <s>piśāca</s>s, and others on the dark ninth, twelfth, and festival days;
the <s>Pitṛ</s>s on the tenth and new-moon days, and others on the eighth and ninth;
teachers, elders, and the like are generally to be recognized at the twilights.
One whose face is like a blossoming lotus, with a gentle gaze, not prone to anger,
speaking little, with little sweat, feces, and urine, and without desire for food,
devoted to gods and twice-borns, pure, and speaking refined Sanskrit,
keeping his eyes closed for a long time, fragrant, and bestowing boons,
fond of white garlands and garments, rivers, mountains, and tall buildings,
sleepless and unassailable, should be known as brought under the power of a god.
One with crooked gaze, evil-minded, hating teachers, gods, and twice-borns,
fearless, proud, heroic, angry, and determined,

children.text: rudraḥ skando viśākho 'ham indro 'ham iti vādinam
children.translated_text: saying, "I am <s>Rudra</s>, I am <s>Skanda</s>, I am <s>Viśākha</s>, or I am <s>Indra</s>,"
and fond of liquor and meat should be known as seized by a <s>daitya</s>-graha.
One of good conduct, fragrant, joyful, making song and dance,
fond of bathing and gardens, with red garments, garlands, and unguents,
and delighting in erotic play, one should call inhabited by a <s>gandharva</s>.
If he has red eyes, is irascible, has a fixed gaze, moves crookedly, and is restless,
breathes constantly, lets his tongue loll, and licks the corners of his mouth,
is fond of milk, jaggery, and bathing, and lies with his face downward,
one should know him to be possessed by an <s>uraga</s> (serpent-being), and to be frightened by parasols.
If his eyes are rolling, frightened, and red, while he has an auspicious fragrance and strong radiance,
is fond of dancing, stories, singing, bathing, garlands, and anointing,
likes fish and meat, and is joyful, satisfied, strong, and free from distress,
moves the tips of his hands and says, "To whom shall I give something, and what?",
speaks in secret and shows contempt for physicians and twice-born men,
is only slightly angry and moves quickly, one should know him as seized by a <s>yakṣa</s>.
If he loves laughter and dancing, behaves fiercely, and strikes at vulnerable places,
abuses others, moves swiftly, and hates gods, twice-born men, and physicians,
strikes himself with sticks, weapons, and the like, and utters the sound "bhoḥ",
while reciting śāstra and Veda, one should know him to be seized by <s>brahmarākṣasas</s>.
If he has an angry look, raises his frowning brows, and is agitated,
strikes, runs about, makes noises, and has a terrifying face,
is strong even without food, has lost sleep, and roams at night,
is shameless, impure, bold, cruel, and harsh in speech,
is wrathful and fond of red garlands, women, blood, liquor, and meat,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca raktaṃ māṃsaṃ vālihānaṃ daśanacchadau
children.translated_text: and, on seeing blood or meat, licks his lips,
and laughs at meal-time, one should say that he is possessed by a <s>rākṣasa</s>.
If his mind is unsettled, he does not stay in one place, and he runs about,
is fond of leftovers, dancing, music, laughter, liquor, and meat,
has a dejected face when rebuked and cries without cause,
scratches himself with his nails, and has a rough, ruined body and voice,
announces pains and other troubles, and speaks in both coherent and incoherent ways,
has lost memory, delights in empty places, is fickle, naked, and dirty,
wears rags from the road and is adorned with garlands of grass,
mounts a wooden horse and also a rubbish heap,
and eats a great deal, one should recognize him as possessed by a <s>piśāca</s>.
If he has the appearance, actions, and smell of a <s>preta</s>, is afraid, hates food,

children.text: tṛṇacchidaṃ ca pretena gṛhītaṃ naram ādiśet
children.translated_text: and cuts grass, one should declare that man to be seized by a <s>preta</s>.
If he babbles much, has a blackened face, and walks with a drooping gait,
with swollen, hanging testicles, one should say that he is possessed by a <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>.
If he takes up sticks, clods, and the like, wanders about, and wears rags,
runs naked, has a terrified look, and is adorned with grass,
frequents cremation grounds, deserted shrines, roads, and solitary trees,
has his eyes constantly fixed on sesame-food, liquor, and meat,
and says harsh things, one should know him to be possessed by a <s>niṣāda</s>.
If he begs for water and food and has frightened, blood-red eyes,
and speaks fierce words, one should know that man to be afflicted by <s>aukiraṇa</s>.
If he delights in perfumes and garlands, speaks the truth, and trembles,
and sleeps a great deal, one should know him to be brought under the control of a <s>vetāla</s>.
If his gaze is not clear, his face is pitiable, and his palate is dry,
his eyes and eyelashes tremble, he is sleepy, and his digestive fire is weak,
he wears his garment in the inauspicious reversed fashion and is fond of sesame, meat, and jaggery,
and his speech falters, one should know him to be under the control of a <s>pitṛgraha</s>.
According to the form of a curse from teachers, elders, seers, or accomplished beings, or according to his preoccupation,
one should identify that particular <s>graha</s> by his speech, food, and behavior, each in its own way.
One who is accompanied by a band of children, naked, with hair standing up,
of disordered mind, long afflicted, and possessed by a <s>graha</s>, should be abandoned.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the countermeasures against <s>bhūtas</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
A person wishing to avoid harm should conquer a <s>bhūta</s> by recitation, oblations, offerings, and vows,
and by austerity, good conduct, meditation, generosity, knowledge, compassion, and the like.
<s>Hiṅgu</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>āla</s>, <s>nepālī</s>, garlic, the root of <s>arka</s>, and <s>jaṭā</s>,
<s>ajalomī</s>, <s>sagolomī</s>, <s>bhūtakeśī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>latā</s>,
<s>kukkuṭī</s>, the herb called <s>sarpagandhā</s>, sesame seeds, <s>kāṇā</s> and <s>vikāṇikā</s>,
<s>vajraproktā</s>, <s>vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, and also <s>mohanavallī</s>,
<s>srotoja</s> collyrium, <s>rakṣoghna</s>, and any other medicine that destroys harmful spirits,
and from donkey, horse, dog, sheep, camel, bear, iguana, mongoose, and porcupine,
as well as from leopard, cat, cow, lion, tiger, and sea creatures,
the hide, bile, teeth, and nails: with this group one should prepare ghee.

children.text: purāṇam athavā tailaṃ navaṃ tat pānanasyayoḥ
children.translated_text: Or old oil, or fresh oil, should be used for drinking and nasal administration,

children.text: abhyaṅge ca prayoktavyam eṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ ca dhūpane ||
children.translated_text: and also for massage; the powder of these substances should be used for fumigation.
With these one should use a pill for collyrium and for forceful nasal application,

children.text: pralepe kalkam eteṣāṃ kvāthaṃ ca pariṣecane ||
children.translated_text: their paste for anointing, and their decoction for sprinkling.
This procedure brings <s>graha</s>-insanities, together with epilepsy, to pacification.
<s>Gajāhvā</s>, root of <s>pippalī</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and mustard seeds,
ground with the bile of iguana, mongoose, cat, and fish,
should be applied in nasal therapy, massage, and sprinkling as removers of <s>grahas</s>.
<s>Siddhārthaka</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, and the two <s>rajanīs</s>,
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>śvetakaṭabhī</s>, <s>varā</s>, and <s>śvetādrikarṇikā</s>,
the leaves of the neem, and the seeds of <s>naktamāla</s> and <s>śirīṣa</s>,
<s>surāhva</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and ghee, cooked with these in four times as much cow urine,

children.text: siddhaṃ siddhārthakaṃ nāma pāne nasye ca yojitam
children.translated_text: becomes the preparation named <s>Siddhārthaka</s>; administered as a drink and as nasal medicine,

children.text: grahān sarvān nihantyāśu viśeṣād āsurān grahān ||
children.translated_text: it quickly destroys all <s>grahas</s>, especially the <s>āsura</s> grahas,
and also sorcery, misfortune, poison, insanity, fever, epilepsy, and evil.
An <s>agada</s> (antidotal preparation) prepared with these very medicines and goat's urine
is applied for drinking, <s>nasya</s> (nasal therapy), collyrium, paste, bathing, and rubbing.

children.text: guṇaiḥ pūrvavad uddiṣṭo rājadvāre ca siddhikṛt ||
children.translated_text: It is taught to have the same virtues as before, and it brings success at the royal gate.
White mustard, the three pungents, <s>vacā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, the two <s>niśās</s>, asafoetida, and onion bulb;

children.text: bījaṃ karañjāt kusumaṃ śirīṣāt phalaṃ ca valkaṃ ca kapitthavṛkṣāt ||
children.translated_text: seed from <s>karañja</s>, flower from <s>śirīṣa</s>, and the fruit and bark of the <s>kapittha</s> tree;

children.text: samāṇimanthaṃ sanataṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ śyoṇākamūlaṃ kiṇihī sitā ca
children.translated_text: together with <s>aṇimantha</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>śyoṇāka</s> root, <s>kiṇihī</s>, and sugar:

children.text: bastasya mūtreṇa subhāvitaṃ tat pittena gavyena guḍān vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: when this has been well impregnated with goat's urine, one should make pills with cow's bile.
Those pills cure bad wounds, insanity, darkness of sight and night-blindness, those who have hanged themselves or whose bodies have sunk in water,
those struck by poisoned weapons, and those bitten by enraged snakes, through collyrium, <s>nasya</s>, and pastes.
A fumigation made with cotton seed, peacock feathers, <s>bṛhatī</s>, used garlands, <s>piṇḍītaka</s> bark, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>vṛṣadaṃśa</s> dung, husk, <s>vacā</s>, hair, and snake slough,
with <s>nāgendradvijaśṛṅga</s>, asafoetida, and black pepper, all in equal measure,
is supreme for destroying fever caused by <s>Skanda</s>, madness, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and possession by gods.
With the three pungents, <s>dala</s>, saffron, <s>granthika</s>, alkali, <s>siṃhī</s>, <s>niśā</s>, deodar, the two white mustards, water, and the herb called <s>Śakrāhvā</s>,
with <s>sati</s>, garlic, the three fruits, <s>uśīra</s>, bitter <s>vacā</s>, blue vitriol, licorice, <s>balā</s>, red arsenic, cardamom, realgar, and lotus,
and with curds, <s>tagara</s>, essence of <s>madhūka</s>, <s>priyāhvā</s>, poison-name herbs, antidotal substances, <s>tārkṣyaśaila</s>, and <s>cavyā</s>, all ground into a paste,

children.text: ghṛtam anavam aśeṣamūtrāṃśasiddhaṃ mataṃ bhūtarāvāhvayaṃ pānatas tad grahaghnaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: fresh ghee cooked with all kinds of urine is considered <s>Bhūtarāva</s>; when drunk, it is supreme for destroying <s>grahas</s>.
With <s>nata</s>, licorice, <s>karañja</s>, lac, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, asafoetida, white mustard, <s>siṃhī</s>, the two <s>niśās</s>, and <s>tārohiṇī</s>,
with jujube, the three pungent fruits, <s>kāṇḍadāru</s>, <s>kṛmighna</s>, <s>ajagandhā</s>, <s>amarā</s>, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, neem, water, and <s>Indrāhvā</s>,

with the flowers and seeds of the <s>gadaśuka</s> tree, strong licorice, <s>adrikarṇī</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>bilva</s>, all in equal parts and ground, ghee is cooked with the class of urines.

children.text: vidhivinihitam āśu sarvaiḥ kramair yojitaṃ hanti sarvagrahonmādakuṣṭhajvarāṃs tan mahābhūtarāvaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Properly prepared and applied quickly by all the prescribed methods, it destroys all <s>grahas</s>, insanity, skin disease, and fever; it is remembered as <s>Mahābhūtarāva</s>.

children.text: grahā gṛhṇanti ye yeṣu teṣāṃ teṣu viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: On whatever days particular <s>grahas</s> seize people,
on those days especially the physician should perform offerings, oblations, and the like for them.
Bathing, garments, fat, meat, liquor, milk, molasses, and so on:

children.text: rocate yad yadā yebhyas tat teṣām āharet tadā ||
children.translated_text: whatever is pleasing to whichever beings at a given time, that he should bring for them then.
Jewels, perfume, garlands, seeds, honey, and ghee,
and all kinds of foods for all of them: this is the general rule.
For gods, seers, teachers, elders, and perfected beings, in a temple of the gods,
in the northern direction, and there too to the deity, he should offer a <s>bali</s> (offering).
In the western direction, at the proper time, for a <s>daitya</s> or <s>bhūta</s>, at a crossroads,
and for a <s>gandharva</s>, on a cattle path, he should offer a <s>bali</s> together with clothes and ornaments.
For a <s>Pitṛ</s> or <s>Nāga</s> graha, he should make the offering in a river; for nāgas, in the southeast.
For a <s>yakṣa</s>, it should be in a yakṣa shrine or at the confluence of rivers.
For a <s>rākṣasa</s>, it should be at a crossroads and in terrifying wilderness places.
For rākṣasas it is in the southern direction, but for <s>brahmarakṣasas</s> in the eastern direction.
For a <s>piśāca</s>, it should be in an empty house, taking up the western direction.
Pure white garlands, perfumes, milk-rice, and boiled rice

children.text: dadhi chattraṃ ca dhavalaṃ devānāṃ baliriṣyate
children.translated_text: with curds, and a white umbrella: these are regarded as the <s>bali</s> for gods.
With asafoetida, mustard, <s>ṣaḍgrantha</s>, and the three pungents, each measured at half a <s>pala</s>,
one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee in four times as much cow's urine.
By drinking, nasal instillation, and anointing with it, there is release from a divine <s>graha</s>.
For <s>nasya</s> and collyrium in the case of a <s>daitya</s>, <s>vacā</s>, asafoetida, and garlic are prepared with goat's urine;
for a <s>daitya</s>, a fruitful <s>bali</s> is made with <s>uśīra</s>, lotus, and blue lotus.
For nāgas, the offering consists of jasmine, parched grain, molasses cakes, and rice cooked with molasses,
with sweet milk-rice, honey, milk, black earth, and <s>nāgakesara</s>.
The <s>bali</s> uses <s>vacā</s>, lotus, <s>uśīra</s>, and red lotus petals.

children.text: śvetapattraṃ ca lodhraṃ ca tagaraṃ nāgasarṣapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: White-leaved plant, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>tagara</s>, and <s>nāgasarṣapa</s>
ground with cold water are suitable for nasal instillation and collyrium.
For yakṣas, there should be rice mixed with milk, curds, and ghee, and guggul resin,
deodar, blue lotus, lotus, <s>uśīra</s>, cloth, and gold.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ ca balir yojyo mūtrājyakṣīram ekataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gold too should be used in the <s>bali</s>; urine, ghee, and milk are cooked together
in equal measure, and this is good for drinking, nasal instillation, and anointing.

children.text: harītakī haridre dve laśuno maricaṃ vacā ||
children.translated_text: Harītakī, the two haridrās, garlic, black pepper, and <s>vacā</s>,
and neem leaves, ground with goat's urine, are used for nasal instillation and collyrium.
The <s>bali</s> for a <s>brahmarakṣas</s> is a full <s>āḍhaka</s> of prepared barley,

children.text: toyasya kumbhaḥ palalaṃ chattraṃ vastram vilepanam
children.translated_text: a water pot, minced meat, an umbrella, cloth, and unguent.
In a decoction of twenty <s>palas</s> of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> plant one should cook half-<s>pala</s> portions
of the three pungents, <s>triphala</s>, asafoetida, <s>ṣaḍgrantha</s>, anise, and mustard,
together with neem leaves and garlic, in seven <s>kuḍavas</s> of ghee.
Cooked in three times as much cow's urine, that is good for drinking, nasal therapy, and anointing.
For rākṣasas, the <s>bali</s> is white minced meat, flowers, mixed rice,
cooked and uncooked meats, niṣpāva beans sprinkled with blood,
and the bark, root, flowers, and fruits of <s>naktamāla</s> and <s>śirīṣa</s>.
Likewise there should be black <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>bilva</s> root, and the three pungents,
with asafoetida, <s>indrayava</s>, white mustard, garlic, and emblic myrobalan fruit.
An <s>agada</s> mixed with goat's urine is to be used for nasal instillation and collyrium.

children.text: ebhireva ghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ gavāṃ mūtre caturguṇe ||
children.translated_text: With these same substances, ghee is cooked in four times as much cow's urine;
by drinking, anointing, and nasal instillation, it wards off <s>rākṣasa-grahas</s>.

children.text: piśācānāṃ baliḥ sīdhuḥ piṇyākaḥ palalaṃ dadhi ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>piśācas</s>, the offering is <s>sīdhu</s> liquor, oil-cake, minced meat, and curd;
radish, salt, ghee, and barley gruel together with an offering to beings;
the two kinds of haridrā, mañjiṣṭhā, miśi, rock salt, and dry ginger;
hiṅgu, priyaṅgu, trikaṭu, garlic, triphalā, and vacā;
with flowers of pāṭalī, śveta, kaṭabhī, and śirīṣa, ghee
cooked with a quarter part of cow urine is useful for drinking and anointing.
For collyrium and nasal medication, those same substances should be applied after being ground with goat's urine.
In the case of gods, seers, ancestors, or <s>gandharvas</s>, one should avoid sharp nasal medications and the like.
In this case one should administer mild remedies, beginning with the drinking of ghee.

children.text: ṛte piśācāt sarveṣu pratikūlaṃ ca nācaret
children.translated_text: Except in the case of a <s>piśāca</s>, in all cases one should not act contrary to the possessing being.

children.text: savaidyam āturaṃ ghnanti kruddhās te hi mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when angered, those of great power kill the patient together with the physician.
By reciting the sovereign, the twelve-armed lord <s>Āryāvalokita</s>,
and the cure for all diseases, one conquers all the <s>grahas</s>.
Likewise, with regard to <s>unmāda</s>, <s>apasmāra</s>, or any other derangement of the mind,

children.text: mahāvidyāṃ ca māyūrīṃ śuciṃ taṃ śrāvayet sadā ||
children.translated_text: one should always have the pure <s>Mahāvidyā Māyūrī</s> recited to that person.
One should worship <s>Bhūteśa</s>, <s>Sthāṇu</s>, and his hosts called <s>Pramathas</s>;

children.text: japan siddhāṃśca tanmantrān grahān sarvān apohati ||
children.translated_text: reciting those perfected mantras of his, one drives away all <s>grahas</s>.
Whatever useful measure will be taught in the next two chapters,

children.text: yaccoktam iha tat sarvaṃ prayuñjīta parasparam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever has been stated here, one should apply all of it in mutual combination.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>unmāda</s>.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
The <s>unmādas</s> are six: arising from the separate <s>doṣas</s>, from their accumulation, from mental distress, and from poison.
<s>Unmāda</s> is the intoxication-like derangement of the mind caused by <s>doṣas</s> that have gone into wrong channels.
By bodily and mental <s>doṣas</s> vitiated through unwholesome food and drink,
through the use of what is unsuitable, impure, or irregular,
in one who is despondent and of little mental strength, from the outbreak of the force of disease,
in one who is depleted, from irregular behavior, and from transgression in the worship of those worthy of worship,
from derangement of the mind through anxieties, and from poison or minor poison,

children.text: ebhir hi hīnasattvasya hṛdi doṣāḥ pradūṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: by these causes, in a person of deficient <s>sattva</s>, the <s>doṣas</s>, vitiated in the heart,

children.text: dhiyo vidhāya kāluṣyaṃ hṛtvā mārgān manovahān
children.translated_text: produce turbidity in the intellect and seize the channels that carry the mind.
Thereby, through confusion of intellect, discernment, and memory, they cause <s>unmāda</s>.
The body, fallen away from normal pain and pleasure, is like a chariot whose charioteer has fallen away;
it wanders, undertaking actions without thought. In that condition, from <s>vāta</s> there is emaciation of the limbs,
weeping, crying out, laughing, smiling, and dancing in improper places,
singing, playing instruments, speech, tossing of the limbs, and clapping or slapping;
frequent imitation of discordant sounds of flute, vīṇā, and the like,
constant foam from the mouth, wandering about, and excessive talking;
ornamenting oneself with things that are not ornaments, and an effort to travel by unsuitable conveyances;
greed for foods, and contempt for them when they are obtained;
swollen reddish eyes, and the arising of the disease when the food has been digested.
From <s>pitta</s> there are threatening, anger, and assault with fists, clods, and the like;
longing for cold, shade, and water, nakedness, and yellow coloration,
and the seeing of unreal fires, flames, stars, lamps, and the like.
From <s>kapha</s> there are anorexia, vomiting, and scant activity, food intake, and speech;
desire for women, delight in solitude, and flowing of saliva and nasal mucus;
filthiness, hatred of cleanliness, sleep, and swelling of the face.

children.text: unmādo balavān rātrau bhuktamātre ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Unmāda</s> from <s>kapha</s> becomes strong at night and just after eating.
When all the seats and forms are combined, it has the nature of all of them;

children.text: unmādaṃ dāruṇaṃ vidyāt taṃ bhiṣak parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: one should know this as terrible <s>unmāda</s> from <s>saṃnipāta</s>; the physician should avoid it.
Through the loss of wealth, a beloved woman, or the like, one possessed by unbearable attachment

children.text: pāṇḍur dīno muhur muhyan hāheti paridevate ||
children.translated_text: becomes pale and wretched, repeatedly faints, and laments, 'alas, alas!'
He weeps without cause, longs to die, and thinks highly of those lost qualities.
With his mind tormented by grief, brooding and wakeful, he behaves abnormally.
From poison, his face is dark, and his complexion, strength, and senses are lost;
he is agitated even between attacks and has red eyes; one should abandon him.
Now, in <s>unmāda</s> born of <s>anila</s>, one should prescribe the drinking of unctuous substances.

children.text: pūrvam āvṛtamārge tu sasnehaṃ mṛdu śodhanam ||
children.translated_text: But first, when the channels are obstructed, one should prescribe mild purification with unctuous substance.
Even in that born of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, at the beginning one should use emesis together with purgation,
and, when the patient has been oleated and fomented, enema and evacuation of the head.
Thus, when his body has been purified, the mind obtains clarity.

children.text: ittham apyanuvṛttau tu tīkṣṇaṃ nāvanam añjanam ||
children.translated_text: But if it continues even so, one should use sharp nasal medication and collyrium,
gladdening, reassurance, frightening, inducing fear, beating, and threatening,
massage, rubbing, anointing, fumigations, and drinking of ghee.

children.text: yuñjyāt tāni hi śuddhasya nayanti prakṛtiṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: One should employ them; for, in a purified person, they lead the mind back to its natural state.
With hiṅgu, sauvarcala salt, and vyoṣa, two palas of each, an āḍhaka of ghee
cooked together with cow urine is supreme for removing <s>unmāda</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, and <s>apasmāra</s>.

children.text: dvau prasthau svarasād brāhmyā ghṛtaprasthaṃ ca sādhitam ||
children.translated_text: Two prasthas of fresh juice of brāhmī and one prastha of ghee, cooked
with vyoṣa, śyāmā, trivṛt, dantī, śaṅkhapuṣpī, and nṛpadruma,
with saptalā and krimihara, made into a paste in the measure of an akṣa,
one should administer in increments of a pala; the maximum dose is four palas.
It removes <s>unmāda</s>, skin disease, and <s>apasmāra</s>, and grants a son to a barren woman.
It produces speech, voice, memory, and intelligence, and is known as the auspicious brāhmī-ghee.
With varā, viśālā, bhadrā, elā, devadāru, and elavāluka,
the two śārivās, the two rajanīs, the two sthirās, phalinī, and nata,
bṛhatī, kuṣṭha, mañjiṣṭhā, nāgakesara, and dāḍima,
vella, tālīśapattra, elā, mālatī buds, and utpala,
with dantī, padmaka, and hima, one karṣa each, one should cook a prastha of ghee;
it is for <s>bhūta</s>, <s>graha</s>, <s>unmāda</s>, cough, <s>apasmāra</s>, and pāpman.

children.text: pāṇḍukaṇḍūviṣe śoṣe mohe mehe gare jvare ||
children.translated_text: in pallor, itching, poisoning, wasting, stupor, urinary disorder, artificial poison, and fever;
or in one without semen or offspring, or whose mind has been struck by fate;
in one of poor intelligence, faltering speech, desiring memory, or having weak digestive fire.
This <s>Kalyāṇaka</s> ghee is strengthening, auspicious, life-promoting,

children.text: kalyāṇakam idaṃ sarpiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ puṃsavaneṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: and gives complexion, good fortune, and nourishment; it is also the best among <s>puṃsavana</s> preparations.
For these conditions, one should boil in water the twenty-one drugs beginning with the two <s>Śārivā</s>s,
and in that decoction cook ghee with four times as much milk from a first-calved cow.
With <s>Vīrā</s>, the two <s>Medā</s>s, <s>Kākolī</s>, <s>Kapikacchū</s>, and <s>Viṣāṇī</s>,
together with <s>Śūrpaparṇī</s>, this is the supreme <s>Mahākalyāṇaka</s>.
It is nourishing, destroys disorders of combined doṣas, and is superior in its qualities to the preceding one.

children.text: jaṭilā pūtanā keśī cāraṭī markaṭī vacā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Keśī</s>, <s>Cāraṭī</s>, <s>Markaṭī</s>, and <s>Vacā</s>;
<s>Trāyamāṇā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Vīrā</s>, <s>Coraka</s>, and <s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s>;
<s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>Śūkarī</s>, <s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Sāticchattrā</s>, and <s>Palaṅkaṣā</s>;
<s>Mahāpuruṣadantā</s>, <s>Kāyasthā</s>, the two <s>Nākulī</s>s,

children.text: kaṭambharā vṛścikālī śāliparṇī ca tair ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭambharā</s>, <s>Vṛścikālī</s>, and <s>Śāliparṇī</s>: ghee prepared with these
destroys quartan fever, insanity, graha-seizure, and epilepsy.
This ghee, named <s>Mahāpaiśācaka</s>, is like nectar.
It produces intelligence, understanding, and memory, and promotes the growth of children's limbs.

children.text: brāhmīm aindrīṃ viḍaṅgāni vyoṣaṃ hiṅgu jaṭāṃ murām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Aindrī</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Vyoṣa</s>, <s>Hiṅgu</s>, <s>Jaṭā</s>, and <s>Murā</s>;

children.text: rāsnāṃ viṣaghnāṃ laśunaṃ viśalyāṃ surasāṃ vacām
children.translated_text: <s>Rāsnā</s>, <s>Viṣaghnā</s>, garlic, <s>Viśalyā</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, and <s>Vacā</s>;
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>Nāgavinnā</s>, <s>Anantā</s>, together with <s>Harītakī</s>,
and <s>Kāṅkṣī</s>, ground with elephant urine and dried in the shade,
make a wick that destroys insanity when used as nasal medication, collyrium, paste, and fumigation.
Various pressed nasal applications are also used, and mustard seeds mixed with an unctuous substance.
He should be massaged with pungent oil, and that powder should be blown into him.
Sharp smoke with <s>Hiṅgu</s>, as taught in the <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>, is beneficial.
With substances derived from jackal, porcupine, owl, leech, bull, and goat,
namely their urine, bile, feces, hair, nails, and skin, one should perform
fumigation, smoking, collyrium, massage, smearing, and sprinkling.
One should constantly fumigate him with very putrid materials from dog, cow, and fish.
These are generally for conditions of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>; in the pitta type, however, what is praised is

children.text: tiktakaṃ jīvanīyaṃ ca sarpiḥ snehaśca miśrakaḥ
children.translated_text: bitter ghee, life-promoting ghee, and the mixed unctuous preparation,
as well as cold foods and drinks that are sweet and light.

children.text: vidhyet sirāṃ yathoktāṃ vā tṛptaṃ medyāmiṣasya vā
children.translated_text: One should pierce the vein as prescribed, or after the patient has been satisfied with fatty meat.
He should be made to lie in a windless place; in this way he is freed from derangement of mind.
One may throw him into a waterless well, or weaken him by hunger.

children.text: āśvāsayet suhṛt taṃ vā vākyair dharmārthasaṃhitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or a friend should reassure him with words joined to <s>dharma</s> and practical welfare.

children.text: brūyād iṣṭavināśaṃ vā darśayed adbhutāni vā
children.translated_text: One may tell him of the loss of something dear, or show him astonishing things.
Bound, smeared with mustard oil, he may be laid face upward in the sun.
Or he may be touched with a decoction of <s>Kapikacchū</s>, or with heated iron, oil, and water.

children.text: kaśābhis tāḍayitvā vā baddhaṃ śvabhre viniṣkṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Or, after beating him with whips, one may throw him bound into a pit.
Or else, in a completely dark house free from weapons, stones, and people,
he may be frightened with a serpent whose fangs have been removed, and with tamed lions and elephants.
Or royal officers, having led him outside while he is well restrained,
should frighten him with execution, threatening him by the king's command.
For beyond bodily pain and other fears, fear for one's life is considered supreme.

children.text: tena yāti śamaṃ tasya sarvato viplutaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that, his mind, agitated on every side, comes to quiet.
This successful procedure should be applied with regard to place, time, and the like.
But when a person's mind is harmed by the destruction of a desired object,
one should bring it to quiet by obtaining something like it, and by consolation and reassurance.
Mental disorders arising from desire, grief, fear, anger, joy, envy, and greed
should be pacified by these very states when they are mutually opposed to one another.
If, in insanity, one observes an appearance especially marked by the signs already stated for spirit-involvement,
then one should administer the medicine prescribed for spirits.

children.text: baliṃ ca dadyāt palalaṃ yāvakaṃ saktupiṇḍikām ||
children.translated_text: One should also give an offering of <s>palala</s>, barley preparation, and balls of roasted grain flour;
unctuous and sweet food, and rice sprinkled with blood;
cooked and uncooked meats, <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and <s>āsava</s>;
and flowers of <s>Atimukta</s>, <s>Jāti</s>, and <s>Sahacara</s>,

children.text: catuṣpathe gavāṃ tīrthe nadīnāṃ saṃgameṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: at crossroads, at cow-fords, and at the confluences of rivers.
One who has given up meat and alcohol, who eats wholesome food, is self-controlled and pure,
and possesses strength of mind, is not affected by either endogenous or exogenous insanities.
Clarity of the sense faculties and their objects, and likewise of intellect, self, and mind,
and the bodily elements standing in their natural condition: these are the signs that insanity has departed.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>apasmāra</s>.
Thus indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
<s>Apasmāra</s> is loss of memory; it arises from an overwhelming of intelligence and mental steadiness,
when the mind has been injured by anxiety, grief, fear, and the like.
As in insanity, it arises from the vitiated wastes located in mind and body.

children.text: hate sattve hṛdi vyāpte saṃjñāvāhiṣu kheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: When mental steadiness is struck, and the heart and the channels carrying consciousness are pervaded,

children.text: tamo viśan mūḍhamatir bībhatsāḥ kurute kriyāḥ
children.translated_text: darkness enters; with deluded mind, the patient performs repulsive acts.

children.text: dantān khādan vaman phenaṃ hastau pādau ca vikṣipan ||
children.translated_text: Biting his teeth, vomiting foam, and tossing his hands and feet,

children.text: paśyann asanti rūpāṇi praskhalan patati kṣitau
children.translated_text: seeing forms that do not exist, stumbling, he falls to the ground.
With eyes and brows distorted, he wakes up when the surge of doṣas has passed.
After an interval he again behaves in exactly the same way.
<s>Apasmāra</s> is fourfold: from <s>vāta</s> and the other doṣas, and from their combination.
When it is about to arise, there is trembling of the heart, emptiness, dizziness,
seeing darkness, brooding, raising of the brows, and deformity of the eyes.
Hearing sounds that are not there, sweating, and a flow of saliva and nasal mucus,
indigestion, loss of taste, fainting, rumbling in the abdomen, and loss of strength;
sleeplessness, aching of the limbs, thirst, and, in dreams, singing together with dancing,

children.text: pānaṃ tailasya madyasya tayoreva ca mehanam ||
children.translated_text: drinking oil and liquor, and urinating those very things:

children.text: tatra vātāt sphuratsakthiḥ prapataṃśca muhur muhuḥ
children.translated_text: in that condition, from vāta, his thighs twitch and he falls again and again;

children.text: apasmarati saṃjñāṃ ca labhate visvaraṃ rudan ||
children.translated_text: he has an <s>apasmāra</s> seizure, then regains consciousness, crying in a discordant voice.
With eyes bulging upward he breathes hard, vomits foam, trembles,
throws his head about, bites his teeth, and has a swollen neck.
He flings his limbs all around irregularly, with bent fingers;
his eyes, skin, nails, and mouth are dry, dusky, reddish, and he sees blackness.
With pitta, he perceives a restless, harsh, frightening form with a distorted face,

children.text: apasmarati pittena muhuḥ saṃjñāṃ ca vindati ||
children.translated_text: has an <s>apasmāra</s> seizure repeatedly, and then regains consciousness.
His foam, eyes, mouth, and skin are yellow, and he beats the ground;
he sees terrifying, blazing, angry forms and is afflicted with thirst.
From kapha, the seizure comes on slowly and awakening too is slow;
his movements are slight, saliva is abundant, and the eyes, nails, and mouth are white.
He sees white cloudy forms; but one should reject a case that has all the signs.
Now, in <s>apasmāra</s>, when the channels of intellect, mind, and heart are obstructed, first one should awaken them
by sharp procedures, beginning with emesis.
One should treat vātika <s>apasmāra</s> chiefly with enemas, the paittika type mostly with purgations,
and the ślaiṣmika type mostly with emesis.
For one who has been thoroughly purified in every way
and properly reassured, listen now to pacifying formulations for release from <s>apasmāra</s>.
Ghee cooked with the expressed juice of cow dung, milk, curd, and urine
should be drunk; it ends <s>apasmāra</s>, fever, insanity, and jaundice.
The two groups of five roots, <s>triphala</s>, the two <s>niśā</s> herbs, and <s>kuṭaja</s> bark,
<s>saptaparṇa</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>nīlinī</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,
<s>śamyāka</s>, <s>puṣkarajaṭā</s>, <s>phalgu</s> root, and <s>durālabhā</s>,
two <s>palas</s> each, should be cooked in a <s>droṇa</s> of water until one quarter remains.
With <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>āḍhakī</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and <s>rohiṣa</s>,
with <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>bhūtika</s>, <s>bhūnimba</s>, <s>śreyasī</s>, and the two <s>śārivā</s> herbs,
with <s>madayantī</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>nicula</s>, each in one-<s>akṣa</s> measures, one should cook ghee.

children.text: prasthaṃ tadvad dravaiḥ pūrvaiḥ pañcagavyam idaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: A <s>prastha</s> of ghee is cooked in the same way with the previous liquids; this is the great <s>pañcagavya</s>.
It is supreme for removing fever, <s>apasmāra</s>, abdominal disease, and fistula,
and it removes swelling, piles, jaundice, anemia, abdominal tumors, cough, and <s>grahas</s>.
Old ghee cooked with the juices of <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>
promotes intellect and conquers insanity, misfortune, <s>apasmāra</s>, and evil.
One should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil and a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with life-promoting herbs measured by <s>palas</s>
in a <s>droṇa</s> of milk; when prepared, it releases from <s>apasmāra</s>.
In a bronze vessel, in eight times as much juice of <s>kāśmarī</s>, milk, and sugarcane juice,
one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with life-promoting herbs in <s>karṣa</s> measures.
That quickly destroys <s>apasmāra</s> arising from vāta and pitta.
Likewise, milk cooked with a decoction of <s>kāśa</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, sugarcane, and <s>kuśa</s> is beneficial.
Ghee cooked in eighteen times as much expressed juice of bottle gourd,
with a paste of licorice, removes <s>apasmāra</s> and bestows intellect, speech, and voice.

children.text: kapilānāṃ gavāṃ pittaṃ nāvane paramaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: The bile of tawny cows is supremely useful for nasal instillation,
as is the esteemed bile of dogs, jackals, cats, lions, and the like,
and also that of monitor lizards, mongooses, elephants, spotted deer, bears, and cattle.

children.text: pitteṣu sādhitaṃ tailaṃ nasye 'bhyaṅge ca śasyate
children.translated_text: Oil prepared with these biles is recommended for nasal therapy and massage.
Oil cooked with <s>triphala</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, yellow sandalwood, barley alkali, and <s>phaṇijjaka</s>,
with seeds of <s>śryāhvā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>kārañja</s>,

children.text: bastamūtre hitaṃ nasyaṃ cūrṇaṃ vā dhmāpayed bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: in goat's urine is good as nasal therapy; or the physician may blow the powder into the nose.
From the beaks, wings, and dung produced by mongooses, owls, cats, vultures, insects, snakes, and crows,

children.text: tuṇḍaiḥ pakṣaiḥ purīṣaiśca dhūpam asya prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: he should apply fumigation for this patient.
He should habitually take garlic with oil, or <s>śatāvarī</s> with milk,
or juice of <s>brāhmī</s>, juice of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, or <s>vacā</s>, mixed with honey.
Since <s>apasmāra</s> arises equally from aggravated bodily and mental <s>doṣas</s>,
and since it is lodged in a great vital point,
therefore one should treat this hard-to-cure disease with <s>rasāyana</s> therapies.
One should always protect the patient afflicted by it from fire, water, and other dangers, and from uneven places.

children.text: muktaṃ manovikāreṇa tvam itthaṃ kṛtavān iti
children.translated_text: When he is freed from the disturbance of mind, one should not say, "You acted like this";

children.text: na brūyād viṣayairiṣṭaiḥ kliṣṭaṃ ceto 'sya bṛṃhayet ||
children.translated_text: one should nourish his distressed mind with pleasing sense objects.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter on the diagnosis of diseases of the eyelids.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
The morbid humors, aggravated by the harmful factors stated in the diagnosis of all diseases,
and especially by things injurious to the eyes, generally following pitta,
spread upward through the vessels and lodge in the parts of the eye.

children.text: vartma saṃdhiṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ vā sarvam akṣi vā ||
children.translated_text: They produce diseases of the eyelid, the junction, the white part, the black part, the sight, the whole eye, or all of the eye.

children.text: rogān kuryuścalas tatra prāpya vartmāśrayāḥ sirāḥ
children.translated_text: Among them, mobile vāyu, reaching the vessels located in the eyelids,
causes painful stiffness of the eyelids in one who has just risen from sleep,
a feeling as if the eyes were full of dust, difficult opening, and tears.

children.text: vimardanāt syācca śamaḥ kṛcchronmīlaṃ vadanti tat ||
children.translated_text: Relief may come from rubbing; they call this difficult opening.
Vāyu, moving the eyelids, repeatedly produces blinking and opening of the eyes.

children.text: karotyaruṅ nimeṣo 'sau vartma yat tu nimīlyate ||
children.translated_text: That is painless blinking; but when the eyelid is closed,

children.text: vimuktasaṃdhi niśceṣṭaṃ hīnaṃ vātahataṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: separated from its junction, inactive, and drooping, that is indeed paralyzed by vāta.
By pitta, many black pustules on the inner eyelid, like seeds of <s>kumbhīkā</s>,
swell up; when they later burst, they are called <s>kumbhī</s>.
It has burning, moisture, and pricking pain, is blood-red in appearance, and cannot bear touch.

children.text: pittena jāyate vartma pittotkliṣṭam uśanti tat
children.translated_text: It arises from pitta; they call that eyelid condition <s>pittotkliṣṭa</s>.

children.text: karoti kaṇḍūṃ dāhaṃ ca pittaṃ pakṣmāntam āsthitam ||
children.translated_text: Pitta, lodged at the ends of the eyelashes, causes itching and burning,

children.text: pakṣmaṇāṃ śātanaṃ cānu pakṣmaśātaṃ vadanti tam
children.translated_text: and then the falling out of the eyelashes; that condition they call <s>pakṣmaśāta</s>.

children.text: pothakyaḥ piṭikāḥ śvetāḥ sarṣapābhā ghanāḥ kaphāt ||
children.translated_text: From kapha arise <s>pothakī</s> pustules: white, resembling mustard seeds, and hard,
accompanied by swelling, coating, pain, itching, and slimy tears.
The eyelid becomes <s>kaphotkliṣṭa</s>, with stiffness, moisture, and coating.
From kapha there is a pale granthi, without pain or suppuration, itchy and hard;

children.text: kolamātraḥ sa lagaṇaḥ kiṃcid alpas tato 'thavā ||
children.translated_text: it is the size of a jujube fruit, or else somewhat smaller; that is <s>lagaṇa</s>.
A red pustule caused by blood, covered with pustules similar to itself,
is called <s>utsaṅga</s>; likewise an inflamed condition with streaks and unable to bear touch.
<s>Arśas</s> is an overgrowth of flesh inside the eyelid, fixed, unctuous, with burning and pain.

children.text: raktaṃ raktena tatsrāvi chinnaṃ chinnaṃ ca vardhate ||
children.translated_text: Caused by blood, it is red and discharges blood; when cut again and again, it grows back.

children.text: madhye vā vartmano 'nte vā kaṇḍūṣārugvatī sthirā
children.translated_text: In the middle of the eyelid or at its edge there is a firm pustule with itching, slight pain,
coppery from blood and the size of a mung bean; it is named <s>añjana</s>.

children.text: doṣair vartma bahiḥ śūnaṃ yad antaḥ sūkṣmakhācitam
children.translated_text: When the eyelid, because of the doṣas, is swollen externally and internally marked with minute holes,
with discharge and internal fluid, resembling a lotus fiber, that is <s>bisavartma</s>.

children.text: yad vartmotkliṣṭam utkliṣṭam akasmān mlānatām iyāt
children.translated_text: When an inflamed eyelid, though inflamed, suddenly falls into withering,
from the aggravation of blood and the three doṣas, that is <s>utkliṣṭavartma</s>.
<s>Śyāvavartma</s> is a dark eyelid, caused by impurities together with blood, with pain, moisture, and swelling.
The condition called <s>śliṣṭa</s> occurs when the eyelids are stuck together, with itching, swelling, and redness.
Inside the eyelid there are rough, dry pustules resembling grains of sand;
this is <s>sikatāvartma</s>. The black, mud-like one is <s>kardama</s>, resembling mud.
<s>Bahala</s> is built up with thick masses of flesh, of the same color and evenly spread.
<s>Kukūṇaka</s> belongs only to an infant and arises on account of tooth eruption.
Because of it the infant has swollen, coppery eyes and is unable to look;
there is pain in the eyelids, sliminess, and rubbing of the ears, nose, and eyes.
In obstruction by the eyelashes, contraction of the eyelids also arises,

children.text: kharatāntarmukhatvaṃ ca romṇām anyāni vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as roughness, inward turning of the hairs, or other such abnormalities.
The eye, rubbed by those sharp-pointed hairs as if by thorns, swells,
and burns; it is hostile to wind and the other factors, gives little relief, and is calmed when the hairs are removed.
At the outer eyelid near the canthus, a hard, raised granthi
becomes coppery when ripe and discharges blood and pus; <s>alajī</s> repeatedly becomes distended.
Inside the eyelid, like a lump of flesh, there is a swelling, knotted and painless;

children.text: sāsraiḥ syād arbudo doṣair viṣamo bāhyataścalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the blood and the doṣas it becomes an <s>arbuda</s> tumor, irregular and mobile externally.
Thus these are the twenty-four diseases situated in the eyelids.

children.text: ādyo 'tra bheṣajaiḥ sādhyo dvau tato 'rśaśca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the first is curable with medicines; the next two and <s>arśas</s> should be rejected as incurable.
<s>Pakṣmoparodha</s> is manageable; the remaining ones should be treated with the knife.
One should pound <s>pakṣmasadana</s>; among those, one should also excise <s>arbuda</s>.
One should split open <s>lagaṇa</s>, <s>kumbhīkā</s>, <s>bisa</s>, <s>utsaṅga</s>, <s>añjana</s>, and <s>alajī</s>.
<s>Pothakī</s>, <s>śyāva</s>, <s>sikatā</s>, <s>śliṣṭa</s>, and the four <s>utkliṣṭa</s> conditions
together with <s>kardama</s>, <s>bahala</s>, and <s>kukūṇaka</s>, one should scrape.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of eyelid diseases.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
In difficult opening of the eyes, one should use old ghee cooked with paste of grapes and water,
with sugar, and also oleation, nasal therapy, fumigation, collyrium, and the like.
<s>Kumbhīkāvartma</s>, after being scraped and rubbed with rock salt,
should be sprinkled with a decoction of licorice, emblic myrobalan, and pointed gourd.
For a patient who has been purified, is in a windless place, attended by reliable assistants, and lying supine,
the eyelid should be fomented externally with cloth heated by warm water.
Having turned it out, covered with another cloth, and held by the left thumb and finger,

children.text: na sraṃsate calati vā vartmaivaṃ sarvatas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the eyelid does not slip or move; thus, from all sides,
with a round-tipped instrument, marking it crosswise with cuts from the knife,
one should scrape it with that very instrument, or with leaves of vegetables, jasmine, and the like.

children.text: phenena toyarāśer vā picunā pramṛjann asṛk
children.translated_text: Wiping away the blood with sea foam or with a cotton pad,
when the bleeding has stopped and it has been well scraped, one should rub it with substances mixed with honey.
After washing it with the substances prescribed for each case, or with warm water,
it should be sprinkled with ghee, anointed, and bandaged with honey and ghee.

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥ karṇayor dattvā piṇḍīṃ ca yavasaktubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed a bolus made of barley flour above and below the ears,
on the second day, when it has been unbound, one should perform sprinkling as appropriate.
On the fourth day one should apply nasal therapies and the like; on the fifth day one should leave it unbound.
One should know the eyelid to have been well scraped when it is even, like a fingernail, and free from swelling, itching, rubbing, and other distress.

children.text: vidyāt sulikhitaṃ vartma likhed bhūyo viparyaye
children.translated_text: In the opposite case one should scrape the eyelid again.
Pain, falling of eyelashes and eyelid tissue, and slipping result from excessive scraping.
In that case a wind-pacifying regimen, beginning with oleation and fomentation, is desired.
After anointing with fresh butter, one should apply a paste of white <s>lodhra</s>.
One should cook it in a sealed-bolus preparation with a paste of castor root; then,
when steamed, washed, dried, powdered, and made into a small bundle,

children.text: striyāḥ kṣīre chagalyā vā mṛditaṃ netrasecanam
children.translated_text: it is rubbed in the milk of a woman or of a she-goat and used as an eye irrigation.
Prepared in the same way, coated with rice-grain paste,
one should use it, rubbed with whey, for an over-scraped eye;
or one should irrigate with whey alone, for one who eats the meat of animals of dry country.
Having split hard, raised pustules with the rice-grain-shaped instrument,

children.text: niṣpīḍayed anu vidhiḥ pariśeṣas tu pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: one should squeeze them out; the remaining procedure is as before.

children.text: lekhane bhedane cāyaṃ kramaḥ sarvatra vartmani
children.translated_text: In scraping and in incision, this procedure applies in every case concerning the eyelid.
For conditions aggravated by <s>pitta</s> and blood, bloodletting is to be done after oleation with ghee prepared with the sweet group of drugs.
For one who has been made unctuous, venesection is prescribed; <s>trivṛt</s> is the best purgative.

children.text: likhite srutarakte ca vartmani kṣālanaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: When the eyelid has been scraped and the blood has flowed out, washing is beneficial.
A decoction of <s>Yaṣṭī</s> is useful, and sprinkling with milk cooked with sandalwood.
When the eyelashes fall out, one should pierce the hair follicles with a needle,
or have them seized by leeches; one may also use milk or sugarcane juice for sprinkling.
Emesis, nasal medication, and ghee cooked with sweet and cooling substances are prescribed.
Having powdered <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s>, one should impregnate it with the juices of <s>Surasā</s>.

children.text: tāmre daśāhaṃ paramaṃ pakṣmaśāte tad añjanam ||
children.translated_text: Kept in a copper vessel for at most ten days, that is the collyrium for <s>pakṣmaśāta</s>.
<s>Pothakī</s> lesions, after being scraped, should be rubbed with dry ginger and rock salt.
After washing them with warm water, one should sprinkle them with decoctions of <s>Khadira</s>, <s>Āḍhakī</s>, and <s>Śigru</s> boiled in water,
or with the two <s>Niśā</s>s, <s>Śreṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Madhuka</s>, together with honey.
When a kapha-aggravated lesion has been scraped, rubbing with honey is prescribed,
using fine powders of rock salt, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>kaṇa</s>, and <s>tārkṣyaja</s>.
Emesis, collyrium, nasal treatment, and everything else that conquers <s>kapha</s> are beneficial.
This should also be done in <s>lagaṇa</s>; if it does not subside, it should be cauterized with fire.
In <s>kukūṇa</s>, the wet nurse should drink ghee cooked with <s>Khadira</s>, <s>Śreṣṭhā</s>, and neem leaves.
After drinking it, the wet nurse should vomit with <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, mustard, and rock salt.
She should be purged with a decoction of <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, and grapes.
Her breasts should be smeared with a paste of <s>Musta</s>, the two <s>Rajanī</s>s, and <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>.

children.text: dhūpayet sarṣapaiḥ sājyaiḥ śuddhāṃ kvāthaṃ ca pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: She should be fumigated with mustard seeds mixed with ghee; when purified, she should be given a decoction to drink,
made from <s>Paṭola</s>, <s>Musta</s>, raisins, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, and <s>Triphala</s>.

children.text: śiśos tu likhitaṃ vartma srutāsṛg vāmbujanmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the child, however, when the eyelid has been scraped and the blood drawn with leeches,
one should sprinkle it with a decoction of leaves from <s>Dhātrī</s>, <s>Aśmantaka</s>, and <s>Jambū</s>.
Since diseases in children generally arise from <s>śleṣman</s> because they consume milk and ghee,
therefore emesis is praised first in all their diseases.
Rock salt, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Apāmārga</s> seed, ghee, breast milk, and honey,
powder of <s>Vacā</s> with honey, and <s>Madana</s> with <s>Madhuka</s>,

children.text: kṣīraṃ kṣīrānnam annaṃ ca bhajataḥ kramataḥ śiśoḥ ||
children.translated_text: are emetic measures for a child who successively takes milk, milk-rice, and solid food.
Emesis is useful in all diseases, and especially in <s>kukūṇaka</s>.
Ghee prepared with the juice of <s>Saptalā</s> should also be applied for both purifications.
With the two <s>Niśā</s>s, <s>Lodhra</s>, <s>Yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and shoots of neem,
a <s>varti</s> (medicinal wick), ground together with copper dust, is beneficial in <s>kukūṇaka</s>.
Or burnt iron dust may be used, combined with milk, honey, and ghee.
With <s>Elā</s>, garlic, <s>Katakā</s>, conch, pungent drugs, and <s>Phaṇijjaka</s>,
a <s>varti</s>, ground in liquor with <s>Kaṭphala</s>, is used for <s>kukūṇa</s> and <s>pothakī</s>.
In advanced <s>pakṣmarodha</s>, when the hairs have grown, after the body has been purified,

children.text: utsṛjya dvau bhruvo 'dhastād bhāgau bhāgaṃ ca pakṣmataḥ
children.translated_text: leaving two parts below the eyebrow and one part from the eyelashes,
one should cut crosswise a barley-sized, barley-shaped strip and remove the blood with a moist cloth.
When the bleeding becomes slight there,
it should be sutured with a curved needle, with stitches placed at intervals the size of a mung bean.

children.text: baddhvā lalāṭe paṭṭaṃ ca tatra sīvanasūtrakam
children.translated_text: Having tied a bandage on the forehead, the suture thread should be placed there.
With the needle one should set it neither too tight nor too slack, and then apply
a pledget of honey and ghee; no bandage should be put on this.
