If there is pain, one should sprinkle it with milky decoctions such as that of <s>Nyagrodha</s>.
On the fifth day the thread should be removed, and the wound should be dusted.

children.text: gairikeṇa vraṇaṃ yuñjyāt tīkṣṇaṃ nasyāñjanādi ca ||
children.translated_text: One should apply red ochre to the wound, and use sharp nasal medicines, collyria, and the like.
If it does not subside, one should turn out the fold that is the seat of the eyelid disorder and cauterize it.
Having removed excessive eyelashes with forceps, one should cauterize their base.
For external <s>alajī</s>, cautery is again performed with the tip of a needle heated to the color of fire.
The same applies to an <s>arbuda</s> that has been opened by alkali and fire and has been well excised.
Now then, we shall explain the diagnosis of diseases of the junctions and of the white and black parts of the eye.
Thus indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.

children.text: vāyuḥ kruddhaḥ sirāḥ prāpya jalābhaṃ jalavāhinīḥ
children.translated_text: Aggravated <s>vāyu</s>, reaching the water-carrying vessels, which are watery in nature,
causes tears to flow from the inner canthus, at the junction of the eyelid and the white of the eye.

children.text: tena netraṃ sarugrāgaśophaṃ syāt sa jalāsravaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of it, the eye becomes painful, red, and swollen; that condition is <s>jalāsrava</s>.

children.text: kaphāt kaphāsrave śvetaṃ picchilaṃ bahalaṃ sravet ||
children.translated_text: From <s>kapha</s>, in <s>kaphāsrava</s>, a white, slimy, thick discharge flows.
From <s>kapha</s> there is a swelling with a sharp point, like a bubble of caustic alkali,
broad-rooted, firm, unctuous, of the same color, soft, and slimy.

children.text: mahān apākaḥ kaṇḍūmān upanāhaḥ sa nīrujaḥ
children.translated_text: Large, unripe, itchy, and painless, it is called <s>upanāha</s>.

children.text: raktād raktāsrāve tāmraṃ bahūṣṇaṃ cāśru saṃsravet ||
children.translated_text: From blood, in <s>raktāsrāva</s>, copper-colored and very hot tears flow.
A pustule based at the eyelid-junction in the white of the eye, burning and painful,

children.text: tāmrā mudgopamā bhinnā raktaṃ sravati parvaṇī ||
children.translated_text: coppery and like a mung bean, when broken discharges blood; it is <s>parvaṇī</s>.
In <s>pūyāsrava</s>, the impurities, along with blood, from the inner canthus of the eyelid-junction
repeatedly discharge pus mixed with blood because of suppuration of skin and flesh.
<s>Pūyālasa</s> is a small ulcer preceded by swelling and inflammation,
located in the inner canthus, swollen, discharging pus, and painful.
<s>Antaralajī</s> of the inner canthus is a swelling with pain, pricking, and burning.
In the outer or inner canthus, it has itching, suppuration, and eruptions at the eyelashes.
<s>Kṛmigranthi</s> is a painful nodule containing worms and discharging pus.
<s>Upanāha</s>, <s>kṛmigranthi</s>, <s>pūyālasa</s>, and <s>parvaṇī</s>,

children.text: śastreṇa sādhayet pañca sālajīn āsravāṃs tyajet
children.translated_text: these five should be treated with the knife; the <s>alajī</s>s and the discharges should be abandoned.
<s>Pitta</s> produces spots in the white of the eye that are black, dusky, or yellow.
Or it makes the whole white resemble a mirror smeared with dirt, with burning and pain.
This disease is called <s>śuktikā</s>; it is accompanied by diarrhea, thirst, and fever.
From <s>kapha</s>, in the white of the eye, there is a white fleshy growth, of the same color, slowly increasing;
a white <s>arma</s> has swelling, little pain, the same color, is thick, and is not soft.
When it is heavy, unctuous, and like a drop of water, it is known as <s>balāsagrathita</s>.
When there are raised spots as white as flour, one should call it <s>piṣṭaka</s>.
When the white of the eye is covered with red streaks, burns, and is painful,
and when there is no swelling but there are tears and coating, that <s>sirotpāta</s> is due to blood.

children.text: upekṣitaḥ sirotpāto rājīs tā eva vardhayan
children.translated_text: If neglected, <s>sirotpāta</s>, increasing those very streaks,
produces bloody <s>sirāharṣa</s>; because of it the eye becomes unable to look up.
In <s>sirājāla</s> there is a network of vessels in the white of the eye, large, red, dense, and raised.
<s>Śoṇitārma</s> is a smooth, lotus-red fleshy overgrowth caused by blood.
<s>Arjuna</s> is a painless, smooth spot, red like a hare's blood.
A spreading fleshy growth, dark red, soft, rapidly increasing, and painless is
<s>prastāryarma</s>, produced by the morbid factors together with blood; <s>snāvārma</s> resembles sinew.
A dark, thick, broad piece of flesh, like a lump of dried blood,
is <s>adhimāṃsārma</s>. The small lesions that burn and rub, covered with vessels,
lying near the black part of the eye and like mustard seeds, are called <s>sirā</s>.
The group of six, namely <s>śukti</s>, <s>harṣa</s>, <s>sirotpāta</s>, <s>piṣṭaka</s>, <s>grathita</s>, and <s>arjuna</s>,

children.text: sādhayed auṣadhaiḥ ṣaṭkaṃ śeṣaṃ śastreṇa saptakam ||
children.translated_text: should be cured with medicines; the remaining group of seven is to be treated with the knife.

children.text: navotthaṃ tad api dravyairarmoktaṃ yacca pañcadhā
children.translated_text: Even among these, a newly arisen one may be treated with drugs. Of the five kinds described as <s>arma</s>,
that which is fit for cutting should be excised; but one should avoid one that has reached the black part, or is covered with flesh, sinew, and vessels,
one that rises like a torn flap of skin, and one that has reached the organ of sight.
When <s>pitta</s> is in the black part or in the visual organ, it produces <s>śukra</s> with pricking pain, tears, and redness.

children.text: chittvā tvacaṃ janayati tena syāt kṛṣṇamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Cutting through the layer, it gives rise thereby to a black circle.
<s>Kṣataśukraka</s> is somewhat depressed and has the appearance of a ripe <s>jambū</s> fruit.
When the second layer is penetrated, that is difficult to cure, or merely manageable;
there there is an abundance of pricking pain and the like, and a blackness like a needle-prick.
When the third layer is cut, it is incurable, being covered with wounds.
From <s>kapha</s>, <s>śuddhaśukraka</s> is conch-white, curable, and not very painful.
When it is reddish, slimy, exudes blood, has a reddish pustule, and is very painful,
with a black raised form like goat droppings, <s>ajakā</s> caused by blood is to be rejected.
<s>Sirāśukra</s> is when the black circle, affected by the morbid factors together with blood,
is overspread by reddish vessels accompanied by pricking pain and burning.
One should reject the condition that, without apparent cause, discharges blood that is hot or cold, clear or thick.

children.text: doṣaiḥ sāsraiḥ sakṛt kṛṣṇaṃ nīyate śuklarūpatām ||
children.translated_text: When the black part is once turned into the form of the white by the morbid factors together with blood,
having the appearance of being coated with a white cloud and shaped like half a split <s>niṣpāva</s> bean,
and oppressed by extremely severe pain, redness, burning, and swelling,
one should reject that intensely painful <s>śukra</s> caused by over-ripening,

children.text: yasya vā liṅganāśo 'ntaḥ śyāvaṃ yad vā salohitam ||
children.translated_text: or that in which vision has been lost internally, or which is dark or blood-stained,
excessively raised or deeply sunk, tearful, or covered with a sinus wound,

children.text: purāṇaṃ viṣamaṃ madhye vicchinnaṃ yacca śukrakam
children.translated_text: old, irregular, depressed in the middle, or split: such is <s>śukraka</s>.
Thus five diseases in the black part of the eye have been stated, according to their curability and incurability.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of the junctions, the white part, and the black part of the eye.
Thus indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.

children.text: upanāhaṃ bhiṣak svinnaṃ bhinnaṃ vrīhimukhena ca
children.translated_text: The physician should foment <s>upanāha</s>, then incise it with a rice-pointed instrument,
scrape it with a round-tipped instrument, and afterward rub in the medicine.
He should bandage it as before with long pepper, honey, and rock salt,
and then irrigate it with a decoction of <s>paṭola</s> leaves and <s>āmalaka</s>.
A <s>parvaṇī</s>, grasped with a hook from the outer junction at one third of it,
should be cut halfway with a growth-knife; otherwise the passage of tears would be affected.
The treatment is as for <s>arma</s>, with rubbing in honey and rock salt.

children.text: pūyālase sirāṃ vidhyet tatas tam upanāhayet ||
children.translated_text: In <s>pūyālasa</s> one should pierce the vein and then apply a poultice to it.
One should also perform all the procedures described for <s>akṣipāka</s> according to rule.
With rock salt, fresh ginger, <s>kāsīsa</s>, iron, and copper, finely powdered,
one should apply a powdered collyrium, or a thick extract preparation with honey.

children.text: kṛmigranthiṃ karīṣeṇa svinnaṃ bhittvā vilikhya ca ||
children.translated_text: A <s>kṛmigranthi</s>, after being fomented with dung, should be split open and scraped,
and rubbed with <s>triphala</s>, honey, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and rock salt.
A <s>śukti</s> should be treated as in bilious <s>abhiṣyanda</s>; in <s>balāsa</s> and in <s>piṣṭaka</s>,
one should treat as in phlegmatic <s>abhiṣyanda</s>, except for venesection.
A collyrium made of <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>kaṭphala</s>, soaked in the juice of <s>bījapūra</s>,
together with buds of <s>jātī</s>, rock salt, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>mahauṣadha</s>,
ground with clear liquor and made into a stick, is a collyrium that removes swelling and itching.
For <s>utpāta</s>, <s>harṣa</s>, <s>jāla</s>, and <s>arjuna</s>, the procedure is as for bloody discharge.
In <s>sirotpāta</s>, especially, ghee and honey are used as a collyrium.
But in <s>sirāharṣa</s>, <s>rasāñjana</s>, smoothly rubbed with honey, is used.
In <s>arjuna</s>, an eye-drop with sugar, whey-water, and honey is beneficial.
Alum, saffron, conch, and licorice are a honey-based collyrium.

children.text: madhunā cāñjanaṃ śaṅkhaḥ pheno vā sitayā saha ||
children.translated_text: Conch, or sea-foam, is also a collyrium with honey or together with sugar.

children.text: armoktaṃ pañcadhā tatra tanu dhūmāvilaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: For the fivefold <s>arma</s> described, among them that which is thin, smoky, and clouded,

children.text: raktaṃ dadhinibhaṃ yacca śukravat tasya bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: red, like curd, or like <s>śukra</s>, has this medicine.
This applies to the superficial one; the other, after being fomented and anointed with rock salt
and the juice of <s>bījapūra</s>, should be rubbed while the eye is closed.
When the eye has been irritated in this way and the <s>arma</s> or fleshy overgrowth has become movable,
ghee should be placed unmoving on the head, and especially on the eyelids.
When the patient is looking toward the outer corner, in an enlarged <s>arma</s>, from the inner canthus
there should be a fold at the place where the <s>arma</s> has been held up with a hook.

children.text: nātyāyataṃ mucuṇḍyā vā sūcyā sūtreṇa vā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with a <s>mucuṇḍī</s> instrument, or with a needle and thread, without drawing it out too far,
he should loosen it on all sides with a round-pointed knife; then, when it has been loosened,
he should draw it toward the inner canthus and cut it off, leaving one fourth remaining;
he should protect the inner canthus and the vessels that carry tears.
From puncture of the inner canthus, tears flow, and a sinus forms in the eye;
in an enlarged <s>arma</s>, likewise, he should work from the outer canthus while keeping the inner canthus in view.
When it has been properly cut, it should be rubbed with honey, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and rock-salt,
sprinkled with warm ghee, anointed with honey and ghee,
and bound up. After unbinding it, from the third day onward he should wash it
with milk cooked with <s>karañja</s> seeds, and also with decoctions
of the two <s>niśā</s>s, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, and <s>kiṃśuka</s>, mixed with honey,
together with buds of <s>kuraṇṭa</s>. He should remove the bandage on the seventh day.
When it has been properly cut there is health; disorders arising from deficient or excessive cutting
he should overcome with sprinkling, collyrium, and the like, using scraping or nourishing measures.
Sugar, realgar, <s>ileya</s>, best salt, and <s>nāgara</s> ginger,
with <s>tārkṣya</s> measured at half a <s>karṣa</s> and half a <s>pala</s>, liquefied with honey,
form a collyrium that conquers phlegmatic <s>timira</s>, <s>pilla</s>, <s>śukra</s>, <s>arma</s>, and dryness.
The bark of any one substance from <s>triphala</s>, made into a paste with water,
should be covered with a dish and burned on a potsherd; then it should be powdered.
It is then to be separately steeped in the juices of the remaining medicines, each one separately.

children.text: sā maṣī śoṣitā peṣyā bhūyo dvilavaṇānvitā
children.translated_text: That soot, once dried, should be ground again, combined with the two salts.
These three collyria, says <s>Nimi</s>, are supreme scraping agents.

children.text: sirājāle sirā yās tu kaṭhinā lekhanauṣadhaiḥ
children.translated_text: In a network of vessels, the veins that are hard and do not yield to scraping medicines,

children.text: na sidhyantyarmavat tāsāṃ piṭikānāṃ ca sādhanam ||
children.translated_text: and also the pustules there, have a treatment like that of <s>arma</s>.
In <s>śukra</s> disorders, treatment follows the doṣas; unctuous and dry measures are used, and bitter ghee is best.
Afterward, bloodletting from above, purgation, sprinkling, and similar measures are prescribed.

children.text: tris trivṛdvāriṇā pakvaṃ kṣataśukre ghṛtaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: In traumatic <s>śukra</s>, one should drink ghee cooked three times with water of <s>trivṛt</s>;
he should draw off blood by venesection, and from the eye with leeches.
Irrigation should be done with goat's milk, with sugar, prepared with blue lotus, <s>kākolī</s>, grapes, licorice, and <s>vidārī</s>,
or else simply with water.
When redness, tears, and pain have subsided, a scraping collyrium is best.
Wicks made from jasmine buds, lac, red ochre, and sandalwood
clarify pitta and blood, and destroy traumatic <s>śukra</s>.
With teeth produced from elephant, boar, camel, cow, horse, goat, and donkey,
together with conch, pearl, sea-foam, and ingredients such as black pepper,
a tooth-wick removes even traumatic <s>śukra</s> that has spread widely.
A wick of tamāla leaf, cow's tooth, conch-foam, donkey bone,
and copper, prepared with urine, destroys every particle of <s>śukra</s>.

children.text: ratnāni dantāḥ śṛṅgāṇi dhātavas tryūṣaṇaṃ truṭī
children.translated_text: Jewels, teeth, horns, metals, the three pungents, <s>truṭī</s>,
<s>karañja</s> seed, garlic, and medicines that break down wounds
make a collyrium that destroys <s>śukra</s> whether wounded or unwounded, deep-seated or lodged in the skin-layer.
A depressed lesion should be raised by drinking fats, nasal medication, juice-prepared collyria,
and, whether painful or painless, by a satisfying <s>puṭapāka</s> treatment for <s>śukraka</s>.
In pure <s>śukra</s>, irrigation is done with water of <s>niśā</s>, licorice, <s>śārivā</s>, and <s>śābara</s>,
or with a packet of <s>lodhra</s> dipped in warm water.
The root of <s>bṛhatī</s>, licorice, copper, rock-salt, and <s>nāgara</s> ginger
are ground with the water of <s>dhātrī</s> fruit and smeared on a copper vessel.
Then it should be fumigated repeatedly with barley, ghee, and leaves of <s>āmalakī</s>.
There one should make pills; ground with water and honey,
they are known as <s>Mahānīlā</s> and are supremely effective in removing pure <s>śukra</s>.

children.text: sthire śukre ghane cāsya bahuśo 'pahared asṛk
children.translated_text: When the <s>śukra</s> is fixed and dense, one should repeatedly draw off blood from him,
and should perform purgations of the head and body, and many <s>puṭapāka</s> treatments.
He should perform stimulation with black pepper, long pepper, <s>śirīṣa</s> fruit, and rock-salt,
or with salt that has been drunk together with a decoction of <s>triphala</s>.
Or he should prepare the following two collyrium formulas, each stated in half a verse:
with conch, the bone of <s>kola</s>, <s>kataka</s>, grapes, <s>madhuka</s>, and honey,
with <s>surā</s>, teeth, sea-derived impurities, and <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers;
the alkali obtained from <s>lāṅgalikā</s>, kept in the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> and <s>phaṇijjaka</s>,
then dried and powdered, is a collyrium for stimulating <s>śukra</s>.
Or hulled mung beans, ground and combined with conch and honey;
the essence from <s>madhūka</s>, mixed with honey, or marrow from <s>akṣa</s>, mixed with honey;
teeth of cow, donkey, horse, and camel, conch, and sea-born foam
make a wick with <s>arjuna</s> water that destroys stimulated particles of <s>śukra</s>.

children.text: utsannaṃ vā saśalyaṃ vā śukraṃ vālādibhir likhet ||
children.translated_text: If <s>śukra</s> is raised, or contains a foreign body, he should scrape it with hair and similar implements.
But in vascular <s>śukra</s> that has not destroyed sight, the treatment is like that for traumatic <s>śukra</s>.
<s>Puṇḍra</s>, licorice, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>siṃhī</s>, iron, <s>niśā</s>, and collyrium,
made into a paste with goat's milk and fumigated with ghee-smeared barley,
and alternately with <s>dhātrī</s> leaves, form here a wick that is the supreme collyrium.
If it is not pacified, one should apply surgery as for <s>arma</s>, and also in the disease called <s>ajakā</s>.
In incurable <s>ajakā</s>, and in <s>śukra</s> elsewhere when it is of that kind,
one should relieve pain by drinking fats, bloodletting, and the like.
To overcome its repulsiveness, one should undertake treatment for the elevation of <s>śukra</s>.
From coconut shell, <s>bhallātaka</s>, palm, bamboo, and <s>karīra</s>,
one should leach ash-water, and with those waters repeatedly steep powder made from camel bone.
In incurable <s>śukra</s> disorders, that collyrium removes discoloration;

children.text: sādhyeṣu sādhanāyālam idam eva ca śīlitam ||
children.translated_text: and, when used habitually, this same preparation is sufficient for curing curable cases.

children.text: ajakāṃ pārśvato viddhvā sūcyā visrāvya codakam
children.translated_text: In <s>ajakā</s>, after piercing from the side with a needle, one should drain out the fluid.
Having pressed evenly with the thumb, one should then fill it with material moistened with fat.

children.text: vraṇaṃ gomāṃsacūrṇena baddhaṃ baddhaṃ vimucya ca
children.translated_text: The wound should be dressed with powdered cow-flesh, bound up, and repeatedly unbound.

children.text: saptarātrād vraṇe rūḍhe kṛṣṇabhāge same sthire ||
children.translated_text: After seven nights, when the wound has healed and the black part is even and steady,

children.text: snehāñjanaṃ ca kartavyaṃ nasyaṃ ca kṣīrasarpiṣā
children.translated_text: unctuous collyrium should be applied, and nasal therapy should be done with milk-ghee.
Even so, if swelling recurs, procedures such as incision and excision

children.text: yuktyā kuryād yathā nāticchedena syāt nimajjanam ||
children.translated_text: should be performed with judgment, so that sinking does not result from excessive cutting.

children.text: nityaṃ ca śukreṣu śṛtaṃ yathāsvaṃ pāne ca marśe ca ghṛtaṃ vidadhyāt
children.translated_text: And in disorders of the white part, one should regularly prescribe ghee prepared as appropriate, both for drinking and for nasal unction.

children.text: na hīyate labdhabalā tathāntas tīkṣṇāñjanair dṛk satataṃ prayuktaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when sight has gained strength inwardly in that way, it is not impaired by sharp collyria used constantly.
Now then, we shall explain the chapter on the diagnosis of diseases of vision.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
When the impurity, following the channels, has first lodged in the first layer,
one sees forms indistinctly, even though they are distinct, without any evident cause.

children.text: prāpte dvitīyaṃ paṭalaṃ abhūtam api paśyati
children.translated_text: When it has reached the second layer, one sees even what is not present;

children.text: bhūtaṃ tu yatnād āsannaṃ dūre sūkṣmaṃ ca nekṣate ||
children.translated_text: but what is present, near, distant, and subtle one does not see even with effort.
One also takes a form that is far or near to be the opposite.
When the doṣa is situated in the circular field, one sees things as if they were circles.
When it is in the middle of sight, one thing appears twofold; when it is in many places, it appears manifold.
When it has gone inside the organ of sight, there is reversal of small and large.
When it is situated below, one does not see what is near; when it is situated above, one does not see what is far.

children.text: pārśve paśyen na pārśvasthe timirākhyo 'yam āmayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it is at the side, one does not see what is lateral; this disease is called <s>timira</s>.
When the doṣa has lodged in the third layer, it reaches the state of <s>kāca</s>.
Through that, one sees upward and not downward, as if covered by a thin cloth.

children.text: yathāvarṇaṃ ca rajyeta dṛṣṭir hīyeta ca kramāt
children.translated_text: The sight becomes colored according to the doṣa, and gradually declines.
If even then it is neglected, the impurity, having gone to the fourth layer,
causes <s>liṅganāśa</s> and covers the circle of sight.

children.text: tatra vātena timire vyāviddham iva paśyati ||
children.translated_text: In <s>timira</s> caused by vāta, one sees as if things were scattered or pierced through.
One repeatedly sees a moving, turbid, reddish appearance, and at times a clear one.
And if this is neglected, one sees nets, hairs, gnats, and rays.
When the eye has become affected by <s>kāca</s>, it is red and sees a face as noseless.
It sees the moon, lamps, and the like as multiple, and thinks even a straight thing crooked.

children.text: vṛddhaḥ kāco dṛśaṃ kuryād rajodhūmāvṛtām iva
children.translated_text: Advanced <s>kāca</s> makes the sight appear as if covered with dust and smoke,
clearly reddish in hue, expanded, contracted, or deprived of vision.

children.text: sa liṅganāśo vāte tu saṃkocayati dṛksirāḥ
children.translated_text: That is <s>liṅganāśa</s>; in the vāta type it constricts the vessels of sight.

children.text: dṛṅmaṇḍalaṃ viśatyantar gambhīrā dṛg asau smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: It enters within the visual circle; that condition of sight is remembered as the deep type.
In pitta-born <s>timira</s>, one sees things lit by flashes like lightning and fireflies,
with the appearance of peacock or partridge feathers, and most often blue.

children.text: kāce dṛk kācanīlābhā tādṛg eva ca paśyati
children.translated_text: In <s>kāca</s>, the eye has an appearance like yellow and blue, and it sees just such things.
It also sees halos around the sun and moon, fire, rays, and rainbows.
Because of <s>liṅganāśa</s>, the sight is glossy, dark-blue like a bee, and without light.

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ pittena hrasvākhyā sā hrasvā hrasvadarśinī ||
children.translated_text: Sight affected by pitta is called the short type; being short, it sees things as short.
It becomes the type called pitta-burnt: yellow, and seeing yellowish things.

children.text: kaphena timire prāyaḥ snigdhaṃ śvetaṃ ca paśyati ||
children.translated_text: In <s>timira</s> caused by kapha, one generally sees things as oily and white,
as if covered with conches, the moon, jasmine flowers, and white lotuses.
But in <s>kāca</s>, it sees as if things were covered with dim moons, suns, lamps, and the like.

children.text: sitābhā sā ca dṛṣṭiḥ syālliṅganāśe tu lakṣyate
children.translated_text: That sight becomes white in appearance; in <s>liṅganāśa</s> it is observed that
kapha, embodied and lodged in sight, oily in nature, destroys vision.
It is movable like a drop of water, situated in the cup of a lotus petal.
In heat it contracts; in shade it spreads about.
Its whiteness is like conch, jasmine, the moon, white lotus, and crystal.

children.text: raktena timire raktaṃ tamobhūtaṃ ca paśyati ||
children.translated_text: In <s>timira</s> caused by blood, one sees things as red and as covered in darkness.

children.text: kācena raktā kṛṣṇā vā dṛṣṭis tādṛk ca paśyati
children.translated_text: With <s>kāca</s>, the sight is red or black, and it sees things accordingly.
Even in <s>liṅganāśa</s>, the eye is like that: lusterless and deprived of vision.
In combined and all-doṣa conditions, one should know the symptoms to be mixed.
From <s>timira</s> onward, because of them, the vision suddenly becomes manifestly confused.

children.text: timire śeṣayor dṛṣṭau citro rāgaḥ prajāyate
children.translated_text: In the two remaining kinds of <s>timira</s>, a variegated discoloration arises in the sight.
When one's eye, filled with impurities, gleams like that of a mongoose,

children.text: nakulāndhaḥ sa tatrāhni citraṃ paśyati no niśi
children.translated_text: he is called <s>nakulāndha</s>; in the daytime he sees variegatedly, but not at night.
When the sun has set and its rays rest on the western summit, the doṣas become fixed,

children.text: sthagayanti dṛśaṃ doṣā doṣāndhaḥ sa gado 'paraḥ
children.translated_text: and cover the sight; that is another disease, called <s>doṣāndha</s>.
When touched by the rays of the sun, the impurities fall away from the path of sight;
dissolved and withdrawn, they allow clear vision there in the daytime.
When a person heated by warmth suddenly plunges into cold water,
heat, mixed with the three doṣas and blood, goes upward from there into the eyes.
There arise burning, heat, a dirty whiteness, and turbid vision by day;

children.text: rātrāvāndhyaṃ ca jāyeta vidagdhoṣṇena sā smṛtā
children.translated_text: night blindness also arises. That is remembered as the condition burnt by heat.

children.text: bhṛśam amlāśanād doṣaiḥ sāsrair yā dṛṣṭirācitā ||
children.translated_text: The sight that is filled with doṣas together with blood because of excessive eating of sour foods,
moist, itchy, and turbid, is remembered as the condition burnt by sourness.
In one who is distressed by grief, fever, or disease of the head, vāta and the other doṣas

children.text: dhūmāvilāṃ dhūmadṛśaṃ dṛśaṃ kuryuḥ sa dhūmaraḥ
children.translated_text: make the sight smoky and turbid, a smoke-seeing sight; that condition is <s>dhūmara</s>.
When a person of slight strength suddenly looks at a wondrous form,
or at something brilliant, such as the sun, vāta and the other doṣas lodged in the eye
dry up its radiance and make the sight robbed of vision,
colored like beryl, motionless, and as if natural and painless.
This is called adventitious <s>liṅganāśa</s>; here one should reject it as untreatable.
Except for kapha-born cases of <s>liṅganāśa</s>, one should also reject the deep type and the short-born type...

children.text: ṣaṭ kācā nakulāndhaśca yāpyāḥ śeṣāṃstu sādhayet
children.translated_text: The six forms of <s>kāca</s> and <s>nakulāndha</s> are manageable; the remaining ones should be cured.
Thus, with the twelve diseases of sight, twenty-seven disorders have been specified.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>timira</s>.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
<s>Timira</s> becomes the state of <s>kāca</s>, and <s>kāca</s> too becomes blindness if neglected.
Therefore, among eye diseases, one should treat dreadful <s>timira</s> quickly.
One should cook one <s>tulā</s> of <s>jīvantī</s> in a <s>droṇa</s> of water until one quarter remains.
In that decoction, with twice as much milk, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee.
It should be prepared with <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and rock salt,
and with <s>śatāhvā</s>, licorice, grapes, sugar, deodar, and the three myrobalans.

children.text: kārṣikair niśi tat pītaṃ timirāpaharaṃ param
children.translated_text: When drunk at night, with those ingredients in one-<s>karṣa</s> measures, it is supreme for removing <s>timira</s>.
With grapes, sandalwood, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
with sugar, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>medā</s>, white lotus, licorice, and blue lotus,
one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of old ghee with an equal quantity of milk and with paste-ingredients measured by the <s>picu</s>.
That destroys <s>kāca</s>, <s>timira</s>, red streaks, and headache.
Pointed gourd, neem, <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>sevya</s>, <s>varā</s>, and <s>vṛṣa</s>,
together with <s>dhanvayāsa</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, and <s>parpaṭa</s>, each in one-<s>pala</s> portions,
and a <s>prastha</s> of emblic myrobalans, should be decocted in brackish water.
In an <s>āḍhaka</s> of that, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with ground ingredients of half-<s>pala</s> measure,
namely <s>musta</s>, <s>bhūnimba</s>, licorice, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>udīcya</s>, and sandalwood,
together with <s>pippalī</s>; that ghee conquers diseases of the nose, ears, and mouth.
It removes abscess, fever, bad ulcers, erysipelas, scrofula, and skin disease.
In particular it removes white opacity, <s>timira</s>, night-blindness, and burning from heat and sourness.
Eight <s>palas</s> of <s>triphala</s> should be decocted in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water until one quarter remains.
With that decoction, with an equal amount of milk, and with a paste of one <s>pala</s> of <s>triphala</s>,

children.text: ardhaprastho ghṛtāt siddhaḥ sitayā mākṣikeṇa vā ||
children.translated_text: a half-<s>prastha</s> of ghee is prepared; a patient with <s>timira</s> should drink it with sugar or honey,

children.text: yuktaṃ pibet tat timirī tadyuktaṃ vā varārasam
children.translated_text: or should drink <s>varā</s> juice combined with it.
With licorice, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, <s>vyāghrī</s>, black <s>amṛtā</s>, and blue lotus,
each in one-<s>pala</s> portions and together with sugar and grapes, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee,
with separate equal quantities of goat's milk, <s>varā</s> fat, <s>mārkava</s>, and its fresh juice.
This is called the great <s>Traiphala</s>; it is supreme for conquering disorders of sight.
Then, while licking <s>triphala</s> at night with <s>traiphala</s> ghee,
combined with licorice and thoroughly mixed with honey,
and for one month, eating wholesome food and drinking water infused with emblic myrobalan,
one obtains eyesight like <s>Suparṇa</s>'s; so said the blessed <s>Nimi</s>.
<s>Varā</s>, when combined as desired with <s>tāpya</s>, iron, gold, licorice, sugar, old ghee, and honey,
is an excellent destroyer of <s>timira</s>.
Or a person suffering from <s>timira</s> should regularly use a decoction of <s>varā</s> with ghee.
Or one may use cakes, soups, or roasted flour mixed with <s>triphala</s> powder,
or cold milk-rice joined with <s>varā</s> and with honey and sugar.

children.text: prātar bhaktasya vā pūrvam adyāt pathyāṃ pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: In the morning, before the meal, one should eat <s>pathyā</s> separately,
constantly, with raisins, sugar, and honey, if one is afflicted by <s>timira</s>.
Sixty-four parts of <s>srotoja</s>, joined separately with one part each
of copper, iron, silver, and gold, and placed inside a closed crucible,
should be heated until fully fused; then it should be quenched
seven times each, separately, in decoctions of mercury and sulphur.
Then, joined with three parts each of beryl, pearl, and conch shell,
one should use it as powdered collyrium; it removes every <s>timira</s>.
With <s>māṃsī</s>, the three aromatics, iron, saffron, blue lotus, chebulic myrobalan, and blue vitriol,
with white <s>kāca</s>, cuttlefish bone, pepper, collyrium, long pepper, and licorice,
all well powdered under the moon when <s>Aśvinī</s> is lord, one should anoint the pair of eyes,
if one desires the pacification of <s>timira</s>, pterygium, red streaks, itching, <s>kāca</s>, and the like.
There are one part each of pepper and excellent salt, and two parts each of long pepper and sea foam.
Nine parts of <s>sauvīra</s>, powdered under <s>Citrā</s>, conquer disorders caused by <s>kapha</s>.
In the fresh juices of grapes and lotus stalk, and in milk, wine, and fat,
and separately in divine waters, <s>srotoja</s> should be quenched seven times.
That, powdered and kept in a conch shell, is a sight-clearing collyrium.
It is praised in all eye diseases and was made by the king of <s>Videha</s>.
Blue vitriol, burnt with jujube charcoal and quenched in this way,
successively in goat's milk, ghee, and honey, should be taken from that in a quantity of two <s>palas</s>.
It is joined with one-<s>karṣa</s> portions of <s>tāpya</s>, pepper, <s>srotoja</s>, <s>kaṭuka</s>, and <s>natā</s>,
and with pointed gourd, <s>lodhra</s>, realgar, <s>pathyā</s>, long pepper, cardamom, collyrium, and sea foam.
Together with one <s>pala</s> of licorice, it is heated inside a crucible and powdered.
When regularly used, it removes <s>kāca</s>, pterygium, night-blindness, and red streaks.

children.text: cūrṇo viśeṣāt timiraṃ bhāskaro bhāskaro yathā
children.translated_text: In particular, the powder removes <s>timira</s>, like the sun, the sun indeed.
There are thirty parts of serpent, and five of sulphur stone,
two parts each of copper and orpiment, one of tin, and three of collyrium.
Made in a closed crucible, heated, and cooked, it becomes a stainless collyrium.
In the world it ends <s>timira</s>, like a second sun.

children.text: gomūtre chagaṇarase 'mlakāñjike ca strīstanye haviṣi viṣe ca mākṣike ca
children.translated_text: Blue vitriol, heated and repeatedly quenched in cow urine, dung juice, sour gruel, woman's breast milk, ghee, poison, and honey,

children.text: yat tutthaṃ jvalitam anekaśo niṣiktaṃ tat kuryād garuḍasamaṃ narasya cakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: makes a man's sight equal to <s>Garuḍa</s>'s.
Lead which, separately, seven times, has been heated again and again and made to drink

children.text: yaṣṭīrasaṃ ca yat sīsaṃ saptakṛtvaḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: water from <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, ghee with poison, goat's milk,

children.text: taptaṃ taptaṃ pāyitaṃ tacchalākā netre yuktā sāñjanānañjanā vā
children.translated_text: and licorice juice, becomes a probe applied to the eye, either with collyrium or without collyrium.

children.text: taimiryārmasrāvapaicchilyapaillaṃ kaṇḍūṃ jāḍyaṃ raktarājīṃ ca hanti ||
children.translated_text: It destroys dimness, pterygium, discharge, sliminess, whiteness, itching, dullness, and red streaks.
Mercury and serpent are equal, and the collyrium made from them is likewise equal in measure.
That <s>añjana</s> (collyrium), joined with a little camphor, removes <s>timira</s>.
For the vulture whose neck shines like the young sun, its mouth, when it has died at the proper time, is to be burned with cow dung.

children.text: nirdagdhaṃ samaghṛtam añjanaṃ ca peṣyaṃ yogo 'yaṃ nayanabalaṃ karoti gārdhram ||
children.translated_text: Ground together with ghee and collyrium, this preparation gives the eyes the strength of a vulture.
The smoke issuing from collyrium burned, together with poison, in the mouth of a black snake

children.text: cūrṇitaṃ naladapattravimiśraṃ bhinnatāram api rakṣati cakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: when powdered and mixed with leaves of <s>nalada</s>, protects the eye even when the pupil is split.
One should place a dead black snake and also four scorpions
in a pot of milk, moisten them for twenty-one days, and then churn it.

children.text: tatra yannavanītaṃ syāt puṣṇīyāt tena kukkuṭam
children.translated_text: With whatever butter arises there, one should nourish a cock.
By collyrium made from its excrement, a blind man surely sees.
Fat of a black snake, conch shell, fruit of <s>kataka</s>, and collyrium:
this <s>rasakriyā</s> soon grants sight to the blind.

children.text: maricāni daśārdhapicustāpyāt tutthāt palaṃ picur yaṣṭyāḥ
children.translated_text: Five <s>picus</s> of pepper, a <s>pala</s> of heated blue vitriol, and a <s>picu</s> of licorice,
burned while moist with milk, make the excellent collyrium called <s>Apratisāra</s> for <s>timira</s>.
Pills made from seeds of <s>akṣa</s>, pepper, bark of emblic myrobalan, blue vitriol, and licorice, ground with water
and dried only in the shade, quickly destroy forms of <s>timira</s>.
With pepper, emblic myrobalan, water-born blue vitriol, collyrium, and <s>tāpya</s> mineral, each increasing successively in amount,
there is the preparation called <s>Ṣaṇmākṣika</s>; it destroys <s>timira</s>, pterygium, moistness, <s>kāca</s>, and itching.

children.text: ratnāni rūpyaṃ sphaṭikaṃ suvarṇaṃ sroto'ñjanaṃ tāmram ayaḥ saśaṅkhaṃ
children.translated_text: Gems, silver, crystal, gold, <s>sroto'ñjana</s>, copper, iron, and conch shell,
together with inferior sandalwood and red ochre, form a powdered collyrium that cures all diseases of sight.
Sesame oil, oil of <s>akṣa</s>, fresh juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and a decoction from <s>asana</s>,
cooked in an iron vessel, make a <s>nasya</s> (nasal medicine) that gives strength to vision.
According to the doṣa involved, one should treat it in many ways, as suitable, with oleation, bloodletting, drainage, purgation, and nasal therapy,
with collyrium, head enema, enema procedures, <s>tarpaṇa</s> (eye-satiation), pastes, and sprinklings.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ sādhanam idaṃ pratidoṣam ataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: This is the general treatment. Now listen to what is specific to each doṣa.
In <s>timira</s> born of <s>vāta</s>, one should drink ghee cooked with water of <s>daśamūla</s>,
with four times as much milk, and with a paste of <s>śreṣṭhā</s>.
One should also prescribe purgation with a decoction of <s>triphala</s> and the five roots,
combined with milk and joined with castor oil.
One should boil a <s>tulā</s> of <s>jīvantī</s> together with its root and network of rootlets in a <s>droṇa</s> of water.
When one eighth remains, one should cook in it a <s>prastha</s> of oil, with an equal amount of milk.
With one-<s>pala</s> portions of the three <s>balā</s>s, <s>jīvantī</s>, and roots of <s>varī</s>,
and with four <s>palas</s> of licorice, one should cook it in an iron vessel.

children.text: loha eva sthitaṃ māsaṃ nāvanād ūrdhvajatrujān
children.translated_text: After it has remained in that same iron vessel for a month, by nasal administration it destroys diseases above the clavicles
arising from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, especially those situated in the eyes.
It gives nourishment, beauty, and luster to the hair, mouth, neck, and shoulders.
Oil cooked with white castor root, <s>siṃhī</s>, <s>phaladāru</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>natā</s>,
<s>ghoṣā</s>, and roots of bilva, together with milk,
as <s>nasya</s> conquers pain from all diseases of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> arising above the clavicles.

children.text: vasāñjane ca vaiyāghrī vārāhī vā praśasyate
children.translated_text: Among fatty collyria, that from tiger or from boar is recommended,
or that originating from vulture, snake, or cock, each separately combined with licorice.
For a secondary collyrium, <s>srotoja</s> should be steeped successively in mercury, milk, and ghee,
and applied as before; it is an unsurpassed destroyer of <s>timira</s>.

children.text: na ced evaṃ śamaṃ yāti tatastarpaṇam ācaret
children.translated_text: If it does not become pacified in this way, then one should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s>.
With dill seed, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>nalada</s>, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, and licorice,
with <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>sarala</s>, long pepper, and deodar,
ghee cooked with eight times as much milk makes an excellent <s>tarpaṇa</s>.
Likewise, from the fat of an antelope, prepared with milk and churned with a churn-stick,
one should extract the essence and prepare it with licorice, <s>uśīra</s>, and sandalwood.
The fat of porcupines, hedgehogs, and iguanas, and of cocks, partridges, and peacocks,

children.text: pṛthak pṛthag anenaiva vidhinā kalpayed vasām ||
children.translated_text: should be prepared separately by this same method.
One should employ a clarifying and oleating <s>puṭapāka</s> preparation,
and here also a decoction enema with an oil enema, as in <s>vātapīnasa</s>.
In <s>timira</s> born of <s>pitta</s>, after giving the patient ghee cooked with life-promoting herbs and the three fruits to drink,
one should, when he has become oleated, pierce a vein.
One should purge him with powders of sugar, cardamom, and turpeth, mixed with honey.
One should apply very cooling sprinklings, pastes, and the like to the eyes, mouth, and head.
A collyrium stick made with <s>śārivā</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, pearl, <s>śābara</s>, and sandalwood is recommended,
as is a powder for collyrium with leaves, blue lotus, and collyrium,
together with <s>nāgapuṣpa</s>, camphor, licorice, gold, and red ochre.
Of <s>sauvīrāñjana</s>, blue vitriol, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, emblic myrobalan fruit, crystal, and camphor,

children.text: pañcāṃśaṃ pañcāṃśaṃ tryaṃśam athaikāṃśam añjanaṃ timiraghnam
children.translated_text: five parts, five parts, three parts, and then one part respectively make a collyrium that destroys <s>timira</s>.
And ghee cooked with milk, life-promoting herbs, sugar, and blue lotus is used as <s>nasya</s>.
In <s>timira</s> arising from <s>śleṣman</s>, one should give ghee cooked with decoction of <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>varā</s>, and <s>kaṇa</s> to drink.
When he has drunk it, one should pierce a vein and afterward give purgation.
One should give a decoction made from areca nut, chebulic myrobalan, dry ginger, black pepper, <s>kumbha</s>, and <s>nikumbha</s>,
with pastes of <s>hrīvera</s>, deodar, the two turmerics, and black pepper, mixed with milk.
Oil cooked in a decoction of the two sets of five roots is a nasal medicine,
with conch shell, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>nepālī</s>, the pungent triad, and the three fruits.

children.text: dṛgvaimalyāya vimalā vartiḥ syāt kokilā punaḥ
children.translated_text: For clarity of sight, there is the stainless collyrium stick; the <s>Kokilā</s> again...
with filings of black iron, <s>vyoṣa</s>, rock salt, <s>triphala</s>, and collyrium;
and with the frontal bone of hare, cow, donkey, lion, camel, and birds,
with white cow's hair, pepper, conch shell, sandalwood, and sea foam,
ground with breast milk, ghee, and milk, a wick conquers <s>timira</s> and <s>śukra</s>.
In the blood-born type, success is as in the pitta-born type; one should also soothe the blood with cooling measures.
With grapes, lotus stalk, <s>lodhra</s>, and licorice, with conch shell, copper, snow, lotus, and <s>padmaka</s>,
and with blue lotus, made into wicks with goat's milk, blood-born <s>timira</s> quickly disappears.
When it arises from association of doṣas or from all doṣas together, treatment should follow the predominance of the doṣas.
An oil prepared with <s>madhūka</s>, <s>kṛmijit</s>, pepper, and <s>amaradāru</s>,

children.text: sakṣīraṃ nāvanaṃ tailaṃ piṣṭair lepo mukhasya ca
children.translated_text: together with milk, is used as a nasal medication; and a paste of these ground drugs is applied to the face.
Oil prepared with <s>natā</s>, blue lotus, <s>anantā</s>, licorice, and <s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>

children.text: sādhitaṃ nāvane tailaṃ śirovastau ca śasyate
children.translated_text: is recommended for nasal medication and for a head-retaining treatment.
One should put powdered <s>kaṇa</s> and rock salt into a decoction of <s>uśīra</s>;

children.text: tat srutaṃ saghṛtaṃ bhūyaḥ pacet kṣaudraṃ ghane kṣipet
children.translated_text: after straining it, one should cook it again with ghee, and add honey when it has thickened.

children.text: śīte cāsmin hitam idaṃ sarvaje timire 'ñjanam ||
children.translated_text: When cold, this is a beneficial collyrium for <s>timira</s> produced by all doṣas.
Bones of night-roaming creatures, filled with marrow,
combined with <s>srotoja</s> collyrium, should be tied up and soaked in water.
After a month or twenty nights, one should take them out and dry them.
Then, together with flowers of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s> and with licorice,
they are powdered; this is the best collyrium for <s>timira</s> caused by all doṣas.
In <s>kāca</s> too this procedure applies, except for veins compressed by an instrument,

children.text: āndhyāya syur malā dadyāt srāvye tvasre jalaukasaḥ
children.translated_text: for the humors would cause blindness; but when blood is to be discharged, one should apply leeches.

children.text: guḍaḥ pheno 'ñjanaṃ kṛṣṇā maricaṃ kuṅkumād rajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Jaggery, sea foam, collyrium, long pepper, pepper, and powder from saffron
make this extract preparation with honey, a collyrium that keeps <s>kāca</s> in check.
For <s>nakulāndha</s> arising from the three doṣas, the procedure prescribed for <s>timira</s> applies.
An extract preparation with ghee, honey, and fresh cow-dung juice
and with <s>tārkṣya</s>, red ochre, and <s>tālīśa</s> is a beneficial collyrium in night-blindness.
Pepper rubbed with curd is an excellent collyrium in night-blindness.
With <s>karañjika</s>, blue lotus, gold, red ochre, and lotus filaments,
ground with cow-dung water, a wick destroys blindness caused by the doṣas.
Or, with goat urine, <s>kauntī</s>, long pepper, <s>srotoja</s>, and rock salt,
with <s>kālānusārī</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>triphala</s>, orpiment, and realgar,
and with sea foam and goat's milk, wicks are beneficial in night-blindness.
One should place long peppers in the middle of a liver and cook it without burning them;

children.text: tāḥ śuṣkā madhunā ghṛṣṭā niśāndhe śreṣṭham añjanam ||
children.translated_text: when dried and rubbed with honey, they are the best collyrium in night-blindness.
One should also eat the spleen and liver of a buffalo with oil and ghee,

children.text: ghṛte siddhāni jīvantyāḥ pallavāni ca bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: and should eat tender leaves of <s>jīvantī</s> cooked in ghee.
Likewise one should eat those of <s>atimuktaka</s>, castor, <s>śephālī</s>, and <s>abhīru</s>.

children.text: bhṛṣṭaṃ ghṛtaṃ kumbhayoneḥ pattraiḥ pāne ca pūjitam ||
children.translated_text: Ghee fried with leaves of <s>Agastya</s> is esteemed for drinking.
In smoky vision, sour-pitta, heat, and burning, one should make the patient unctuous with old ghee
and purge him with cooling purgatives; one should also anoint him everywhere with cooling applications.
A collyrium cooked with cow-dung juice, milk, and ghee is recommended.
It is an extract preparation with powders of gold, red ochre, and <s>tālīśa</s> added.
With <s>medā</s>, <s>śābaraka</s>, <s>anantā</s>, madder, barberry, and licorice,

children.text: kṣīrāṣṭāṃśaṃ ghṛtaṃ pakvaṃ satailaṃ nāvanaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: ghee cooked with one eighth part milk and with oil is beneficial as a nasal medication.
Satiating the eye should be done with milk and ghee; if it is not pacified, venesection is prescribed.
From anxiety, injury, fear, grief, dryness, excessive weeping or coughing,
from improper use of purgation, nasal medication, emesis, <s>puṭapāka</s>, and the like,
from vomiting after indigestible food, or from suppression of hunger, thirst, and so on,
and after eye diseases, a person may see as one suffering from <s>timira</s> sees.

children.text: yathāsvaṃ tatra yuñjīta doṣādīn vīkṣya bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: There one should apply medicine according to the specific condition, after examining the doṣas and other factors.
For one whose sight has been injured by looking at an eclipse of the sun, fire, lightning, and the like,

children.text: saṃtarpaṇaṃ snigdhahimādi kāryaṃ tathāñjanaṃ hema ghṛtena ghṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: nourishing treatment, unctuous and cooling measures, and the like should be done, as well as a collyrium of gold rubbed with ghee.

children.text: cakṣūrakṣāyāṃ sarvakālaṃ manuṣyair yatnaḥ kartavyo jīvite yāvad icchā
children.translated_text: For the protection of the eyes, people should always make effort for as long as they desire life.

children.text: vyartho loko 'yaṃ tulyarātriṃdivānāṃ puṃsām andhānāṃ vidyamāne 'pi vitte ||
children.translated_text: For blind men, even if wealth is present, this world is useless, since night and day are the same.

children.text: triphalā rudhirasrutir viśuddhir manaso nirvṛtirañjanaṃ sanasyam
children.translated_text: <s>Triphala</s>, bloodletting, purification, calmness of mind, collyrium with nasal medication,

children.text: śakunāśanatā sapādapūjā ghṛtapānaṃ ca sadaiva netrarakṣā ||
children.translated_text: eating bird meat, worship of the feet, and drinking ghee are always protection for the eyes.
Constant abstention from unsuitable food, and from looking intensely at very bright, moving, or minute objects,

children.text: muninā niminopadiṣṭam etat paramaṃ rakṣaṇam īkṣaṇasya puṃsām ||
children.translated_text: this was taught by the sage <s>Nimi</s> as the supreme protection of men's sight.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of <s>liṅganāśa</s>.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
One should puncture a mature, non-seeing <s>liṅganāśa</s> born of kapha,
provided it is free from the six complications beginning with <s>āvartakī</s>.
For when it is not yet mature, it is irregular, thin, and like the whey of curd;
even when drawn down with a probe, it rises upward again.

children.text: karoti vedanāṃ tīvrāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ ca sthagayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: It produces intense pain and again obstructs sight.
It is quickly filled by kapha-producing substances, and, because of other complications, persists for a long time.
Since kapha is white, kapha-born <s>liṅganāśa</s> is white;
when other doṣas overpower it, the disease becomes bluish.
In <s>āvarta</s>, the sight is unsteady and whirling; in <s>āvartakī</s> it is reddish-black,
as though filled with particles of gravel or the milky sap of the arka plant, and very dense.
In <s>rājīmatī</s>, the sight is filled with lines like the awns of rice,
and when it has an uneven, cut, or burnt appearance and is painful, it is known as <s>chinnāṃśukā</s>.
When the visual field has a bronze-like color, it is <s>Candrakī</s>, shaped like the moon;

children.text: chattrābhā naikavarṇā ca chattrakī nāma nīlikā ||
children.translated_text: and when it has the appearance of an umbrella and many colors, the <s>nīlikā</s> is called <s>Chattrakī</s>.
One should not puncture the eyes of those unfit for the knife, nor of those with thirst, coryza, or cough;
nor of those with indigestion, fear, vomiting, or pain in the head, ears, or eyes.
Then, at a suitable ordinary season, when the patient has been purified and fed,
in a bright place in the forenoon, the physician should sit on a knee-high seat.
The patient should be seated and restrained, and the eye should be warmed with breaths from the mouth;
with the eye rubbed by the thumb, when the physician sees the impurity lifted in the visual field,

children.text: svāṃ nāsāṃ prekṣamāṇasya niṣkampaṃ mūrdhni dhārite
children.translated_text: while the patient looks at his own nose and keeps the head motionless,
leaving half an <s>aṅgula</s> from the black part and likewise a quarter <s>aṅgula</s> from the outer canthus,
holding the probe steady with the index finger, middle finger, and thumb,

children.text: daivacchidraṃ nayet pārśvād ūrdhvam āmanthayan iva ||
children.translated_text: he should guide it upward from the side through the natural opening, as if churning.
He should puncture the left eye with the right hand, and the other eye with the left;

children.text: vidhyet suviddhe śabdaḥ syād aruk cāmbulavasrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it is well punctured, there is a sound, absence of pain, and a trickling of water.

children.text: sāntvayann āturaṃ cānu netraṃ stanyena secayet
children.translated_text: Then, soothing the patient, he should sprinkle the eye with breast milk,
and afterward scrape the circle of the eye with the tip of the probe.
Without causing obstruction or injury, slowly pressing it toward the nose,
he should remove the <s>kapha</s> situated in the visual circle by making the patient sniff upward.

children.text: sthire doṣe cale vāti svedayed akṣi bāhyataḥ
children.translated_text: If the <s>doṣa</s> remains fixed, or if it moves about, he should foment the eye externally;
then, when forms are seen, he should slowly withdraw the probe.

children.text: ghṛtāplutaṃ picuṃ dattvā baddhākṣaṃ śāyayet tataḥ
children.translated_text: After placing a pad soaked in ghee, he should bind the eye and then have the patient lie down,

children.text: viddhād anyena pārśvena tam uttānaṃ dvayor vyadhe ||
children.translated_text: on the side opposite the punctured eye, or supine if both eyes have been punctured.
In a windless bed, with head and feet anointed, he should remain devoted to what is wholesome.

children.text: kṣavathuṃ kāsam udgāraṃ ṣṭhīvanaṃ pānam ambhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sneezing, coughing, belching, spitting, and drinking water,
lying face down, bathing, cleaning the teeth, and chewing or eating
he should not do for seven days; here the restriction is like that for one who has drunk unctuous medicine.

children.text: śaktito laṅghayet seko ruji koṣṇena sarpiṣā
children.translated_text: According to his strength, he should be made to fast; if there is pain, sprinkling should be done with lukewarm ghee.
He should eat a liquid gruel made with pungents and emblic myrobalan, together with ghee,

children.text: vilepīṃ vā tryahāccāsya kvāthair muktvākṣi secayet
children.translated_text: or a thick gruel; after three days, uncovering his eye, one should sprinkle it with decoctions
that pacify <s>vāta</s>; but on the seventh day one should release the eye completely.
He should observe the restrictions until the sight has gained steadiness,
and should not suddenly look at subtle or brilliant forms.
Swelling, redness, pain, and the like, and the arising of <s>adhimantha</s>,
come from unwholesome behavior and from faults in puncturing; one should treat them each according to its nature.
Pastes of <s>dūrvā</s>, barley, red ochre, and <s>śārivā</s>, mixed with ghee,
should be used as applications to the face for the pacification of pain and redness.
Sesame seeds with mustard, likewise, soaked in citron juice,
together with <s>payasyā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>pattra</s>, madder, and licorice,
make a pleasantly warm poultice mixed with goat's milk, bringing the highest comfort.
Goat's milk boiled with <s>lodhra</s>, rock salt, raisins, and licorice
should be used as an eye-drop; it destroys pain and redness.
Or with licorice, blue lotus, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, together with grapes, lac, and sugar,
ghee cooked in milk prepared with <s>vāta</s>-pacifying drugs and with four times the quantity of liquid,
with <s>padmaka</s> and the like added as the paste-drug, is praised for all such procedures.
If there is still no relief, he should open a vein after the patient has been oleated and fomented,

children.text: manthoktāṃ ca kriyāṃ kuryād vedhe rūḍhe 'ñjanaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: and should perform the treatment taught for <s>mantha</s>; when the puncture has healed, a mild collyrium should be used.
With <s>āḍhakī</s> root, pepper, orpiment, and extract-collyrium,
a collyrium stick with jaggery, ground in rainwater, should be applied to the punctured eye.
Jasmine, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>dhava</s>, the flower of <s>meṣaviṣāṇī</s>, beryl, and pearl-fruit are finely ground with milk;

children.text: ājena tāmram amunā pratanu pradigdhaṃ saptāhataḥ punaridaṃ payasaiva piṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: copper is thinly coated with this using goat's milk, and after seven days it is again ground with milk.

children.text: piṇḍāñjanaṃ hitam anātapaśuṣkam akṣṇi viddhe prasādajananaṃ balakṛcca dṛṣṭeḥ
children.translated_text: This lump-collyrium, dried out of the sun, is beneficial for a punctured eye, producing clarity and strengthening sight.
A preparation with <s>srotoja</s>, coral, realgar, sea-foam, and pungent substances is said to be equal to it in qualities and preparation.
Now then, we shall explain the diagnosis of all eye diseases.
So indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
When the eye is affected by <s>vāta</s> <s>abhiṣyanda</s>, there is nasal obstruction and slight swelling,
with piercing, throbbing, and splitting pain in the temples, eyes, brows, and forehead.

children.text: śuṣkālpā dūṣikā śītam acchaṃ cāśru calā rujaḥ
children.translated_text: The discharge is dry and scanty; the tears are cold and clear, and the pains are shifting.
Closing and opening the eyelids is difficult, and there is a crawling sensation as if of small creatures.
The eye appears as though distended and as though filled with fine thorns.
It is relieved by unctuous and warm measures. That <s>abhiṣyanda</s>, if neglected,

children.text: adhimantho bhavet tatra karṇayor nadanaṃ bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: becomes <s>adhimantha</s>; in that condition there is ringing in the ears and dizziness,
and the forehead, eyes, brows, and the rest seem to be churned like fire-sticks in wood.

children.text: hatādhimanthaḥ so 'pi syāt pramādāt tena vedanāḥ
children.translated_text: Through negligence that too may become <s>hatādhimantha</s>; because of it pains

children.text: anekarūpā jāyante vraṇo dṛṣṭau ca dṛṣṭihā ||
children.translated_text: of many forms arise, along with an ulcer in the visual field and loss of sight.
When <s>vāyu</s>, proceeding from the neck, eye, temple, or from elsewhere,
causes intense pain and contracts the eye, without sliminess, redness, or swelling,
and with streaming tears, it is called <s>anyato-vāta</s>.
Likewise the eye becomes crooked, or becomes diminished, in <s>vāta-paryaya</s>.

children.text: dāho dhūmāyanaṃ śophaḥ śyāvatā vartmano bahiḥ
children.translated_text: Burning, a smoky sensation, swelling, and dark discoloration outside the eyelid,
internal moistness, yellow and hot tears, redness, and seeing things as yellowish:
an eye as if sprinkled with caustic and wounded are the signs of <s>pittābhiṣyanda</s>.
In <s>adhimantha</s> the eye becomes like one strewn with burning coals and with the lustre of a lump of liver;

children.text: adhimanthe bhaven netraṃ syande tu kaphasaṃbhave
children.translated_text: but in a discharge arising from <s>kapha</s>, the eye...
There are dullness, great swelling, itching, sleepiness, and no delight in food.
The discharge is said to be dense, oily, abundant, white, and like mucus.
In <s>adhimantha</s>, the black circle is depressed and the white circle is raised.
There is watering, distension of the nose, and the eye seems as if filled with dust.
One sees red tears, streaks, discharge, and a red circle.
In <s>raktasyanda</s>, the eye has the signs of <s>pittasyanda</s> as well.
In <s>adhimantha</s>, the eye is coppery at the edges, with pain like being torn out.
Through redness it becomes like a bandhūka flower, burns, and cannot bear touch.
The black part appears as if sunk in blood, like an ominous mark, and like fire.
The <s>adhimanthas</s>, each according to its kind, are all <s>syandas</s> with intensified pain.
They produce very severe pain in the temples, teeth, cheeks, and skull.
The condition born of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> is accompanied by rubbing pain, pricking, splitting, and coating.
The eyelids and eye are rough and harsh, and opening and closing them is difficult.
There is contraction, dryness, desire for cold, pain, and suppuration.

children.text: uktaḥ śuṣkādipāko 'yaṃ saśophaḥ syāt tribhir malaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is called <s>śuṣkākṣipāka</s>; when there is swelling, it is caused by the three impurities.
When these are joined with blood, the swelling there has excessive pain, burning, and oozing and the like.
The white circle becomes like a ripe udumbara fruit.
The tears are repeatedly hot, cold, clear, slimy, transparent, or thick.
When the swelling is slight, it is <s>alpaśopha</s>; the inflammation is otherwise the same in its signs.
In <s>akṣipākātyaya</s> there are swelling, violent inflammation, and turbid tears.
The black and white parts are smeared with <s>kapha</s>, moist, and reddened.
There is burning, obstruction of vision, and pains that do not remain fixed.
The nutritive essence of food, made sour by impurities dominated by <s>pitta</s> and blood,
ascends to the eye through the vessels and makes it dusky red.
It has swelling, burning, suppuration, tears, and very clouded sight.
This is called <s>amloṣita</s>; the sixteen diseases affecting the whole eye have been stated.
Among these, one should give up <s>hatādhimantha</s> together with <s>akṣipākātyaya</s>.
<s>Adhimantha</s> arising from <s>vāta</s> destroys sight in five nights; that born of <s>śleṣman</s>, in a week.

children.text: raktotpanno hanti tadvat trirātrān mithyācārāt paittikaḥ sadya eva ||
children.translated_text: That produced from blood does so in three nights, while the <s>paittika</s> form, because of improper conduct, does so at once.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment for all eye diseases.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
In the preliminary stage of <s>syanda</s>, one should administer sharp gargling and nasal therapy,

children.text: kārayed upavāsaṃ ca kopād anyatra vātajāt ||
children.translated_text: and should prescribe fasting, except when the disorder has arisen from aggravated <s>vāta</s>.
For the calming of burning, coating, redness, tears, and swelling, one should make a <s>biḍālaka</s>,
in every case, with <s>pattra</s>, cardamom, pepper, and red ochre,
with fresh collyrium, licorice, <s>nata</s>, sandalwood, and rock salt.

children.text: saindhavaṃ nāgaraṃ tārkṣyaṃ bhṛṣṭaṃ maṇḍena sarpiṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rock salt, dry ginger, and <s>tārkṣya</s>, roasted in the thin portion of ghee,
or <s>śābaraka</s> roasted in ghee, should be used in a disorder born of <s>vāta</s>.
For <s>pitta</s> and blood, one should use <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>kālīya</s>, and licorice.
For <s>kapha</s>, one should use <s>manohvā</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, and honey; for a disorder of all doṣas, all of them.
One part each of sugar and pepper, four parts of <s>manohvā</s>, and sixteen parts of <s>śābaraka</s>,
powdered and tied in cloth, are an eye-covering when the eye has merely become irritated.
Wild horse gram, well steamed in goat-dung juice, tied in cloth, and husked with the nails,

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ sakṛd avacūrṇanānniśīthe netrāṇāṃ vidhamati sadya eva kopam ||
children.translated_text: has a powder which, by a single dusting at midnight, immediately disperses irritation of the eyes.
With <s>ghoṣā</s>, chebulic myrobalan, blue vitriol, licorice, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>mūtī</s>, made very fine and tied loosely in cloth,
the mass immersed in sour grain gruel kept in a copper vessel conquers the manifold pain in the eye.

children.text: ṣoḍaśabhiḥ salilapalaiḥ palaṃ tathaikaṃ kaṭaṅkaṭeryāḥ siddham
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of <s>kaṭaṅkaṭerī</s>, cooked with sixteen <s>palas</s> of water,
reduced to an eighth part and joined with honey, is a sprinkling for an eye aggravated by all doṣas.
The juice of <s>śigru</s> shoots, applied with honey, quickly conquers

children.text: śīghram eva jayati prayojitaḥ śigrupallavarasaḥ samākṣikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the many kinds of pain in the eyes born of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and their combined derangement.

children.text: taruṇam urubūkapattraṃ mūlaṃ ca vibhidya siddham āje kṣīre
children.translated_text: A tender leaf of <s>urubūka</s> and its root, cut up and cooked in goat's milk,
and a warm cake of roasted flour immediately destroy the pain of <s>vātābhiṣyanda</s>.
As eye drops in a disorder born of <s>māruta</s>, a decoction with the <s>bilva</s> group is beneficial,
warm, together with castor root, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and <s>madhuśigru</s>.
Cooked in water and goat's milk with <s>hrīvera</s>, <s>vakra</s>, <s>śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, and udumbara bark,
it is an excellent eye-drop for pain.
A decoction of madder, turmeric, lac, grapes, <s>ṛddhi</s>, licorice, and blue lotus,
cold and with sugar, is an irrigation that conquers disorders of blood and <s>pitta</s>.
The powder of <s>kaseru</s> and licorice, placed loosely in a fiber cloth,
and put in pure water, is beneficial in <s>syanda</s> born of blood and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Puṇḍra</s>, licorice, turmeric, and <s>mūtī</s>, soaked in breast milk with sugar,
or else in goat's milk, remove burning, pain, redness, and tears.
White <s>lodhra</s> with licorice, roasted in ghee and finely powdered,
kept in cloth and rubbed with breast milk, conquers affliction from <s>pitta</s>, blood, and injury.
In <s>kapha</s>, the juice of dry ginger, <s>triphala</s>, neem, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>
is a warm eye-drop; in a combined disorder, one uses mixed medicines.
One should drink old ghee for <s>pavana</s>, and for <s>pitta</s> ghee combined with sugar.
For <s>kapha</s>, one should drink ghee cooked with the three pungents and sprinkled with barley alkali.
One should draw blood repeatedly; after that, having oleated the patient, one should purge him.
There should be an application to the head and face with the broth of marshland flesh.

children.text: uṣṇena śūle dāhe tu payaḥsarpiryutair himaiḥ
children.translated_text: When there is pain, it should be warm; but when there is burning, cold applications with milk and ghee should be used.
Having considered the treatment of <s>timira</s> too, one should apply the measures as appropriate.

children.text: ayam eva vidhiḥ sarvo manthādiṣvapi śasyate
children.translated_text: This very procedure, in its entirety, is also recommended for <s>mantha</s> and similar disorders.
If <s>mantha</s> is in no way pacified, one should cauterize above the eyebrows.
One should smear silver with dry cow's curd; when it has turned blue,
then, when dry, with whey. This <s>varti</s> (medicated wick) destroys diseases of <s>vātākṣi</s>.
Jasmine buds, conch shell, <s>triphala</s>, licorice, and <s>balā</s>,
ground with rainwater, make a <s>varti</s> that removes disorders of pitta and blood.
Rock salt, <s>triphala</s>, the three pungents, conch-navel, sea-foam,
<s>aileyaka</s>, and <s>sarja</s> resin make a <s>varti</s> that removes kapha eye diseases.
<s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, licorice, and <s>dārvī</s>, eight <s>palas</s> in all, should be cooked

children.text: jaladroṇe rase pūte punaḥ pakve ghane kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: in a <s>droṇa</s> of water; when the filtered decoction is cooked again until thick, one should add

children.text: puṣpāñjanād daśapalaṃ karṣaṃ ca maricāt tataḥ
children.translated_text: ten <s>palas</s> of <s>puṣpāñjana</s> and one <s>karṣa</s> of pepper; then,
made into powder or a <s>varti</s>, it destroys all conditions arising from <s>abhiṣyanda</s>,
redness, pain, and scratching, and immediately makes vision clear.

children.text: ayaṃ pāśupato yogo rahasyaṃ bhiṣajāṃ param ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Pāśupata</s> formula, the supreme secret of physicians.
In dry inflammation of the eye, drinking ghee and nourishing the eyes
with <s>jīvanīya</s> ghee are prescribed, and nasal therapy with <s>aṇu</s> oil.
Here a sprinkling with warm milk containing rock salt is beneficial,
as is collyrium made from <s>mahauṣadha</s>, mixed with ghee and ground in breast milk.
Or one may use fat from marsh-dwelling animals, with a little rock salt and dry ginger.
Hairs smeared with ghee, rubbed on a mirror, and placed in a covered earthen cup,

children.text: dagdhvājyapiṣṭā lohasthā sā maṣī śreṣṭham añjanam
children.translated_text: are to be burnt, ground with ghee, and kept in iron; that soot is the best collyrium.

children.text: saśophe vālpaśophe ca snigdhasya vyadhayet sirām ||
children.translated_text: When there is swelling, or even slight swelling, one should puncture a vein in an oleated patient.
In one already oleated, purgation should again be done with raisin-and-<s>pathyā</s> decoction, <s>trivṛt</s>, and ghee.
White <s>lodhra</s>, fried in ghee, powdered, and placed in cloth,
is rubbed with hot water; as a sprinkling it is supremely pain-relieving.
Or a decoction of <s>dārvī</s> and <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s> is beneficial as eye-drops.

children.text: tāmraṃ lohe mūtraghṛṣṭaṃ prayuktaṃ netre sarpirdhūpitaṃ vedanāghnam
children.translated_text: Copper rubbed on iron with urine, fumigated with ghee and applied to the eye, removes pain.

children.text: tāmre ghṛṣṭo gavyadadhnaḥ saro vā yuktaḥ kṛṣṇāsaindhavābhyāṃ variṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or the cream of cow's curd rubbed on copper, combined with black pepper and rock salt, is best.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ tāmre stanyaghṛṣṭaṃ ghṛtāktaiḥ śamyāḥ pattrair dhūpitaṃ tad yavaiśca
children.translated_text: Conch shell rubbed on copper with breast milk, fumigated with ghee-smeared <s>śamī</s> leaves and with barley,

children.text: netre yuktaṃ hanti saṃdhāvasaṃjñaṃ kṣipraṃ gharṣaṃ vedanāṃ cātitīvrām ||
children.translated_text: when applied to the eye, quickly removes the condition called <s>saṃdhāva</s>, scratching, and extremely severe pain.
<s>udumbara</s> fruit, rubbed on iron with breast milk and fumigated
with ghee-smeared <s>śamī</s> leaves, overcomes burning, pain, redness, tears, and irritation.
The exudate of young <s>śigru</s> shoots, well rubbed in a copper vessel
and fumigated with ghee, destroys swelling, scratching, tears, and pain.
A shard of earthenware with sesame water, rubbed on bronze and well fumigated
with neem leaves smeared with ghee, overcomes scratching, pain, tears, and redness.
When the eye has been anointed for <s>saṃdhāva</s> and the pain from the medicine has passed,

children.text: stanyenāścyotanaṃ kāryaṃ triḥ paraṃ nāñjayecca taiḥ
children.translated_text: breast milk should be used as eye-drops; one should not anoint with those preparations more than three times.
<s>tālīśa</s> leaves, <s>capalā</s>, <s>nata</s>, iron filings, and collyrium,
jasmine buds, green vitriol, and rock salt are ground with urine.

children.text: tāmram ālipya saptāhaṃ dhārayet peṣayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should coat copper with them and keep it for seven days; then one should grind it
again with that same urine, make pills, and dry them in the shade.
Rubbed with breast milk, they destroy scratching, tears, swelling, and itching.
<s>vyāghrī</s> bark, licorice, and copper dust, made into a paste with goat's milk
and fumigated with ghee-smeared <s>śamī</s> and emblic leaves, remove swelling and pain.
In <s>amloṣita</s>, one should employ the treatment prescribed for <s>pittābhiṣyanda</s>.
The aggravated disorders arising from accumulations of kapha, pitta, and blood, <s>kukūṇaka</s>,
obstruction by the eyelashes, dry eye inflammation, <s>pūyālasa</s>, and <s>bisa</s>,
<s>pothakī</s>, <s>amloṣita</s>, the one called minor, and <s>syanda</s> and <s>mantha</s>, except the vātic kind,
these eighteen are called <s>pillā</s> disorders and persist for a long time.

children.text: cikitsā pṛthag eteṣāṃ svaṃsvam uktātha vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Their respective treatments have been stated separately; now the common treatment will be taught.
When they have become <s>pillī</s>, then, in general, for a patient with the disease called <s>pillā</s>,
after he has been oleated, made to vomit, and had blood removed by vein-puncture,

children.text: viriktasya ca vartmānu nirlikhed ā viśuddhitaḥ
children.translated_text: and after he has been purged, one should scrape the eyelids until they are cleansed.
One <s>pala</s> of blue vitriol and twenty white peppercorns,
ground with thirty <s>palas</s> of sour gruel, should be deposited on copper.
It makes <s>pillā</s>s into non-<s>pillā</s>s, even when they have arisen many years before.
By washing with it, one should destroy coating, tears, itching, and swelling.
<s>karañja</s> seed, <s>surasa</s>, and jasmine buds

children.text: saṃkṣudya sādhayet kvāthe pūte tatra rasakriyā
children.translated_text: should be crushed and boiled in a decoction; when it has been filtered, a thick extract is made there.
As collyrium, it is medicine for <s>pillā</s> and promotes the regrowth of eyelashes.
<s>rasāñjana</s>, <s>sarja</s> resin, <s>rīti</s> flower, and realgar,
sea-foam, salt, red ochre, and pepper,
ground with honey, make an excellent collyrium that removes discharge and itching.
Or <s>tagara</s> ground with the juice of <s>abhayā</s> destroys <s>pillā</s>.
So too <s>devadāru</s>, impregnated with goat urine and used with oil.
Rock salt, <s>triphala</s>, black pepper, <s>kaṭukā</s>, and conch-navel,
together with copper dust, make a <s>varti</s> that destroys <s>pillā</s>, corneal opacity, and specks.
Or powder of <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s>, impregnated with the juice of <s>surasa</s>,
kept on copper for ten days, is a collyrium that conquers <s>paillya</s> and loss of eyelashes.

children.text: alaṃ ca sauvīrakam añjanaṃ ca tābhyāṃ samaṃ tāmrarajaḥ susūkṣmam
children.translated_text: Alum, <s>sauvīraka</s> collyrium, and copper dust equal to those two, very finely powdered,
when used on <s>pillā</s>s, that powder produces hairs even with a single applicator.
The best cotton, impregnated seven times with the juice of lac, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>dārvī</s>,

children.text: dīpaḥ prajvālyaḥ sarpiṣā tatsamutthā śreṣṭhā pillānāṃ ropaṇārthe maṣī sā ||
children.translated_text: A lamp should be lit with ghee; the soot produced from it is best for healing <s>pillā</s> lesions.
The patient with <s>pillaroga</s> should resort repeatedly to scraping of the eyelids, and likewise to bloodletting,

children.text: punaḥ punar virekaṃ ca nityam āścyotanāñjanam
children.translated_text: again and again to purgation, and constantly to eye-drops and collyrium,
as well as to nasal medication and medicinal smoking.
But when <s>pūyālasa</s> is not pacified, at the end cauterization should be done with a fine probe.
Thus, with their causes, symptoms, and treatments, the diseases of the eye, ninety-four in number,
have been described completely, each distinct from the others.
And even when healthy, one should always use what is pleasing to the eyes:
old barley, wheat, rice, sixty-day rice, and <s>kodrava</s>,
mung beans and the like, which pacify kapha and pitta, well drenched with abundant ghee,

children.text: śākaṃ caivaṃvidhaṃ māṃsaṃ jāṅgalaṃ dāḍimaṃ sitām
children.translated_text: vegetables of the same kind, meat from animals of dry land, pomegranate, sugar,

children.text: saindhavaṃ triphalāṃ drākṣāṃ vāri pāne ca nābhasam ||
children.translated_text: rock salt, <s>triphala</s>, grapes, and rainwater for drinking.
One should use a parasol, footwear, and proper purification of the doṣas,
and should avoid suppression of urges, indigestion, and eating too much or too soon after a meal,
anger, grief, daytime sleep, night-waking, and exposure to sun,
and whatever food or medicine is burning or causes obstruction here.

children.text: dve pādamadhye pṛthusaṃniveśe sire gate te bahudhā ca netre
children.translated_text: Two broad vessels situated in the middle of the feet go to the eyes, branching there in many ways.
They convey to the eyes the effects of rubbing, massage, unguents, and the like applied to the feet.
When those vessels are impaired by dirt, heat, friction, pressure, and the like, they damage the eyes.
Therefore one should always practice measures beneficial to sight: footwear, oiling, and washing of the feet.
Now, then, we shall explain the diagnosis of diseases of the ear.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Through coryza, playing in water, scratching the ear,
improper use of sound, and other aggravating factors, vāta becomes provoked.
Having reached the vessels of hearing, it produces a forceful pain in the auditory passage,
splitting pain on one side of the head, stiffness, and dislike of cold.

children.text: cirācca pākaṃ pakvaṃ tu lasīkām alpaśaḥ sravet
children.translated_text: After a long time it suppurates; when mature, it discharges a little serum,
and the ear may suddenly feel empty, with a sensation as though things are moving about.
From pitta there is pain with burning and heat, desire for cold, swelling, and fever;
there is quick suppuration, and when it has fully ripened, a discharge of yellow serum.

children.text: sā lasīkā spṛśed yad yat tat tat pākam upaiti ca
children.translated_text: Whatever that serum touches, that part too comes to suppuration.
From kapha there is heaviness of the head, jaw, and neck, and the pain is dull;
there is itching, swelling, desire for heat, and, after suppuration, a white and thick discharge.
Blood, vitiated by injury and the like in the ear, produces ear pain
with distress like that caused by pitta, though with some additional symptoms.
Pain caused by all the doṣas together arises with swelling, fever, and intense pain,
with alternating desire for heat and cold, and with dullness of hearing.
When suppurated, it flows with thick pus that is white, black, and red.
When vāta is lodged in the sound-carrying vessels, one repeatedly hears

children.text: nādān akasmād vividhān karṇanādaṃ vadanti tam ||
children.translated_text: various sounds suddenly; this is called <s>karṇanāda</s>, ringing in the ear.
Vāyu accompanied by śleṣman, or ringing that has been neglected,

children.text: uccaiḥ kṛcchrācchrutiṃ kuryād badhiratvaṃ krameṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: makes hearing difficult, so that one hears only loud sounds with effort, and gradually causes deafness.

children.text: vātena śoṣitaḥ śleṣmā śroto limpet tato bhavet
children.translated_text: When śleṣman has been dried by vāta, it adheres to the auditory passage; then there is
pain, heaviness, and obstruction, and this is called <s>pratīnāha</s>.
Itching and swelling in the ear, arising from kapha and remaining fixed, are remembered by those respective names.

children.text: kapho vidagdhaḥ pittena sarujaṃ nīrujaṃ tvapi ||
children.translated_text: Kapha corrupted by pitta produces <s>pūtikarṇaka</s>, which may be painful or painless,
with thick, foul-smelling, abundant moisture.
In an ear vitiated by vāta and the other doṣas, creatures born of flesh, blood, and moisture,
as they eat, cause intense pain; this is <s>kṛmikarṇaka</s>, worm disease of the ear.
In a wound produced by scratching the ear, there may be an abscess with the previously stated symptoms;
another swelling is described in the same way; <s>arśas</s> and <s>arbuda</s> are also taught.

children.text: teṣu ruk pūtikarṇatvaṃ badhiratvaṃ ca bādhate ||
children.translated_text: Among these, pain, foulness of the ear, and deafness cause distress.
When, through vāta in the womb, the auricle is contracted, it is <s>kucikarṇaka</s>.

children.text: eko nīrug aneko vā garbhe māṃsāṅkuraḥ sthiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A stable, painless sprout of flesh, whether single or multiple, in the cavity of the ear,
is <s>pippalī</s> when it is the size of a long pepper; from the combined doṣas comes <s>vidārikā</s>.

children.text: savarṇaḥ sarujaḥ stabdhaḥ śvayathuḥ sa upekṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is a swelling of the same color as the surrounding tissue, painful, and rigid; when neglected,
after ripening it discharges something like pungent oil and heals with difficulty.

children.text: saṃkocayati rūḍhā ca sā dhruvaṃ karṇaśaṣkulīm ||
children.translated_text: And when healed, it certainly contracts the auricle of the ear.
Vāyu situated in the vessels causes wasting of the ear-lobe, known by that name.

children.text: kṛśā dṛḍhā ca tantrīvat pālī vātena tantrikā ||
