children.translated_text: A lobe made thin, firm, and string-like by vāta is <s>tantrikā</s>.
In a delicate ear that has been stretched for a long time and has suddenly enlarged,

children.text: karṇe śophaḥ saruk pālyām aruṇaḥ paripoṭavān ||
children.translated_text: there is a painful, reddish swelling in the lobe, marked by fissuring.
That is <s>paripoṭa</s>, arising from vāta; <s>utpāta</s> arises from pitta and blood.
From the weight of heavy ornaments and the like, there is a dark swelling with pain, burning, and suppuration,
accompanied by blisters, pimples, redness, heat, and moisture.
A swelling in the lobe from vāta and kapha, all around, painless, and fixed,

children.text: stabdhaḥ savarṇaḥ kaṇḍūmān unmantho galliraśca saḥ
children.translated_text: stiff, of the same color, and itchy, is <s>unmantha</s>, also called <s>gallira</s>.
In an ear that has been badly pierced and stretched, there is swelling with itching, burning, suppuration, and pain,
arising from the combined doṣas; by name it is <s>duḥkhavardhana</s>.
From kapha, blood, and worms arise minute pimples, with itching, moisture, and pain;

children.text: lihyuḥ pālīm upekṣitāḥ lehyākhyāḥ piṭikāstā hi
children.translated_text: when neglected they lick away the lobe, and those pimples are called <s>lehyā</s>.
<s>Pippalī</s>, pain arising from all the doṣas, <s>vidārī</s>, and <s>kucikarṇaka</s>
are incurable among these; <s>tantrikā</s> alone is manageable, while the others should be treated.
Thus twenty-five diseases of the ear have been stated according to their divisions.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of the ear.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
In earache born of vāta, at night, after eating meat broth, one should drink

children.text: vātaghnasādhitaṃ sarpiḥ karṇaṃ svinnaṃ ca pūrayet ||
children.translated_text: ghee prepared with vāta-pacifying drugs, and should fill the ear after it has been fomented.
Of the leaves produced separately from <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>bilva</s>, <s>arka</s>, and castor,
smeared with oil and rock salt and steamed by the <s>puṭapāka</s> method,
the lukewarm juices should be used in the same way; also those of radish and <s>aralu</s>.
<s>Mahāsneha</s>, cooked with the vāta-pacifying group, sour substances, and urines,

children.text: mahāsneho drutaṃ hanti sutīvrām api vedanām
children.translated_text: quickly destroys even very severe pain.
From a stick of the great <s>pañcamūla</s>, wrapped in linen,
soaked in oil, and lit at the tip, the fat that comes off at once removes pain.
It should be applied in this same way from <s>bhadrakāṣṭha</s>, from <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and from <s>sārala</s> wood.
The treatment prescribed for vāta disease and coryza is also beneficial here.
One should avoid bathing the head and drinking cold water, even by day.
In pitta earache, one should purge a patient who has been made unctuous with ghee mixed with sugar.
Breast milk decocted with grapes and licorice is recommended for filling the ear.
With licorice, <s>anantā</s>, sandalwood, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
and also with lotus stalk, lotus fiber, madder, and <s>śārivā</s>, one should prepare
one <s>kuḍava</s> of oil, combined with a <s>prastha</s> of licorice juice
and two <s>prasthas</s> of milk; used as nasal medication, ear-filling, and massage, this

children.text: nihanti śūladāhoṣāḥ kevalaṃ kṣaudram eva vā
children.translated_text: destroys pain, burning, and heat; or honey alone may be used.
The ears should also be anointed all around with licorice and the other drugs mixed with ghee.
In an earache arising from kapha, one should make the patient vomit after he has been made unctuous with ghee cooked with long pepper.
One should apply smoking, nasal medication, gargles, and fomentations that remove kapha.
The fresh juices of garlic, ginger, <s>śigru</s>, <s>muraṅgī</s>, radish,
and plantain are best, used slightly warm, for filling the ear.
Shoots of <s>arka</s>, ground with sour liquid, smeared with oil, and mixed with salt,
should be placed in a hollowed stem of <s>snuhī</s> and covered with its leaves.

children.text: svedayet puṭapākena sa rasaḥ śūlajit param
children.translated_text: One should heat it by the <s>puṭapāka</s> method; that juice is supreme for conquering pain.
One should fill the ear with the juice of <s>bījapūra</s> or of wood-apple.
Or, after filling it with fermented sour liquid, one should sprinkle it over with its froth.
Oil cooked with goat or sheep urine and bamboo bark is also an ear-filling.
Or mustard oil cooked with asafoetida, <s>tumburu</s>, and dry ginger may be used.

children.text: raktaje pittavat kāryaṃ sirāṃ cāśu vimokṣayet ||
children.translated_text: In the blood-born type, treatment should be as in the pitta type, and a vein should be opened quickly.
When the ear is mature and discharging pus, one should employ smoking, gargling, and nasal medication,

children.text: yuñjyān nāḍīvidhānaṃ ca duṣṭavraṇaharaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: as well as the procedure for sinus tracts and whatever removes foul ulcers.

children.text: srotaḥ pramṛjya digdhaṃ tu dvau kālau picuvartibhiḥ
children.translated_text: After cleansing the channel, twice daily one should use cotton wicks that have been smeared,
and, after fumigating with <s>pūra</s>, should fill it completely with honey.
One should apply a cotton wick smeared with molasses and the decoction of the <s>surasādi</s> group,
and sprinkle it over with very fine powders of those same drugs.
This is the procedure that removes pain, moisture, and heaviness.
With <s>priyaṅgu</s>, licorice, <s>ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, blue lotus, and <s>parṇī</s>,
with madder, <s>lodhra</s>, lac, and the juice of wood-apple,

children.text: pacet tailaṃ tad āsrāvaṃ nigṛhṇātyāśu pūraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: one should cook oil; when used for filling, it quickly restrains that discharge.
For tinnitus and deafness, one should use the medicine stated for vāta earache.
When kapha is associated with them, one should first conquer the kapha by emesis and the like.
In four times the juice of the leaves of castor, <s>śigru</s>, <s>varuṇa</s>, and radish,
and in eight times as much milk, one should cook oil.
Combined with a paste of licorice and <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, it destroys
tinnitus, deafness, and pain, through nasal medication, massage, and ear-filling.
Oil cooked with <s>prativiṣā</s>, asafoetida, <s>miśi</s>, cinnamon bark, <s>svarjikā</s>, pungent drugs,
and sour ferment, when used for filling, removes pain, discharge, deafness, and tinnitus.

children.text: karṇanāde hitaṃ tailaṃ sarṣapotthaṃ ca pūraṇe
children.translated_text: Oil from mustard seed is beneficial in tinnitus when used for filling the ear.
The alkali of dried radish pieces, asafoetida, dry ginger,
<s>śatapuṣpā</s>, sweet flag, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s>,
black salt, barley alkali, <s>svarjikā</s>, <s>audbhida</s>, and rock salt,
birch-knot, <s>viḍa</s> salt, <s>mustā</s>, and honeyed sour ferment in fourfold quantity,
as well as citron juice in the same measure and fresh plantain juice, with these

children.text: pakvaṃ tailaṃ jayatyāśu sukṛcchrān api pūraṇāt
children.translated_text: oil cooked and used for filling quickly conquers even very difficult cases:
itching, moisture, deafness, foul ear, pain, and worms.
This alkaline oil is also best in diseases of the mouth and teeth.

children.text: atha suptāviva syātāṃ karṇau raktaṃ haret tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, if the two ears seem as though numb, one should then draw blood.
When there is swelling and moisture with dull hearing, one should perform emesis.
One should avoid treating deafness that occurs in a child or an old person, and that which is chronic.
In obstruction, after moistening with unctuousness and fomentation, one should cleanse it.
Then, after using an ear-cleaning instrument, one should fill the ear with oil.
It may be oil with sour ferment, rock salt, and honey, or with citron juice.
If dryness arises from cleansing, filling with the scum of ghee is prescribed.
This same sequence applies also when the ear is full of wax; in itching, it should remove kapha.
Nasal medication and the rest are the same in swelling too; here a paste with pungent and hot substances is used.
In foul ear and worm ear, one should perform the treatment described for ear discharge.
Filling with pungent oil is especially indicated in worm ear.
In ear abscess, after preliminary emesis, the treatment for abscess is beneficial.
In traumatic abscess, the treatment stated for pitta-born earache should be done.
In hemorrhoid-like growths and tumors, treatment is as for the nose; an unripe ear-splitting lesion
should be treated like an ear abscess and according to the arising doṣa.
In wasting of the ear lobe, nasal medication and external paste are as in vāta ear pain.

children.text: svedaṃ ca kuryāt svinnāṃ ca pālīm udvartayet tilaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should also foment it, and when the lobe has been fomented, rub it with sesame.
with <s>priyāla</s> seed, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>hayagandhā</s>, and barley;
then one should regularly perform massage with nourishing fats.
Oil cooked together with milk, with <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vājigandhā</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, castor, and <s>jīvaka</s>,

children.text: tailaṃ vipakvaṃ sakṣīraṃ pālīnāṃ puṣṭikṛt param ||
children.translated_text: is supreme for producing nourishment of the ear lobes.
Oil cooked in milk with a paste of the <s>jīvanīya</s> (life-promoting) drugs
and in a decoction of marshland meat nourishes and enlarges the ear lobes.
Having cut away an ear lobe that is excessively wasted and joined what remains, one should nourish it.
Even the condition called <s>tantrikā</s> is manageable in this way; in <s>paripoṭa</s> too this is the procedure.
In <s>utpāta</s>, after blood has been removed by leeches, a cooling paste should be applied
with tender shoots of rose-apple and mango, <s>balā</s>, licorice, <s>lodhra</s>, sesame, and blue lotus;
with sour gruel, madder, <s>kadamba</s>, and <s>śārivā</s> included,
oil cooked for massage is used, as well as the ghees prescribed for <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas).
In <s>unmantha</s>, the oil for massage should contain the fat of monitor lizard and crab.
With <s>tālapatrī</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>vākucī</s> fruit, and rock salt,

children.text: surasālāṅgalībhyāṃ ca siddhaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca nāvanam
children.translated_text: and with <s>surasā</s> and <s>lāṅgalī</s>, a cooked preparation is used as a sharp nasal medication.
In a badly pierced ear lobe, after it has been sprinkled with a decoction of leaves of <s>aśmantaka</s>, rose-apple, and mango,
and the lobe has been well anointed with oil, one should dust it with very fine powders
made from licorice, madder, <s>prapuṇḍrāhva</s>, and turmeric.
Oil cooked with lac and <s>viḍaṅga</s> is also beneficial for massage.
After fomenting <s>parilehikā</s> repeatedly with balls made from cow dung,
one should smear it with the essence of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, ground with sheep urine,
and with barks of <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>iṅguda</s>, and <s>kārañja</s> seed and <s>śamyāka</s>.
Or one may use those same substances for massage, or cook a pungent oil
with neem leaves, pepper, and <s>madana</s> for a <s>lehikā</s> wound.

children.text: chinnaṃ tu karṇaṃ śuddhasya bandham ālocya yaugikam
children.translated_text: But for a cut ear, after the patient has been purified, one should consider the appropriate bandage.
If the blood is clean, one should attach it; once attached, cleansing is done for a fresh cut.
Then, after arranging the edge up to the hairline and performing trimming and scraping,

children.text: niveśya saṃdhiṃ suṣamaṃ na nimnaṃ na samunnatam ||
children.translated_text: one should set the junction evenly, neither depressed nor raised.
After anointing it with honey and ghee, and covering it with cotton and cloth,
one should bind it with a thread, neither tight nor loose, and dust it with powders.
Then one should prescribe blood-stanching and wound-healing measures and the proper regimen.
After seven days one should gently remove the cotton, which has been smeared with raw oil.
When it is well healed, when hair has grown, and when the junction is adherent, even, and firm,

children.text: suvarṣmāṇam arogaṃ ca śanaiḥ karṇaṃ vivardhayet ||
children.translated_text: well shaped and healthy, one should gradually enlarge the ear.
<s>Jalaśūka</s>, <s>svayaṅguptā</s>, the two turmerics, fruit of <s>bṛhatī</s>,
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>hastipippalī</s>, and white mustard;
roots of <s>kośātakā</s>, <s>aśvaghna</s>, <s>rūpikā</s>, and <s>saptaparṇa</s>;
<s>chucchundarī</s>, <s>kālamṛtā</s>, and a house made by bees;
<s>jatūkā</s>, an aquatic product, and also <s>śabarakandaka</s>:

children.text: ebhiḥ kalkaiḥ kharaṃ pakvaṃ satailaṃ māhiṣaṃ ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: with pastes of these, buffalo ghee cooked strongly together with oil
and with elephant and horse urine is supreme for enlarging the ear by massage.

children.text: atha kuryād vayaḥsthasya chinnāṃ śuddhasya nāsikām ||
children.translated_text: Next, after purification, one should operate on the cut nose of a person of mature age.

children.text: chindyān nāsāsamaṃ pattraṃ tattulyaṃ ca kapolataḥ
children.translated_text: One should cut a leaf equal to the nose, and then from the cheek cut skin and flesh equal to that.
Keeping it near the nose and preserving its connection, one should make it thin.

children.text: sīvyed gaṇḍaṃ tataḥ sūcyā sevinyā picuyuktayā
children.translated_text: Then one should suture the cheek with a needle, using a seam and cotton.
Next, when the cut of the nose has been incised, one should turn the skin upward.

children.text: kapolavadhraṃ saṃdadhyāt sīvyen nāsāṃ ca yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: One should join the cheek-flap and carefully suture the nose.
Inside, one should raise it with two tubes, so that comfortable breathing may take place.
After sprinkling it with raw oil, one should dust it with very fine powders of <s>pattaṅga</s>, licorice, collyrium,
and other blood-stanching substances.
Then, after anointing it with honey and ghee and binding it, one should prescribe the regimen.
Thereafter, knowing each change of condition, one should perform the procedure for a fresh wound.

children.text: chindyād rūḍhe 'dhikaṃ māṃsaṃ nāsopāntācca carma tat
children.translated_text: When it has healed, one should cut away excess flesh, and that skin from the edge of the nose.

children.text: sīvyet tataśca suślakṣṇaṃ hīnaṃ saṃvardhayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should suture it and make it very smooth; if it is deficient, one should enlarge it again.
When it has been set in its proper position, this same method applies even to a freshly severed nose.
For a lip, apart from the use of tubes, the procedure is like that for joining the nose.
Now then, we shall explain the diagnosis of diseases of the nose.
So indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
Through dew, wind, dust, excessive speech, excessive sleep and wakefulness,
through a pillow that is too low or too high, through water that has been drunk improperly or otherwise,
through excessive drinking of water, intercourse, vomiting, suppression of tears, and the like,

children.text: kruddhā vātolbaṇā doṣā nāsāyāṃ styānatāṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the aggravated <s>doṣas</s> (pathogenic factors), dominated by <s>vāta</s>, become thickened in the nose.
They produce <s>pratiśyāya</s> (nasal catarrh), increasing and causing wasting.

children.text: tatra vātāt pratiśyāye mukhaśoṣo bhṛśaṃ kṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, in <s>pratiśyāya</s> from <s>vāta</s>, there is dryness of the mouth and violent sneezing,
obstruction of smell, pricking pains in the teeth, temples, and head,

children.text: kīṭikā iva sarpantīr manyate parito bhruvau ||
children.translated_text: and one thinks that insects are crawling all around the eyebrows.
There is weakness of voice, slow maturation, and a cold, clear flow of phlegm.
From <s>pitta</s> there are thirst, fever, formation of pimples in the nose, and dizziness.
There is suppuration at the tip of the nose and a rough, hot, coppery-yellow flow of phlegm.
From <s>kapha</s> there are cough, loss of appetite, difficult breathing, vomiting, and heaviness of the limbs.
There is sweetness in the mouth, itching, and an unctuous white flow of phlegm.
The type arising from all <s>doṣas</s> has all the symptoms, and it suddenly increases and subsides.
Blood, having reached the corrupted vessels of the nose, produces a bloody <s>pratiśyāya</s>.
There is numbness of the chest, copperiness of the eyes, and foulness of the breath.
There is itching in the ears, eyes, and nose, and here the symptoms stated for <s>pitta</s> also occur.
All coryzas, when neglected, become corrupted and severe.
Because the complications described above become excessive, it torments all the senses,
and is accompanied by depression of digestive fire, fever, dyspnea, cough, and pain in the chest and flanks.
It flares up suddenly and repeatedly, producing foul odor of the mouth and swelling,
and repeatedly causing dampness, drying, and obstruction of clearance in the nose.
There is a flow of phlegm like pus, dark or red, and clotted,
and worms arise there, long, unctuous, white, and minute.
In these, the signs of maturation are lightness of the limbs and cessation of sneezing,
sticky yellow mucus, and loss of perception of taste and smell.
Through the use of sharp-smelling substances, sun-rays, thread, grass, and the like,
or by other things that aggravate <s>vāta</s>, when the tender bone of the nose
is irritated, <s>vāta</s>, enraged and obstructed, goes to the <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>;
then, turned back, it causes extremely forceful sneezing. This is <s>bhṛśakṣava</s>.
By drying the nasal channels and the <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>
then makes the nose seem full of awns, so that breathing is difficult.
This is known as <s>nāsikāśoṣa</s>. But in <s>nāsānāha</s> there arises
a condition as though the nose were stopped up, because <s>vāta</s> is obstructed by phlegm.
Because inhalation and exhalation are blocked, the two channels seem closed.
In the nostril, <s>pitta</s> cooks the skin and flesh, with burning and pain.
That is <s>ghrāṇapāka</s>; but the discharge bearing that name arises from phlegm,
clear, like water, continuous, and especially occurring at night.
In the nose, increased <s>kapha</s>, obstructing the channels, causes <s>apīnasa</s>,
with rumbling breathing and more severe pain than in <s>pīnasa</s>.
His nose flows as if like that of a sheep, and by it the nose is kept wet;

children.text: ajasraṃ picchilaṃ pītaṃ pakvaṃ siṅghāṇakaṃ ghanam ||
children.translated_text: the mature nasal mucus is constant, slimy, yellow, and dense.
When affected by blood, the nose seems burned and cannot bear touch outside or inside;
the breath is like smoke. That condition is <s>dīpti</s>, and it seems to burn.
At the root of the palate, because of corrupted impurities, <s>māruta</s> from the mouth and nose

children.text: śleṣmā ca pūtir nirgacchet pūtināsaṃ vadanti tam ||
children.translated_text: and foul phlegm come out; they call that <s>pūtināsa</s>.

children.text: nicayād abhighātād vā pūyāsṛṅ nāsikā sravet
children.translated_text: From accumulation or from trauma, pus and blood may flow from the nose;
that is called <s>pūyarakta</s>, causing burning and pain in the head.
<s>Marut</s>, obstructed inside the nose by <s>pitta</s> and phlegm, dries

children.text: kaphaṃ sa śuṣkaḥ puṭatāṃ prāpnoti puṭakaṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: the phlegm; when dry it becomes crusted, and that is <s>puṭaka</s>.
Hemorrhoid-like growths and tumors should be distinguished by the signs of the <s>doṣas</s>, each as appropriate.
In all of them there is difficult breathing, <s>pīnasa</s>, and constant sneezing,
nasal speech, foul nasal odor, and headache.
Among these eighteen disorders, chronic corrupted <s>pīnasa</s> should be managed palliatively.
Now then, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of the nose.
Thus, indeed, said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
In all forms of <s>pīnasa</s>, at the beginning one should stay in a room sheltered from wind and should undertake
oleation, fomentation, emesis, smoking, and the holding of mouth-rinses.
Clothing should be heavy and warm, and the head should be wrapped densely and thickly.
The food should be light, sour, salty, unctuous, hot, and not liquid.
It should be rich in desert-animal meat, jaggery, milk, chickpeas, and the three pungents,
chiefly barley and wheat, and accompanied by curds, pomegranate, and <s>sārika</s>.
Soup made from young radish and soup made from horse gram are praised.

children.text: kavoṣṇaṃ daśamūlāmbu jīrṇāṃ vā vāruṇīṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: One should drink lukewarm <s>daśamūla</s> water, or old <s>vāruṇī</s> liquor.
One should inhale <s>coraka</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, sweet flag, <s>ajājī</s>, and <s>upakuñcikā</s>,
the three pungents, <s>tālīśa</s>, <s>cavikā</s>, tamarind, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
with <s>agni</s> and <s>ajājī</s>, two <s>palas</s> each, and cinnamon, cardamom, and bay leaf in quarter-measures,
made into pills with half a <s>tulā</s> of old jaggery after it has been cooked.
It destroys <s>pīnasa</s>, dyspnea, and cough, and is excellent for producing appetite and voice.
With dill, cinnamon bark, <s>balā</s> root, and the roots of <s>śyoṇāka</s>, castor, and <s>bilva</s>,
one should inhale smoke made with <s>sāragvadha</s>, fat, ghee, and <s>madana</s>.
Or else, having made roasted flour with ghee and placed it within a covered earthen cup,

children.text: tyajet snānaṃ śucaṃ krodhaṃ bhṛśaṃ śayyāṃ himaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: one should avoid bathing, grief, anger, excessive lying in bed, cold, and water.
In <s>vāta-pratiśyāya</s>, one should drink ghee prepared with <s>vāta</s>-alleviating drugs,
or prepared with the <s>paṭu-pañcaka</s>, or with the <s>vidāryādi</s> group.
One should perform treatment beginning with fomentation and nasal medication as taught for facial paralysis.
In the types arising from <s>pitta</s> and blood, ghee cooked with sweet drugs should be drunk;
cool sprinklings and cool applications should be made with cooling substances.
With <s>dhava</s> bark, <s>triphala</s>, <s>śyāmā</s>, <s>śrīparṇī</s>, licorice, and <s>tilvaka</s>,

children.text: kṣīre daśaguṇe tailaṃ nāvanaṃ saniśaiḥ pacet ||
children.translated_text: oil should be cooked in ten times as much milk, with the two <s>niśās</s>, as a nasal medication.
In the kapha-born type, lightening therapy is used; a paste for the head is made with white mustard seeds.

children.text: sakṣāraṃ vā ghṛtam pītvā vamet piṣṭaistu nāvanam ||
children.translated_text: Or, after drinking ghee with alkali, one should vomit; nasal medication should be made with pastes
ground in goat's urine, with salt, the three pungents, <s>vella</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, and cumin.

children.text: kaṭutīkṣṇair ghṛtair nasyaiḥ kavaḍaiḥ sarvajaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: One should conquer the type caused by all <s>doṣas</s> with pungent and sharp ghees, nasal medicines, and mouthful gargles.
Managing corrupted <s>pīnasa</s>, one should follow the procedure for consumption and for worms.
The three pungents, <s>urubūka</s>, <s>kṛmijit</s>, <s>dāru</s>, <s>mādrīgada</s>, and <s>iṅguda</s>,
eggplant seed, <s>trivṛt</s>, white mustard, and foul-smelling fish,
the flowers of <s>agnimantha</s>, and the fruits of <s>pīlu</s> and <s>śigru</s>,
together with the juice of horse dung and horse urine, and also with elephant urine,

children.text: kṣaumagarbhāṃ kṛtāṃ vartiṃ dhūmaṃ ghrāṇāsyataḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: should be made into a wick with a linen core; one should inhale the smoke through the nose and mouth.

children.text: kṣavathau puṭakākhye ca tīkṣṇaiḥ pradhamanaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: In sneezing and in the disorder called <s>puṭaka</s>, sharp insufflation is beneficial.
Oil or ghee cooked with dry ginger, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>vella</s>, and grape, as paste and decoction,

children.text: sādhitaṃ tailam ājyaṃ vā nasyaṃ kṣavapuṭapraṇut
children.translated_text: used as nasal medication, removes sneezing and <s>puṭaka</s>.
In dryness of the nose, <s>balā</s> oil is used for drinking and the like, and food should be taken with meat broths.
Unctuous smoking and likewise fomentation are used; this is the procedure also in obstruction of the nose.

children.text: pāke dīptau ca pittaghnaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ nasyādi saṃsrutau ||
children.translated_text: In suppuration and burning one should use pitta-alleviating treatment, and in discharge, sharp nasal medication and the like.
For foul-nose and <s>pīnasa</s>, the treatment is as in kapha-type <s>pīnasa</s>.
With lac, <s>karañja</s>, black pepper, <s>vella</s>, asafoetida, long pepper, and molasses,
liquefied with sheep urine, one should administer nasal medication after emesis has been performed.
With the seeds of <s>śigru</s>, <s>siṃhī</s>, and <s>nikumbha</s>, along with the three pungents and rock salt,
and with <s>vella</s> and <s>surasa</s>, oil for nasal instillation is supremely beneficial.
When pus and blood are fresh, one should follow the procedure for blood-type <s>pīnasa</s>.
When it is greatly developed, one should treat it like a sinus; so too in cauterized hemorrhoid-like growths and tumors.
With <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, rock salt, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>āla</s>, long pepper, and <s>agni</s>,
made into a paste and smeared with ghee and honey, one should insert a wick into the nose.
Here one should also use the nasal instillation beginning with <s>śigru</s>, taught for foul-nose.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of diseases of the mouth.
So indeed said the great seers headed by <s>Ātreya</s>.
Fish, buffalo and boar meat, raw radish,
soup of black gram, curd, milk, sour ferment, sugarcane juice, and treacle,
lying face downward, aversion to tooth-cleaning,
and to smoking, emesis, gargling, and proper venesection:

children.text: kruddhāḥ śleṣmolbaṇā doṣāḥ kurvantyantar mukhaṃ gadān
children.translated_text: when the <s>doṣas</s>, predominated by kapha, are aggravated, they cause diseases inside the mouth.

children.text: tatra khaṇḍauṣṭha ityukto vātenauṣṭho dvidhā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them, split lip is so called when a lip is divided in two by vāta.
In inflammation of the lips from vāta, the two lips are stiff and very painful;
they split, crack apart, and become rough, dark, and hard.
From pitta they cannot bear sharp substances, are yellow, and are covered with mustard-seed-like pustules;
they are very moist and suppurate quickly. From kapha, however,
they cannot bear cold, are heavy and swollen, and are covered with pustules of their own color.
From the combined <s>doṣas</s> they have many appearances, foul smell, discharge, and sliminess.
Suddenly they become faded, swollen, and painful, and suppurate irregularly.
When affected by blood, they bleed and have the appearance of blood.
Here, when the blood is depleted, a tumor like a date fruit may arise.
From flesh, they resemble lumps of flesh and in due order become numb and worm-infested.
From fat, they have oily-looking swelling and moisture, itch, and are soft.
Trauma-born lips split open and burst repeatedly.

children.text: grathitau ca punaḥ syātāṃ kaṇḍūlau daśanacchadau
children.translated_text: Again the coverings of the teeth may become knotted and itchy.
From vāta and kapha in the lip, a watery tumor arises like a water bubble.
<s>Gaṇḍālajī</s> is a fixed swelling in the cheek, accompanied by burning and fever.
From vāta, the teeth tolerate warmth but are more painful when touched by cold.

children.text: dālyanta iva śūlena śītākhyo dālanaśca saḥ
children.translated_text: They seem to be split by colic-like pain; that is called <s>śīta</s>, and also <s>dālana</s>.
In tooth sensitivity, the teeth cannot bear wind, sour things, cold, or food.
They become painful and seem loose, as if from eating sour food.
In tooth-splitting, the teeth are accompanied by pricking, splitting pain, and cracking.
<s>Cāla</s> is looseness, with teeth that move and become more painful during chewing.
<s>Karāla</s> is the eruption of irregular teeth among teeth that are misshapen.
An extra tooth is called <s>adhidanta</s>; it is also indeed called <s>vardhana</s>.

children.text: jāyamāne 'tirug dante jāte tatra tu śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: While the tooth is emerging there is excessive pain, but once it has emerged, the pain subsides.

children.text: adhāvanān malo dante kapho vā vātaśoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: From not cleaning the teeth, dirt on a tooth, or kapha dried by vāta,
becomes foul-smelling and hardened; if that tartar is neglected,
<s>kapālikā</s> makes small plates fall away from the tooth little by little.
<s>Śyāva</s> is a tooth that has become dusky through blood, pitta, and vāta.
When the <s>doṣas</s>, with vāta predominant, have occupied the whole tooth down to its root,
and the marrow is dried in a hollow tooth that is filled with food residue,

children.text: pūtitvāt kṛmayaḥ sūkṣmā jāyante jāyate tataḥ
children.translated_text: because of putridity tiny worms arise; from that there occurs
severe pain without apparent cause, subsiding without cause, with inflammation; the tooth is dark and loose,
broken off, and discharges pus and blood. That is called <s>kṛmidantaka</s>.
By kapha and blood, the gums become foul and carry blood without apparent cause.
The tooth-flesh crumbles, and is soft, moist, and dark.
This is <s>śītāda</s>; <s>upakuśa</s> is a suppuration arising from pitta and blood.
The gums burn, are red, and therefore become raised.
They itch, discharge blood, and swell when blood is retained.

children.text: calā mandarujo dantāḥ pūti vaktraṃ ca jāyate
children.translated_text: The teeth are loose and mildly painful, and the mouth becomes foul.
A swelling on two or three teeth, hard like a jujube stone,
arises from kapha and blood; with severe pain it quickly suppurates. This is <s>dantapuppuṭa</s>.

children.text: dantamāṃse malaiḥ sāsrair bāhyāntaḥ śvayathur guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the gum, from impurities together with blood, a heavy swelling occurs externally and internally.
Painful and burning, when it breaks it discharges pus and blood; this is a dental abscess.
A painful swelling at the roots of the teeth is born of pitta and blood.
It discharges saliva, is hollow, and causes decay of the gums.
When it arises from the combined <s>doṣas</s>, it has fever and a discharge of pus and blood.
It is called <s>mahāsuṣira</s>, destroying the attachments of the teeth.
At the end of a tooth, a peg-like swelling causes pain in the jaw and ear.
Caused by kapha, it obstructs eating; that is <s>adhimāṃsaka</s>.
When the gums have been abraded, a great inflammation arises;
when the teeth move in it, that trauma-born condition is <s>vidarbha</s>.
For one who neglects diseases situated in the gums, even though they are curable,
the <s>doṣa</s>, suppurating inside, produces a subtle passage.
That passage repeatedly discharges pus and splits skin, flesh, and bone.

children.text: tāḥ punaḥ pañca vijñeyā lakṣaṇaiḥ svair yathoditaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those are again to be understood as five, according to their own symptoms as stated.
The tongue vitiated by vāta is like a rough vegetable leaf, numb, and cracked.
From pitta, the tongue has burning and heat and is covered with red fleshy sprouts.
But when due to <s>kapha</s>, it is thick, heavy, and like the thorns of the silk-cotton tree.
From <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> there is a swelling below, raised up and causing stiffness of the tongue.
When it has matured, it smells like fish; that is <s>alasa</s>, which destroys the flesh.
At the binding of the tongue below, there is a swelling resembling the tip of the tongue.
It has sprouts, is caused by <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood, and has salivation, burning, stiffness, and roughness.
This is <s>adhijihva</s>, painful and itchy, obstructing speech and eating.
The <s>upajihvā</s> is just like it, but is situated above the tongue.
When the flesh of the palate is vitiated by <s>vāta</s>, painful rough pustules arise.
They are many, firm, and accompanied by discharge; these are known as <s>tālupiṭikā</s>.
At the root of the palate, from <s>kapha</s> together with blood, there is a soft swelling like a fish bladder,
hanging down, slimy, and driving food toward the nose.
It causes obstruction of the throat, thirst, cough, and vomiting, and is <s>galaśuṇḍikā</s>.
In the middle of the palate, compact painless flesh is <s>tālusaṃhati</s>.
In the middle of the palate, a blood-born tumor-swelling shaped like a lotus is an <s>arbuda</s>.
The <s>kacchapa</s> is tortoise-shaped, slowly enlarging, caused by <s>kapha</s>, and painless.
The <s>puppuṭa</s>, produced by phlegm and fat, is like a jujube, painless, and stable.
From <s>pitta</s> comes suppuration, called <s>pāka</s>, discharging pus and very painful.
Drying of the palate, caused by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, fever, and exertion, bears that very name, <s>tāluśoṣa</s>.
Flesh-sprouts born from the binding of the tongue arise in the throat, dreadful and obstructing the passage.
They grow quickly; this rapidly acting disorder is <s>rohiṇī</s>.
When due to <s>vāta</s>, it causes dryness of the throat and mouth and pain in the jaw and ear.
When due to <s>pitta</s>, it is accompanied by fever, heat, thirst, faintness, and a smoky sensation in the throat.
It arises quickly, suppurates quickly, is very red, and cannot bear touch.
When due to <s>kapha</s>, it is slimy and pale; when due to blood, it is covered with blisters.
It resembles burning charcoal and causes ear pain, having the form of the <s>pitta</s>-born type.
When caused by the combined doṣas, it has deep suppuration and is furnished with all the symptoms.
From doṣas in which <s>kapha</s> predominates, there is a swelling like a jujube, knotted and raised.
In the throat it is like an awn or thorn, and <s>śālūka</s> obstructs the passage.
<s>Vṛnda</s> is round and raised, located at the side of the throat, and produces burning and fever.
Situated at the jaw-joint in the throat, resembling the fruit of cotton,
slimy, with slight pain, and hard, the swelling is <s>tuṇḍikerikā</s>.
The <s>galaugha</s> is a terrible swelling, external and internal, like a bar across the throat passage.
It brings heaviness of the head, drowsiness, salivation, and fever.
<s>Valaya</s> is a ring-like swelling, not very painful, and likewise elongated and raised.
A <s>māṃsakīla</s> is a fleshy peg in the throat, caused by the doṣas, one or many, with slight pain.
The <s>gilāyuka</s> has a broad root and makes breathing and swallowing difficult.
Surrounded by many flesh-sprouts and causing intense thirst, fever, and headache,
the <s>śataghnī</s> is a studded mass like a <s>śataghnī</s> weapon and causes extreme pain.
The <s>galavidradhi</s> occupies the whole throat, arises and matures quickly, and is very painful.
It is a swelling that discharges foul, pus-like fluid.
At the end of the tongue and the beginning of the throat, the morbid factors generate an unripe swelling,

children.text: janayanti sthiraṃ raktaṃ nīrujaṃ tad galārbudam
children.translated_text: firm, blood-colored, and painless; that is <s>galārbuda</s>, a throat tumor.
Externally, from <s>vāta</s>, phlegm, and fat, there arises <s>galagaṇḍa</s>.
As it increases with time, it hangs down like a scrotum and is very painful.

children.text: kṛṣṇo 'ruṇo vā todāḍhyaḥ sa vātāt kṛṣṇarājimān
children.translated_text: When due to <s>vāta</s>, it is black or reddish, full of piercing pain, and marked with black streaks.
When enlarged, it causes dryness in the palate and throat, and a bad taste in the mouth.

children.text: sthiraḥ savarṇaḥ kaṇḍūmān śītasparśo guruḥ kaphāt
children.translated_text: When due to <s>kapha</s>, it is steady, of the same color, itchy, cold to the touch, and heavy.
When enlarged, it causes coating in the palate and throat, and a sweet taste in the mouth.
The fat-born type follows the phlegmatic type in its decrease and increase.

children.text: dehaṃ vṛddhaśca kurute gale śabdaṃ svare 'lpatām ||
children.translated_text: When enlarged, it makes the body heavy, produces sound in the throat, and weakens the voice.
When the movement of <s>vāta</s> is obstructed by phlegm, the throat becomes dry and the voice is lost.

children.text: tāmyan prasaktaṃ śvasiti yena sa svarahānilāt ||
children.translated_text: Fainting, he breathes continually; this condition is caused by the wind that destroys the voice.
<s>Vāta</s>, moving everywhere, produces ulcers inside the mouth.
They are shifting, reddish, and dry; the lips become coppery and their skin peels.
The tongue cannot bear cold, is heavy, cracked, and covered with thorn-like projections.

children.text: vivṛṇoti ca kṛcchreṇa mukhaṃ pāko mukhasya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: He opens the mouth only with difficulty; this is <s>mukhapāka</s>, inflammation of the mouth.
When <s>vāyu</s> is checked downward by hemorrhoids, abdominal tumors, phlegm, and the like,
it goes upward, causing foul odor in the mouth; that is <s>ūrdhvaguda</s>.
In <s>pitta</s>-born inflammation of the mouth there are burning, heat, and a bitter taste in the mouth.
In the blood-born type, the ulcers are like wounds sprinkled with alkali.
In the <s>kapha</s>-born type there is sweetness of the mouth, and the ulcers are itchy and slimy.
Taking its seat inside the cheek, <s>kapha</s> produces a dark-pale tumor.

children.text: kuryāt tad ghaṭṭitaṃ chinnaṃ mṛditaṃ ca vivardhate
children.translated_text: When struck, cut, or rubbed, it grows larger.

children.text: mukhapāko bhavet sāsraiḥ sarvaiḥ sarvākṛtir malaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Inflammation of the mouth caused by all the morbid factors together with blood has the forms of all of them.
Foulness of the mouth and aversion to tooth-sticks and the like arise from those same factors.

children.text: oṣṭhe gaṇḍe dvije mūle jihvāyāṃ tāluke gale ||
children.translated_text: On the lips, cheeks, teeth, roots of the teeth, tongue, palate, throat,
and everywhere in the mouth, seventy-five diseases have thus been stated.

children.text: ekādaśaiko daśa ca trayodaśa tathā ca ṣaṭ ||
children.translated_text: In order, they are eleven, one, ten, thirteen, six,
eight, eighteen, and eight; among these, the following are not to be treated.
<s>Karāla</s>, the fleshy and bloody lip disorders, and tumors except for the fluid-born one,
<s>kacchapa</s>, <s>tālupiṭikā</s>, <s>galaugha</s>, <s>suṣira</s>, and <s>mahān</s>,
<s>svaraghna</s>, <s>ūrdhvaguda</s>, <s>śyāva</s>, <s>śataghnī</s>, <s>valaya</s>, and <s>alasa</s>,
sinus tracts and lip inflammations due to combined doṣas, blood, or all doṣas, and <s>rohiṇī</s>,
among the teeth, <s>sphuṭita</s> and <s>dantabheda</s>, and a mature <s>upajihvikā</s>,
<s>galagaṇḍa</s>, loss of voice, difficult breathing, and any condition more than a year old are incurable.
But <s>harṣa</s> and <s>bheda</s> are manageable; the rest should be conquered by surgery and medicines.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of the mouth.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great sages.
For a split lip, after scraping the two edges and suturing them, one should treat it like a wound.
With <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, and <s>utpala</s>,

children.text: paṭolyā kākamācyā ca tailam abhyañjanaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: and with <s>paṭolī</s> and <s>kākamācī</s>, one should cook an oil for anointing.
And an oil for nasal medication should be prepared with vāta-subduing drugs and the sweet group.
In vāta disease of the lip, a cotton pad smeared with prepared <s>mahāsneha</s> is beneficial.
With <s>devadhūpa</s>, beeswax, <s>guggulu</s>, and <s>amaradāru</s>,
mixed with the powder called <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, rubbing should be done with that same preparation.
One should foment a tubular swelling of the lip with castor leaves cooked in milk.

children.text: khaṇḍauṣṭhavihitaṃ nasyaṃ tasya mūrdhni ca tarpaṇam
children.translated_text: For it, the nasal medication prescribed for split lip should be used, and the head should be nourished.
The pitta-born and trauma-born lip diseases should be treated with leeches.
Rubbing should be done with <s>lodhra</s>, <s>sarjarasa</s>, honey, and <s>madhuka</s>.
For anointing, ghee cooked with <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, and <s>pattaṅga</s> should be used.
Here, and also in the blood-born condition, the treatment is as for a pitta abscess.

children.text: idam eva nave kāryaṃ karmauṣṭhe tu kaphāture ||
children.translated_text: This very treatment should be done when the condition is recent; but in a kapha-afflicted lip disease called <s>karmauṣṭha</s>,
after blood has been removed, rubbing should be done with <s>pāṭhā</s>, alkali, honey, and <s>vyoṣa</s>.
Smoking, nasal medication, and gargles that cut kapha should also be employed.

children.text: svinnaṃ bhinnaṃ vimedaskaṃ dahen medojam agninā
children.translated_text: A fatty growth, after it has been fomented, opened, and freed from fat, should be cauterized with fire.
One should rub it with <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and honey.
In a water-blister, once it has been opened and cleansed, strong rubbing with honey should be done.
If it is deep-seated or excessively enlarged, alkali or fire is the countermeasure.
In the immature and other stages, one should treat <s>alajī</s> on the cheek like a swelling.
For one with sensitive teeth, after fomentation one should scrape and cauterize the gum margin.
It should also be rubbed with oil mixed with honey, <s>ghana</s>, and rock salt.
A bolus should be made with pomegranate bark, <s>varā</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, <s>kāntā</s>, jambu seed, and dry ginger,
and with decoctions of milky trees; <s>aṇutaila</s> should be used as nasal medication.

children.text: dantaharṣe tathā bhede sarvā vātaharā kriyā ||
children.translated_text: In tooth sensitivity and splitting, all vāta-removing treatment is appropriate.
Milk boiled with sesame and licorice should be held as a gargle.
For loose teeth, an unctuous decoction of <s>daśamūla</s> should be used as a gargle.
Rubbing should be done with copper sulphate, <s>lodhra</s>, long pepper, <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>pattaṅga</s>, and salt.
Unctuous nasal medications, foods, boluses, and the like should be adopted according to the condition.
When <s>adhidantaka</s>, smeared with alkali, has become brittle,
one should pull it out like a worm-eaten tooth and then treat it in the same way.

children.text: anavasthitarakte ca dagdhe vraṇa iva kriyā
children.translated_text: When the bleeding has not stopped, and after cauterization, treatment is as for a wound.
Without injuring the roots of the teeth, one should remove the tartar from the teeth.
Then one should rub them with alkaline powders mixed with honey.
In <s>kapālikā</s> too this same procedure should be done, along with what was stated for tooth sensitivity.
One should conquer an immobile worm-eaten tooth, after fomentation, by evacuations,
and by unctuous pastes, gargles, nasal medications, and diets that remove looseness.

children.text: guḍena pūrṇaṃ suṣiraṃ madhūcchiṣṭena vā dahet
children.translated_text: One should fill the cavity with molasses or beeswax and cauterize it.
Filling with the milks of <s>saptacchada</s> and <s>arka</s> conquers the pain caused by worms.
A powder made from asafoetida, <s>kaṭphala</s>, green vitriol, <s>svarjikā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>vella</s>,

children.text: rajo rujaṃ jayatyāśu vastrasthaṃ daśane ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: placed in cloth on the tooth with ghee, quickly conquers pain.

children.text: gaṇḍūṣaṃ grāhayet tailam ebhireva ca sādhitam
children.translated_text: One should make the patient hold as a gargle an oil cooked with these same substances,
or combined with decoctions prepared from castor, <s>dvivyāghrī</s>, <s>bhū</s>, and <s>kadamba</s>.
If the pain is very severe and is not pacified by many kinds of therapeutic applications,

children.text: dṛḍham apyuddhared dantaṃ pūrvaṃ mūlād vimokṣitam ||
children.translated_text: one should extract even a firm tooth, first having loosened it from the root.
This is done with small forceps or with a tooth-extracting instrument.

children.text: tailaṃ sayaṣṭyāhvarajo gaṇḍūṣo madhu vā tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward there should be a gargle of oil with licorice powder, or honey.
Then, with <s>vidārī</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, and <s>kaseru</s>,
one should use as nasal medication oil cooked with ten times as much milk.
One should not extract the teeth of the thin, the weak, the old, or those afflicted by vāta.
Nor should one extract an upper tooth, for it causes many complications.
Even when teeth are extracted in these people, an unctuous, sweet, and cooling regimen is beneficial.
After blood has been let in <s>śītāda</s>, rubbing should be done with honeyed drugs.
These consist of <s>mustā</s>, bark of <s>arjuna</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, and dry ginger.
Their decoction is used as a bolus, and oil cooked with sweet substances is used as nasal medication.
In <s>upakuśa</s>, after the gums have been fomented by holding hot water in the mouth,
one should scrape them many times with a round-pointed instrument or with leaves such as vegetable leaves.
Then they should be rubbed with the scum of ghee and liquid honey,
together with lac, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>pattaṅga</s>, excellent salt, and red ochre,
as well as <s>kuṣṭha</s>, dry ginger, black pepper, licorice, and collyrium.
Afterward, warm scum of ghee, or oil, should be held as a bolus.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ ca madhuraiḥ siddhaṃ hitaṃ kavaḍanasyayoḥ
children.translated_text: Ghee cooked with sweet substances is beneficial for boluses and nasal medications.
In <s>dantapuppuṭaka</s>, after fomenting, cutting, opening, and scraping,
rubbing should be done with licorice, <s>svarjikā</s>, dry ginger, and rock salt.
In abscess, boluses and applications should be made with pungent, sharp, hot, and dry substances.
Rubbing should be done with materials produced from <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>vṛścikālī</s>, and barley.

children.text: rakṣet pākaṃ himaiḥ pakvaḥ pāṭyo dāhyo 'vagāḍhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should prevent suppuration with cooling measures; when ripe, it should be cut, and if deep-seated, cauterized.
In a cavity, after cutting and scraping, rubbing should be done with honeyed drugs,
namely <s>lodhra</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, <s>pattaṅga</s>, and <s>kiṃśuka</s>.
With <s>kaṭphala</s> added, their astringent decoctions are prescribed for gargling.
With licorice, <s>lodhra</s>, blue lotus, <s>anantā</s>, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and sandalwood,
and with red ochre, sugar, and white lotus, oil cooked from them is used as nasal medication.
After cutting away the excess flesh, one should rub it with powders mixed with honey.
A mouthful gargle is beneficial when made from the decoction of <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>,
together with substances produced from <s>vacā</s>, <s>tejovatī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>svarjikā</s>, and barley awns.
In <s>vidarbha</s>, one should clean the roots of the teeth with a round-pointed instrument.

children.text: kṣāraṃ yuñjyāt tato nasyaṃ gaṇḍūṣādi ca śītalam ||
children.translated_text: Then one should apply alkali, and afterward use nasal medication and cooling gargles and the like.
Having purified the body in both ways, and the head as well, one should then treat it.
After extracting the tooth connected with a dental sinus, one should cauterize the sinus with fire.

children.text: kubjāṃ naikagatiṃ pūrṇāṃ guḍena madanena vā
children.translated_text: If it is crooked, has more than one tract, and is full, it should be filled with molasses or with <s>madana</s>.
Washing should be done with <s>jātī</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>khadira</s>, and <s>svādukaṇṭaka</s>.
A gargle should be made with water of milky trees, and oil prepared from that should be used as nasal medication.
For thorn-like lesions of vāta nature, one should do what was taught for vāta disorders of the lips.
In tongue disorders produced by pitta, when they have been rubbed and blood has flowed,
rubbing, gargling, and nasal medication with sweet substances are beneficial.
In those arising from kapha, the same should be done with sharp substances such as mustard and <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: nave jihvālase 'pyevaṃ taṃ tu śastreṇa na spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: In recent <s>jihvālasa</s> too this same treatment is used, but it should not be touched with a knife.
Having raised the tongue and drawn out <s>adhijihvikā</s> with a hook,
one should cut it with a round-pointed instrument, and then perform rubbing and the like with sharp and hot substances.
After draining <s>upajihvā</s>, one should rub it with barley alkali.
<s>Śuṇḍikā</s> is curable by kapha-removing nasal medication, gargles, and rubbing.
When the enlarged part is like the seed of an <s>ervāru</s> cucumber, not spread through with vessels,
and is lodged at the tip of the tongue, one should hold it suspended with a hook or the like.

children.text: chedayen maṇḍalāgreṇa nātyagre na ca mūlataḥ
children.translated_text: One should cut it with a round-pointed instrument, neither too near the tip nor at the root.
If the cut is excessive, death occurs from loss of blood; if deficient, the disease increases.
When it has been cut, rubbing should be done with black pepper, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>,
together with salt and honey; afterward a mouthful gargle should be given.
With waters of <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
in <s>saṃghāta</s>, <s>puppuṭa</s>, and <s>kūrma</s>, one should scrape and then act in this same way.
When <s>tālupāka</s> is unripe, rubbing should be done with preparations made from green vitriol, honey, and <s>tārkṣya</s>.
The gargle should be made with cooling, astringent, and sweet medicines.
When it is ripe and has burst like an <s>aṣṭāpada</s>, rubbing should be done with sharp and hot substances.
One should hold a mouthful gargle made from bitter substances such as <s>vṛṣa</s>, <s>nimba</s>, and <s>paṭola</s>.
In dryness of the palate, if there is no thirst, ghee should be taken after the meal.
One should drink it boiled with <s>kaṇā</s> and dry ginger, and hold sour liquids as gargles.
Unctuous meat soups of animals from dry lands are useful, and milk and ghee should be used as nasal medication.
In diseases of the throat, bloodletting is indicated, along with sharp procedures such as nasal medication.
A decoction of bark of <s>dārvī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, and <s>kaliṅgaja</s> should be drunk,
or a decoction of <s>harītakī</s> may be drunk mixed with honey.
A preparation of <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, barley alkali, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>dvīpī</s>, <s>rasāñjana</s>,
together with <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>tejinī</s>, and <s>nimba</s>, cooked in sour gruel and cow's urine,
is to be prepared here as a mouthful gargle or as pills for rubbing.
A warm paste of <s>nicula</s>, <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, the great medicine,

children.text: vacā dantī ca mūrvā ca lepaḥ koṣṇo 'rtiśophahā
children.translated_text: <s>vacā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>mūrvā</s> removes pain and swelling.
Next, after fomenting <s>vātarohiṇikā</s> internally and externally, one should scrape it quickly
with a finger-knife or with a fingernail provided with salt.
Water of <s>pañcamūla</s> should be used as a mouthful gargle, and oil for gargling and nasal medication.
After draining the type produced by pitta, one should rub it with sugar, honey, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
together with <s>lodhra</s> and <s>pattaṅga</s>; a gargle should be made with these boiled as a decoction.
A decoction of grapes and <s>parūṣaka</s> is also beneficial for holding as a mouthful gargle.
The type produced by blood should be treated in just this same way, after declaring its prognosis.
The kapha-born type should be rubbed with pungent substances together with soot from a house.
Oil cooked for nasal medication and gargling is also recommended.
It should be prepared with fruits of <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>jantughna</s>, and rock salt.
The same treatment applies in <s>vṛnda</s>, <s>śālūka</s>, <s>tuṇḍikerī</s>, and <s>gilāyu</s>.
When an abscess has been drained, <s>śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, <s>tārkṣya</s>, and red ochre,
together with <s>lodhra</s>, salt, <s>pattaṅga</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>, are used for gargling and rubbing.
A vāta-born <s>galagaṇḍa</s>, after being fomented and having its blood let,
should be poulticed with sesame and with seeds produced from <s>laṭvā</s>, flax, <s>priyāla</s>, and garlic.

children.text: upanāhyo vraṇe rūḍhe pralepyaśca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: When the wound has healed, it should be anointed again and again
with <s>śigru</s>, <s>tilvaka</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, <s>gajakṛṣṇā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,
with roots of <s>kālāmṛta</s> and <s>arka</s>, and with flowers of <s>karahāṭa</s>,
ground together with <s>ekaiṣīkā</s> in liquor or sour gruel.
One should make the patient drink oil cooked with <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>nimba</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>haṃsapadī</s>, and the two <s>balā</s>s,
together with black pepper and <s>devadāru</s>.
This should also be done in the kapha-born type, but fomenting and softening measures are especially important.
A paste consists of <s>ajagandhā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>viśalyā</s>, <s>viṣāṇikā</s>,
<s>guñjā</s>, bottle-gourd, and <s>śukāhvā</s>, mixed with the alkali of <s>palāśa</s>.
Having cooked strong alkali filtered through urine, one who eats <s>kodrava</s> should drink it.
Or oil cooked with the <s>vatsaka</s> group and with the five salts should be used.
One should regularly practice kapha-removing measures such as medicated smoke, emesis, and nasal medication.

children.text: medobhave sirāṃ vidhyet kaphaghnaṃ ca vidhiṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: In the type produced by fat, one should puncture a vein and adopt the kapha-removing regimen.
One should make the patient drink the powder of the <s>asana</s> group in the morning with urine.

children.text: aśāntau pācayitvā ca sarvān vraṇavad ācaret
children.translated_text: If it is not pacified, after bringing it to suppuration, one should treat all of them as wounds.
In inflammations of the mouth, mouthwashes mixed with honey should be employed.
They are decoctions of <s>triphalā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, raisins, and young shoots of <s>jātī</s>.
Or, after chewing the <s>kuṭherādi</s> group, one should spit it out.
In mouth inflammation caused by vāta, black pepper, salt, and cardamom are used for rubbing.
Oil cooked with vāta-removing substances is beneficial for gargling and nasal medication.
For pitta and blood there is a pitta-and-blood-removing regimen; for kapha, a kapha-removing regimen.
One should scrape hard, fixed eruptions with leaves such as vegetable leaves.
In a condition involving all the doṣas, treatment should be done according to the arising of each doṣa.
In a fresh <s>arbuda</s> (tumor), when it has not grown too large and has been cut, rubbing is prescribed.
A decoction with <s>svarjikā</s>, dry ginger, and honey is regarded as a gargle.
It is made from a paste of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>nimba</s>, combined with honey and oil.
Eating barley-food, one should also practice nasal medication and massage with sharp oils.
After emesis, in putrid-smelling mouth, sharp medicinal smoke and nasal insufflation are used.
Water with <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>phalinī</s>, and <s>padmaka</s>,
when powdered, is sprinkled inside the mouth as a cleansing wash.
One should also follow the nasal medications and other measures taught for <s>śītāda</s> and <s>upakuśa</s>.
<s>Triphala</s>, <s>dvīpikā</s>, <s>kirātatiktā</s>, licorice, white mustard, and <s>trikaṭu</s>,
<s>mustā</s>, the two kinds of turmeric, barley awns, <s>vṛkṣāmla</s>, sour pomegranate, and <s>vetasa</s>,
the barks of <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>jambū</s>, mango, and <s>dhanañjaya</s>, the bark of <s>ahimāra</s>, and heartwood of <s>khadira</s>:

children.text: kvāthena teṣāṃ ghanatāṃ gatena taccūrṇayuktā guṭikā vidheyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with their decoction reduced to thickness, pills should be made together with their powder.

children.text: tā dhāritā ghnanti mukhena nityaṃ kaṇṭhauṣṭhatālvādigadān sukṛcchrān
children.translated_text: When these are regularly held in the mouth, they destroy even very difficult diseases of the throat, lips, palate, and the like.
They are especially effective for <s>rohiṇikā</s>, dryness of the mouth, and bad odor, and were prescribed by the lord of <s>Videha</s>.

children.text: khadiratulām ambughaṭe paktvā toyena tena piṣṭaiśca
children.translated_text: After cooking a <s>tulā</s> of <s>khadira</s> in a water-pot, and with that water, together with pastes of
<s>candana</s>, <s>joṅgaka</s>, saffron, <s>paripelava</s>, <s>vālaka</s>, and <s>uśīra</s>,
<s>surataru</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, grapes, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>coca</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>,
<s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>nakha</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, fine cardamom, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, and <s>pattaṅga</s>,
one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil, using one <s>karṣa</s> of each; used for drinking, nasal medication, and gargling,

children.text: hatvāsye sarvagadān janayati gārdhrīṃ dṛśaṃ śrutiṃ ca vārāhīm ||
children.translated_text: that oil destroys all diseases in the mouth and produces vulture-like sight and boar-like hearing.
When the face has been rubbed with <s>prapunāṭa</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>dārvī</s>, and anointed with this oil,
it becomes free from freckles, dark patches, facial blemishes, and the like, with a luster like the moon.

children.text: palaśataṃ bāṇāt toyaghaṭe paktvā rase 'smiṃśca palārdhikaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having cooked one hundred <s>palas</s> of <s>bāṇa</s> in a water-pot, and in that extract, with half-<s>pala</s> portions of
<s>khadira</s>, <s>jambū</s>, licorice, <s>anantā</s>, and mango, together with <s>ahimāra</s> and blue lotus,

children.text: tailaprasthaṃ pācayecchlakṣṇapiṣṭairebhir dravyair dhāritaṃ tan mukhena
children.translated_text: one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil with these substances finely ground; when it is held in the mouth,

children.text: rogān sarvān hanti vaktre viśeṣāt sthairyaṃ dhatte dantapaṅkteścalāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: it destroys all diseases in the mouth especially, and gives firmness to a loose row of teeth.

children.text: khadirasārād dve tule paced valkāt tulāṃ cārimedasaḥ
children.translated_text: One should cook two <s>tulās</s> of <s>khadira</s> heartwood and one <s>tulā</s> of <s>arimeda</s> bark

children.text: ghaṭacatuṣke pādaśeṣe 'smin pūte punaḥ kvathanād ghane ||
children.translated_text: in four pots of water until a quarter remains; when this has been strained and then boiled again to thickness,
one should add one <s>akṣa</s> each of very fine powder of <s>sevyā</s>, <s>ambupattaṅga</s>, red ochre,
the two sandalwoods, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>puṇḍrāhva</s>, licorice, lac, and the two collyriums,
<s>dhātakī</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, the two turmerics, <s>triphala</s>, the four aromatics, and <s>joṅgaka</s>,
<s>mustā</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, banyan shoots, <s>māṃsī</s>, and <s>vāsaka</s>,
as well as <s>padmaka</s>, cardamom, and <s>samaṅgā</s>; when it is cool, one <s>pala</s> each separately of
<s>jātī</s> leaf, with nutmeg, cloves, and <s>kaṅkollaka</s>,
and a <s>kuḍava</s> of crystal-white fragrant camphor should be added to it.

children.text: kārayed guṭikāḥ sadā caitā dhāryā mukhe tadgadāpahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then pills should be made; these should always be held in the mouth and remove its diseases.
By reversing the arrangement of the decoction-drugs, oil should be cooked by this same procedure.

children.text: sarvāsyarogoddhṛtaye tad āhur dantasthiratve tvidam eva mukhyam ||
children.translated_text: They say that it removes all mouth diseases, but this preparation is especially important for firming the teeth.
These pills are famous as made with <s>khadira</s>, and this oil as made with <s>arimeda</s>.
Even a healthy person who uses them every day becomes one whose teeth are firm.
A decoction of small <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>sumanaḥ</s> shoots, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>triphala</s>,

children.text: kṣaudreṇa yuktaḥ kavaḍagraho 'yaṃ sarvāmayān vaktragatān nihanti ||
children.translated_text: combined with honey and held as a mouthful, destroys all diseases located in the mouth.
A powder of <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>dārvī</s> bark, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, <s>pītāṅgī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>tejovatī</s>,
with honey, when rubbed on, removes pain, itching, suppuration, and discharge in the gums.
In disorders of the mouth, teeth, and throat, a black powder with honey, made of house-smoke, <s>tārkṣya</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, alkali, <s>agni</s>, <s>ayovarā</s>, and <s>tejohrā</s>,
should be kept in the mouth.
A yellow powder made of <s>dārvī</s> bark, rock salt, realgar, barley awns, and orpiment,
mixed with honey and ghee, should be held in diseases of the teeth, mouth, and throat.
With the two alkalis, smoke, <s>kavarā</s>, the five salts, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>giri</s>, and <s>tārkṣya</s>,
this thick extract, cooked in cow urine, destroys diseases of the throat.
For a man who eats <s>pathyā</s> fruits whose bodies have dissolved through boiling in cow urine and have been infused with <s>jalamiśi</s> and <s>kuṣṭha</s>,

children.text: attāraṃ naram aṇavo 'pi vaktrarogāḥ śrotāraṃ nṛpam iva na spṛśantyanarthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: even minute mouth diseases do not touch him, just as misfortunes do not touch a king who listens well.
One should drink a decoction of <s>saptacchada</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>harītakī</s>, <s>tiktaka</s>, and <s>rohiṇī</s>,
with licorice, <s>rājadruma</s>, and sandalwood; it removes suppuration in the mouth.
A decoction of <s>paṭola</s>, dry ginger, <s>triphala</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, <s>trāyantī</s>, the two <s>tiktā</s>s, the two turmerics, and <s>amṛtā</s>,

children.text: pītaḥ kaṣāyo madhunā nihanti mukhe sthitaścāsyagadān aśeṣān ||
children.translated_text: when drunk with honey and kept in the mouth, destroys all mouth diseases without remainder.
The fresh juice of <s>dārvī</s>, boiled down until thick and mixed with red ochre,
when kept in the mouth with honey, removes mouth suppuration, fistula, and wounds.
For <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nimba</s>, licorice, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>jātī</s>, and <s>arimeda</s>,
as well as for <s>khadira</s> and <s>varā</s>, the same separate preparation is prescribed.
With <s>khadira</s>, <s>ayovarā</s>, <s>pārtha</s>, <s>madayantī</s>, and <s>ahimāraka</s>,
a gargle boiled in water should be held for the pacification of weak teeth.
Diseases arising in the mouth, the roots of the teeth, and the throat are generally dominated by <s>kapha</s> and blood.

children.text: tasmāt teṣām asakṛd rudhiraṃ visrāvayed duṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore their vitiated blood should be let out repeatedly.
Purgation for the body and head, emesis, and pungent and bitter mouthfuls for gargling

children.text: prāyaḥ śastaṃ teṣāṃ kapharaktaharaṃ tathā karma ||
children.translated_text: are generally beneficial for them, as are procedures that remove <s>kapha</s> and blood.
Food made from barley and coarse grains, split pulses soaked in alkali, and dishes without fat,
soups and eatables are wholesome, along with whatever else destroys phlegm.
Diseases of the throat, situated in the pathway of the vital breath, may even obstruct breathing in a negligent person.
Therefore treatment should be undertaken quickly in them.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of diseases of the head.
Thus indeed said the great sages headed by <s>Ātreya</s>.
Through smoke, sun, frost, playing in water, excessive sleep, and wakefulness,
through sweating, facing the east wind, suppression of tears, and weeping,
through excessive drinking of water and liquor, through worms, and through suppression of natural urges,
through aversion to pillows, cleansing, and anointing, and through continually looking downward,
and through incompatible smells, bad unripe food, excessive speech, and the like, the <s>doṣas</s> go to the head.
There they produce diseases; among them, when <s>vāta</s> is aggravated,

children.text: nistudyete bhṛśaṃ śaṅkhau ghāṭā saṃbhidyate tathā
children.translated_text: the temples are violently pierced with pain, and the occipital region seems to be split apart.
The space between the eyebrows and the forehead seem to be falling, with extreme pain.
The ears are troubled by ringing, and the eyes seem as if they are being pulled out.

children.text: ghūrṇatīva śiraḥ sarvaṃ saṃdhibhya iva mucyate ||
children.translated_text: The whole head seems to whirl and to come loose from its joints.
The network of veins throbs excessively, and there is stiffness of the neck and jaws.
There is intolerance of light, nasal discharge, and sudden arising and calming of pain.
Relief and softness arise from rubbing, oleation, sweating, and bandaging.
This is <s>śirastāpa</s>; when it is in half of the head, it is <s>ardhāvabhedaka</s>.

children.text: pakṣāt kupyati māsād vā svayam eva ca śāmyati
children.translated_text: It flares up after a fortnight or a month and then subsides by itself.
But when greatly increased, it destroys the eye or the hearing.
In burning of the head caused by <s>pitta</s>, there is a smoky sensation in the head and fever.
There are sweating, burning of the eyes, fainting, and relief at night and by cold applications.
In the <s>kapha</s>-born type there is anorexia, heaviness of the head, dullness, and coldness.
There is lack of pulsation in the veins, lassitude, and pain that is slight by day but greater at night.
There are drowsiness, swelling around the eyes, itching in the ears, and vomiting.
When it arises from blood, the pain is greater than in the <s>pitta</s> type; when it arises from all the <s>doṣas</s>, all symptoms occur.
When the blood and flesh in the head have become moist through mixed foods,

children.text: kopite saṃnipāte ca jāyante mūrdhni jantavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when <s>saṃnipāta</s> is provoked, living parasites arise in the head.
Drinking the blood of the head, those dreadful creatures produce pains.
They cause derangement of mind, fever, cough, and loss of strength.
Dryness, swelling, piercing pain, cutting pain, burning, throbbing, and putridity occur,
with itching, drying, and drooping in the skull, palate, and head.
In the parasitic type there is coppery and clear nasal mucus and ringing in the ears.
When <s>vāta</s> is predominant, the morbid wastes cause shaking of the head, known by that name.
With <s>vāta</s> and the others dominated by <s>pitta</s> and accompanied by blood, swelling arises in the temple.
There are intense burning, pain, redness, delirium, fever, thirst, and dizziness.
The mouth is bitter, the face is yellow, and the disease acts quickly; this is <s>śaṅkhaka</s>.
It destroys life in three nights, though it succeeds in cure if treated quickly.
<s>Vāta</s>, joined with <s>pitta</s>, in the temples, eyes, brows, and forehead
produces throbbing pain that rises with the rising of the sun.

children.text: ā madhyāhnaṃ vivardhiṣṇuḥ kṣudvataḥ sā viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: It increases until midday, especially in a hungry person.
Its comfort from cold or heat is irregular, and after that it subsides.

children.text: sūryāvartaḥ sa ityuktā daśa rogāḥ śirogatāḥ
children.translated_text: This is called <s>sūryāvarta</s>; these are the ten diseases located in the head.

children.text: śirasyeva ca vakṣyante kapāle vyādhayo nava ||
children.translated_text: And nine diseases of the skull will be described just as diseases of the head.
When <s>vāta</s> is vitiated in the skull, even in one still in the womb,
a swelling of the same color and without pain arises; know it as <s>upaśīrṣaka</s>.
Pustules, tumors, and abscesses should be described according to the arising of the respective <s>doṣa</s>.
On the skull, when there is much moisture from <s>pitta</s>, blood, <s>kapha</s>, and parasites,
pustules resembling millet and mustard seeds are <s>arūṃṣikā</s>.
A very fine cracking of the skin that causes itching, loss of hair, numbness, and dryness

children.text: susūkṣmaṃ kaphavātābhyāṃ vidyād dāruṇakaṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: through <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> should be known as <s>dāruṇaka</s>.
<s>Pitta</s>, following the hair follicles and combined with <s>vāta</s>,
makes the hairs fall out; then <s>kapha</s>, together with blood,
blocks this person's hair follicles, and because of that other hairs do not arise.

children.text: tad indraluptaṃ rujyāṃ ca prāhuścāceti cāpare
children.translated_text: They call that <s>indralupta</s>; others also call it <s>rujyā</s> and <s>cācā</s>.

children.text: khalaterapi janmaivaṃ śātanaṃ tatra tu kramāt ||
children.translated_text: The origin of <s>khalati</s> too is the same, but in that case the shedding is gradual.
From <s>vāta</s> it has the appearance of being burned by fire; from <s>pitta</s> it is covered with sweating veins.

children.text: kaphād ghanatvag varṇāṃśca yathāsvaṃ nirdiśet tvaci ||
children.translated_text: From <s>kapha</s> it has thick skin; the colors on the skin should be stated according to each <s>doṣa</s>.
When produced by all the <s>doṣas</s>, it has all forms; that which has the sheen of a nail is incurable.

children.text: dagdhāgnineva nīromā sadāhā yā ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: Also incurable is that which arises hairless, as if burned by fire, and with burning.
Body heat produced by grief, exertion, and anger, having gone to the head,
cooks the hairs together with the <s>doṣas</s>; from this greying arises.

children.text: tad vātāt sphuṭitaṃ śyāvaṃ kharaṃ rūkṣaṃ jalaprabham
children.translated_text: That due to <s>vāta</s> is split, dark, coarse, dry, and water-like in sheen.

children.text: pittāt sadāhaṃ pītābhaṃ kaphāt snigdhaṃ vivṛddhimat ||
children.translated_text: That due to <s>pitta</s> has burning and is yellowish; that due to <s>kapha</s> is unctuous and abundant.
It is thick and very white; when due to all of them, it should be known by mixed symptoms.
Another kind, arising from head pain, is discolored and cannot bear touch.
Alopecia and greying caused by <s>saṃnipāta</s> are incurable.
Those arising from bodily transformation require <s>rasāyana</s> therapy.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of the head.
Thus indeed said the great sages headed by <s>Ātreya</s>.
In a head affliction arising from <s>vāta</s>, one should follow the regimen prescribed for <s>vātavyādhi</s>.
At night, with the head anointed, he should drink ghee, followed by warm milk.

children.text: māṣān kulatthān mudgān vā tadvat khāded ghṛtānvitān
children.translated_text: Likewise he should eat <s>māṣa</s>, <s>kulattha</s>, or <s>mudga</s>, combined with ghee.

children.text: tailaṃ tilānāṃ kalkaṃ vā kṣīreṇa saha pāyayet ||
children.translated_text: One should make him drink sesame oil, or sesame paste, together with milk.
Bolus poultices and fomentations made with meat and grain are beneficial,
as is sprinkling with milk cooked with the <s>daśamūla</s> and other <s>vāta</s>-pacifying drugs.
Unctuous nasal medication, fumigation, and nourishing treatment of the head and ears should also be used.

children.text: varaṇādau gaṇe kṣuṇṇe kṣīram ardhodakaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having crushed the group beginning with <s>varaṇa</s>, one should cook milk mixed with half as much water.
When only the milk remains, it should be cooled and churned, and the essence should be taken from it.

children.text: tato madhurakaiḥ siddhaṃ nasyaṃ tat pūjitaṃ haviḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then ghee cooked with the sweet drugs from that is a praised nasal medicine.

children.text: varge 'tra pakvaṃ kṣīre ca peyaṃ sarpiḥ saśarkaram
children.translated_text: Ghee cooked in milk with this group should also be drunk with sugar.
The pith of <s>kārpāsa</s>, bark, <s>mustā</s>, and buds of <s>sumanaḥ</s>,
ground with warm water and used as nasal medication, remove every pain of the head.
When pitta and blood are involved, ghee boiled with sugar and saffron is used.
Pastes mixed with ghee, made from <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kuṭila</s>, blue lotus, and sandalwood, should be applied.
Because of the danger of aggravating <s>vāta</s>, blood should not be let in this condition.

children.text: ityaśāntau cale dāhaḥ kaphe ceṣṭo yathoditaḥ
children.translated_text: If it is not pacified in this way, cauterization is desired in the mobile type, and in the kapha type as stated above.
In <s>ardhāvabhedaka</s> too, this same treatment is used according to the association of the doṣas.
The seed of <s>śirīṣa</s> and the root of <s>apāmārga</s>, mixed with <s>viḍa</s>, are used as nasal medication.
Or the juice of <s>sthirā</s> may be used; for a paste, <s>prapunnāṭa</s> should be ground with something sour.
In <s>sūryāvarta</s> too this is used; but in that condition blood should be removed through a vein.
In head affliction dominated by pitta, after oleation, one should puncture a vein.
Cold applications and affusions for the head and face, and cleansing enemas, are appropriate.
Milk and ghee boiled with the <s>jīvanīya</s> drugs should be used for drinking and for nasal medication.
This should also be done in the blood-born type; in <s>śaṅkhaka</s>, however, one should first declare the prognosis hopeless.
In a kapha head affliction, after oleating with old ghee, one should induce vomiting with pungent drugs.
Fomentation, pastes, nasal medication, and the like are recommended with dry, sharp, and hot remedies.
Fasting is also praised here; when there is an accumulation of doṣas, mixed treatment should be used.

children.text: kṛmije śoṇitaṃ nasyaṃ tena mūrchanti jantavaḥ
children.translated_text: In the worm-caused type, blood is used as nasal medication; by it the creatures become stupefied.
Maddened by the smell of blood, they come out through the nose and mouth.
Then one should bring about their expulsion with very sharp nasal medicines and fumigations.
Nasal medication should be prepared with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>svarjikā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, asafoetida, and cow urine,
or separately with the oils of <s>kaṭunimba</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, and <s>pīlu</s>.
A nasal medicine liquefied with goat urine is worm-killing, supremely worm-killing.
One should make fumigation with putrid fish and with the medicines used for nasal insufflation.

children.text: kṛmibhiḥ pītaraktatvād raktam atra na nirharet ||
children.translated_text: Because the blood has been drunk by the worms, blood should not be removed here.
In tremor, the procedure prescribed for vāta head affliction is used, except for cauterization.
In a newly arisen <s>upaśīrṣaka</s> occurring after birth, one should employ,
when it has suppurated, the treatment for <s>vātavyādhi</s> and the procedure taught for abscess.
In an unripe or ripe abscess, pustule, or tumor, treatment should be according to what is appropriate.
In <s>arūṃṣikā</s>, after blood has been removed with leeches, the lesions should be sprinkled with neem water,
and smeared with plentiful salt and the juice of horse dung.
Or they should be treated with well-ground leaves of <s>paṭola</s> and neem, together with turmeric,
and also with oilcake aged in cow urine and the droppings of <s>kṛkavāku</s> birds.
Or <s>kuṣṭha</s> roasted on a potsherd, powdered, and mixed with oil may be used.
An application for <s>rūṃṣikā</s> removes itching, moisture, burning, and pain.
Oil cooked with <s>mālatī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>aśvaghna</s>, and <s>naktamāla</s>,
is used as an anointing in <s>cācā</s> and <s>rūṃṣikā</s>, after scraping with a razor.
If there is no pacification, one should strive to purify the head by vomiting and the other purificatory measures.

children.text: vidhyet sirāṃ dāruṇake lālāṭyāṃ śīlayen mṛjām ||
children.translated_text: In <s>dāruṇaka</s>, one should puncture the vein on the forehead and make a habit of cleansing.
Nasal medication and an oil-retaining treatment on the head should be used, and one should apply pastes mixed with honey,
made from <s>priyāla</s> seed, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>māṣa</s>, and mustard,
as well as lac, <s>śamyāka</s> leaves, <s>aiḍa</s>, and the fruits of <s>gajadhātrī</s>.
Washing with alkaline water from <s>koradūṣa</s> grass is beneficial.
In <s>indralupta</s>, after puncturing a nearby vein, one should apply a paste.
After thorough scarification, this paste should be made with <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, and hot substances,
or with the two wild <s>amara</s> trees, and likewise with the roots and fruits of <s>guñjā</s>,
or with the roots of <s>lāṅgalikā</s>, or with the juice of <s>karavīra</s>.
It may also be made with honey and the juice of small <s>vārtāka</s>,
or with the juice of <s>dhattūra</s> leaves, or with the juice of <s>bhallātaka</s>.
Alternatively, with <s>mākṣika</s>, ghee, sesame flowers, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>,
the soot of elephant tusk, anointed with oil, is the best medicine for <s>cācā</s>.
For the growth of white hair too, soot produced from a ram's horn is used in the same way.
One should avoid sprinkling with water until the hair has grown out.

children.text: khalatau palite valyāṃ haridromni ca śodhitam
children.translated_text: In baldness, greying, wrinkling, and <s>haridromnī</s>, after purification,
one should treat with nasal medicines and anointing and applications for the mouth and head.
Oil cooked with the group beginning with <s>bṛhatī</s> and with the <s>jīvanīya</s> drugs is used as nasal medication.

children.text: māsaṃ vā nimbajaṃ tailaṃ kṣīrabhuṅnāvayed yatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, for a month, a disciplined patient living on milk should take neem oil as nasal medication.
It should have been repeatedly infused with the juices of <s>nīlī</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>koraṇṭa</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
The seeds of <s>śelū</s>, black sesame, and <s>rāmā</s>, equal in amount to <s>kākāṇḍakī</s>,
are ground with goat's milk and smeared on an iron plate heated by the sun's rays.
The oil that exudes, used as nasal medication by one living on milk, puts an end to grey hair.
From milk, from <s>sāhacara</s>, from the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and from the juice of <s>saurasa</s>,
a <s>kuḍava</s> of oil is cooked with one <s>prastha</s> of each and with a <s>pala</s> of licorice added.

children.text: nasyaṃ śailāsane bhāṇḍe śṛṅge meṣasya vā sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Kept in a stone vessel or in the horn of a ram, it is used as nasal medication.
Or <s>dugdhikā</s> and <s>karavīra</s>, finely ground with milk,
should be applied at the root after plucking out the grey hair; they remove grey hair.
Milk, <s>priyāla</s>, licorice, the <s>jīvanīya</s> group, and sesame seeds;
black sesame seeds make a facial application, together with turmeric and <s>umā</s> rubbed in.
Sesame seeds with emblic myrobalan, lotus filaments, <s>madhuka</s>, and honey:
when applied as a paste on the head, this nourishes and colors the hair.

children.text: māṃsī kuṣṭhaṃ tilāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ śārivā nīlam utpalam ||
