children.translated_text: <s>Māṃsī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, black sesame seeds, <s>śārivā</s>, and blue lotus,
together with honey, ground in milk, are an excellent means for increasing the hair.
Iron filings, <s>bhṛṅgaraja</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and black earth,

children.text: sthitam ikṣurase māsaṃ samūlaṃ palitaṃ rajet
children.translated_text: kept for a month in sugarcane juice, dye grey hair, roots and all.
A gruel made with black gram, <s>kodrava</s>, and sour grain-water, left standing for three days,
and ground with abundant white iron dross, would dye even a heron.
With <s>prapauṇḍarīka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, long pepper, sandalwood, and blue lotus,
oil cooked in emblic-myrobalan juice, used as nasal medication and for anointing,

children.text: sarvān mūrdhagadān hanti palitāni ca śīlitam ||
children.translated_text: when regularly practiced, destroys all diseases of the head and grey hairs as well.
One should cook a double-fat preparation with water, <s>jīvantī</s> exudate, and milk,
and with the <s>jīvanīya</s> drugs; as nasal medication it conquers all diseases above the clavicles.
A peacock, with its feathers, bile, entrails, feet, feces, and beak removed,
joined with three palas each of <s>daśamūla</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>,

children.text: jale paktvā ghṛtaprasthaṃ tasmin kṣīrasamaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: should be cooked in water; in that decoction one should cook a prastha of ghee with an equal quantity of milk,
and with sweet substances made into a paste; it conquers all diseases above the clavicles.
When this has been made habitual through drinking, enemas, anointing, and nasal applications,
with this same decoction one should cook a prastha of ghee,
with four times as much milk and with these pastes, each one karṣa in measure:
<s>jīvantī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>medā</s>, raisins, <s>ṛddhi</s>, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
<s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>cavikā</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>kāśmarī</s>, and <s>karkaṭāhvaya</s>,
<s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>mahāmedā</s>, palmyra pith, date palm, and <s>mastaka</s>,
lotus stalk, lotus fiber, dates, licorice, and <s>jīvaka</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, sugarcane, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and the two <s>śārivā</s>s,
<s>mūrvā</s>, <s>aśvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, water chestnut, and <s>kaseruka</s>,
<s>rāsnā</s>, <s>sthirā</s>, <s>tāmalakī</s>, small cardamom, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and <s>pauṣkara</s>,
<s>punarnavā</s>, bark, <s>kṣīrī</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, and <s>dhanvayāsaka</s>,
<s>madhūka</s>, walnut, almond, <s>muñjāta</s>, and <s>abhiṣuka</s> too.
This is called <s>Mahāmāyūra</s>, superior in qualities to <s>Māyūra</s>.
It removes impairment of the tissues, senses, and voice, and it removes dyspnea, cough, facial paralysis, and fever.
It is recommended in disorders of the uterus, blood, and semen; it grants offspring to a barren woman.
One should prepare the same with mice, chickens, geese, and hares.
Two hundred and thirty-one diseases arising above the clavicles
have been explained in detail, mutually unmixed.
The seers know the person as having roots above and branches below.
Therefore one should conquer diseases that strike at the root with the greatest speed.

children.text: sarvendriyāṇi yenāsmin prāṇā yena ca saṃśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Since all the sense faculties are lodged in this, and the vital breaths too are established in it,
one should be attentive to the protection of that highest limb.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the prevention and treatment of wounds.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers, <s>Ātreya</s> and the others.
A wound is of two kinds, by the distinction of endogenous and traumatic, and by the distinction of impure and pure.
The endogenous is caused by doṣas arising within the body; the traumatic is caused by an external cause.
One occupied by doṣas is impure; one not occupied by them is pure.
Being closed or being open, hardness or softness,
being excessively raised or sunken, excessive heat or excessive cold,
redness, paleness, blackness, discharge of foul pus,
being covered with foul flesh, vessels, and sinews, having cavities, and excessive pain,
being beset by inflammation, burning, swelling, itching, and the like,
and persisting for a long time: one should know these as the form of an impure wound.
That wound is of fifteen kinds through the doṣas, together with blood; among them, from wind
it is dark, black, ruddy, or like ash, a pigeon, or bone;
its discharge is thin and scanty, like whey, flesh-washing water, chaff-water, or water;
it is fleshless, full of pricking and splitting pain, dry, and it crackles.
From bile it arises quickly and is yellow, blue, tawny, or reddish brown;
its hot and abundant discharge resembles urine, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, ash-water, or oil.
It has pain like a wound sprinkled with alkali, and has redness, heat, and suppuration.
From phlegm it is pale, itchy, and has much white, thick discharge;
its lips are thick, it is hard, spread over with a network of sinews and vessels, and has little pain.
From blood it is coral-red and emits pus mixed with blood;
in smell it is like a horse-stable, and it is joined with the signs belonging to bile.
When produced by two, by three, or by all doṣas, one should know it from a mixture of the symptoms.
A pure wound is tongue-colored, soft, smooth, with dark wound-lips and pimples, even,
or with the middle somewhat raised, and free from complications.
Skin, flesh, vessels, sinews, joints, and bones are the seats of wounds,
as are the abdominal cavity and vital spots; these eight are successively harder to cure.
A wound is easy to cure in one whose mind, flesh, digestive fire, age, and strength are strong,
and one that is round, long, triangular, or quadrangular in shape.
Likewise one located on the buttocks, anus, penis, lips, back, inside of the mouth, or cheeks
is difficult to cure when it is on the eyes, teeth, nose, outer corner of the eye, or navel,
and on the raphe, belly, ears, sides, armpits, and breasts.
A wound that carries foam, pus, and wind, that contains a foreign body, that vomits upward,
a fistula-in-ano, one inside the mouth, and one lodged in the hip-bone
in lepers, in those affected by poison, in consumptives, and in diabetics:

children.text: vraṇāḥ kṛcchreṇa sidhyanti yeṣāṃ ca syur vraṇe vraṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: wounds heal with difficulty in such people, and in those who have wounds within a wound.
They do not heal at all in those with <s>visarpa</s>, fever, diarrhea, or cough.
in those who are thirsty, sleepless, dyspneic, or afflicted with indigestion;
or when the skull is split and the brain is visible,
because of moistening of the sinews, cutting of vessels, depth, or being eaten by worms,
because of fracture of bone, retention of a foreign body, poisoning, or an unforeseen cause,
because of wrong bandaging, excessive oiliness, dryness, or rubbing by hairs and the like,
because of agitation, an unpurified bowel, overfeeding, or excessive emaciation,
because of drinking liquor, sleeping by day, sexual intercourse, or waking at night,
and because of wrong treatment, a wound, even if curable, does not heal at all.
One whose wound-edges resemble the color of a pigeon and are free from moisture,
firm and furnished with small scabs, should be declared to be healing.
Now, here in the stage of swelling, purificatory treatment should be applied as appropriate,

children.text: yojyaṃ śopho hi śuddhānāṃ vraṇaścāśu praśāmyati
children.translated_text: for swelling, and also a wound, quickly subsides in those who have been purified.
And for one in the swelling stage one should constantly perform cooling treatment,
for thereby the fire of the <s>doṣas</s>, like ordinary fire, suddenly becomes pacified.

children.text: śophe vraṇe ca kaṭhine vivarṇe vedanānvite ||
children.translated_text: In a swelling or wound that is hard, discolored, and accompanied by pain,
and especially when poison is involved, one should remove blood by leeches and the like.
When the vitiated blood has gone out, swelling, redness, and pain are immediately calmed.

children.text: hṛte hṛte ca rudhire suśītaiḥ sparśavīryayoḥ
children.translated_text: And when blood has been removed again and again, with substances very cooling in touch and potency,
with very smooth preparations ground that same day, using milk and sugarcane juice as liquids,
mixed with hundred-times-washed ghee and with other non-drying substances,
a paste applied against the direction of the hairs is beneficial, as are sprinklings and anointments made from them.
With the barks of <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>plakṣa</s>, and <s>vetasa</s>,
a poultice with abundant ghee is the supreme cooling application for swelling.
For swellings predominated by <s>vāta</s>, stiff, hard, and very painful,

children.text: srutāsṛjāṃ ca śophānāṃ vraṇānām api cedṛśām ||
children.translated_text: and for wounds of this same kind too, from which blood has flowed,
fomentation with preparations of marshland animal flesh and the like is beneficial; again, <s>soma</s> and sesame,
roasted, quenched in milk, and ground in that milk, remove burning and pain.
Firm swellings with slight pain should be anointed with unguents that remove <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>,

children.text: abhyajya svedayitvā ca veṇunāḍyā śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, after fomenting them, by means of a bamboo tube, gradually,
one should massage them for dispersion with the palm or with the thumb.
One should apply a plaster of barley, wheat, and mung beans cooked and ground.

children.text: vilīyate sa cen naivaṃ tatastam upanāhayet
children.translated_text: If it does not dissolve in this way, then one should bind it with a poultice.
When unripe it thereby reaches pacification; when ripe it undergoes suppuration.
A warm lump of gruel made from roasted flour, with jujube, sesame, and sheep's wool, with sour curd,
with ferment, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and salt, is praised for poulticing.
When a swelling is well ripened, collected into a lump, and compressed by pressure,
opening is prescribed for one fit to be opened, and also for a delicate case.
<s>guggulu</s>, flaxseed, cow's tooth, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, and pigeon dung,
alkaline herbs and alkalis open a ripened swelling.
Those containing pus, with minute openings, with cavities, and even those situated in vital spots,
should be compressed all around with fat-free pressing substances.
One should allow the plaster used for pressing to dry,

children.text: na mukhe cainam ālimpet tathā doṣaḥ prasicyate ||
children.translated_text: but one should not smear it over the mouth of the wound, for thus the <s>doṣa</s> flows out.
<s>kalāya</s>, barley, wheat, black gram, mung bean, and <s>hareṇu</s>,
and the bark and roots of mucilaginous substances are materials for pressing.
Among the seven measures beginning with washing, the groups of <s>surasā</s> and <s>āragvadha</s>

children.text: bhṛśaṃ duṣṭe vraṇe yojyau mehakuṣṭhavraṇeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: should be employed in an extremely foul wound, and also in urinary disorders, skin disease, and wounds.
Or else, for washing when the wound is unclean, there is a decoction made from leaves of <s>paṭolī</s> and <s>nimba</s>;
but when it is clean, one made from the bark of the <s>nyagrodha</s> group is used.
<s>paṭolī</s>, sesame, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and the two <s>niśā</s>s,
and <s>nimba</s> leaves: a paste with salt purifies a wound.
One should purify wounds with a wick, those with narrow mouths and those in joints or vital spots,
made from <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, honey, and rock salt.
Wounds overcome by <s>vāta</s>, discharging and intensely painful, should be fumigated
with barley, ghee, birch bark, <s>madana</s>, <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, and <s>surāhva</s>.
Those dominated by <s>pitta</s>, blood, or poison should be cooled with very cold applications.
In a wound that is dry, has little flesh, and is deep, raising of the tissue is beneficial.
With <s>nyagrodha</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, and the like, with <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>balā</s>, and sesame,
one should eat the meat of carnivorous animals, properly prepared and administered as well.
For flesh increases by the flesh of flesh-eating animals in one whose mind is pure.
For wounds with raised, soft flesh, lowering is required.
With jasmine buds, green vitriol, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>ālā</s>, and old <s>agnika</s>,
raised, hard, itchy, long-standing
and very difficult-to-clean wounds should be cleansed by alkaline cautery.
Those that flow, those caused by stones, those that carry urine, and others that carry blood,

children.text: chinnāśca saṃdhayo yeṣāṃ yathoktair ye ca śodhanaiḥ
children.translated_text: and those whose joints are cut, and those which, with the purifications as stated,
do not become clean while being purified, should be purified by fire-cautery.

children.text: śuddhānāṃ ropaṇaṃ yojyam utsādāya yad īritam
children.translated_text: For cleansed wounds, healing treatment should be applied; what was stated for raising is also used.
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>ruhā</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, and <s>madhuyaṣṭikā</s>,
<s>samaṅgā</s> and <s>dhātakī</s> flowers are the supreme agents for wound-healing.
For wounds whose putrid flesh has departed, which are seated in flesh and do not heal,
one should make a healing paste of sesame mixed with <s>madhuka</s>.
Because of its unctuous, hot, bitter, sweet, and astringent qualities, it conquers all.
Combined with honey and <s>nimba</s> leaves, it is the supreme cleanser.

children.text: pūrvābhyāṃ sarpiṣā cāsau yuktaḥ syād āśu ropaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Combined with the preceding two and with ghee, it becomes a rapid healer.

children.text: tilavad yavakalkaṃ tu kecid icchanti tadvidaḥ
children.translated_text: But some experts desire barley paste in the same way as sesame.
Wounds accompanied by blood, <s>pitta</s>, poison, external injury, depth, and heat...
One should cause healing with ghee cooked with milk and wound-healing medicines,
and wounds born of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> with oil prepared with healing herbs.
<s>Kācchī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>sarja</s> resin, red lead, collyrium, and blue vitriol,
powdered and joined with oil-pressing residues, are an excellent healer.
For wounds that are even, firm-fleshed, and situated in the skin, a powder is recommended
made from <s>kakubha</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>jambū</s>, <s>kaṭphala</s>, and <s>lodhra</s> bark.
Wounds dusted with powders of bark quickly make the skin take hold.
A plaster made with lac, realgar, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, orpiment, and the two kinds of turmeric,
together with ghee and honey, is supreme for purifying the skin.
A plaster made with <s>kālīyaka</s>, copper, bone, gold, black iron, and excellent mercury,
together with cow-dung juice, is supreme for restoring the natural color.
Burnt elephant tusk, smoke-soot collected within, oil, and <s>rasāñjana</s>
make a plaster that produces hair; likewise, when soaked in oil,
is the ash made from the nails, hair, bones, skin, horns, and hooves of quadrupeds.
For a wounded person, one should prescribe wholesome and unwholesome foods as stated under surgical procedures.

children.text: dve pañcamūle vargaśca vātaghno vātike hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The two sets of five roots and the group that alleviates <s>vāta</s> are beneficial in a <s>vāta</s>-type wound.
The <s>nyagrodha</s> and <s>padmaka</s> groups are likewise useful when <s>pitta</s> is vitiated,
the <s>āragvadhādi</s> group, which destroys phlegm, when <s>kapha</s> is involved, and mixed groups in a mixed wound.

children.text: ebhiḥ prakṣālanaṃ lepo ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ rasakriyā
children.translated_text: With these, washing, plaster, ghee, oil, thick extract,

children.text: cūrṇo vartiśca saṃyojya vraṇe sapta yathāyatham ||
children.translated_text: powder, and wick should be prepared for a wound, seven treatments according to the case.
Ghee should be cooked with <s>jātī</s>, neem, <s>paṭola</s> leaves, pungent herbs, <s>dārvī</s>, turmeric, <s>śārivā</s>,
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, beeswax, blue vitriol, licorice, and seeds of <s>naktāhva</s>.

children.text: sarpiḥ sādhyam anena sūkṣmavadanā marmāśritāḥ kledino gambhīrāḥ sarujo vraṇāḥ sagatayaḥ śudhyanti rohanti ca ||
children.translated_text: By this, wounds with small openings, lodged in vital spots, moist, deep, painful, and having tracts are cleansed and heal.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the prevention and treatment of fresh wounds.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers, <s>Ātreya</s> and the others.
Fresh wounds are those that arise suddenly from injury.
Although they are endless in number, the affected limb is said to be of eight kinds.
Abraded, incised, severed, hanging, fallen off,

children.text: viddhaṃ bhinnaṃ vidalitaṃ tatra ghṛṣṭaṃ lasīkayā ||
children.translated_text: pierced, split open, and crushed: among these, an abrasion is accompanied by lymph,

children.text: raktaleśena vā yuktaṃ saploṣaṃ chedanāt sravet
children.translated_text: or by a trace of blood, and by burning; from cutting, it oozes.

children.text: avagāḍhaṃ tataḥ kṛttaṃ vicchinnaṃ syāt tato 'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: When it is deep, it is then an incised wound; even more than that, it is severed.
A hanging wound remains attached to some bone; a fallen wound is one fallen from the body.
A wound pierced by a fine-mouthed foreign body is 'pierced,' if it does not enter a cavity.
One that does enter a cavity is 'split open'; 'crushed' is flooded with marrow and blood,
and has become broad, together with the bone, from a blow, pressure, or pounding.
One should immediately sprinkle a fresh wound with ghee of <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>,
or, when the pain is intense, again with lukewarm oil of <s>balā</s>.
To restrain the heat of the injury and what has spread at that moment,
astringent, cold, sweet, and unctuous plasters and the like are beneficial.
In fresh wounds that are elongated, especially for the sake of joining,
one should apply honey and ghee, and cooling procedures that alleviate <s>pitta</s>.
In those accompanied by inflammation, purification upward and downward should be performed.
Fasting, suitable food after eating, and repeated bloodletting are beneficial.

children.text: ghṛṣṭe vidalite caiṣa sutarām iṣyate vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: In an abrasion and a crushed wound this procedure is desired all the more,
for in those two little blood flows, and therefore suppuration quickly arises.
In other wounds, for the most part, blood flows excessively.
Then, from loss of blood, <s>vāyu</s> becomes provoked and causes extreme pain.
One should perform drinking of unctuous substances, sprinkling with unctuous liquids, fomentation, unguent application, poulticing,
and an unctuous enema prepared with medicines that alleviate <s>vāta</s>.
Thus the seven-day regimen beneficial for fresh wounds has been taught.

children.text: saptāhād gatavege tu pūrvoktaṃ vidhim ācaret ||
children.translated_text: After a week, when the force has subsided, one should follow the previously stated procedure.

children.text: prāyaḥ sāmānyakarmedaṃ vakṣyate tu pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: This is generally the common procedure; now it will be stated separately.

children.text: ghṛṣṭe rujaṃ nigṛhyāśu vraṇe cūrṇāni yojayet ||
children.translated_text: In an abrasion, after quickly checking the pain, one should apply powders to the wound.
In an incised wound, pastes and the like are used; in severed and hanging wounds,
there should be suturing according to the stated rule, and afterward bandaging and compression.

children.text: asādhyaṃ sphuṭitaṃ netram adīrṇaṃ lambate tu yat
children.translated_text: A burst eye is incurable; but when it is not torn open and hangs down,
the physician should set it in its proper place, provided the vessels are not twisted.
He should press it with his hand, with lotus petals placed between.

children.text: tato 'sya secane nasye tarpaṇe ca hitaṃ haviḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then ghee is beneficial for its sprinkling, nasal therapy, and nourishing eye treatment.
It should be well cooked from goat's ghee with <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>utpala</s>,
and milk, for that is supreme and conquers every injury to the eye.
When the eye has sunk because of pressure on the throat, vomiting, coughing, or sneezing,
or else <s>prāṇāyāma</s> should be performed, and the treatment is as for an injured eye.
When the ear has slipped from its place and been sutured, one should fill the auditory channel with oil.
When the <s>kṛkāṭikā</s> is cut and air is even escaping,

children.text: samaṃ niveśya badhnīyāt syūtvā śīghraṃ nirantaram
children.translated_text: one should set it evenly and bind it, after suturing quickly and continuously.
Here sprinkling with goat's ghee is recommended.
The patient should eat foods while lying face upward and should sleep well restrained.
After suturing a transverse wound on the limbs, with the limb properly set,
one should bind it with a twisted bandage and thick cloth.
For a wound that has not come together, a <s>goṣphaṇā</s> bandage with leather should be made.

children.text: pādau vilambimuṣkasya prokṣya netre ca vāriṇā
children.translated_text: For one whose scrotum hangs down, one should sprinkle the feet and eyes with water,
replace the testicles, and suture along the seam called <s>tunna</s>.
A <s>goṣphaṇā</s> bandage should be made, placing a strap around the waist.

children.text: snehasekaṃ na kurvīta tatra klidyati hi vraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should not apply oily sprinkling there, for the wound becomes too moist.
With <s>kālānusārī</s>, <s>aguru</s>, cardamom, <s>jātī</s>, sandalwood, and <s>parpaṭa</s>,
and with <s>śilā</s>, <s>dārvī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>tuttha</s>, oil prepared by cooking is also healing.

children.text: chinnāṃ niḥśeṣataḥ śākhāṃ dagdhvā tailena yuktitaḥ
children.translated_text: After completely cutting off a severed limb and cauterizing it,
one should bind it properly with oil by means of a sheath-bandage; after that one should treat it as a wound.

children.text: kāryā śalyāhṛte viddhe bhaṅgād vidalite kriyā
children.translated_text: When a pierced part has been split by fracture, the procedure should be performed after the foreign body has been removed.
When the foreign body has been removed from the head, one should insert a hair-wick.
Otherwise <s>vāta</s>, enraged by the flowing of brain matter, would kill him.
And as the wound heals, one should slowly remove the hairs one by one.
When brain matter has flowed out, he should eat the brains of other living creatures.
When a foreign body has been removed from some other limb, one should place an oily wick there.
Wounds that are deeply penetrated, have a minute opening, and have discharged blood
should be irrigated with <s>cakrataila</s>, applied through a fine nozzle.
When the abdominal cavity is ruptured and filled with blood, there are fainting, pain in the heart and sides,
fever, burning, thirst, distension, and aversion to food,
obstruction of feces, urine, and flatus, dyspnea, sweating, and redness of the eyes;

children.text: lohagandhitvam āsyasya syād gātre ca vigandhatā ||
children.translated_text: the mouth has the smell of iron, and the body too has a foul odor.
When the blood is in the stomach, he also vomits blood;
it is diagnosed by excessive distension and by pain.
When the blood is in the large intestine, painful heaviness occurs,
with coldness below the navel and blood issuing from the orifices.
Even an unruptured cavity is filled through minute channels
by flowing blood, as the bladder is filled with urine.
In that condition, one should give up a patient with internal bleeding, cold feet, breath, hands, and face,
red eyes, a pale face, and abdominal distension.
When it is located in the stomach, emesis is beneficial; when it is lodged in the large intestine,
purgation and a decoction enema should be given, using cleansing agents that are without oil and warm.
He should eat food with soups of barley, jujube, and horse gram, free from fat,
or he should drink gruel mixed with rock salt.
But one whose abdominal cavity is ruptured and whose blood has flowed out excessively should drink blood.
Rupture of the abdominal cavity is remembered as twofold: by bruised intestines and by cut intestines.
Fainting and the other symptoms are slight in the first; in the second they are extremely distressing.

children.text: kliṣṭāntraḥ saṃśayī dehī chinnāntro naiva jīvati ||
children.translated_text: A person whose intestines are bruised is doubtful; one whose intestines are cut does not live at all.
When a person's feces, urine, and flatus have reached their proper channels,
and he is free from complications, he certainly lives even when the abdominal cavity is ruptured.

children.text: abhinnam antraṃ niṣkrāntaṃ praveśyaṃ na tvato 'nyathā
children.translated_text: An intestine that has come out but is not ruptured should be put back in, but not otherwise.
Some, however, say that even one whose end is caught by an <s>utpaṅgila</s> should be replaced.
If it is smeared with grass, blood, and dust, one should wash it with milk,
and, with nails clipped and the intestine anointed with ghee, should insert it slowly, slowly.
If it is dry, one should moisten it with milk and drench it with abundant ghee.
One should stroke the throat with a finger and also provoke retching with water.
In that way the intestines enter inside; at that moment they also cause pain.

children.text: vraṇasaukṣmyād bahutvād vā koṣṭham antram anāviśat ||
children.translated_text: If, because of the smallness of the wound or because of their great quantity, the intestines do not enter the abdomen,
one should cut open the belly to that measure and insert them.

children.text: yathāsthānaṃ sthite samyak antre sīvyed anu vraṇam ||
children.translated_text: When the intestines are properly situated in their place, one should then sew up the wound.

children.text: sthānād apetam ādatte jīvitaṃ kupitaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: An intestine displaced from its place takes away life, and when irritated it does so as well.
After wrapping it with a bandage, one should sprinkle it with ghee.
After that one should make him drink warm milk mixed with <s>citrātaila</s>,
for soft action of the feces and for the downward movement of flatus.
For a year he should follow the regimen for managing wounds as previously taught.

children.text: udarān medaso vartiṃ nirgatāṃ bhasmanā mṛdā ||
children.translated_text: When a wick of fat has come out from the abdomen, one should sprinkle it with ash or clay,

children.text: avakīrya kaṣāyair vā ślakṣṇair mūlaistataḥ samam
children.translated_text: or with smooth astringent roots; then, evenly

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā ca sūtreṇa vardhayet kuśalo bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: and firmly tying it with thread, the skilled physician should draw it out.
With a sharp instrument heated in fire, he should cut it only once;

children.text: syād anyathā rug āṭopo mṛtyur vā chidyamānayā ||
children.translated_text: otherwise there would be pain, gurgling distension, or death while it is being cut.

children.text: sakṣaudre ca vraṇe baddhe sujīrṇe 'nne ghṛtaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: When the wound has been bandaged with honey and the meal is well digested, he should drink ghee,
or milk boiled with sugar, <s>citrā</s>, <s>lākṣā</s>, and <s>gokṣuraka</s>,
conquering pain and burning and containing licorice. Afterward the previously stated procedure is supreme.
There the oil taught for fatty tumors is beneficial for massage.
<s>Tālīśa</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>hareṇu</s>, <s>aguru</s>, sandalwood,

children.text: haridre padmabījāni sośīraṃ madhukaṃ ca taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>haridrā</s>s, lotus seeds, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>: with these
the oil taught for fresh wounds, prepared by cooking, is an excellent healing oil.
For one struck by a hidden blow or fallen from an uneven height,
one should perform satiating, rubbing, anointing, and the other measures that conquer <s>vāta</s> and blood.
One whose body is dislocated, crushed, wasted, struck in a vital spot, or stunned
should be placed in a trough filled with oil and should eat meat soup.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the prevention and treatment of fractures.
Thus indeed spoke the great seers, <s>Ātreya</s> and the others.
Through falling, blows, and the like, fracture of bones is twofold: involving a joint and not involving a joint.
Inability to extend and contract is dislocation of a joint.
In the other case there is severe swelling and, in all states, extreme pain,
inability even with slight movement, and, when pressed, a sound.

children.text: samāsād iti bhaṅgasya lakṣaṇaṃ bahudhā tu tat
children.translated_text: This, in brief, is the sign of fracture; yet it is manifold.
According to the variety of the fracture, the treatment of all of it

children.text: yathā syād upayogāya tathā tad upadekṣyate
children.translated_text: will be taught in such a way as to be useful.

children.text: prājyāṇudāri yat tvasthi sparśe śabdaṃ karoti yat ||
children.translated_text: A bone that is abundant, minute, split apart, and makes a sound when touched...
Where a splinter of bone has entered the middle of a split bone,
and where a fracture caused by trauma has only a little remaining,
and where, when it is raised, it is like a wound and sinks into the marrow,
that is difficult to cure, even in those who are emaciated, weak, afflicted by <s>vāta</s>, or eat little.

children.text: bhinnaṃ kapālaṃ yat kaṭyāṃ saṃdhimuktaṃ cyutaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: A split skull, one in the hip, one freed from its joint, and one displaced,

children.text: jaghanaṃ prati piṣṭaṃ ca bhagnaṃ yat tad vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: and a fracture crushed toward the pelvis: such a fracture should be avoided.
Also a skull-bone that is not united, and a forehead bone that is similarly crushed,
and a fracture that occurs in the temple, head, back, or between the breasts,
and even a bone that has been properly reduced,

children.text: saṃkṣobhād api yad gacched vikriyāṃ tad vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: if it becomes deformed through bad placement, bad binding, or even agitation, should be avoided.

children.text: ādito yacca durjātam asthi saṃdhirathāpi vā
children.translated_text: And from the beginning, too, a bone or joint that has developed badly should be avoided.
Young bones bend; reed-like bones break.
Skull-bones split, and other bones mostly crack.
Then what is depressed should be raised, and what is raised should be pressed down.
What is thrown too far aside should be drawn back, and what has gone downward should be turned upward.
By traction, pressure, elevation, drawing together of the skin, and bandaging,
all the joints in the body, both movable and immovable,
should first be properly restored by these methods of setting and made steady.
Then, after wrapping them with comfortable bandages rich in ghee,
one should use broad, thin, well-arranged splints made from <s>kadamba</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>sarja</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, or <s>palāśa</s>,
or from bamboo, broad and thin, well positioned,
very smooth and furnished with supports, or with bark and pieces of wood.
With splints called <s>kuśa</s>, one should apply an even bandage over the cloth.

children.text: śithilena hi bandhena saṃdhisthairyaṃ na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: For with a loose bandage stability of the joint does not arise.
With one that is too tight, excessive pain, burning, suppuration, and swelling arise.

children.text: tryahāt tryahād ṛtau gharme saptāhān mokṣayeddhime ||
children.translated_text: In the hot season one should loosen it every third day, and in the cold season after seven days.
In an ordinary season, after five days, or else according to the fracture and the <s>doṣa</s>.
Then one should sprinkle it with a cold decoction of the <s>nyagrodha</s> group.
When it is painful, one should sprinkle it with milk cooked with the five roots,
or a skilled physician should apply comfortably warm <s>Cakra</s> oil.
After considering the region and the time, and combined with medicines that remove <s>vāta</s>,
he should continually prescribe very cooling irrigations and poultices.
Milk from a first-calved cow, with ghee and prepared with sweet medicines,

children.text: prātaḥ prātaḥ pibed bhagnaḥ śītalaṃ lākṣayā yutam ||
children.translated_text: the fractured patient should drink cold every morning, mixed with <s>lākṣā</s>.
But for a fracture accompanied by a wound, the wound should first be rubbed
with astringent decoctions in which honey and ghee predominate; then the remaining procedure is the sequence taught for fractures.
Having smeared the hanging wound-flesh with honey and ghee,
the physician should join the wounds together and make them suitable by means of bandages.
Knowing them to be even and well positioned, he should dust them with powdered <s>phalinī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>kaṭphala</s>,
mixed with <s>samaṅgā</s> and <s>dhātakī</s>.
Or with powders of <s>dhātakī</s> and <s>lodhra</s>; in that way wounds heal quickly.
Thus treatment for fracture has been set forth. In the cold season, when the bodily elements are firm,
it is very curable in a fleshy person with slight <s>doṣa</s>; otherwise it is severe.
For those in early, middle, and final age respectively, in one, two, and three months,

children.text: māsaiḥ sthairyaṃ bhavet saṃdher yathoktaṃ bhajatāṃ vidhim
children.translated_text: stability of the joint will occur when they follow the prescribed rule.
For fractures of the hip, shank, and thigh, lying on a board is beneficial.

children.text: yantraṇārthaṃ tathā kīlāḥ pañca kāryā nibandhanāḥ
children.translated_text: For restraint, five pegs should likewise be made as fastenings:

children.text: jaṅghorvoḥ pārśvayor dvau dvau tala ekaśca kīlakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: two on each side of the shanks and thighs, and one peg at the sole.
In the pelvis, or in the spine, or in the chest and collarbones,
when fractured joints are displaced, one should follow this same procedure.
But joints that have long been dislocated should be oiled, fomented, and softened,

children.text: uktair vidhānair buddhyā ca yathāsvaṃ sthānam ānayet ||
children.translated_text: and by the stated methods, and by judgment, brought back to their own proper places.
When a non-articular fracture has healed but was treated in a crooked or excessive way,

children.text: āpothya bhaṅgaṃ yamayet tato bhagnavad ācaret ||
children.translated_text: one should strike the fracture apart, straighten it, and then treat it as a fracture.

children.text: bhagnaṃ naiti yathā pākaṃ prayateta tathā bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The physician should take care that a fracture does not suppurate.
When flesh, vessels, and sinews have suppurated, a joint does not unite.
For a fractured patient one should use the oleations prescribed for diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
One should also regularly employ the four modes of application, strengthening measures, and <s>basti</s> therapy.
With nourishing and non-burning foods such as <s>śāli</s> rice, ghee, meat broth, and milk,
one should treat a fracture in proper measure, using things that promote union of the joint.

children.text: glānir na śasyate tasya saṃdhiviśleṣakṛddhi sā
children.translated_text: Exhaustion is not recommended for him, since it causes separation of the joint.

children.text: lavaṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāram amlaṃ maithunam ātapam
children.translated_text: A fractured person should not use salt, pungent foods, alkali, sour foods, sexual intercourse, or sun exposure,

children.text: vyāyāmaṃ ca na seveta bhagno rūkṣaṃ ca bhojanam ||
children.translated_text: nor exercise, nor dry food.

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃstilān virajaso dṛḍhavastrabaddhān sapta kṣapā vahati vāriṇi vāsayet
children.translated_text: Black sesame seeds, free of dust and tied in a firm cloth, should be soaked for seven nights in running water.

children.text: saṃśoṣayed anudinaṃ pravisārya caitān kṣīre tathaiva madhukakvathite ca toye ||
children.translated_text: One should dry them each day after spreading them out, and do the same in milk and in water decocted with <s>madhuka</s>.

children.text: punarapi pītapayaskāṃstān pūrvavad eva śoṣitān bāḍham
children.translated_text: Then again, when those sesame seeds have drunk milk, they should be thoroughly dried as before.
Having removed their husks and dust and ground them into powder, one should combine them with finely powdered ingredients:
<s>nalada</s>, <s>vāla</s>, <s>kāloha</s>, red <s>yaṣṭikā</s>, <s>nakha</s>, <s>miśi</s>, <s>plava</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and the three <s>balā</s>s,
with <s>aguru</s>, saffron, sandalwood, <s>śārivā</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>sarja</s> resin, and <s>devadāru</s>,
together with the <s>padmaka</s> group; then that sesame paste
should be pressed with milk prepared with all fragrant medicines.
With <s>śaileya</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>aṃśumatī</s>, <s>keseru</s>, <s>kālānusārī</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>pattra</s>, and <s>lodhra</s>...

children.text: sakṣīraśuklaiḥ sapayaḥ sadūrvaistailaṃ pacet tan naladādibhiśca ||
children.translated_text: One should cook the oil with milk, white substances, water, and <s>dūrvā</s>, and also with the drugs beginning with <s>nalada</s>.

children.text: gandhatailam idam uttamam asthisthairyakṛj jayati cāśu vikārān
children.translated_text: This excellent fragrant oil makes the bones firm and quickly conquers disorders
arising from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, even when they are extremely strong and pervasive, through various modes of use.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>bhagandara</s>.
So indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Through riding on the backs of elephants and horses, through hard and uneven seats,
and through the other causes stated in the etiology of piles when they are indulged in,
or through an undesirable, unseen ripening, or immediately through acts censured by good people,
there generally arises, preceded by a pustule, at one or even two finger-breadths

children.text: pāyor vraṇo 'ntar bāhyo vā duṣṭāsṛṅmāṃsago bhavet
children.translated_text: from the anus, an internal or external wound situated in vitiated blood and flesh.
Because it is close to the root of the bladder and the urinary reservoir, it has the nature of discharging.
That is <s>bhagandara</s>; when untreated it tears all the parts
of the genital region, bladder, and rectum. When these have been much torn,
it gradually vomits out wind, urine, feces, and semen through minute openings.

children.text: doṣaiḥ pṛthag yutaiḥ sarvairāgantuḥ so 'ṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is remembered as of eight kinds: from the <s>doṣa</s>s separately, from combinations, from all of them, and the accidental kind.
When unripe they call it a pustule; when it has reached suppuration, <s>bhagandara</s>.
One should know a pustule that causes <s>bhagandara</s> as deep-rooted, inflamed, full of pain,
and liable to flare up after healing; but not one otherwise.
Among them, from <s>vāta</s> the pustule is dark-red and produces pricking, splitting, throbbing, and pain.
From <s>pitta</s> it rises up like a camel's neck, is reddened, thin-skinned, full of heat,
and accompanied by fever and a smoky sensation.

children.text: sthirā snigdhā mahāmūlā pāṇḍuḥ kaṇḍūmatī kaphāt
children.translated_text: From <s>kapha</s> it is fixed, unctuous, deep-rooted, pale, and itchy.
From <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> it is dark, coppery, burning, hot, and terribly painful.
From <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> it is pale, somewhat dark, and difficult to bring to suppuration.
From all the <s>doṣa</s>s it is the size of the big toe and has many kinds of pain,
being afflicted by colic, anorexia, thirst, burning, fever, and vomiting.

children.text: vraṇatāṃ yānti tāḥ pakvāḥ pramādāt tatra vātajā ||
children.translated_text: When through negligence these ripen, they become wounds. There, the one born of <s>vāta</s>
gradually fills with small-mouthed holes like a sieve with a hundred perforations,
which constantly discharge a clear exudate mixed with foam.
This is called <s>śataponaka</s>; the <s>pitta</s>-born one is <s>uṣṭragrīva</s>.
The one arising from <s>kapha</s> discharges much slimy matter and is called <s>parisrāvī</s>.
From <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> comes <s>parikṣepī</s>: after encircling the anus, a tract
arises all around there, like a wall and a surrounding ditch.

children.text: ṛjur vātakaphād ṛjvyā gudo gatyātra dīryate
children.translated_text: From <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> comes <s>ṛju</s>, in which the rectum is torn by a straight tract.
When <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> are involved, having taken support in a previously arisen pile and becoming aggravated,
a swelling appears at the root of the pile, with itching, burning, and the like.

children.text: sa śīghraṃ pakvabhinno 'sya kledayan mūlam arśasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that quickly ripens and bursts, moistening the root of the pile,
it constantly discharges through tracts; this is <s>arśobhagandara</s>.
The one produced by all the <s>doṣa</s>s is <s>śambukāvarta</s>, resembling the whorl of a conch.
In it the tracts tear the rectum with violent surges of pain.
When a fragment of bone has been swallowed out of craving for meat, and as it emerges obliquely

children.text: kṣiṇoti tiryaṅ nirgacchann unmārgaṃ kṣatato gatiḥ
children.translated_text: it injures the rectum, then from that wound an abnormal tract comes to be.

children.text: syāt tataḥ pūyadīrṇāyāṃ māṃsakothena tatra ca ||
children.translated_text: When that has been split by pus, and when the flesh there has become putrid,
worms arise in it and, eating all around the rectum,

children.text: vidārayanti na cirād unmārgī kṣatajaśca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: tear it open before long. This is <s>unmārgī</s>, and it is also called traumatic.
In these, pain, burning, itching, and the like should be understood according to the teaching on wounds.
Six of them are difficult to cure; one should abandon the accumulated-all-<s>doṣa</s> type and the traumatic type,

children.text: pravāhiṇīṃ valīṃ prāptaṃ sevanīṃ vā samāśritam
children.translated_text: as well as one that has reached the draining fold or has lodged in a fold or in the perineal seam.

children.text: athāsya piṭikām eva tathā yatnād upācaret ||
children.translated_text: Then one should treat its pustule itself carefully,
by purgation, bloodletting, sprinkling, and the like, so that it does not proceed to suppuration.
But when it has suppurated, after it has again been oleated and fomented by immersion,
one should restrain it with instruments as in the case of piles and examine the <s>bhagandara</s> properly:
whether it is nearer or farther, and whether its mouth is internal or external.
Then, after probing the internal-mouthed one, one should split it properly with a knife.

children.text: bahirmukhaṃ ca niḥśeṣaṃ tataḥ kṣāreṇa sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: The external-mouthed one too should be treated completely with alkali.
Or the physician may treat it properly with fire-cautery; the camel-neck type, however, with alkali alone.
In <s>śataponaka</s>, having left alternate channels, one should cut them open.

children.text: tāsu rūḍhāsu śeṣāśca mṛtyur dīrṇe gude 'nyathā
children.translated_text: When those have healed, the remaining ones should be cut; otherwise, when the rectum is torn, death follows.
In <s>parikṣepin</s> too one should proceed in the same way, with the alkaline threads prescribed for sinus tracts.
In <s>arśobhagandara</s>, one should first treat the piles.
The traumatic type should be treated after removing the foreign body, as in the case of a wound with a foreign body.
One should also extract it in the same way, and should give worm-killing plasters and foods.
Fomentations such as bolus-fomentation and tube-fomentation, well unctuous, are praised when there is pain.

children.text: sarvatra ca bahucchidre chedān ālocya yojayet
children.translated_text: And everywhere, in a lesion with many openings, one should plan the cuts after inspecting them:
<s>gotīrthaka</s>, <s>sarvatobhadra</s>, petal-shaped, half-plough, and plough-shaped.

children.text: pārśvaṃ gatena śastreṇa chedo gotīrthako mataḥ
children.translated_text: A cut made with the knife passing to one side is regarded as <s>gotīrthaka</s>.
When it is on all sides, it is <s>sarvatobhadra</s>; a side-cut is half-plough.
On both sides it is plough-shaped. One should burn all of them with fire,
leaving no remainder of the channels of discharge; in this way it does not become diseased again.
The physician should also strive, at intervals, for purification of the bowel in that patient.
For the wound, there is a plaster of cat bone ground with the juice of <s>triphala</s>.
With <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>malayū</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>śelu</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>kumbha</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>sarja</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>sudhā</s>, and <s>arka</s>,

children.text: abhyañjanāya vipaceta bhagandarāṇāṃ tailaṃ vadanti paramaṃ hitam etad eṣām ||
children.translated_text: one should cook an oil for anointing; they say this is supremely beneficial for cases of <s>bhagandara</s>.
<s>madhuka</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>truṭi</s>, <s>reṇukā</s>, the two <s>rajanī</s>s, <s>phalinī</s>, <s>paṭu</s>, and <s>śārivā</s>...
<s>kamalakesara</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>sarja</s> resin, and <s>mayarodikā</s> are the ingredients.
Oil cooked with these, together with the seeds and rind of <s>bījapūra</s>,
removes <s>bhagandara</s> (fistula), <s>apacī</s> (scrofulous swelling), skin disease, <s>madhumeha</s> (diabetes-like urinary disorder), and wounds.
The essence of <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>māgadhikā</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>, licked with honey and oil,
heal worms, skin disease, <s>bhagandara</s>, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), injuries, and sinus wounds.
<s>amṛtā</s>, <s>truṭi</s>, <s>vella</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>kali</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>guggulu</s>,
in gradually increasing quantity and mixed with honey and melted ghee, overcome eruptions, corpulence, and <s>bhagandara</s>.
With <s>māgadhikā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>kaliṅga</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, with ghee prepared from <s>bilva</s>, and with six palas of <s>varā</s>,
combined with an equal amount of <s>guggulu</s> and mixed with honey, there is destruction of all diseases.

children.text: guggulupañcapalaṃ palikāṃśā māgadhikā triphalā ca pṛthak syāt
children.translated_text: There should be five palas of <s>guggulu</s>, and one pala each, separately, of <s>māgadhikā</s> and <s>triphalā</s>.
Licked with honey and joined with a karṣa of <s>tvak</s> and <s>truṭi</s>, it destroys skin disease, <s>bhagandara</s>, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal mass), and disorders of movement.
That same preparation, mixed with ginger powder and well impregnated,
with a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>, especially conquers diseases of <s>vāta</s>.
One who regularly uses powder made from the best heartwood of <s>khadira</s>, moistened with water of <s>asana</s>,
together with equal <s>mahiṣākṣa</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>, destroys skin disease, <s>meha</s>, eruptions, and <s>bhagandara</s>.

children.text: bhagandareṣveṣa viśeṣa uktaḥ śeṣāṇi tu vyañjanasādhanāni
children.translated_text: This special treatment has been stated for cases of <s>bhagandara</s>; the remaining measures are auxiliary preparations.
From the section on wounds and from practical experience, one should understand them correctly and prescribe what is suitable.
After it has healed, one should avoid riding on horseback, suppression of bodily movements, alcohol, sexual intercourse, indigestion, unsuitable food,

children.text: sāhasāni vividhāni ca rūḍhe vatsaraṃ parihared adhikaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: and various rash exertions for a year, or even longer.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the diagnosis of <s>granthi</s> (glandular swelling), <s>arbuda</s> (tumor), <s>ślīpada</s> (elephantiasis), <s>apacī</s>, and <s>nāḍī</s> (sinus).
Thus, indeed, said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
The wastes, chiefly <s>kapha</s>, acting in fat, flesh, and blood,

children.text: vṛttonnataṃ yaṃ śvayathuṃ sa granthir grathanāt smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: produce a round, raised swelling; because of its knotting, it is remembered as a <s>granthi</s>.
There are nine kinds: arising from the <s>doṣa</s>s, from blood, flesh, fat, bone, vessel, and wound.
Among these, the one from <s>vāta</s> is black and accompanied by stretching, pricking, and splitting pains.
It moves from one place to another and suddenly decreases and increases.
It is soft, distended like a bladder, and, when split, discharges clear blood.

children.text: pittāt sadāhaḥ pītābho rakto vā pacyate drutam
children.translated_text: The one from <s>pitta</s> has burning, is yellowish or red, and suppurates quickly.

children.text: bhinno 'sram uṣṇaṃ sravati śleṣmaṇā nīrujo ghanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When split, it discharges hot blood. The one from <s>śleṣman</s> is painless and firm,

children.text: śītaḥ savarṇaḥ kaṇḍūmān pakvaḥ pūyaṃ sraved ghanam
children.translated_text: cold, of the same color as the skin, and itchy; when ripe, it discharges thick pus.

children.text: doṣair duṣṭe 'sṛji granthir bhaven mūrchatsu jantuṣu ||
children.translated_text: When the blood has been vitiated by the <s>doṣa</s>s and has congealed, a <s>granthi</s> arises in living beings.
Taking hold of the vessels and flesh, it is accompanied by numbness and has the marks of <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: māṃsalair dūṣitaṃ māṃsam āhārair granthim āvahet ||
children.translated_text: Flesh spoiled by flesh-producing foods brings about a <s>granthi</s>.
It is unctuous, large, hard, bound with vessels, and has the form of <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: pravṛddhaṃ medurair medo nītaṃ māṃse 'thavā tvaci ||
children.translated_text: Fat, increased by fatty substances and carried by <s>vāyu</s> into flesh or skin,

children.text: vāyunā kurute granthiṃ bhṛśaṃ snigdhaṃ mṛduṃ calam
children.translated_text: produces a <s>granthi</s> that is very unctuous, soft, and movable,
with the form of <s>śleṣman</s>, waxing and waning as the body grows or wastes.
When it is split, it exudes thick fat that is coppery, black, or white.
What is raised or depressed because of fracture of bone or injury
is a bone <s>granthi</s>. In one fatigued by walking, from suddenly plunging into water,
or from exercise while exhausted, <s>vāyu</s>, together with blood, compresses the network of vessels,

children.text: vāyuḥ saṃpīḍya saṃkocya vakrīkṛtya viśoṣya ca
children.translated_text: contracts it, makes it crooked, and dries it up,

children.text: niḥsphuraṃ nīrujaṃ granthiṃ kurute sa sirāhvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and produces a <s>granthi</s> called vessel-born, without throbbing and without pain.
In an unhealed wound, or in one only just healed, in a person who eats all tastes indiscriminately,
or in a limb that is moist, without a bandage, or struck by stones and the like,

children.text: vāto 'sram asrutaṃ duṣṭaṃ saṃśoṣya grathitaṃ vraṇam
children.translated_text: <s>vāta</s> dries the unflowed, vitiated blood and makes the wound knotted.
With burning and itching, this is remembered as a wound <s>granthi</s>.
Those born of the <s>doṣa</s>s, blood, and fat are curable, but not those that are thick, rough, and immovable,
nor those situated in vital spots, the throat, or the abdomen. A large <s>granthi</s> is an <s>arbuda</s>.

children.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ ca medo'ntaiḥ ṣoḍhā doṣādibhistu tat
children.translated_text: Its characteristics are those same ones, and it is sixfold, up to the fat-born type, from the <s>doṣa</s>s and the rest.
Because it is generally rich in fat and <s>kapha</s>, and because of its stability, it does not suppurate.

children.text: sirāsthaṃ śoṇitaṃ doṣaḥ saṃkocyāntaḥ prapīḍya ca
children.translated_text: A <s>doṣa</s> compresses blood located in the vessels and presses it inward,
and ripens that bound mass, which has discharge and is like a lump of flesh.

children.text: māṃsāṅkuraiścitaṃ yāti vṛddhiṃ cāśu sravet tataḥ
children.translated_text: Covered with sprouts of flesh, it quickly increases, and then from it there constantly flows
a great quantity of vitiated blood; that is <s>śoṇitārbuda</s>, blood-tumor.
Among these, the blood-born and flesh-born are to be abandoned; the other four should be treated.
The <s>doṣa</s>s, dominated by <s>kapha</s>, proceeding toward the groin, thighs, and the lower body,
and situated in flesh and blood, take shelter in the feet over time.

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair ghanaṃ śophaṃ ślīpadaṃ tat pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: Gradually they produce a dense swelling; that is called <s>ślīpada</s>.
From <s>vāta</s> it is cracked, black, hard, rough, and painful without apparent cause.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ ca vātāt pittāt tu pītaṃ dāhajvarānvitam ||
children.translated_text: From <s>pitta</s>, it is yellow and accompanied by burning and fever.

children.text: kaphād guru snigdham aruk citaṃ māṃsāṅkurair bṛhat
children.translated_text: From <s>kapha</s>, it is heavy, unctuous, painless, large, and covered with sprouts of flesh.
One should abandon it when it has passed a year, is very large, or has profuse discharge.
Some say that <s>ślīpada</s> arises in the hands, nose, lips, and ears just as in the feet,

children.text: ślīpadaṃ jāyate tacca deśe 'nūpe bhṛśaṃ bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: and that it occurs very frequently in marshy regions.
The wastes situated in fat and located in the throat, sides of the neck, eyes, axillae, and groins
produce many swellings of the same color, hard, unctuous, deep-seated, and shaped like eggplants or <s>āmalaka</s> fruits.
They are numerous glandular swellings and ripen slowly.
Some ripen with little pain, others discharge, and others are intensely itchy.
Some disappear, others arise, and others persist for a long time.
And this <s>gaṇḍamālā</s>-<s>apacī</s> undergoes wasting and growth, like <s>dūrvā</s> grass.
One should abandon it when it is accompanied by fever, vomiting, pain in the flanks, cough, and nasal catarrh,
and when, because a ripe swelling has not been opened, there is a wound in one who follows an unwholesome regimen.
Entering deeply into the flesh and the other tissues, the pus runs far away.

children.text: gatiḥ sā dūragamanān nāḍī nāḍīva saṃsruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: That passage is called a <s>gati</s> because it goes far, and a <s>nāḍī</s> because it flows like a channel.
In some persons the <s>nāḍī</s> is single and straight; in others that same tract has many courses.

children.text: sā doṣaiḥ pṛthag ekasthaiḥ śalyahetuśca pañcamī ||
children.translated_text: It arises from the <s>doṣa</s>s separately or combined; the fifth kind has a foreign body as its cause.
From <s>vāta</s> it is painful, has a small opening, is discolored, and emits frothy discharge.
It discharges more at night; from <s>pitta</s> it causes thirst, fever, and burning.
It pours out yellow, hot, foul-smelling pus and blood, especially by day.
From <s>kapha</s> it has a thick, slimy discharge, is itchy, and is hard.
At night it is especially moist. When caused by all the <s>doṣa</s>s, having all forms, it should be abandoned.

children.text: antaḥsthitaṃ śalyam anāhṛtaṃ tu karoti nāḍīṃ vahate ca sāsya
children.translated_text: An internal foreign body, when not removed, makes a <s>nāḍī</s>; from its mouth there flows

children.text: phenānuviddhaṃ tanum alpam uṣṇaṃ sāsraṃ ca pūyaṃ sarujaṃ ca nityam ||
children.translated_text: thin, scanty, warm pus, mixed with foam, with blood, and constantly painful.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the treatment of <s>granthi</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, <s>ślīpada</s>, <s>apacī</s>, and <s>nāḍī</s>.
Thus indeed spoke <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
In unripe <s>granthi</s>s, treatment should be done as for swellings, according to each case.
With ghee prepared with <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>,
one should oleate a patient who requires purification; after purification, sharp applications are used.

children.text: saṃsvedya bahuśo granthiṃ vimṛdnīyāt punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After repeatedly fomenting the <s>granthi</s>, one should press and rub it again and again.

children.text: eṣa vāte viśeṣeṇa kramaḥ pittāsraje punaḥ
children.translated_text: This sequence is especially for <s>vāta</s>. In those caused by <s>pitta</s> and blood, however,

children.text: jalaukaso himaṃ sarvaṃ kaphaje vātiko vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: leeches and all cooling measures are used; in one caused by <s>kapha</s>, the <s>vāta</s>-type procedure is used.
Even so, after cutting it while still unripe, when the bleeding has stopped, one should cauterize it with fire.
It must be properly left without residue; for if a residue remains, it certainly grows again.

children.text: māṃsavraṇodbhavau granthī yāpayed evam eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Granthi</s>s arising from flesh and from wounds should be managed in just this same way.
In one arising from fat, this same treatment is also to be done; and with heated fruits and the like
one should knead it, covered with a double cloth that has been smeared with sesame paste.

children.text: śastreṇa pāṭayitvā vā dahen medasi sūddhṛte ||
children.translated_text: Or, after cutting it open with a knife, one should cauterize it when the fat has been thoroughly extracted.

children.text: sirāgranthau nave peyaṃ tailaṃ sāhacaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: In a recent venous <s>granthi</s>, <s>sāhacara</s> oil should be drunk,
and poultices with <s>vāta</s>-removing substances, <s>basti</s> therapy, and venesection should be used.

children.text: arbude granthivat kuryāt yathāsvaṃ sutarāṃ hitam
children.translated_text: In <s>arbuda</s>, one should act as in <s>granthi</s>; the treatment suited to each type is especially beneficial.
In <s>ślīpada</s> caused by <s>vāta</s>, after oleation, fomentation, and poulticing, one should puncture

children.text: sirām upari gulphasya dvyaṅgule pāyayecca tam
children.translated_text: a vein two finger-breadths above the ankle, and should make the patient drink
castor oil mixed with cow urine for one month.
When it has been digested, he should eat food made from old grain, together with milk boiled with dry ginger.

children.text: traivṛtaṃ vā pibed evam aśāntāvagninā dahet ||
children.translated_text: Or he may drink <s>traivṛta</s> in the same way; if it is not pacified, one should cauterize with fire.

children.text: gulphasyādhaḥ sirāmokṣaḥ paitte sarvaṃ ca pittajit
children.translated_text: In the <s>pitta</s> type, bloodletting is done below the ankle, along with every <s>pitta</s>-conquering measure.

children.text: sirām aṅguṣṭhake viddhvā kaphaje śīlayed yavān ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>kapha</s> type, after puncturing a vein at the big toe, he should regularly use barley,
decoctions with honey, and increasing doses of <s>abhayā</s>.
One should smear it with the roots of <s>sarṣapa</s> and <s>vārttākī</s>, or else with <s>dhanvayāsa</s>.
In <s>apacī</s>, upward and downward purificatory therapy is to be drunk, as well as medicated ghee
prepared with <s>dantī</s>, <s>dravantī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>ajālinī</s>, and <s>devadālī</s>.
One should regularly use smoking, gargling, and nasal therapy that remove <s>kapha</s> and fat.
One should remove blood by venesection and drink <s>tārkṣyaja</s> with urine.
Unripe glands should be smeared with <s>nākulī</s>, <s>paṭu</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>.
After they have been fomented with a pouch of salt, one should massage the hard ones repeatedly.
A paste made from the seeds of <s>śamī</s>, radish, and <s>śigru</s>, with barley and mustard,
ground with sour buttermilk, dissolves <s>granthi</s>s and glandular swellings.
When they are beginning to ripen, after the blood has flowed out, one should overcome them with remedies that remove <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.
Or, after extracting them while still unripe, one should treat them with alkali and fire-cautery.
With the fruits of <s>kākādanī</s>, <s>lāṅgalikā</s>, <s>nahikottuṇḍikī</s>,
with <s>jīmūta</s> seeds, <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, and <s>kṛtavedhana</s>,
together with <s>pāṭhā</s>, in half-<s>pala</s> portions, and with one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>viṣa</s>, one should cook
one <s>prastha</s> of <s>karañja</s> oil in one <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice.
By this, an old chain of neck glands that carries pus,
even if considered almost incurable, is cured by drinking, anointing, and nasal application.
Oil with a paste, one quarter part, of the tuber of <s>lāṅgalikī</s>, cooked in four times its amount
of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, drives away <s>apacī</s> through nasal application and the other methods.
With <s>bhadraśrī</s>, <s>dāru</s>, pepper, the two <s>haridrā</s>s, <s>trivṛt</s>, and <s>ghana</s>,
with <s>manaḥśilā</s>, <s>nalada</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, and <s>karavīra</s>,
each one <s>pala</s> and ground in cow urine, together with half a <s>pala</s> of <s>viṣa</s>,
mixed with the juice of <s>brāhmī</s>, the latex of <s>arka</s>, and the juice of cow dung,
one <s>prastha</s> of mustard oil, when properly prepared, quickly removes
skin disease, foul <s>nāḍī</s>-wounds, and <s>apacī</s>, when habitually used by drinking and the other methods.
Oil prepared with <s>vacā</s>, <s>harītakī</s>, <s>lākṣā</s>, <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>, and sandalwood,

children.text: tailaṃ prasādhitaṃ pītaṃ samūlām apacīṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: when drunk, overcomes <s>apacī</s> root and branch.
The root produced from <s>śarapuṅkha</s>, ground with rice-water,
conquers foul ulcers, <s>apacī</s>, poison, and parasites when used as a nasal medicine and as a plaster.
With the roots of <s>uttamakāraṇī</s>, <s>pīluparṇī</s>, and <s>sahacara</s>,
together with <s>lodhra</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>śatāhvā</s>, and <s>dvīpidāru</s>,

children.text: tailaṃ kṣīrasamaṃ siddhaṃ nasye 'bhyaṅge ca pūjitam
children.translated_text: oil cooked with an equal amount of milk is esteemed for nasal therapy and anointing.
The burnt hooves of cow, sheep, goat, and horse form a plaster with pungent oil.

children.text: aiṅgudena tu kṛṣṇāhir vāyaso vā svayaṃ mṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Or, with <s>aiṅguda</s> oil, one may use a black snake or a crow that has died by itself.
Thus, if the disease is not pacified, one should take fat located on the other flank or thigh of the disease,

children.text: vasterūrdhvam adhastād vā medo hṛtvāgninā dahet
children.translated_text: above or below the bladder, remove it, and cauterize it with fire.

children.text: sthitasyordhvaṃ padaṃ mitvā tanmānena ca pārṣṇitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the patient is standing, having measured one foot upward, and from the heel by that same measure...

children.text: tata ūrdhvaṃ hared granthīn ityāha bhagavān nimiḥ
children.translated_text: Thereafter one should remove the nodules, so said the blessed <s>Nimi</s>.

children.text: pārṣṇiṃ prati dvādaśa cāṅgulāni muktvendravastiṃ ca gadānyapārśve
children.translated_text: Toward the heel, leaving twelve finger-breadths and also the <s>Indravasti</s>, on the side opposite the disease,

children.text: vidārya matsyāṇḍanibhāni madhyājjālāni karṣed iti suśrutoktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should cut open and draw out from the middle the net-like structures resembling fish eggs; this is the statement of <s>Suśruta</s>.

children.text: ā gulphakarṇāt sumitasya jantostasyāṣṭabhāgaṃ khuḍakād vibhajya
children.translated_text: From the ankle to the ear, in a well-measured person, one should divide off an eighth part from the little toe,
and below the <s>Indravasti</s>, in line with the nose, others say that one should pierce to the measure of an axle-pin.
When a <s>nāḍī</s> (sinus tract) caused by <s>vāta</s> has been poulticed and opened, one should plaster it well
with oils prepared with <s>pratyakpuṣpī</s> and fruit, ground together with rock salt.
But a pitta-type one should be treated with sesame, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>nāgadantī</s>, and the two <s>niśā</s>s,
and a kapha-type one with sesame, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, <s>nikumbha</s>, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, and rock salt.
One caused by a foreign body, after it has been cut open and cleansed, should be plastered with sesame, honey, and ghee.
If it is not to be treated by the knife, after it has been pierced at the end with a probe and properly probed,
one should split the channel repeatedly with a thread soaked in alkali.
In wounds that are foul, narrow-mouthed, deep, and the like, this is the treatment.

children.text: yā vartyo yāni tailāni tan nāḍīṣvapi śasyate
children.translated_text: The wicks and the oils that are recommended for wounds are also recommended for <s>nāḍī</s> wounds.
A paste of <s>cañcu</s> fruit, used as a plaster, is an excellent remover of <s>nāḍī</s> wounds.

children.text: ghoṇṭāphalatvak lavaṇaṃ salākṣaṃ būkasya pattraṃ vanitāpayaśca
children.translated_text: The bark of <s>ghoṇṭā</s> fruit, salt with lac, leaves of <s>būka</s>, and women's milk,

children.text: snugarkadugdhānvita eṣa kalko vartīkṛto hantyacireṇa nāḍīm ||
children.translated_text: this paste, combined with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> and made into a wick, quickly destroys a <s>nāḍī</s> wound.
Sea salt, <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, rock salt, well-ripened <s>ghoṇṭā</s> fruit, house-soot,
and the young shoots of <s>āmrāta</s>, <s>gāyatrī</s>, and <s>japa</s>, together with <s>kaṭaṅkaṭerī</s> and <s>cetakī</s>,
when these are regularly used as paste, unguent, powder, and wick,
the channel vanishes as if it had no path, like unsteady prosperity among the fickle.
Now, then, we shall explain the diagnosis of minor diseases.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
A smooth, same-colored, knotted, painless pustule resembling a mung bean,
arising in children from kapha and <s>vāta</s>, is <s>ajagallikā</s>.
<s>Yavaprakhyā</s>, named because it resembles barley, is caused by the same two; it is lodged in the flesh and hard.
<s>Alajī</s> is without an opening, round, with little pus, solid, and raised.

children.text: granthayaḥ pañca vā ṣaḍ vā kacchapī kacchaponnatāḥ
children.translated_text: Five or six nodules, raised like a tortoise, are <s>kacchapī</s>.
Above the ear or all around it, a pustule that is hard and very painful,
resembling a lotus-root, called <s>panasikā</s>, is a swelling, slight in pain and fixed,
arising at the jaw-joint from those two doṣas; it is called <s>pāṣāṇagardabha</s>.
Pustules shaped like silk-cotton thorns, painful and hard,

children.text: medogarbhā mukhe yūnāṃ tābhyāṃ ca mukhadūṣikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: containing fat and occurring on the faces of young people from those same two doṣas, are <s>mukhadūṣikā</s>s.

children.text: te padmakaṇṭakā jñeyā yaiḥ padmam iva kaṇṭakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those are to be known as <s>padmakaṇṭaka</s> by which, as a lotus with thorns,
the body is covered with painless white eruptions arising from kapha and <s>vāta</s>.
From pitta comes a round pustule resembling a ripe fig,
causing great burning and fever, open, with an opened mouth.
On the limbs and inside the mouth, accompanied by burning, fever, and pain,
hard pustules of the size and color of lentils are known by that name.
Still more difficult than these are eruptions called <s>visphoṭa</s>, with severe pain.
A pustule shaped like the pericarp of a lotus and studded with pustules,

children.text: sā viddhā vātapittābhyāṃ tābhyām eva ca gardabhī
children.translated_text: is <s>viddhā</s>, caused by <s>vāta</s> and pitta; from those same two also comes <s>gardabhī</s>,
a broad circular swelling, much raised, red, and studded with pustules.
It is called <s>kakṣā</s> when it occurs, generally from <s>vāta</s>, in places near the armpits.

children.text: pittād bhavanti piṭikāḥ sūkṣmā lājopamā ghanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From pitta arise minute, hard pustules like parched grain.
One such pustule, but large, is known by the name <s>gandhanāma</s>.
On a body covered with heat and sweat, painful hard pustules,
having the color, shape, and size of mustard seeds, are called <s>rājikā</s>.
A swelling caused by the doṣas, in which pitta predominates and which are sluggish, spreads like <s>visarpa</s>.
Thin, coppery, fever-producing, unripe swelling is <s>jālagardabha</s>.
From the wastes, with pitta predominating, blisters arise in feverish patients, tearing the flesh.
Those that arise in the armpit regions and resemble fire are <s>agnirohiṇī</s>.

children.text: pañcāhāt saptarātrād vā pakṣād vā hanti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys life in five days, or in seven nights, or in a fortnight.
A round pustule with the three signs above the collarbone is <s>irivellikā</s>.
<s>Vidārī</s> is hard like a <s>vidārī</s> tuber and occurs in the armpit or groin.
From fat, <s>vāta</s>, and kapha, a nodule arises, lodged in sinew, flesh, and vessels.
When broken, it discharges material like fat, ghee, and honey; there <s>vāta</s> is predominant.
Drying up the flesh, it produces a knotted gravel-like mass.

children.text: durgandhaṃ rudhiraṃ klinnaṃ nānāvarṇaṃ tato malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the morbid wastes make it discharge foul-smelling, wet blood of many colors.
One should know that accumulated mass to be <s>śarkarārbuda</s>.
On the soles of the hands and feet, at a joint, or above the collarbone it grows,
like an anthill, slowly, as a nodule with many tiny openings like that.
Rich in pain, burning, itching, and moisture, that is <s>valmīka</s>, born of all the doṣas together.
When the foot is torn by gravel, or wounded by thorns and the like,

children.text: granthiḥ kīlavad utsanno jāyate kadaraṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: a raised nodule like a peg arises; that is <s>kadara</s>.
From suppression of urges, <s>apāna</s> <s>vāyu</s>, dwelling in the seat of <s>apāna</s>,
makes its outer and inner passage narrow; therefore feces
comes out with difficulty. This disease is considered <s>ruddhaguda</s>, obstruction of the anus.
Pitta and <s>vāta</s> produce suppuration in the flesh around the nail, with pain and fever.

children.text: cipyam akṣatarogaṃ ca vidyād upanakhaṃ ca tam
children.translated_text: One should know that as <s>cipya</s>, a disorder at the edge of the nail, and also as <s>upanakha</s>.
A nail that is black from injury, dry and rough, is a bad nail, <s>kunakha</s>.
From contact with foul mud, the spaces between the fingers or toes become affected with itching and moisture;
the authorities call that <s>alasa</s>, and sesame-like spots are <s>tilakālaka</s>s.
The black, painless ones located in the skin are <s>māṣa</s> marks, and those same ones when raised,
and those still more raised than <s>māṣa</s> marks, whether white or black, are <s>carmakīla</s> warts.
A <s>jatumaṇi</s> is of that same sort; it is congenital and red.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ sitaṃ vā sahajaṃ maṇḍalaṃ lāñchanaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: A congenital, even, circular mark, black or white, is a <s>lāñchana</s>.
From <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> aggravated by grief, anger, and the like, on the face a thin

children.text: śyāmalaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vyaṅgaṃ vaktrād anyatra nīlikā ||
children.translated_text: dark patch is <s>vyaṅga</s>; when it occurs away from the face it is <s>nīlikā</s>.

children.text: paruṣaṃ paruṣasparśaṃ vyaṅgaṃ śyāvaṃ ca mārutāt
children.translated_text: Due to <s>māruta</s>, <s>vyaṅga</s> is rough, rough to the touch, and dusky;

children.text: pittāt tāmrāntam ānīlaṃ śvetāntaṃ kaṇḍumat kaphāt ||
children.translated_text: due to <s>pitta</s> it has coppery margins and is bluish; due to <s>kapha</s> it has whitish margins and itches.
Due to blood it has red margins, is coppery, has slight swelling, and prickles.
Phlegm, driven by wind, reaches the skin and dries up;

children.text: tatastvag jāyate pāṇḍuḥ krameṇa ca vicetanā
children.translated_text: then the skin becomes pale and gradually loses sensation.
With little itching and no moistness, that is <s>prasupti</s>, because of numbness.
From improper emesis, from aggravated <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, and from withholding food,
many intensely itching, reddened circular eruptions arise.
That is <s>utkoṭha</s>; when it is persistent it is called <s>koṭha</s>.
Thus these thirty-six minor diseases have been described according to their divisions.
Now then we shall explain the treatment of minor diseases.
So indeed said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
One should drain an unripe <s>ajagallikā</s> with leeches;
after fomenting a <s>yavaprakhyā</s>, one should apply a paste for its dissolution.
With <s>dāru</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and <s>manohvā</s>, and so on as far as <s>pāṣāṇagardabha</s>, the same rule applies;
and when they are ripe, including <s>ajagallikā</s>, one should treat them as wounds.
For <s>mukhadūṣikā</s>, the paste is <s>lodhra</s>, <s>kustumburu</s>, and <s>vacā</s>;
or coconut shells combined with young banyan leaves.

children.text: aśāntau vamanaṃ nasyaṃ lalāṭe ca sirāvyadhaḥ
children.translated_text: If it does not subside, emesis, nasal therapy, and venesection on the forehead should be used.
In <s>padmakaṇṭaka</s>, after vomiting with neem-water, one should drink
ghee prepared with neem-water and mixed with honey; neem and <s>āragvadha</s> are used as a paste.
The diseases beginning with <s>vivṛta</s> and ending with <s>jāla</s>, together with <s>erivellikā</s>, should be treated
as <s>pittavisarpa</s>; likewise <s>agnirohiṇī</s> should be treated after giving a guarded prognosis.

children.text: vilaṅghanaṃ raktavimokṣaṇaṃ ca virūkṣaṇaṃ kāyaviśodhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Fasting, bloodletting, drying measures, and cleansing of the body,
uses of <s>dhātrī</s>, and cold applications should always be done for <s>jālakagardabha</s>.
In <s>vidārikā</s>, after blood has been removed, one should proceed as for a phlegmatic glandular swelling;
for <s>śarkarārbuda</s>, one should perform especially the treatment for a fatty tumor.
A <s>valmīka</s> that is enlarged, has many openings, is swollen, and is situated in a vital spot,

children.text: valmīkaṃ hastapāde ca varjayed itarat punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or on the hand or foot, should be avoided; but in other cases,
after purifying the patient and removing blood, one should smear it with <s>paṭvā</s>, <s>revatā</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>,
with roots of <s>śyāmā</s> and <s>kulatthikā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, sesame paste, and roasted grain flour.

children.text: pakve tu duṣṭamāṃsāni gatīḥ sarvāśca śodhayet
children.translated_text: But when it is ripe, one should clean away the putrid flesh and all sinus tracts

children.text: śastreṇa samyag anu ca kṣāreṇa jvalanena vā ||
children.translated_text: properly with the knife, and afterward with alkali or with fire.
Having completely cut out a <s>kadara</s> with a knife, one should cauterize it with oil;
the treatment of <s>ruddhapāyu</s> should be carried out as for <s>niruddhamaṇi</s>.
After purification, when its heat has been subdued, one should cure <s>cipya</s> by surgical operation;
a diseased <s>kunakha</s> likewise; and in <s>caraṇāvalasa</s>, again,
after sprinkling with sour gruel, one should smear with <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, sesame,
and neem leaves; but one should cauterize <s>tilakālaka</s> lesions,
and <s>māṣa</s> moles, with a sun-crystal, or else with alkali or fire.
In the same way, after cutting them out with a knife, one treats <s>carmakīla</s> and <s>jatūmaṇi</s>.
For the three beginning with <s>lāñchana</s>, one should perform venesection as close as possible,
and apply bark and sprouts of latex-bearing trees, ground with milk.

children.text: vyaṅgeṣu cārjunatvag vā mañjiṣṭhā vā samākṣikā
children.translated_text: For <s>vyaṅga</s>, the bark of <s>arjuna</s>, or <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, mixed with honey,
is a paste; or ash from a white horse's hoof, together with fresh butter.
Red sandalwood, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, and <s>priyaṅgu</s>,
banyan sprouts, and lentils remove <s>vyaṅga</s> and give beauty to the face.

children.text: dve jīrake kṛṣṇatilāḥ sarṣapāḥ payasā saha
children.translated_text: The two cumin seeds, black sesame, and mustard seeds, together with milk,
when ground, make the face a moon whose <s>vyaṅga</s> and marks have been removed.
Lentils, husked after roasting, ground with milk, or mixed with ghee and honey,
or sharp <s>śālmalī</s> thorns ground with milk,
or the pith of <s>kola</s> with jaggery, or made into a paste with hare's blood and honey,
or <s>kuṣṭha</s> kept for seven days inside a citron and then combined with honey,

children.text: piṣṭā vā chāgapayasā sakṣaudrā mausalī jaṭā
children.translated_text: or <s>mausalī</s> root ground with goat's milk and honey,
or cow bone mixed with <s>musalī</s> root, ghee, and honey,

children.text: jambvāmrapallavā mastu haridre dve navo guḍaḥ
children.translated_text: or young leaves of rose-apple and mango, whey, the two turmeric plants, and fresh jaggery:

children.text: lepaḥ savarṇakṛt piṣṭaṃ svarasena ca tindukam ||
children.translated_text: this paste restores natural color; so too <s>tinduka</s> ground with its own juice.
Blue lotus, <s>utpalakuṣṭha</s>, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>kālīyaka</s>, and jujube pith:
this rubbing powder makes the face resemble a hundred-petalled lotus.
With these same medicines, ground for facial anointing, one should prepare
oils suited to the <s>doṣa</s> and season, combined with a decoction of <s>madhuka</s>.

children.text: yavān sarjarasaṃ lodhram uśīraṃ madanaṃ madhu
children.translated_text: Barley, <s>sarja</s> resin, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>madana</s>, honey,

children.text: ghṛtaṃ guḍaṃ ca gomūtre paced ā darvilepanāt ||
children.translated_text: ghee, and jaggery should be cooked in cow urine until the ladle is coated.
Anointing with that quickly destroys <s>nīlikā</s>, <s>vyaṅga</s>, and <s>dūṣikā</s>,
and makes the face lotus-like and the feet like lotus petals.
Saffron, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>kālīya</s>, lac, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, and sandalwood,
young aerial roots of the banyan, <s>padmaka</s>, and lotus filaments,
with blue lotus and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, one <s>pala</s> each, in an <s>āḍhaka</s> of water:
having cooked them down to one quarter, with that decoction and with powders of one <s>karṣa</s> each,
of lac, <s>pattaṅga</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s>, and saffron...
One should cook a <s>kuḍava</s> of oil with twice as much goat's milk.
Blue-black discoloration, grey hair, facial blemishes, wrinkles, moles, and eruptions that spoil the face
are removed by that nasal medication when it is used habitually; it produces fullness and good color in the face.

children.text: mañjiṣṭhā śabarodbhavastubarikā lākṣā haridrādvayaṃ nepālī haritālakuṅkumagadā gorocanā gairikam
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>śabarodbhava</s>, <s>stubarikā</s>, lac, the two kinds of <s>haridrā</s>, <s>nepālī</s>, orpiment, saffron, <s>gadā</s>, <s>gorocanā</s>, and red ochre,

children.text: pattraṃ pāṇḍu vaṭasya candanayugaṃ kālīyakaṃ pāradaṃ pattaṅgaṃ kanakatvacaṃ kamalajaṃ bījaṃ tathā kesaram ||
children.translated_text: leaf, pale bark of the banyan, the two sandalwoods, <s>kālīyaka</s>, mercury, <s>pattaṅga</s>, golden bark, lotus seed, and also filaments,

children.text: sikthaṃ tutthaṃ padmakādyo vasājyaṃ majjā kṣīraṃ kṣīrivṛkṣāmbu cāgnau
