children.translated_text: beeswax, copper sulfate, the <s>padmakādi</s> group, fat, ghee, marrow, milk, and the water of milk-sapped trees, cooked over the fire,

children.text: siddhaṃ siddhaṃ vyaṅganīlyādināśe vaktre chāyām aindavīṃ cāśu dhatte ||
children.translated_text: when properly prepared, quickly removes blemishes, blue discoloration, and the like, and gives the face a moonlike radiance.
The expressed juice of <s>mārkava</s>, milk, and water are desired for nasal administration.

children.text: prasuptau vātakuṣṭhoktaṃ kuryād dāhaṃ ca vahninā
children.translated_text: In numbness one should do what was prescribed for <s>vātakuṣṭha</s>, and should also cauterize with fire.

children.text: utkoṭhe kaphapittoktaṃ koṭhe sarvaṃ ca kauṣṭhikam ||
children.translated_text: In <s>utkoṭha</s> one should use what was prescribed for kapha and pitta; in <s>koṭha</s>, all treatment appropriate to <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Now, then, we shall explain the diagnosis of diseases of the private parts.
Thus, indeed, said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
When a man who has abstained from intercourse suddenly has sexual union, or
when he approaches a passage of menstrual blood occupied by the <s>doṣas</s>, mixed, impure, and minute,
or a woman of another womb, an unwilling woman, a forbidden woman, or one who has newly given birth,
or when he touches polluted water after intercourse, or does not do so at all,
or when, from a desire to enlarge the organ, he applies sharp plasters and the like,
or through pressure from fists, teeth, and nails, or by dropping bristle-like irritants as dangerous as poison,
or through suppression of natural urges, excessive duration, harsh contact, and friction,

children.text: doṣā duṣṭā gatā guhyaṃ trayoviṃśatim āmayān ||
children.translated_text: the corrupted <s>doṣas</s>, having gone to the private parts, produce twenty-three diseases,
beginning with <s>upadaṃśa</s>. Here <s>upadaṃśa</s> is fivefold:
from the <s>doṣas</s> separately, from blood, and from all combined. In the type caused by <s>māruta</s>,
there is swelling on the penis, varied pains, stiffness, and cracking of the skin.
In the pitta type the swelling resembles a ripe <s>udumbara</s> fruit and is accompanied by fever.
In the <s>śleṣman</s> type it is hard, unctuous, itchy, cold, and heavy.
In the blood type, black blisters arise, with discharge of blood and fever.
In the type born of all the <s>doṣas</s>, all the signs are present, and there is swelling also of the testicles,
severe pain, rapid suppuration, tearing, and the production of worms.
Among these, the one arising from blood is manageable; the one born of the combined <s>doṣas</s> leads to death.
By aggravated <s>doṣas</s> lodged in the blood and flesh of the private parts,

children.text: antar bahir vā meḍhrasya kaṇḍūlā māṃsakīlakāḥ
children.translated_text: itching fleshy projections arise either inside or outside the penis,
and likewise in the vagina, slimy, discharging blood, and shaped like umbrellas.
These are <s>arśas</s>; when neglected they destroy the penis, virility, the vulva, and menstruation.
Kapha-and-blood-born pustules may occur outside or inside the private part.
They are dense and shaped and sized like mustard seeds; they are called <s>sarṣapikā</s>.

children.text: piṭikā bahavo dīrghā dīryante madhyataśca yāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When many long pustules split open in the middle,
that is <s>avamantha</s>, caused by kapha and blood, with pain and horripilation.
<s>Kumbhīkā</s>, arising from blood and pitta, is painful and resembles the stone of a <s>jambu</s> fruit.
One should know <s>alajī</s> as resembling a urinary disorder, situated at the foremost part, and born of pitta and blood.
A pustule resembling a black gram or green gram, covered with other pustules,
and like the pericarp of a lotus, is to be known as <s>puṣkarikā</s>.
When it has been violently pressed together with the hands, it becomes <s>saṃvyūḍhapiṭikā</s>.
When repeatedly rubbed and irritated by cloth, through aggravation of <s>vāta</s>,
an uneven, hard, bent swelling is called <s>aṣṭhīlikā</s>, being caused by <s>vāyu</s>.
Through rubbing and the like, when <s>vāyu</s> has vitiated the skin of the penis,

children.text: nivartate sarugdāhaṃ kvacit pākaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: the skin turns back with pain and burning, and in some cases it suppurates.

children.text: piṇḍitaṃ granthitaṃ carma tat pralambam adho maṇeḥ
children.translated_text: When the skin below the glans is massed together, knotted, and hanging down,
that is <s>pralamba</s>; when it is called <s>nivṛtta</s>, it is accompanied by kapha, itching, and hardness.
Skin that is badly healed and split is described as <s>avapāṭikā</s>.

children.text: vātena dūṣitaṃ carma maṇau saktaṃ ruṇaddhi cet ||
children.translated_text: If skin vitiated by <s>vāta</s> adheres to the glans and obstructs
the urinary passage, then urine comes out in a slow stream and without pain.
There is also obstruction to the opening of the glans; that disease is <s>niruddhamaṇi</s>.
A penis filled as if with bristles is called <s>grathita</s>; it is born of kapha.
Loss of tactile sensation arising from blood vitiated by bristles is known by that same name.
When the penis is covered everywhere with holes having tiny openings,
one should know it as <s>śataponaka</s>, caused by provocation of <s>vāta</s> and blood.
Suppuration of the skin from pitta and blood is <s>tvakpāka</s>, marked by fever and burning.
Suppuration of the flesh, caused by all the <s>doṣas</s>, has every kind of pain and destroys the flesh.
When the penis is afflicted by red and black blisters and pustules,

children.text: mehanaṃ vedanā cogrā taṃ vidyād asṛgarbudam ||
children.translated_text: with fierce pain, one should know that as <s>asṛgarbuda</s>.
<s>Māṃsārbuda</s> has been stated before, and <s>vidradhi</s> is caused by the three <s>doṣas</s>.
When the flesh has become black and disintegrates on every side,
being suppurated by the combined <s>doṣas</s>, one should know those as <s>tilakālaka</s>.
Of these, the flesh-born tumor, suppuration, abscess, and <s>tilakālaka</s>
are four that one should abandon; the remaining ones should be treated quickly.
Twenty disorders of the vagina arise from bad food,
from sleeping with the limbs in an uneven position, and from excessive sexual intercourse,
from corrupted menstrual blood, from mishaps, from defect in the seed, and from fate.
When <s>anila</s>, aggravated in the vagina, produces pain, pricking, constriction, and numbness,
a sensation as if ants were crawling, stiffness, roughness, and sound,
and a discharge of menstrual blood that is foamy, reddish, black, scanty, thin, and dry,

children.text: sraṃsaṃ vaṅkṣaṇapārśvādau vyathāṃ gulmaṃ krameṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: as well as prolapse, pain in the groin, side, and other places, and then a <s>gulma</s>,

children.text: tāṃstāṃśca svān gadān vyāpad vātikī nāma sā smṛtā
children.translated_text: and its various own disorders, that disorder is known as the <s>vātikī</s> type.
That same condition, when accompanied by swelling, arises from excessive walking and excessive intercourse.
Because of intercourse with a girl who is too young, <s>vāyu</s>, causing pain in the back, shanks, thighs, and groins,

children.text: rujan saṃdūṣayed yoniṃ vāyuḥ prākcaraṇeti sā ||
children.translated_text: vitiates the <s>yoni</s> (female generative tract); that is called <s>prākcaraṇā</s>.
From the upward reversal of natural urges, <s>māruta</s> (vāta-wind) presses upon the <s>yoni</s>.

children.text: sā phenilaṃ rajaḥ kṛcchrād udāvṛttaṃ vimuñcati ||
children.translated_text: She discharges foamy menstrual blood with difficulty, turned upward; this disorder is <s>udāvṛttā</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ vyāpad udāvṛttā jātaghnī tu yadānilaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>jātaghnī</s> is when <s>anila</s> (vāta-wind),

children.text: jātaṃ jātaṃ sutaṃ hanti raukṣyād duṣṭārtavodbhavam ||
children.translated_text: because of dryness, destroys each child as soon as it is born, the child having arisen from corrupted menstrual blood.
In a woman who has overeaten and has an irregular posture during intercourse, <s>marut</s>,
compressed by food and situated in the channel of the <s>yoni</s>, bends its mouth.
That condition, in which the mouth with bone and flesh is turned inward and is very painful, is <s>antarmukhī</s>.
In the womb of a woman who consumes vāta-provoking food, aggravated <s>anila</s>

children.text: striyo yonim aṇudvārāṃ kuryāt sūcīmukhīti sā
children.translated_text: makes the woman's <s>yoni</s> have a minute opening; that is <s>sūcīmukhī</s>.
Because of suppression of urges during menstruation, deranged <s>vāyu</s>

children.text: karoti yoneḥ śoṣaṃ ca śuṣkākhyā sātivedanā
children.translated_text: causes retention of feces and urine and drying of the <s>yoni</s>; this is called <s>śuṣkā</s> and is very painful.

children.text: ṣaḍahāt saptarātrād vā śukraṃ garbhāśayān marut ||
children.translated_text: When, after six days or seven nights, <s>marut</s>

children.text: vamet saruṅ nīrujo vā yasyāḥ sā vāminī matā
children.translated_text: expels semen from the uterus, with or without pain, that condition is regarded as <s>vāminī</s>.
When the <s>yoni</s> is afflicted by <s>vāta</s>, from a defect of the male seed in pregnancy with a female fetus,
she becomes man-hating and breastless; this is called <s>ṣaṇḍhā</s> and is not amenable to treatment.

children.text: duṣṭo viṣṭabhya yonyāsyaṃ garbhakoṣṭhaṃ ca mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Deranged <s>māruta</s>, obstructing the mouth of the <s>yoni</s> and the womb-cavity,

children.text: kurute vivṛtāṃ srastāṃ vātikīm iva duḥkhitām
children.translated_text: makes it opened out, prolapsed, and painful like a vāta disorder.
They call that <s>mahāyoni</s>, with protruding flesh and great pain.

children.text: yathāsvair dūṣaṇair duṣṭaṃ pittaṃ yonim upāśritam
children.translated_text: Pitta, deranged by its own respective aggravating factors and lodged in the <s>yoni</s>,
makes it accompanied by burning, suppuration, heat, foul odor, and fever,
and with menstrual flow that is intensely hot, abundant, corpse-smelling, blue, yellow, and black.
That disorder is pittic; it is called <s>raktayoni</s> because of excessive blood-flow.
Kapha, angered by things that cause discharge and obstruction, makes the <s>yoni</s> painless,
cold, itchy, pale, slimy, and discharging fluid of that same kind.
That disorder is phlegmatic. When menstrual blood is diminished by <s>vāta</s> and pitta,
with burning, emaciation, and discoloration, that condition is <s>lohitakṣayā</s>.
In a woman of pittic constitution, through intercourse with a man and from holding back sneezing and belching,
the <s>yoni</s> becomes vitiated by <s>marut</s> joined with pitta.
It is swollen, unable to bear touch, painful, and flowing with blue and yellow blood,
causing heaviness of the bladder and abdomen, diarrhea, and anorexia.
It produces pain in the hips and groins, thirst, and fever; that is <s>pariplutā</s>.
A <s>yoni</s> pervaded by diseases of <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> flows with white, slimy discharge.
It is remembered as <s>upaplutā</s>; but the one called <s>viplutā</s> arises from not washing.
It develops worms, is itchy, and through itching becomes excessively fond of intercourse.
From untimely bearing down, <s>vāyu</s>, combined with <s>śleṣman</s> and blood,
produces in the <s>yoni</s> a fleshy growth that blocks the path of menstruation.
That is <s>karṇinī</s>. A disorder produced by the three <s>doṣa</s>s lodged in the <s>yoni</s> and uterus,
causing complications according to each of their own natures, is <s>sāṃnipātikī</s>.

children.text: iti yonigadā nārī yaiḥ śukraṃ na pratīcchati
children.translated_text: These are the diseases of the <s>yoni</s> by which a woman does not receive semen.

children.text: tato garbhaṃ na gṛhṇāti rogāṃścāpnoti dāruṇān
children.translated_text: Therefore she does not conceive and obtains terrible diseases,
such as excessive uterine bleeding, piles, and abdominal tumors, and afflictions caused by <s>anila</s> and the other doṣas.
Now, then, we shall explain the treatment of diseases of the private parts.
Thus indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
In a newly arisen <s>upadaṃśa</s> (genital ulcer), one should pierce a vein in the middle of the penis,

children.text: śītāṃ kuryāt kriyāṃ śuddhiṃ virekeṇa viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: apply cooling treatment, and especially cleanse by purgation.
When it is mature and has been incised, a plaster should be made with sesame paste, ghee, and honey.
One should boil in water shoots of jambu, mango, sumanas, nīpa, and white kāmbojikā,
as well as bark produced from śallakī, badarī, bilva, palāśa, and tiniśa,

children.text: tvacaḥ kṣīridrumāṇāṃ ca triphalāṃ ca pacej jale ||
children.translated_text: and the milky trees, together with <s>triphala</s>.

children.text: sa kvāthaḥ kṣālanaṃ tena pakvaṃ tailaṃ ca ropaṇam
children.translated_text: That decoction is for washing; oil cooked with it is healing.
A plaster made of finely powdered tuttha, gairika, lodhra, elā, manohvā, rasāñjana,
hareṇu, puṣpakāsīsa, saurāṣṭrī, and excellent salt,
mixed with honey, removes sores of <s>upadaṃśa</s>.

children.text: kapāle triphalā dagdhā saghṛtā ropaṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: <s>Triphala</s> burned in an earthen saucer and mixed with ghee is the best healing agent.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ sādhanam idaṃ pratidoṣaṃ tu śophavat ||
children.translated_text: This is the general treatment; according to each doṣa it should be as for swelling.

children.text: na ca yāti yathā pākaṃ prayateta tathā bhṛśam
children.translated_text: One should strive vigorously so that it does not go on to suppuration.

children.text: pakvaiḥ snāyusirāmāṃsaiḥ prāyo naśyati hi dhvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For when the sinews, vessels, and flesh have suppurated, the penis is generally destroyed.
For piles that have been cut or cauterized, the treatment should be as for <s>upadaṃśa</s>.
Mustard seeds, ground with fine astringent decoctions, should be sprinkled on.
With those same decoctions one should prepare an anointing oil that heals wounds.
This treatment also applies in <s>avamantha</s>; in both conditions blood should likewise be let.

children.text: kumbhīkāyāṃ hared raktaṃ pakvāyāṃ śodhite vraṇe
children.translated_text: In <s>kumbhīkā</s>, one should remove blood; when it is mature, in the cleansed wound,
a plaster with tinduka, triphala, and lodhra, and oil, are healing.
In <s>alajī</s>, when blood is flowing, this same course of treatment applies.
But the pustule called <s>uttamā</s> should be cut open and drawn out with a hook.
It should be treated with pastes and powders of astringent drugs mixed with honey.
The procedure prescribed for pittic <s>visarpa</s> is beneficial for <s>puṣkara</s> and <s>vyūḍha</s>.
In cooking of the skin and loss of sensation, one should again sprinkle with the crushed preparation,
and apply warm <s>balātaila</s> and poultices with sweet substances.
For <s>aṣṭhīlikā</s>, after drawing blood, one should treat it like a phlegmatic glandular swelling.
A retracted foreskin should be anointed with ghee, fomented, and poulticed.
For three nights or five nights, with well-unctuous <s>śālvaṇa</s> and similar poultices,

children.text: svedayitvā tato bhūyaḥ snigdhaṃ carma samānayet ||
children.translated_text: after fomenting it, one should then again restore the lubricated skin to its proper place.
Gently pressing the glans; when it has entered, a poultice is to be applied.

children.text: maṇau punaḥ punaḥ snigdhaṃ bhojanaṃ cātra śasyate ||
children.translated_text: In the glans, too, repeated unctuous food is recommended here.

children.text: ayam eva prayojyaḥ syād avapāṭyām api kramaḥ
children.translated_text: This very procedure should also be applied in <s>avapāṭikā</s>.
When the passage is obstructed, one should take a tube open at both ends, passed through with lac,
anoint it with oil, place it in the channel, and irrigate with oils that remove disturbance by vāta.

children.text: tryahāt tryahāt sthūlatarāṃ nyasya nāḍīṃ vivardhayet ||
children.translated_text: Every third day one should insert a thicker tube and gradually enlarge it.

children.text: srotodvāram asiddhau tu vidvān śastreṇa pāṭayet
children.translated_text: But if the opening of the channel is not achieved, a skilled physician should split it with a knife.
Avoiding the seam, he should then apply the procedure for a fresh wound.
When a knotty lesion has been fomented, one should poultice it with unctuous and warm applications through a tube.
After scraping <s>śataponaka</s>, one should smear it with astringent decoctions mixed with honey.
In a bloody tumor, treatment should be carried out as for a blood-born abscess.
In all of them one should apply wound care according to the condition.
In disorders of the female genital tract, measures that conquer vāta are mostly recommended.
Oleation, fomentation, enemas, and the like are especially indicated in those caused by vāta.

children.text: na hi vātād ṛte yonir vanitānāṃ praduṣyati
children.translated_text: For a woman's genital tract is not deranged without vāta.

children.text: ato jitvā tam anyasya kuryād doṣasya bheṣajam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after conquering it, one should perform the remedy for the other doṣa.
One should give <s>balātaila</s>, <s>miśraka</s>, or <s>sukumāraka</s> to drink.

children.text: snigdhasvinnāṃ tathā yoniṃ duḥsthitāṃ sthāpayet samām ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, after oleating and fomenting her, one should set a malpositioned genital tract straight.
One should bend a crooked one by hand; and one should pierce one that is closed.
One should put back one that has come out, and turn around one that is opened out.

children.text: sthānāpavṛttā yonir hi śalyabhūtā striyo matā
children.translated_text: For a female genital tract displaced from its position is considered like a foreign body for a woman.
One should subject the woman to mild procedures such as emesis and the rest.
When she has been well purified on all sides, the remaining treatment is prescribed:
enema, massage, sprinkling, paste, and the retention of a tampon.
One should cook, from ghee, one <s>prastha</s> with one <s>akṣa</s> each of kāśmarya, triphalā, grapes, kāsamarda, the two niśās,
guḍūcī, sairyaka, abhīru, śukanāsā, and punarnavā,
and also parūṣaka.
When drunk, that is supreme for giving conception and destroys vāta disorders of the female genital tract.
Vacā, upakuñcikā, ajājī, kṛṣṇā, vṛṣaka, and rock salt,
together with ajamodā, alkali of barley, sugar, and citraka,
should be ground, stirred with clear wine, fried in ghee, and eaten.
It is for removing pain in the genital tract and flanks, heart disease, abdominal masses, and hemorrhoids.
One should drink vṛṣaka, roots of citron, madayantikā,
and also kṛṣṇā and upakuñcikā with salted wines.
Milk boiled with rāsnā, śvadaṃṣṭrā, and vṛṣaka removes colic.
Sprinkling should be done with decoctions of guḍūcī, triphalā, and dantī.
A tampon prepared from oil with nata, vārtākinī, kuṣṭha, rock salt, and devadāru
should be kept in the genital tract; it removes pain.
For genital tracts of a pitta nature, sprinkling, massage, and tampon procedures

children.text: śītāḥ pittajitaḥ kāryāḥ snehanārthaṃ ghṛtāni ca ||
children.translated_text: should be cooling and should conquer pitta; and ghees should be used for oleation.
From four <s>tulās</s> of śatāvarī root, pounded and pressed,
one should cook one <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee with its juice and an equal amount of milk.
With life-promoting herbs, śatāvarī, raisins, parūṣaka,
and priyāla, ground in one-<s>akṣa</s> portions, together with the two balās and madhuka,
when it has been cooked and cooled, one should add eight <s>palas</s> each of honey and pippalī,
and ten <s>palas</s> of sugar; then one should lick a tampon-sized dose.
It destroys disorders of menstrual blood and semen, is virilizing, and is supreme for begetting a male child.

children.text: kṣataṃ kṣayam asṛkpittaṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ halīmakam ||
children.translated_text: It removes injury, wasting, bleeding disorders, cough, dyspnea, and chlorosis,
jaundice, vātarakta, erysipelas, seizure of the heart and head,
epilepsy, facial paralysis, stiffness, intoxication, and insanity.
In the same way, milk and ghee prepared with life-promoting herbs

children.text: garbhadaṃ pittajānāṃ ca rogāṇāṃ paramaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: are conception-giving and supremely beneficial for diseases born of pitta.
In a decoction of two <s>droṇas</s> of balā, one should cook an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee and oil,
with four times as much milk, together with kṛṣṇā, kākanāsā, and sugar,
and with jīvantī, kṣīrakākolī, sthirā, vīrā, ṛddhi, and jīvaka,
payasyā, śrāvaṇī, mudgaparṇī, pīluparṇī, and māṣaparṇī.

children.text: vātapittāmayān hatvā pānād garbhaṃ dadhāti tat
children.translated_text: When drunk, that overcomes diseases of vāta and pitta and causes conception.
In a bloody disorder of the genital tract, after observing the associated factors by the color of the blood
one should apply blood-stanching medicine according to the rise of the doṣa.
Pāṭhā, the stones of jambu and mango, śilodbheda, rasāñjana,
ambaṣṭhā, śālmalī gum, samaṅgā, bark of vatsaka,
saffron, bilva, ativiṣā, lodhra, toyada, and gairika,
dry ginger, madhūka, mācīka, red sandalwood, and kaṭphala,
kaṭvaṅga, vatsaka, anantā, dhātakī, madhuka, and arjuna:
having collected them under the Puṣya constellation, powdered them, and mixed them with honey,
one should drink them with rice-water for hemorrhoids, diarrhea, and blood that is passed downward.

children.text: doṣā jantukṛtā ye ca bālānāṃ tāṃśca nāśayet
children.translated_text: It also destroys doṣas produced by parasites, and those of children.
This powder, called <s>Puṣyānuga</s>, is beneficial for disorders of the genital tract and of menstruation, whether dark, white, red, or black,
and is honored by <s>Ātreya</s>.
When the genital tract is corrupted by phlegm, every medicine should be dry and hot.
With dhātakī, āmalakī leaves, srotoja, madhuka, and utpala,
jambu, mango heartwood, kāsīsa, lodhra, kaṭphala, and tinduka,
saurāṣṭrikā, pomegranate bark, and unripe udumbara fruit,
one <s>akṣa</s> each, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of oil in goat urine and twice as much milk.
That should be used for massage, tampons, and enemas.

children.text: tena śūnonnatā stabdhā picchilā srāviṇī tathā ||
children.translated_text: By it a swollen, raised, rigid, slimy, and discharging genital tract,
whether disordered or further afflicted, with blisters and pain, becomes cured.

children.text: yavānnam abhayāriṣṭaṃ sīdhu tailaṃ ca śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: One should habitually use food made of barley, <s>abhayāriṣṭa</s>, <s>sīdhu</s>, and oil.
also the powder of the two <s>pippalī</s> plants, and courses of <s>pathyā</s> mixed with honey;
<s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, the stones of mango and rose-apple, and <s>dhātakī</s>:
in sliminess, this powder, combined with honey, produces cleansing clarity.
<s>palāśa</s>, <s>dhātakī</s>, rose-apple, <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>moca</s>, and <s>sarja</s> resin:
in foul smell, sliminess, and moist discharge, this powder is considered a checking astringent.
A decoction of the group beginning with <s>āragvadha</s> is used for sprinkling and washing.
For those that are stiff and rough, a softening treatment should be performed.
One should apply and retain <s>vesavāra</s>, <s>kṛśarā</s>, and <s>pāyasa</s>.

children.text: durgandhānāṃ kaṣāyaḥ syāt tailaṃ vā kalka eva vā
children.translated_text: For those that are foul-smelling, there should be a decoction, or an oil, or else a paste.
Or a powder of all fragrant substances removes the putrid smell.
For conditions dominated by <s>śleṣman</s>, enemas mostly pungent and mixed with urine are beneficial.
For <s>pitta</s>, they should be mixed with <s>madhuka</s> and milk; for <s>vāta</s>, with oil and sour substances.
For disorders arising from the combined <s>doṣas</s>, a common combined treatment is beneficial.

children.text: evaṃ yoniṣu śuddhāsu garbhaṃ vindanti yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the womb-channels have thus been purified, women obtain conception.
When the seed is uncorrupted and natural, and the beginning of life is present,
the semen of the man too, purified by the five cleansing procedures,
should be examined by the colors of the <s>doṣas</s>; if corrupted, it should be treated by measures that counteract them.
<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, sugar, and <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: dve niśe madhukaṃ medāṃ dīpyakaṃ kaṭurohiṇīm
children.translated_text: the two <s>niśā</s> plants, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>dīpyaka</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>,
<s>payasyā</s>, asafoetida, <s>kākolī</s>, <s>vājigandhā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>:
grinding these in equal one-<s>akṣa</s> portions, one should cook a <s>prastha</s> of ghee with four times as much milk.
That is praised in all disorders of the womb-channel and semen.

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ medhyaṃ dhanyaṃ puṃsavanaṃ param
children.translated_text: It promotes life, nourishment, intelligence, and good fortune, and is the supreme <s>puṃsavana</s> preparation.

children.text: phalasarpiriti khyātaṃ puṣpe pītaṃ phalāya yat ||
children.translated_text: It is known as <s>phalasarpis</s>; when drunk at the menstrual period, it is for obtaining offspring.
It is honored for pregnant women and for women whose offspring die.

children.text: etat paraṃ ca bālānāṃ grahaghnaṃ dehavardhanam ||
children.translated_text: It is also supreme for children, dispelling <s>grahas</s> and increasing the body.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the prevention and treatment of poison.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
When the ocean was being churned by the gods and asuras for the sake of nectar,
before the production of nectar there was born a man terrible to behold,
blazing with splendor, four-fanged, tawny-haired, and fire-eyed.

children.text: jagad viṣaṇṇaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā tenāsau viṣasaṃjñitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the world was despondent; because of that he was given the name <s>viṣa</s>, poison.
Being checked by <s>Brahmā</s> with the syllable huṃ, he then entered forms both stationary and moving.
He took up his own form there, abandoning the deceptive form.

children.text: sthiram ityulbaṇaṃ vīrye yat kandeṣu pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: That which is stable, terribly strong in potency, and lodged in bulbs and roots
is such as <s>kālakūṭa</s>, <s>indravatsa</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>hālāhala</s>, and the like.
In the fangs of snakes, spiders, and the like there is the dreadful moving poison.

children.text: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ceti viṣaṃ proktam akṛtrimam ||
children.translated_text: Poison is said to be natural when it is either stationary or moving.
But the artificial poison called <s>gara</s> is made with various drugs.
According to the force of its combination, it kills quickly, after a long time, or after a very long time.
Or it causes swelling, pallor, abdominal enlargement, madness, piles, and other disorders.
Poison is sharp, hot, dry, clear, pervasive, quick-acting, and light;
it is diffusive, subtle, of indistinct taste, and irregular in digestion.
It is the opposite of <s>ojas</s>, being endowed with qualities such as sharpness.
Predominated by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, it immediately takes away the life of human beings.

children.text: viṣaṃ hi dehaṃ samprāpya prāg dūṣayati śoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: For poison, having entered the body, first corrupts the blood,
and then equally the <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>anila</s>, together with their seats.
Then, taking hold of the heart, it becomes capable of cutting off the body.
When stationary poison has been consumed, in the first stage there arise

children.text: jihvāyāḥ śyāvatā stambho mūrchā trāsaḥ klamo vamiḥ ||
children.translated_text: blackening of the tongue, stiffness, fainting, terror, exhaustion, and vomiting.

children.text: dvitīye vepathuḥ svedo dāhaḥ kaṇṭhe ca vedanā
children.translated_text: In the second, there are trembling, sweating, burning, and pain in the throat;

children.text: viṣaṃ cāmāśayaṃ prāptaṃ kurute hṛdi vedanām ||
children.translated_text: the poison, having reached the stomach, produces pain in the heart.
In the third, there is dryness of the palate and severe colic in the stomach;

children.text: durbale harite śūne jāyete cāsya locane ||
children.translated_text: his eyes become weak, greenish, and swollen.
When it has gone to the colon, there are piercing pains, hiccup, cough, and rumbling of the bowels.
In the fourth stage there is also excessive heaviness of the head.
In the fifth, there are flow of phlegm, discoloration, and splitting pain in the joints;
there is aggravation of all the <s>doṣas</s> and pain in the lower digestive tract.
In the sixth there is loss of consciousness, and he has extremely severe diarrhea.
Breaking pain in the shoulders, back, and waist occurs, and death comes in the seventh.
In the first stage of poisoning, after the patient has vomited and been sprinkled with cold water,
one should quickly give an <s>agada</s> antidote mixed with ghee and honey.
In the second, as before, after vomiting and purging, one should make him drink a follow-up potion.
In the third, drinking an <s>agada</s> is beneficial, and so are nasal therapy and collyrium.
In the fourth, one should apply an <s>agada</s> joined with unctuous substance.
In the fifth, a decoction of <s>madhuka</s> mixed with honey is beneficial.
In the sixth, treatment is as in diarrhea; in the seventh, there should be forceful nasal medication.

children.text: mūrdhni kākapadaṃ kṛtvā sāsṛg vā piśitaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Making a crow's-foot incision on the head, one should place flesh there, or flesh together with blood.
<s>kośātakī</s>, <s>agnika</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>sūryavallī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>,
<s>śelu</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>kiṇihī</s>, the two <s>haridrā</s> plants, and the plant called <s>kṣaudra</s>,
the two <s>punarnavā</s> plants, <s>trikaṭu</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants, <s>śārivā</s>, and <s>balā</s>:
from the decoction of these, one should use a cold gruel with ghee and honey.
Between the stages, after the proper procedure has been done, it destroys all poisons.
Likewise, with <s>madhūka</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, lotus filaments, and sandalwood,
<s>añjana</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, yellow orpiment, and realgar,
<s>phalinī</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>nāgapuṣpa</s> together with its filaments,
<s>hareṇu</s>, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, and <s>kākamālikā</s>,
<s>śrīveṣṭaka</s>, <s>sarja</s> resin, <s>śatāhvā</s>, saffron, and <s>balā</s>.
<s>Tamāla</s> leaves, <s>tālīśa</s>, <s>bhūrja</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and the two <s>niśā</s>s;
a fasting maiden, bathed and dressed in white, should prepare them with honey and melted ghee.

children.text: dvijān abhyarcya taiḥ puṣye kalpayed agadottamam
children.translated_text: After honoring the twice-born, on the <s>Puṣya</s> day, she should prepare with these the best <s>agada</s> (antidote).

children.text: vaidyaścātra tadā mantraṃ prayatātmā paṭhed imam ||
children.translated_text: Then the physician, self-controlled, should recite this mantra over it:
Homage to the Man-lion; homage also to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Just as he knows no defeat of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in battle,
by this true utterance may my <s>agada</s> be accomplished.

children.text: namo vaiḍūryamāte hulu hulu rakṣa māṃ sarvaviṣebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Vaiḍūryamātā</s>; hulu hulu, protect me from all poisons.
<s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Cāṇḍālī</s>, <s>Mātaṅgī</s>: svāhā.

children.text: piṣṭe ca dvitīyo mantraḥ harimāyi svāhā ||
children.translated_text: And when it is being ground, a second mantra is: <s>Harimāyī</s>, svāhā.
Against all poisons, <s>vetāla</s>s, seizing spirits, sorcery, and evils,
and in dangers from deadly disease, famine, war, and lightning,
when used as a drink, nasal medicine, collyrium, paste, amulet-binding, and the like,
this preparation called <s>Candrodaya</s> is the supreme rite for appeasement and well-being.

children.text: jīrṇaṃ viṣaghnauṣadhibhir hataṃ vā dāvāgnivātātapaśoṣitaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Poison that is old, or has been overcome by anti-poison medicines, or dried by forest fire, wind, and sun,

children.text: svabhāvato vā na guṇaiḥ suyuktaṃ dūṣīviṣākhyāṃ viṣam abhyupaiti ||
children.translated_text: or by nature is not well furnished with its qualities, takes on the name <s>dūṣīviṣa</s> (latent poison).
Because its potency is slight, it is hard to discern, covered by <s>kapha</s>, and persists for years.
Afflicted by it, a person has altered stool color, diseased vitiated blood, thirst, and anorexia.

children.text: mūrchan vaman gadgadavāg vimuhyan bhavecca dūṣyodaraliṅgajuṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: He faints, vomits, speaks indistinctly, becomes confused, and may show signs of <s>dūṣyodara</s>.
When it is lodged in the stomach he has disorders of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; when lodged in the colon, disorders of <s>vāta</s> and pitta.

children.text: bhaven naro dhvastaśiroruhāṅgo vilūnapakṣaḥ sa yathā vihaṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: The man becomes one whose hair and limbs are ruined, like a bird with its wings shorn.

children.text: sthitaṃ rasādiṣvathavā vicitrān karoti dhātuprabhavān vikārān ||
children.translated_text: Or, settled in <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues, it produces various disorders arising from the bodily elements.
Aggravated by east wind, indigestion, cold clouds, daytime sleep, and unwholesome food,

children.text: duṣṭaṃ dūṣayate dhātūn ato dūṣīviṣaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: it vitiates the tissues; therefore it is remembered as <s>dūṣīviṣa</s>.
One afflicted by <s>dūṣīviṣa</s> should be well fomented and cleansed both upward and downward.
He should be given the <s>Dūṣīviṣāri</s> <s>agada</s>, moistened with honey, to lick.

children.text: pippalyo dhyāmakaṃ māṃsī lodhram elā suvarcikā
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>elā</s>, <s>suvarcikā</s>,
<s>kuṭannaṭa</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, sandalwood, and red ochre:
this is named <s>Dūṣīviṣāri</s>, and it is not forbidden even in other cases.
But one wounded by a poison-smeared weapon faints again and again.
He becomes discolored and quickly falls into despondency.
His body tingles as if covered with insects.
The joints of the hips, back, head, and shoulders become painful.
Black, vitiated blood flows out, and he has thirst, fainting, fever, and burning.
In a moment it causes clouding of vision, vomiting, dyspnea, and cough.
The wound has reddish-yellow edges, a dusky center, and excessive pain.

children.text: śūyate pacyate sadyo gatvā māṃsaṃ ca kṛṣṇatām
children.translated_text: It swells and suppurates at once, and when the poison has entered the flesh, it turns black.
Wet and decomposing, it repeatedly sloughs away with slimy discharge.
For one pierced in a non-vital spot, one should quickly perform protection of the heart.

children.text: śalyam ākṛṣya taptena lohenānu dahed vraṇam ||
children.translated_text: After drawing out the foreign body, one should cauterize the wound with heated iron.
Or one should rub it with alkali made from <s>muṣkaka</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>soma</s> bark, <s>tāmravallī</s>,
from <s>śirīṣa</s>, and from <s>gṛdhranakhī</s>.
One should apply a paste of the roots of <s>śukanāsā</s>, <s>prativiṣā</s>, and <s>vyāghrī</s>.
And one should carry out treatment for an insect bite as appropriate for him.
But when the flesh in the wound is putrid, the procedure is as for pittic <s>visarpa</s>.
Women, for the sake of good fortune with their husbands, or attendants incited by enemies against a king,
give <s>gara</s> mixed with food when they are close at hand.
A compound of parts and wastes from various creatures, incompatible medicines, ashes,

children.text: viṣāṇāṃ cālpavīryāṇāṃ yogo gara iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: and poisons of slight potency is remembered as <s>gara</s>.
By it a person becomes pale, emaciated, weak in digestion, and afflicted by cough, dyspnea, and fever.
With <s>vāyu</s> moving in reverse, he becomes absorbed in dreams and anxious thoughts.
He has great abdominal enlargement, diseased liver and spleen, weak speech, debility, and lassitude.
He is swollen, constantly distended, dry in hands and feet, and consumptive.
In dreams he generally sees jackals, cats, mongooses, snakes, and monkeys,
and also dried-up trees and reservoirs.

children.text: manyate kṛṣṇam ātmānaṃ gauro gauraṃ ca kālakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A fair man thinks himself dark, and a dark man thinks himself fair.
With his senses impaired, he may see his ears, nose, and eyes as distorted.
Afflicted by these and by many other terrible complications,
a person suffering from <s>gara</s> comes to destruction; some die at once if untreated.

children.text: garārto vāntavān bhuktvā tat pathyaṃ pānabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: A person suffering from <s>gara</s>, after eating and vomiting, should take suitable drink and food.
With his stomach purified, he should regularly use gold, remembering the rule from the <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>.
A powder of <s>tāpya</s> and gold, combined with sugar and honey,
as an electuary, pacifies severe poison produced by all kinds of combinations.
<s>Mūrvā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>cavya</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
as well as <s>vacā</s>, <s>musta</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, should be taken with buttermilk, warm water, or whey.
Or the person whose digestive fire has been harmed by <s>gara</s> should drink them with a sour juice.
A cold preparation boiled with pigeon meat, <s>śaṭhī</s>, and what is called <s>puṣkara</s>
removes thirst, pain, cough, dyspnea, hiccup, and fever caused by <s>gara</s>.
When poison combines with constitution, time, food, doṣa, vulnerable tissues, and the like,
a poison crisis is declared; here only one in a hundred survives.
Poison is increased by hunger, thirst, heat, weakness, anger, grief, fear, and exertion,
by indigestion, looseness of stool, burning, and increases of pitta and <s>māruta</s>.
It is increased by smelling sesame flowers and fruits, by earth-vapor, and by the rumbling of clouds,
by the sounds of elephants, mice, and musical instruments, in poison crises,
and by east wind, the fragrance of lotuses, and intoxicants that excite it.
In the rainy season too, because water is its source, it becomes moist and dissolved like molasses.

children.text: visarpati ghanāpāye tad agastyo hinasti ca
children.translated_text: When the mass of clouds has passed away, it spreads; but <s>Agastya</s> destroys it.
Therefore, at the end of the rainy season, poison becomes weak in potency.
Thus, having carefully considered with intelligence the strength and weakness of constitution, habituation, season, place, impulse, and force,
one should carry out the subsequent procedure.
One should pacify phlegmatic poison with emetics and with warm, dry, sharp applications,
and with foods that are astringent, pungent, and bitter.
One should pacify pittic poison with purgatives, sprinklings, and applications that are very cooling,
and with foods that are astringent, bitter, and sweet, and mixed with ghee.
One should conquer poison of the nature of <s>vāta</s> with sweet, unctuous, sour, and salty things,
with foods and applications containing ghee, and likewise with meat-foods.

children.text: nāghṛtaṃ sraṃsanaṃ śastaṃ pralepo bhojyam auṣadham
children.translated_text: A purgative without ghee is not praised; nor are an application, food, or medicine without it.
For all poisons and in all conditions, nothing exists equal to ghee.
There is no medicine at all like it, especially when <s>anila</s> is strong.
Poison lodged in the seat of <s>śleṣman</s> is curable without effort; that lodged in the seat of pitta with effort;
poison that has gone to the seat of <s>vāta</s> is very difficult to cure, or incurable.
Now, then, we shall explain the counteraction of snake poison.
Thus indeed said the great sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
Serpents are hooded, ring-marked, and streaked;

children.text: tridhā samāsato bhaumā bhidyante te tvanekadhā ||
children.translated_text: in summary, terrestrial snakes are divided threefold, though in detail they are of many kinds.
They are not described at length by distinctions of birth, since that is of no practical use.
The poisons of the hooded snakes and the others are, respectively, especially dry and pungent, sour and hot, and sweet and cooling,
and they aggravate <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣa</s>s in order.
In youth, middle age, and old age, and during rain, cold, and heat,
these become predominant in poison; the mixed types do so at the junctions of the seasons.
Those bearing marks of a wheel, plough, umbrella, svastika, or goad,
hooded and swift-moving, are remembered as hooded snakes.
Ring-marked snakes should be known as broad-bodied, marked with various circles;
they are tall and slow-moving. The streaked snakes are marked with streaks,
smooth and of varied colors, painted both crosswise and upward.
The gaudhera, offspring of the monitor lizard, is equal to hooded snakes in poison.

children.text: catuṣpād vyantarān vidyād eteṣām eva saṃkarāt ||
children.translated_text: One should know the four-footed mixed types as arising from the intermingling of these very snakes.
For they have mixed characteristics and provoke a combined aggravation of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
Snakes bite for food, from fear, from the touch of the foot, from excessive poison, from anger,
from evil disposition, from enmity, or at the urging of gods, seers, or <s>Yama</s>.
Among these causes, the excess of poison is said to increase in the order just stated.
Having understood the cause from the indication, one should counteract it appropriately.
Because of its evil nature, a mixed snake stays occupying a path.
Where only wetness from saliva is seen on the body,

children.text: na tu daṃṣṭrākṛtaṃ daṃśaṃ tat tuṇḍāhatam ādiśet ||
children.translated_text: but no bite made by fangs, that should be diagnosed as a blow from the mouth.

children.text: ekaṃ daṃṣṭrāpadaṃ dve vā vyālīḍhākhyam aśoṇitam
children.translated_text: One fang-mark, or two without blood, is called licked by a snake;

children.text: daṃṣṭrāpade sarakte dve vyāluptaṃ trīṇi tāni tu ||
children.translated_text: two fang-marks with blood are torn by a snake, while three such marks,
with cut flesh and a continuous flow of blood, are a bite.
Four fang-marks are likewise a bitten-and-crushed wound.

children.text: nirviṣaṃ dvayam atrādyam asādhyaṃ paścimaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: Of these, the first two are without poison; the last should be declared incurable.

children.text: viṣaṃ nāheyam aprāpya raktaṃ dūṣayate vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Poison, when not to be discarded and when it has reached the blood, vitiates the body.

children.text: raktam aṇvapi tu prāptaṃ vardhate tailam ambuvat
children.translated_text: But when it has reached even a minute amount of blood, it increases like oil on water.
In a timid person, from contact with a snake, <s>anila</s>, aggravated by fear,

children.text: kadācit kurute śophaṃ sarpāṅgābhihataṃ tu tat
children.translated_text: may sometimes produce swelling; that is an injury from the body of a snake.
When someone has been pierced in a difficult dark place and suspects being bitten by something,

children.text: viṣodvego jvaraśchardir mūrchā dāho 'pi vā bhavet
children.translated_text: agitation over poison, fever, vomiting, fainting, or burning may occur,
or weariness, delusion, or diarrhea; that is called suspected poison.
A poisonous bite pricks and is accompanied by itching, swelling, and pain;
it burns and is somewhat indurated. A bite opposite in character is without poison.
In the first impulse of a hooded-snake bite, the vitiated blood becomes dusky.

children.text: śyāvatā tena vaktrādau sarpantīva ca kīṭakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that duskiness, insects seem to crawl about on the face and elsewhere.

children.text: dvitīye granthayo vege tṛtīye mūrdhni gauravam
children.translated_text: In the second impulse there are glandular swellings; in the third, heaviness in the head,
obstruction of vision, and wetness of the bite; in the fourth, spitting and vomiting;
in the fifth, loosening of the joints, drowsiness, and breaking pain in the joints;

children.text: dāho hidhmā ca ṣaṣṭhe tu hṛtpīḍā gātragauravam ||
children.translated_text: in the sixth, burning and hiccup, pain in the heart-region, and heaviness of the limbs;
and, when it has reached the semen in the seventh, fainting, indigestion, and diarrhea,
breaking pain of the shoulders, back, and waist, and cessation of all activity.
Now, in one bitten by a ring-marked snake, the vitiated blood turns yellow.
Because of it there is yellowness of the limbs and burning; in the second impulse swelling arises.
In the third, wetness of the bite, sweating, and thirst are produced.
In the fourth he becomes feverish, and in the fifth there is burning throughout the whole body.

children.text: daṣṭasya rājilair duṣṭaṃ pāṇḍutāṃ yāti śoṇitam
children.translated_text: In a person bitten by streaked snakes, the vitiated blood becomes pale.

children.text: pāṇḍutā tena gātrāṇāṃ dvitīye gurutāti ca ||
children.translated_text: Because of it there is pallor of the limbs, and in the second impulse heaviness too.
In the third there is wetness of the bite and discharge from the nose, eyes, and mouth.
In the fourth there is heaviness of the head, and stiffness of the neck in the fifth.

children.text: gātrabhaṅgo jvaraḥ śītaḥ śeṣayoḥ pūrvavad vadet
children.translated_text: Breaking pain of the limbs, fever, and cold occur; for the remaining two impulses one should state the symptoms as before.

children.text: kuryāt pañcasu vegeṣu cikitsāṃ na tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: One should undertake treatment in the first five impulses, but not after that.
Snakes that are flooded with water, exhausted by mating, frightened, overcome by a mongoose,
afflicted by cold, wind, heat, disease, hunger, thirst, or fatigue,
that have quickly come from another region, or have shed their venomous slough,
and those that move through a forest as if through kuśa grass, herbs, and thorns,
as well as those inhabiting a place occupied by divine beings, are considered to have little poison.
One should abandon a person bitten at a cremation ground, funeral pyre, shrine, and the like, on the fifth lunar day or at the junctions of the lunar fortnights,
at the twilight of the eighth or ninth lunar day, at midnight, or during the day,
under the southern, fiery, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, former, or <s>Nairṛta</s> asterisms,

children.text: nairṛtākhye muhūrte ca daṣṭaṃ marmasu ca tyajet
children.translated_text: and also in the muhūrta called <s>Nairṛta</s>, and when bitten in vital spots.
Immediately after being bitten, if his mouth and eyes become white and his hair falls out,

children.text: stabdhajihvo muhur mūrchan śītocchvāso na jīvati
children.translated_text: if his tongue is rigid, he repeatedly faints, and his breath is cold, he does not live.

children.text: hidhmā śvāso vamiḥ kāso daṣṭamātrasya dehinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If hiccup, dyspnea, vomiting, and cough arise all at once in the bitten person

children.text: jāyante yugapad yasya sa hṛcchūlī na jīvati
children.translated_text: as soon as he is bitten, and he has pain in the heart, he does not live.
If he vomits foam, is unconscious, and his feet, hands, and face are dark,
with collapse of the nose, breaking pain in the limbs, looseness of stool, and slack joints,
these signs occur in one who has drunk poison, has been bitten, or has been struck with a poisoned weapon
when the end of life has arrived.

children.text: na nasyaiścetanā tīkṣṇair na kṣatāt kṣatajāgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If consciousness does not return even with sharp nasal medicines, if blood does not flow from a wound,
or if no mark appears on one struck with a staff, he has gone to <s>Yama</s>'s realm.
But otherwise, with the speed one would use in a burning house, the physician

children.text: rakṣan kaṇṭhagatān prāṇān viṣam āśu śamaṃ nayet
children.translated_text: should protect the breaths that have reached the throat and quickly bring the poison to pacification.

children.text: mātrāśataṃ viṣaṃ sthitvā daṃśe daṣṭasya dehinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After remaining in the bite for one hundred <s>mātrās</s>, the poison of a bitten person
moves through the body, corrupting the blood and the other bodily constituents.
In that interval one should quickly perform such measures as cutting out the bite,

children.text: kuryācchīghraṃ yathā dehe viṣavallī na rohati
children.translated_text: so that the poison-creeper does not take root in the body.

children.text: daṣṭamātro daśed āśu tam eva pavanāśinam ||
children.translated_text: As soon as he is bitten, he should quickly bite that very wind-destroying agent,

children.text: loṣṭaṃ mahīṃ vā daśanaiśchittvā cānu sasaṃbhramam
children.translated_text: or cut a clod or the earth with his teeth, and then, in agitation,
smear the bite thoroughly with saliva or with earwax.
Above the bite, four finger-breadths away, he should bind a protective band
with linen and the like, with a braid, and with perfected mantras, if he knows mantras.
Poison is stopped by a bandage as water is stopped by a dam,
and his veins, compressed by the binding, do not carry the poison onward.
After squeezing it, he should extract the bite, except when it lies in a vital spot or joint.

children.text: na jāyate viṣād vego bījanāśād ivāṅkuraḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the destruction of the seed, the surge of poison does not arise, just as a sprout does not arise.
Except for bites of <s>maṇḍalin</s> snakes, because they are pitta-dominant, the other bite
should quickly be cauterized with heated gold, iron, and the like, or with a firebrand.

children.text: karoti bhasmasāt sadyo vahniḥ kiṃ nāma tu kṣatam
children.translated_text: Fire at once reduces things to ash; how much more, then, a wound.
Or one should suck it out with the mouth filled with earth, ash, antidote, or cow dung,
especially from a fleshy part when there is no contrary fatal sign from shade and reflection.

children.text: aṅgaṃ sahaiva daṃśena lepayed agadair muhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should repeatedly smear the limb together with the bite with antidotes,
and sprinkle it with water mixed with sandalwood and <s>uśīra</s>.

children.text: viṣe pravisṛte vidhyet sirāṃ sā paramā kriyā ||
children.translated_text: When the poison has spread, one should open a vein; that is the highest treatment.

children.text: rakte nirhriyamāṇe hi kṛtsnaṃ nirhriyate viṣam
children.translated_text: For when the blood is being drawn out, the whole poison is drawn out.
Poisoned blood is foul-smelling and crackles in fire;
when purified, it should be recognized according to the doṣa, as described before.
When the veins are not visible, horns and leeches should be applied.
The remaining blood that has flowed and has been liquefied by the heat of poison
should be checked again and again with very cold poultices and affusions.
For when it has not clotted, fainting, intoxication, and agitation of the heart arise from the force of the poison;
one should overcome them with cold measures and fan the patient until the hairs stand erect.

children.text: skanne tu rudhire sadyo viṣavegaḥ praśāmyati
children.translated_text: But when the blood has clotted, the force of the poison is immediately pacified.
Because of its sharpness, poison draws toward the heart; to protect that heart,

children.text: pibed ghṛtaṃ ghṛtakṣaudram agadaṃ vā ghṛtāplutam
children.translated_text: one should drink ghee, ghee with honey, or an antidote soaked in ghee.
When the heart has been covered in this way, phlegm accumulates in the heart;
then, when heaviness, retching, and nausea have begun, one should make him vomit.
This should be done with liquids free from sour gruel, <s>kulattha</s>, oil, liquor, and the like,

children.text: vamanair viṣahṛdbhiśca naivaṃ vyāpnoti tad vapuḥ
children.translated_text: and with emetics that remove poison; in this way it does not pervade his body.
After examining very precisely the snake's doṣa, nature, location, and particular stage of action,

children.text: susūkṣmaṃ samyag ālocya viśiṣṭāṃ cācaret kriyām
children.translated_text: one should perform the specific treatment.
Roots of <s>sindhuvārita</s> and white <s>girikarṇikā</s>

children.text: pānaṃ darvīkarair daṣṭe nasyaṃ madhu sapākalam
children.translated_text: are a drink for one bitten by <s>darvīkara</s> snakes; honey with <s>sapākala</s> is a nasal medicine.
For one bitten by a black snake, after the blood has been removed, one should smear the bite
with <s>cāraṭī</s> and <s>nākulī</s>, or with <s>tīkṣṇamūlaviṣā</s>.
As a drink, ghee combined with honey, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, and house soot should be used.
<s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s>, <s>kāśmarya</s>, <s>kiṇihī</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>,
<s>mātuluṅgī</s>, sugar, and <s>śelu</s> are beneficial as drink, nasal medicine, and collyrium.

children.text: agadaḥ phaṇināṃ ghore viṣe rājīmatām api
children.translated_text: This antidote is good against the terrible poison of hooded snakes and also of striped snakes.
Equal parts of <s>sugandhā</s>, raisins, the herb called <s>śvetā</s>, and <s>gajadantikā</s>,
with a half part of <s>saurasa</s> leaf, <s>kapittha</s>, <s>bilva</s>, and pomegranate,
mixed with honey, is an antidote especially beneficial against the poison of <s>maṇḍalin</s> snakes.
<s>Pañcavalkala</s>, <s>varā</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>nāgapuṣpa</s>, and <s>elavāluka</s>,
<s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>śīta</s>, sugar, <s>padmaka</s>, and lotus,

children.text: sakṣaudro himavān nāma hanti maṇḍalināṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: mixed with honey, is the antidote called <s>Himavān</s>, which destroys the poison of <s>maṇḍalin</s> snakes.
By application it removes swelling, erysipelas, blisters, fever, and burning.
<s>Kāśmarya</s>, shoots of the banyan, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, sugar,

children.text: mañjiṣṭhā madhukaṃ ceti daṣṭo maṇḍalinā pibet ||
children.translated_text: <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, and <s>madhuka</s>: one bitten by a <s>maṇḍalin</s> snake should drink these.
Bamboo bark, the seed of <s>kaṭukā</s>, seeds of <s>pāṭalī</s>, and dry ginger,
<s>śirīṣa</s> seeds, <s>ativiṣā</s> roots, <s>gāvedhuka</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,
these eight ingredients, ground with cow's urine, destroy poison produced by a <s>gonasa</s> snake.
<s>Kaṭukā</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, house soot, and <s>hareṇukā</s>,
with honey, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and <s>tagara</s>, destroy the poison of striped snakes.
One should bury the bite of a <s>kāṇḍacitrā</s> snake in the earth for two <s>yāmas</s>.
After drawing it out and scarifying it, one should smear the place with ghee, grain, and clay.
And one should drink old ghee dusted with powder of varā.
When that has been digested, after purgation, one should eat barley food prepared with soup.
Karavīra, arka flowers, root of lāṅgalikā, and kaṇā,
together with pāṭhā and marica, should be ground with sour gruel.
This is an all-purpose <s>agada</s> (antidote) for those bitten by vyantara creatures.
White marica, steeped for seven days in the juice of śirīṣa flowers,
is beneficial for those bitten by snakes as a drink, nasal medicine, and collyrium.
Two <s>palas</s> each of nata and kuṣṭha, and four <s>palas</s> of ghee and honey:
this drink gives ease even to those bitten by <s>Takṣaka</s>.

children.text: atha darvīkṛtāṃ vege pūrve visrāvya śoṇitam
children.translated_text: Now, in the first stage of a bite by a darvīkara snake, after letting out the blood,
one should quickly drink an <s>agada</s> (antidote) mixed with honey and ghee.

children.text: dvitīye vamanaṃ kṛtvā tadvad evāgadaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: In the second stage, after producing vomiting, one should drink the antidote in the same way.
In the third, one should use poison-removing medicine as collyrium and nasal therapy.
In the fourth, after emesis has been done, one should drink the gruel mentioned before.
In the fifth and sixth, one should repeatedly anoint and sprinkle the body with cooling substances.

children.text: pāyayed vamanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ yavāgūṃ ca viṣāpahaiḥ
children.translated_text: One should administer a strong emetic and gruel prepared with poison-removing drugs.
In the seventh, one should apply a sharp <s>agada</s> in collyrium and nasal therapies.
Then, having made a deep crow's-foot incision on the head with a blade,

children.text: māṃsaṃ sarudhiraṃ tasya carma vā tatra nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: one should place there flesh together with blood, or else its skin.

children.text: tṛtīye vamitaḥ peyāṃ vege maṇḍalināṃ pibet
children.translated_text: In the third stage of a bite by maṇḍalin snakes, after vomiting, the patient should drink thin gruel.

children.text: atīkṣṇam agadaṃ ṣaṣṭhe gaṇaṃ vā padmakādikam ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth, he should take a mild <s>agada</s>, or the group beginning with padmaka.
In the first stage for one bitten by rājila snakes, after making a deep scarification,
one should draw off the blood with a gourd and drink the antidote as before.
In the sixth, one should apply the very sharpest collyrium and a pressed nasal medicine.
For stages not explicitly mentioned, one should apply the procedure stated for the darvīkara snake.

children.text: garbhiṇībālavṛddheṣu mṛduṃ vidhyet sirāṃ na ca
children.translated_text: In pregnant women, children, and the elderly, the treatment should be mild, and one should not puncture a vein.

children.text: tvaṅ manohvā niśe vakraṃ rasaḥ śārdūlajo nakhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tvak, manohvā, the two niśās, vakra, rasa, and a tiger-born claw,
together with tamāla, kesara, and śīta, drunk with rice-water,
destroy all poisons; this vajra destroys them as the thunderbolt destroys the Asuras.

children.text: bilvasya mūlaṃ surasasya puṣpaṃ phalaṃ karañjasya nataṃ surāhvam
children.translated_text: Bilva root, surasa flower, karañja fruit, nata, and surāhva,

children.text: phalatrikaṃ vyoṣaniśādvayaṃ ca bastasya mūtreṇa susūkṣmapiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: together with triphalā, vyoṣa, and the two niśās, finely ground in goat's urine,
restore to health people afflicted by snakes, spiders, mice, scorpions, and the like, and by cholera, indigestion, artificial poison, and fevers,
as well as those assaulted by spirits, when used as collyrium, drink, and nasal medicine.
And by poultices and the like it draws out the poison completely even from the bite.

children.text: bhūyo vegāya jāyeta śeṣaṃ dūṣīviṣāya vā ||
children.translated_text: Any remainder may again arise as a paroxysm, or may become latent <s>dūṣīviṣa</s> (residual poison).
When the poison has subsided, one should treat aggravated <s>vāta</s> with oleation and the other therapies,
using wind-subduing measures that avoid sesame oil, wine, horse gram, and sour substances.
One should treat <s>pitta</s> with remedies that remove pitta-fever and with astringent unctuous enemas,
and <s>kapha</s> with the group mixed with honey and with the group beginning with āragvadha.

children.text: sitā vaigandhiko drākṣā payasyā madhukaṃ madhu
children.translated_text: Sugar, vaigandhika, grapes, payasyā, madhuka, honey,
water purified by mantra for drinking, sprinkling, consolation, and gladdening
should be used for one struck by a snake's body, and also for one afflicted by poison-anxiety.
Karketana, emerald, diamond, elephant pearl,
vaiḍūrya, gardabhamaṇi, picuka, viṣamūṣikā,
somarājī and punarnavā born on the Himalayan mountain,

children.text: tathā droṇāṃ mahādroṇāṃ mānasīṃ sarpajaṃ maṇim
children.translated_text: as well as droṇā, mahādroṇā, mānasī, and the snake-born jewel:
one should wear potent poisons and substances for the pacification of poison.
Especially at night one should move about carrying an umbrella and a rattle in the hand.
Snakes, terrified by its shade and sound, disappear.
Now therefore we shall explain the prevention and treatment of poison from insects, spiders, and the like.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
Insects are born from the feces, urine, semen, eggs, and decaying corpses of snakes themselves.
Joined with the <s>doṣas</s> separately and collectively, they are of four kinds.
In one bitten by insects of a vāta nature, the bite is severe with piercing pain.
With those of an agni nature, there is slight discharge, along with burning, redness, and spreading inflammation.
It may resemble the fruit of a ripe pīlu, or be like a date.
Those in which kapha predominates cause slight pain and resemble a ripe udumbara.
A bite rich in discharge and possessing all the signs, being caused by all the doṣas together, is to be rejected as incurable.
The paroxysms are like those from snakes: swelling that increases, and a state of foul, bloody discharge.
There is heaviness of the head and eyes, fainting, dizziness, dyspnea, and excessive pain.
In all cases there is a pustular swelling, fever, itching, and lack of appetite.

children.text: vṛścikasya viṣaṃ tīkṣṇam ādau dahati vahnivat
children.translated_text: The poison of a scorpion is sharp; at first it burns like fire.

children.text: ūrdhvam ārohati kṣipraṃ daṃśe paścāt tu tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: It quickly ascends upward, but afterward remains at the bite.
The bite at once has extreme pain, is dark, is pierced with pain, and seems as if splitting open.
They arise from the decay of cow dung and the like, from the decay of envenomed bites and similar wounds,
and from the decay of snakes; their poison is mild, medium, or great.

children.text: mandāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śyāvā rūkṣāḥ karburamecakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mild ones are yellow, white, dark, dry, variegated, and blackish.
They are hairy, many-jointed, red, and pale-bellied.
Those with smoky bellies and three joints are medium; they are tawny-red.
The highly poisonous ones are brown, mottled, variegated, and blood-colored.
They are fire-colored, have two joints or one, and have red, black, or white bellies.
One bitten by them has a swollen tongue, stiff limbs, and is afflicted with fever.
Vomiting black blood from the openings, he does not perceive the objects of the senses.
He sweats, faints, has a dry mouth, is bewildered, and is tormented by pain.
And, his flesh falling apart, he generally gives up his life.
But the ucciṭiṅga bites with its mouth and causes especially severe pain.
More than a curable scorpion, it produces stiffness of the penis and horripilation.

children.text: karoti sekam aṅgānāṃ daṃśaḥ śītāmbuneva ca
children.translated_text: The bite also causes the limbs to be soaked, as if with cold water.
That same creature is called uṣṭradhūma, and, because it moves at night, rātrika.
Insects are predominantly of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; the kaṇabha and the undura are phlegmatic.
Scorpions, along with the uṣṭradhūmaka, are generally possessed of poison in which <s>vāta</s> is strong.
Whichever <s>doṣa</s>'s signs one judges to be predominant,
for each of those one should apply treatment with medicines having opposite qualities.
Pain in the heart, upward movement of wind, stiffness, stretching of the veins, pain in the bones and joints,
reeling, twisting, and dusky color of the limbs occur in <s>vāta</s>-type poison.
Loss of consciousness, hot breath, burning in the heart, and pungency in the mouth,
tearing of flesh, swelling, and red-yellow coloration occur in <s>pitta</s>-type poison.
By vomiting, anorexia, nausea, salivation, distress, and coryza,
together with coldness and sweetness in the mouth, one should recognize poison dominated by <s>kapha</s>.
In a <s>vāta</s>-type case, the wound should be plastered with oil-cake and the body anointed with oil.
Fomentation with tubular steam, pulāka, and the like, and a nourishing regimen, are beneficial.
A <s>pitta</s>-type case should be restrained by very cooling affusions and plasters.
A <s>kapha</s>-type case should be overcome by scraping, cutting, fomentation, and emesis.
For the three kinds of insects, treatment according to the threefold classification is beneficial.
Generally one should apply warm fomentations, plasters, and affusions,
except in a fainting patient, or when the bite is suppurating, or when there is putrefaction.

children.text: nṛkeśāḥ sarṣapāḥ pītā guḍo jīrṇaśca dhūpanam ||
children.translated_text: Human hair, mustard seeds, yellow pigment, jaggery, and old ghee are the fumigation
that <s>Kāśyapa</s> declared supreme for every poisonous bite.

children.text: viṣaghnaṃ ca vidhiṃ sarvaṃ kuryāt saṃśodhanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: And one should carry out the whole poison-destroying procedure, including purificatory measures.
Those bitten by insects and scorpions with fierce poison should be treated as in snakebite.
One should drink trivṛt equal in measure to taṇḍulīyaka, with ghee.

children.text: yāti kīṭaviṣaiḥ kampaṃ na kailāsa ivānilaiḥ
children.translated_text: By insect poisons he does not go into trembling any more than <s>Kailāsa</s> does from winds.
After purification, a plaster of the bark of milk-exuding trees removes insect poison.
A pearl plaster is excellent; it dispels swelling, pricking pain, burning, and fever.
Vacā, hiṅgu, viḍaṅga, rock salt, and gajapippalī,
together with pāṭhā, prativiṣā, and the three pungents, were prepared by <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
Having drunk the ten-ingredient <s>agada</s> (antidote), one overcomes every insect poison.
A scorpion bite should immediately be sprinkled with cakra oil,
or with another oil made lukewarm and prepared with vidārigandhā.
Or it should be sprinkled again and again with ghee mixed with the best salt,
or with warm sour gruel together with milk and salt.
A poultice is a paste of goat's dung, fried in ghee and mixed with rock salt.
After fomenting the bite and scarifying it, one should rub it with powders
made from rajanī, rock salt, the three pungents, and the fruits and flowers of śirīṣa.
Also beneficial is surasāgraja, ground with the sour juice of citron and cow urine.

children.text: lepaḥ sukhoṣṇaśca hitaḥ piṇyāko gomayo 'pi vā
children.translated_text: A pleasantly warm plaster is beneficial, as are oil-cake or even cow dung.

children.text: pāne sarpir madhuyutaṃ kṣīraṃ vā bhūriśarkaram ||
children.translated_text: For drinking, ghee mixed with honey is prescribed, or milk with abundant sugar.
Pigeon dung, pathyā, tagara, and viśvabheṣaja,
mixed with the juice of bījapūra, are the supreme <s>agada</s> for scorpions.
Together with moss and the fang of a camel, it destroys scorpion-born poison.
With hiṅgu, orpiment, and citron juice,
a pill, used as plaster and collyrium, is the supreme remover of scorpion poison.
The flowers of karañja, arjuna, śelū, kaṭabhī, kuṭaja,
and śirīṣa are to be applied to the bite with whey.
For one who faints, breathes with difficulty, raves, and has intense pain,
pathyā, niśā, kṛṣṇā, mañjiṣṭhā, ativisa, and uṣaṇa,
with the stalk of bottle gourd, ground in eggplant juice, are a plaster.
In every case of fierce scorpion poison, one should make the patient drink curds and ghee.
One should puncture a vein and prescribe emesis, collyrium, and nasal medication,
as well as food that is hot, unctuous, sour, and sweet, and that alleviates <s>anila</s>.
Dry ginger, domestic pigeon dung, bījapūra juice, orpiment,

children.text: saindhavaṃ ca vinihantyagado 'yaṃ lepato 'likulajaṃ viṣam āśu ||
children.translated_text: and rock salt: this <s>agada</s>, used as a plaster, quickly destroys poison born from scorpions.
At the end, when the poison has become greatly aggravated in those bitten by scorpions,
one should smear the bite with poison; this same procedure applies also for ucciṭiṅga.
One should make a pill from elephant dung, mushroom, and rohiṣa root with śelu water.

children.text: kuryād guṭikāṃ lepād iyam aliviṣanāśanī śreṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: When applied as a plaster, this is the best destroyer of scorpion poison.

children.text: arkasya dugdhena śirīṣabījaṃ trir bhāvitaṃ pippalicūrṇamiśram
children.translated_text: Śirīṣa seed, steeped three times in the milk of arka and mixed with pippalī powder,
is an <s>agada</s> that destroys the poisons of insects, snakes, spiders, mice, and scorpions.
Śirīṣa flower with karañja seed, saffron, kuṣṭha, and realgar:
this <s>agada</s> for rātrika scorpions is said by <s>Jina</s> to cause transference.

children.text: kīṭebhyo dāruṇatarā lūtāḥ ṣoḍaśa tā jaguḥ
children.translated_text: Spiders are more terrible than insects; they say there are sixteen of them.
Some say there are twenty-eight, while still others say there are even more than that.
Others say that, as attendants of the thousand-rayed sun, they exist in thousands.
But the poisonous spider is in fact one, though it has many forms of complication.
Its forms and names are very hard to know because they are greatly intermixed.
There is no fixed rule of location either; therefore they describe it according to <s>doṣa</s>.
It is difficult to cure when there are separate <s>doṣa</s>s, and incurable when they are combined.
Its bite, when <s>pitta</s>-type, has burning, thirst, blisters, fever, and stupor.
It is intensely hot, red-yellow in appearance, moist, and like the fruit of a grape.
The <s>kapha</s>-type bite is hard, pale, and shaped like a parūṣaka fruit.

children.text: nidrāṃ śītajvaraṃ kāsaṃ kaṇḍūṃ ca kurute bhṛśam
children.translated_text: It produces sleep, cold fever, cough, and severe itching.
The <s>vātika</s> type is rough and dusky, and produces fever with splitting pain in the joints.
One should determine its classification, in each case, by the respective signs of the <s>doṣa</s>s.
But in an incurable case there are bewilderment of the heart, dyspnea, hiccup, and stiffness of the head;
white, yellow, black, and red pustules, swelling,
trembling, vomiting, burning, thirst, blindness, and crookedness of the nose;
darkening of the lips, face, and teeth, and bending of the back and neck;
and from the bite flows blood the color of ripe <s>jambu</s> wine.
Every variety is usually produced by all the <s>doṣa</s>s; the name, however, is based on predominance.
According to sharp, middling, and slight intensity, it is threefold; if neglected it kills,

children.text: saptāhena daśāhena pakṣeṇa ca paraṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: respectively, at the latest in seven days, in ten days, and in a fortnight.
Every bite of a <s>lūtā</s> is like a ring of <s>dadrū</s>.
It may be white, black, red, yellow, or dusky, soft and raised,
black or else dusky in the middle, and covered at the edges with a net-like pattern.
It has spreading inflammation and is accompanied by swelling; it burns and is very painful,
with fever, rapid suppuration, moistening, putrefaction, and bursting.

children.text: kledena yat spṛśatyaṅgaṃ tatrāpi kurute vraṇam
children.translated_text: Whatever limb it touches with its moisture, there too it produces a wound.
Through eight means--breath, fangs, feces, urine, semen, saliva, nails, and menstrual fluid--
this creature emits poison, especially from the mouth.

children.text: lūtā nābher daśatyūrdhvam ūrdhvaṃ cādhaśca kīṭakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>lūtā</s> bites above the navel; insects bite both above and below.

children.text: taddūṣitaṃ ca vastrādi dehe pṛktaṃ vikārakṛt
children.translated_text: Cloth and the like, contaminated by that poison and coming into contact with the body, produce disorder.
For half a day a bite arising from <s>lūtā</s> poison is not perceived at all.
Then, on the first day, it appears like a needle-prick,
indistinct in color, unstable, and accompanied by slight itching and pain.
On the second day it becomes raised, as if edged at the margins with pustules,
clear in color, depressed in the middle, itchy, and like a nodule.
On the third day it is feverish, causes horripilation, and has a red circle;
it is saucer-shaped, full of pricking pain, and has discharge from the hair-follicles.
On the fourth day a great swelling causes heat, dyspnea, and dizziness.
On the fifth it produces various disorders arising from the aggravation of the poison.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe vyāpnoti marmāṇi saptame hanti jīvitam
children.translated_text: On the sixth it pervades the vital spots; on the seventh it destroys life.

children.text: iti tīkṣṇaṃ viṣaṃ madhyaṃ hīnaṃ ca vibhajed ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should distinguish sharp, middling, and slight poison from this point.
After twenty-one nights the poison subsides completely.
Now, in one bitten by a <s>lūtā</s>, one should quickly excise the bitten spot with a knife

children.text: dahecca jāmbavauṣṭhādyair na tu pittottaraṃ dahet
children.translated_text: and cauterize it with <s>jāmbavauṣṭha</s> and the like; but one should not cauterize when <s>pitta</s> predominates.
A bite that is rough, has broken hairs, or is lodged in a vital spot, joint, or the like,

children.text: prasṛtaṃ sarvato daṃśaṃ na chindīta dahen na ca
children.translated_text: or one that has spread everywhere, should not be cut or cauterized.
The cauterized place should be smeared with antidotes combined with honey and rock salt.
Afterwards one should irrigate it with very cold decoctions made from milky trees.
One should draw blood away from all sides with a horn and similar instruments, or even by venesection.
Then cold irrigations and pastes should be applied with <s>bodhi</s>, <s>śleṣmātaka</s>, and <s>akṣaka</s>,
with <s>phalinī</s>, the two <s>niśā</s>s, honey, and ghee; this is called <s>Padmaka</s>.
It is an antidote effective in every action against all <s>lūtā</s>s and insects.
With the two <s>haridrā</s>s, <s>pattaṅga</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>nata</s>, and <s>kesara</s>,
together with honey and ghee, the one called <s>Campaka</s> is more powerful than the preceding.
Similarly, with squeezed cow-dung, sugar, ghee, and honey,
with <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>aladārvī</s>, <s>dhyāmaka</s>, and red ochre,
and with <s>nata</s>, cardamom, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, pepper, <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, ghee, and honey,
there is the antidote named <s>Mandara</s>, and likewise another named <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
It is prepared with <s>nata</s>, <s>lodhra</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>kaṭvī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, cardamom, leaf, and saffron.
In poisons with many <s>doṣa</s>s, one should employ purificatory treatment that destroys poison.
<s>Yaṣṭyāhva</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>aṅkolla</s>, <s>jālinī</s>, and <s>sindhuvārikā</s>,

children.text: kaphe jyeṣṭhāmbunā pītvā viṣam āśu samudvamet
children.translated_text: when drunk with water of <s>jyeṣṭhā</s> in a <s>kapha</s> condition, cause the poison to be vomited quickly.
Or the leaf, bark, root, and fruit of <s>śirīṣa</s> may be used, as with the root of <s>aṅkolla</s>.
One should also purge with <s>triphalā</s>, <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and the like.
When burning, swelling, and the other symptoms have ceased, one should make the core fall out from the wound.
<s>Kusumbha</s> flower, <s>godanta</s>, <s>svarṇakṣīrī</s>, pigeon dung,
<s>trivṛt</s>, rock salt, and <s>dantī</s> are likewise agents for making the core fall.
The root of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>, combined with bamboo scrapings,
and likewise rock salt, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>kaṭukadaugdhika</s>, serve the same purpose.
So too do the root of <s>rājakośātakī</s>, or yeast produced from churned curds.
At the time when the core falls, one should nourish the patient with poison-removing substances.
And every oleating procedure should be performed only with ghee.
Oil increases poison, just as grass and tinder increase fire.
<s>Hrīvera</s>, <s>vaikaṅkata</s>, <s>gopakanyā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>śamī</s>, sandalwood, and <s>ṭuṇṭuka</s>,
<s>śaivāla</s>, blue lotus, <s>vakra</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s> bark, <s>nākulī</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, <s>rāṭha</s>, and <s>madhya</s>,
turmeric, <s>ghana</s>, <s>sarpalocanā</s>, <s>kaṇa</s>, dry ginger, <s>kaṇamūla</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
<s>varuṇa</s>, aloe-wood, <s>bilva</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>picumanda</s>, <s>āmaya</s>, <s>śelu</s>, and <s>kesara</s>,
<s>bilva</s>, sandalwood, <s>nata</s>, lotus, dry ginger, long pepper, <s>nicula</s>, reed, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>,
oyster shell, <s>śākavara</s>, <s>pāṭalī</s>, <s>bhārgī</s>, <s>sindhuvāra</s>, <s>karaghāṭa</s>, and <s>varāṅga</s>--
for <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, <s>anila</s>, and <s>lūtā</s> poisons, through drinking, collyrium, nasal therapy, paste, and irrigation,
these excellent antidotes, properly established in their applications, ward off bad courses as good conduct wards them off.

children.text: lodhraṃ sevyaṃ padmakaṃ padmareṇuḥ kālīyākhyaṃ candanaṃ yacca raktam
children.translated_text: <s>Lodhra</s>, <s>sevya</s>, <s>padmaka</s>, lotus pollen, what is called <s>kālīya</s>, sandalwood, and red sandalwood,

children.text: kāntāpuṣpaṃ dugdhinīkā mṛṇālaṃ lūtāḥ sarvā ghnanti sarvakriyābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>kāntā</s> flower, <s>dugdhinīkā</s>, and lotus fiber destroy all <s>lūtā</s>s by all modes of application.
Now then, we shall explain the prevention and treatment of the poison of mice and rabid dogs.
Thus, so indeed, said the great seers beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.
<s>Lālana</s>, <s>Capala</s>, <s>Putra</s>, <s>Hasira</s>, <s>Cikkira</s>, and <s>Ajira</s>,
<s>Kaṣāyadanta</s>, <s>Kulaka</s>, <s>Kokila</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Asita</s>;
<s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Śabara</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Kapota</s>, <s>Palita</s>, <s>Undura</s>,
and <s>Chucchundara</s>, called <s>Rasāla</s>: thus there are eighteen mice.

children.text: śukraṃ patati yatraiṣāṃ śukradigdhaiḥ spṛśanti vā
children.translated_text: Where their semen falls, or when they touch a limb smeared with semen,

children.text: yad aṅgam aṅgaistatrāsre dūṣite pāṇḍutāṃ gate ||
children.translated_text: in that limb, when the blood has been vitiated by their bodies and has become pale,
there are nodules, swelling, urticarial eruptions, circular patches, dizziness, and loss of appetite,
cold fever, excessive pain, exhaustion, trembling, and splitting pain in the joints,
horripilation, discharge, fainting, and a condition that persists for a long time,
vomiting of much phlegm mixed with young mice, together with thirst.
Mouse poison is diffusive and difficult to treat; it flares up again and again.
Fainting, swelling of the limbs, discoloration, moistness, loss of hearing, and fever,
heaviness of the head, salivation, vomiting of blood: these are signs of incurability.
One should reject as hopeless a person whose bladder is swollen, whose lips are discolored, and who is covered with nodules from mice,
and whose mouse-contaminated body smells like a <s>chucchundara</s>.
In a dog, the doṣas, with <s>śleṣman</s> predominant, lodge in the channels that carry consciousness;
stealing away consciousness, they produce an extremely dreadful disturbance of the tissues.
Salivating, blind, and deaf, it runs at everything from every side,
with tail, jaw, and shoulders drooping, suffering pain in the head, and with its face bent down.
The bite made by such a dog is numb and black in the bitten person, and blood oozes from it.
Then pain in the heart and head, fever, rigidity, thirst, and fainting arise.
By this, other fierce animals that strike with fangs should also be understood:
