jackals, mules, horses, bears, leopards, tigers, wolves, and the like.
Itching, pricking pain, discoloration, numbness, moistness, fever, and dizziness,
burning, redness, pain, suppuration, swelling, nodules, and contraction,
tearing open of the bite, blisters, pustules, and circular patches

children.text: sarvatra saviṣe liṅgaṃ viparītaṃ tu nirviṣe
children.translated_text: are everywhere the signs when poison is present; when there is no poison, the signs are the opposite.

children.text: daṣṭo yena tu tacceṣṭārutaṃ kurvan vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: One who has been bitten and imitates the actions and cries of the creature by which he was bitten perishes,
and so does one who suddenly sees that very creature in mirrors, water, and the like.
One who, even unbitten, is terrified of water through sounds, touch, and sights
is called afflicted by terror of water; if he has been bitten, one should reject him too.
Immediately after a mouse has bitten, one should cauterize the bite with a stalk
or else with a mirror; otherwise there will be a pustule with severe pain.

children.text: dagdhaṃ visrāvayed daṃśaṃ pracchitaṃ ca pralepayet ||
children.translated_text: After it has been cauterized, one should drain the bitten spot, incise it, and apply a paste
of <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>rajanī</s>, <s>vakra</s>, saffron, and <s>amṛtavallī</s>.
A paste of house soot, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, <s>rajanī</s>, and the best salt
overcomes mouse poison and makes the pustule fall off.
Then, after washing it with sour liquids and afterward with water, one should apply another paste
of <s>pālindī</s>, white <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>bilva</s> root, and <s>guḍūcī</s>,

children.text: anyaiśca viṣaśophaghnaiḥ sirāṃ vā mokṣayed drutam ||
children.translated_text: and with other substances that remove poison and swelling; or one should quickly open a vein.
Emesis should be induced with decoctions of <s>nīlinī</s>, of <s>śukākhya</s>, and of <s>aṅkolla</s> also.
The fruit of <s>kośātakī</s>, of <s>śukākhya</s>, of <s>jīmūtaka</s>,

children.text: madanasya ca saṃcūrṇya dadhnā pītvā viṣaṃ vamet
children.translated_text: and of <s>madana</s>, powdered and drunk with curds, makes one vomit the poison.
Or <s>vacā</s>, <s>madana</s>, <s>jīmūta</s>, and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, ground with urine,
should be drunk according to the previous procedure; it removes every kind of rat poison.
For purgation, a paste of <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, and <s>triphalā</s> is recommended.
For purging the head, the pith of <s>śirīṣa</s> and its fruits are recommended.
For collyrium, cow-dung juice mixed with fine powder of <s>vyoṣa</s> is used.
Juice of <s>kapittha</s> and cow dung, with honey, is used as a lickable medicine.
Ghee cooked with the root of <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> is beneficial for drinking,
or with the two <s>niśā</s>s, <s>kaṭabhī</s>, <s>raktā</s>, and <s>yaṣṭyāhva</s>, together with <s>amṛtā</s>.
Or ghee cooked with the root of <s>āsphota</s>, or the fivefold <s>kapittha</s> preparation, may be used.
<s>Sindhuvāra</s>, <s>nata</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>bilva</s> root, <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>vacā</s>, <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>jīmūta</s>: one should drink a decoction of these with honey,
while eating rice boiled from <s>śāli</s> rice with curds, if afflicted by a mouse.

children.text: takreṇa śarapuṅkhāyā bījaṃ saṃcūrṇya vā pibet ||
children.translated_text: Or one should powder and drink the seed of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s> with buttermilk.
Or a paste of <s>aṅkolla</s> root prepared with goat's urine,
used both for drinking and for smearing, destroys every kind of mouse poison.
One should drink the pith of <s>kapittha</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, sesame, and roots of <s>aṅkolla</s>,

children.text: gavāṃ mūtreṇa payasā mañjarīṃ tilakasya vā ||
children.translated_text: with cow's urine or milk; or the flowering cluster of <s>tilaka</s>,
or the root of <s>sairyaka</s> with honey and rice-water.
Or one may drink water placed in a bitter gourd and left to concentrate.
Roots of <s>sindhuvāra</s>, cat bone, poison, and <s>nata</s>,
ground with water as an antidote, destroy mouse-born poison through nasal therapy and the other routes.
Residual mouse poison flares up at the sight of clouds,
or at the times when the doṣas respectively have causes for increase.
In such cases all treatments should be applied according to the condition,
as well as those separately prescribed for removing latent poison.
But the bite of one bitten by a rabid dog, after cauterization, should be smeared with hot ghee

children.text: pradihyād agadaistaistaiḥ purāṇaṃ ca ghṛtaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: and with various antidotes, and he should drink old ghee.
A quick purgative joined with the latex of <s>arka</s> should also be administered to him.
He should drink three <s>pala</s>s of water from the upper root of <s>aṅkolla</s>, together with one <s>pala</s> of ghee,
or white <s>punarnavā</s> together with <s>dhattūra</s> fruit.

children.text: aikadhyaṃ palalaṃ tailaṃ rūpikāyāḥ payo guḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sesame paste, oil, the milk of <s>rūpikā</s>, and jaggery, combined together,
break up the poison of a rabid dog as wind breaks up a dense mass of clouds.
Bathing accompanied by mantra, herbs, and jewels should also be employed.
When a wound has been scratched by the nails or teeth of quadrupeds or bipeds,
it swells, suppurates, and is accompanied by redness, fever, discharge, and pain.
Somavalka, aśvakarṇa, gojihvā, haṃsapādikā,
the two rajanīs, and gairika, used as a plaster, remove poison from nails and teeth.

children.text: dīrgham āyuḥ smṛtiṃ medhām ārogyaṃ taruṇaṃ vayaḥ
children.translated_text: Long life, memory, intelligence, health, youthful age,
radiance, complexion, nobility of voice, and the rise of strength in body and senses,
perfection of speech, virility, and beauty: these one obtains from <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative therapy).
For <s>rasāyana</s> is the means of obtaining excellent <s>rasa</s> and the other bodily constituents.

children.text: pūrve vayasi madhye vā tat prayojyaṃ jitātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be applied in early life or in middle age to one who has mastered himself,
who has been oleated, whose blood has been let, and who has been thoroughly purified in every way.

children.text: aviśuddhe śarīre hi yukto rāsāyano vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: For when the body is not purified, the prescribed <s>rasāyana</s> procedure,

children.text: vājīkaro vā maline vastre raṅga ivāphalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or an aphrodisiac one, is fruitless, like dye on a dirty cloth.
The seers know a twofold application of <s>rasāyana</s>s:
the principal one is <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> (entering a treatment hut), while the other is <s>vātātapika</s> (exposure to wind and sun).
In a town where the necessary equipment can be obtained, in a windless, secure mansion,

children.text: diśy udīcyāṃ śubhe deśe trigarbhāṃ sūkṣmalocanām ||
children.translated_text: in a good place in the northern quarter, he should have made a hut with three inner chambers and small windows,
not entered by smoke, sun, dust, snakes, women, fools, and the like,
well cleaned and furnished with ready physicians and equipment.

children.text: atha puṇye 'hni sampūjya pūjyāṃs tāṃ praviśec chuciḥ
children.translated_text: Then, on an auspicious day, after honoring those worthy of honor, he should enter it purified,

children.text: tatra saṃśodhanaiḥ śuddhaḥ sukhī jātabalaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there, purified by cleansing procedures, comfortable, and with strength restored,
celibate, steadfast, faithful, and self-controlled,
devoted to generosity, good conduct, compassion, truth, vows, and <s>dharma</s>,
intent on recollection of the deities, with proper sleep and waking,
fond of the medicine and gentle in speech, he should begin the <s>rasāyana</s>.
He should drink harītakī, āmalaka, rock salt, dry ginger, vacā,

children.text: haridrāṃ pippalīṃ vellaṃ guḍaṃ coṣṇāmbunā pibet ||
children.translated_text: haridrā, pippalī, vella, and jaggery with warm water.

children.text: snigdhasvinno naraḥ pūrvaṃ tena sādhu viricyate
children.translated_text: A person who has first been oleated and sweated is well purged by this.
Then, for one whose body has been purified and who has completed the restorative diet,

children.text: trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ vā saptāhaṃ vā ghṛtānvitam
children.translated_text: for three nights, five nights, or a week he should give yāvaka mixed with ghee,
until the old fecal matter has been cleared away.
To one whose bowel has been prepared in this way, he should administer a <s>rasāyana</s>,

children.text: yasya yad yaugikaṃ paśyet sarvam ālocya sātmyavit ||
children.translated_text: choosing what he sees to be suitable for that person, after considering everything, as one who knows habituation.
A thousand pathyā fruits, combined with three times as many dhātrī fruits,
together with two and a half hundred palas of the five sets of five roots,
should be boiled in ten times as much water, until the decoction is reduced to one tenth.
Then, after pounding and removing the stones from the vijayā and āmalaka fruits,
he should put them into that decoction and add a kuḍava each
of tvak, elā, musta, rajanī, pippalī, aguru, and candana,
of maṇḍūkaparṇī, kanaka, śaṅkhapuṣpī, vacā, and plava,
and of yaṣṭyāhvaya and viḍaṅga, powdered, in a quantity exceeding a tulā,
as well as half a bhāra of sugar-candy, three vessels of ghee,

children.text: dve ca tailāt pacet sarvaṃ tad agnau lehatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and two of oil; he should cook all this on the fire until it becomes a linctus.

children.text: avatīrṇaṃ himaṃ yuñjyād viṃśaiḥ kṣaudraśatais tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: When it has been taken down and cooled, he should combine it with three hundred measures of honey,
then churn it with a churning stick and store it in a vessel for ghee.

children.text: yā noparundhyād āhāram ekaṃ mātrāsya sā smṛtā
children.translated_text: A single dose of it is said to be an amount that does not impede the meal.

children.text: ṣaṣṭikaḥ payasā cātra jīrṇe bhojanam iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: When it has been digested, ṣaṣṭika rice with milk is the desired food here.
The Vaikhānasas, the Vālakhilyas, and likewise other ascetics rich in austerity,

children.text: brahmaṇā vihitaṃ dhanyam idaṃ prāśya rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: having eaten this blessed <s>rasāyana</s> prescribed by <s>Brahmā</s>,
became free from drowsiness, fatigue, exhaustion, wrinkles, grey hair, and disease,
endowed with intelligence, memory, and strength, and possessed of immeasurable life.
A thousand abhayā and āmalaka fruits, free from blemish and joined with a thousand pippalīs,
liquefied with alkali from young palāśa, should be placed in a vessel.
When the alkali has been used up, a powder dried in the shade should be added,
with a quarter portion of sugar and with fourfold quantities of honey and ghee.

children.text: tad ghṛtakumbhe bhūmau nidhāya ṣaṇmāsasaṃstham uddhṛtya
children.translated_text: Putting it in a ghee jar and burying it in the ground, after it has stood for six months he should take it out.

children.text: prāhṇe prāśya yathānalam ucitāhāro bhavet satatam ||
children.translated_text: Eating it in the forenoon according to his digestive fire, he should always follow a suitable diet.
Having used all of it in this way, he lives a hundred years, free from disease and old age,
especially endowed with strength, nourishment, a fine body, memory, intelligence, and the like.
Of a fresh, healthy palāśa tree, when its top has been cut off, that wound,

children.text: antar dvihastaṃ gambhīraṃ pūryam āmalakair navaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: two cubits deep inside, should be filled with fresh āmalakas.
Wrapped down to the root with darbha grass and smeared with mud from a lotus pond,

children.text: ādīpya gomayair vanyair nirvāte svedayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: it should be heated in a windless place by lighting wild cow-dung fuel around it.

children.text: svinnāni tāny āmalakāni tṛptyā khāden naraḥ kṣaudraghṛtānvitāni
children.translated_text: A man should eat those steamed āmalakas to satisfaction, mixed with honey and ghee,

children.text: kṣīraṃ śṛtaṃ cānu pibet prakāmaṃ tenaiva varteta ca māsam ekam ||
children.translated_text: and should drink boiled milk afterward as much as he likes; he should live on just that for one month.

children.text: varjyāni varjyāni ca tatra yatnāt spṛśyaṃ ca śītāmbu na pāṇināpi
children.translated_text: There, forbidden things are to be carefully avoided, and cold water should not be touched even with the hand.

children.text: ekādaśāhe 'sya tato vyatīte patanti keśā daśanā nakhāś ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, when eleven days have passed for him, his hair, teeth, and nails fall out.

children.text: athālpakair eva dinaiḥ surūpaḥ strīṣv akṣayaḥ kuñjaratulyavīryaḥ
children.translated_text: After only a few days, he becomes handsome, inexhaustible among women, and equal to an elephant in virility;
he becomes exceptional in intelligence, strength, understanding, and spirit, and lives for a thousand years.
Daśamūla, balā, musta, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, and utpala,

children.text: parṇinyau pippalī śṛṅgī medā tāmalakī truṭī ||
children.translated_text: the two parṇinīs, pippalī, śṛṅgī, medā, tāmalakī, and truṭī,

children.text: jīvantī joṅgakaṃ drākṣā pauṣkaraṃ candanaṃ śaṭhī
children.translated_text: jīvantī, joṅgaka, drākṣā, pauṣkara, candana, and śaṭhī,
punarnavā, ṛddhi, kākolī, kākanāsā, and the two amṛtās,

children.text: vidārī vṛṣamūlaṃ ca tad aikadhyaṃ palonmitam
children.translated_text: as well as vidārī and vṛṣamūla: all these together, each measured by a pala,
one should cook in a droṇa of water, along with five hundred dhātrī fruits.

children.text: pādaśeṣaṃ rasaṃ tasmād vyasthīny āmalakāni ca
children.translated_text: From that, one should take the decoction reduced to one quarter, and the seedless āmalaka fruits,
and fry them with twelve palas of oil and ghee.
Mixed with half a tulā of matsyaṇḍikā sugar, it should be cooked as an electuary.

children.text: snehārdhaṃ madhu siddhe tu tavakṣīryāś catuḥpalam ||
children.translated_text: When it is prepared, honey equal to half the fat should be added, and four palas of tvak-kṣīrī.
One should add two palas of pippalī and the caturjāta spices, increased with half as much kaṇā.
Staying in a cottage and eating wholesome food, one should lick a proper dose of this.

children.text: ity eṣa cyavanaprāśo yaṃ prāśya cyavano muniḥ
children.translated_text: This is <s>cyavanaprāśa</s> (Cyavana electuary); after eating it, the sage <s>Cyavana</s>,
though decrepit with old age, became delightful to the eyes of women.

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ jvaraṃ śoṣaṃ hṛdrogaṃ vātaśoṇitam
children.translated_text: It removes cough, dyspnea, fever, wasting disease, heart disease, and <s>vātaśoṇita</s> (gout-like vāta-blood disorder),
as well as disorders located in urine and semen, and hoarseness of voice.
It promotes the growth of the body in children, the elderly, the wounded, the depleted, and the emaciated.

children.text: medhāṃ smṛtiṃ kāntim anāmayatvam āyuḥprakarṣaṃ pavanānulomyam
children.translated_text: Used according to rule, it produces intelligence, memory, beauty, freedom from illness, extension of life, and the regular movement of <s>pavana</s> (vāta),

children.text: strīṣu praharṣaṃ balam indriyāṇām agneś ca kuryād vidhinopayuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as delight among women, strength of the senses, and strength of the digestive fire.
With madhuka, tvak-kṣīrī, pippalī, and rock salt,
separately with iron preparations, gold, vacā, honey, and ghee,

children.text: sitayā vā samā yuktā samāyuktā rasāyanam
children.translated_text: or mixed in equal quantity with sugar, it becomes a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating preparation).
Triphalā, destroyer of all diseases, gives intelligence, long life, memory, and understanding.

children.text: maṇḍūkaparṇyāḥ svarasaṃ yathāgni kṣīreṇa yaṣṭīmadhukasya cūrṇam
children.translated_text: One should use fresh juice of maṇḍūkaparṇī, and powder of yaṣṭīmadhuka with milk,

children.text: rasaṃ guḍūcyāḥ sahamūlapuṣpyāḥ kalkaṃ prayuñjīta ca śaṅkhapuṣpyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the juice of guḍūcī, and the paste of śaṅkhapuṣpī together with its root and flower.
These <s>rasāyana</s>s grant life, destroy disease, and increase strength, digestive fire, complexion, and voice;

children.text: medhyāni caitāni rasāyanāni medhyā viśeṣeṇa tu śaṅkhapuṣpī ||
children.translated_text: they also promote intelligence, but śaṅkhapuṣpī is especially intellect-promoting.
Nalada, kaṭurohiṇī, payasyā, madhuka, candana, sārivā, and ugragandhā,

children.text: triphalā kaṭukatrayaṃ haridre sapaṭolaṃ lavaṇaṃ ca taiḥ supiṣṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: triphalā, the three pungents, the two haridrās, with paṭola and salt: with these finely ground,

children.text: triguṇena rasena śaṅkhapuṣpyāḥ sapayaskaṃ ghṛtanalvaṇaṃ vipakvam
children.translated_text: unsalted ghee, cooked with three times as much juice of śaṅkhapuṣpī and with milk,

children.text: upayujya bhavej jaḍo 'pi vāgmī śrutadhārī pratibhānavān arogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when used, makes even a dull man eloquent, retentive of what he has heard, imaginative, and healthy.

children.text: peṣyair mṛṇālabisakesarapattrabījaiḥ siddhaṃ sahemaśakalaṃ payasā ca sarpiḥ
children.translated_text: Ghee cooked with ingredients to be ground, namely lotus stalks, fibers, filaments, petals, and seeds, together with milk and a piece of gold,

children.text: pañcāravindam iti tat prathitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ prabhraṣṭapauruṣabalapratibhair niṣevyam ||
children.translated_text: is renowned on earth as Pañcāravinda; it should be taken by those whose virility, strength, and brilliance have fallen away.

children.text: yan nālakandadalakesaravad vipakvaṃ nīlotpalasya tad api prathitaṃ dvitīyam
children.translated_text: That which is similarly cooked with the stalk, tuber, petals, and filaments of blue lotus is also known as the second preparation.

children.text: sarpiś catuṣkuvalayaṃ sahiraṇyapattraṃ medhyaṃ gavām api bhavet kimu mānuṣāṇām ||
children.translated_text: The four-kuvalaya ghee, with a gold leaf, would promote intelligence even in cows; how much more in human beings.
Brāhmī, vacā, rock salt, śaṅkhapuṣpī, matsyākṣaka, brahmasuvarcalā, and aindrī,

children.text: vaidehikā ca triyavāḥ pṛthak syur yavau suvarṇasya tilo viṣasya ||
children.translated_text: and vaidehikā should each be three yavas; gold should be two yavas, and poison one sesame-seed measure.

children.text: sarpiṣaś ca palam ekata etad yojayet pariṇate ca ghṛtāḍhyam
children.translated_text: One should combine all this with one pala of ghee, and when it has been digested, take food rich in ghee.

children.text: bhojanaṃ samadhu vatsaram evaṃ śīlayann adhikadhīsmṛtimedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Practicing this for a year, together with honey, one gains superior understanding, memory, and intelligence.
He passes beyond old age, disease, drowsiness, laziness, fatigue, and exhaustion,
and lives a full hundred years, endowed with prosperity, splendor, beauty, and brilliance.
In particular, kuṣṭha skin disease, kilāsa, gulma tumors, poison, fever, insanity, artificial poison, and abdominal enlargement,

children.text: atharvamantrādikṛtāś ca kṛtyāḥ śāmyanty anenātibalāś ca vātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and sorceries made with Atharvanic mantras and the like are pacified by this, as are very strong vāta disorders.
At the beginning of autumn, under the Puṣya conjunction, one should uproot nāgabalā.

children.text: akṣamātraṃ tato mūlāc cūrṇitāt payasā pibet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should drink, with milk, an akṣa-measure of the powdered root,
or lick it with honey and ghee, living on milk and taking no solid food.
By using it thus for a year, one lives a hundred years, strong.
Gokṣuraka in fruit, together with its root, dried in the shade and with all its parts well powdered,

children.text: subhāvitaḥ svena rasena tasmān mātrāṃ parāṃ prāsṛtikīṃ pibed yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: well steeped in its own juice: from this, one who drinks the highest dose, a prasṛta measure,

children.text: kṣīreṇa tenaiva ca śālim aśnan jīrṇe bhavet sa dvitulopayogāt
children.translated_text: with milk, and eats śāli rice only after that has digested, becomes so after taking two tulās of it:

children.text: śaktaḥ surūpaḥ subhagaḥ śatāyuḥ kāmī kakudmān iva gokulasthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: capable, handsome, fortunate, living a hundred years, virile, like a humped bull standing in the herd.
One living on milk should drink fresh, moist vārāhīkanda with milk.

children.text: māsaṃ niranno māsaṃ ca kṣīrānnādo jarāṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: Taking no other food for one month, and milk-rice for another month, he conquers old age.
Or its tuber, finely powdered and well steeped in its own juice,

children.text: ghṛtakṣaudraplutaṃ lihyāt tatpakvaṃ vā ghṛtaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: should be licked drenched with ghee and honey, or one should drink ghee cooked with it.
In the same way one should use vidārī, atibalā, balā, madhuka, and vāyasī,
as well as śreyasī, śreyasīyuktā, pathyā, dhātrī, sthirā, and amṛtā,
maṇḍūkī, śaṅkhakusuma, vājigandhā, and śatāvarī;
one should use these, for they give intelligence, understanding, steadiness of age, and strength.
Citraka is to be recognized respectively by yellow, white, and black flowers;

children.text: yathottaraṃ sa guṇavān vidhinā ca rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: in that order each later kind is better, and, used according to rule, it is a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: chāyāśuṣkaṃ tato mūlaṃ māsaṃ cūrṇīkṛtaṃ lihan
children.translated_text: Having dried its root in the shade and powdered it, an ascetic should lick it for a month

children.text: sarpiṣā madhusarpirbhyāṃ piban vā payasā yatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with ghee, with honey and ghee, or should drink it with milk,

children.text: ambhasā vā hitānnāśī śataṃ jīvati nīrujaḥ
children.translated_text: or with water, while eating wholesome food; he lives a hundred years, free from disease,
intelligent, strong, beautiful, well-bodied, and with blazing digestive fire.

children.text: tailena līḍho māsena vātān hanti sudustarān
children.translated_text: Licked with oil for a month, it destroys vāta disorders that are very hard to overcome.
Drunk with urine, it destroys śvitra and kuṣṭha; drunk with buttermilk, diseases of the anus.
One should place well-developed bhallātaka fruits in a heap of grain.
Having gathered them in summer, in winter one should prepare the body with sweet, unctuous, and cooling substances.
Then one should process eight of them in eight times as much water,
and when one eighth remains, drink that cooled decoction together with milk.
And each day thereafter one should increase the dose there by one aruṣkara fruit.

children.text: saptarātratrayaṃ yāvat trīṇi trīṇi tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: For three periods of seven nights, three at a time; thereafter,

children.text: ā catvāriṃśatas tāni hrāsayed vṛddhivat tataḥ
children.translated_text: up to forty, one should reduce them in the same way as the increase.
Thus one should use a thousand over seven periods of seven days.
Restraining himself, eating ghee, milk, and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice,
he should observe that same regimen for three times the duration even after the course is finished.
He obtains unprecedented blessings, and especially the kindling of the digestive fire,
free from urinary disorders, worms, skin disease, piles, and disorders of fat.
A vessel, smeared for paste-steaming and filled with sound, crushed <s>bhallātaka</s>s,
set in a pit in the ground and coated with black clay,

children.text: parivāritaṃ samantāt pacet tato gomayāgninā mṛdunā
children.translated_text: surrounded on every side, should then be cooked over a gentle cow-dung fire.

children.text: tatsvaraso yaś cyavate gṛhṇīyāt taṃ dine 'nyasmin ||
children.translated_text: The juice that drips from it should be collected on the following day.
Having used that fresh juice with one eighth part honey and twice as much ghee,

children.text: pūrvavidhiyantritātmā prāpnoti guṇān sa tān eva ||
children.translated_text: a self-controlled person, following the previous regimen, obtains those very same benefits.
Plump <s>bhallātaka</s>s, fallen off through ripening and measuring an <s>āḍhaka</s>,

children.text: ghṛṣṭveṣṭikācūrṇakaṇair jalena prakṣālya saṃśoṣya ca mārutena ||
children.translated_text: after being rubbed with grains of powdered brick, washed with water, and dried by the wind,
should be crushed and cooked in a jar of water; when a quarter remains, it is filtered and cooled.

children.text: tadrasaṃ punar api śrapayeta kṣīrakumbhasahitaṃ caraṇasthe ||
children.translated_text: That liquid should again be cooked together with a jar of milk, set in place.

children.text: sarpiḥ pakvaṃ tatra tulyapramāṇaṃ yuñjyāt svecchaṃ śarkarayā rajobhiḥ
children.translated_text: One should use there an equal measure of cooked ghee, as desired, with powdered sugar.

children.text: ekībhūtaṃ tat khajakṣobhaṇena sthāpyaṃ dhānye saptarātraṃ suguptam ||
children.translated_text: When it has become unified by stirring with a churning stick, it should be kept well hidden in grain for seven nights.

children.text: tam amṛtarasapākaṃ yaḥ prage prāśam aśnann anupibati yatheṣṭaṃ vāri dugdhaṃ rasaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Whoever eats a morning morsel of that preparation, the cooking of nectar-juice, and drinks as much water, milk, or broth as he wishes,

children.text: smṛtimatibalamedhāsattvasārair upetaḥ kanakanicayagauraḥ so 'śnute dīrgham āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: endowed with memory, intelligence, strength, wisdom, and firmness of spirit, golden in complexion, enjoys long life.

children.text: droṇe 'mbhaso vraṇakṛtāṃ triśatād vipakvāt kvāthāḍhake palasamais tilatailapātram
children.translated_text: From three hundred wound-producing fruits cooked in a <s>droṇa</s> of water down to an <s>āḍhaka</s> of decoction, with a vessel of sesame oil measured in equal <s>pala</s>s,
prepared with <s>tiktā</s>, the two <s>viṣā</s>s, <s>varā</s>, mountain-born resin, and <s>tārkṣya</s>, it is supreme for removing every skin disease.

children.text: sahāmalakaśuktibhir dadhisareṇa tailena vā guḍena payasā ghṛtena yavasaktubhir vā saha
children.translated_text: Together with <s>āmalaka</s> and sour ferment, or with the cream of curds, oil,

children.text: tilena saha mākṣikeṇa palalena sūpena vā vapuṣkaram aruṣkaraṃ paramamedhyam āyuṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: jaggery, milk, ghee, barley meal, sesame, honey, meat paste, or soup, <s>aruṣkara</s> is excellent for the body, supremely purifying, and life-promoting.
<s>Bhallātaka</s>s are sharp, ripening, and equal to fire,
but, when used according to rule, they become like nectar.

children.text: kaphajo na sa rogo 'sti na vibandho 'sti kaścana
children.translated_text: There is no disease born from <s>kapha</s>, nor any constipation,

children.text: yaṃ na bhallātakaṃ hanyāc chīghram agnibalapradam ||
children.translated_text: that <s>bhallātaka</s>, quickly giving strength to the digestive fire, does not destroy.
Even under the regimen of wind and sun, one should especially avoid
<s>kulattha</s>, curds, sour fermented liquids, oil massage, and exposure to fire.
There are trees called <s>tubaraka</s>, born on the shore of the western ocean,
whose leaves are shaken by winds stirred up by the tossing of wave-surges.
From them one should take fully ripe fruits when the rains arrive;
taking the kernels from the fruits, drying them, and pulverizing them,

children.text: tilavat pīḍayed droṇyāṃ kvāthayed vā kusumbhavat
children.translated_text: one should press them in a trough like sesame, or boil them like <s>kusumbha</s>.

children.text: tattailaṃ saṃbhṛtaṃ bhūyaḥ paced ā salilakṣayāt ||
children.translated_text: The oil thus collected should again be cooked until the water is exhausted.
Taking it down, one should keep it in dung for a fortnight.

children.text: snigdhasvinno hṛtamalaḥ pakṣād uddhṛtya tat tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After a fortnight, the patient, oleated, fomented, and cleansed of impurity, should take it out;
with meals separated by a fourth-day interval, he should drink a palmful in the morning
of the oil purified by the following mantra on an auspicious day:
O essence of marrow, of great power, purify all the bodily tissues;
<s>Acyuta</s>, holding conch, discus, and mace in his hand, commands you.

children.text: tenāsyordhvam adhastāc ca doṣā yānty asakṛt tataḥ
children.translated_text: By it his <s>doṣa</s>s go upward and downward again and again; then,
in the evening he should drink cool <s>yavāgū</s> without fat and salt.

children.text: pañcāhāni pibet tailam itthaṃ varjyān vivarjayan
children.translated_text: In this way he should drink the oil for five days, avoiding the prohibited things.
For a fortnight, eating rice with <s>mudga</s> broth, he is freed from all skin diseases.

children.text: tad eva khadirakvāthe triguṇe sādhu sādhitam
children.translated_text: The same oil, well cooked in three times the quantity of <s>khadira</s> decoction,

children.text: nihitaṃ pūrvavat pakṣaṃ piben māsaṃ suyantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: kept for a fortnight as before, should be drunk for a month by one who is well restrained.
And with his body anointed by it, following the prescribed diet,
by this swift course one should treat a man suffering from <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: sarpirmadhuyutaṃ pītaṃ tad eva khadirād vinā
children.translated_text: The same oil, drunk with ghee and honey, without <s>khadira</s>,
while one lives on meat broth for a fortnight, makes a man live for two hundred years.

children.text: tad eva nasye pañcāśad divasān upayojitam
children.translated_text: The same oil, used as nasal medication for fifty days,
makes one handsome, retentive of learning, and three hundred years old.

children.text: pañcāṣṭau sapta daśa vā pippalīr madhusarpiṣā
children.translated_text: Five, eight, seven, or ten <s>pippalī</s>s with honey and ghee,
one seeking <s>rasāyana</s> benefits should use for one full year.

children.text: tisras tisras tu pūrvāhṇe bhuktvāgre bhojanasya ca
children.translated_text: Or three <s>pippalī</s>s each in the morning, before eating, and after the meal,
steeped in <s>kiṃśuka</s> alkali and fried in ghee,
should be used mixed with honey by one seeking <s>rasāyana</s> benefits.
By gradual increase for ten days, up to a day of ten <s>pippalī</s>s,
he should increase them with milk, and then withdraw them again in the same way.
When the medicine has been digested, he should eat <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.
This course of a thousand <s>pippalī</s>s is a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: piṣṭās tā balibhiḥ peyāḥ śṛtā madhyabalair naraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Pounded <s>pippalī</s>s should be drunk by strong men, and boiled ones by men of middling strength.

children.text: tadvac ca chāgadugdhena dve sahasre prayojayet
children.translated_text: In the same way, with goat's milk, one should use two thousand.
By these courses, <s>pippalī</s>s remove cough, dyspnea, and obstruction of the throat,
consumption, urinary disorders, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, piles, pallor, and irregular fevers.

children.text: ghnanti śophaṃ vamiṃ hidhmāṃ plīhānaṃ vātaśoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: They destroy swelling, vomiting, hiccup, splenic enlargement, and <s>vātaśoṇita</s>.

children.text: bilvārdhamātreṇa ca pippalīnāṃ pātraṃ pralimped ayaso niśāyām
children.translated_text: With a quantity of long pepper measuring half a <s>bilva</s>, one should smear an iron vessel at night.

children.text: prātaḥ pibet tat salilāñjalibhyāṃ varṣaṃ yatheṣṭāśanapānaceṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the morning he should drink that with two handfuls of water for a year, eating, drinking, and acting as he wishes.
Dry ginger, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, turmeric, <s>atibalā</s>, and <s>balā</s>,
<s>mustā</s>, <s>surāhvā</s>, aloe-wood, <s>citraka</s>, fragrant lotus, lotus, and blue lotuses,
and the heartwood of <s>dhava</s>, <s>aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>āsana</s>, and <s>bālapattrasāra</s> are likewise to be used in the manner of long pepper.

children.text: lohopaliptāḥ pṛthag eva jīvet samāḥ śataṃ vyādhijarāvimuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Smeared separately on iron, they make one live a hundred years, freed from disease and old age.

children.text: kṣīrāñjalibhyāṃ ca rasāyanāni yuktāny amūny āyasalepanāni
children.translated_text: And these <s>rasāyana</s> preparations, when joined with two handfuls of milk and applied to iron,

children.text: kurvanti pūrvoktaguṇaprakarṣam āyuḥprakarṣaṃ dviguṇaṃ tataś ca ||
children.translated_text: produce an increase in the qualities mentioned before, and thereafter a twofold increase of life span.
One should prepare <s>somarājī</s>, steeped in decoctions of <s>āsana</s> and <s>khadira</s>, together with honey, ghee, <s>śikhi</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, and iron powder.

children.text: śaradam avalihānaḥ pāriṇāmān vikārāṃs tyajati mitahitāśī tadvad āhārajātān ||
children.translated_text: By licking it for a year, while eating measured and wholesome food, one abandons disorders of digestion and likewise those arising from food.

children.text: tīvreṇa kuṣṭhena parītamūrtir yaḥ somarājīṃ niyamena khādet
children.translated_text: A man whose body is overcome by severe <s>kuṣṭha</s> should eat <s>somarājī</s> according to rule.
For a year, with black sesame as its companion, he surpasses <s>somarājī</s> in bodily appearance.

children.text: ye somarājyā vituṣīkṛtāyāś cūrṇair upetāt payasaḥ sujātāt
children.translated_text: Those who take the essence from well-prepared milk mixed with powders of husked <s>somarājī</s>,

children.text: uddhṛtya sāraṃ madhunā lihanti takraṃ tad evānupibanti cānte ||
children.translated_text: lick it with honey, and afterwards drink that same buttermilk as an after-drink,
though suffering from <s>kuṣṭha</s>, with limbs wasting away, become people whose fingers and noses have formed again.
They shine like trees that have once more put forth fresh new shoots.

children.text: rāhor amṛtacauryeṇa lūnād ye patitā galāt
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāhu</s> stole the nectar, the drops of nectar that fell to the earth from his severed throat

children.text: amṛtasya kaṇā bhūmau te laśunatvam āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: became garlic.
Therefore twice-born men do not eat it, since it arose from the body of a demon.
Yet, because it was born directly from nectar, that chief among cultivated plants is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
A person in whom <s>kapha</s> is excessive should habitually take garlic in the cold season and also in spring.
One afflicted by <s>vāta</s> should take it even when the clouds rise, or always, following a summer regimen.
His body should be oleated and purified, and his digestive tract prepared with cold and sweet adjuncts.
The rows of his attendants should be marked with garlic crests and ear-ornaments.
At the end of spring, he should take its bulbs, grown in the snowy mountain and Śaka regions,
remove their skins, and soak them at night in liquor and the like.
In the morning, the juice of that paste, squeezed through a clean cloth,
should be combined with one third part of well-fermented wine.
Or it may be combined with another liquor, buttermilk, whey, or sour gruel,

children.text: tatkāla eva vā yuktaṃ yuktam ālocya mātrayā ||
children.translated_text: or even mixed at that very time, after considering the proper dose.
It may be used separately with oil, ghee, fat, marrow, milk, and meat broth,

children.text: kvāthena vā yathāvyādhi rasaṃ kevalam eva vā ||
children.translated_text: or with a decoction according to the disease, or else simply as the juice alone.
First he should drink a mouthful, in order to cleanse the channel of the throat.
Afterwards, continuous fomentation is recommended when there is pain.
In vomiting or fainting, cold water should suddenly be sprinkled on the face.

children.text: śeṣaṃ pibet klamāpāye sthiratāṃ gata ojasi ||
children.translated_text: He should drink the rest when fatigue has passed and the <s>ojas</s> has become steady.
To prevent burning, he should be thoroughly treated with cold anointments.
He should wear garlands of watery drops, pearls, and camphor.

children.text: kuḍavo 'sya parā mātrā tadardhaṃ kevalasya tu
children.translated_text: A <s>kuḍava</s> is its highest dose; for the pure juice, half of that is the dose.

children.text: palaṃ piṣṭasya tanmajjñaḥ sabhaktaṃ prāk ca śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: For its paste, a <s>pala</s> is the dose; one who knows the measure should take it with food and before food.
When it has been digested, he should eat old <s>śāli</s> rice, white like conch, jasmine, and the moon,

children.text: bhuñjīta yūṣair payasā rasair vā dhanvacāriṇām ||
children.translated_text: with soups, milk, or broths of animals that roam in arid land.

children.text: madyam ekaṃ pibet tatra tṛṭprabandhe jalānvitam
children.translated_text: In that regimen, when thirst persists, he should drink wine alone, mixed with water.
But one who does not drink liquor should drink <s>āranāla</s>, fruit-water, or <s>parisikthaka</s>.
Or he may take its paste mixed with an equal amount of ghee, churned in a ghee-vessel,

children.text: sthitaṃ daśāhād aśnīyāt tadvad vā vasayā samam ||
children.translated_text: after it has stood for ten days; or similarly he may take it mixed with fat.
He may freely eat skewered meats stuffed with abundant peeled garlic bulbs, along with various relishes,

children.text: nimardakān vā ghṛtaśuktayuktān prakāmam adyāllaghu tuccham aśnan ||
children.translated_text: or <s>nimardaka</s> preparations mixed with ghee and vinegar, while otherwise eating light and little food.
When <s>vāyu</s> is freed from <s>pitta</s> and blood and stripped of all coverings,

children.text: śuddhe vā vidyate vāyau na dravyaṃ laśunāt param ||
children.translated_text: or when it has been purified, there is no substance superior to garlic.
For one fond of water, jaggery, and milk, who dislikes meat, liquor, and sour things,

children.text: atitikṣor ajīrṇaṃ ca laśuno vyāpade dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: and who is very intolerant, indigestion from garlic is certain to bring harm.
At the end, because of the danger of provoking <s>pitta</s>, one should apply a mild purgation.
In this way he obtains the <s>rasāyana</s> qualities in full.
What the mountains, heated by the sun in summer, exude like lac
is called <s>śilājatu</s>, the essence of the six metals beginning with gold.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca tiktakaṭukaṃ nātyuṣṇaṃ kaṭu pākataḥ
children.translated_text: All of it is bitter and pungent, not excessively hot, and pungent in post-digestive effect.

children.text: chedanaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa lauhaṃ tatra praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: It is especially scraping; among its types, the iron type is praised.
The best <s>śilājatu</s> smells like cow urine, is black, resembles <s>guggulu</s>, is free from grit, and is smooth.

children.text: snigdham anamlakaṣāyaṃ mṛdu guru ca śilājatu śreṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, neither sour nor astringent, soft, and heavy.
Remembering the disease, the patient, and what is suitable to him, one should process it in an iron vessel.

children.text: prāk kevalajaladhautaṃ śuṣkaṃ kvāthais tato bhāvyam ||
children.translated_text: First it is washed with plain water and dried; afterwards it is to be processed with decoctions.
The processing herb, equal in amount to the mountain-born substance, should be decocted in eight times its water.
When that extract has been reduced to one eighth, strained, and kept warm, one should put the <s>girija</s> into it.

children.text: tat samarasatāṃ yātaṃ saṃśuṣkaṃ prakṣiped rase bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: When it has become homogeneous and dried, one should put it again into the liquid.

children.text: svaiḥ svair evaṃ kvāthair bhāvyaṃ vārān bhavet sapta ||
children.translated_text: In this way it should be processed seven times with each of its own decoctions.
Then, for one who has been oleated and purified, ghee cooked with bitter drugs

children.text: tryahaṃ yuñjīta girijam ekaikena tathā tryaham ||
children.translated_text: should be used for three days; then <s>girija</s> should likewise be used for three days with each preparation.
With the decoction of the three fruits, of <s>paṭolā</s>, and of <s>madhuka</s>...

children.text: yogaṃ yogyaṃ tatas tasya kālāpekṣaṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should administer to him a preparation suited to him, with regard to the proper time.
In this way <s>śilājatu</s> becomes extremely beneficial for the body.

children.text: guṇān samagrān kurute sahasā vyāpadaṃ na ca ||
children.translated_text: It quickly produces the full set of virtues, and no mishap occurs.
One, three, seven, or seven weeks; a karṣa, half a pala, or a pala:
these are considered respectively the mild, medium, and superior regimens of <s>śilājatu</s>.
When the substance called mountain-born has been processed and is used in a processed body,
combined with copper, iron, silver, or gold, either separately or all together,
and stirred into milk, it should quickly produce the result of a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).

children.text: kulatthān kākamācīṃ ca kapotāṃśca sadā tyajet ||
children.translated_text: One should always avoid <s>kulattha</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and pigeons.

children.text: na so 'sti rogo bhuvi sādhyarūpo jatvaśmajaṃ yaṃ na jayet prasahya
children.translated_text: There is no curable disease on earth that the rock-born bitumen does not conquer by force,

children.text: tatkālayogair vidhivat prayuktaṃ svasthasya corjāṃ vipulāṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: when used according to rule with the proper timing; and for a healthy person it bestows abundant vitality.
Entering a medicinal hut is beneficial for those who have time and possess the required equipment.

children.text: ato 'nyathā tu ye teṣāṃ sauryamārutiko vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for others than these, the procedure is one exposed to sun and wind.
Therefore preparations that tolerate wind and sun will now be described in particular,

children.text: sukhopacārā bhraṃśe 'pi ye na dehasya bādhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which are easy to manage and, even if the regimen lapses, do not harm the body.

children.text: śītodakaṃ payaḥ kṣaudraṃ ghṛtam ekaikaśo dviśaḥ
children.translated_text: Cold water, milk, honey, and ghee, each singly, in pairs,

children.text: triśaḥ samastam athavā prāk pītaṃ sthāpayed vayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in groups of three, or all together, when drunk beforehand, stabilize age.

children.text: guḍena madhunā śuṇṭhyā kṛṣṇayā lavaṇena vā
children.translated_text: If one regularly eats two <s>harītakī</s> fruits with jaggery, honey, dry ginger, long pepper, or salt,

children.text: dve dve khādan sadā pathye jīved varṣaśataṃ sukhī ||
children.translated_text: while maintaining a wholesome diet, one lives happily for a hundred years.

children.text: harītakīṃ sarpiṣi sampratāpya samaśnatas tat pibato ghṛtaṃ ca
children.translated_text: For one who heats <s>harītakī</s> in ghee, eats it, and drinks that ghee too,

children.text: bhaveccirasthāyi balaṃ śarīre sakṛt kṛtaṃ sādhu yathā kṛtajñe ||
children.translated_text: strength remains long in the body, as a single good deed remains with a grateful person.
For men of wholesome diet who lick <s>dhātrī</s> juice, honey, sugar, and ghee,

children.text: praṇāśam āyānti jarāvikārā granthā viśālā iva durgṛhītāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the disorders of old age go to destruction, like large knots badly tied.
For a man who uses powder of <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>kṛmighna</s>, and <s>asana</s> heartwood, with oil, ghee, honey, and iron filings,
youthfulness and beauty remain unlost.

children.text: lauhaṃ rajo vellabhavaṃ ca sarpiḥkṣaudradrutaṃ sthāpitam abdamātram
children.translated_text: Iron powder, powder produced from <s>vella</s>, ghee, honey, and a liquid, kept for a full year

children.text: samudgake bījakasārakﾱpte lihan balī jīvati kṛṣṇakeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in a covered casket prepared from the heartwood of <s>bījaka</s>: licking it, a strong man lives with black hair.
Those who eat <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>, combined with ghee and honey,

children.text: jarānadīṃ rogataraṃgiṇīṃ te lāvaṇyayuktāḥ puruṣās taranti ||
children.translated_text: cross the river of old age, with its waves of disease, as men endowed with beauty.
Those who regularly use <s>triphalā</s> steeped in a broth of <s>khadira</s> and <s>asana</s>, drenched with ghee and honey,

children.text: niyamena narā niṣevitāro yadi jīvantyarujaḥ kim atra citram ||
children.translated_text: live free from illness; what wonder is there in that?

children.text: bījakasya rasam aṅgulihāryaṃ śarkarāṃ madhu ghṛtaṃ triphalāṃ ca
children.translated_text: In men who habitually use juice of <s>bījaka</s> in a quantity that can be carried on a finger, along with sugar, honey, ghee, and <s>triphalā</s>,

children.text: śīlayatsu puruṣeṣu jarattā svāgatāpi vinivartata eva ||
children.translated_text: old age turns back, even when it has arrived as a welcome guest.

children.text: punarnavasyārdhapalaṃ navasya piṣṭaṃ pibed yaḥ payasārdhamāsam
children.translated_text: One who drinks half a pala of fresh <s>punarnavā</s>, ground with milk, for half a month,

children.text: māsadvayaṃ tattriguṇaṃ samāṃ vā jīrṇo 'pi bhūyaḥ sa punarnavaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: or three times that amount for two months or for a year, becomes renewed again even when old.
For <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>aṃśumatī</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>asana</s>, and <s>sārivā</s>,
and for <s>kālānusārī</s>, <s>aguru</s>, and sandalwood, they prescribe the same <s>punarnavā</s> regimen.
Those who eat ghee prepared with paste and decoction of <s>śatāvarī</s>, accompanied by sugar,
are not robbed by the thieves that are diseases after they have set out on the road of life.

children.text: pītāśvagandhā payasārdhamāsaṃ ghṛtena tailena sukhāmbunā vā
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvagandhā</s>, drunk with milk for half a month, or with ghee, oil, or pleasant water,

children.text: kṛśasya puṣṭiṃ vapuṣo vidhatte bālasya sasyasya yathā suvṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: produces nourishment in the body of a thin person, like good rain for a young crop.
For those who eat a <s>prakuñca</s> of black sesame day by day, followed by cold water,

children.text: poṣaḥ śarīrasya bhavatyanalpo dṛḍhībhavanty ā maraṇācca dantāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the body's nourishment becomes considerable, and the teeth grow firm until death.
A bull-like, steady man who licks powder of <s>śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>, mixed with a portion of ghee and honey,

children.text: vṛṣaḥ sthiraḥ śāntavikāraduḥkhaḥ samāḥ śataṃ jīvati kṛṣṇakeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lives a hundred years, with black hair and with the pains of disorders pacified.

children.text: sārdhaṃ tilair āmalakāni kṛṣṇair akṣāṇi saṃkṣudya harītakīr vā
children.translated_text: Those who crush <s>āmalaka</s> fruits together with black sesame, or <s>akṣa</s> fruits, or <s>harītakī</s> fruits,

children.text: ye 'dyur mayūrā iva te manuṣyā ramyaṃ parīṇāmam avāpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: and eat them, like peacocks, attain a beautiful ripening of age.
One whose food is <s>śilājatu</s>, honey, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, ghee, iron, <s>abhayā</s>, mercury, and pyrite
has his weakened bodily tissues filled out in fifteen days, like the moon.

children.text: ye māsam ekaṃ svarasaṃ pibanti dine dine bhṛṅgarajaḥsamuttham
children.translated_text: Those who for one month drink fresh juice produced from <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> day by day,

children.text: kṣīrāśinas te balavīryayuktāḥ samāḥ śataṃ jīvitam āpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: while living on milk, obtain life for a hundred years, endowed with strength and virility.

children.text: māsaṃ vacām apyupasevamānāḥ kṣīreṇa tailena ghṛtena vāpi
children.translated_text: Those who also use <s>vacā</s> for a month, with milk, oil, or ghee,
become unassailable by demons, intelligent, and speakers of pure, polished speech.

children.text: maṇḍūkaparṇīm api bhakṣayanto bhṛṣṭāṃ ghṛte māsam anannabhakṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who eat <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> too, fried in ghee for a month and taking no other food,
live a long time, bold and established in the rise of the qualities of youthfulness and beauty.
With <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and fifty palas of iron,
three hundred pills are made with sixty palas of the fresh juice of <s>mārkava</s>.

children.text: chāyāviśuṣkaṃ guṭikārdham adyāt pūrvaṃ samastām api tāṃ krameṇa
children.translated_text: After they have been dried in the shade, one should eat half a pill at first, and then all of it gradually.

children.text: bhajed viriktaḥ kramaśaśca maṇḍaṃ peyāṃ vilepīṃ rasakaudanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Having been purged, he should gradually take thin gruel, thicker gruel, linctus, and rice with meat broth.

children.text: sarpiḥsnigdhaṃ māsam ekaṃ yatātmā māsād ūrdhvaṃ sarvathā svairavṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Self-controlled, with the body oleated by ghee, he should continue for one month; after the month he may live freely in every respect.

children.text: varjyaṃ yatnāt sarvakālaṃ tvajīrṇaṃ varṣeṇaivaṃ yogam evopayuñjyāt ||
children.translated_text: At all times, however, indigestion must be carefully avoided; in this way one should use the regimen for a full year.

children.text: bhavati vigatarogo yo 'pyasādhyāmayārtaḥ prabalapuruṣakāraḥ śobhate yo 'pi vṛddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Even one afflicted by an incurable illness becomes free from disease; even an old man, strong in manly vigor, shines forth

children.text: upacitapṛthugātraśrotranetrādiyuktas taruṇa iva samānāṃ pañca jīvecchatāni ||
children.translated_text: with well-developed broad limbs and with hearing, sight, and the other faculties intact; like a youth among his peers, he may live five hundred years.
One should pound <s>gāyatrī</s>, <s>śikhi</s>, <s>śiṃśipā</s>, <s>sana</s>, <s>śivā</s>, <s>vellā</s>, <s>akṣa</s>, and <s>kāruṣkara</s>,
and keep them in eighteen times as much water together with pieces made of iron.

children.text: pātre lohamaye tryahaṃ ravikarair āloḍayan pācayet
children.translated_text: In an iron vessel, stirring them for three days under the sun's rays, one should cook them,

children.text: agnau cānu mṛdau salohaśakalaṃ pādasthitaṃ tat pacet ||
children.translated_text: and then cook them over a mild fire, with a piece of iron included, until a quarter remains.

children.text: pūtasyāṃśaḥ kṣīrato 'ṃśastathāṃśau bhārgān niryāsād dvau varāyās trayo 'ṃśāḥ
children.translated_text: Of the strained liquid there is one part; from milk, one part; likewise two parts from the exudate of <s>bhārgī</s>, and three parts of <s>varā</s>;

children.text: aṃśāś catvāraś ceha haiyaṃgavīnād ekīkṛtyaitat sādhayet kṛṣṇalauhe ||
children.translated_text: and here four parts from fresh butter; combining this, one should prepare it in black iron.

children.text: vimalakhaṇḍasitāmadhubhiḥ pṛthag yutam ayuktam idaṃ yadi vā ghṛtam
children.translated_text: This ghee, whether separately mixed with <s>vimalā</s>, sugar candy, white sugar, and honey, or left unmixed,
if taken regularly while following food, drink, and activity according to one's own taste, does not let a man wither.
Prosperous, with sin shaken off, strong as a forest buffalo, swift as a horse, and firm-limbed,
with hair dark blue like female bees, with a mouth fragrant as honey, and enjoying many women,
rich in speech, intelligence, and understanding, and with a very sharp digestive fire, after only a month's use
he bears the body of <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, gleaming like gold heated by a flame.
Diseases do not touch even the eater of the <s>Nārasiṃha</s> preparation,
just as frightened demons do not touch <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, whose arms shine with the discus.

children.text: bhṛṅgapravālān amunaiva bhṛṣṭān ghṛtena yaḥ khādati yantritātmā
children.translated_text: Whoever, self-controlled, eats <s>bhṛṅga</s> shoots fried with this very ghee,
with his bowel purified, using as a drink afterward milk prepared with <s>asana</s> heartwood extract, and taking food prepared from it,
after a month's use lives happily for three hundred years,
and grasps what has been said even once, with memory and senses unimpaired.

children.text: anenaiva ca kalpena yas tailam upayojayet
children.translated_text: And whoever uses oil by this very same procedure

children.text: tān evāpnoti sa guṇān kṛṣṇakeśaś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: obtains those same qualities, and his hair becomes black.
The <s>rasāyana</s> preparations that are practicable, effective, and suited to the age have been stated;
other preparations, though of great benefit, have not been described, because obtaining them and the like is difficult.
If diseases should arise from a lapse in the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure,

children.text: yathāsvam auṣadhaṃ teṣāṃ kāryaṃ muktvā rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: their appropriate medicine should be applied, after abandoning the <s>rasāyana</s>.
One should know a truthful man, free from anger, whose senses are inclined toward the self,
peaceful and devoted to good conduct, to be a perpetual <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: guṇair ebhiḥ samuditaḥ sevate yo rasāyanam
children.translated_text: A person endowed with these qualities who uses <s>rasāyana</s>

children.text: sa nivṛttātmā dīrghāyuḥ paratreha ca modate ||
children.translated_text: becomes self-restrained and long-lived, and rejoices both here and in the next world.
Conduct that follows the treatise, attendants who understand one's mind,
and intelligence that does not falter regarding its objects: this is complete <s>rasāyana</s>.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the method of <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>.
So indeed said <s>Ātreya</s> and the other great seers.
A man devoted to sensual enjoyment should constantly seek <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>;

children.text: tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirapatyaṃ ca guṇavat tatra saṃśritam ||
children.translated_text: satisfaction, nourishment, and excellent offspring are based upon it.
That which produces a line of offspring and immediately causes exhilaration,
by which, being exceedingly strong like a stallion, one goes to women unhindered,
and by which one becomes especially dear to women and grows in whatever respect,
that is <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>; for it is the supreme maker of vigor for the body.
We approve of celibacy as righteous, fame-giving, life-promoting, and a <s>rasāyana</s> for both worlds,
absolutely stainless in every respect.
But for a passionate man of little fortitude, oppressed by afflictions,
<s>vājīkaraṇa</s> is taught for the protection of the body from wasting.
For one who is healthy, in the prime of life, and using <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>,
sexual intercourse day after day in all seasons is not prohibited.
Then, for those who have been oleated and purified, he should first administer decoction enemas together with oil enemas,
combined with ghee, oil, meat broth, milk, sugar, and honey.
An expert in formulations should first apply them to people who eat milk and meat broth;
after that, he should apply the <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> formulations, which give semen, offspring, and strength.
A tree without shade, with foul-smelling flowers and without fruit,
standing alone and with a single branch, is like a man without offspring.
With stumbling gait, indistinct speech, covered with dust,
even with a mouth wet with drool, a child brings delight to the heart.
What is equal to offspring in sight, touch, and the other senses?
How much more so when it increases fame, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), honor, prosperity, and family?
On a purified body, according to one's strength, one should apply virility-producing formulations.
The roots of <s>śara</s>, <s>ikṣu</s>, <s>kuśa</s>, <s>kāśa</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and <s>vīraṇa</s>,
and of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>; <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>balā</s>;

children.text: mede dve dve ca kākolyau śūrpaparṇyau śatāvarīm ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>medā</s>s, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, the two <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>s, and <s>śatāvarī</s>;
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: vīrāṃ payasyāṃ jīvantīm ṛddhiṃ rāsnāṃ trikaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>vīrā</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>ṛddhi</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s>;
<s>madhuka</s> and <s>śāliparṇī</s>, three <s>pala</s>s of each separately,

children.text: māṣāṇām āḍhakaṃ caitad dvidroṇe sādhayed apām ||
children.translated_text: and an <s>āḍhaka</s> of black gram: this should be cooked in two <s>droṇa</s>s of water.
When one <s>āḍhaka</s> of decoction remains, one should cook an <s>āḍhaka</s> of ghee with it,
adding half an <s>āḍhaka</s> each of the juices of <s>vidārī</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, and sugarcane.
One should add milk four times the quantity of the ghee, and these substances to be ground:

children.text: vīrāṃ svaguptāṃ kākolyau yaṣṭīṃ phalgūni pippalīm ||
children.translated_text: <s>vīrā</s>, <s>svaguptā</s>, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, <s>yaṣṭī</s>, <s>phalgūni</s>, and <s>pippalī</s>,
<s>drākṣā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, dates, <s>madhuka</s>s, and <s>śatāvarī</s>.

children.text: tat siddhapūtaṃ cūrṇasya pṛthak prasthena yojayet ||
children.translated_text: When that has been cooked and strained, one should combine it with a <s>prastha</s> each of powder
of sugar and of <s>tugā</s>, and with a <s>kuḍava</s> of <s>pippalī</s>,
with a <s>prakuñca</s> of black pepper, and with separate half-<s>pala</s> measures.
With fine powders of <s>tvak</s>, <s>elā</s>, and <s>kesara</s>, and with two <s>kuḍava</s>s of honey,
he should then eat a <s>pala</s> measure every day, living on meat-juice and milk.
By that he mounts like a stallion and becomes exhilarated like a <s>kuliṅga</s> bird.
Powder of <s>vidārī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>śāli</s> rice, <s>priyāla</s>, and <s>ikṣuraka</s>,
and separately a <s>kuḍava</s> portion of <s>svaguptā</s> root, and the same amount of honey,
half a <s>tulā</s> of powdered sugar and half a <s>prastha</s> of fresh ghee:

children.text: so 'kṣamātram ataḥ khādet yasya rāmāśataṃ gṛhe
children.translated_text: of this, the man in whose house there are a hundred beloved women should eat an <s>akṣa</s> measure.
Fruits of <s>ātmaguptā</s>, cooked in milk with wheat and cooled,
or black gram with ghee and honey, eaten with fresh milk as the after-drink,

children.text: jāgarti rātriṃ sakalām akhinnaḥ khedayan striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: keep him awake the whole night, unwearied, tiring out women.
Sesame seeds repeatedly steeped in milk cooked with goat's testicles,

children.text: yaḥ khādet sasitān gacchet sa strīśatam apūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: if a man eats them with sugar, he goes to a hundred women as though untouched by prior exhaustion.
Powder of <s>vidārī</s>, repeatedly steeped in its own fresh juice,
when licked with honey and ghee, enables him to reach a hundred young women.
Powder of <s>kṛṣṇā</s> and <s>dhātrī</s> fruits, well steeped in their juice,
if a man licks it with sugar, honey, and ghee and then drinks milk,
that man, even at eighty years, becomes delighted like a youth.
A <s>karṣa</s> of <s>madhuka</s> powder, combined with ghee and honey,

children.text: payo'nupānaṃ yo lihyān nityavegaḥ sa nā bhavet
children.translated_text: if he licks it with milk as the after-drink, makes him a man of constant virile impulse.

children.text: kulīraśṛṅgyā yaḥ kalkam āloḍya payasā pibet ||
children.translated_text: If one stirs the paste of <s>kulīraśṛṅgī</s> with milk and drinks it,
while eating sugar, ghee, milk, and rice, he becomes bull-like among women.
If one eats <s>payasyā</s> cooked in milk and joined with honey and ghee,

children.text: pibed bāṣkayaṇaṃ cānu kṣīraṃ na kṣayam eti saḥ
children.translated_text: and afterward drinks <s>bāṣkayaṇa</s> milk, he does not decline.
Seed powder of <s>svayaṅguptā</s> and <s>ikṣuraka</s>, mixed with sugar,
when a man drinks it with milk warm from the udder, makes him like a donkey in sexual vigor.
Powder of <s>uccaṭā</s> too should be used in this same way, and also that of <s>śatāvarī</s>.
The cream of curds, white as the moon, with sugar and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice,
eaten after being well cleansed through cloth, makes even an old man youthful.
<s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>ikṣura</s>, black gram, <s>ātmaguptā</s> seed, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
if drunk with milk, enable even an aged man to go to a hundred young women.

children.text: yat kiṃcin madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ balavardhanam
children.translated_text: Whatever is sweet, unctuous, nourishing, and strength-increasing,

children.text: manaso harṣaṇaṃ yacca tat sarvaṃ vṛṣyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and whatever gladdens the mind, all of that is called <s>vṛṣya</s> (virility-promoting).
Therefore, stimulated by substances of this kind, he should approach a young woman,
aroused by his own impulse and exhilarated by the qualities of women.
The five sense-objects, pleasures for all the senses and shoots of the wish-granting tree of <s>dharma</s>, are to be enjoyed;
they are the supreme excellences of the senses, the five arrows of <s>Kusumadhanvan</s>.
For desired objects, even one by one, bring the highest delight and affection;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ strīśarīre ye saṃghātena pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: how much more those that are established together in a woman's body.

children.text: nāmāpi yasyā hṛdayotsavāya yāṃ paśyatāṃ tṛptiranāptapūrvā
children.translated_text: She whose very name is a festival for the heart, at seeing whom there is a satisfaction never gained before,
who becomes a snare drawing all the senses, who is consecrated to the vow of following her beloved,
adorned with arts, playfulness, limbs, and youth, pure, modest, and bold in private,

children.text: priyaṃvadā tulyamanaḥśayā yā sā strī vṛṣyatvāya paraṃ narasya ||
children.translated_text: sweet-speaking and of like mind and intention: such a woman is supreme for a man's virility.
He should practice the whole course of love, faultless and prescribed in the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>,
according to place, time, strength, and capacity, and not contrary to the statements accepted in the medical treatise.
Oil massage, rubbing with fragrant powders, sprinkling, perfumes, garlands, varied garments, and ornaments,
and companions skilled in music, poetry, and similar conversation, equal in disposition and compliant, should be present.
There should be a pond set within one's own house, with birds intoxicated by the honey of lotus pollen,
and groves at the edge of the city, on the slopes of blue-flanked mountain peaks.
A variety of trees gives pleasure to the eye; the melodious call of cuckoos gives pleasure to the ear.
Adornment suited to the season gives pleasure to the body, and the whole retinue gives pleasure to the mind.

children.text: tāmbūlam acchamadirā kāntā kāntā niśā śaśāṅkāṅkā
children.translated_text: Betel, clear wine, a lovely beloved, and a lovely moon-marked night:

children.text: yad yacca kiṃcid iṣṭaṃ manaso vājīkaraṃ tat tat ||
children.translated_text: whatever is dear to the mind, that very thing is aphrodisiac.

children.text: madhu mukham iva sotpalaṃ priyāyāḥ kalaraṇanā parivādinī priyeva
children.translated_text: Mead is like the lotus-bearing face of the beloved, and the softly sounding lute is like the beloved herself.

children.text: kusumacayamanoramā ca śayyā kisalayinī latikeva puṣpitāgrā ||
children.translated_text: A bed charming with a heap of flowers is like a tender creeper with flowering tips.

children.text: deśe śarīre ca na kācid artirartheṣu nālpo 'pi manovidhānaḥ
children.translated_text: When there is no distress in the place or in the body, and not even slight mental distraction over affairs,

children.text: vājīkarāḥ saṃnihitāśca yogāḥ kāmasya kāmaṃ paripūrayanti ||
children.translated_text: and aphrodisiac preparations are at hand, they fully satisfy the desire of passion.

children.text: mustā parpaṭakaṃ jvare tṛṣi jalaṃ mṛdbhṛṣṭaloṣṭodbhavaṃ lājāśchardiṣu vastijeṣu girijaṃ meheṣu dhātrīniśe
children.translated_text: <s>Mustā</s> and <s>parpaṭaka</s> are best in fever; in thirst, water produced from a clay-roasted clod; parched grain in vomiting; mountain resin in bladder disorders; <s>dhātrī</s> with <s>niśā</s> in urinary diseases.

children.text: pāṇḍau śreṣṭham ayo 'bhayānilakaphe plīhāmaye pippalī saṃdhāne kṛmijā viṣe śukatarur medo'nile gugguluḥ ||
children.translated_text: In pallor, iron is best; <s>abhayā</s> for wind and phlegm; <s>pippalī</s> in spleen disease; what is born of worms in poisoning; <s>śukataru</s> in healing; and <s>guggulu</s> for fat and wind disorders.
<s>Vṛṣa</s> is best in blood-pitta, <s>kuṭaja</s> in diarrhea, <s>bhallātaka</s> in piles, and gold in artificial poisons.

children.text: sthūleṣu tārkṣyaṃ kṛmiṣu kṛmighnaṃ śoṣe surā chāgapayo 'tha māṃsam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tārkṣya</s> is best for the corpulent, <s>kṛmighna</s> for worms, and liquor, goat's milk, and meat for wasting.

children.text: akṣyāmayeṣu triphalā guḍūcī vātāsraroge mathitaṃ grahaṇyām
children.translated_text: <s>Triphalā</s> is best in eye diseases, <s>guḍūcī</s> in <s>vātarakta</s>, and churned curd in <s>grahaṇī</s> disease.

children.text: kuṣṭheṣu sevyaḥ khadirasya sāraḥ sarveṣu rogeṣu śilāhvayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The heartwood of <s>khadira</s> is to be used in skin diseases, and <s>śilāhvaya</s> in all diseases.

children.text: unmādaṃ ghṛtam anavaṃ śokaṃ madyaṃ vyapasmṛtiṃ brāhmī
children.translated_text: Fresh ghee overcomes insanity, wine overcomes grief, and <s>brāhmī</s> overcomes disordered memory.
Milk conquers sleeplessness, and <s>rasālā</s> conquers catarrh.

children.text: māṃsaṃ kārśyaṃ laśunaḥ prabhañjanaṃ stabdhagātratāṃ svedaḥ
children.translated_text: Meat conquers emaciation, garlic conquers deranged wind, and sweating conquers stiffness of the body.
As nasal medication, the <s>khapura</s> of <s>guḍamañjarī</s> conquers pain of the shoulders, upper arms, and arms.
Camel's urine and milk, rubbed with a lump of fresh butter, destroys abdominal disease.
Nasal therapy removes disorders of the head; letting blood quickly removes a newly arisen abscess.
Nasal therapy and mouthful gargling remove diseases of the mouth; nasal therapy, collyrium, and eye-tarpana remove pains of the eyes.
For an old person, milk and ghee are best; for fainting, cold water, wind, and shade.

children.text: samaśuktārdrakamātrā mande vahnau śrame surā snānam
children.translated_text: When the digestive fire is weak, an equal measure of sour ferment and fresh ginger is best; in fatigue, liquor and bathing.

children.text: duḥkhasahatve sthairye vyāyāmo gokṣurur hitaḥ kṛcchre ||
children.translated_text: For the capacity to endure hardship and for steadiness, exercise is beneficial; in urinary difficulty, <s>gokṣura</s> is beneficial.
In cough, <s>nidigdhikā</s> is best; in pain of the side, the root of <s>puṣkaraja</s>.

children.text: vayasaḥ sthāpane dhātrī triphalā guggulur vraṇe ||
children.translated_text: For sustaining age, <s>dhātrī</s> is best; in wounds, <s>triphalā</s> and <s>guggulu</s>.

children.text: vastir vātavikārān paittān rekaḥ kaphodbhavān vamanam
children.translated_text: Enema conquers disorders of vāta; purgation conquers those of pitta; emesis conquers those arising from kapha.

children.text: kṣaudraṃ jayati balāsaṃ sarpiḥ pittaṃ samīraṇaṃ tailam ||
children.translated_text: Honey conquers <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic disorder); ghee conquers pitta; oil conquers vāta.

children.text: ityagryaṃ yat proktaṃ rogāṇām auṣadhaṃ śamāyālam
children.translated_text: Thus what has been stated as the foremost medicine for the pacification of diseases is sufficient.
It should be adapted, according to suitability, with regard to place, time, and strength.
Having received from <s>Ātreya</s> the concise meaning of these elegant sayings, and still unsatisfied,
<s>Agniveśa</s>, humble with devotion and doubtful, asked this, approved by <s>Bheḍa</s> and the others:
'Blessed sir, some people are seen to be sick even though they are self-controlled,
provided with medicines and attendants, and following the opinions of elder physicians.
Their diseases, vitality, and life are wasting away; and others, though the opposite, are otherwise.
Therefore the fruit of the distinction between wholesome and unwholesome is uncertain.

children.text: kiṃ śāsti śāstram asmin iti kalpayato 'gniveśamukhyasya
children.translated_text: What, then, does the śāstra teach in this matter?' To <s>Agniveśa</s>, foremost among the pupils, as he was thinking thus,
<s>Punarvasu</s> explained the whole truth.

children.text: na cikitsācikitsā ca tulyā bhavitum arhati
children.translated_text: 'Treatment and non-treatment cannot rightly be equal,
because those who attain health even without intervention are only a sixteenth share.
For those sunk in the mud of disease, the physician's victory is a supporting hand;
but the life of all those who are dying does not come from medicine alone.

children.text: na hyupāyam apekṣante sarve rogā na cānyathā
children.translated_text: For not all diseases require a remedy, nor is it otherwise:
those curable by remedies are cured, because what has a cause is not without a cause.
As for the statement that death occurs even with treatment endowed with every excellence,
that is not so; there is no absence of method in the method.
Still, for an intelligent man furnished with the proper means, an action may sometimes

children.text: na sidhyed daivavaiguṇyān na tviyaṃ ṣoḍaśātmikā ||
children.translated_text: fail because of a defect in fate, but this sixteenfold therapy does not fail in itself.
For whom have fire, hot water, and the like failed in procedures such as sweating and immobilizing?

children.text: na prīṇanaṃ karṣaṇaṃ vā kasya kṣīraṃ gavedhukam ||
children.translated_text: For whom are milk and <s>gavedhuka</s> not, respectively, nourishing and emaciating?
For whom is there no certainty about the aphrodisiac effect of <s>māṣa</s>, <s>ātmaguptā</s>, and the rest?
For whom are the production of feces and urine, and the drawing-out action, doubtful in barley?
For whom does poison become digested when it is not accompanied by mantra and tantra?

children.text: kaḥ prāptaḥ kalyatāṃ pathyād ṛte rohiṇikādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: Who has attained well-being without a wholesome regimen in diseases such as <s>rohiṇikā</s>?
Moreover, untimely death is established with certainty in all systems;
otherwise how could it be warded off even by great effort?
The use of sandalwood and the like in burning conditions is established and preceded by tradition.

children.text: śāstrād eva gataṃ siddhiṃ jvare laṅghanabṛṃhaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Fasting and nourishing in fever have attained success only from the śāstra.
When the four limbs are endowed with their qualities, properly considered, and applied,
do not entertain doubt about the destruction of disease in treatment.
For this is a firm cutting of the nooses of death before their time;
for those terrified and frightened by disease, it is a protective thread, though not made of thread.
This is indeed that nectar itself, free from the distress of the world;
but when it is placed in an unworthy vessel, it immediately turns into deadly <s>hālāhala</s> poison.
Those who do not know the true nature of the śāstra, and those devoted to scripture alone,

children.text: tyajed dūrād bhiṣakpāśān pāśān vaivasvatān iva ||
children.translated_text: one should abandon from afar as snares in the form of physicians, like the snares of <s>Vaivasvata</s>.
Blessing upon physicians of good conduct, rich in tradition;
blessing upon those practiced in their work; blessing upon those who desire what is auspicious.
Thus this medical śāstra, furnished with the virtues of a tantra and free from the faults of a tantra,

children.text: cikitsāśāstram akhilaṃ vyāpya yat paritaḥ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: stands pervading the whole field of treatment in every direction.
It follows the views of great sages whose knowledge is vast and stainless,
and it indicates a collected meaning as deep as the great ocean.
By churning the great ocean of eight-branched medicine, the great mass of nectar, the <s>Aṣṭāṅgasaṃgraha</s>, was obtained.

children.text: tasmād analpaphalam alpasamudyamānāṃ prītyartham etad uditaṃ pṛthag eva tantram ||
children.translated_text: From that, this separate tantra, yielding much fruit for little effort, has been stated for the pleasure of those who undertake little exertion.
Because this is established by tradition and because its results are seen directly,
it should be applied like a mantra and should not be investigated in any way.

children.text: dīrghajīvitam ārogyaṃ dharmam arthaṃ sukhaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Long life, health, dharma, wealth, happiness, and fame
one certainly obtains from this through recitation, understanding, and practice.

children.text: etat paṭhan saṃgrahabodhaśaktaḥ svabhyastakarmā bhiṣag aprakampyaḥ
children.translated_text: A physician who reads this, is able to understand the compendium, and has well-practiced his work is unshakable.
If he shakes off the attacks made by authors of other extensive tantras, that is no wonder.

children.text: yadi carakam adhīte taddhruvaṃ suśrutādipraṇigaditagadānāṃ nāmamātre 'pi bāhyaḥ
children.translated_text: If he studies <s>Caraka</s>, still he is certainly outside even the mere names of diseases taught by <s>Suśruta</s> and others.

children.text: atha carakavihīnaḥ prakriyāyām aklinnaḥ kim iva khalu karotu vyādhitānāṃ varākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if, lacking <s>Caraka</s>, he is not fatigued in procedure, what indeed can the poor man do for the sick?

children.text: abhiniveśavaśād abhiyujyate subhaṇite 'pi na yo dṛḍhamūḍhakaḥ
children.translated_text: The man who, under the sway of stubborn attachment, does not engage even with a well-spoken text is deeply foolish.

children.text: paṭhatu yatnaparaḥ puruṣāyuṣaṃ sa khalu vaidyakam ādyam anirvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let him, intent on effort and without despondency, study the foremost medical work, <s>Puruṣāyuṣa</s>.

children.text: vāte pitte śleṣmaśāntau ca pathyaṃ tailaṃ sarpir mākṣikaṃ ca krameṇa
children.translated_text: For the pacification of vāta, pitta, and śleṣma, the wholesome things are, in order, oil, ghee, and honey.

children.text: etad brahmā bhāṣatāṃ brahmajo vā kā nirmantre vaktṛbhedoktiśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether <s>Brahmā</s> said this, or one born from <s>Brahmā</s>, what power has a statement about difference of speaker where there is no mantra?'
Or rather, is the power of a substance distinguished according to the will of the speaker?
Therefore, abandoning envy, one should adopt impartiality.
If there is affection for what was composed by sages, then, apart from <s>Caraka</s> and <s>Suśruta</s>,

children.text: bheḍādyāḥ kiṃ na paṭhyante tasmād grāhyaṃ subhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: why are <s>Bheḍa</s> and the others not studied? Therefore a well-spoken statement should be accepted.
This is, as it were, the heart of the whole ocean of Ayurvedic literature;

children.text: kṛtvā yacchubham āptaṃ śubham astu paraṃ tato jagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made it, whatever good has been obtained, from that may there be supreme good for the world.
